# Links, images and media

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/page-media/

A page is more than text: it links to other pages, shows pictures, plays sound and video and draws shapes. This lesson covers the elements for all of that, and the attributes that make them fast, accessible and safe.

## Links

A `link` takes the reader somewhere. Its `url` is required and its `content` is the text the reader clicks. The address can point to another site, to a file next to your page, or to a place on the same page: a `url` that starts with `#` scrolls to the element whose `id` is the rest of it. Two more kinds are worth knowing. `mailto:` opens the mail program with a new message, and `tel:` offers to call the number on a phone.

web-media-links.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Links"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.8 end
    paragraph:
        content = "Read the "
        link: url = "#rules" content = "house rules" end
        span: content = " first, then write to " end
        link: url = "mailto:club@example.com" content = "the club" end
        span: content = " or call " end
        link: url = "tel:+15550100" content = "555 0100" end
        span: content = "." end
    end
    paragraph:
        link: url = "https://example.com/guide" target = "new" rel = "noopener" content = "The full guide (new tab)" end
    end
    paragraph:
        link:
            url = "maps/garden.pdf"
            download = "garden-map.pdf"
            type = "application/pdf"
            hreflang = "en"
            content = "Download the garden map"
        end
    end
    heading: id = "rules" size = 2 content = "House rules" end
    paragraph: content = "Keep the gate closed. Water the beds in the morning." end
end
```

The attributes in the example each do one job. `target` says where the page opens: `new` is a new tab (the HTML word is `_blank`, and both work), `same` is the current tab, and `parent` and `top` matter only inside frames. `rel` describes the relationship to the target. With `noopener` the new tab cannot reach back to your page, which matters for a link to a site you do not control, and `nofollow` asks search engines not to count the link. `download` makes the browser save the file instead of showing it, and its value is the suggested file name. `type` is the kind of file you expect and `hreflang` the language of the target page. Both are hints. `ping` lists addresses that are told when someone follows the link, and `referrer policy` controls how much of your address the target site is given.

Write link text that makes sense on its own, such as "the house rules", and not "click here": screen readers can read out a list of all the links on a page. A link cannot contain another link or a button, and the compiler reports an error (E116) if you try. It also refuses addresses like `javascript:` that would run code (E018).

## Images

`image` shows a picture. The `url` is required. The text description is the `alt` attribute, and `content` sets the same attribute, so you can write whichever reads better. The description is what a screen reader says and what the browser shows when the file cannot be loaded. Describe what the picture tells, not what it is: "A red kite over green hills", not "image". If the picture is only decoration, give it an empty description, `alt = ""`, and screen readers will skip it. When you give neither, the compiler writes the empty one for you.

web-media-image.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Images"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    paragraph: content = "A photo with a description:" end
    image:
        content = "A red kite flying over green hills"
        width = 160
        height = 100
        loading = lazy
        decoding = async
        url = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20viewBox=%270%200%20160%20100%27%20width=%27160%27%20height=%27100%27%3E%3Crect%20width=%27160%27%20height=%27100%27%20fill=%27%23bae6fd%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M0%20100%20Q50%2055%20100%2085%20T160%2075%20V100Z%27%20fill=%27%2316a34a%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M110%2012%20L130%2032%20L110%2052%20L90%2032Z%27%20fill=%27%23dc2626%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M110%2052%20Q100%2070%20112%2082%27%20stroke=%27%23475569%27%20fill=%27none%27/%3E%3Ctext%20x=%276%27%20y=%2714%27%20font-size=%2711%27%20font-family=%27sans-serif%27%20fill=%27%230c4a6e%27%3E%3C/text%3E%3C/svg%3E"
    end
    paragraph: content = "A decorative picture has an empty description:" end
    image: alt = "" width = 80 height = 50 url = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20viewBox=%270%200%20160%20100%27%20width=%27160%27%20height=%27100%27%3E%3Crect%20width=%27160%27%20height=%27100%27%20fill=%27%23bae6fd%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M0%20100%20Q50%2055%20100%2085%20T160%2075%20V100Z%27%20fill=%27%2316a34a%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M110%2012%20L130%2032%20L110%2052%20L90%2032Z%27%20fill=%27%23dc2626%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M110%2052%20Q100%2070%20112%2082%27%20stroke=%27%23475569%27%20fill=%27none%27/%3E%3Ctext%20x=%276%27%20y=%2714%27%20font-size=%2711%27%20font-family=%27sans-serif%27%20fill=%27%230c4a6e%27%3E%3C/text%3E%3C/svg%3E" end
    paragraph: content = "A picture that fails to load shows its description instead:" end
    image: content = "Photo of the garden gate" width = 200 height = 40 url = "missing/gate.jpg" end
end
```

Always set `width` and `height` to the real size of the file. The browser then reserves the space before the picture arrives, and the text below does not jump when it does. `loading = lazy` tells the browser to fetch the picture only when the reader scrolls near it, which saves data for pictures far down the page. Leave the first picture on the page at the default, `eager`. `decoding` chooses whether decoding may happen off to the side (`async`) and `fetch priority` lets you mark the most important picture as `high`.

The long text in `url` is a data address: the whole picture written as text, so the example needs no extra file. The compiler accepts data addresses for images, audio, video and fonts and refuses the rest. In your own pages you will usually write a file name or an address instead.

## One picture, many sizes

A phone and a large monitor do not need the same file. `srcset` lists several versions of the picture, and the browser picks one. There are two ways to describe them. With density descriptors, as in the example, each file is marked `1x`, `2x` and so on, and the browser chooses by the pixel density of the screen. With width descriptors, `photo-480.jpg 480w, photo-960.jpg 960w`, each file is marked with its real width, and `sizes` tells the browser how wide the picture will be drawn, for example `sizes = "(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px"`. The `url` stays as the fallback for browsers that do not know `srcset`.

web-media-srcset.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Image sets"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    image:
        id = "swatch"
        content = "A color swatch (the files do not exist here)"
        width = 160
        height = 100
        srcset = "swatch.png 1x, swatch-2x.png 2x"
        url = "swatch.png"
        error = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("chosen"), "The browser chose: " + dom.GetStr(dom.ById("swatch"), "currentSrc")) end
    end
    paragraph: id = "chosen" content = "Waiting for the browser." end
end
```

The files in this example do not exist, so the browser draws nothing. It still decides which one it would load, and the function named after `error =` runs when the image cannot be loaded and reads that choice from the `currentSrc` property of the image. On a screen with twice the pixels you would read the second name.

When the versions are not the same picture, for example a wide crop for a desktop and a tall one for a phone, use `picture`. Inside it, each `source` has a `media` condition and a `srcset`, and the browser takes the first source whose condition is true. The last child is always a normal `image`: it is the fallback and it carries the description. A `source` can also have a `type`, such as `image/webp`, so that browsers that do not know the format skip it.

web-media-picture.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Picture"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    picture:
        source: media = "(min-width: 500px)" srcset = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20viewBox=%270%200%20320%20120%27%20width=%27320%27%20height=%27120%27%3E%3Crect%20width=%27320%27%20height=%27120%27%20fill=%27%23bae6fd%27/%3E%3Ccircle%20cx=%27260%27%20cy=%2736%27%20r=%2720%27%20fill=%27%23facc15%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M0%20120%20Q90%2060%20170%20100%20T320%2085%20V120Z%27%20fill=%27%2316a34a%27/%3E%3Ctext%20x=%278%27%20y=%2716%27%20font-size=%2712%27%20font-family=%27sans-serif%27%20fill=%27%230c4a6e%27%3Ewide%3C/text%3E%3C/svg%3E" end
        image:
            content = "Green hills under a yellow sun"
            url = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20viewBox=%270%200%20120%20160%27%20width=%27120%27%20height=%27160%27%3E%3Crect%20width=%27120%27%20height=%27160%27%20fill=%27%23bae6fd%27/%3E%3Ccircle%20cx=%2790%27%20cy=%2730%27%20r=%2716%27%20fill=%27%23facc15%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M0%20160%20Q40%2090%2080%20140%20T120%20120%20V160Z%27%20fill=%27%2316a34a%27/%3E%3Ctext%20x=%278%27%20y=%2716%27%20font-size=%2712%27%20font-family=%27sans-serif%27%20fill=%27%230c4a6e%27%3Enarrow%3C/text%3E%3C/svg%3E"
        end
    end
    paragraph: content = "In a window narrower than 500 pixels you see the tall picture. In a wider window the browser swaps in the wide one." end
end
```

## Clickable image maps

An image map makes parts of one picture into separate links. The `image` names the map with `use map = "#shapes"`, and an `image map` with `name = "shapes"` holds one `area` per hotspot. An `area` has a `shape`: `rect` with the coordinates `left,top,right,bottom`, `circle` with `center-x,center-y,radius`, `poly` with the corners as `x1,y1,x2,y2` and so on, or `default` for everything not covered. The coordinates are in pixels of the picture as it is drawn. An `area` is a link, so it also takes `url`, `target`, `rel`, `download`, `ping` and `referrer policy`, and it needs `alt`, the text for people who cannot click the picture.

web-media-map.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Image map"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    image:
        content = "A red square next to a blue circle"
        use map = "#shapes"
        width = 200
        height = 100
        url = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20viewBox=%270%200%20200%20100%27%3E%3Crect%20x=%2710%27%20y=%2710%27%20width=%2780%27%20height=%2780%27%20fill=%27%23dc2626%27/%3E%3Ccircle%20cx=%27150%27%20cy=%2750%27%20r=%2740%27%20fill=%27%232563eb%27/%3E%3C/svg%3E"
    end
    image map: name = "shapes"
        area: shape = "rect" coords = "10,10,90,90" alt = "red square" url = "#" click = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("said"), "You chose the square.") end end
        area: shape = "circle" coords = "150,50,40" alt = "blue circle" url = "#" click = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("said"), "You chose the circle.") end end
    end
    paragraph: id = "said" content = "Click a shape." end
end
```

In the example each area also has a `click` handler that writes into the paragraph. The older `ismap` attribute is different: on an image inside a link it makes the browser send the clicked coordinates to the server, which then decides what to do.

## Audio and video

`audio` and `video` play sound and moving pictures without any plug-in. Add `controls` or the reader gets no way to start them. Give the file with `url` or, better, with one or more `source` children, each with its `type`. The browser takes the first one it can play, so list the best format first. The `content` text is shown only by a browser that cannot play the element at all.

web-media-audio.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Audio"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    paragraph: content = "A short beep. Press play:" end
    audio:
        controls = true
        preload = "auto"
        content = "Your browser cannot play audio."
        source: url = "data:audio/wav;base64," type = "audio/wav" end
        source: url = "beep.mp3" type = "audio/mpeg" end
    end
    paragraph: content = "The browser plays the first source it understands." end
end
```

`preload` says how much to fetch before the reader presses play: `none`, `metadata` (only the duration and size) or `auto`. `loop` starts again at the end, and `muted` starts silent. `autoplay` starts at once, but browsers usually refuse it for sound, so it works reliably only together with `muted`. A `video` also has `width` and `height`, a `poster` picture shown until it plays, and `plays inline`, which stops phones from forcing it to full screen.

web-media-video.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Video"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    video:
        width = 288
        controls = true
        autoplay = true
        muted = true
        loop = true
        plays inline = true
        preload = "auto"
        poster = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20viewBox=%270%200%2096%2054%27%3E%3Crect%20width=%2796%27%20height=%2754%27%20fill=%27%23134e4a%27/%3E%3Cpath%20d=%27M40%2018%20L40%2036%20L56%2027Z%27%20fill=%27%23ccfbf1%27/%3E%3C/svg%3E"
        content = "Your browser cannot play video."
        source: url = "data:video/webm;base64," type = "video/webm" end
        track: url = "captions/en.vtt" kind = "subtitles" srclang = "en" label = "English" default = true end
    end
end
```

The `track` element adds text to a video or an audio file from a WebVTT file. Its `kind` is `subtitles` (a translation), `captions` (speech and sounds, for the deaf), `descriptions`, `chapters` or `metadata`. `srclang` is the language of the text, `label` is the name in the menu, and `default` turns it on at the start. The file in the example does not exist. Real pages need captions for anything that is spoken.

## Frames and embedded objects

`iframe` shows another page inside yours. The page can be an address in `url` or a short document written in `srcdoc`. Give it a `title` so screen readers can announce it, and a `width` and `height`. Use `loading = lazy` for frames far down the page.

web-media-iframe.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Frames"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    paragraph: content = "A separate little page, locked in a sandbox with no scripts:" end
    iframe:
        title = "Greeting"
        width = 320
        height = 90
        sandbox = ""
        loading = lazy
        srcdoc = "<body style='font-family:sans-serif'><h3>Inside the frame</h3><p>This page cannot run scripts.</p></body>"
        border = "2px solid #0f766e"
    end
end
```

A frame can bring a stranger's code into your page, so lock it down with `sandbox`. An empty `sandbox = ""` removes every permission: no scripts, no forms, no popups. You then give back only what the frame needs, by listing words such as `allow-scripts` or `allow-forms`, separated by spaces. Never combine `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin` for a page you do not trust. `allow` is a separate list for browser features, such as `"fullscreen; camera"`, and `allow fullscreen` permits the full screen button. `name` gives the frame a name for scripts, and `referrer policy` works as for links.

`embed` and `object` place an external resource, such as a PDF, into the page. Both take a `url`, a `type` and a size. `embed` has no content. `object` shows its `content` when the browser cannot display the file, which is the place for a download link, and its `form` and `name` attributes connect it to a form. For a PDF, a plain `link` is often the better choice.

## Canvas, SVG and math

`canvas` is a blank rectangle you draw on with code. Set its size with the `width` and `height` attributes, which are the number of pixels of the drawing surface. A size set with CSS only stretches those pixels, and the drawing turns blurry. Drawing itself is done through the `dom` package. `dom.GetContext(canvas, "2d")` returns the drawing tool, `dom.SetStr` sets a property of it such as `fillStyle`, and `dom.Call4` calls one of its methods with four numbers. The example stamps a square where you click: `dom.GetNum(e, "offsetX")` reads the click position inside the canvas from the event. The two functions above the page, `stamp` and `wipe`, are connected to the canvas and the button with `click = stamp` and `click = wipe`.

web-media-canvas.salam

```salam
import dom

func stamp(e: i64):
    ctx := dom.GetContext(dom.ById("pad"), "2d")
    dom.SetStr(ctx, "fillStyle", "#0f766e")
    _ := dom.Call4(ctx, "fillRect", dom.GetNum(e, "offsetX") - 10, dom.GetNum(e, "offsetY") - 10, 20, 20)
end

func wipe():
    ctx := dom.GetContext(dom.ById("pad"), "2d")
    _ := dom.Call4(ctx, "clearRect", 0, 0, 320, 160)
end

page:
    title = "Canvas"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    paragraph: content = "Click the canvas to stamp a square." end
    canvas: id = "pad" width = 320 height = 160 background = "#f1f5f9" border = "1px solid #94a3b8" click = stamp end
    box: margin top = 8
        button: content = "Clear" click = wipe end
    end
end
```

Text inside the canvas element, if you add some, is shown only when the browser cannot draw, and screen readers cannot see into the drawing. Put any information the drawing carries into the page as text as well.

`svg` draws with shapes that stay sharp at every size. The `content` of an `svg` is the markup of its shapes, written as it is, and it is not escaped, so use it only for markup you wrote yourself. `view box` is the coordinate system inside, four numbers `min-x min-y width height`, and `width` and `height` are the size on the page. The drawing scales to fit. `xmlns` is only needed when the SVG is a file of its own. `math` works the same way for mathematics, with MathML in its `content`: `mi` for a name, `mo` for an operator, `mn` for a number, `mfrac` for a fraction and `msup` for a power.

web-media-svg.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "SVG and math"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    svg:
        view box = "0 0 120 60"
        width = 240
        height = 120
        content = "<rect width='120' height='60' rx='8' fill='#ccfbf1'/><circle cx='30' cy='30' r='18' fill='#0f766e'/><text x='58' y='36' font-size='16' fill='#134e4a'>Salam</text>"
    end
    paragraph:
        content = "The area of a circle is "
        math: content = "<mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>&#960;</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>" end
        span: content = "." end
    end
end
```

## Reference: links, images and media

Every element of this lesson is below, with its attributes and a short example. The examples are checked by the compiler, so you can paste any of them inside a `page:` block. Files such as `photo.jpg` in the examples are only names, you need your own files to see them. The attributes that every element has, such as `id` and `title`, are in the lesson on the head and global attributes.

### Links

### `link` (Persian: `پیوند`; HTML: `<a>`)

A link (HTML `a`). The required `url` is where it goes and the `content` is the text to click. It can hold text, an image or other inline content, but not another link or a button.

```salam
link: url = "/guide" content = "Read the guide" end
```

Required: `url`

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type`
نوع | A hint about the kind of file at the address, as a MIME type such as `application/pdf`. The browser may use it before it has fetched the file. It does not change what the file is. [mime] | `link: url = "notes.pdf" type = "application/pdf" content = "Notes (PDF)" end` |

| `download`
دانلود | Makes the browser save the target instead of opening it. The value is the file name to suggest; an empty value keeps the original name. It works for files from your own site. [string] | `link: url = "report.pdf" download = "report-2026.pdf" content = "Save the report" end` |

| `rel`
رابطه | A space separated list of words that describe how the target relates to this page, such as `noopener` (the new page cannot control this one), `noreferrer`, `nofollow` (search engines should not count the link) or `external`. [token (list)] | `link: url = "https://example.org" target = "new" rel = "noopener nofollow" content = "A site we do not vouch for" end` |

| `referrer policy`
سیاست ارجاع | How much of this page's address is sent to the target: `no-referrer` (nothing), `same-origin`, `origin` (only the site), `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and others. Use `no-referrer` when the address of your page is private. [enum: referrer_policy] | `link: url = "https://example.com" referrer policy = "no-referrer" content = "Leave quietly" end` |

| `ping`
پینگ | A space separated list of addresses that the browser notifies when the link is followed. It is used for click counting. Some browsers ignore it. [url (list)] | `link: url = "/offer" ping = "https://example.com/count" content = "See the offer" end` |

| `hreflang`
زبان مقصد | The language of the target page, as a language code such as `fa` or `en`. It is a hint for browsers and search engines. [lang] | `link: url = "/fa/" hreflang = "fa" content = "Persian version" end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address the link goes to, required. It can be a full address (`https://...`), a file name next to the page, a place on this page (`#id`), `mailto:` or `tel:`. Addresses that run code, such as `javascript:`, are refused. [url] | `link: url = "#prices" content = "Jump to the prices" end` |

| `target`
هدف | Where the page opens: `new` (or `_blank`) for a new tab, `same` (`_self`) for the current one, `parent` and `top` for the enclosing frame or the whole window. [enum: target] | `link: url = "https://example.com" target = "new" content = "Open in a new tab" end` |

### Images and maps

### `image` (Persian: `تصویر`; HTML: `<img>`)

A picture (HTML `img`). The `url` is required. It has no children. Give it a description in `alt` or `content`, and its `width` and `height`.

```salam
image: url = "photo.jpg" content = "The garden gate in spring" width = 320 height = 200 end
```

Required: `url` · Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the picture. A bare number means pixels. Set it, with `height`, to the real size of the file so the browser can reserve the space before the picture loads. [ulength] | `image: url = "photo.jpg" alt = "Gate" width = 240 height = 150 end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the picture, in pixels when it is a bare number. Together with `width` it lets the browser keep the picture's shape while it loads. [ulength] | `image: url = "photo.jpg" alt = "Gate" width = 240 height = 150 end` |

| `srcset`
مجموعه منبع | A list of picture files for the browser to choose from, separated by commas. Each item is an address followed by `1x`, `2x` (screen density) or `480w`, `960w` (file width in pixels). [srcset] | `image: url = "photo-480.jpg" alt = "Gate" srcset = "photo-480.jpg 480w, photo-960.jpg 960w" sizes = "480px" end` |

| `sizes`
اندازه‌ها | How wide the picture will be drawn, so the browser can pick from a `srcset` that uses `w` descriptors. A list of conditions with widths, ending with a default, for example `(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px`. [string] | `image: url = "photo-480.jpg" alt = "Gate" srcset = "photo-480.jpg 480w, photo-960.jpg 960w" sizes = "(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px" end` |

| `crossorigin`
میان‌مبدا | Whether the request for a picture from another site carries credentials: `anonymous` (none) or `use-credentials`. It is needed when a script reads the pixels of a picture from another site. [enum: crossorigin] | `image: url = "https://cdn.example.com/map.png" alt = "Map" crossorigin = "anonymous" end` |

| `referrer policy`
سیاست ارجاع | How much of this page's address is sent when the picture is requested. The words are the same as for a link: `no-referrer`, `origin`, `same-origin` and so on. [enum: referrer_policy] | `image: url = "https://img.example.com/a.png" alt = "Ad" referrer policy = "no-referrer" end` |

| `loading`
بارگذاری | When to fetch the picture: `eager` at once (the default) or `lazy` only when the reader scrolls close to it. Use `lazy` for pictures below the first screen. [enum: loading] | `image: url = "footer-photo.jpg" alt = "The team" width = 320 height = 180 loading = "lazy" end` |

| `decoding`
رمزگشایی | Whether the browser may decode the picture off to the side: `async` (yes, so the page is not held up), `sync` (decode together with the rest) or `auto` (the browser decides, the default). [enum: decoding] | `image: url = "big.jpg" alt = "A large panorama" width = 640 height = 200 decoding = "async" end` |

| `fetch priority`
اولویت دریافت | A hint about how urgent the picture is: `high`, `low` or `auto`. Mark the main picture of the page `high`. [enum: fetch_priority] | `image: url = "hero.jpg" alt = "The harbour at dawn" width = 640 height = 260 fetch priority = "high" end` |

| `use map`
نقشه | Connects the picture to an `image map`. The value is a `#` followed by the `name` of the map. [string] | `image: url = "plan.png" alt = "Floor plan" use map = "#rooms" end
image map: name = "rooms"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Kitchen" url = "#kitchen" end
end` |

| `ismap`
نقشه سمت سرور | A boolean. On an image inside a `link`, it makes the browser add the click position to the address, so a server can decide what the click meant. Rarely needed today. [bool] | `link: url = "/where"
image: url = "map.png" alt = "Map" ismap = true end
end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address of the picture file, required. It can be a file name, a full address or a data address for small pictures. [url] | `image: url = "images/kite.png" alt = "A red kite" end` |

| `alt`
جایگزین | The text description of the picture. Screen readers read it, and the browser shows it if the file cannot be loaded. Use an empty value (`alt = ""`) for a picture that is only decoration. [string] | `image: url = "chart.png" alt = "Rainfall by month, highest in March" end` |

| `content`
محتوا | Another way to write `alt`: the text you give as `content` becomes the description. Use whichever reads better; do not give both. [string] | `image: url = "logo.png" content = "Salam logo" end` |

### `picture` (Persian: `عکس`; HTML: `<picture>`)

A container that lets the browser choose between several versions of a picture. It holds `source` elements and ends with the normal `image`, which is the fallback and carries the description.

```salam
picture:
    source: media = "(min-width: 700px)" srcset = "wide.jpg" end
    image: url = "narrow.jpg" alt = "The harbour" end
end
```

### `source` (Persian: `منبع`; HTML: `<source>`)

One candidate file for a `picture`, an `audio` or a `video`. The browser uses the first one whose conditions it meets and whose `type` it understands. It has no content.

```salam
video: controls = true
    source: url = "intro.webm" type = "video/webm" end
    source: url = "intro.mp4" type = "video/mp4" end
end
```

Only inside: `picture`, `video`, `audio` · Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the picture file of this candidate, in pixels. It helps the browser keep the right shape before the file arrives. [ulength] | `picture:
source: srcset = "wide.jpg" media = "(min-width: 700px)" width = 1200 height = 600 end
image: url = "narrow.jpg" alt = "The harbour" end
end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the picture file of this candidate, in pixels. Give it together with `width`. [ulength] | `picture:
source: srcset = "square.jpg" media = "(max-width: 400px)" width = 400 height = 400 end
image: url = "wide.jpg" alt = "The harbour" end
end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address of the audio or video file. Inside a `picture` use `srcset` instead. [url] | `audio: controls = true
source: url = "song.mp3" type = "audio/mpeg" end
end` |

| `srcset`
مجموعه منبع | The picture files of this candidate inside a `picture`, written like the `srcset` of an image. [srcset] | `picture:
source: srcset = "photo.avif 1x, photo-2x.avif 2x" type = "image/avif" end
image: url = "photo.jpg" alt = "Gate" end
end` |

| `sizes`
اندازه‌ها | How wide the picture will be drawn, as for an image, used with `w` descriptors in `srcset`. [string] | `picture:
source: srcset = "s-480.jpg 480w, s-960.jpg 960w" sizes = "(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px" end
image: url = "s-480.jpg" alt = "Gate" end
end` |

| `type`
نوع | The file type of this candidate, as a MIME type such as `image/webp` or `video/mp4`. A browser that does not know it skips the candidate without fetching. [mime] | `picture:
source: srcset = "photo.webp" type = "image/webp" end
image: url = "photo.jpg" alt = "Gate" end
end` |

| `media`
رسانه | A media condition, written as in CSS. The candidate is used only while the condition is true, such as `(min-width: 700px)` or `(orientation: portrait)`. [media_query] | `picture:
source: media = "(orientation: portrait)" srcset = "tall.jpg" end
image: url = "wide.jpg" alt = "The harbour" end
end` |

### `image map` (Persian: `نقشه تصویر`; HTML: `<map>`)

A set of clickable regions for an image (HTML `map`). The `name` is required and an `image` points at it with `use map`. Its children are `area` elements.

```salam
image map: name = "rooms"
    area: shape = "circle" coords = "40,40,30" alt = "Kitchen" url = "#kitchen" end
end
```

Required: `name`

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name`
نام | The name of the map, required. An `image` refers to it as `use map = "#name"`. [string] | `image map: name = "shapes"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,40,40" alt = "Box" url = "#box" end
end` |

### `area` (Persian: `ناحیه`; HTML: `<area>`)

One clickable region of an `image map`. It is a link: it takes `url`, `target` and the other link attributes, and its `shape` and `coords` say where it is. It has no content.

```salam
image map: name = "m"
    area: shape = "rect" coords = "10,10,90,60" alt = "Home" url = "/" end
end
```

Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url`
نشانی | Where a click on the region goes. Same kinds of address as for a link. [url] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Contact" url = "mailto:hi@example.com" end
end` |

| `coords`
مختصات | The points of the region as numbers separated by commas, in pixels of the picture. For `rect`: `left,top,right,bottom`. For `circle`: `x,y,radius`. For `poly`: `x1,y1,x2,y2,...`. [string] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "poly" coords = "10,60,50,10,90,60" alt = "Roof" url = "#roof" end
end` |

| `shape`
قالب ناحیه | The shape of the region: `rect`, `circle`, `poly`, or `default` for everything not covered by another area. [enum: area_shape] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "circle" coords = "50,50,30" alt = "Sun" url = "#sun" end
end` |

| `target`
هدف | Where the page opens, with the same words as for a link: `new`, `same`, `parent`, `top`. [enum: target] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Docs" url = "https://example.com" target = "new" end
end` |

| `download`
دانلود | Saves the target as a file instead of opening it, as for a link. The value is the suggested file name. [string] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Menu" url = "menu.pdf" download = "menu.pdf" end
end` |

| `rel`
رابطه | How the target relates to the page, with the same words as for a link, such as `noopener` or `nofollow`. [token (list)] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Partner" url = "https://example.org" target = "new" rel = "noopener" end
end` |

| `referrer policy`
سیاست ارجاع | How much of this page's address is sent to the target, as for a link. [enum: referrer_policy] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Away" url = "https://example.com" referrer policy = "no-referrer" end
end` |

| `ping`
پینگ | Addresses that are notified when the region is followed, as for a link. [url (list)] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Offer" url = "/offer" ping = "https://example.com/count" end
end` |

| `alt`
جایگزین | The text for the region, for people who cannot click on the picture. Screen readers read it as the name of the link. Always give it. [string] | `image map: name = "m"
area: shape = "rect" coords = "0,0,50,50" alt = "Open the kitchen page" url = "/kitchen" end
end` |

### Audio and video

### `audio` (Persian: `صدا`; HTML: `<audio>`)

A sound player. Add `controls` so the reader can start it. Give the file with `url` or with `source` children. The `content` is shown only by a browser that cannot play audio.

```salam
audio: controls = true url = "song.mp3" content = "Your browser cannot play audio." end
```

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url`
نشانی | The address of the sound file. Use `source` children instead when you offer several formats. [url] | `audio: url = "rain.ogg" controls = true end` |

| `crossorigin`
میان‌مبدا | Whether the request for a file from another site carries credentials: `anonymous` or `use-credentials`. Needed when a script analyses the sound. [enum: crossorigin] | `audio: url = "https://cdn.example.com/a.mp3" controls = true crossorigin = "anonymous" end` |

| `preload`
پیش‌بارگذاری | How much to fetch before the reader presses play: `none` (nothing), `metadata` (only the length) or `auto` (as much as the browser likes). [enum: preload] | `audio: url = "long-talk.mp3" controls = true preload = "metadata" end` |

| `autoplay`
پخش خودکار | A boolean. Start playing as soon as possible. Browsers ignore it for sound unless the element is also `muted` or the reader has already interacted with the page. [bool] | `audio: url = "ambient.mp3" autoplay = true muted = true loop = true end` |

| `loop`
حلقه | A boolean. When the sound ends, start again from the beginning. [bool] | `audio: url = "rain.ogg" controls = true loop = true end` |

| `muted`
بی‌صدا | A boolean. Start with the sound off. The reader can turn it on in the controls. [bool] | `audio: url = "rain.ogg" controls = true muted = true end` |

| `controls`
کنترل‌ها | A boolean. With `true` the browser shows its own play, pause, volume and position controls. Without them the player is invisible. [bool] | `audio: url = "song.mp3" controls = true end` |

### `video` (Persian: `ویدیو`; HTML: `<video>`)

A video player. Add `controls` so the reader can start it, and give `width` and `height`. The file comes from `url` or from `source` children, and subtitles from `track` children.

```salam
video: width = 320 controls = true poster = "cover.jpg"
    source: url = "clip.mp4" type = "video/mp4" end
end
```

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the player in pixels. Set it, with `height`, to keep the page from jumping when the video loads. [ulength] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true width = 480 height = 270 end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the player in pixels. [ulength] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true width = 480 height = 270 end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address of the video file. Use `source` children instead when you offer several formats. [url] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true width = 320 end` |

| `crossorigin`
میان‌مبدا | Whether the request for a file from another site carries credentials: `anonymous` or `use-credentials`. Needed when a script reads the frames, or when subtitles come from another site. [enum: crossorigin] | `video: url = "https://cdn.example.com/v.mp4" controls = true crossorigin = "anonymous" width = 320 end` |

| `preload`
پیش‌بارگذاری | How much to fetch before the reader presses play: `none`, `metadata` or `auto`. `metadata` is a good choice for a page with many videos. [enum: preload] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true preload = "metadata" width = 320 end` |

| `autoplay`
پخش خودکار | A boolean. Start at once. Browsers allow it only for a video that is also `muted`. [bool] | `video: url = "loop.mp4" autoplay = true muted = true loop = true plays inline = true width = 320 end` |

| `loop`
حلقه | A boolean. When the video ends, start again from the beginning. [bool] | `video: url = "loop.mp4" controls = true loop = true width = 320 end` |

| `muted`
بی‌صدا | A boolean. Start with the sound off. [bool] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true muted = true width = 320 end` |

| `controls`
کنترل‌ها | A boolean. With `true` the browser shows its play, pause, volume, position and full screen controls. [bool] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true width = 320 end` |

| `poster`
پوستر | A picture shown in place of the video until it plays. Give it a file name or address. [url] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true poster = "cover.jpg" width = 320 end` |

| `plays inline`
پخش درجا | A boolean. On phones that would otherwise open every video in full screen, keep it playing inside the page. [bool] | `video: url = "clip.mp4" controls = true plays inline = true width = 320 end` |

### `track` (Persian: `شیار`; HTML: `<track>`)

A text track for a `video` or `audio`: subtitles, captions, descriptions or chapters, from a WebVTT file. The `url` is required. It has no content.

```salam
video: url = "talk.mp4" controls = true width = 320
    track: url = "talk.en.vtt" kind = "subtitles" srclang = "en" label = "English" end
end
```

Required: `url` · Only inside: `video`, `audio` · Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url`
نشانی | The address of the WebVTT file, required. [url] | `video: url = "talk.mp4" controls = true width = 320
track: url = "captions/talk.vtt" kind = "captions" srclang = "en" label = "Captions" end
end` |

| `kind`
نوع شیار | What the text is: `subtitles` (a translation of the speech), `captions` (speech and sounds, for deaf readers), `descriptions` (what is seen, for blind readers), `chapters` (titles for navigation) or `metadata` (for scripts, not shown). [enum: track_kind] | `video: url = "talk.mp4" controls = true width = 320
track: url = "talk.vtt" kind = "chapters" srclang = "en" label = "Chapters" end
end` |

| `srclang`
زبان شیار | The language of the text, as a language code such as `en` or `fa`. Required for `subtitles`. [lang] | `video: url = "talk.mp4" controls = true width = 320
track: url = "talk.fa.vtt" kind = "subtitles" srclang = "fa" label = "Persian" end
end` |

| `label`
برچسب | The name of the track in the player's menu, for example `English`. [string] | `video: url = "talk.mp4" controls = true width = 320
track: url = "talk.vtt" kind = "subtitles" srclang = "en" label = "English (UK)" end
end` |

| `default`
پیش‌فرض | A boolean. Turn this track on when the video starts, unless the reader has chosen another. Use it on one track only. [bool] | `video: url = "talk.mp4" controls = true width = 320
track: url = "talk.vtt" kind = "subtitles" srclang = "en" label = "English" default = true end
end` |

### Frames and embedded objects

### `iframe` (Persian: `قاب درونی`; HTML: `<iframe>`)

A frame that shows another page inside this one. The page is an address in `url` or a short document in `srcdoc`. Give it a `title` and a size, and lock it down with `sandbox`.

```salam
iframe: url = "https://example.com/widget" title = "Widget" width = 400 height = 240 sandbox = "allow-scripts" end
```

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the frame. A bare number means pixels. Browsers give a frame 300 pixels by default. [ulength] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/embed" title = "Embedded" width = 480 height = 270 end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the frame. A bare number means pixels. The default is 150 pixels. [ulength] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/embed" title = "Embedded" width = 480 height = 270 end` |

| `name`
نام | A name for the frame, so that scripts can find it as a named window. The page language accepts only the four words (`new`, `same`, `parent`, `top`) as the `target` of a link. [string] | `iframe: name = "preview" title = "Preview" width = 300 height = 160 srcdoc = "<p>Empty</p>" end` |

| `referrer policy`
سیاست ارجاع | How much of this page's address is sent when the frame's page is requested, with the same words as for a link. [enum: referrer_policy] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/embed" title = "Embedded" width = 300 height = 160 referrer policy = "no-referrer" end` |

| `loading`
بارگذاری | When to load the frame: `eager` at once or `lazy` when the reader scrolls close to it. Use `lazy` for a frame far down the page. [enum: loading] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/map" title = "Map" width = 400 height = 240 loading = "lazy" end` |

| `srcdoc`
محتوای سند | A complete small document, written as HTML text, to show in the frame instead of loading an address. It is escaped for you. [string] | `iframe: title = "Note" width = 300 height = 80 srcdoc = "<p style=&#x27;font-family:sans-serif&#x27;>Hello from the frame</p>" end` |

| `allow fullscreen`
اجازه تمام‌صفحه | A boolean. With `true` the page in the frame may go full screen. [bool] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/player" title = "Player" width = 400 height = 240 allow fullscreen = true end` |

| `sandbox`
قرنطینه | Restrictions for the frame. An empty value removes every permission. Words separated by spaces give some back: `allow-scripts`, `allow-forms`, `allow-popups`, `allow-same-origin` and others. Do not give `allow-scripts` and `allow-same-origin` together to a page you do not trust. [string] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/form" title = "Form" width = 400 height = 240 sandbox = "allow-forms allow-scripts" end` |

| `allow`
اجازه | A list of browser features the frame may use, separated by semicolons, such as `fullscreen`, `camera`, `microphone` or `geolocation`. The default is to allow none for pages from another site. [string] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/call" title = "Video call" width = 400 height = 300 allow = "camera; microphone" end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address of the page to show in the frame. Use `srcdoc` instead for a short document written right here. [url] | `iframe: url = "https://example.com/embed" title = "Embedded page" width = 400 height = 200 end` |

### `embed` (Persian: `جاسازی`; HTML: `<embed>`)

Places an external resource, such as a PDF, into the page (HTML `embed`). The `url` is required. It has no content, so there is no fallback text.

```salam
embed: url = "report.pdf" type = "application/pdf" width = 400 height = 300 end
```

Required: `url` · Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the embedded area, in pixels when it is a bare number. [ulength] | `embed: url = "report.pdf" type = "application/pdf" width = 500 height = 300 end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the embedded area, in pixels when it is a bare number. [ulength] | `embed: url = "report.pdf" type = "application/pdf" width = 500 height = 300 end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address of the resource, required. [url] | `embed: url = "slides.pdf" type = "application/pdf" width = 400 height = 300 end` |

| `type`
نوع | The MIME type of the resource, such as `application/pdf`. It helps the browser choose how to show it. [mime] | `embed: url = "report.pdf" type = "application/pdf" width = 400 height = 300 end` |

### `object` (Persian: `شیء`; HTML: `<object>`)

An external resource shown in the page, with fallback content (HTML `object`). The `url` is required. If the browser cannot show the file, it shows the children instead, which is the place for a link to download it.

```salam
object: url = "report.pdf" type = "application/pdf" width = 400 height = 300
    link: url = "report.pdf" content = "Download the report" end
end
```

Required: `url`

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the object, in pixels when it is a bare number. [ulength] | `object: url = "chart.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = 320 height = 200 content = "A chart" end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the object, in pixels when it is a bare number. [ulength] | `object: url = "chart.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = 320 height = 200 content = "A chart" end` |

| `type`
نوع | The MIME type of the resource, such as `application/pdf` or `image/svg+xml`. [mime] | `object: url = "chart.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = 300 height = 200 content = "A chart" end` |

| `name`
نام | A name for the object, for scripts and forms. [string] | `object: url = "chart.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" name = "chart" width = 300 height = 200 content = "A chart" end` |

| `url`
نشانی | The address of the resource, required. It becomes the `data` attribute in HTML. [url] | `object: url = "chart.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = 300 height = 200 content = "A chart" end` |

| `form`
فرم | The `id` of a form this object belongs to. The compiler checks that an element with that id exists on the page. [idref] | `box: id = "order" end
object: form = "order" url = "widget.svg" type = "image/svg+xml" width = 200 height = 100 content = "Widget" end` |

### Drawing

### `canvas` (Persian: `بوم`; HTML: `<canvas>`)

A blank drawing surface (HTML `canvas`). You draw on it with code, through `dom.GetContext`. Give it an `id` so the code can find it, and set its size with the attributes, not with CSS.

```salam
canvas: id = "pad" width = 300 height = 150 background = "#f1f5f9" end
```

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض | The width of the drawing surface in pixels. This is the number of pixels you draw on. A width set with CSS only stretches them. [ulength] | `canvas: width = 400 height = 200 border = "1px solid #94a3b8" end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the drawing surface in pixels. The default is 150. [ulength] | `canvas: width = 400 height = 200 border = "1px solid #94a3b8" end` |

### `svg` (Persian: `اس‌وی‌جی`; HTML: `<svg>`)

A vector picture written in place (HTML `svg`). Its `content` is the markup of the shapes, inserted as written and not escaped, so use only markup you wrote yourself. The picture stays sharp at every size.

```salam
svg: view box = "0 0 100 100" width = 120 height = 120 content = "<circle cx=&#x27;50&#x27; cy=&#x27;50&#x27; r=&#x27;40&#x27; fill=&#x27;tomato&#x27;/>" end
```

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `view box`
جعبه دید | The coordinate system inside the picture: four numbers, `min-x min-y width height`. The shapes are drawn in these units and scaled to the `width` and `height` on the page. [string] | `svg: view box = "0 0 200 100" width = 200 height = 100 content = "<rect width=&#x27;200&#x27; height=&#x27;100&#x27; fill=&#x27;#ccfbf1&#x27;/>" end` |

| `width`
عرض | The width of the picture on the page, such as `120` or `50%`. [string] | `svg: view box = "0 0 100 100" width = "50%" height = 100 content = "<circle cx=&#x27;50&#x27; cy=&#x27;50&#x27; r=&#x27;40&#x27; fill=&#x27;gold&#x27;/>" end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع | The height of the picture on the page, such as `120`. [string] | `svg: view box = "0 0 100 100" width = 100 height = 100 content = "<circle cx=&#x27;50&#x27; cy=&#x27;50&#x27; r=&#x27;40&#x27; fill=&#x27;gold&#x27;/>" end` |

| `xmlns`
فضای نام | The XML namespace address, `http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`. It is only needed when the SVG is saved as a file of its own. Inside a page you can leave it out. [absolute_url] | `svg: xmlns = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" view box = "0 0 100 100" width = 100 height = 100 content = "<circle cx=&#x27;50&#x27; cy=&#x27;50&#x27; r=&#x27;40&#x27; fill=&#x27;teal&#x27;/>" end` |

### `math` (Persian: `ریاضی`; HTML: `<math>`)

A mathematical formula written in MathML (HTML `math`). Its `content` is the markup, inserted as written: `mi` for a name, `mn` for a number, `mo` for an operator, `mfrac` for a fraction, `msup` for a power, `msqrt` for a square root.

```salam
math: content = "<msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac>" end
```

## Try it yourself

- Write a page with a table of contents: a list of links that point with `#` to three headings further down. Add a link at the bottom that goes back to the top.

- Draw your own picture in an `svg`: a house from a `rect`, a `polygon` for the roof and a `circle` for the sun. Then change the `width` and `height` but keep the `view box`, and watch it scale.

- Change the image map so that the red square is a `link` to a heading on the same page, and add a third hotspot with `poly`.

- Open the canvas example, make the stamp a different color on every click by using `dom.Random()`, and add a second button that fills the whole canvas.

# Tables

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/page-tables/

A table is the right element when your data has rows and columns: prices, timetables, scores. This lesson shows how to build one that screen readers can follow, how to join cells, how to style whole columns, and how to keep a wide table usable on a small screen.

## When to use a table

Use a table for data that you would also put in a spreadsheet: every cell means something because of its row and its column. A list of prices, a school timetable and a table of results are all tables. A page that has a menu on the left and text on the right is not: that is a job for layout with CSS, which the layout lesson teaches. Screen readers announce a table as a table and read each cell together with its headings, so a table used for layout makes the page harder to understand for the people who depend on them.

## The parts of a table

A `table` holds rows, and a `row` holds cells. A cell is written `column` in Salam. The name can mislead you: `column` is one cell (HTML `td`), and the rows are what make up the columns. Rows can go straight into the table, but real tables are split into three sections: `header` for the headings, `main` for the data and `footer` for totals. Inside a table these three words mean the HTML `thead`, `tbody` and `tfoot`. Outside a table the same words are the page header, the main part and the page footer, and the compiler picks the right one from where you wrote it.

The `caption` is the title of the table. It must be the first thing inside the table: the compiler stops with an error if it is not. A table can have only one `header` and one `footer`, but as many `main` sections as you need to group rows.

web-tables-basic.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Price list"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = "8px 14px" border bottom = "1px solid #cbd5e1" text align = left end
    global: selector = "table" border collapse = collapse end
    table:
        caption: content = "Fruit prices this week" end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "Fruit" end
                column: content = "Kilos" end
                column: content = "Price" end
            end
        end
        main:
            row:
                column: content = "Apples" end
                column: content = "3" end
                column: content = "4.50" end
            end
            row:
                column: content = "Pears" end
                column: content = "2" end
                column: content = "3.20" end
            end
        end
        footer:
            row:
                column: content = "Total" end
                column: content = "5" end
                column: content = "7.70" end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

Two global rules do the styling here. `th, td` selects every cell, and the rule gives them padding and a line under them. `table` with `border collapse = collapse` joins the lines of neighbouring cells into one. Without CSS a table has no borders at all, so every table you want to look like a table needs some.

The cells of the header row became `th` without you asking. That is the context rule: a `column` inside `header` is a heading cell. Browsers draw heading cells in bold and centred, and, more important, they tell assistive technology that these cells are headings. The footer is different. It only holds data cells unless you say otherwise, so the word Total in the last row is plain here. The next section fixes that.

## Heading cells and scope

Headings are not only in the top row. When the first cell of every row names that row, it is a heading too. Write `heading = true` on a `column` and it becomes a `th`. The word `heading` here is an attribute of the cell, not the heading element of the text lesson.

Then tell the browser which way the heading points with `scope`: `col` for a heading that describes the cells below it and `row` for one that describes the cells to its right. There are two more values for headings that cover a whole group of rows or columns: `rowgroup` and `colgroup`. For a simple table browsers guess the scope correctly, but writing it costs nothing and removes the guess.

If a heading is long, give it a short form in `abbr`. A screen reader may read the short form when it repeats the heading for every cell, which saves the listener time.

web-tables-scope.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Row and column headers"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = "8px 16px" border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" end
    global: selector = "table" border collapse = collapse end
    table:
        caption: content = "Quiz scores" end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "Student" scope = col end
                column: content = "Quiz 1" scope = col abbr = "Q1" end
                column: content = "Quiz 2" scope = col abbr = "Q2" end
            end
        end
        main:
            row:
                column: heading = true scope = row content = "Sara" end
                column: content = "17" end
                column: content = "19" end
            end
            row:
                column: heading = true scope = row content = "Omid" end
                column: content = "14" end
                column: content = "18" end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

`header column` and `heading column` are the two names the reference below gives to the heading cell: the first is a cell that stands in a header row, the second a cell that you marked with `heading = true`. Both are written `column` in your code and both produce `th`.

## Cells that span

A cell can cover more than one place. `colspan` stretches it over several columns and `rowspan` over several rows. When you stretch a cell, the cells it covers must not be written: a row with a `colspan = 2` cell has one cell less, and the row below a `rowspan = 2` cell has one cell less on that side. If you write too many, the table looks broken and no error appears, so count the cells of every row as you write it.

web-tables-span.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Timetable"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = "10px 18px" border = "1px solid #94a3b8" text align = center end
    global: selector = "table" border collapse = collapse end
    table:
        caption: content = "Tuesday" end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "Time" end
                column: content = "Room A" end
                column: content = "Room B" end
            end
        end
        main:
            row:
                column: heading = true content = "09:00" end
                column: content = "Maths" rowspan = 2 background = "#dbeafe" end
                column: content = "Art" end
            end
            row:
                column: heading = true content = "10:00" end
                column: content = "Music" end
            end
            row:
                column: heading = true content = "12:00" end
                column: content = "Lunch for everyone" colspan = 2 background = "#fef3c7" end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

In the timetable the Maths cell has `rowspan = 2`, so the second row lists only Music, which fills Room B. The lunch row has `colspan = 2` and fills both rooms.

## Complex tables and headers

Sometimes one heading is not enough to explain a cell. In a table with two levels of headings, or with spanning cells, a data cell may belong to several headings. Give each heading cell an `id` and list those ids in the `headers` attribute of the data cell, separated by spaces. Salam checks that every id exists. The example below gives every data cell both of its headings, the row heading and the column heading, so you can see the shape. Do not write `headers` on a simple table: `scope` is enough there and is much less work.

web-tables-headers.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Opening hours"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = "8px 16px" border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" end
    global: selector = "table" border collapse = collapse end
    table:
        caption: content = "Opening hours of two shops" end
        row:
            column: heading = true id = "shop" content = "Shop" end
            column: heading = true id = "wk" content = "Weekdays" end
            column: heading = true id = "we" content = "Weekend" end
        end
        row:
            column: heading = true id = "bk" content = "Books" end
            column: content = "9-18" headers = "bk wk" end
            column: content = "10-14" headers = "bk we" end
        end
        row:
            column: heading = true id = "cf" content = "Coffee" end
            column: content = "7-20" headers = "cf wk" end
            column: content = "8-22" headers = "cf we" end
        end
    end
end
```

## Styling whole columns

You often want a colour or a width for a whole column. Writing it on every cell is long and easy to get wrong. A `column group` before the sections of the table lets you describe the columns once. Each `column definition` inside stands for one column from the left (from the right in a Persian page). Give it `span` to cover several columns with one line. Only a few properties work on these elements: `background`, `width`, `visibility` and, when borders are collapsed, `border`. They have no text and no children.

web-tables-columns.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Styling columns"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = "8px 16px" end
    global: selector = "table" border collapse = collapse end
    table:
        column group:
            column definition: background = "#e2e8f0" end
            column definition: span = 2 background = "#ecfccb" end
            column definition: background = "#fee2e2" end
        end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "City" end
                column: content = "Mon" end
                column: content = "Tue" end
                column: content = "Wed" end
            end
        end
        main:
            row:
                column: heading = true content = "Oslo" end
                column: content = "4" end
                column: content = "6" end
                column: content = "3" end
            end
            row:
                column: heading = true content = "Rome" end
                column: content = "18" end
                column: content = "21" end
                column: content = "19" end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

The first definition colours the first column grey, the second one has `span = 2` and colours the next two green, and the last one colours the final column red.

## Making a table look good

Four properties do most of the work. `border collapse = collapse` merges the borders of neighbouring cells into one line, where the default `separate` draws a double line. `border spacing` sets the gap between cells when they are separate. `padding` on the cells makes the text breathe, and `text align` lines the numbers up, usually to the right. `vertical align` chooses where a short cell's text sits in a tall row.

Stripes make long rows easier to follow. You can colour every other row yourself, but it is simpler to write one CSS rule. The page-wide `style` element takes raw CSS, and `tbody tr:nth-child(even)` selects every second row of the body. The hover colour uses the `hover` prefix in front of a style property, written on the row; the CSS lessons cover such states in detail. The table itself gets `width = "100%"` so that it fills the space, and `max width` stops it from growing past 28rem. `color = white` on the heading cells keeps the text readable on the dark green. The caption sits above the table by default, and `caption side = bottom` moves it under.

web-tables-style.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "A styled table"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = 10 text align = left end
    global: selector = "th" background = "#0f766e" color = white end
    style: content = "tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f1f5f9 }" end
    table:
        border collapse = collapse
        width = "100%"
        max width = "28rem"
        caption: content = "Team members" caption side = bottom color = "#64748b" padding = 8 end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "Name" end
                column: content = "Role" end
                column: content = "Age" end
            end
        end
        main:
            row: hover background = "#ccfbf1"
                column: content = "Sara" end
                column: content = "Designer" end
                column: content = "31" end
            end
            row: hover background = "#ccfbf1"
                column: content = "Omid" end
                column: content = "Engineer" end
                column: content = "28" end
            end
            row: hover background = "#ccfbf1"
                column: content = "Lina" end
                column: content = "Writer" end
                column: content = "35" end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

Do not make a table narrower with `width` on every cell. Put `width` or `max width` on the table, and use `table layout = fixed` if you want the columns to take the widths of the first row, which also makes large tables draw faster.

## Wide tables on small screens

A table is as wide as its content needs, and a phone is narrow. If the table cannot shrink, it pushes the whole page sideways. The fix is a box around the table with `overflow = auto`: the page keeps its width and the table scrolls inside the box. Give the box a `max height` as well and it scrolls up and down too, and then a heading row with `position = sticky` and `top = 0` stays visible while the data moves under it. Put the sticky rule on the `th` cells, not on the row: that is the form that works in every browser.

web-tables-scroll.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Scrolling table"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1rem" end
    global: selector = "th, td" padding = 8 text align = left end
    global: selector = "th" position = sticky top = 0 background = "#1e293b" color = white end
    box:
        max width = "26rem"
        max height = "11rem"
        overflow = auto
        border = "1px solid #cbd5e1"
        table:
            border collapse = collapse
            width = "40rem"
            header:
                row:
                    column: content = "Day" end
                    column: content = "Steps" end
                    column: content = "Distance" end
                    column: content = "Sleep" end
                end
            end
            main:
                row: column: content = "Monday" end column: content = "8200" end column: content = "6.1 km" end column: content = "7 h" end end
                row: column: content = "Tuesday" end column: content = "10400" end column: content = "7.8 km" end column: content = "6 h" end end
                row: column: content = "Wednesday" end column: content = "5900" end column: content = "4.4 km" end column: content = "8 h" end end
                row: column: content = "Thursday" end column: content = "9100" end column: content = "6.8 km" end column: content = "7 h" end end
                row: column: content = "Friday" end column: content = "12000" end column: content = "9.0 km" end column: content = "6 h" end end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

Scroll the preview above to see the heading stay in place. The box has a `max width` and a `max height` that are smaller than the table, `overflow = auto` adds the scroll bars only when they are needed, and the table is given a fixed `width` of 40rem so that it is wider than the box. Put a background on sticky cells, or the text that scrolls under them shows through.

## Accessible tables, in short

- Give every table a `caption`. It says what the table is before anyone reads a cell.

- Make every heading a heading cell, in a `header` row or with `heading = true`, and write `scope`.

- Do not leave a cell empty to make space: use padding for space. A cell that really has no data can say "none" or "n/a", so that a screen reader has something to read.

- Keep the table simple. Two tables are better than one with spans in every row.

## Reference: every table element

Each element is shown with an example, and the attributes that belong only to that element are listed under it. The attributes that every element has are in the lesson on the head and global attributes. The examples are checked by the compiler, so you can paste any of them into a `page:` block. Persian names work in any file, and the Persian lessons use them.

### `table` (Persian: `جدول`; HTML: `<table>`)

A table of data in rows and columns. Use it for information that has a natural grid, such as prices, schedules or results, and never to lay out a page. Browsers draw no borders by default, so style it with CSS. Its children are, in this order: an optional `caption`, optional `column group`s, the sections `header`, `main` and `footer` (or plain `row`s), and cells go inside rows.

```salam
table:
    caption: content = "Pets" end
    row:
        column: content = "Cat" end
        column: content = "4 legs" end
    end
end
```

### `caption` (Persian: `عنوان جدول`; HTML: `<caption>`)

The title of the table. It must be the first child of the table, and the compiler reports an error when it is not. Screen readers announce it before the cells, so it is better than a heading placed above the table. `caption side` moves it below.

```salam
table:
    caption: content = "Pets" end
    row: column: content = "Cat" end end
end
```

Only inside: `table`

### `column group` (Persian: `گروه ستون`; HTML: `<colgroup>`)

A group of column definitions that describe whole columns, so that you can style a column without touching every cell. It goes before the sections of the table. Without children it covers as many columns as its `span` says.

```salam
table:
    column group:
        column definition: background = "#fee2e2" end
        column definition: end
    end
    row:
        column: content = "Red column" end
        column: content = "Plain column" end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `table`

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `span`
پوشش | A whole number, the count of columns this group covers when it has no `column definition` children. Without it the group covers one column. [uint] | `table:
column group: span = 2 background = "#e0f2fe" end
row:
column: content = "A" end
column: content = "B" end
end
end` |

### `column definition` (Persian: `تعریف ستون`; HTML: `<col>`)

Describes one column, or several with `span`, inside a `column group`. It has no content and no children. Only a few properties work on it: `background`, `border`, `width` and `visibility`. Text properties on it do nothing.

```salam
table:
    column group:
        column definition: width = 160 background = "#fef9c3" end
    end
    row: column: content = "Wide yellow cell" end end
end
```

Only inside: `column group` · Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `span`
پوشش | A whole number, how many neighbouring columns this one definition covers. Use it to style three columns the same way with one line. [uint] | `table:
column group:
column definition: span = 3 background = "#dcfce7" end
end
row:
column: content = "A" end
column: content = "B" end
column: content = "C" end
end
end` |

### `table header` (Persian: `سرصفحه`; HTML: `<thead>`)

Written as `header` inside a table. It becomes the `thead` section, which holds the heading rows and repeats on every page when the table is printed. A table has at most one. The same word outside a table is the page `header` element, the compiler decides by where it stands. Cells in its rows turn into heading cells.

```salam
table:
    header:
        row:
            column: content = "Name" end
            column: content = "Age" end
        end
    end
    main:
        row:
            column: content = "Sara" end
            column: content = "31" end
        end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `table`

### `table body` (Persian: `اصلی`; HTML: `<tbody>`)

Written as `main` inside a table. It becomes `tbody`, the section with the data rows. You may have several of them to group rows. Rows written directly inside the table, with no section, work too, and then the browser adds an implicit body.

```salam
table:
    main:
        row:
            column: content = "Sara" end
            column: content = "31" end
        end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `table`

### `table footer` (Persian: `پاورقی`; HTML: `<tfoot>`)

Written as `footer` inside a table. It becomes `tfoot`, the place for a totals row. A table has at most one. Browsers draw it at the bottom even though it can be written before the body.

```salam
table:
    main:
        row:
            column: content = "Tea" end
            column: content = "3" end
        end
    end
    footer:
        row:
            column: heading = true content = "Total" end
            column: content = "3" end
        end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `table`

### `row` (Persian: `ردیف`; HTML: `<tr>`)

One row of cells. It goes inside the table or inside `header`, `main` or `footer`, and its children are cells.

```salam
table:
    row:
        column: content = "Left" end
        column: content = "Right" end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `table`, `table header`, `table body`, `table footer`

### `column` (Persian: `ستون`; HTML: `<td>`)

A data cell, the `td` element. Despite its name it is one cell, not a whole column. Inside a `header` row it becomes a heading cell automatically, and anywhere else you ask for a heading cell with `heading = true`.

```salam
table:
    row:
        column: content = "Plain data" end
        column: content = "More data" background = "#f1f5f9" end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `row`

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `colspan`
پوشش ستون | A whole number, how many columns this cell stretches over to the right (or to the left in a right to left page). The next cells of the row are pushed along, so write fewer of them. [uint] | `table:
row:
column: content = "Wide cell" colspan = 2 background = "#fef3c7" end
end
row:
column: content = "One" end
column: content = "Two" end
end
end` |

| `rowspan`
پوشش ردیف | A whole number, how many rows this cell stretches down. The rows below must leave out the cells that it covers. [uint] | `table:
row:
column: content = "Tall" rowspan = 2 background = "#dbeafe" end
column: content = "Top" end
end
row:
column: content = "Bottom" end
end
end` |

| `headers`
سرستون‌ها | A list of ids, separated by spaces, of the heading cells that describe this data cell. It is for tables so complex that `scope` is not enough. Every id must exist in the same page, and the compiler checks that. [idref (list)] | `table:
row:
column: heading = true id = "h-day" content = "Day" end
column: heading = true id = "h-sales" content = "Sales" end
end
row:
column: content = "Monday" headers = "h-day" end
column: content = "120" headers = "h-sales h-day" end
end
end` |

### `header column` (Persian: `ستون`; HTML: `<th>`)

The name of a `column` when it stands in a `header` row: the compiler writes `th` for it, with no extra work from you. It takes `scope` (`col` or `row`, `colgroup` or `rowgroup`), `abbr` (a short form that screen readers read instead of a long heading), and also `colspan`, `rowspan` and `headers`.

```salam
table:
    header:
        row:
            column: content = "Temperature" scope = col abbr = "Temp" end
            column: content = "Rain" scope = col end
        end
    end
end
```

### `heading column` (Persian: `ستون`; HTML: `<th>`)

A heading cell outside the header, made by writing `heading = true` on a `column`. Use it for the first cell of every row (a row heading) with `scope = row`, or in a footer for the word Total. It takes the same attributes as the header cell, `scope` and `abbr` among them.

```salam
table:
    row:
        column: heading = true scope = row content = "Monday" end
        column: content = "Sunny" end
    end
end
```

Only inside: `row`

## Try it yourself

- Make a table of your week with the days as columns and morning, noon and evening as rows. Use `heading = true` with `scope = row` for the times.

- Add a footer to the price list above with a total row, and style the total in bold with a line above it.

- Take the scrolling table and widen it to 60rem. What changes on a narrow window? Then remove the `overflow` line and look at the page.
