## Skipping work for big pages

Three properties help a long page load and scroll faster, at the price of some promises. `contain` tells the browser that the inside of an element does not affect anything outside it, so a change inside never needs the whole page to be laid out again. `content visibility = auto` goes further: the browser does not draw or lay out the element while it is far off screen. Because a skipped element has no height, add `contain intrinsic size` with a guess, `auto 600px` meaning "use the real size once you have seen it, and 600px before". Use it on the sections of a page that is long, not on small pages, where it only adds risk.

```salam
section:
    content visibility = auto
    contain intrinsic size = "auto 600px"
    heading: size = 2 content = "Far down the page" end
    paragraph: content = "Drawn only when the reader scrolls near it." end
end
```

## Reset and field sizing

`all` resets every property of an element at once. Only the keywords that work for any property are allowed: `initial`, `inherit`, `unset` and `revert`. Put it first and then add back the styles you want, the way the reference example turns a button into a plain box. `field sizing = content` lets a text box grow while the user types, with no script, in browsers that support it. The properties `appearance`, `resize` and `zoom` are in the responsive lesson.

web-css-fieldsizing.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "field sizing"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    global: selector = "p" margin = "0 0 8px" end
    paragraph: content = "Type in the box: it grows with the text." end
    input:
        id = "name"
        field sizing = content
        min width = "6ch"
        max width = "100%"
        padding = 6
        font size = 18
        placeholder = "Your name"
    end
    paragraph: content = "Without it, a text box keeps one fixed width:" margin top = 24 end
    input: padding = 6 font size = 18 placeholder = "Your name" end
end
```

## Reference: sizing, space, display and overflow

Every property of this lesson is below with what it accepts and a short example that the compiler has checked. Persian names work in any file and are what the Persian lessons use. First the `global` element, then the properties in groups.

### The global rule

### `global` (Persian: `سراسری`)

Holds a style rule for the whole page instead of for one element. With no `selector` the rule applies to every element, which is the place for resets such as `box sizing`. With a `selector` it applies to everything the selector matches. It takes any style property, with the `hover`, `focus` and similar prefixes too.

```salam
global: selector = ".tip" background = "#fef3c7" padding = 12 hover background = "#fde68a" end
```

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selector`
گزینشگر | A CSS selector as text: a tag such as `"h2"`, a class `".card"`, an id `"#intro"`, a state `"a:hover"`, a position `"li:nth-child(odd)"` or a combination `"nav a"`. The text is passed to the stylesheet as it is, so the compiler does not check it. [string] | `global: selector = "li:nth-child(odd)" background = "#f1f5f9" end` |

### Width, height and shape

Each size has a physical form (`width`, `height`) and a logical form (`inline size`, `block size`), and a minimum and a maximum of each.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`
عرض
width | The width of the element. A number is pixels. `auto` (the default) lets a block fill its parent, a percentage is a share of the parent's width, and `min-content`, `max-content` and `fit-content` size the box by its text. With the default `box sizing` it is the width of the content only. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: width = "60%" background = "#bfdbfe" padding = 8 content = "60% of the parent" end` |

| `min width`
کمینه عرض
min-width | The smallest width the element may have. It beats both `width` and `max width`. Use it to keep a column readable when the window shrinks. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: width = "20%" min width = 160 background = "#bfdbfe" padding = 8 content = "never under 160px" end` |

| `max width`
بیشینه عرض
max-width | The largest width the element may have; `none` (the default) means no limit. The classic pair is `width = "100%"` with `max width = "40rem"`: full width on a phone, a comfortable line length on a monitor. [length / percentage / none, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: max width = "24rem" background = "#bfdbfe" padding = 8 content = "As wide as the parent allows, but never over 24rem." end` |

| `height`
ارتفاع
height | The height of the element. `auto` (the default) makes the box as tall as its content. A percentage works only when the parent has a height of its own. A fixed height with more content inside needs an `overflow` choice. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: height = 80 background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 content = "80px tall" end` |

| `min height`
کمینه ارتفاع
min-height | The smallest height the element may have. Unlike a fixed `height` it lets the box grow when the content needs more room, which makes it the safer choice for cards and sections. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: min height = 100 background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 content = "At least 100px, taller if needed" end` |

| `max height`
بیشینه ارتفاع
max-height | The largest height the element may have; `none` means no limit. Combine it with `overflow = auto` to get a box that scrolls once its content is taller than the limit. [length / percentage / none, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: max height = 60 overflow = auto background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 content = "A long text that does not fit in sixty pixels, so the box gets a scrollbar instead of growing taller and taller." end` |

| `inline size`
اندازه خطی
inline-size | The size along the direction text runs: the width in English and Persian pages, the height in vertical writing modes. It is the logical form of `width`, so a layout written with it keeps working when the writing mode changes. Values are the same as for `width`. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: inline size = "50%" background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 8 content = "inline size = 50%" end` |

| `min inline size`
کمینه اندازه خطی
min-inline-size | The logical `min width`: the smallest size along the text direction. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: inline size = "20%" min inline size = 160 background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 8 content = "never under 160px" end` |

| `max inline size`
بیشینه اندازه خطی
max-inline-size | The logical `max width`: the largest size along the text direction. `max inline size = "60ch"` keeps lines of text near sixty characters in any language and direction. [length / percentage / none, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: max inline size = "30ch" background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 8 content = "A line of text never gets longer than thirty characters in this box." end` |

| `block size`
اندازه بلوکی
block-size | The size across the direction text runs: the height in English and Persian pages. It is the logical form of `height`. Values are the same as for `height`. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: block size = 70 background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 8 content = "block size = 70" end` |

| `min block size`
کمینه اندازه بلوکی
min-block-size | The logical `min height`: the smallest size across the text direction. [length / percentage / auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: min block size = 90 background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 8 content = "at least 90px" end` |

| `max block size`
بیشینه اندازه بلوکی
max-block-size | The logical `max height`: the largest size across the text direction. Pair it with `overflow` for a scrolling box. [length / percentage / none, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: max block size = 50 overflow = auto background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 8 content = "A long text that needs more than fifty pixels of height, so it scrolls." end` |

| `aspect ratio`
نسبت ابعاد
aspect-ratio | Keeps the box in a fixed shape: the width divided by the height, written `"16 / 9"` or as one number such as `1.5`. It takes effect when one of the two sizes is `auto`, so give a width and let the height follow. `auto` uses the natural ratio of an image or video when it has one. [ratio / auto] | `box: width = 240 aspect ratio = "16 / 9" background = "#c7d2fe" content = "16 / 9" end` |

| `box sizing`
اندازه جعبه
box-sizing | What `width` and `height` measure. `content-box` (the default) is the content alone, so padding and border are added on top. `border-box` includes padding and border, so the box is exactly the size you wrote. Most pages set `border-box` once for every element with a `global` rule. [content-box, border-box] | `box: box sizing = border-box width = 200 padding = 20 border = "4px solid teal" content = "Exactly 200px wide" end` |

### Margin

The space outside the border. `margin` sets all sides, the `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` forms set one physical side, and the `block` and `inline` forms follow the text direction.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `margin`
فضا
margin | The space outside the border. One value is for all four sides, two are vertical then horizontal (`"10 20"`), three are top, horizontal, bottom, and four go clockwise from the top. `auto` shares out the free space, so `"0 auto"` centers a box that has a width. Negative values are allowed. A percentage is a share of the parent's width. [length / percentage / auto; up to 4 values] | `box: margin = "10 40" background = "#fed7aa" content = "margin = 10 40" end` |

| `margin top`
فضا بالا
margin-top | The space above the box. Vertical margins of neighbouring blocks collapse into the larger of the two instead of adding up. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: margin top = 30 background = "#fed7aa" content = "30px of space above" end` |

| `margin right`
فضا راست
margin-right | The space on the right of the box, whatever the text direction. `margin left = auto` pushes a box to the right edge. Prefer `margin inline end` when the side should follow the language. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: width = 200 margin left = auto background = "#fed7aa" content = "pushed to the right" end` |

| `margin bottom`
فضا پایین
margin-bottom | The space below the box. Vertical margins of neighbouring blocks collapse into the larger of the two. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: margin bottom = 30 background = "#fed7aa" content = "30px of space below" end` |

| `margin left`
فضا چپ
margin-left | The space on the left of the box, whatever the text direction. `margin right = auto` pushes a box to the left edge, and `margin left` with `margin right` both `auto` centers it. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: width = 200 margin left = 60 background = "#fed7aa" content = "60px from the left" end` |

| `margin block`
فضا بلوکی
margin-block | The margin at the start and end of the block direction, which is top and bottom in English and Persian pages. One value sets both, two values are start then end. [length / percentage / auto; up to 2 values] | `box: margin block = "20 40" background = "#fed7aa" content = "20 before, 40 after" end` |

| `margin block start`
فضا بلوکی ابتدا
margin-block-start | The margin before the box in the block direction: the top in English and Persian pages. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: margin block start = 24 background = "#fed7aa" content = "24px before" end` |

| `margin block end`
فضا بلوکی انتها
margin-block-end | The margin after the box in the block direction: the bottom in English and Persian pages. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: margin block end = 24 background = "#fed7aa" content = "24px after" end` |

| `margin inline`
فضا خطی
margin-inline | The margin at the start and end of the text direction, which is left and right in English and right and left in Persian. One value sets both, two values are start then end. [length / percentage / auto; up to 2 values] | `box: margin inline = "10 60" background = "#fed7aa" content = "10 at the start, 60 at the end" end` |

| `margin inline start`
فضا ابتدا
margin-inline-start | The margin on the side where text starts: the left in English, the right in Persian. It is the side to use for indents, because it flips with the language. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: margin inline start = 40 background = "#fed7aa" content = "indented from the start side" end` |

| `margin inline end`
فضا انتها
margin-inline-end | The margin on the side where text ends: the right in English, the left in Persian. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: margin inline end = 40 background = "#fed7aa" content = "space kept at the end side" end` |

### Padding

The space inside the border. It has the same set of sides as margin, and it never takes `auto` or a negative value.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `padding`
فاصله
padding | The space between the content and the border, inside the box. It shows the element's background. One value is for all four sides, two are vertical then horizontal, three are top, horizontal, bottom, and four go clockwise from the top. It cannot be negative or `auto`. [length / percentage; up to 4 values] | `box: padding = "8 24" background = "#bbf7d0" content = "padding = 8 24" end` |

| `padding top`
فاصله بالا
padding-top | The padding above the content. [length / percentage] | `box: padding top = 30 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "30px of padding above" end` |

| `padding right`
فاصله راست
padding-right | The padding on the right of the content, whatever the text direction. [length / percentage] | `box: padding right = 60 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "60px of padding on the right" end` |

| `padding bottom`
فاصله پایین
padding-bottom | The padding below the content. [length / percentage] | `box: padding bottom = 30 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "30px of padding below" end` |

| `padding left`
فاصله چپ
padding-left | The padding on the left of the content, whatever the text direction. [length / percentage] | `box: padding left = 60 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "60px of padding on the left" end` |

| `padding block`
فاصله بلوکی
padding-block | The padding at the start and end of the block direction, which is top and bottom in English and Persian pages. One value sets both, two values are start then end. [length / percentage; up to 2 values] | `box: padding block = "4 20" background = "#bbf7d0" content = "4 before, 20 after" end` |

| `padding block start`
فاصله بلوکی ابتدا
padding-block-start | The padding before the content in the block direction: the top in English and Persian pages. [length / percentage] | `box: padding block start = 24 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "24px before" end` |

| `padding block end`
فاصله بلوکی انتها
padding-block-end | The padding after the content in the block direction: the bottom in English and Persian pages. [length / percentage] | `box: padding block end = 24 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "24px after" end` |

| `padding inline`
فاصله خطی
padding-inline | The padding at the start and end of the text direction, which is left and right in English and right and left in Persian. One value sets both, two values are start then end. [length / percentage; up to 2 values] | `box: padding inline = "30 10" background = "#bbf7d0" content = "30 at the start, 10 at the end" end` |

| `padding inline start`
فاصله ابتدا
padding-inline-start | The padding on the side where text starts: the left in English, the right in Persian. [length / percentage] | `box: padding inline start = 40 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "40px of padding at the start side" end` |

| `padding inline end`
فاصله انتها
padding-inline-end | The padding on the side where text ends: the right in English, the left in Persian. [length / percentage] | `box: padding inline end = 40 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "40px of padding at the end side" end` |

### Overflow

What happens to content that does not fit.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overflow`
سرریز
overflow | What happens to content that is bigger than its box. `visible` (the default) lets it spill out, `hidden` cuts it off, `clip` cuts it off with no way to scroll at all, `scroll` always shows scrollbars and `auto` shows them only when needed. One value sets both directions, two values are horizontal then vertical. [visible, hidden, clip, scroll, auto; up to 2 values] | `box: width = 160 height = 50 overflow = auto border = "1px solid #94a3b8" content = "A text that is longer than the small box it sits in, so it has to go somewhere." end` |

| `overflow x`
سرریز افقی
overflow-x | What happens to content that is too wide for the box. Values are the same as for `overflow`. If you set one axis to something other than `visible`, a `visible` on the other axis becomes `auto`. [visible, hidden, clip, scroll, auto] | `box: width = 160 overflow x = scroll white space = nowrap border = "1px solid #94a3b8" content = "One long line that does not wrap and runs past the right edge." end` |

| `overflow y`
سرریز عمودی
overflow-y | What happens to content that is too tall for the box. Values are the same as for `overflow`. `auto` is the usual choice for a panel with a fixed height. [visible, hidden, clip, scroll, auto] | `box: height = 50 width = 160 overflow y = auto border = "1px solid #94a3b8" content = "A text that is longer than the small box it sits in, so it has to go somewhere." end` |

| `overflow block`
سرریز بلوکی
overflow-block | The overflow along the block direction (vertical in English and Persian pages). It is the logical form of `overflow y`. Only some browsers support it yet, so `overflow y` is the safer choice today. [visible, hidden, clip, scroll, auto] | `box: block size = 50 inline size = 160 overflow block = auto border = "1px solid #94a3b8" content = "A text that is longer than the small box it sits in, so it has to go somewhere." end` |

| `overflow inline`
سرریز خطی
overflow-inline | The overflow along the text direction (horizontal in English and Persian pages). It is the logical form of `overflow x`. Only some browsers support it yet, so `overflow x` is the safer choice today. [visible, hidden, clip, scroll, auto] | `box: inline size = 160 overflow inline = scroll white space = nowrap border = "1px solid #94a3b8" content = "One long line that does not wrap and runs past the end." end` |

| `overflow anchor`
لنگر سرریز
overflow-anchor | Turns scroll anchoring on (`auto`, the default) or off (`none`). Anchoring is the browser's trick of keeping what you are reading in place when content above it loads or changes size. Turn it off only for a scroller whose own script manages the scroll position. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: height = 60 overflow = auto overflow anchor = none border = "1px solid #94a3b8" content = "A text that is longer than the small box it sits in, so it has to go somewhere." end` |

| `overflow clip margin`
فضا برش سرریز
overflow-clip-margin | With `overflow = clip`, how far past the box edge the content may still be painted before it is cut: a length such as `"12px"`, optionally after `content-box`, `padding-box` or `border-box` to say which edge to measure from. It does nothing with the other overflow values. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: overflow = clip overflow clip margin = "12px" border = "2px solid #6366f1" padding = 8 width = 140 height = 40 content = "A text that is longer than the small box it sits in, so it has to go somewhere." end` |

### Display and containment

How the element takes part in the layout, whether it is drawn, and what the browser may skip.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `display`
نمایش
display | How the element takes part in the layout. `block` starts a new line and fills the width, `inline` flows inside a line of text and ignores width and height, `inline-block` flows like text but accepts width and height, `none` removes the element from the page, `flex` and `grid` lay the children out in rows or tracks, `flow-root` makes a box that contains its floats, and `contents` removes the box but keeps the children. The elements have their own default: `span` is inline, `box` is block. [block, inline, inline-block, flex, inline-flex, grid, ...] | `box: display = flex gap = 8 span: content = "one" background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 end span: content = "two" background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 end end` |

| `visibility`
دیدپذیری
visibility | Hides an element but keeps its place: `hidden` leaves an empty gap, `visible` is the default. Unlike `display = none` the space is still used. A hidden element cannot be clicked or focused, and screen readers skip it. `collapse` removes a table row or column and frees its space, and acts like `hidden` elsewhere. [visible, hidden, collapse] | `box: visibility = hidden background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "You cannot see me, but my space is kept" end` |

| `contain`
محدودسازی
contain | Promises the browser that what is inside the element does not affect the rest of the page, so it can skip work. `layout`, `paint`, `size`, `inline-size` and `style` are the single promises; `content` means layout, paint and style; `strict` adds size to those; `none` promises nothing. With `size` the box no longer grows with its content, so give it a size. [none, strict, content, size, inline-size, layout, ...; up to 4 values] | `box: contain = content background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "A widget whose inside never changes the layout outside" end` |

| `content visibility`
دیدپذیری محتوا
content-visibility | Lets the browser skip the work for parts of the page that are not on screen. `auto` skips an element until it is near the visible area, `hidden` always skips it but keeps its rendered state (cheaper to show again than `display = none`), and `visible` is the default. Pair `auto` with `contain intrinsic size` so the scroll bar does not jump. [visible, auto, hidden] | `box: content visibility = auto contain intrinsic size = "auto 120px" background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "A long section far down the page" end` |

| `contain intrinsic size`
اندازه ذاتی محدود
contain-intrinsic-size | The size the browser should assume for an element whose content is being skipped (by `content visibility`) or contained by `size`. One or two lengths, width then height. An `auto` in front, as in `"auto 300px"`, means: use the last size it really had, and 300px until then. [length; up to 4 values] | `box: content visibility = auto contain intrinsic size = "auto 300px 200px" background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "placeholder 300 wide, 200 tall" end` |

| `contain intrinsic width`
عرض ذاتی محدودسازی
contain-intrinsic-width | Only the width part of `contain intrinsic size`: the width assumed for a skipped or size-contained element, optionally with `auto` in front. [length; up to 2 values] | `box: content visibility = auto contain intrinsic width = "auto 300px" background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "assumed 300px wide" end` |

| `contain intrinsic height`
ارتفاع ذاتی محدودسازی
contain-intrinsic-height | Only the height part of `contain intrinsic size`: the height assumed for a skipped or size-contained element, optionally with `auto` in front. [length; up to 2 values] | `box: content visibility = auto contain intrinsic height = "auto 200px" background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "assumed 200px tall" end` |

| `contain intrinsic inline size`
اندازه ذاتی محدودسازی خطی
contain-intrinsic-inline-size | The logical form of `contain intrinsic width`: the size along the text direction assumed for a skipped or size-contained element. [length; up to 2 values] | `box: content visibility = auto contain intrinsic inline size = "auto 300px" background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "assumed 300px along the text" end` |

| `contain intrinsic block size`
اندازه ذاتی محدودسازی بلوکی
contain-intrinsic-block-size | The logical form of `contain intrinsic height`: the size across the text direction assumed for a skipped or size-contained element. [length; up to 2 values] | `box: content visibility = auto contain intrinsic block size = "auto 200px" background = "#fef9c3" padding = 8 content = "assumed 200px across the text" end` |

### Reset and field size

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all`
همه ویژگی‌ها
all | Resets every style property of the element at once. Only the CSS-wide keywords are allowed: `initial` (the property's own default), `inherit`, `unset` (inherit if the property normally inherits, otherwise initial) and `revert` (the browser's stylesheet). Write it first, then add the styles you want back. It leaves `direction` alone. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `button: all = unset padding = "8 16" background = "#0f766e" color = white cursor = pointer content = "A button with no browser look" end` |

| `field sizing`
اندازه فیلد
field-sizing | Lets a text box, text area or select size itself to what it contains. `content` makes it grow and shrink as the user types, `fixed` (the default) keeps the usual fixed size. Browsers that do not know it keep the fixed size, so the page still works. [fixed / content] | `input: field sizing = content min width = "8ch" padding = 6 placeholder = "Type here" end` |

## Try it yourself

- Build a card with `padding = 24`, a border and `max width = "24rem"`. Put five of them in a column and add `margin = "0 auto 16px"`. Is the gap between two cards 16px or 32px?

- Take the box example and write `global: box sizing = "border-box" end` at the top. Which sizes change, and why does the box look smaller?

- Make a 150 by 100 box with a long sentence in it and try each value of `overflow`. Then replace `height = 100` with `min height = 100`.

- Replace every `margin left` and `margin right` of a page with the logical forms, then add `dir = rtl` to the page and look at the result.


---

# Fonts and text styling

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/css-text/

A page is mostly letters, and how they look decides whether people read it. This lesson covers the font properties (which font, how big, how heavy, which features), the text properties (alignment, lines, spacing, wrapping, direction) and the web font element, with examples you can run and a short guide for Persian and Arabic text.

## Choosing a font

You cannot know which fonts a visitor has installed. `font family` therefore takes a list, called a font stack: the browser tries the names from left to right and uses the first font that exists and has the letters it needs to draw. A name that contains spaces goes in single quotes inside the string. The last name should be a generic family, which every browser can always fill: `serif` (letters with small feet), `sans-serif` (without feet), `monospace` (equal width, for code), `cursive` and `fantasy` (decorative, and different on every system) and `system-ui` (the font of the operating system's own windows). `ui-monospace` is the system's code font.

web-font-family.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Font stacks"
    global: selector = "body" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    paragraph: font family = "Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif" content = "Serif: Georgia, then Times New Roman, then any serif font." end
    paragraph: font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" content = "Sans serif: the interface font of the system." end
    paragraph: font family = "ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace" content = "Monospace: every letter is equally wide." end
    paragraph: font family = "cursive" content = "Cursive: the look of handwriting." end
    paragraph: font family = "NoSuchFont, serif" content = "The first name does not exist, so the browser takes the next." end
end
```

Look at the last line of the preview. The first name does not exist, so the browser skips it silently and takes the next. This is also how a missing Persian glyph is handled: if the first font has no such letter, the browser asks the next font in the list for that single letter.

Put the rule on `body` with a `global` element, as the examples do, and every element inherits it. Only set `font family` on a single element when that element really needs a different font, such as code.

## Size

`font size` accepts a bare number (pixels), or a string with a unit. The useful units are `rem`, which is relative to the font size of the whole page, `em` and `%`, which are relative to the parent element, and `vw`, which is a part of the window width. There are also keywords from `xx-small` to `xx-large`, and `clamp(min, preferred, max)`, which grows with the window but never leaves the two limits. Prefer `rem` to pixels for text: people who raise the default size in their browser then get bigger text on your page too.

web-font-size.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Font sizes"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    paragraph: font size = 12 content = "12 means 12px" end
    paragraph: font size = 12 + 6 content = "An expression: 12 + 6 is 18px" end
    paragraph: font size = "1.5rem" content = "1.5rem is one and a half root sizes" end
    paragraph: font size = "150%" content = "150% of the parent size" end
    paragraph: font size = "x-large" content = "The keyword x-large" end
    paragraph: font size = "clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem)" content = "clamp() grows with the window, within limits" end
end
```

The second line is an expression. Any number or string that the compiler can compute is a valid value, so you can also use a constant declared above the page, such as `font size = BASE * 2`, and change one number to resize many elements.

Before the next sections, try the settings yourself. The slider and the list below run small functions that use the `dom` package, which is explained in its own page. Each time the slider moves, its function reads the value and sets the CSS property `font-size` of the sample. Inside such a function, CSS properties keep their original names with dashes.

web-font-tester.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Type tester"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    paragraph: id = "label" content = "Size: 28px" end
    box: display = "flex" gap = 12
        input: id = "size" type = "range" min = 12 max = 64 value = 28
            input = ():
                size := dom.GetValue(dom.ById("size"))
                dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("sample"), "font-size", size + "px")
                dom.SetText(dom.ById("label"), "Size: " + size + "px")
            end
        end
        select: id = "family" change = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("sample"), "font-family", dom.GetValue(dom.ById("family"))) end
            option: value = "Georgia, serif" content = "Serif" end
            option: value = "system-ui, sans-serif" content = "Sans serif" end
            option: value = "ui-monospace, monospace" content = "Monospace" end
        end
    end
    paragraph: id = "sample" font family = "Georgia, serif" font size = 28 content = "Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow." end
end
```

## Weight, style and width

`font weight` is a number from 1 to 1000: 400 is normal text, 700 is bold. `normal` and `bold` are the same as 400 and 700, and `bolder` and `lighter` move one step away from the parent. A font file has only the weights its designer drew. If you ask for 300 and the font has 400 and 700, the browser shows 400, so in the preview below the first lines may look equal. `font style` chooses upright, `italic` (a separate design) or `oblique` (the upright letters leaned over). `font stretch` and its newer name `font width` choose narrower or wider designs and only matter for fonts that have them.

web-font-weight.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Weight, style and width"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    paragraph: font weight = 300 content = "Weight 300, light" end
    paragraph: font weight = 400 content = "Weight 400, normal" end
    paragraph: font weight = 700 content = "Weight 700, bold" end
    paragraph: font weight = 900 content = "Weight 900, black" end
    paragraph: font style = "italic" content = "Italic: the italic design of the font" end
    paragraph: font style = "oblique" content = "Oblique: the upright letters slanted" end
    paragraph: font stretch = "condensed" content = "Condensed, if the font has a narrow design" end
    paragraph: font = "italic 700 1.25rem/1.4 Georgia, serif" content = "All of it in one shorthand" end
end
```

The last line uses the shorthand `font`. It sets style, weight, width, size, line height and family in one string, in this order, with the line height after a slash. Only the size and the family are required.

The shorthand `font` resets every property it does not mention. If you write `font = "16px serif"` after a `font weight = 700` on the same element, the weight is back to 400. When you only want to change one thing, write that one property.

If a font has no bold or italic design, the browser fakes one by thickening or leaning the normal letters. The result is often a little ugly. `font synthesis` forbids this, and its parts `font synthesis weight`, `font synthesis style`, `font synthesis small caps` and `font synthesis position` forbid a single kind of faking.

## Web fonts

To use a font that visitors do not have, ship the file with the page. The `font` element describes one file: `name` is the name you will use in `font family`, and `url` is the address of the file. Salam turns it into an `@font-face` rule, and the browser downloads the file only when some text uses the font. When one family has several files, write one `font` element per file with the same name and the `weight` or `style` that the file provides.

web-font-face.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "A web font"
    font:
        name = "Course Serif"
        url = "/fonts/course-serif.woff2"
        weight = 400
        style = normal
        display = swap
    end
    font:
        name = "Course Serif"
        url = "/fonts/course-serif-bold.woff2"
        weight = 700
        display = swap
    end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "'Course Serif', Georgia, serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.7 end
    heading: size = 2 content = "Reading in comfort" end
    paragraph: content = "The font files are not part of this preview, so the browser shows the next name in the stack." end
    paragraph: font weight = 700 content = "This line asks for weight 700 and would use the second file." end
end
```

The two files of this example do not exist in the preview, so the page shows the next font of the stack. That is the right way to build a page: the fallback must always be good enough to read. On your own site, put the files in a folder that your server serves, and the page starts using them. Salam checks the address while compiling: an unsafe address is an error, and a relative file that cannot be found next to the program is a warning. If you leave out `type`, Salam finds out the format from the end of the address.

Three attributes shape the loading. `display = swap` shows the fallback font at once and swaps in the real one when it arrives, so the text is never invisible. `range` lists the Unicode ranges a file covers, so a Persian file is downloaded only by pages that contain Persian letters. `weight` can be a range such as `"100 900"` for a variable font.

Every font file is a download, and a page that waits for five of them feels slow. Use one or two families, only the weights you really use, and the `woff2` format, which is the smallest. And check the licence: a font on your computer is not always a font you may publish.

## Features, variants and variable fonts

A good font contains more than letters: small capitals, several kinds of digits, ligatures (shapes where two letters join, such as fi) and alternate forms. They are called OpenType features, and each has a four letter tag such as `smcp` or `liga`. The properties that start with `font variant` switch the common ones in words: `font variant caps`, `font variant numeric`, `font variant ligatures`, `font variant position`, `font variant alternates`, `font variant east asian` and `font variant emoji`. `font feature settings` is the raw version for the rest: `"'smcp' 1"` turns a feature on, and 0 turns it off. `font kerning` controls the pair spacing, which is on by default and should stay on.

web-font-variants.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Font variants"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "Georgia, serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.8 end
    paragraph: font variant caps = "small-caps" content = "Small capitals for a book title" end
    paragraph: font variant numeric = "tabular-nums" content = "1111 and 8888 line up in tables" end
    paragraph: font variant numeric = "oldstyle-nums" content = "Old style figures 2026 sit in the line" end
    paragraph: font variant ligatures = "none" content = "office affinity: ligatures switched off" end
    paragraph: font kerning = "none" content = "AVATAR WAVE: kerning switched off" end
    paragraph: font feature settings = "'smcp' 1" content = "The same small capitals through the raw feature tag" end
    paragraph: font variation settings = "'wght' 650" content = "A variable font reads this axis; others ignore it" end
end
```

A variable font is one file that contains a whole range of designs along axes, such as weight (`wght`) or width (`wdth`). `font variation settings` sets the axes by their tag, and `font optical sizing` lets a font with an optical size axis change its shape with the text size. When an ordinary property exists, use it: `font weight = 650` sets the weight axis and is easier to read. `font palette` picks one of the colour sets of a colour font.

Features only work if the font has them. A font without small capitals shows the normal letters or, in some browsers, faked ones, and a line in the preview above may look unchanged. Test with the font you really use.

## Aligning and transforming text

`text align` places the lines of a block. Use `start` and `end` and not `left` and `right`: they follow the direction of the text, so the same rule is correct for English and for Persian. `center` centres every line and `justify` stretches every line but the last to the full width. `text align last` sets the last line separately, and `text justify` chooses whether the extra space goes between words or between letters. `text indent` pushes the first line in, the way books mark a new paragraph. `text transform` changes the case of the shown letters without changing the text, which is better than typing capitals because a screen reader and a search still see the real text.

web-font-align.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Aligning text"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    box: text align = "start" content = "Start: the side where reading begins." border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" padding = 8 margin bottom = 8 end
    box: text align = "center" content = "Center: lines in the middle." border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" padding = 8 margin bottom = 8 end
    box: text align = "end" content = "End: the side where reading ends." border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" padding = 8 margin bottom = 8 end
    box:
        text align = "justify"
        text align last = "center"
        text indent = "2em"
        border = "1px solid #cbd5e1"
        padding = 8
        margin bottom = 8
        max width = 420
        content = "Justified text stretches every line to the same width, and the last line can be placed on its own. The first line is indented by two letters."
    end
    box: text transform = "uppercase" content = "uppercase letters" end
    box: text transform = "capitalize" content = "every word starts large" end
end
```

Justified text needs wide lines. In a narrow column the gaps between words become large and uneven, so use `justify` only for wide blocks.

## Lines, shadows and outlines

`text decoration` draws lines on text. It is a shorthand of four properties: `text decoration line` (`underline`, `overline`, `line-through`), `text decoration style` (`solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed`, `wavy`), `text decoration color` and `text decoration thickness`. Two more properties tune underlines: `text underline offset` moves the line away from the letters, and `text decoration skip ink` decides if the line jumps over the tails of letters like g and y. `text shadow` adds one or more shadows, each as horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur and colour; two shadows of the same colour make a glow. `webkit text stroke` and `webkit text fill color` outline letters; the name starts with `webkit` because browsers adopted the idea under that prefix, and all of them still use it.

web-font-decoration.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Decoration and shadow"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.8 font size = 20 end
    paragraph: text decoration line = "underline" text decoration style = "wavy" text decoration color = "crimson" text decoration thickness = 2 content = "A red wavy underline" end
    paragraph: text decoration line = "underline" text underline offset = 6 text decoration skip ink = "none" content = "An underline moved down from the letters" end
    paragraph: text decoration = "line-through 2px #64748b" content = "Crossed out in one shorthand" end
    paragraph: text decoration line = "overline underline" text decoration style = "double" content = "A line above and a double line below" end
    paragraph: text shadow = "2px 2px 4px #94a3b8" font size = 32 font weight = 700 content = "Soft shadow" end
    paragraph: text shadow = "0 0 8px #38bdf8, 0 0 16px #0ea5e9" color = "white" background = "#0f172a" padding = 8 content = "A glow made of two shadows" end
    paragraph: webkit text stroke = "1px #0f172a" webkit text fill color = "transparent" font size = 40 font weight = 700 content = "Outline" end
end
```

People expect an underline to mean a link. Do not underline other text, and do not remove the underline of real links without another clear sign, such as a different colour plus a weight. Shadows and outlines also reduce contrast, so check that the text stays readable.

## Line height and spacing

`line height` is the most important property for reading. Give it a plain number, without a unit: `1.6` means 1.6 times the font size of that element, and a child with a larger size gets a larger line height by itself. A length such as `"24px"` is passed to the children as a fixed result and makes big headings overlap. Around 1.5 suits English, and Persian needs about 1.9 because of its dots and marks above and below the line. `letter spacing` and `word spacing` add space between letters and between words. A small positive letter spacing is good for capitals, and a tiny negative one for very large headings. `vertical align` moves an inline element up or down within the line, as `super` and `sub` do for powers and indices. `tab size` sets the width of a tab character in preformatted text.

web-font-spacing.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Spacing"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    box: width = 300 line height = 1 background = "#f1f5f9" margin bottom = 12 content = "line height 1: the lines of this paragraph are packed tightly together." end
    box: width = 300 line height = 1.6 background = "#f1f5f9" margin bottom = 12 content = "line height 1.6: comfortable for reading long text in a paragraph." end
    box: width = 300 line height = 2.2 background = "#f1f5f9" margin bottom = 12 content = "line height 2.2: so open that the lines start to fall apart." end
    box: letter spacing = "0.25em" text transform = "uppercase" font size = 14 margin bottom = 12 content = "Letter spacing for a label" end
    box: word spacing = "0.5em" content = "Words spread apart by half a letter" end
end
```

Do not use `letter spacing` on Persian or Arabic. The letters of these scripts are joined, and a gap between them cuts the word into pieces. Browsers treat it differently, and where a gap is added it cuts the word apart, so the safe value is always `0` or nothing.

## Wrapping and cutting

Normally the browser breaks a line at spaces. `white space` changes this: `nowrap` never breaks, `pre` keeps the text as typed, `pre-wrap` keeps it and still wraps, and `pre-line` keeps only the line breaks. `white space collapse` is the "what happens to spaces" half of it. When a single word is longer than its box, `overflow wrap = "anywhere"` lets it break so it does not stick out of the page, which is exactly what a long web address needs. `word break = "break-all"` breaks everywhere, even where the word would fit, and `keep-all` is for Chinese, Japanese and Korean, where it forbids breaks inside a word. `hyphens = "auto"` hyphenates words in languages the browser has a dictionary for, if the element has the right `lang`. `text wrap = "balance"` evens out the lines of a short heading, and `pretty` avoids a last line with one short word.

web-font-wrapping.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Wrapping long text"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    box: width = 180 white space = "nowrap" overflow = "hidden" text overflow = "ellipsis" background = "#f1f5f9" margin bottom = 12 content = "This sentence is far too long for its box" end
    box: width = 180 overflow wrap = "anywhere" background = "#e0f2fe" margin bottom = 12 content = "https://example.com/a/very/long/address/that-does-not-fit" end
    box: width = 180 word break = "break-all" background = "#fef9c3" margin bottom = 12 content = "Break-all cuts at any letter, even in short words." end
    box: width = 180 hyphens = "auto" lang = "en" background = "#dcfce7" margin bottom = 12 content = "Hyphenation helps incomprehensibilities fit narrow columns." end
    box: width = 180 white space = "pre-line" background = "#fae8ff" content = "Line breaks in the source\nare kept\nwith pre-line." end
end
```

To show only the first lines of a long text, you have two tools. `text overflow = "ellipsis"` replaces the cut-off end of one line with an ellipsis, and `line clamp` limits a block to a number of lines. Both are new or fussy, so build the example below the way it is written: with a `max height` and `overflow = "hidden"` as a safety net that works everywhere.

web-font-clamp.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Clamping lines"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    box:
        width = 260
        line height = 1.5
        line clamp = 3
        overflow = "hidden"
        max height = "4.5em"
        background = "#f1f5f9"
        padding = "0 10"
        content = "A card preview shows only the first lines of a long text, so every card in a list keeps the same height, however much the author wrote. Everything after the third line is cut off here."
    end
    heading: size = 3 text wrap = "balance" max width = 260 content = "A long headline that is split into two lines of similar length" end
end
```

`text overflow` does nothing alone. It needs three properties together: `overflow` (anything but visible), `white space = "nowrap"` and a limited width. If you see no ellipsis, one of the three is missing.

## Direction and vertical text

`direction` chooses `ltr` or `rtl` for the text of an element. In practice you set the direction with the `dir` attribute (see the lesson on the head and global attributes) because it tells screen readers too, and use the CSS property only for a rule that applies to many elements. `unicode bidi` controls how text of mixed directions is ordered, and `bidi-override` forces the order whatever the letters are; the elements `isolate` and `direction override` in the lesson on text elements do the same job.

`writing mode` goes further and turns the lines themselves: `vertical-rl` writes down the page and stacks the lines from right to left, as in Japanese and Chinese. `text orientation` decides whether the letters of other scripts stand up or lie down, and `text combine upright` squeezes a short run, such as a year, into the space of one character.

web-font-vertical.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Vertical writing"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    box: display = "flex" gap = 32 font size = 22 height = 200
        box: writing mode = "vertical-rl" content = "Vertical lines run top to bottom" end
        box: writing mode = "vertical-rl" text orientation = "upright" content = "UPRIGHT" end
        box: writing mode = "vertical-rl"
            content = "In "
            span: text combine upright = "all" content = "2026" end
        end
    end
end
```

## Ruby and emphasis marks

Ruby is a small annotation above or below a word, mostly the pronunciation of a Chinese or Japanese word, written with the `ruby` and `ruby text` elements. `ruby position` sets the side and `ruby align` how the annotation is spread over the word. East Asian text has no italics, so emphasis is drawn as small marks on each character, with `text emphasis style`, `text emphasis color` and `text emphasis position`. The shorthand is `text emphasis`.

web-font-ruby.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Ruby and emphasis"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" font size = 26 line height = 2.2 end
    paragraph:
        ruby: ruby position = "over" ruby align = "center"
            content = "東京"
            ruby parenthesis: content = "(" end
            ruby text: content = "とうきょう" end
            ruby parenthesis: content = ")" end
        end
    end
    paragraph: text emphasis style = "filled dot" text emphasis color = "crimson" content = "Dots mark the emphasis" end
    paragraph: text emphasis style = "open circle" text emphasis position = "under right" content = "Circles below the text" end
end
```

## Persian and Arabic text

Everything above works for Persian, and a few points need care. A page in a Persian file already has `lang = "fa"` and the right-to-left direction. Then:

- Choose a font that has Persian letters, and put a safe one at the end of the stack, such as `Tahoma`. Many fonts made for English have no Persian letters, and the browser fills the gap letter by letter from another font, which looks uneven. A web font such as Vazirmatn or Estedad is the real fix: load it with the `font` element and the `range` of the Persian block.

- Set `line height` to about 1.9 for body text. Persian letters carry dots and marks that need space above and below.

- Use `text align` `start` and `end`, never `left` and `right`.

- Keep `letter spacing` at zero. Do not turn ligatures off either, because the joined forms are the script itself.

- Digits are characters, not a style. `۱۲۳` and `123` are different letters, and no CSS property converts one into the other. `font variant numeric` only changes the look of the digits a font has, such as the equal width form for columns.

- Browsers do not hyphenate Persian, and `justify` works well if the lines are long.

- Italics are rare in Persian type. A line that is only `oblique` looks slanted, which is fine for a short quotation but tiring for a paragraph. Use bold, or a different size, for emphasis.

web-font-persian.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Persian text"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "Tahoma, system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" end
    box: dir = "rtl" lang = "fa" line height = 1.9 margin bottom = 16 border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" padding = 10 max width = 340
        content = "هر کتاب برای خواننده‌ای نوشته می‌شود. این بند ۳ سطر دارد و ارتفاع خطش ۱٫۹ است تا نقطه‌ها و کسره‌ها جا داشته باشند."
    end
    box: dir = "rtl" lang = "fa" line height = 1.2 margin bottom = 16 border = "1px solid #fecaca" padding = 10 max width = 340
        content = "همین متن با ارتفاع خط ۱٫۲ فشرده و خسته‌کننده می‌شود، چون سطرها به هم می‌چسبند و نقطه‌ها روی هم می‌افتند."
    end
    box: dir = "rtl" lang = "fa" line height = 1.9 text align = "justify" max width = 340 border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" padding = 10
        content = "ترازشدن دوطرفه در متن فارسی خوب کار می‌کند، به شرط آنکه خط‌ها به اندازه‌ی کافی بلند باشند."
    end
end
```

The example puts the same text three times. The first box has a comfortable line height, the second a tight one where the lines nearly touch, and the third is justified. The preview shows the page as the compiler built it, with Persian letters from the system.

## Reference: every font and text property

Each entry shows the name in Salam, its name in CSS, the values it accepts and an example. The examples are checked by the compiler, so you can paste any of them inside a `page:` block. The colour of text, `color`, belongs to the lesson on colours and backgrounds, and the box around the text to the lessons that follow it. Persian names work in any file, and the Persian lessons use them.

### Fonts: family, size, weight and style

These choose the font and its basic look.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font family`
خانواده قلم
font-family | The fonts to try, in order. The browser uses the first one that is installed (or loaded) and has the letters it needs, so always end the list with a generic family: `serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy` or `system-ui`. A name with spaces goes in single quotes inside the string. [comma list of names, quoted names and generic families (serif, sans-serif, ...)] | `box: font family = "Georgia, &#x27;Times New Roman&#x27;, serif" content = "A serif stack" end` |

| `font size`
اندازه قلم
font-size | The size of the letters. A bare number means pixels. `"1.5rem"` is relative to the size of the page root, `"1.2em"` and percentages to the size of the parent, and `vw` to the width of the window. The keywords `xx-small` to `xx-large` are fixed steps chosen by the browser, and `smaller` and `larger` move one step from the parent. [length / percentage / xx-small, x-small, small, medium, large, x-large, ...] | `box: font size = "1.5rem" content = "One and a half root sizes" end` |

| `font size adjust`
تنظیم اندازه قلم
font-size-adjust | Rescales a fallback font so that its lowercase letters look as tall as the first font's. The number is the wanted ratio of lowercase height to font size, for example `0.5`, and `none` switches it off. It stops text from jumping in size when a web font is replaced by a fallback. [number / none] | `box: font size adjust = "0.5" content = "Same apparent size in every font" end` |

| `font weight`
وزن قلم
font-weight | How heavy the strokes are. Use a number from 1 to 1000 (100 is thin, 400 is normal, 700 is bold, 900 is black) or the words `normal` and `bold`. `bolder` and `lighter` go one step from the parent. A font that has only two weights shows the nearest one, and a variable font can show every number. [number / normal, bold, bolder, lighter] | `box: font weight = 700 content = "Bold text" end` |

| `font style`
سبک قلم
font-style | Chooses the upright, italic or oblique design. `italic` uses the font's own italic letters if it has them, and `oblique` slants the upright letters. Persian fonts rarely have an italic design, so the browser slants the letters. [normal, italic, oblique] | `box: font style = "italic" content = "Italic text" end` |

| `font stretch`
کشیدگی قلم
font-stretch | Selects a narrower or wider design of the font, from `50%` to `200%` or with words such as `condensed` and `expanded`. It only does something when the font has width variants, and it never squeezes letters by itself. [percentage / normal, condensed, expanded] | `box: font stretch = "condensed" content = "A narrow design" end` |

| `font width`
پهنای قلم
font-width | The newer name of `font stretch`, with the same values. Older browsers only know `font stretch`, so use that one when the page must work everywhere. [a percentage / a font-stretch keyword] | `box: font width = "75%" content = "Seventy five percent wide" end` |

| `font`
قلم
font | The shorthand for style, weight, width, size, line height and family in one string: `"italic 700 1.25rem/1.5 Georgia, serif"`. The size and the family are required, in that order, and every property you leave out is reset to its normal value, so it can wipe settings made earlier. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: font = "italic 700 1.25rem/1.5 Georgia, serif" content = "Style, weight, size, line height and family at once" end` |

| `font synthesis`
ساخت قلم
font-synthesis | Decides what the browser may fake when the font lacks it: `weight` (bold), `style` (italic), `small-caps` and `position` (sub and superscript). `none` forbids all of it, which keeps the shapes true to the type designer. [up to 4 values] | `box: font synthesis = "none" content = "No faked bold or italic" end` |

| `font synthesis weight`
ساخت وزن قلم
font-synthesis-weight | Allows (`auto`) or forbids (`none`) a bold that the browser draws by thickening the regular letters. [auto / none] | `box: font synthesis weight = "none" content = "No fake bold" end` |

| `font synthesis style`
ساخت سبک قلم
font-synthesis-style | Allows (`auto`) or forbids (`none`) an italic made by slanting the upright letters. `oblique-only` keeps the slant but never uses it for `italic`. [auto / none / oblique-only] | `box: font synthesis style = "none" content = "No fake italic" end` |

| `font synthesis small caps`
ساخت حروف کوچک قلم
font-synthesis-small-caps | Allows (`auto`) or forbids (`none`) small capitals made by shrinking full capitals. [auto / none] | `box: font synthesis small caps = "none" content = "No fake small capitals" end` |

| `font synthesis position`
ساخت جایگاه قلم
font-synthesis-position | Allows (`auto`) or forbids (`none`) subscripts and superscripts made by shrinking and moving the normal letters. [auto / none] | `box: font synthesis position = "none" content = "No fake superscript" end` |

### Fonts: features, variants and variable fonts

These switch the extra forms and axes a font offers. The effect depends on the font.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font kerning`
فاصله‌گذاری قلم
font-kerning | Turns the font's kerning on or off. Kerning pulls certain pairs of letters, such as AV, closer together. `auto` and `normal` use it, `none` does not. Leave it on for text, and only switch it off for tests or special effects. [auto, normal, none] | `box: font kerning = "none" content = "AVATAR WAVE without kerning" end` |

| `font optical sizing`
اندازه بصری قلم
font-optical-sizing | Lets a variable font that has an optical size axis change the shape of its letters with the text size: sturdier at small sizes, finer at large ones. `auto` does it, `none` keeps one design. It has no effect on ordinary fonts. [auto, none] | `box: font optical sizing = "none" content = "Same design at every size" end` |

| `font variant`
نسخه قلم
font-variant | A shorthand that picks several alternate letter forms at once: `small-caps`, a numeric style, ligatures and so on, or `normal` to reset them. Use the longer properties below when you want to set only one thing. [up to 99 values] | `box: font variant = "small-caps" content = "Small capitals" end` |

| `font variant caps`
حروف بزرگ قلم
font-variant-caps | Chooses capital-letter forms: `small-caps` (lowercase letters become small capitals), `all-small-caps` (capitals too), `petite-caps`, `unicase` and `titling-caps`. If the font has no such shapes, browsers may fake the first two. [normal, small-caps, all-small-caps] | `box: font variant caps = "all-small-caps" content = "Every letter a small capital" end` |

| `font variant ligatures`
پیوندها نسخه قلم
font-variant-ligatures | Controls ligatures, the joined shapes such as fi. Words: `common-ligatures`, `no-common-ligatures`, `discretionary-ligatures`, `historical-ligatures`, `contextual`, or `none` for all off. Do not switch ligatures off for Persian and Arabic, where joined forms are the script itself. [up to 4 values] | `box: font variant ligatures = "no-common-ligatures" content = "office affinity without ligatures" end` |

| `font variant numeric`
عددی نسخه قلم
font-variant-numeric | Chooses the shape and spacing of digits: `lining-nums`, `oldstyle-nums`, `proportional-nums`, `tabular-nums` (every digit equally wide, for columns), `diagonal-fractions`, `slashed-zero` and `ordinal`. The font must contain these forms. It does not turn English digits into Persian digits: that is a matter of the characters you write. [up to 5 values] | `box: font variant numeric = "tabular-nums" content = "1111 and 8888 line up" end` |

| `font variant east asian`
آسیایی شرق نسخه قلم
font-variant-east-asian | Picks forms of Chinese and Japanese characters: `simplified`, `traditional`, the JIS standards `jis78` to `jis04`, `full-width`, `proportional-width` and `ruby`. It only matters for a font that carries several forms of the same character. [up to 3 values] | `box: font variant east asian = "traditional" content = "漢字 in the traditional forms" end` |

| `font variant alternates`
جایگزین های نسخه قلم
font-variant-alternates | Switches on alternate glyphs the font offers: `historical-forms`, or the functions `stylistic()`, `styleset()`, `swash()`, `ornaments()` and `annotation()`, which take a name defined by a font feature values rule. [up to 9 of historical-forms or a function like swash()] | `box: font variant alternates = "historical-forms" content = "Historical letter forms" end` |

| `font variant position`
جایگاه نسخه قلم
font-variant-position | Uses the font's own subscript (`sub`) or superscript (`super`) glyphs, which are drawn to match the weight of the text. `normal` uses neither. [normal / sub / super] | `box: font variant position = "super" content = "x2 as a real superscript" end` |

| `font variant emoji`
گونه شکلک قلم
font-variant-emoji | Chooses how characters that exist both as symbols and as emoji are drawn: `text` (a plain monochrome glyph), `emoji` (the colour picture), `unicode` (as the character itself says) or `normal` (the browser decides). [normal / text / emoji / unicode] | `box: font variant emoji = "text" content = "A heart as plain text: ❤" end` |

| `font feature settings`
تنظیمات ویژگی قلم
font-feature-settings | Switches OpenType features by their four letter tags: a comma list such as `'smcp' 1, 'liga' 0`, where 1 is on and 0 is off. It is the low level tool, so prefer the `font variant` properties and use this one for features that have none. [comma list] | `box: font feature settings = "&#x27;smcp&#x27; 1, &#x27;liga&#x27; 0" content = "Small capitals, no ligatures" end` |

| `font variation settings`
تنظیمات تغییر قلم
font-variation-settings | Sets the axes of a variable font by their four letter tags, as a comma list such as `'wght' 650, 'wdth' 90`. Ordinary fonts ignore it. When a normal property exists, such as `font weight` for `wght`, use that property instead. [comma list] | `box: font variation settings = "&#x27;wght&#x27; 650, &#x27;wdth&#x27; 90" content = "A weight between two steps" end` |

| `font palette`
پالت قلم
font-palette | Chooses the colour palette of a colour font: `light`, `dark`, `normal`, or the name of a palette defined with a `@font-palette-values` rule. Fonts without colour layers ignore it. [normal / light / dark / an ident / palette-mix()] | `box: font palette = "dark" content = "A colour font in its dark palette" end` |

| `font language override`
جایگزینی زبان قلم
font-language-override | Forces the OpenType language system, written as a four letter tag in quotes such as `'TRK'`, instead of the one taken from the `lang` attribute. `normal` goes back to the default. Rarely needed. [a quoted string / normal] | `box: font language override = "&#x27;TRK&#x27;" content = "Turkish forms of the letters" end` |

### Web font element

The `font` element goes directly inside the page.

### `font` (Persian: `قلم`)

Declares a web font, which becomes an `@font-face` rule. `name` and `url` are required, and the element goes directly inside the page. Afterwards write the name in `font family`. Browsers download the file only when some text uses the font, and until then they show the next font of the stack.

```salam
font:
    name = "Course Serif"
    url = "/fonts/course-serif.woff2"
    weight = 400
    display = swap
end
box: font family = "Course Serif, Georgia, serif" content = "Set in the course font" end
```

Required: `name`, `url` · Only inside: `page` · Void element, it cannot have children

| Attribute | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name`
نام | The family name you choose for the font. It is free text and has nothing to do with the name of the file: you write the same name later in `font family`. Required. [string] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif.woff2" end
box: font family = "Course Serif, serif" content = "The name is what font family uses" end` |

| `url`
نشانی | Where the font file is. Write one address, or several separated by spaces, best first: the browser takes the first format it understands (woff2 before woff). A relative address is read from the page, an unsafe one such as `javascript:` is an error, and a relative file that does not exist next to the program gives a warning. Required. [url (list)] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif.woff2 /fonts/course-serif.woff" end` |

| `type`
نوع | The file format: `woff2`, `woff`, `ttf` (`truetype`), `otf` (`opentype`) or `collection`. Leave it out and Salam works it out from the end of the address, then from the bytes of a file next to the program. A type that disagrees with the file is an error. [enum: font_format] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif.bin" type = woff2 end` |

| `weight`
وزن | The weight this file provides, a number from 1 to 1000 such as `400` or `700`. For a variable font give the range inside a string, such as `"100 900"`. A number outside the range is an error. Declare one `font` per weight with the same name. [string] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif-bold.woff2" weight = 700 end` |

| `style`
سبک | The style this file provides: `normal`, `italic` or `oblique`. The browser picks the file whose style matches the text. [enum: font_style] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif-italic.woff2" style = italic end` |

| `display`
نمایش | What the browser shows while the font file is still loading. `swap` shows the fallback font at once and swaps when the file arrives (the usual choice), `block` hides the text for a moment, `fallback` and `optional` swap late or never on a slow line, and `auto` leaves it to the browser. [enum: font_display] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif.woff2" display = swap end` |

| `range`
بازه | The characters this file covers, as Unicode ranges separated by commas. The browser downloads the file only when the page contains a character of that range, so a font split into a Latin file and a Persian file loads only what the page uses. `U+0600-06FF` is the Arabic and Persian block. [string] | `font: name = "Course Serif" url = "/fonts/course-serif-arabic.woff2" range = "U+0600-06FF, U+200C-200D" end` |

### Text appearance: alignment, case, lines and shadows

These change how a line of text is placed and drawn.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text align`
ترازمتن
text-align | How the lines of a block sit between its sides: `start` and `end` follow the reading direction (right and left in Persian), `left` and `right` are fixed, `center` and `justify` stretch every line but the last to the full width. Prefer `start` to `left` so that one page works in both directions. [start, end, left, right, center, justify] | `box: text align = "center" content = "Centered text" end` |

| `text align last`
تراز خط آخر
text-align-last | Sets the alignment of the last line of a block, and of lines that end with a forced break. It takes the same words as `text align` plus `auto`. It is mostly used with `text align = "justify"`. [auto, start, end, left, right, center, ...] | `box: text align last = "center" content = "The last line of a justified block is centered. It wraps over a few lines in a narrow box to show it." end` |

| `text justify`
چینش متن
text-justify | Where a justified line gets its extra space: `inter-word` (between words), `inter-character` (between letters), `auto` or `none`. It only matters when `text align` is `justify`. [auto, none, inter-word, inter-character] | `box: text align = "justify" text justify = "inter-character" width = 260 content = "Space is added between letters when the text is justified, which is how Chinese and Japanese are set." end` |

| `text indent`
تورفتگی متن
text-indent | The empty space before the first line of a block. A length or a percentage, and a negative number pushes the first line out, which together with padding makes a hanging indent. [length / percentage] | `box: text indent = "2em" content = "The first line of a paragraph starts two letters in. The rest of the lines do not move, so the paragraph reads like in a book." end` |

| `text transform`
تبدیل متن
text-transform | Changes the case of the shown letters without touching the text itself: `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize` (the first letter of each word) or `none`. Persian and Arabic have no case, so it does nothing to them. [none, uppercase, lowercase, capitalize] | `box: text transform = "uppercase" content = "shout in capitals" end` |

| `text decoration`
تزیین متن
text-decoration | The shorthand for line, style, colour and thickness of the lines drawn on text: `"underline wavy crimson"`. Links have an underline by default, and `"none"` removes it. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: text decoration = "underline wavy crimson" content = "A wavy red underline" end` |

| `text decoration line`
خط تزیین متن
text-decoration-line | Which lines are drawn: `underline`, `overline`, `line-through` or `none`. You can list several words in one string. [none, underline, overline, line-through; up to 3 values] | `box: text decoration line = "underline overline" content = "A line above and a line below" end` |

| `text decoration style`
سبک تزیین متن
text-decoration-style | The look of the line: `solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed` or `wavy`. It needs a decoration line to be visible. [solid, double, dotted, dashed, wavy] | `box: text decoration style = "dashed" content = "A dashed underline" end` |

| `text decoration color`
رنگ تزیین متن
text-decoration-color | The colour of the decoration line. Without it the line takes the colour of the text. [color] | `box: text decoration line = "underline" text decoration color = "crimson" content = "A crimson underline" end` |

| `text decoration thickness`
ضخامت تزیین متن
text-decoration-thickness | The thickness of the line: a length, a percentage of the font size, `auto` or `from-font`, which uses what the font recommends. [length / percentage / auto, from-font] | `box: text decoration line = "underline" text decoration thickness = 4 content = "A thick underline" end` |

| `text decoration skip ink`
پرش جوهر تزیین
text-decoration-skip-ink | Whether an underline or overline skips the parts of letters it would touch, such as the tail of a `g`. `auto` skips, `none` draws through them, and `all` skips for every script. [auto, none, all] | `box: text decoration line = "underline" text decoration skip ink = "none" content = "The line runs through gypsy and jumpy" end` |

| `text underline offset`
فاصله زیرخط
text-underline-offset | How far the underline sits from the baseline: a length, a percentage or `auto`. A bigger number moves it away from the letters. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: text decoration line = "underline" text underline offset = 8 content = "An underline moved down" end` |

| `text underline position`
جای زیرخط
text-underline-position | Where an underline goes: `auto`, `under` (below every descender) or, for vertical text, `left` and `right`. Useful for scripts with long descenders. [auto, under, left, right; up to 2 values] | `box: text decoration line = "underline" text underline position = "under" content = "The line sits below the lowest letters" end` |

| `text shadow`
سایه متن
text-shadow | One or more shadows, separated by commas. Each one is: horizontal offset, vertical offset, an optional blur and a colour, for example `"2px 2px 4px #94a3b8"`. Several shadows make glows and outlines. Keep enough contrast so the text stays readable. [comma list] | `box: text shadow = "2px 2px 4px #94a3b8" content = "A soft shadow" end` |

| `webkit text stroke`
خط دور متن
-webkit-text-stroke | Draws an outline around each letter: a width and a colour, such as `"1px #0f172a"`. Every current browser supports it under the `-webkit-` name. Combine it with a transparent fill colour for outlined text. [length and color, in either order] | `box: webkit text stroke = "1px #0f172a" webkit text fill color = "transparent" font size = 36 font weight = 700 content = "Outline" end` |

| `webkit text stroke width`
ضخامت خط دور متن
-webkit-text-stroke-width | The width of the outline only: a length or `thin`, `medium`, `thick`. A thick stroke eats into the letters, since it is centred on their edge. [length / thin / medium / thick] | `box: webkit text stroke width = 2 webkit text stroke color = "teal" font size = 36 font weight = 700 content = "Thick outline" end` |

| `webkit text stroke color`
رنگ خط دور متن
-webkit-text-stroke-color | The colour of the outline only. It needs a stroke width above zero to be seen. [color] | `box: webkit text stroke width = 1 webkit text stroke color = "crimson" font size = 36 font weight = 700 content = "Red outline" end` |

| `webkit text fill color`
رنگ پر متن
-webkit-text-fill-color | The colour that fills the letters. It beats `color` when both are set, and `transparent` lets the background or the stroke show through. [color] | `box: webkit text fill color = "#0f766e" content = "Filled with teal" end` |

| `text rendering`
نمایش متن
text-rendering | A hint about speed against quality: `auto`, `optimizeSpeed`, `optimizeLegibility` (kerning and ligatures on) or `geometricPrecision`. Browsers may ignore it. [auto, optimizeSpeed, optimizeLegibility, geometricPrecision] | `box: text rendering = "optimizeLegibility" content = "Optimised for reading" end` |

### Spacing and wrapping

These set the space between lines, letters and words, and decide where lines break or are cut.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `line height`
ارتفاع خط
line-height | The height of each line. A bare number (`1.6`) is multiplied by the font size of the element and is the best choice, because children inherit the number and not a fixed result. A length or a percentage gives a fixed height. Use about 1.5 for English and about 1.9 for Persian. [number / length / percentage / normal] | `box: line height = 1.7 width = 260 background = "#f1f5f9" content = "Lines that have room to breathe. A number is multiplied by the font size, so it follows the text when the size changes." end` |

| `letter spacing`
فاصله حروف
letter-spacing | Extra space between letters: a length, best in `em` so it grows with the text, or `normal`. A small positive value suits capitals and labels. Never use it on Persian or Arabic, whose letters join and must stay joined. [length / normal] | `box: letter spacing = "0.2em" text transform = "uppercase" content = "spaced capitals" end` |

| `word spacing`
فاصله واژه‌ها
word-spacing | Extra space between words: a length, a percentage or `normal`. A negative value pulls them closer. [length / percentage / normal] | `box: word spacing = "0.6em" content = "Words pushed apart a little" end` |

| `vertical align`
تراز عمودی متن
vertical-align | Where an inline element or a table cell sits vertically: `baseline`, `sub`, `super`, `top`, `middle`, `bottom`, `text-top`, `text-bottom`, or a length that raises (positive) or lowers (negative) it. It does not centre a box inside its parent. [length / percentage / baseline, sub, super, text-top, text-bottom, middle, ...] | `box: vertical align = "super" font size = 22 content = "x2 raised on the line" end` |

| `white space`
فضای سفید
white-space | How spaces and line breaks in the text are treated: `normal` merges them and wraps, `nowrap` never wraps, `pre` keeps everything and never wraps, `pre-wrap` keeps everything and wraps, `pre-line` keeps the line breaks only and `break-spaces` keeps spaces that can wrap. [normal, nowrap, pre, pre-wrap, pre-line, break-spaces] | `box: white space = "pre-line" width = 220 background = "#f1f5f9" content = "Breaks in the text\nare kept as they are\nin this box." end` |

| `white space collapse`
ادغام فضای سفید
white-space-collapse | Only the spaces half of `white space`: `collapse` (merge), `preserve` (keep all), `preserve-breaks` (keep line breaks, merge spaces), `preserve-spaces` and `break-spaces`. [collapse, preserve, preserve-breaks, preserve-spaces, break-spaces] | `box: white space collapse = "preserve-breaks" width = 220 background = "#f1f5f9" content = "Line breaks\nstay, extra    spaces go." end` |

| `word break`
شکستن واژه
word-break | Where a line may break inside words: `normal`, `break-all` (between any two letters), `keep-all` (never inside Chinese, Japanese and Korean words) or `break-word`. For ordinary text `overflow wrap` is the better tool. [normal, break-all, keep-all, break-word] | `box: word break = "break-all" width = 150 background = "#fef9c3" content = "Break-all cuts words anywhere" end` |

| `overflow wrap`
شکستن سرریز
overflow-wrap | Lets a word that is too long for the box break so it does not stick out. `normal` never breaks it, `break-word` breaks only if there is no other way, and `anywhere` does the same and also counts the break points when the box size is computed. [normal, break-word, anywhere] | `box: overflow wrap = "anywhere" width = 150 background = "#e0f2fe" content = "https://example.com/an/address/with/no/spaces" end` |

| `line break`
قاعده شکستن خط
line-break | How strict the rules are for where a line may break, mostly for Chinese and Japanese: `auto`, `loose`, `normal`, `strict` or `anywhere`. [auto, loose, normal, strict, anywhere] | `box: line break = "anywhere" width = 150 background = "#e0f2fe" content = "Strict rules or loose rules for where lines may break." end` |

| `hyphens`
خط تیره
hyphens | Whether a word may be split with a hyphen at the end of a line: `none`, `manual` (only at soft hyphens you write) or `auto` (the browser decides). `auto` needs a `lang` it has a dictionary for, and browsers do not hyphenate Persian. [none, manual, auto] | `box: hyphens = "auto" lang = "en" width = 160 background = "#dcfce7" content = "Hyphenation helps incomprehensibilities fit narrow columns." end` |

| `hyphenate character`
نویسه خط تیره
hyphenate-character | The character shown where a word is broken by hyphenation. `auto` uses the hyphen of the language, and a string such as `"~"` uses that instead. [string / auto] | `box: hyphens = "auto" hyphenate character = "\"~\"" lang = "en" width = 160 background = "#dcfce7" content = "Incomprehensibilities break with a tilde." end` |

| `hyphenate limit chars`
