# Layout: flow, flex and grid

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/css-layout/

Layout decides where each box goes: below the previous one, beside it, over it, or in a cell of a grid. In Salam you write the same CSS properties as plain names, and the compiler turns them into a stylesheet. This lesson goes from the normal flow to flexbox and grid and shows each idea with a page you can run.

## Normal flow

If you set nothing, the browser lays boxes out in the normal flow. A block box, such as a `box` or a `paragraph`, takes the full width of its parent and starts on a new line. An inline box, such as a `span` or a `link`, stays inside the line of text and is only as wide as its content. Width and height do not apply to inline boxes. `display = "inline-block"` is the middle way: it sits in the line like a word, but it has a width, a height and vertical margins like a block.

web-layout-flow.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Normal flow"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box: background = "#dbeafe" padding = 10 margin bottom = 8 content = "Block one takes the full width." end
    box: background = "#bfdbfe" padding = 10 margin bottom = 8 content = "Block two starts on a new line." end
    paragraph:
        content = "Inline items stay in the line: "
        span: background = "#fde68a" padding = "2 6" content = "one" end
        span: background = "#fcd34d" padding = "2 6" content = "two" end
        span: background = "#fbbf24" padding = "2 6" content = "three" end
    end
    box: display = "inline-block" width = 120 height = 50 background = "#bbf7d0" margin = 4 content = "inline-block" end
    box: display = "inline-block" width = 120 height = 50 background = "#86efac" margin = 4 content = "inline-block" end
end
```

Everything else in this lesson changes how boxes leave this flow. Most of the time you do not take boxes out of it. You set `display = flex` or `display = grid` on a parent, and the parent arranges its children.

Two things in the examples are worth knowing. `global: box sizing = "border-box"` makes `width` include padding and border, which is easier to reason about. And a bare number such as `padding = 10` means pixels; for another unit write a string, like `"2rem"` or `"50%"`.

## Position and the offsets

`position` chooses how a box is placed, and `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` (or the shorthand `inset`) say how far from which edge. The default is `static`: normal flow, and the offsets do nothing.

- `relative`: the box keeps its place and its space in the flow, and is then drawn shifted by the offsets. The other boxes do not notice.

- `absolute`: the box leaves the flow completely. It is placed against the nearest ancestor that is itself positioned (anything but `static`), or against the page if there is none.

- `fixed`: like absolute, but against the window, so it stays in place while the page scrolls. Use it for a bar that must always be visible.

- `sticky`: normal flow until the box would scroll past its offset, then it sticks there until its parent ends.

The usual pattern is a `relative` parent with `absolute` children: the parent is only there to be the reference. Below, the card is the reference for the badge and the bottom strip.

web-layout-position.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Relative and absolute"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        position = relative width = 280 height = 150 background = "#e0f2fe" border = "2px solid #0284c7"
        paragraph: margin = 12 margin inline end = 70 content = "The card is the positioned parent." end
        box: position = absolute top = 10 inset inline end = 10 background = "#dc2626" color = "white" padding = "4 10" border radius = 12 content = "New" end
        box: position = absolute bottom = 0 left = 0 right = 0 background = "#0369a1" color = "white" padding = 8 content = "Pinned to the bottom edge" end
    end
    paragraph: content = "Text after the card is not pushed by the absolute boxes." end
end
```

An absolute box with no positioned ancestor is placed against the whole page, which is rarely what you want. If a badge flies off to a corner of the window, give its parent `position = relative`.

Try the three values yourself. The blue box has `top = 30` and an offset from the start side. While it is `static` the offsets are ignored. With `relative` it moves but its space stays, so the green box does not move up. With `absolute` it leaves the flow: the green box moves up to take its place, and the blue box is measured from the dashed container.

web-layout-position-play.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Try every position"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 16 end
    box:
        display = flex gap = 8 margin bottom = 12
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("target"), "position", "static") end content = "static" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("target"), "position", "relative") end content = "relative" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("target"), "position", "absolute") end content = "absolute" end
    end
    box:
        position = relative height = 150 background = "#f1f5f9" border = "2px dashed #94a3b8" padding = 8
        box: background = "#fca5a5" width = 90 height = 36 content = "first" end
        box: id = "target" top = 30 inset inline start = 120 background = "#2563eb" color = "white" width = 90 height = 36 content = "target" end
        box: background = "#86efac" width = 90 height = 36 content = "third" end
    end
end
```

The offsets come in two families. `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` are physical: right is always the right of the screen. `inset inline start`, `inset inline end`, `inset block start` and `inset block end` are logical: they follow the writing direction, so the start is the left in English and the right in Persian. The two-value forms `inset inline` and `inset block` set both ends. Prefer the logical ones for anything that is about reading order, such as the badge above.

## Sticky and fixed

A sticky box needs an offset to know where to stick, usually `top = 0`. It sticks inside the nearest scrolling ancestor, and it can never leave its own parent, so a sticky heading is pushed away when the next section arrives. The box has a fixed `height` and `overflow = auto`, so it scrolls by itself. Scroll it: each heading stays at the top until the next one takes over.

web-layout-sticky.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Sticky headings"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 16 end
    box:
        height = 220 overflow = auto border = "2px solid #94a3b8"
        heading: size = 3 position = sticky top = 0 margin = 0 padding = 8 background = "#fde68a" content = "Fruit" end
        paragraph: padding = 8 content = "Apples, pears and plums. Scroll this box and watch the heading stay at the top." end
        paragraph: padding = 8 content = "Cherries and apricots in early summer." end
        paragraph: padding = 8 content = "Quinces and medlars in the autumn." end
        heading: size = 3 position = sticky top = 0 margin = 0 padding = 8 background = "#bbf7d0" content = "Vegetables" end
        paragraph: padding = 8 content = "Carrots, leeks and beetroot keep well in a cool cellar." end
        paragraph: padding = 8 content = "Spinach and lettuce grow fast but do not last." end
        paragraph: padding = 8 content = "Potatoes and onions can be stored for months." end
    end
end
```

`fixed` works like this too, but against the window and without the parent limit. Give a fixed bar `top = 0 left = 0 right = 0` and it spans the window. Because it leaves the flow, the content below it starts under the bar, so add the bar's height as padding at the top of the page.

## Stacking and z index

When positioned boxes overlap, the one that comes later in the code is drawn on top. `z index` changes that: a bigger whole number is drawn above a smaller one, and a negative number goes behind. It applies to positioned boxes and to flex and grid items.

web-layout-zindex.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Stacking order"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        position = relative height = 180
        box: position = absolute top = 60 left = 120 width = 150 height = 110 background = "#86efac" z index = 3 padding = 8 font size = 28 content = "3" end
        box: position = absolute top = 0 left = 0 width = 150 height = 110 background = "#fca5a5" z index = 1 padding = 8 font size = 28 content = "1" end
        box: position = absolute top = 30 left = 60 width = 150 height = 110 background = "#93c5fd" z index = 2 padding = 8 font size = 28 content = "2" end
    end
    paragraph: content = "The box with the biggest z index is painted on top, whatever the order in the code." end
end
```

A few boxes create their own stacking context, a group that is ordered as one block: a positioned box with a `z index`, an element with `opacity` below 1, or one with a `transform`. Inside a context the numbers only compete with each other. This is why a menu with `z index = 9999` can still hide behind a box that has `z index = 2`: they are in different contexts. When a number seems to do nothing, look for a parent that made a context.

## Float and clear

A floated box leaves the line and moves to one side, and the text that follows wraps around it. That is its job today: a picture or a pull quote inside text. Pages were once built with floats, but flexbox and grid replaced that. `clear` makes a box start below the floats instead of beside them. The value `inline-start` follows the text direction, so the example works in both languages.

web-layout-float.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Text wrapping around a box"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 max width = 480 line height = 1.5 end
    box: float = inline-start width = 110 height = 90 margin = "4 0 6" margin inline end = 14 background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "Floated" end
    paragraph: content = "A floated box leaves the normal flow on one side, and the lines of text that follow flow around it. This is how a picture sits inside a paragraph in a magazine. Keep going until the text is longer than the box and it wraps underneath." end
    box: clear = both background = "#e2e8f0" padding = 8 content = "clear = both: this box starts below the float." end
end
```

A float is ignored on a flex or grid item. If the parent of a float is shorter than the float, the parent does not grow to hold it. Put a `clear = both` element after it, or make the parent `display = "flow-root"`.

## Flexbox: items in a line

Set `display = flex` on a parent and its children become flex items, laid out along one line called the main axis. The other direction is the cross axis. `flex direction` chooses the main axis: `row` (the default, along the text direction), `column`, or their `-reverse` forms. Two properties place the items:

- `justify content` spreads the items along the main axis: `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`.

- `align items` places them across the cross axis: `stretch` (the default, so items are as tall as the line), `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `baseline`.

Together they give the shortest way to center a box, both ways:

web-layout-center.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Centering"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = flex justify content = center align items = center height = 180 background = "#ede9fe" border radius = 12
        box: background = "#7c3aed" color = "white" padding = "14 26" border radius = 8 content = "Centered both ways" end
    end
end
```

The playground below changes the two properties and the direction with buttons. Notice how the meaning of justify and align swaps when you choose `column`: justify is always the main axis, whichever way it points.

web-layout-flex-play.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Flex playground"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 16 end
    box:
        display = flex flex wrap = wrap gap = 6 margin bottom = 12
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "flex-direction", "row") end content = "row" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "flex-direction", "column") end content = "column" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "justify-content", "flex-start") end content = "start" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "justify-content", "center") end content = "center" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "justify-content", "space-between") end content = "space-between" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "align-items", "flex-start") end content = "items start" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "align-items", "center") end content = "items center" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("row"), "align-items", "flex-end") end content = "items end" end
    end
    box:
        id = "row" display = flex align items = flex-start gap = 8 height = 170 background = "#f1f5f9" border = "2px solid #94a3b8" padding = 8
        box: background = "#f87171" padding = 10 content = "1" end
        box: background = "#60a5fa" padding = "20 10" content = "2" end
        box: background = "#4ade80" padding = "30 10" content = "3" end
    end
end
```

`gap` puts space between items without margins on the items. One value is used both ways, two values are the row gap then the column gap. `row gap` and `column gap` set them one at a time. `flex wrap = wrap` lets items move to a new line when they do not fit, and `flex flow` sets direction and wrap together, as in `"row wrap"`. When there is more than one line, `align content` distributes the lines in the container.

## How flex items get their size

Each flex item starts from its `flex basis` (its width in a row, when the basis is `auto`), then the free space is shared out. `flex grow` says how many shares of the extra space the item takes, and `flex shrink` how much of a shortage it absorbs when the items do not fit. The shorthand `flex` sets all three: `flex = 1` means "grow equally, starting from nothing", and `flex = "0 0 120px"` is a fixed 120 pixel item. Prefer the shorthand, because it resets the parts you did not write to sensible values.

web-layout-flex-sizes.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Grow, shrink and basis"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    paragraph: margin = "0 0 6" content = "flex grow 1, 2 and 1" end
    box:
        display = flex gap = 8 margin bottom = 16
        box: flex grow = 1 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 10 content = "1" end
        box: flex grow = 2 background = "#93c5fd" padding = 10 content = "2" end
        box: flex grow = 1 background = "#86efac" padding = 10 content = "1" end
    end
    paragraph: margin = "0 0 6" content = "fixed 120 pixel box, then flex = 1" end
    box:
        display = flex gap = 8
        box: flex = "0 0 120px" background = "#fcd34d" padding = 10 content = "fixed" end
        box: flex = 1 background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 10 content = "takes the rest" end
    end
end
```

Two properties work on a single item. `align self` overrides `align items` for that item. `order` changes where it is drawn: items are sorted by their order number, the lowest first, and items with equal numbers stay in code order.

web-layout-flex-order.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Order and align self"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = flex gap = 8 height = 130 background = "#f1f5f9" align items = flex-start padding = 8
        box: order = 3 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 12 content = "order 3" end
        box: order = 1 background = "#93c5fd" padding = 12 content = "order 1" end
        box: order = 2 align self = flex-end background = "#86efac" padding = 12 content = "order 2, self end" end
        box: align self = center background = "#fcd34d" padding = 12 content = "self center" end
    end
end
```

`order` only changes what people see. Screen readers and the Tab key still follow the order of the code. Use it for small visual adjustments and write the content in its real reading order.

## Flexbox recipes

Four layouts you will write again and again. A navigation bar: a flex row, and an `auto` margin on the end of the first item that pushes the rest away. The auto margin takes all the free space, and `margin inline end` follows the text direction.

web-layout-navbar.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Navigation bar"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 0 end
    nav:
        display = flex align items = center gap = 20 background = "#0f172a" color = "white" padding = "0 20" height = 56
        span: font weight = 700 font size = 18 margin inline end = auto content = "Bakery" end
        link: url = "#" color = "white" content = "Bread" end
        link: url = "#" color = "white" content = "Cakes" end
        link: url = "#" color = "white" content = "Contact" end
        button: background = "#f59e0b" border = "none" padding = "8 14" border radius = 6 content = "Order" end
    end
    paragraph: padding = 20 content = "The auto margin on the name takes all the free space, so everything after it moves to the end." end
end
```

A sidebar with content: the sidebar has a fixed basis and does not grow, the content takes whatever is left.

web-layout-sidebar.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Sidebar and content"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 0 end
    box:
        display = flex min height = 260
        aside: flex = "0 0 160px" background = "#1e293b" color = "white" padding = 16
            heading: size = 3 margin = "0 0 8" content = "Menu" end
            paragraph: content = "Inbox" end
            paragraph: content = "Sent" end
            paragraph: content = "Drafts" end
        end
        main: flex = 1 padding = 20 background = "#f8fafc"
            heading: size = 2 margin = "0 0 8" content = "Inbox" end
            paragraph: content = "The sidebar keeps 160 pixels. The content takes the rest and grows or shrinks with the window." end
        end
    end
end
```

Cards that wrap: every card has `flex = "1 1 160px"`, which says "I would like 160 pixels, but I will grow and shrink". On a wide screen five cards fit in a line, on a phone one per line, with no media query. The last line stretches; if you prefer it not to, use grid below.

web-layout-cards-wrap.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Cards that wrap"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = flex flex wrap = wrap gap = 12
        box: flex = "1 1 160px" background = "#fecaca" padding = 16 border radius = 8 content = "Card one" end
        box: flex = "1 1 160px" background = "#fed7aa" padding = 16 border radius = 8 content = "Card two" end
        box: flex = "1 1 160px" background = "#fde68a" padding = 16 border radius = 8 content = "Card three" end
        box: flex = "1 1 160px" background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 16 border radius = 8 content = "Card four" end
        box: flex = "1 1 160px" background = "#bae6fd" padding = 16 border radius = 8 content = "Card five" end
    end
end
```

A footer at the bottom of a short page: the page is a column with at least the window's height, and the main part grows to fill it.

web-layout-footer.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Sticky footer"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 0 end
    box:
        display = flex flex direction = column min height = "100vh"
        header: background = "#0f766e" color = "white" padding = 14 content = "Header" end
        main: flex = 1 padding = 16 content = "The page is short, yet the footer stays at the bottom." end
        footer: background = "#134e4a" color = "white" padding = 14 content = "Footer" end
    end
end
```

## Grid: rows and columns together

Flexbox lays out one line at a time. Grid lays out both directions at once. Set `display = grid` and describe the columns with `grid template columns`, with one size for each column. Sizes can be lengths, percentages, `auto`, and the unit `fr`, a fraction of the free space: `"1fr 2fr"` makes the second column twice as wide as the first. `repeat(3, 1fr)` is three equal columns. Rows are made as needed, and `grid template rows` and `grid auto rows` size them. `gap`, `row gap` and `column gap` work as in flexbox.

web-layout-grid.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Grid columns"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = grid grid template columns = "100px 1fr 2fr" grid auto rows = 60 gap = 10
        box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "100px" end
        box: background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "1fr" end
        box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "2fr" end
        box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "4" end
        box: background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 8 content = "5" end
        box: background = "#f9a8d4" padding = 8 content = "6" end
    end
end
```

Change the columns in the next page and watch the same five boxes rearrange. The last button is the most useful grid line you will learn:

web-layout-grid-play.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Change the columns"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 16 end
    box:
        display = flex flex wrap = wrap gap = 6 margin bottom = 10
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("grid"), "grid-template-columns", "1fr 1fr 1fr") dom.SetText(dom.ById("code"), "1fr 1fr 1fr") end content = "three equal" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("grid"), "grid-template-columns", "1fr 3fr") dom.SetText(dom.ById("code"), "1fr 3fr") end content = "1fr 3fr" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("grid"), "grid-template-columns", "80px 1fr 80px") dom.SetText(dom.ById("code"), "80px 1fr 80px") end content = "fixed sides" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("grid"), "grid-template-columns", "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(90px, 1fr))") dom.SetText(dom.ById("code"), "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(90px, 1fr))") end content = "auto-fit" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "code" font family = monospace margin = "0 0 10" content = "1fr 1fr 1fr" end
    box:
        id = "grid" display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr 1fr" gap = 8
        box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 14 content = "A" end
        box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 14 content = "B" end
        box: background = "#86efac" padding = 14 content = "C" end
        box: background = "#fcd34d" padding = 14 content = "D" end
        box: background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 14 content = "E" end
    end
end
```

`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(90px, 1fr))` reads "make as many columns as fit, each at least 90 pixels, and share the leftover space". `minmax(a, b)` gives a size between two limits. With `auto-fit` the empty columns shrink to nothing, so the real ones stretch. With `auto-fill` they stay and keep their width. A card grid built this way adapts to every screen with no media queries:

web-layout-autofit.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Responsive card grid"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(140px, 1fr))" gap = 12
        box: background = "#fecaca" padding = 24 border radius = 8 content = "One" end
        box: background = "#fed7aa" padding = 24 border radius = 8 content = "Two" end
        box: background = "#fde68a" padding = 24 border radius = 8 content = "Three" end
        box: background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 24 border radius = 8 content = "Four" end
        box: background = "#bae6fd" padding = 24 border radius = 8 content = "Five" end
        box: background = "#ddd6fe" padding = 24 border radius = 8 content = "Six" end
    end
end
```

## Placing items: lines, spans and areas

Grid lines are numbered from 1: a grid with three columns has four vertical lines, and `-1` is the last one. `grid column` and `grid row` place an item between two lines: `"1 / 3"` is from line 1 to line 3, which is two columns, and `"span 2"` means two tracks wide from wherever the item lands. `grid column start`, `grid column end`, `grid row start` and `grid row end` set the ends one by one. When items of different sizes leave holes, `grid auto flow = "row dense"` back-fills them, at the price of an order that no longer matches the code.

web-layout-grid-span.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Spanning cells"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(4, 1fr)" grid auto rows = 56 gap = 8
        box: grid column = "1 / 3" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "columns 1 to 2" end
        box: grid row = "span 2" background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "two rows" end
        box: grid column start = 4 background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "column 4" end
        box: background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "auto" end
        box: grid column = "span 2" background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 8 content = "span 2" end
        box: background = "#f9a8d4" padding = 8 content = "auto" end
    end
end
```

For a whole page, name the cells instead. `grid template areas` takes one string that draws the layout, one quoted name for each cell of each row; repeating a name merges cells. Then every child says where it goes with `grid area`. In Salam the string goes in backticks, on a single line, so the quotes inside need no escaping.

web-layout-grid-areas.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Page with named areas"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 0 end
    box:
        display = grid grid template columns = "150px 1fr" grid template rows = "50px 1fr 40px" grid template areas = `"top top" "side main" "foot foot"` gap = 6 height = 280 padding = 6
        header: grid area = top background = "#0f766e" color = "white" padding = 12 content = "top" end
        aside: grid area = side background = "#99f6e4" padding = 12 content = "side" end
        main: grid area = main background = "#ccfbf1" padding = 12 content = "main" end
        footer: grid area = foot background = "#134e4a" color = "white" padding = 10 content = "foot" end
    end
end
```

`grid template` is the shorthand for rows, columns and areas together: ``"top top" 50px "side main" 1fr / 150px 1fr``. The areas and the row sizes are written together, then a slash, then the column sizes. `grid` is the longest shorthand; it also sets the automatic tracks and the flow, as in `"auto-flow 60px / 1fr 2fr"`. Beginners do well with the long names; the shorthands are for reading other people's code.

Notice that the page layout above needs no wrapper boxes and no floats, and that moving the sidebar to the other side means editing one string.

## Alignment in flex and grid

The same few words appear everywhere, and a rule makes them easy: justify works along the inline axis (the way text runs), align along the block axis (the way paragraphs stack), content positions the whole set of tracks or lines inside the container, items aligns all the items inside their cells, and self does that for one item. place sets align and justify together. In flexbox `justify` always means the main axis and `align` the cross axis, and `justify items` and `justify self` do not apply to flex items.

The values are `start`, `end`, `center`, `stretch` and, for content, the three `space-` forms. The word `end` also closes an element in Salam, so write `"end"` in quotes when it is a value. The page below shows items inside grid cells, with `place items` on the container and a different alignment on some items.

web-layout-grid-align.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Aligning inside cells"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(3, 1fr)" grid auto rows = 90 gap = 8 place items = center border = "2px dashed #94a3b8" padding = 8
        box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "center" end
        box: justify self = start background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "start" end
        box: justify self = "end" background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "end" end
        box: align self = start background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "top" end
        box: align self = stretch justify self = stretch background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 8 content = "stretch" end
        box: place self = "end" background = "#f9a8d4" padding = 8 content = "place self" end
    end
end
```

## Multi-column text

A long paragraph is hard to read when the lines are very wide. `columns` splits the content of a box into newspaper columns that fill one after the other. Set `column count` for a fixed number, or `column width` for an ideal width and let the browser decide how many fit. `columns = "10rem 3"` says both: at least 10rem wide, at most 3 columns. `column gap` is the space between them and `column rule` draws a line in the middle of the gap, written like a border; its parts are `column rule width`, `column rule style` and `column rule color`, and the style must be set or nothing shows.

web-layout-columns.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Newspaper columns"
    global: box sizing = "border-box" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "Georgia, serif" margin = 20 end
    box:
        columns = "10rem 3" column gap = 28 column rule = "1px solid #94a3b8" line height = 1.5
        heading: size = 2 column span = all margin = "0 0 10" content = "Harbour news" end
        paragraph: margin = "0 0 10" content = "The ferry returned to its summer timetable on Monday after a month of repairs. Passengers filled every seat on the first crossing." end
        paragraph: margin = "0 0 10" content = "Fishermen report a good catch of herring, and the market opened an hour early to cope with the demand." end
        paragraph: break inside = avoid margin = "0 0 10" content = "The lighthouse keeper will give a talk on Saturday about the history of the harbour. Entry is free." end
        paragraph: margin = "0 0 10" content = "Rain is expected on Sunday, clearing by the evening." end
    end
end
```

A child with `column span = all` stretches across all the columns, like the heading above. `column fill` chooses between balanced columns (the default) and filling one column to the box's height before starting the next. The `break` properties control where a column may end: `break inside = avoid` keeps a card in one piece, `break after = avoid` keeps a heading with the paragraph that follows it, and `break before = column` forces a new column. The same properties decide page breaks when the page is printed.

A single number as the value of `columns` is read as pixels, so `columns = "3"` does not mean three columns. Write `column count = 3` for a count.

## Right-to-left pages

Flexbox and grid follow the page direction by themselves. In a Persian page a row starts at the right, the first column of a grid is the right one, and `flex-start` and `start` mean the right edge. The same code gives the mirror image of the English page, which is what a Persian reader expects. You do not have to change anything.

The trap is in the physical names: `left`, `right`, `margin left`, `float = left` and `text align = left` never flip. Wherever the side is about reading order (a badge at the end of a line, a gap after an icon, text that wraps around a picture), use the logical names: `inset inline start` and `end`, `margin inline start` and `end`, `float = inline-start`, `text align = start`. This lesson's examples already do. Use `left` and `right` only when you mean the screen, as for a shadow that falls to the right.

## Reference: every layout property

Each property below has an example the compiler checked, so you can paste it inside a `page:` block. The accepted values are listed in brackets. Many examples place a coloured box on a grey one, so the preview of your own page shows what the property did. Persian names work in any file, and the Persian lessons use them.

### Position and the offsets

Placement of a box, the distance from its edges, and the stacking order.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position`
موقعیت
position | How the element is placed. `static` (the default) is normal flow. `relative` keeps its place in the flow and can be nudged with the offsets. `absolute` leaves the flow and is placed against the nearest positioned ancestor. `fixed` is placed against the window and stays when the page scrolls. `sticky` scrolls like normal until it reaches its offset, then sticks. [static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky] | `box: position = relative top = 10 left = 20 background = "#bfdbfe" padding = 12 content = "Moved 10 down and 20 right" end` |

| `top`
بالا
top | Distance from the top edge of the reference box: the element's own place for `relative`, the nearest positioned ancestor for `absolute`, the window for `fixed`. A number is pixels. Percentages and `auto` work. It does nothing on a `static` element. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 8 left = 8 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "8 px from the top" end
end` |

| `right`
راست
right | Distance from the right edge of the reference box, with the same rules as `top`. It is a physical side: it does not flip in a right-to-left page. Use `inset inline end` when the side should follow the text direction. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 8 right = 8 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "8 px from the right" end
end` |

| `bottom`
پایین
bottom | Distance from the bottom edge of the reference box, with the same rules as `top`. Together with `top` on an element that has no height, it stretches the element between the two edges. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute bottom = 0 left = 0 right = 0 background = "#93c5fd" padding = 6 content = "A strip on the bottom edge" end
end` |

| `left`
چپ
left | Distance from the left edge of the reference box, with the same rules as `top`. It is a physical side. Opposing offsets such as `left` and `right` together stretch an absolute element across its parent. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 8 left = 24 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "24 px from the left" end
end` |

| `inset`
فاصله از لبه
inset | Shorthand for `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` in one value, with up to four values in the same order as `margin`. `inset = 0` makes an absolute box cover its whole reference box. [length / percentage / auto; up to 4 values] | `box: position = relative height = 80 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute inset = "10 40" background = "#86efac" content = "10 px above and below, 40 px at the sides" end
end` |

| `inset block`
فاصله از لبه بلوکی
inset-block | Logical offsets for the block axis (top and bottom in horizontal writing) in one property, with one or two values: the start side, then the end side. [length / percentage / auto; up to 2 values] | `box: position = relative height = 90 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute inset block = "10 30" background = "#86efac" content = "10 px from the start, 30 px from the end" end
end` |

| `inset block start`
فاصله از لبه بلوکی آغاز
inset-block-start | The offset from the start edge of the block axis, which is the top in ordinary horizontal text. It is the logical form of `top`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute inset block start = 12 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "12 px from the block start" end
end` |

| `inset block end`
فاصله از لبه بلوکی انتها
inset-block-end | The offset from the end edge of the block axis, which is the bottom in ordinary horizontal text. It is the logical form of `bottom`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute inset block end = 12 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "12 px from the block end" end
end` |

| `inset inline`
فاصله از لبه خطی
inset-inline | Logical offsets for the inline axis (the direction the text runs) in one property, with one or two values: the start side, then the end side. In an English page start is the left, in a Persian page it is the right. [length / percentage / auto; up to 2 values] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 10 inset inline = "20 60" background = "#86efac" padding = 6 content = "20 px at the start, 60 px at the end" end
end` |

| `inset inline start`
فاصله از لبه خطی آغاز
inset-inline-start | The offset from the start edge of the inline axis: the left edge in a left-to-right page and the right edge in a right-to-left page. It is the logical form of `left`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 10 inset inline start = 16 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "16 px from the start" end
end` |

| `inset inline end`
فاصله از لبه خطی انتها
inset-inline-end | The offset from the end edge of the inline axis: the right edge in a left-to-right page and the left edge in a right-to-left page. It is the logical form of `right`, and the right choice for a badge in the corner of a card. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 70 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 10 inset inline end = 16 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "16 px from the end" end
end` |

| `z index`
ترتیب لایه
z-index | The stacking order of overlapping elements, as a whole number. A higher number is painted on top, a negative number goes behind. It works on positioned elements and on flex and grid items. `auto` is the default. [integer / auto] | `box: position = relative height = 90 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: position = absolute top = 0 left = 0 width = 90 height = 60 background = "#fca5a5" z index = 2 content = "on top" end
box: position = absolute top = 20 left = 40 width = 90 height = 60 background = "#93c5fd" z index = 1 end
end` |

### Float

Wrapping text around a box.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `float`
شناوری
float | Takes the element out of the normal line and pushes it to one side so the text wraps around it. Values: `left`, `right`, `inline-start`, `inline-end` and `none`. Use it to put a picture inside a paragraph, not to lay out a page. [left, right, none, inline-start, inline-end] | `box: float = inline-end width = 80 height = 60 background = "#fcd34d" margin = 6 content = "Floated" end
paragraph: content = "The text wraps around the floated box on its side and carries on beneath it when the box ends." end` |

| `clear`
پاک‌سازی شناوری
clear | Makes the element start below floated boxes instead of wrapping beside them. Values: `left`, `right`, `both` (both sides, the usual choice), `inline-start`, `inline-end` and `none`. [left, right, both, none, inline-start, inline-end] | `box: clear = both background = "#e2e8f0" padding = 8 content = "I start below any floated box" end` |

### Flexbox

Direction, wrapping and sizing of flex items. Put `display = flex` on the parent.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flex`
فلکس
flex | Shorthand for `flex grow`, `flex shrink` and `flex basis` of a flex item. One number such as `1` means "grow equally from zero". `"0 0 160px"` is a fixed 160 pixel item. The keywords `auto` (`1 1 auto`) and `none` (`0 0 auto`) are also accepted. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: display = flex gap = 8
box: flex = "0 0 100px" background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "fixed" end
box: flex = 1 background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 8 content = "takes the rest" end
end` |

| `flex direction`
جهت فلکس
flex-direction | The direction of the main axis of a flex container. `row` (default) goes along the text direction, `column` goes top to bottom, and `row-reverse` and `column-reverse` run the opposite way. [row, row-reverse, column, column-reverse] | `box: display = flex flex direction = column gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "first" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "second" end
end` |

| `flex wrap`
پیچش آرایش
flex-wrap | Whether flex items stay on one line or move to a new line when they do not fit. `nowrap` (default) squeezes them, `wrap` adds lines, and `wrap-reverse` adds them upwards. [nowrap, wrap, wrap-reverse] | `box: display = flex flex wrap = wrap gap = 6 width = 220
box: width = 90 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "one" end
box: width = 90 background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "two" end
box: width = 90 background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "three" end
end` |

| `flex flow`
جریان فلکس
flex-flow | Shorthand for `flex direction` and `flex wrap` in one value, for example `"column wrap"`. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: display = flex flex flow = "row wrap" gap = 6 width = 220
box: width = 90 background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "a" end
box: width = 90 background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 content = "b" end
box: width = 90 background = "#bae6fd" padding = 8 content = "c" end
end` |

| `flex grow`
رشد فلکس
flex-grow | How much of the free space in the line this item takes, as a share compared with the other items. The default is 0 (do not grow). Items with 1, 2 and 1 split the free space in the ratio 1 to 2 to 1. [number] | `box: display = flex gap = 6
box: flex grow = 1 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "1" end
box: flex grow = 3 background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "3" end
end` |

| `flex shrink`
جمع‌شدن فلکس
flex-shrink | How much this item gives up when the items together are wider than the container. The default is 1. With `0` the item keeps its size and may overflow. [number] | `box: display = flex width = 240
box: flex shrink = 0 width = 160 background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "never shrinks" end
box: width = 160 background = "#c4b5fd" padding = 8 content = "shrinks" end
end` |

| `flex basis`
پایه فلکس
flex-basis | The starting size of the item along the main axis, before growing or shrinking. It takes a length, a percentage, `auto` (use the width) or `content`. [length / percentage / auto, content, min-content, max-content, fit-content] | `box: display = flex gap = 6
box: flex basis = 120 background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "basis 120" end
box: flex basis = "30%" background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 8 content = "basis 30%" end
end` |

| `order`
ترتیب نمایش
order | The visual position of a flex or grid item, as a whole number. Items are drawn from the lowest to the highest, and items with the same number keep the order of the code. The default is 0. Keyboard focus still follows the code, so do not use it to reorder content that matters. [integer] | `box: display = flex gap = 6
box: order = 2 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "A (order 2)" end
box: order = 1 background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "B (order 1)" end
end` |

### Alignment and gaps

Most of these work in both flexbox and grid. `justify items` and `justify self` are for grid only.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `justify content`
چینش
justify-content | Places the items along the main axis (the inline axis in a grid) when there is free space. Values: `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between` (equal gaps, no space at the ends), `space-around`, `space-evenly` and `stretch`. [normal, start, end, center, flex-start, flex-end, ...] | `box: display = flex justify content = space-between background = "#e2e8f0" padding = 8
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "first" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "middle" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "last" end
end` |

| `align items`
ترازعمودی
align-items | Places the items across the cross axis of a flex container (and the block axis in a grid). `stretch` is the default and makes items fill the line. `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center` and `baseline` align them without stretching. [normal, stretch, center, start, end, flex-start, ...] | `box: display = flex align items = center height = 90 background = "#e2e8f0" gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = "6 10" content = "short" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = "24 10" content = "tall" end
end` |

| `align content`
محتوا تراز
align-content | Distributes the lines of a container that has more than one line (a wrapping flex box, a grid taller than its rows) along the cross axis. It has no effect on a single line. Values are like `justify content`: `flex-start`, `center`, `space-between` and so on. [normal, start, end, center, flex-start, flex-end, ...] | `box: display = flex flex wrap = wrap align content = flex-start height = 120 width = 200 background = "#e2e8f0" gap = 6
box: width = 90 height = 30 background = "#fca5a5" content = "a" end
box: width = 90 height = 30 background = "#93c5fd" content = "b" end
box: width = 90 height = 30 background = "#86efac" content = "c" end
end` |

| `align self`
خود تراز
align-self | Overrides `align items` for one item. `auto` (default) follows the container. The other values are `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `stretch` and `baseline`. [auto, normal, stretch, center, start, end, ...] | `box: display = flex height = 90 background = "#e2e8f0" gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "default" end
box: align self = flex-end background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "self at the end" end
end` |

| `justify items`
موارد چینش
justify-items | In a grid, aligns every item along the inline axis inside its own cell. `stretch` (the default for grid) fills the cell, and `start`, `end` and `center` shrink the item and place it. It has no effect in a flex container. [normal, stretch, center, start, end, flex-start, ...] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" justify items = center gap = 6 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "centered" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "in its cell" end
end` |

| `justify self`
خود چینش
justify-self | In a grid, aligns one item along the inline axis inside its cell and overrides `justify items`. Values: `auto`, `start`, `end`, `center` and `stretch`. [auto, normal, stretch, center, start, end, ...] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" gap = 6 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: justify self = "end" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "end of its cell" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "default" end
end` |

| `place content`
محتوا جای‌گذاری
place-content | Shorthand for `align content` and then `justify content`. One value sets both. It positions the whole set of tracks or lines inside the container. [normal, stretch, center, start, end, flex-start, ...; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid place content = center height = 100 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 10 content = "in the middle" end
end` |

| `place items`
موارد جای‌گذاری
place-items | Shorthand for `align items` and then `justify items`. One value sets both, so `place items = center` centres every item in its cell. [normal, stretch, center, start, end, flex-start, ...; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" grid auto rows = 70 place items = center gap = 6 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "one" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "two" end
end` |

| `place self`
خود جای‌گذاری
place-self | Shorthand for `align self` and then `justify self` of one grid item. One value sets both. [auto, normal, stretch, center, start, end, ...; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" grid auto rows = 70 gap = 6 background = "#e2e8f0"
box: place self = center background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "centered" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" content = "fills its cell" end
end` |

| `gap`
شکاف
gap | The space between the items of a flex or grid container (and between columns of a multi-column box). One value is used both ways; two values are the row gap, then the column gap, as in `"8 16"`. A number is pixels. [length / percentage / normal; up to 2 values] | `box: display = flex gap = "8 20" flex wrap = wrap width = 200
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "one" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "two" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "three" end
end` |

| `row gap`
شکاف ردیف
row-gap | The space between rows only, in a grid or a wrapping flex container. Together with `column gap` it is the long form of `gap`. [length / percentage / normal] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" row gap = 20
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "a" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "b" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "c" end
box: background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "d" end
end` |

### Grid

Tracks, areas and the placement of items. Put `display = grid` on the parent.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grid`
شبکه
grid | The grid shorthand. It sets the row and column tracks in one value, for example `"auto-flow / 1fr 1fr"` (rows are created as needed, two equal columns), or like `grid template` with areas and a slash between the rows and the columns. [track lists, area strings, auto-flow/dense; up to one /] | `box: display = grid grid = "auto-flow 60px / 1fr 2fr" gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "narrow" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "wide" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "narrow" end
box: background = "#fcd34d" padding = 8 content = "wide" end
end` |

| `grid template`
الگو شبکه
grid-template | Shorthand for `grid template rows`, `grid template columns` and `grid template areas`. Write the area strings with a size after each one, then a slash and the column sizes. [area strings, track sizes and line names; up to one /] | `box: display = grid grid template = `"title title" 40px "menu body" 60px / 90px 1fr` gap = 6
box: grid area = title background = "#fca5a5" content = "title" end
box: grid area = menu background = "#93c5fd" content = "menu" end
box: grid area = body background = "#86efac" content = "body" end
end` |

| `grid template columns`
ستون های شبکه
grid-template-columns | The sizes of the columns, one value per column. A length, a percentage, a fraction such as `1fr` (one share of the free space), `auto`, and the functions `repeat(3, 1fr)` and `minmax(120px, 1fr)`. A bare number means pixels. [length / percentage / fraction; up to 999 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "80px 1fr 2fr" gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "80px" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "1fr" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "2fr" end
end` |

| `grid template rows`
ردیف‌ها الگو شبکه
grid-template-rows | The heights of the rows, written like the columns. Rows that are not listed are created on demand and sized by `grid auto rows`. [length / percentage / fraction; up to 999 values] | `box: display = grid grid template rows = "40px 1fr" height = 120 gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" content = "40px" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" content = "the rest" end
end` |

| `grid template areas`
نواحی الگو شبکه
grid-template-areas | Names the cells of the grid. Write one string with a quoted row for each row of the grid, each holding one name per column. Use backticks around it so the inner quotes need no escape, keep it on a single line, and repeat a name to join cells. A dot (`.`) leaves a cell empty. Items choose their place with `grid area`. [string; up to 99 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "70px 1fr" grid template areas = `"head head" "nav main"` gap = 6
box: grid area = head background = "#fca5a5" padding = 6 content = "head" end
box: grid area = nav background = "#93c5fd" padding = 6 content = "nav" end
box: grid area = main background = "#86efac" padding = 6 content = "main" end
end` |

| `grid auto flow`
جریان خودکار شبکه
grid-auto-flow | How items that have no place of their own are put into the grid. `row` (default) fills row by row, `column` fills column by column, and `dense` backfills holes left by larger items, even if that changes the visual order. [row, column, dense; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(3, 1fr)" grid auto flow = "row dense" gap = 6
box: grid column = "span 2" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "wide" end
box: grid column = "span 2" background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "wide" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "fills the hole" end
end` |

| `grid auto columns`
ستون‌های خودکار شبکه
grid-auto-columns | The size of columns that are created automatically, for items placed outside the columns listed in `grid template columns` or with `grid auto flow = column`. [length / percentage / fraction; up to 99 values] | `box: display = grid grid auto flow = column grid auto columns = 70 gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "a" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "b" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "c" end
end` |

| `grid auto rows`
ردیف‌های خودکار شبکه
grid-auto-rows | The size of rows that are created automatically. `minmax(60px, auto)` gives each row at least 60 pixels and lets it grow with its content. [length / percentage / fraction; up to 99 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" grid auto rows = "minmax(50px, auto)" gap = 6
box: background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "a" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "b" end
box: background = "#86efac" padding = 8 content = "c" end
end` |

| `grid column`
ستون شبکه
grid-column | Shorthand for `grid column start` and `grid column end`, written with a slash: `"1 / 3"` goes from line 1 to line 3 (two columns). `"span 2"` takes two columns from where the item falls. `"1 / -1"` goes all the way across. [integer / name; up to 3 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(3, 1fr)" gap = 6
box: grid column = "1 / 3" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "lines 1 to 3" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" padding = 8 content = "one" end
end` |

| `grid column start`
آغاز ستون شبکه
grid-column-start | The grid line where the item starts in the column direction. Lines are counted from 1, the left edge of the first column in a left-to-right page. Take a number, a name, or `span 2`. [integer / name / auto, span; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(3, 1fr)" gap = 6
box: grid column start = 2 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "starts at line 2" end
end` |

| `grid column end`
انتهای ستون شبکه
grid-column-end | The grid line where the item ends in the column direction. `"span 2"` means "two columns past the start", and `-1` is the last line. [integer / name / auto, span; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(3, 1fr)" gap = 6
box: grid column end = "span 2" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "two columns" end
end` |

| `grid row`
ردیف شبکه
grid-row | Shorthand for `grid row start` and `grid row end`, like `grid column`: `"span 2"` makes the item two rows tall. [integer / name; up to 3 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" grid auto rows = 40 gap = 6
box: grid row = "span 2" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "two rows tall" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" content = "b" end
box: background = "#86efac" content = "c" end
end` |

| `grid row start`
آغاز ردیف شبکه
grid-row-start | The grid line where the item starts in the row direction, counted from 1 at the top. [integer / name / auto, span; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" grid auto rows = 40 gap = 6
box: grid row start = 2 background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "starts in row 2" end
end` |

| `grid row end`
انتهای ردیف شبکه
grid-row-end | The grid line where the item ends in the row direction. `"span 3"` means three rows past the start. [integer / name / auto, span; up to 2 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "1fr 1fr" grid auto rows = 40 gap = 6
box: grid row end = "span 3" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "three rows" end
box: background = "#93c5fd" content = "b" end
end` |

| `grid area`
ناحیه شبکه
grid-area | Places an item in one go. A name refers to an area from `grid template areas`. Four numbers separated by slashes are the row start, column start, row end and column end lines, as in `"1 / 2 / 3 / 4"`. [integer / name; up to 3 values] | `box: display = grid grid template columns = "repeat(3, 1fr)" grid auto rows = 40 gap = 6
box: grid area = "1 / 2 / 3 / 4" background = "#fca5a5" padding = 8 content = "rows 1-2, columns 2-3" end
end` |

### Columns and breaks

Newspaper columns, the lines between them and where they may break.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `break after`
شکستن پس از
break-after | Whether a break is forced or avoided after this element, with the same values as `break before`. `column` ends the column here, and `avoid` keeps a heading together with the paragraph that follows it. [auto, avoid, always, all, avoid-page, page, ...] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 20 line height = 1.4
paragraph: break after = column margin = 0 content = "This paragraph ends the first column." end
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "So this one starts the second column." end
end` |

| `break before`
شکستن پیش از
break-before | Whether a column, page or region break is forced or avoided before this element. In columns, `column` starts a new column here and `avoid` asks to keep it with the content before it. The values `page` and `always` matter when you print. [auto, avoid, always, all, avoid-page, page, ...] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 20 line height = 1.4
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "First column." end
paragraph: break before = column margin = 0 content = "Forced into the second column." end
end` |

| `break inside`
شکستن درون
break-inside | Whether a break may fall inside this element. `avoid` keeps a card, figure or short paragraph in one piece when a column or page ends. The default is `auto`. [auto, avoid, avoid-page, avoid-column] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 20 line height = 1.4
box: break inside = avoid background = "#fef3c7" padding = 8 margin bottom = 8 content = "This card is never split across two columns." end
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "Other text may flow on as usual." end
end` |

| `column count`
تعداد ستون
column-count | The number of columns, as a whole number. With `column width` as well, it is the largest number of columns allowed. [integer / auto] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 20 line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "Two columns of text, whatever the width of the box. The text is shared between them so that both end at about the same height." end
end` |

| `column fill`
پرکردن ستون
column-fill | How the content is shared between columns. `balance` (default) makes the columns about equal in height. `auto` fills one column to the height of the box before starting the next, which matters when the box has a fixed height. [auto, balance] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 20 column fill = auto height = 80 line height = 1.4
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "With auto the first column is filled to the full height of the box before any text moves to the second column." end
end` |

| `column gap`
شکاف ستون
column-gap | The space between columns. It also sets the gap between the columns of a grid or flex container. The default for multi-column text is `normal` (1em). [length / percentage / normal] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 40 line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "A wide gap of 40 pixels separates the two columns of this text, which makes the break easy to see." end
end` |

| `column rule`
خط جداکننده ستون
column-rule | Shorthand for the line drawn between columns: width, style and colour, written like a border, for example `"1px solid #94a3b8"`. The rule takes no space of its own; it sits in the middle of the gap. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 30 column rule = "2px dashed #64748b" line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "A dashed line runs down the middle of the gap between the two columns of this paragraph, just as in a printed newspaper." end
end` |

| `column rule color`
رنگ خط ستون
column-rule-color | The colour of the line between columns. [color] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 30 column rule style = solid column rule width = 2 column rule color = crimson line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "The rule between these two columns is drawn in crimson, set separately from its style and width." end
end` |

| `column rule style`
سبک خط ستون
column-rule-style | The line style between columns: `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double` and the other border styles. `none` (default) draws nothing, so you must set a style for the rule to show. [none, hidden, dotted, dashed, solid, double, ...] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 30 column rule width = 3 column rule style = dotted line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "A dotted rule separates these columns. Without a style the width and colour would draw nothing at all." end
end` |

| `column rule width`
ضخامت خط ستون
column-rule-width | The thickness of the line between columns: a length, or `thin`, `medium` or `thick`. It needs a rule style to show. [length / thin, medium, thick] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 30 column rule style = solid column rule width = 4 line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "A thick rule four pixels wide runs between these two columns, so the division is easy to see." end
end` |

| `column span`
گستره ستون
column-span | Lets an element inside a multi-column box stretch across all the columns. The values are `none` (default) and `all`. It is used for a heading above the columns. [none, all] | `box: column count = 2 column gap = 20 line height = 1.5
heading: size = 3 column span = all margin = "0 0 8" content = "A heading across both columns" end
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "The text below the heading is shared between the two columns, while the heading itself is as wide as the whole box." end
end` |

| `column width`
عرض ستون
column-width | The ideal width of a column. The browser makes as many columns of at least this width as fit and widens them to fill the box, so the number changes with the window. [length / auto] | `box: column width = 140 column gap = 20 line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "The number of columns follows the available width, never narrower than 140 pixels each, so a phone gets one column and a desktop gets several." end
end` |

| `columns`
چندستونی
columns | Shorthand for `column width` and `column count`: `"12rem 3"` means "columns at least 12rem wide, at most 3". Write a single number with `column count`, because a bare number here becomes pixels. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: columns = "9rem 3" column gap = 20 line height = 1.5
paragraph: margin = 0 content = "Text in a multi-column box flows down the first column and continues at the top of the next one, like a newspaper. The browser picks how many columns fit." end
end` |

## Try it yourself

- Build a page header with a logo on one side, three links in the middle and a button on the other side, using only a flex row and `justify content`.

- Make a photo gallery of nine coloured boxes with `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(120px, 1fr))`. Make the first box span two columns and two rows.

- Write a classic page layout with named areas: a header, a left menu, a main part, a right column and a footer. Then change one string so the menu moves to the right.

- Take the sticky example and give the headings `z index` and a shadow. What happens when you remove the `top` value?
