# The rest of CSS

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/css-more/

The earlier lessons covered text, boxes, color and layout. This one finishes the list: the properties for numbered lists and counters, for tables, for scrolling that snaps into place, for tooltips tied to an anchor, and for drawing with SVG. Every one has a short example, and the reference at the end lists all 94 with what they accept.

## Lists and their markers

Every item of a list has a marker: the bullet of a `list` or the number of an `ordered list`. The browser draws it, and you choose how with three properties. `list style type` sets the look. It takes a keyword such as `disc`, `square`, `decimal`, `lower-roman` or `upper-alpha`, `none` for no marker, or a text of your own. A text must keep its quotes in the CSS, so in Salam write it between backticks: `list style type = `"» "``. `list style position` says whether the marker hangs outside the text (`outside`, the default) or sits inside the first line (`inside`). `list style image` uses a picture or a gradient instead of a character.

`list style` is the shorthand for all three, written as one string such as `"square outside"`. Look at the last two lists in the preview: with a marker outside, every line of a long item starts at the same edge, and with a marker inside the second line wraps under the marker.

web-more-lists.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "List markers"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    heading: size = 3 content = "Roman numerals" end
    ordered list: list style type = lower-roman
        item: content = "Preface" end
        item: content = "Chapters" end
        item: content = "Index" end
    end
    heading: size = 3 content = "Your own marker" end
    list: list style type = `"» "`
        item: content = "Open the box" end
        item: content = "Read the label" end
    end
    heading: size = 3 content = "Inside and outside" end
    list: list style position = inside background = "#ccfbf1" max width = "20rem" padding = 8
        item: content = "The marker sits inside the text, so a second line starts under it." end
    end
    list: list style = "square outside" background = "#e2e8f0" max width = "20rem" padding = 8 padding inline start = 32
        item: content = "The marker hangs outside, so every line starts at the same edge." end
    end
    list: list style image = "linear-gradient(#0f766e, #38bdf8)"
        item: content = "An image as the marker" end
    end
end
```

These properties style the marker as a whole. You cannot give one marker a color of its own with them. The marker takes the color and the font of its item, so to change it, change the item.

## Counters: numbering with CSS

A counter is a number that the browser keeps under a name. Three properties work with it. `counter reset` creates it on an element, or sets it back to a start value: `"chapter"` starts at 0 and `"chapter 4"` at 4. `counter increment` adds to it each time an element that has the property is drawn, by 1 or by the number you give. `counter set` puts a value into it without adding. When both increment and set sit on one element, the set wins.

A counter is invisible until you print it. For that, write `counter(chapter)` in the `generated content` of a `before` or `after` rule, which adds text in front of or behind an element. A text next to it goes in quotes inside the string: `"counter(chapter) \". \""`. If you reset a lesson counter on every chapter heading, it starts again in each chapter and gives `1.1`, `1.2`, `2.1`. The example does exactly that: every chapter heading resets the lesson counter and every lesson paragraph increments it.

web-more-counters.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Numbered outline"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    box: counter reset = chapter
        heading:
            size = 3
            counter increment = chapter
            counter reset = lesson
            before generated content = "counter(chapter) \". \""
            content = "Getting started"
        end
        paragraph: counter increment = lesson before generated content = "counter(chapter) \".\" counter(lesson) \"  \"" content = "Install the compiler" end
        paragraph: counter increment = lesson before generated content = "counter(chapter) \".\" counter(lesson) \"  \"" content = "Your first page" end
        heading:
            size = 3
            counter increment = chapter
            counter reset = lesson
            before generated content = "counter(chapter) \". \""
            content = "Styling"
        end
        paragraph: counter increment = lesson before generated content = "counter(chapter) \".\" counter(lesson) \"  \"" content = "Colors and fonts" end
        heading:
            size = 3
            counter set = "chapter 9"
            counter reset = lesson
            before generated content = "counter(chapter) \". \""
            content = "Appendix"
        end
        paragraph: counter increment = lesson before generated content = "counter(chapter) \".\" counter(lesson) \"  \"" content = "Glossary" end
    end
end
```

The appendix heading uses `counter set = "chapter 9"`: it jumps to 9 and its lessons follow as 9.1. The `counter()` function takes a second value, a list style, and the Persian version of the example uses it as `counter(chapter, persian)` to print Persian digits. For nested numbers such as 1.2.3 in one go, `counters(name, ".")` joins every level of the counter with a separator.

The `before` and `after` prefixes work on elements and components, but not inside a `global` rule, where they are silently dropped. If the numbering does not appear, check where the rule is written. Also note that two elements with the same styles share one CSS class, while two with different styles that you named with the same `class` are a compile error, so name a class only on elements that really look alike.

## Quotation marks

The `quote` element puts quotation marks around its text, and which marks it uses comes from the `quotes` property. The value is pairs of strings: the first pair is the outer level, the second pair is for a quote inside a quote, and so on. Quote marks in the value need backticks again. The first two paragraphs of the example show the same nested sentence with two sets of marks. `quotes = "none"` removes the marks, and for a `block quote`, which has none of its own, you can add them with the keywords `open-quote` and `close-quote` in `generated content`, as in the last line of the example. Those keywords use the same `quotes` pairs, so the marks stay consistent.

web-more-quotes.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Quotation marks"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    paragraph: quotes = `"“" "”" "‘" "’"`
        content = "Sara said, "
        quote: content = "Omid told me "
            quote: content = "never stop" end
        end
        span: content = "." end
    end
    paragraph: quotes = `"«" "»" "‹" "›"`
        content = "The same sentence with other marks: "
        quote: content = "Omid told me "
            quote: content = "never stop" end
        end
    end
    block quote: quotes = "none" border = "none" margin = "1rem 0" color = "#475569"
        content = "Quote marks off."
    end
    block quote: quotes = `"[" "]"` color = "#0f766e"
        before generated content = open-quote
        after generated content = close-quote
        content = "Added with open-quote and close-quote."
    end
end
```

## Table borders and layout

A table has two models for its borders. With `border collapse = separate` (the default) every cell keeps a complete border of its own and the gaps between cells are set with `border spacing`: one length for both directions, or two for horizontal and vertical. With `collapse` neighbouring borders merge into a single line and `border spacing` does nothing. `empty cells = hide` leaves out the border and background of a cell with no content, but only in the separate model. `caption side` moves the `caption` to the `bottom`. The first table below shows the separate model with its hidden empty cell, and the second shows collapsed borders.

web-more-table.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Table settings"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    global: selector = "td, th" border = "2px solid #0f766e" padding = "6 14" end
    table: border collapse = separate border spacing = "10 4" empty cells = hide caption side = bottom margin = "0 0 1.5rem"
        caption: content = "Separate borders, empty cells hidden" end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "Item" end
                column: content = "Note" end
            end
        end
        row:
            cell: content = "Tea" end
            cell: end
        end
    end
    table: border collapse = collapse table layout = fixed width = "22rem"
        caption: content = "Collapsed borders, fixed layout" end
        header:
            row:
                column: content = "Item" end
                column: content = "A long heading in a column of fixed width" end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

The second table uses `table layout = fixed`. With the default `auto` layout the browser measures every cell before it decides on column widths, so one long cell can stretch its column and the table can end up wider than you asked. A fixed layout reads only the table width and the first row and divides the space, so the columns stay put and long text wraps inside them. It also draws a big table faster. It needs a `width` on the table to have any effect.

## Scrolling that snaps

Scroll snapping makes a scrolling box come to rest on chosen points instead of anywhere, like the pages of a gallery. It takes two sides. On the scroll container, `scroll snap type` turns it on: an axis (`x`, `y` or `both`) and a strictness. `mandatory` always comes to rest on a point, `proximity` only when the scroll stops near one. On each child, `scroll snap align` says which edge of the child lines up with the container: `start`, `center` or `end`. `scroll snap stop = "always"` adds that a fast flick may not skip past the child, which is what you want for a slide show.

The example below is a strip of four slides. The container has `overflow x = auto` to scroll and `scroll snap type = "x mandatory"`. The slides are styled with one `global` rule using the selector `#strip > *`, which is shorter than repeating the same line on four boxes. Scroll the strip with your finger, a mouse wheel or the keys and watch it settle on a slide.

web-more-snap.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Snapping slides"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    global: selector = "#strip > *" flex = "0 0 80%" height = 120 color = white font size = "1.6rem" display = flex align items = center justify content = center border radius = 12 scroll snap align = start scroll snap stop = always end
    style: content = "#strip::scroll-marker-group { display: flex; gap: 8px; justify-content: center; padding: 8px } #strip > *::scroll-marker { content: ''; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; background: #94a3b8 } #strip > *::scroll-marker:target-current { background: #0f766e }" end
    box: id = "strip" display = flex gap = 12 overflow x = auto padding = "0 20" scroll snap type = "x mandatory" scroll padding = "0 20" scroll marker group = after
        box: background = "#0f766e" content = "One" end
        box: background = "#2563eb" content = "Two" end
        box: background = "#c2410c" content = "Three" end
        box: background = "#7c3aed" content = "Four" end
    end
    paragraph: content = "Scroll the strip sideways. It always stops with a slide at the edge." end
end
```

Two more properties adjust where "start" is. `scroll padding` goes on the container and shrinks the area that counts: `"0 20"` keeps a slide 20 pixels away from the left and right edges, so that the next slide peeks in, and it stops a fixed header from covering a heading that the page jumps to. `scroll margin` goes on the child and grows its snap area on its own. Both come in sides: `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left`, and the logical ones, `block` and `inline` with `start` and `end`, which turn around in a right to left page. Use the logical ones for anything that scrolls sideways, because in a Persian page the first slide is at the right.

The little dots in the preview are made by the browser, not by elements. `scroll marker group = "after"` asks for a row of markers after the container, one for each child, and the raw `style` element styles them with `::scroll-marker` and `::scroll-marker-group`, which the page language has no names for. The dot of the slide in view also matches `:target-current`, so it can have its own color, and clicking a dot scrolls to its slide. `scroll target group = "auto"` does the same job for a list of links, such as a table of contents that highlights the section you are reading. Both exist today in Chromium browsers only, so keep the page usable without them.

Snapping only helps readers who scroll. Do not use it to hide content: keep everything within reach of a plain scroll, and try the page with the keyboard too, which moves the container in the same way.

## Anchor positioning

A tooltip, a menu or a popup belongs next to the thing it explains. For years that needed JavaScript that measured the page. Anchor positioning does it in CSS. You give an element a name with `anchor name`, which must start with two hyphens, like `"--target"`. Another element that is `position = absolute` chooses that name with `position anchor` and says where to sit with `position area`. The area is a cell of a three by three grid around the anchor: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `center`, corners such as `top right`, and stretched cells like `top span-right`.

The example has four buttons. Each one runs a small function when it is clicked, and the function sets the `position-area` of the tooltip with `dom.SetStyle`. The tooltip jumps around the anchor and no coordinates are calculated anywhere. The functions of `dom` are described on the dom page.

web-more-anchor.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Anchored tooltip"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    box: display = flex gap = 8 margin = "0 0 1rem"
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("tip"), "position-area", "top") end content = "Top" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("tip"), "position-area", "right") end content = "Right" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("tip"), "position-area", "bottom") end content = "Bottom" end
        button: click = (): dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("tip"), "position-area", "left") end content = "Left" end
    end
    box: position = relative height = 220 border = "1px dashed #94a3b8" border radius = 8
        box: id = "target" anchor name = "--target" margin = "80 auto 0" width = 120 padding = 12 text align = center background = "#0f766e" color = white border radius = 6 content = "Anchor" end
        box: id = "tip" position = absolute position anchor = "--target" position area = top position try fallbacks = flip-block position visibility = anchors-visible margin = 6 padding = "4 10" background = "#0f172a" color = white border radius = 6 content = "Tooltip" end
    end
end
```

Two more properties make the tooltip behave near the edge of the screen. `position try fallbacks = "flip-block"` lists other places to try when the first one would run off screen: `flip-block` mirrors it to the other side, `flip-inline` does so sideways. `position visibility = "anchors-visible"` hides the tooltip when its anchor has scrolled out of view, so that it does not float alone. `position try order` and the shorthand `position try` rank the fallbacks by the room they leave. Finally `anchor scope` keeps names local to a part of the page, so that a component used ten times can use the same name in each copy without mixing them up.

Anchor positioning is new. Chromium browsers have it and the others are catching up, and a browser that lacks it ignores these lines, so the tooltip stays where it would be without them. Test it in the browsers your readers use, and have a plain fallback such as showing the text below the button.

## SVG presentation properties

The `svg` element holds a drawing. Its `content` is raw SVG markup that the compiler passes on unchanged, so shapes such as `<circle>` and `<path>` are written as text. What the page language adds is the styling. The properties of this section are SVG presentation properties, and they reach the shapes in two ways.

The first way is inheritance. `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke width`, `paint order`, `text anchor` and the `marker` properties are inherited, so one line on the `svg` element styles every shape inside. `fill` is the color inside a shape and `stroke` is the line along its edge; with no stroke only the fill shows. The first example puts them on three drawings. `fill rule = "evenodd"` leaves a hole in the star where its lines cross. `stroke dasharray` alternates dash and gap, `stroke dashoffset` shifts the pattern, and a round `stroke linecap` turns the dashes into dots. `stroke linejoin` shapes a corner, and `stroke miterlimit` cuts a sharp point flat when it would stick out too far.

web-more-svg-stroke.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Fill and stroke"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    box: display = flex gap = 24 flex wrap = wrap
        box:
            svg: view box = "0 0 100 100" width = 120 height = 120 fill = "#5eead4" fill opacity = 0.6 fill rule = evenodd stroke = "#0f766e" stroke width = 3 stroke linejoin = round
                content = "<polygon points='50,5 80,95 5,35 95,35 20,95'/>"
            end
            paragraph: content = "Even-odd fill" end
        end
        box:
            svg: view box = "0 0 100 100" width = 120 height = 120 fill = none stroke = "#c2410c" stroke width = 8 stroke linecap = round stroke dasharray = "1 14" stroke dashoffset = 4
                content = "<circle cx='50' cy='50' r='38'/>"
            end
            paragraph: content = "Dotted line" end
        end
        box:
            svg: view box = "0 0 100 100" width = 120 height = 120 fill = none stroke = "#2563eb" stroke width = 14 stroke linejoin = miter stroke miterlimit = 2
                content = "<polyline points='15,85 50,15 85,85'/>"
            end
            paragraph: content = "Sharp corner, cut by the limit" end
        end
    end
end
```

Text in SVG has its own rules. `text anchor` decides which part of the text sits on its `x` point: `middle` centres it. `paint order = "stroke fill"` draws the outline first, so the fill covers its inner half and outlined letters stay thick. `dominant baseline` and `baseline shift` change the line that letters rest on, and they are not inherited, so they go on one text only. That is the second way to reach a shape: a `global` rule with a `selector` such as `"#b"`. The page language does not name the shapes inside the raw markup, but CSS can still find them by id, class or tag.

web-more-svg-text.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Text in SVG"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    global: selector = "#a" dominant baseline = hanging end
    global: selector = "#b" dominant baseline = middle end
    global: selector = "#sup" baseline shift = super font size = 14 end
    svg: view box = "0 0 360 140" width = 360 height = 140 font size = 20 font weight = bold fill = "#fde68a" stroke = "#0f172a" stroke width = 4 paint order = "stroke fill" text anchor = middle
        content = "<line x1='0' y1='45' x2='360' y2='45' stroke='#ef4444' stroke-width='1'/><text id='a' x='60' y='45'>hanging</text><text id='b' x='180' y='45'>middle</text><text x='300' y='45'>alphabetic</text><text x='180' y='110'>E = mc<tspan id='sup'>2</tspan></text>"
    end
end
```

The same way works for the properties that only a shape has. `cx`, `cy` and `r` place and size a circle, `rx` and `ry` do it for an ellipse or round the corners of a rectangle, `x` and `y` move a rectangle, and `d` holds the outline of a path. They are attributes in old SVG and CSS properties in modern browsers, which is what lets a `hover` rule grow the circle below and a `transition` animate it.

web-more-svg-geometry.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Geometry from CSS"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    global: selector = "#c" cx = 60 cy = 60 r = 30 transition = "r 0.2s" end
    global: selector = "#c:hover" r = 48 end
    global: selector = "#e" cx = 170 cy = 60 rx = 40 ry = 22 end
    global: selector = "#r" x = 230 y = 30 rx = 14 ry = 14 end
    global: selector = "#p" d = "path('M 10 135 C 70 112 130 112 190 135 L 290 135')" end
    svg: view box = "0 0 300 140" width = 300 height = 140 stroke = "#0f172a" stroke width = 2
        content = "<circle id='c' fill='#5eead4'/><ellipse id='e' fill='#fde68a'/><rect id='r' width='60' height='60' fill='#fca5a5'/><path id='p' fill='none'/>"
    end
    paragraph: content = "Point at the circle: its radius is a CSS property here." end
end
```

Write the path in `d` with `C` or `L` rather than `Q`. A number followed by a space and `Q` can be read by the page compiler as the length unit `q`, which breaks the path. This only happens in CSS written with the page language: the `d` attribute inside the raw markup is passed on untouched.

Gradients and filters are written in the raw markup too, but their colors are CSS properties. `stop color` and `stop opacity` color a gradient stop, `flood color` and `flood opacity` color an `feFlood` step of a filter, and `lighting color` does so for the lighting steps. `color interpolation filters` picks the color space in which a filter works, `sRGB` or `linearRGB`. Because stops and filter steps are not inherited, you reach them through `global` rules again.

web-more-svg-paint.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Gradient stops and filters"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    global: selector = ".s1" stop color = "#0f766e" stop opacity = 1 end
    global: selector = ".s2" stop color = "#2563eb" stop opacity = 0.25 end
    global: selector = ".tint" flood color = "#7c3aed" flood opacity = 0.5 end
    global: selector = "filter" color interpolation filters = sRGB end
    svg: view box = "0 0 220 120" width = 220 height = 120
        content = "<defs><linearGradient id='g' x1='0' x2='1'><stop class='s1' offset='0'/><stop class='s2' offset='1'/></linearGradient><filter id='f'><feFlood class='tint' result='c'/><feComposite in='c' in2='SourceGraphic' operator='in' result='t'/><feMerge><feMergeNode in='SourceGraphic'/><feMergeNode in='t'/></feMerge></filter></defs><rect x='5' y='10' width='100' height='100' rx='10' fill='url(#g)'/><rect x='115' y='10' width='100' height='100' rx='10' fill='#38bdf8' filter='url(#f)'/>"
    end
    paragraph: content = "Left: a gradient whose stops are colored with CSS. Right: a filter whose flood color comes from CSS." end
end
```

Markers are small shapes drawn on the points of a line. `marker start`, `marker mid` and `marker end` take `url(#id)` of a `marker` element, and the shorthand `marker` sets all three at once. Put the `marker` elements in a separate `svg` as the example does, because markers inherit the stroke and the marker properties of the drawing they sit in. `vector effect = "non-scaling-stroke"` keeps a line the same thickness when the drawing is scaled, and `shape rendering` and `color interpolation` are hints for how edges and gradients are drawn.

web-more-svg-markers.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Markers on a line"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    svg: width = 0 height = 0 position = absolute
        content = "<defs><marker id='start' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='5' refY='5' markerWidth='6' markerHeight='6'><circle cx='5' cy='5' r='5' fill='#2563eb'/></marker><marker id='mid' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='5' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5'><rect width='10' height='10' fill='#f59e0b'/></marker><marker id='end' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' orient='auto'><path d='M0 0 L10 5 L0 10 z' fill='#dc2626'/></marker></defs>"
    end
    svg: view box = "0 0 300 120" width = 300 height = 120 fill = none stroke = "#0f766e" stroke width = 3 marker start = "url(#start)" marker mid = "url(#mid)" marker end = "url(#end)"
        content = "<polyline points='20,90 100,30 180,80 270,30'/>"
    end
    paragraph: content = "A dot at the start, squares at the corners, an arrow at the end." end
end
```

## Math

The `math` element draws a formula. Like `svg`, its content is raw markup, here MathML, such as `<mfrac>` for a fraction and `<msup>` for a power. Three properties change how it is set. `math style` is `normal` for a display formula, with large operators and limits above and below, or `compact` for one inside a line of text, with everything tighter. `math depth` says how deeply the formula is nested, so that it can be drawn smaller. It changes the size only where `font-size` is the keyword `math`, which the page language does not accept yet, so the example sets it in a raw `style` element. `math shift` chooses how far superscripts are raised: `compact` raises them less, as in the denominator of a fraction.

web-more-math.salam

```salam
page:
    title = "Math styles"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    global: selector = "math" font size = "1.6rem" margin = "0 1.5rem 0 0" end
    paragraph: content = "Math style: normal, then compact" end
    box: display = flex
        math: math style = normal
            content = "<munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></mfrac>"
        end
        math: math style = compact
            content = "<munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></mfrac>"
        end
    end
    style: content = "#d0, #d1, #d2 { font-size: math }" end
    paragraph: content = "Math depth 0, 1 and 2 side by side" end
    box: display = flex align items = baseline font size = "3rem"
        math: id = "d0" math depth = 0 content = "<mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn>" end
        math: id = "d1" math depth = 1 content = "<mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn>" end
        math: id = "d2" math depth = 2 content = "<mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn>" end
    end
end
```

## Reading order, the top layer and HDR

Keyboard focus and screen readers move through a page in the order of the source. When a layout changes the visual order, for example with `flex direction = row-reverse`, the two disagree and a keyboard user jumps around the screen. `reading flow` on the container fixes that: `flex-visual` follows what is drawn, `grid-rows` and `grid-columns` do the same for a grid, and `source-order` lets the `reading order` number of each child decide, lowest first. In the example press Tab: the first row is read in source order, the second in the order you see.

web-more-reading.salam

```salam
import dom

page:
    title = "Reading order"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = "1.5rem" line height = 1.6 end
    paragraph: id = "out" content = "Press Tab and watch the focus." end
    box: display = flex flex direction = row-reverse gap = 8 margin = "0 0 1rem"
        button: focus = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Focus: A") end content = "A" end
        button: focus = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Focus: B") end content = "B" end
        button: focus = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Focus: C") end content = "C" end
    end
    box: display = flex flex direction = row-reverse gap = 8 reading flow = flex-visual
        button: focus = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Focus: D") end content = "D" end
        button: focus = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Focus: E") end content = "E" end
        button: focus = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Focus: F") end content = "F" end
    end
end
```

In a right to left page the visual order starts at the right, so the same property gives a different sequence, and the Persian version of this example shows it. Two more properties are for special cases. `overlay` reports whether an element is in the top layer, where popovers and dialogs are drawn; you list it in a `transition` so that an element leaving the top layer can finish its exit animation first. `dynamic range limit` limits how bright HDR images and video may get on a screen that supports it, from `standard` to `no-limit`.

## Reference: the remaining properties

Every property of this lesson is below with its Persian name, the CSS name, what it accepts and an example that the compiler has checked. A bare number is a length in pixels, and any CSS keyword can be written without quotes unless it is also a word of the page language, such as `end`, in which case put it in quotes.

### Lists, counters and quotes

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list style`
سبک فهرست
list-style | Shorthand for `list-style-type`, `list-style-position` and `list-style-image`. Give the parts in any order, for example `square inside`; a part you leave out keeps its default. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `list: list style = "square inside" background = "#ccfbf1" padding = 8
item: content = "Sugar" end
item: content = "Flour" end
end` |

| `list style type`
نوع نشانه فهرست
list-style-type | The look of the marker. Use a keyword such as `disc`, `circle`, `square`, `decimal`, `decimal-leading-zero`, `lower-roman`, `upper-alpha`, `persian`, or `none`. A text in quotes is used as it is. Set it on the list; the items inherit it. [string / disc, circle, square, decimal, decimal-leading-zero, lower-roman, ...] | `ordered list: list style type = "upper-alpha"
item: content = "Soup" end
item: content = "Salad" end
end` |

| `list style position`
جای نشانه فهرست
list-style-position | Where the marker goes. `outside` (the default) hangs it outside the text box, so wrapped lines stay aligned. `inside` puts it in the first line of the text, and wrapped lines start under it. [inside, outside] | `ordered list: list style position = "inside" background = "#e2e8f0" max width = 220
item: content = "A long step that wraps onto a second line" end
end` |

| `list style image`
تصویر نشانه فهرست
list-style-image | Uses a picture as the marker of every list item. The value is an image, such as `url(star.png)` or a gradient, or `none` to go back to `list-style-type`. [image / none] | `list: list style image = "linear-gradient(#f59e0b, #dc2626)"
item: content = "Gold marker" end
item: content = "Same marker again" end
end` |

| `marker`
نشانه
marker | An SVG shorthand that sets `marker-start`, `marker-mid` and `marker-end` to the same marker in one go, for example `url(#dot)`. It works on the shapes `path`, `line`, `polyline` and `polygon`. It has nothing to do with the `::marker` of list items. [image] | `svg: view box = "0 0 60 40" width = 120 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#0f766e" marker = "url(#dot)"
content = "<defs><marker id=&#x27;dot&#x27; viewBox=&#x27;0 0 10 10&#x27; refX=&#x27;5&#x27; refY=&#x27;5&#x27; markerWidth=&#x27;5&#x27; markerHeight=&#x27;5&#x27;><circle cx=&#x27;5&#x27; cy=&#x27;5&#x27; r=&#x27;5&#x27; fill=&#x27;#dc2626&#x27;/></marker></defs><polyline points=&#x27;5,30 30,8 55,30&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `quotes`
نقل قول‌ها
quotes | The quotation marks that `quote` and the `open-quote` and `close-quote` values use. Give pairs of strings: the first pair for the outer level, the second for a quote inside a quote, and so on. `none` shows no marks and `auto` picks the marks of the language. [string; up to 99 values] | `quote: quotes = `"«" "»"` content = "Slow and steady" end` |

| `counter reset`
بازنشانی شمارنده
counter-reset | Creates a counter on the element, or sets an existing one back to a number. Write the name and, if you want, the start value: `chapter` starts at 0 and `chapter 4` starts at 4. Several counters can be listed together, and `none` does nothing. [name / integer; up to 99 values] | `box: counter reset = "n 4"
paragraph: counter increment = n before generated content = "counter(n) \". \"" content = "Fifth" end
paragraph: counter increment = n before generated content = "counter(n) \". \"" content = "Sixth" end
end` |

| `counter increment`
افزایش شمارنده
counter-increment | Adds to a counter each time the element is drawn. Write the name and, if you want, the step: `step` adds 1, `step 2` adds 2 and `step -1` counts down. The number is shown with `counter()` in `generated content`. [name / integer; up to 99 values] | `box: counter reset = step
paragraph: counter increment = "step 2" before generated content = "counter(step) \". \"" content = "Two" end
paragraph: counter increment = "step 2" before generated content = "counter(step) \". \"" content = "Four" end
end` |

| `counter set`
تنظیم شمارنده
counter-set | Sets a counter to a number without adding to it. Write the name and the value: `page 41`. The elements after it continue from that number. If no counter of that name exists yet, one is created. [name / integer; up to 99 values] | `box: counter reset = page
paragraph: counter set = "page 41" before generated content = "\"p. \" counter(page)" content = "Jump to page 41" end
end` |

### Tables

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `border collapse`
ادغام کادر
border-collapse | How cell borders meet in a table. `collapse` merges neighbouring borders into one line. `separate` (the default) gives every cell its own border with a gap between, which `border-spacing` controls. [collapse, separate] | `table: border collapse = "collapse"
row:
cell: border = "2px solid #0f766e" content = "One" end
cell: border = "2px solid #0f766e" content = "Two" end
end
end` |

| `border spacing`
فاصله کادرها
border-spacing | The gap between cells when borders are separate. One length is used both ways, and two lengths mean horizontal and then vertical. It has no effect when `border-collapse` is `collapse`. [length; up to 2 values] | `table: border collapse = separate border spacing = "12 4"
row:
cell: border = "2px solid #2563eb" content = "Left" end
cell: border = "2px solid #2563eb" content = "Right" end
end
end` |

| `caption side`
جای عنوان جدول
caption-side | Puts the table caption above (`top`, the default) or below (`bottom`) the table. Set it on the `caption`. [top, bottom] | `table:
caption: caption side = "bottom" content = "Prices in euro" end
row: cell: content = "Tea 2" end end
end` |

| `empty cells`
خانه‌های خالی
empty-cells | Whether borders and background of empty cells are drawn, in a table with separate borders. `show` (the default) draws them and `hide` leaves an empty cell blank. [show, hide] | `table: border collapse = separate empty cells = "hide"
row:
cell: border = "2px solid #c2410c" content = "Full" end
cell: border = "2px solid #c2410c" end
end
end` |

| `table layout`
چیدمان جدول
table-layout | How column widths are found. `auto` (the default) measures all the content, so a long cell can widen its column. `fixed` takes widths from the table width and the first row only, which is faster and keeps the table the size you gave it. [auto, fixed] | `table: table layout = "fixed" width = 200
row:
cell: border = "1px solid #64748b" content = "A very long word in a narrow cell" end
cell: border = "1px solid #64748b" content = "Short" end
end
end` |

### Scroll snap and scroll markers

The first three go on the container and its children as described above. The last two build the dots and the highlighted links that follow the scroll.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scroll snap type`
نوع چسبیدن پیمایش
scroll-snap-type | Turns a scroll container into one that snaps. Give the axis (`x`, `y`, `block`, `inline` or `both`) and how strict it is: `mandatory` always rests on a snap point, `proximity` only when it ends close to one. `none` turns snapping off. The children choose the points with `scroll-snap-align`. [CSS-wide keywords only] | `box: scroll snap type = "y mandatory" overflow y = auto height = 80
box: height = 80 scroll snap align = "start" background = "#99f6e4" content = "First" end
box: height = 80 scroll snap align = "start" background = "#bae6fd" content = "Second" end
end` |

| `scroll snap align`
تراز چسبیدن پیمایش
scroll-snap-align | Which part of the child lines up with the snap area of its container: `start`, `center` or `end`, or `none` for no snap point. Two values set the block and the inline direction separately. It works only inside a container that has `scroll-snap-type`. [none, start, end, center; up to 2 values] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" overflow x = auto display = flex width = 220
box: flex = "0 0 120" scroll snap align = "center" background = "#fde68a" content = "Centered" end
box: flex = "0 0 120" scroll snap align = "center" background = "#fecaca" content = "Also centered" end
end` |

| `scroll snap stop`
توقف چسبیدن پیمایش
scroll-snap-stop | Whether a fast scroll may skip past this snap point. `normal` lets it skip, `always` makes it stop at this child every time, which suits slide shows and pickers. [normal, always] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 100%" scroll snap align = "start" scroll snap stop = "always" content = "One" end
box: flex = "0 0 100%" scroll snap align = "start" scroll snap stop = "always" content = "Two" end
end` |

| `scroll marker group`
گروه نشانگر پیمایش
scroll-marker-group | Chromium only. On a scroll container, makes the browser build a group of small clickable markers, one for each child that has a `::scroll-marker`. `before` or `after` says where the group goes around the container, and `none` turns it off. Style the group with `::scroll-marker-group` in raw CSS. [none / before / after] | `box: scroll marker group = "after" overflow x = auto display = flex scroll snap type = "x mandatory" width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 100%" scroll snap align = "start" content = "Slide one" end
box: flex = "0 0 100%" scroll snap align = "start" content = "Slide two" end
end` |

| `scroll target group`
گروه هدف پیمایش
scroll-target-group | Chromium only. `auto` turns an element that holds links into a group of scroll targets: every link inside that points to a place on the same page counts as a scroll marker, and the link whose target is in view matches `:target-current`, so you can highlight it. `none` (the default) does nothing. Used for tables of contents that follow the scroll. [auto / none] | `list: scroll target group = "auto"
item: link: url = "#intro" content = "Introduction" end end
item: link: url = "#usage" content = "Usage" end end
end` |

### Scroll margin

Set on the child. The sides are physical (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`) or logical (`block` and `inline`, with `start` and `end`).

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scroll margin`
فضا پیمایش
scroll-margin | Extra room around a child that counts as part of its snap area, so a snap or a jump to it stops a little short. One to four lengths, like `margin`. It is set on the child, not on the container. [length; up to 4 values] | `box: scroll snap align = "start" scroll margin = 16 background = "#ddd6fe" padding = 12 content = "Stops 16px short" end` |

| `scroll margin top`
فضا پیمایش بالا
scroll-margin-top | Scroll margin on the top edge of the child. One length. A common use is keeping a linked heading clear of a fixed header when the page jumps to it. [length] | `heading: size = 2 id = "prices" scroll margin top = 72 content = "Prices" end` |

| `scroll margin right`
فضا پیمایش راست
scroll-margin-right | Scroll margin on the right edge of the child, whatever the writing direction. One length. [length] | `box: scroll snap align = "end" scroll margin right = 24 background = "#fecdd3" padding = 12 content = "24px on the right" end` |

| `scroll margin bottom`
فضا پیمایش پایین
scroll-margin-bottom | Scroll margin on the bottom edge of the child. One length. [length] | `box: scroll snap align = "end" scroll margin bottom = 10 background = "#e9d5ff" padding = 10 content = "Bottom margin 10" end` |

| `scroll margin left`
فضا پیمایش چپ
scroll-margin-left | Scroll margin on the left edge of the child, whatever the writing direction. One length. [length] | `box: scroll snap align = "start" scroll margin left = 24 background = "#bfdbfe" padding = 12 content = "24px on the left" end` |

| `scroll margin block`
فضا پیمایش بلوکی
scroll-margin-block | Scroll margin in the block direction, start and end together: one length for both sides or two, start then end. In English text the block direction is top and bottom. [length; up to 2 values] | `box: scroll snap align = "start" scroll margin block = "8 24" background = "#bbf7d0" padding = 12 content = "Room above and below" end` |

| `scroll margin block start`
فضا پیمایش بلوکی ابتدا
scroll-margin-block-start | Scroll margin at the start of the block direction, which is the top in horizontal English text. Useful for a heading that must not hide under a sticky bar. [length] | `heading: size = 3 scroll margin block start = 64 content = "Section title" end` |

| `scroll margin block end`
فضا پیمایش بلوکی انتها
scroll-margin-block-end | Scroll margin at the end of the block direction, which is the bottom in horizontal English text. [length] | `box: scroll snap align = "end" scroll margin block end = 20 background = "#fed7aa" padding = 12 content = "20px kept at the end" end` |

| `scroll margin inline`
فضا پیمایش خطی
scroll-margin-inline | Scroll margin in the inline direction, start and end together: one length for both or two, start then end. In English text the inline direction is left and right. [length; up to 2 values] | `box: scroll snap align = center scroll margin inline = "12 12" background = "#a5f3fc" padding = 12 content = "Sideways room" end` |

| `scroll margin inline start`
فضا پیمایش ابتدا
scroll-margin-inline-start | Scroll margin at the start of the inline direction: the left in left to right text and the right in right to left text. [length] | `box: scroll snap align = "start" scroll margin inline start = 30 background = "#fef08a" padding = 12 content = "Room at the start" end` |

| `scroll margin inline end`
فضا پیمایش انتها
scroll-margin-inline-end | Scroll margin at the end of the inline direction: the right in left to right text and the left in right to left text. [length] | `box: scroll snap align = "end" scroll margin inline end = 30 background = "#fbcfe8" padding = 12 content = "Room at the end" end` |

### Scroll padding

Set on the scroll container, with the same sides as scroll margin. Percentages refer to the size of the container.

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scroll padding`
فاصله پیمایش
scroll-padding | Room kept free at the edges of a scroll container when it snaps or jumps to a child, so the child does not touch the edge or hide under a fixed bar. One to four lengths or percentages, like `padding`, or `auto`. It is set on the container. [length / percentage / auto; up to 4 values] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" scroll padding = "0 24" overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 160" scroll snap align = "start" background = "#99f6e4" content = "One" end
box: flex = "0 0 160" scroll snap align = "start" background = "#bae6fd" content = "Two" end
end` |

| `scroll padding top`
فاصله پیمایش بالا
scroll-padding-top | Scroll padding on the top edge of a scroll container. Set it to the height of a sticky header so that a jump or a snap does not hide the target under it. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `global: selector = "html" scroll padding top = 64 end
heading: size = 2 id = "faq" content = "Questions" end` |

| `scroll padding right`
فاصله پیمایش راست
scroll-padding-right | Scroll padding on the right edge of a scroll container, whatever the writing direction. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" scroll padding right = 40 overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 150" scroll snap align = "end" background = "#fecdd3" content = "Right gap 40" end
end` |

| `scroll padding bottom`
فاصله پیمایش پایین
scroll-padding-bottom | Scroll padding on the bottom edge of a scroll container. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll padding bottom = "20%" overflow y = auto height = 100 border = "1px solid #94a3b8"
paragraph: content = "The last paragraph stops above the bottom edge." end
end` |

| `scroll padding left`
فاصله پیمایش چپ
scroll-padding-left | Scroll padding on the left edge of a scroll container, whatever the writing direction. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" scroll padding left = "10%" overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 150" scroll snap align = "start" background = "#bfdbfe" content = "Left gap 10%" end
end` |

| `scroll padding block`
فاصله پیمایش بلوکی
scroll-padding-block | Scroll padding in the block direction, start and end together: one value for both or two, start then end. Lengths, percentages or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto; up to 2 values] | `box: scroll snap type = "y mandatory" scroll padding block = "10 20" overflow y = auto height = 100
box: height = 90 scroll snap align = "start" background = "#fde68a" content = "Row one" end
box: height = 90 scroll snap align = "start" background = "#fecaca" content = "Row two" end
end` |

| `scroll padding block start`
فاصله پیمایش بلوکی ابتدا
scroll-padding-block-start | Scroll padding at the start of the block direction of a scroll container, the top in horizontal English text. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll padding block start = 48 overflow y = auto height = 120
heading: size = 3 id = "part" content = "A part" end
end` |

| `scroll padding block end`
فاصله پیمایش بلوکی انتها
scroll-padding-block-end | Scroll padding at the end of the block direction of a scroll container, the bottom in horizontal English text. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll snap type = "y proximity" scroll padding block end = 40 overflow y = auto height = 100
box: height = 90 scroll snap align = "end" background = "#bbf7d0" content = "Keeps 40px free below" end
end` |

| `scroll padding inline`
فاصله پیمایش خطی
scroll-padding-inline | Scroll padding in the inline direction, start and end together: one value for both or two, start then end. Lengths, percentages or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto; up to 2 values] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" scroll padding inline = "16 32" overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 150" scroll snap align = center background = "#a5f3fc" content = "Card" end
end` |

| `scroll padding inline start`
فاصله پیمایش ابتدا
scroll-padding-inline-start | Scroll padding at the start of the inline direction of a scroll container: the left in left to right text. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll snap type = "x mandatory" scroll padding inline start = 30 overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 150" scroll snap align = "start" background = "#fef08a" content = "First card" end
end` |

| `scroll padding inline end`
فاصله پیمایش انتها
scroll-padding-inline-end | Scroll padding at the end of the inline direction of a scroll container: the right in left to right text. A length, a percentage or `auto`. [length / percentage / auto] | `box: scroll snap type = "x proximity" scroll padding inline end = 30 overflow x = auto display = flex width = 200
box: flex = "0 0 150" scroll snap align = "end" background = "#fbcfe8" content = "Last card" end
end` |

### Anchor positioning

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor name`
نام لنگر
anchor-name | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. Gives an element a name that other elements can position themselves against. The name starts with two hyphens, like `--menu`. A list of names gives the element several, and `none` removes them. [dashed ident list / none] | `button: anchor name = "--menu" content = "Menu" end` |

| `anchor scope`
دامنه لنگر
anchor-scope | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. Limits where anchor names are visible. With names, only the subtree of this element sees those anchors; with `all`, every name defined inside stays inside. It lets many copies of a component each use the same name without mixing up. [dashed ident list / all] | `box: anchor scope = "all"
button: anchor name = "--tip" content = "Help" end
end` |

| `position anchor`
لنگر جایگاه
position-anchor | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. Chooses which anchor name an absolutely or fixed positioned element is placed against. Give a dashed name like `--menu`, or `auto` to use the anchor the browser links to it, such as the button of a popover. [dashed ident / auto] | `box: position = absolute position anchor = "--menu" position area = bottom background = "#0f172a" color = white padding = 6 content = "Under the menu button" end` |

| `position area`
ناحیه جایگاه
position-area | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. Places an anchored element in one cell of a 3 by 3 grid around its anchor. Use `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right` and `center`, or two of them like `top right`. A word with `span-` takes two cells, for example `top span-right`. [up to 2 keywords (top, span-right, center, ...)] | `box: position = absolute position anchor = "--card" position area = "top span-right" background = "#0f766e" color = white padding = 6 content = "Above, stretching right" end` |

| `position try fallbacks`
جایگزین های جایگاه
position-try-fallbacks | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. A comma separated list of other places to try when the element would run out of the screen. Use the tactics `flip-block`, `flip-inline` and `flip-start`, a `position-area` value, or the name of a `@position-try` rule. The first one that fits is used. [comma list of tactics and/or position-area values] | `box: position = absolute position anchor = "--tip" position area = top position try fallbacks = "flip-block, bottom" content = "Moves below if there is no room" end` |

| `position try order`
ترتیب تلاش جایگاه
position-try-order | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. Decides how the fallbacks of `position-try-fallbacks` are ranked. `normal` tries them in the order written. `most-width`, `most-height`, `most-block-size` and `most-inline-size` pick the one that leaves the most room in that direction. [normal / most-width / most-height / most-block-size / most-inline-size] | `box: position = absolute position anchor = "--tip" position area = left position try order = "most-width" position try fallbacks = "right, top" content = "Picks the widest side" end` |

| `position try`
تلاش جایگاه
position-try | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. Shorthand for `position-try-order` and `position-try-fallbacks`. The order word, if any, comes first, then the list of fallbacks. [position-try-order then position-try-fallbacks, shorthand] | `box: position = absolute position anchor = "--tip" position area = top position try = "most-height flip-block" content = "Tries the taller side first" end` |

| `position visibility`
پیدایی جایگاه
position-visibility | A newer feature: Chromium browsers have it and others are catching up. When an anchored element is hidden. `always` never hides it, `anchors-visible` hides it when its anchor scrolls out of view, and `no-overflow` hides it when it would overflow its containing block. [up to 2 of always, anchors-visible, no-overflow] | `box: position = absolute position anchor = "--note" position area = right position visibility = "anchors-visible" content = "Hidden when the anchor is off screen" end` |

### SVG fill and stroke

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fill`
پرکردن
fill | The color that fills the inside of an SVG shape or SVG text. A color, `none` for no fill, or `url(#id)` to use a gradient or pattern. It is inherited, so setting it on the `svg` element paints every shape inside. [color / none] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = "#f97316"
content = "<circle cx=&#x27;20&#x27; cy=&#x27;20&#x27; r=&#x27;16&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `fill opacity`
شفافیت پرکردن
fill-opacity | How see-through the fill of an SVG shape is, from 0 (invisible) to 1 (solid), or as a percentage. The outline is not affected. [number / percentage] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = "#2563eb" fill opacity = 0.4 stroke = "#1e3a8a" stroke width = 2
content = "<rect x=&#x27;6&#x27; y=&#x27;6&#x27; width=&#x27;28&#x27; height=&#x27;28&#x27; rx=&#x27;4&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `fill rule`
قاعده پرکردن
fill-rule | Decides which points count as inside a shape that crosses itself. `nonzero` (the default) fills everything the path winds around. `evenodd` leaves a hole wherever the path crosses itself, like the middle of a star. [nonzero, evenodd] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = "#14b8a6" fill rule = "evenodd"
content = "<polygon points=&#x27;20,3 32,37 3,15 37,15 8,37&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `clip rule`
قاعده برش
clip-rule | The same choice as `fill-rule`, but for the shape used inside a `clipPath`: `nonzero` or `evenodd` decides which parts of the clipping shape let the picture show through. [nonzero, evenodd] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 clip rule = "evenodd"
content = "<defs><clipPath id=&#x27;c&#x27;><polygon points=&#x27;20,3 32,37 3,15 37,15 8,37&#x27; style=&#x27;clip-rule:inherit&#x27;/></clipPath></defs><rect width=&#x27;40&#x27; height=&#x27;40&#x27; fill=&#x27;#7c3aed&#x27; clip-path=&#x27;url(#c)&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke`
خط دور
stroke | The color of the line drawn along the edge of an SVG shape or text. A color, `none` for no line, or `url(#id)` for a gradient. Without a stroke only the fill shows. It is inherited. [color / none] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#dc2626" stroke width = 3
content = "<circle cx=&#x27;20&#x27; cy=&#x27;20&#x27; r=&#x27;14&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke width`
ضخامت خط دور
stroke-width | The thickness of the outline of an SVG shape, as a length or a percentage of the drawing size. The default is 1. A line is centred on the edge, so half of it falls inside the shape. [length / percentage] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#0f766e" stroke width = 6
content = "<rect x=&#x27;8&#x27; y=&#x27;8&#x27; width=&#x27;24&#x27; height=&#x27;24&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke opacity`
شفافیت خط دور
stroke-opacity | How see-through the outline of an SVG shape is, from 0 to 1 or as a percentage. The fill is not affected. [number / percentage] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = "#fde68a" stroke = "#7c2d12" stroke width = 6 stroke opacity = 0.35
content = "<circle cx=&#x27;20&#x27; cy=&#x27;20&#x27; r=&#x27;13&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke dasharray`
الگوی خط‌چین خط دور
stroke-dasharray | Turns the outline into dashes. A list of lengths that alternate between a dash and a gap, for example `6 3`. An odd number of values is repeated to make it even. `none` draws a solid line. [length / percentage / number; up to 99 values; comma list] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#2563eb" stroke width = 3 stroke dasharray = "6 3"
content = "<line x1=&#x27;4&#x27; y1=&#x27;20&#x27; x2=&#x27;36&#x27; y2=&#x27;20&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke dashoffset`
فاصله خط‌چین
stroke-dashoffset | Where in the dash pattern the line starts: a length or percentage that shifts the pattern along the line. Changing it over time makes marching ants and line drawing animations. [length / percentage] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#c2410c" stroke width = 3 stroke dasharray = "8 4" stroke dashoffset = 6
content = "<line x1=&#x27;4&#x27; y1=&#x27;20&#x27; x2=&#x27;36&#x27; y2=&#x27;20&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke linecap`
سر خط دور
stroke-linecap | The shape of the two ends of an open line: `butt` (flat, the default), `round` (a half circle) or `square` (flat, but longer by half the width). [butt, round, square] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#0f766e" stroke width = 8 stroke linecap = "round"
content = "<line x1=&#x27;10&#x27; y1=&#x27;20&#x27; x2=&#x27;30&#x27; y2=&#x27;20&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke linejoin`
اتصال خط دور
stroke-linejoin | The shape of a corner where two segments of a line meet: `miter` (a sharp point, the default), `round` or `bevel` (cut flat). [miter, round, bevel] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#7c3aed" stroke width = 8 stroke linejoin = "round"
content = "<polyline points=&#x27;6,32 20,8 34,32&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `stroke miterlimit`
حد گوشه خط دور
stroke-miterlimit | Limits how long a sharp corner may stretch. When the point would be longer than this number times the line width, the corner is cut flat like `bevel`. A number of 1 or more; the default is 4. [number] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 fill = none stroke = "#be123c" stroke width = 6 stroke linejoin = miter stroke miterlimit = 1.5
content = "<polyline points=&#x27;6,34 20,6 34,34&#x27;/>"
end` |

| `paint order`
ترتیب نقاشی
paint-order | The order in which fill, outline and markers of an SVG shape or text are drawn. `normal` is fill, then stroke, then markers. `stroke fill` draws the outline first, so the fill covers its inner half and the text looks outlined without thinning. [up to 3 values] | `svg: view box = "0 0 40 40" width = 80 height = 80 font size = 28 font weight = bold fill = "#fde68a" stroke = "#0f172a" stroke width = 5 paint order = "stroke fill"
content = "<text x=&#x27;4&#x27; y=&#x27;30&#x27;>Ab</text>"
end` |

### SVG text and baselines

### Reading order, top layer and HDR

| Property | What it does and what it accepts | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reading flow`

| `reading order`
ترتیب خواندن

| `overlay`
روکش

| `dynamic range limit`

[standard / no-limit / constrained / dynamic-range-limit-mix()] | `video: source: url = "clip.mp4" end dynamic range limit = "constrained" controls = true end` |

## Try it yourself

- Make a numbered table of contents for a page with three headings. Use one counter, `counter increment` on each heading and `generated content` with `counter()` to number them.

- Change the slide strip to a vertical one: `scroll snap type = "y mandatory"` with `overflow y` and a fixed `height`. Then give the container a `scroll padding top` and see how the slides stop.

- Add a fifth button to the tooltip example that sets the area to `"top right"`, and a sixth for `"bottom span-left"`. Which cell of the grid does each pick?

- Draw a house in an `svg`, a square and a triangle, and give both one `fill` and `stroke` on the `svg` element. Then use a `global` rule to give only the roof a dashed stroke.
