# Drag, touch, scroll and window

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/events-drag-touch/

A page often has to follow something that moves: a card carried across the screen, a finger on a phone, the scroll bar, the size of the window. This lesson covers the 27 events for that, shows each idea in a page you can run, and explains the traps that make drag and drop fail on the first try.

## Events that move

An event attribute takes a function. You can give it the name of a function declared above the `page:` block, a short lambda such as `(): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "hi") end`, or a plain JavaScript string. A function that needs the event itself takes one parameter, `e: i64`, and passes it to the helpers of the dom package: `dom.EventX(e)`, `dom.PreventDefault(e)`, `dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer")` and so on. The lesson on mouse events explains the model in full. Here you will use it for events that carry more data than a click: where the finger is, what is being dragged, how far the page has scrolled.

## Drag and drop

HTML has its own drag and drop, and it needs three parts. The element you pick up has `draggable = true` and a `drag start` handler that puts something in `dataTransfer`, the small package the browser carries during the drag. The place you drop on has a `drag over` handler that calls `dom.PreventDefault`, because the browser refuses every drop unless it is told that this place accepts one. And that place has a `drop` handler that takes the package out again.

In the example the package is the text `parcel`, set with `dom.CallS2(dt, "setData", ...)`. On drop, `getData` gives it back and the handler uses it to find the element and move it into the zone. `dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer")` returns the package as an object, and `dom.CallS1` and `dom.CallS2` call its methods with one or two strings.

web-drag-basic.salam

```salam
import dom

func lift(e: i64):
    dt := dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer")
    _ := dom.CallS2(dt, "setData", "text/plain", "parcel")
end

func allow(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
end

func land(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
    dt := dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer")
    id := dom.CallS1(dt, "getData", "text/plain")
    dom.Append(dom.ById("zone"), dom.ById("" + id))
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("status"), "Dropped: " + id)
end

page:
    title = "Drag and drop"
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: id = "parcel" draggable = true drag start = lift
        content = "Parcel" display = "inline-block" padding = "10px 20px" cursor = grab
        background = "#fde68a" border radius = 6
    end
    box: id = "zone" drag over = allow drop = land
        margin top = 20 padding = 30 min height = 40 border = "2px dashed #94a3b8" border radius = 8
        content = "Drop zone"
    end
    paragraph: id = "status" content = "Drag the parcel onto the zone." end
end
```

The most common reason a drop does nothing is a missing `drag over` handler. The second most common is a missing `setData` in `drag start`: Firefox does not start a drag at all without it. Write both, even when you do not need the data.

## Feedback while dragging

Four more events tell you what is going on. `drag` fires on the dragged element again and again, `drag end` fires once when the drag is over, and `drag enter` and `drag leave` fire on the places the item passes. A drop zone usually uses the last two to add and remove a highlight: a class that the `style:` element defines, switched with `dom.AddClass` and `dom.RemoveClass`.

The example also reads `dataTransfer.dropEffect` in `drag end`. It is `none` when the item was dropped on a place that did not accept it, so you can tell a successful drop from a cancelled one. Other values (`copy`, `move`) depend on the browser, so only compare with `none`.

web-drag-feedback.salam

```salam
import dom

mut ticks := 0

func begin(e: i64):
    dt := dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer")
    _ := dom.CallS2(dt, "setData", "text/plain", "note")
    ticks = 0
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), "drag start")
end

func moving():
    ticks += 1
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), "drag fired " + ticks + " times")
end

func over(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
end

func leave():
    dom.RemoveClass(dom.ById("zone"), "hot")
end

func drop(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
    leave()
end

func finish(e: i64):
    effect := dom.GetStr(dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer"), "dropEffect")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), "drag end, dropEffect = " + effect)
end

page:
    style: content = ".hot { background: #dcfce7; border-color: #16a34a }" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: id = "note" draggable = true drag start = begin drag = moving drag end = finish
        content = "Sticky note" display = "inline-block" padding = "10px 20px" background = "#fde68a"
    end
    box: id = "zone" drag over = over
        drag enter = (): dom.AddClass(dom.ById("zone"), "hot") end
        drag leave = leave drop = drop
        content = "Drop here" margin top = 20 padding = 30 border = "2px dashed #94a3b8" border radius = 8
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" content = "Nothing yet." end
end
```

## Moving items between lists

A board with columns is the same recipe with one change: the handlers are shared. `drag start` stores the id of the card in the package, and every column's `drop` reads the id, finds the card with `dom.ById` and appends it to the column that received the drop. `dom.GetProp(e, "currentTarget")` is the element the handler is attached to, so one function serves all columns even when the drop lands on a card inside the column. Each card and column here is a component, which keeps the page short.

web-drag-board.salam

```salam
import dom

component Task(key, label):
    box: id = key draggable = true drag start = lift content = label
        padding = "8px 12px" margin bottom = 8 background = "white" border radius = 6 cursor = grab
    end
end

component Column(key, label):
    box: id = key drag over = over drag leave = leave drop = land
        background = "#e2e8f0" border radius = 8 padding = 12 min height = 140 width = 150
        heading: size = 3 content = label margin = "0 0 10px" end
        content: end
    end
end

func lift(e: i64):
    dt := dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer")
    _ := dom.CallS2(dt, "setData", "text/plain", dom.GetStr(dom.EventTarget(e), "id"))
end

func over(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
    dom.AddClass(dom.GetProp(e, "currentTarget"), "hot")
end

func leave(e: i64):
    dom.RemoveClass(dom.GetProp(e, "currentTarget"), "hot")
end

func land(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
    column := dom.GetProp(e, "currentTarget")
    dom.RemoveClass(column, "hot")
    id := dom.CallS1(dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer"), "getData", "text/plain")
    dom.Append(column, dom.ById("" + id))
end

page:
    style: content = ".hot { outline: 2px solid #2563eb }" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: display = flex gap = 16
        Column: key = "todo" label = "To do" Task: key = "t1" label = "Write" end Task: key = "t2" label = "Test" end end
        Column: key = "doing" label = "Doing" Task: key = "t3" label = "Review" end end
        Column: key = "done" label = "Done" end
    end
end
```

Sorting inside one list needs a decision: before or after the row you dropped on? The example compares the pointer's height with the middle of that row, taken from `getBoundingClientRect`, and then puts the rows back in order with `dom.Append`, which moves an element that is already in the page.

web-drag-sort.salam

```salam
import dom

mut held := 0 as i64

component Row(key, label):
    box: id = key draggable = true drag start = pick drag over = over drop = land
        content = label padding = "10px 14px" margin bottom = 6 background = "#f1f5f9" border radius = 6 cursor = grab
    end
end

func pick(e: i64):
    held = dom.EventTarget(e)
    _ := dom.CallS2(dom.GetProp(e, "dataTransfer"), "setData", "text/plain", "row")
end

func over(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
end

func land(e: i64):
    dom.PreventDefault(e)
    target := dom.GetProp(e, "currentTarget")
    rect := dom.Call0(target, "getBoundingClientRect")
    middle := dom.GetNum(rect, "top") + dom.GetNum(rect, "height") / 2.0
    above := dom.EventY(e) < middle
    list := dom.ById("list")
    rows := dom.QueryAll("#list > div")
    repeat dom.CountOf(rows) in i:
        row := dom.ItemAt(rows, i)
        if row == target:
            if above: dom.Append(list, held) end
            dom.Append(list, row)
            if not above: dom.Append(list, held) end
        else row != held:
            dom.Append(list, row)
        end
    end
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 max width = 320 end
    box: id = "list"
        Row: key = "a" label = "Wake up" end
        Row: key = "b" label = "Make tea" end
        Row: key = "c" label = "Read the lesson" end
        Row: key = "d" label = "Write a page" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "hint" content = "Drag a row to a new place." end
end
```

## Pointer events

A mouse, a pen and a finger are all pointers, and pointer events cover them with one set of names: `pointer down`, `pointer move` and `pointer up`. New code uses these and leaves `mouse down` and `touch start` to old pages, because one handler then works on every device. `event.pointerType` tells which device it was.

The example drags a ball by hand, without HTML drag and drop. On `pointer down` it remembers where the pointer and the ball were. On each `pointer move` it adds the distance travelled to the ball's position with `dom.SetStyle`. The important call is `setPointerCapture`: it tells the browser to send all later events of this pointer to the ball, even when the pointer runs ahead of it or leaves it. The events `pointer capture start` and `pointer capture end` report when that begins and ends. The `touch action = none` property keeps a finger from scrolling the page instead.

web-drag-pointer.salam

```salam
import dom

mut dragging := false
mut startX := 0.0
mut startY := 0.0
mut baseX := 0.0
mut baseY := 0.0

func grab(e: i64):
    ball := dom.EventTarget(e)
    _ := dom.Call1(ball, "setPointerCapture", dom.GetNum(e, "pointerId"))
    dragging = true
    startX = dom.EventX(e)
    startY = dom.EventY(e)
    baseX = dom.GetNum(ball, "offsetLeft")
    baseY = dom.GetNum(ball, "offsetTop")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("info"), "pointer down (" + dom.GetStr(e, "pointerType") + ")")
end

func move(e: i64):
    if dragging:
        ball := dom.EventTarget(e)
        dom.SetStyle(ball, "left", (baseX + dom.EventX(e) - startX) + "px")
        dom.SetStyle(ball, "top", (baseY + dom.EventY(e) - startY) + "px")
    end
end

func release():
    dragging = false
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("info"), "pointer up")
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: position = relative width = 320 height = 180 background = "#e0f2fe" border radius = 10
        box: id = "ball" position = absolute left = 20 top = 20 width = 60 height = 60 background = "#0284c7"
            border radius = "50%" cursor = grab touch action = none
            pointer down = grab pointer move = move pointer up = release
            pointer capture start = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("cap"), "captured") end
            pointer capture end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("cap"), "released") end
        end
    end
    paragraph: id = "info" content = "Drag the ball." end
    paragraph: id = "cap" content = "-" end
end
```

Hand made dragging is the better choice when the item must follow the pointer exactly, as in a slider, a drawing tool or a game. HTML drag and drop is the better choice when something is carried to a drop target, and it comes with the browser's drag image and the keyboard escape for free.

## Entering and leaving

Four events tell where the pointer is. `pointer enter` and `pointer leave` fire once as the pointer comes and goes, and ignore the children of the element. `pointer over` and `pointer out` bubble, so they also fire when the pointer crosses between the element and a child. Pick enter and leave for hover effects. The fifth event, `pointer cancel`, means the browser took the pointer away, most often because a touch turned into a page scroll; end your gesture there.

web-drag-states.salam

```salam
import dom

mut trail := ""

func note(what: str):
    if trail.len() > 110: trail = "" end
    trail = trail + what + "  "
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("trail"), trail)
end

func sees(e: i64):
    note("over:" + dom.GetStr(dom.EventTarget(e), "id"))
end

func leaves(e: i64):
    note("out:" + dom.GetStr(dom.EventTarget(e), "id"))
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: id = "outer" width = 280 padding = 24 background = "#ede9fe" border radius = 10
        content = "outer"
        pointer enter = (): note("enter") end pointer leave = (): note("leave") end
        pointer over = sees pointer out = leaves
        pointer cancel = (): note("cancel") end
        box: id = "inner" margin top = 12 padding = 20 background = "#c4b5fd" border radius = 8 content = "inner" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "trail" white space = "pre-wrap" content = "Move a mouse, pen or finger over the boxes." end
end
```

In the log, a mouse that moves from the outer box into the inner one gives `out:outer` and then `over:inner`, with no `enter` or `leave`, because it never left the outer box.

## Touch events

Touch events came first, and they still exist: `touch start`, `touch move`, `touch end` and `touch cancel`. They give you every finger, which pointer events do one at a time. `dom.TouchX(e)` and `dom.TouchY(e)` read the position of the finger that changed, and `touches` counts all fingers on the screen, as the example shows. On `touch end` the finger is already gone from `touches`, so the last position comes from the changed finger.

The CSS property `touch action` belongs with these events. By default a finger that moves on the page may scroll or zoom it, and the browser then cancels your gesture. `touch action = none` on your element says that you handle it yourself. Use `pan-y` instead if the page may still scroll vertically.

web-drag-touch.salam

```salam
import dom

func place(e: i64):
    rect := dom.Call0(dom.ById("pad"), "getBoundingClientRect")
    mark := dom.ById("mark")
    dom.SetStyle(mark, "left", (dom.TouchX(e) - dom.GetNum(rect, "left") - 20.0) + "px")
    dom.SetStyle(mark, "top", (dom.TouchY(e) - dom.GetNum(rect, "top") - 20.0) + "px")
    dom.SetStyle(mark, "display", "block")
    fingers := dom.GetNum(dom.GetProp(e, "touches"), "length")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("info"), "fingers on the pad: " + fingers)
end

func lift(what: str):
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("mark"), "display", "none")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("info"), what)
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: id = "pad" position = relative width = 320 height = 180 background = "#fef3c7" border radius = 10
        touch action = none user select = none
        touch start = place touch move = place
        touch end = (): lift("touch end") end
        touch cancel = (): lift("touch cancel") end
        content = "Touch here with a finger"
        box: id = "mark" position = absolute display = none width = 40 height = 40 border radius = "50%" background = "#f59e0b" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "info" content = "Waiting for a touch." end
end
```

## Scroll and scroll end

`scroll` fires on a scrollable element every time its position changes, and a single flick causes dozens of events. Read `scrollTop`, `scrollHeight` and `clientHeight` with `dom.GetNum`: the first is how far you are, and the last two give the room there is. The example turns that into a progress bar. `scroll end` fires once when the movement has come to rest, which is the moment to save a position or load a picture. The button sets `scrollTop` back to zero with `dom.SetNum`, and `scroll behavior = smooth` makes that an animation.

web-drag-scroll-bar.salam

```salam
import dom

func fill_bar():
    area := dom.ById("text")
    room := dom.GetNum(area, "scrollHeight") - dom.GetNum(area, "clientHeight")
    percent := dom.GetNum(area, "scrollTop") * 100.0 / room
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("bar"), "width", percent + "%")
end

func settled():
    where := dom.GetNum(dom.ById("text"), "scrollTop")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("note"), "Scrolling stopped at " + where + " px.")
end

func to_top():
    dom.SetNum(dom.ById("text"), "scrollTop", 0.0)
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 max width = 420 end
    box: height = 6 background = "#e2e8f0" border radius = 3
        box: id = "bar" height = 6 width = "0%" background = "#2563eb" border radius = 3 end
    end
    box: id = "text" height = 150 overflow y = auto padding = "0 12px" border = "1px solid #cbd5e1"
        scroll behavior = smooth scroll = fill_bar scroll end = settled
        paragraph: repeat = 12 content = "Scrolling changes scrollTop, and every change fires a scroll event." end
    end
    button: click = to_top content = "Back to top" margin top = 10 end
    paragraph: id = "note" content = "Scroll the text above." end
end
```

An endless list is a scroll handler that checks how much room is left and adds items when it gets small. This one adds five paragraphs with `dom.Create` and `dom.Append` whenever the reader is within 30 pixels of the end.

web-drag-scroll-more.salam

```salam
import dom

mut total := 6 as i64

func load_more():
    feed := dom.ById("feed")
    left := dom.GetNum(feed, "scrollHeight") - dom.GetNum(feed, "scrollTop") - dom.GetNum(feed, "clientHeight")
    if left < 30.0:
        repeat 5 in i:
            item := dom.Create("p")
            dom.SetText(item, "Loaded item " + (total + i + 1))
            dom.Append(feed, item)
        end
        total += 5
        dom.SetText(dom.ById("count"), total + " items so far")
    end
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 max width = 360 end
    box: id = "feed" height = 130 overflow y = auto padding = "0 12px" background = "#f8fafc" border = "1px solid #cbd5e1" scroll = load_more
        paragraph: repeat = 6 content = "A first item" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "count" content = "6 items so far" end
end
```

Keep scroll handlers cheap, because they run very often. The example above does arithmetic and one style change. Work that is slow, such as a network request, belongs in `scroll end`, which runs once.

## The window, and images

Two events belong to the window and not to an element. `scroll` on the whole page and `resize` are fired at the window, and the page language cannot attach code to the window: the HTML attribute exists only on the `body` element, which a page does not write. The way out is to register them with `dom.OnWindow("scroll", ...)` and `dom.OnResize(...)`, and to run that registration from the `load` event of a one pixel image, which the browser fires as soon as the page is ready. The example shows the size of the window, and a progress bar for the whole page.

web-drag-window.salam

```salam
import dom

func show_size():
    text := "Window: " + dom.WinWidth() + " x " + dom.WinHeight() + " px"
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("size"), text)
end

func move_bar():
    room := dom.DocHeight() - dom.WinHeight()
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("bar"), "width", dom.ScrollY() * 100.0 / room + "%")
end

func listen():
    dom.OnResize((): show_size() end)
    dom.OnWindow("scroll", (): move_bar() end)
    show_size()
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 0 end
    image: source = "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==" alt = "" width = 1 height = 1 load = listen end
    box: position = fixed top = 0 left = 0 right = 0 height = 6 background = "#e2e8f0"
        box: id = "bar" height = 6 width = "0%" background = "#16a34a" end
    end
    box: padding = "24px 24px 600px"
        paragraph: id = "size" content = "Waiting for the page to load." end
        paragraph: content = "Resize the window and scroll the page. The bar at the top shows how far you have gone." end
    end
end
```

The `load` event also does its normal job on images, and so do `error` and `abort`. `error` fires when the file cannot be loaded or decoded, and the handler can put a spare picture in its place with `dom.SetAttr`. `abort` fires when loading is stopped half way, for example because the page changed the source. In the example the second picture is not an image at all, so it fails and the page swaps it for a spare. Check that the spare differs from the current source, or a broken spare would start an endless loop.

web-drag-image.salam

```salam
import dom

const SPARE := "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAMvV4QAAACwAAAAAAQABAAACAkQBADs="

mut lines := ""

func say(text: str):
    lines = lines + text + "\n"
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), lines)
end

func broken():
    img := dom.ById("second")
    if dom.GetAttr(img, "src") != SPARE:
        say("error: the second image is broken, using the spare")
        dom.SetAttr(img, "src", SPARE)
    end
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: display = flex gap = 16
        image: id = "first" alt = "A blue square" width = 80 height = 80 load = (): say("load: the first image arrived") end
            source = "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAKExwAAACwAAAAAAQABAAACAkQBADs="
        end
        image: id = "second" alt = "A picture" width = 80 height = 80 error = broken
            source = "data:image/png;base64,not-an-image"
            load = (): say("load: the second image is showing") end
        end
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" white space = "pre-wrap" content = "" end
end
```

## Reference: every event of this lesson

Each event is a global attribute, so it can go on any element, although some only make sense on certain ones. The examples are checked by the compiler. They use lambdas or short JavaScript strings; in a real page a function declared above the page is easier to read. Four events of this lesson end in end: `drag end`, `pointer capture end`, `touch end` and `scroll end`. In Persian their names start with `اتمام` and not `پایان`, because `پایان` on its own would end the element.

### Drag and drop

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drag start`
شروع کشیدن
ondragstart | Fires on the element you start dragging, once, when the drag begins. Put the data you want to carry into `dataTransfer` here. The element must have `draggable = true` (images and links already are). Firefox only starts a drag if you call `setData` in this event. | `box: draggable = true drag start = "event.dataTransfer.setData(&#x27;text/plain&#x27;, &#x27;card&#x27;)" content = "Drag me" end` |

| `drag`
کشیدن
ondrag | Fires on the dragged element again and again while the drag goes on, every few hundred milliseconds even if the mouse stands still. Use it for a live counter or a preview. For a drop target use `drag over` instead. | `box: draggable = true drag = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Dragging...") end content = "Drag me" end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `drag end`
اتمام کشیدن
ondragend | Fires once on the dragged element when the drag is over, whether it was dropped or cancelled with Escape. Read `dataTransfer.dropEffect` here: `none` means nobody accepted the drop. Use it to clean up what `drag start` changed. | `box: draggable = true drag end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The drag is over") end content = "Drag me" end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `drag enter`
ورود کشیدن
ondragenter | Fires on an element when something being dragged moves onto it. It also fires for the children of the element and bubbles, so a highlight that is removed in `drag leave` may flicker; a second check on `relatedTarget` or a counter solves that. To allow dropping, you still need `drag over`. | `box: id = "zone" drag enter = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("zone"), "Something arrived") end content = "Drop zone" padding = 30 end` |

| `drag leave`
خروج کشیدن
ondragleave | Fires on an element when the dragged item leaves it, and also when it moves onto a child of the element. It fires after a drop is cancelled too. Pair it with `drag enter` to add and remove a highlight. | `box: id = "zone" drag leave = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("zone"), "Left the zone") end content = "Drop zone" padding = 30 end` |

| `drag over`
عبور کشیدن
ondragover | Fires on the element under the dragged item every few hundred milliseconds. The browser refuses a drop unless this event is cancelled, so every drop target needs a handler that calls `event.preventDefault()` (`dom.PreventDefault(e)` in a function). The short JavaScript string below does exactly that. | `box: drag over = "event.preventDefault()" content = "Drop target" padding = 30 end` |

| `drop`
رها کردن
ondrop | Fires on the target when the user releases the dragged item over it, but only if `drag over` was cancelled on that target. Read what the item carries with `dataTransfer.getData`, and call `preventDefault` so the browser does not also open a dropped link or file. | `box: id = "zone" drag over = "event.preventDefault()" drop = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("zone"), "Dropped!") end content = "Drop here" padding = 30 end` |

### Pointer

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pointer down`
فشردن اشاره‌گر
onpointerdown | Fires when a mouse button goes down, a pen touches the screen or a finger touches it, one event for all three. `pointerType` tells which one it was. It replaces `mouse down` and `touch start` in new code. | `box: pointer down = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Pointer down") end content = "Touch here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer up`
رها کردن اشاره‌گر
onpointerup | Fires when the button is released or the finger or pen lifts, on the element under the pointer (or on the element that captured it). It does not fire after `pointer cancel`. | `box: pointer up = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Pointer up") end content = "Press and release" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer move`
حرکت اشاره‌گر
onpointermove | Fires whenever the pointer moves over the element, very often. Read the position with `dom.EventX` and `dom.EventY`. To follow a pointer that has left the element, capture it with `setPointerCapture` in `pointer down`. | `box: pointer move = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Moving") end content = "Move over me" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer enter`
ورود اشاره‌گر
onpointerenter | Fires once when the pointer moves onto the element or onto one of its children. It does not bubble, and moving between the element and its children does not fire it again, which makes it the right event for hover effects. Touch fires it at the start of a touch. | `box: pointer enter = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Entered") end content = "Hover me" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer leave`
خروج اشاره‌گر
onpointerleave | Fires once when the pointer leaves the element and all of its children. It does not bubble. It is the partner of `pointer enter`. After a touch ends it fires too. | `box: pointer leave = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Left") end content = "Hover me" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer over`
عبور اشاره‌گر
onpointerover | Fires when the pointer moves onto the element or onto a child. Unlike `pointer enter` it bubbles and fires again each time the pointer crosses into a child, so `event.target` tells which element it is over. | `box: pointer over = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Over") end content = "Hover me" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer out`
بیرون رفتن اشاره‌گر
onpointerout | Fires when the pointer leaves the element or moves onto a child of it. It bubbles. It is the partner of `pointer over`. | `box: pointer out = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Out") end content = "Hover me" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer cancel`
لغو اشاره‌گر
onpointercancel | Fires when the browser takes the pointer away from you, most often because a touch turned into a scroll or a zoom. No `pointer up` follows, so end your gesture here. The CSS property `touch action` tells the browser which touches you handle yourself. | `box: pointer cancel = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Cancelled") end content = "Touch and drag away" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer capture start`
شروع ضبط اشاره‌گر
ongotpointercapture | Fires on the element after it captured the pointer with `setPointerCapture` (HTML name `ongotpointercapture`). From then on all pointer events of that pointer go to this element, even when the pointer is far outside it. That is what makes a drag by hand reliable. | `box: pointer down = "event.target.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)" pointer capture start = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Captured") end content = "Press here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pointer capture end`
اتمام ضبط اشاره‌گر
onlostpointercapture | Fires on the element when it loses the pointer capture (HTML name `onlostpointercapture`): after `pointer up` or `pointer cancel`, or when you call `releasePointerCapture`. Clean up the drag here. | `box: pointer down = "event.target.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)" pointer capture end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Released") end content = "Press here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

### Touch

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `touch start`
شروع لمس
ontouchstart | Fires when a finger touches the element. `dom.TouchX` and `dom.TouchY` read the position of the touch that changed, and `touches` lists all fingers on the screen. For one handler that also works with a mouse prefer `pointer down`. | `box: touch start = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "A finger touched") end content = "Touch here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `touch move`
حرکت لمس
ontouchmove | Fires over and over while a finger that started on this element moves. A page scrolls with such moves unless you set `touch action = none` on the element, so set it when you want to handle the gesture yourself. | `box: touch move = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The finger is moving") end content = "Slide here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `touch end`
اتمام لمس
ontouchend | Fires when a finger lifts from the screen. The finger is no longer in `touches`; its last position is in `changedTouches`, which is what `dom.TouchX` reads. | `box: touch end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The finger lifted") end content = "Touch here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `touch cancel`
لغو لمس
ontouchcancel | Fires when the system interrupts a touch, for example a call arrives, the browser takes the gesture for scrolling, or too many fingers are down. Treat it like `touch end` without a result: drop what the gesture started. | `box: touch cancel = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The touch was interrupted") end content = "Touch here" padding = 30 touch action = none end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

### Scroll, window and loading

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `abort`
لغو
onabort | Fires on an image or a media element when loading is stopped before it finished and it was not an error, for example because the page changed the `src` while the first file was still arriving. A file that cannot be loaded fires `error` instead. | `image: source = "/photos/large.jpg" alt = "A large photo" abort = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Loading was stopped") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `error`
خطا
onerror | Fires on an image, script, media element or style link when its file cannot be loaded or decoded. The usual use is to swap in a spare picture. Set the new `src` only if it differs from the current one, or a broken spare makes an endless loop. | `image: source = "/photos/missing.png" alt = "Logo" error = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The logo could not be loaded") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `load`
بار شد
onload | Fires on an image, frame or similar element when its file has finished loading. It is also the way to run code at the start of a page: the page language cannot attach code to the whole window, but a tiny image that loads at once can, as this snippet does to listen to window resizes. | `image: source = "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==" alt = "" width = 1 height = 1 load = (): dom.OnResize((): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Width " + dom.WinWidth()) end) end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `window resize`
تغییر اندازه پنجره
onresize | The browser fires `resize` only at the window, and HTML only lets you write it on the `body` element, which a page cannot reach. On an ordinary element this attribute never fires. To react to a window resize use `dom.OnResize` (registered from a `load` handler, as here) or, for layout changes, a media query. | `image: source = "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==" alt = "" width = 1 height = 1 load = (): dom.OnResize((): dom.SetText(dom.ById("size"), "" + dom.WinWidth()) end) end end
paragraph: id = "size" content = "-" end` |

| `scroll`
پیمایش
onscroll | Fires on a scrollable element every time its scroll position changes, many times during one flick. Keep the handler small. It is the event for progress bars, a back-to-top button that appears late, and loading more items near the bottom. | `box: height = 80 overflow y = auto scroll = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Scrolled") end
paragraph: repeat = 10 content = "A line of text" end
end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `scroll end`
اتمام پیمایش
onscrollend | Fires once when scrolling has come to rest, after the finger lifts and any momentum or smooth scrolling is over. It is newer than `scroll`, and Safari added it last, so check the browsers you must support. Use it for work that should wait until the movement stops, such as saving the position. | `box: height = 80 overflow y = auto scroll end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Scrolling stopped") end
paragraph: repeat = 10 content = "A line of text" end
end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

## Try it yourself

- Turn the sortable list into a to-do list: a second list called Done, and a drop on it moves the row there and strikes the text through.

- Add a slider to the pointer example: a track and a handle that you drag only sideways, and a paragraph that shows the value from 0 to 100.

- Make a gallery of three images in which the second one has a wrong file name. Show a grey spare for it with the `error` event.

- Combine the scroll progress bar with `scroll end` so that the position of the text is saved in `dom.StoreSetInt` when the reader stops.

# Media, animation and other events

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/learn/events-media-more/

Sound, video, animations and transitions all report what they are doing through events, and so do a few special parts of the page: slots, canvases and the security policy. This lesson covers the 33 events for them, builds a small player, and says exactly when the browser fires the ones you cannot trigger by hand.

## Media elements and a sound to play

The `audio` and `video` elements play a file and report what happens to it. Their attributes are `source` (the file), `controls` (the browser's own buttons), `preload` (how much to fetch before the user presses play: `none`, `metadata` or `auto`), `loop` and `muted`. Their events follow the life of the file: it starts loading, it knows its length, it can play, it plays, it ends. Event attributes work as in the previous lesson: a function name, a short lambda, or a JavaScript string.

The examples of this lesson have no network, so they make their own sound. The function `clip` returns a WAV file as a `data:` address: a 54 byte header, written in base64, and a short square wave tone that is added 400 times, which makes three seconds of beeping. Every example sets the `src` of the audio element from a button, so you see the load events in their real order. Browsers only play sound after the user clicked something on the page, so the Play buttons are real clicks, not code that runs on load.

## The life of a media file

This page logs the events of loading and playing. Press Load, then Play, and compare the log with the list below. The log is what Chrome produces; the order of neighbours such as `suspend` and `loaded data` can differ in other browsers.

web-mediaev-log.salam

```salam
import dom

mut lines := ""
mut count := 0 as i64

func say(what: str):
    if count == 12: lines = "" count = 0 end
    lines = lines + what + "\n"
    count += 1
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), lines)
end

func clip(): str:
    mut sound := "data:audio/wav;base64,UklGRu5dAABXQVZFZm10IBAAAAABAAEAQB8AAEAfAAABAAgASlVOSwIAAAAAAGRhdGHAXQAA"
    repeat 400: sound += "oKCgoKCgoKCgoGBgYGBgYGBgYGCgoKCgoKCgoKCgYGBgYGBgYGBgYKCgoKCgoKCgoKBgYGBgYGBgYGBg" end
    ret sound
end

func load_clip():
    dom.SetAttr(dom.ById("sound"), "src", clip())
end

func play_clip():
    _ := dom.Call0(dom.ById("sound"), "play")
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    audio: id = "sound" controls = true preload = "none"
        load start = (): say("load start") end
        suspend = (): say("suspend") end
        loaded metadata = (): say("loaded metadata") end
        loaded data = (): say("loaded data") end
        can play = (): say("can play") end
        can play through = (): say("can play through") end
        play = (): say("play") end
        playing = (): say("playing") end
        pause = (): say("pause") end
        ended = (): say("ended") end
    end
    box: display = flex gap = 8
        button: click = load_clip content = "Load the sound" end
        button: click = play_clip content = "Play" end
        button: click = (): _ := dom.Call0(dom.ById("sound"), "pause") end content = "Pause" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" white space = "pre-wrap" content = "Events appear here." end
end
```

- `load start`: the browser begins to fetch the file.

- `suspend`: it stopped fetching on purpose. With `preload = "none"` it waits for the first play, and later it also stops when its buffer is full.

- `loaded metadata`: the length (and, for video, the size) is known. Read `duration` here.

- `loaded data`: the first moment can be shown.

- `can play`: enough data to start. `can play through`: enough to reach the end at the current speed.

- `play`: playing was requested. `playing`: it is really running. `pause` and `ended` close the story.

One thing deserves a name: `play` and `playing` are not the same. `play` fires the moment the button is pressed, even when no data has arrived. `playing` fires when sound or picture is moving, and again after every pause for buffering. A button that must show Pause should follow `playing` and `pause`, not the click.

Do not set `src` after the page asked for `play()` and expect the old sound to go on. Changing the source resets the element, and the browser fires `emptied` and starts the whole life cycle again.

## A small custom player

The browser's controls are fine, but a page often wants its own. The example has a button, a progress bar and a volume slider, and every part reacts to an event instead of to the click that caused it. `play` and `pause` change the label of the button, so it is right even when something else pauses the sound. `time update` fires about four times a second and moves the bar with the share `currentTime / duration`. `volume change` writes the new volume next to the slider. The slider itself sets `volume` from its `input` event.

The state of the element is read with `dom.GetNum` and `dom.GetBool` (`currentTime`, `duration`, `paused`) and changed with `dom.SetNum` and `dom.Call0`, which calls methods such as `play` and `pause`.

web-mediaev-player.salam

```salam
import dom

func clip(): str:
    mut sound := "data:audio/wav;base64,UklGRu5dAABXQVZFZm10IBAAAAABAAEAQB8AAEAfAAABAAgASlVOSwIAAAAAAGRhdGHAXQAA"
    repeat 400: sound += "oKCgoKCgoKCgoGBgYGBgYGBgYGCgoKCgoKCgoKCgYGBgYGBgYGBgYKCgoKCgoKCgoKBgYGBgYGBgYGBg" end
    ret sound
end

func play_pause():
    sound := dom.ById("sound")
    if dom.GetAttr(sound, "src") == "":
        dom.SetAttr(sound, "src", clip())
    end
    if dom.GetBool(sound, "paused"):
        _ := dom.Call0(sound, "play")
    else:
        _ := dom.Call0(sound, "pause")
    end
end

func move_bar():
    sound := dom.ById("sound")
    now := dom.GetNum(sound, "currentTime")
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("fill"), "width", now * 100.0 / dom.GetNum(sound, "duration") + "%")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("time"), dom.Call1(dom.Global("Math"), "floor", now) + " s of 3 s")
end

func set_volume():
    dom.SetNum(dom.ById("sound"), "volume", dom.GetNum(dom.ById("level"), "valueAsNumber") / 100.0)
end

func show_volume():
    percent := dom.Call1(dom.Global("Math"), "round", dom.GetNum(dom.ById("sound"), "volume") * 100.0)
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("say"), "Volume " + percent + "%")
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 max width = 360 end
    audio: id = "sound" preload = "none" play = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("go"), "Pause") end
        pause = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("go"), "Play") end time update = move_bar volume change = show_volume
    end
    box: display = flex gap = 12 align items = center
        button: id = "go" click = play_pause content = "Play" width = 70 end
        box: flex = 1 height = 8 background = "#e2e8f0" border radius = 4
            box: id = "fill" width = "0%" height = 8 background = "#7c3aed" border radius = 4 end
        end
    end
    paragraph: id = "time" content = "0 s of 3 s" end
    box: display = flex gap = 12 align items = center
        input: id = "level" type = "range" min = 0 max = 100 value = 100 input = set_volume end
        span: id = "say" content = "Volume 100%" end
    end
end
```

## Seeking, speed and length

`seeking` fires when a jump to another time starts and `seeked` when it is finished. Setting `currentTime` causes both, and so does the user dragging the slider of the browser controls. `rate change` fires when `playbackRate` changes: 1 is normal, 0.5 is half speed. `duration change` fires when the length becomes known or changes, and `emptied` when the element is reset, as the Reset button does by calling `load()`.

web-mediaev-seek.salam

```salam
import dom

mut lines := ""

func say(what: str):
    lines = lines + what + "\n"
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), lines)
end

func clip(): str:
    mut sound := "data:audio/wav;base64,UklGRu5dAABXQVZFZm10IBAAAAABAAEAQB8AAEAfAAABAAgASlVOSwIAAAAAAGRhdGHAXQAA"
    repeat 400: sound += "oKCgoKCgoKCgoGBgYGBgYGBgYGCgoKCgoKCgoKCgYGBgYGBgYGBgYKCgoKCgoKCgoKBgYGBgYGBgYGBg" end
    ret sound
end

func load_clip():
    dom.SetAttr(dom.ById("sound"), "src", clip())
end

func skip():
    dom.SetNum(dom.ById("sound"), "currentTime", 2.0)
end

func set_speed(rate: f64):
    dom.SetNum(dom.ById("sound"), "playbackRate", rate)
end

func restart():
    _ := dom.Call0(dom.ById("sound"), "load")
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    audio: id = "sound" preload = "auto"
        duration change = (): say("duration change: " + dom.GetNum(dom.ById("sound"), "duration") + " s") end
        seeking = (): say("seeking") end seeked = (): say("seeked") end
        rate change = (): say("rate change: " + dom.GetNum(dom.ById("sound"), "playbackRate")) end
        emptied = (): say("emptied") end
    end
    box: display = flex gap = 8 flex wrap = wrap
        button: click = load_clip content = "Load" end
        button: click = skip content = "Jump to 2 s" end
        button: click = (): set_speed(0.5) end content = "Half speed" end
        button: click = (): set_speed(1.0) end content = "Normal speed" end
        button: click = restart content = "Reset" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" white space = "pre-wrap" content = "Press Load first." end
end
```

## Captions and cue change

A `track` element inside an audio or video element holds captions in the WebVTT format, a plain text file with time ranges. Its `cue change` event fires whenever a caption begins or ends. The text of the current one is in `track.activeCues`: the example reads the list with `dom.GetProp`, checks its `length`, and shows the first cue's `text` in a heading. The track needs `default = true` (or a script that sets its mode) or no cues become active. The page language accepts only ordinary addresses for the file, so the example gives the track a placeholder name and sets the real `src`, a `data:` address, from code when Play is pressed.

web-mediaev-cues.salam

```salam
import dom

const WORDS := "data:text/vtt,WEBVTT%0A%0A00:00.000 --> 00:01.000%0ASalam%0A%0A00:01.000 --> 00:02.000%0Aeveryone%0A%0A00:02.000 --> 00:03.000%0Awelcome"

func show_cue():
    cues := dom.GetProp(dom.GetProp(dom.ById("words"), "track"), "activeCues")
    if dom.GetNum(cues, "length") > 0.0:
        dom.SetText(dom.ById("line"), dom.GetStr(dom.ItemAt(cues, 0), "text"))
    else:
        dom.SetText(dom.ById("line"), "...")
    end
end

func clip(): str:
    mut sound := "data:audio/wav;base64,UklGRu5dAABXQVZFZm10IBAAAAABAAEAQB8AAEAfAAABAAgASlVOSwIAAAAAAGRhdGHAXQAA"
    repeat 400: sound += "oKCgoKCgoKCgoGBgYGBgYGBgYGCgoKCgoKCgoKCgYGBgYGBgYGBgYKCgoKCgoKCgoKBgYGBgYGBgYGBg" end
    ret sound
end

func play_captioned():
    sound := dom.ById("sound")
    dom.SetAttr(dom.ById("words"), "src", WORDS)
    dom.SetAttr(sound, "src", clip())
    _ := dom.Call0(sound, "play")
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    audio: id = "sound" controls = true
        track: id = "words" kind = "captions" default = true cue change = show_cue source = "captions.vtt"
        end
    end
    button: click = play_captioned content = "Play with captions" end
    heading: size = 2 id = "line" content = "Press play." end
end
```

## Animation events

A CSS animation moves an element by itself, and four events tell what stage it is at. `animation start` fires when it begins, `animation iteration` at the end of each round except the last, `animation end` after the last round, and `animation cancel` if it is cut off: for instance when the element is hidden with `display: none`. The animation here is defined in a `style:` element with `@keyframes`, and a class switches it on, three rounds of half a second each. So the log of an uninterrupted run is one start, two iterations and one end, and a cancelled run is a start and a cancel.

The end handler removes the class, which lets the button start it again. That is the usual job of `animation end`. An animation that never ends (`infinite`) never fires it.

web-mediaev-animation.salam

```salam
import dom

mut lines := ""

func say(what: str):
    lines = lines + what + "\n"
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), lines)
end

func run_ball():
    lines = ""
    dom.AddClass(dom.ById("ball"), "run")
end

func run_over():
    dom.RemoveClass(dom.ById("ball"), "run")
    say("animation end")
end

func restore():
    dom.RemoveClass(dom.ById("ball"), "run")
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("ball"), "display", "")
end

func cancel_ball():
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("ball"), "display", "none")
    dom.SetTimeout((): restore() end, 300)
end

page:
    style: content = "@keyframes slide { to { transform: translateX(200px) } } .run { animation: slide 0.5s ease-in-out 3 }" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: width = 260 padding = "10px 0"
        box: id = "ball" width = 40 height = 40 border radius = "50%" background = "#e11d48"
            animation start = (): say("animation start") end
            animation iteration = (): say("animation iteration") end
            animation end = run_over
            animation cancel = (): say("animation cancel") end
        end
    end
    box: display = flex gap = 8
        button: click = run_ball content = "Run 3 times" end
        button: click = cancel_ball content = "Cancel it" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" white space = "pre-wrap" content = "" end
end
```

## Transition events

A transition is the smooth change of a property after it was set, and it has four events. `transition run` fires when the transition is created, before its delay. `transition start` fires when the delay is over and the value begins to move. `transition end` fires when it arrives. `transition cancel` fires when something interrupts it. All four carry `propertyName`, so a transition of two properties fires each event twice. The example gives the move a delay of 0.3 seconds, so run and start are visible apart, and the second button flips the class twice at once to cut the transition off.

There is one trap that is not in your code. In our tests Chromium, the engine of Chrome and Edge, read `transition end` from an HTML attribute but not `transition run`, `transition start` or `transition cancel`; Firefox reads all four. Writing them as attributes compiles and works in Firefox, and silently does nothing in Chrome. The reliable way is `dom.OnEventE(element, "transitionrun", ...)`, which the example uses for those three, and it also shows the plain attribute for `transition end`.

web-mediaev-transition.salam

```salam
import dom

mut lines := ""
mut wired := false

func record(kind: str, e: i64):
    lines = lines + kind + ": " + dom.GetStr(e, "propertyName") + "\n"
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), lines)
end

func transition_ended(e: i64):
    record("end", e)
end

func wire_events():
    if not wired:
        wired = true
        chip := dom.ById("chip")
        dom.OnEventE(chip, "transitionrun", (e: i64): record("run", e) end)
        dom.OnEventE(chip, "transitionstart", (e: i64): record("start", e) end)
        dom.OnEventE(chip, "transitioncancel", (e: i64): record("cancel", e) end)
    end
end

func move_chip():
    wire_events()
    lines = ""
    dom.ToggleClass(dom.ById("chip"), "moved")
end

func move_and_undo():
    move_chip()
    dom.SetTimeout((): dom.ToggleClass(dom.ById("chip"), "moved") end, 150)
end

page:
    style: content = ".moved { transform: translateX(180px) }" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: width = 240 padding = "10px 0"
        box: id = "chip" width = 50 height = 40 border radius = 8 background = "#2563eb"
            transition = "transform 0.4s 0.3s" transition end = transition_ended
        end
    end
    box: display = flex gap = 8
        button: click = move_chip content = "Move it" end
        button: click = move_and_undo content = "Move and undo" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" white space = "pre-wrap" content = "" end
end
```

## Slots and slot change

A `template` with `shadow root mode = "open"` turns its parent into a shadow host: the content of the template becomes a separate little tree, and the original children of the host are shown wherever a `slot` is. `slot change` fires on the slot when the nodes that fill it change, so it is how a component notices that someone added a child. `assignedNodes()`, called with `dom.Call0`, lists them. Page styles do not reach inside a shadow tree, which is why the example puts the colours on the host.

web-mediaev-slot.salam

```salam
import dom

mut members := 0 as i64

func slot_changed(e: i64):
    nodes := dom.Call0(dom.EventTarget(e), "assignedNodes")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), "slot change: " + dom.GetNum(nodes, "length") + " in the slot")
end

func add_member():
    members += 1
    person := dom.Create("p")
    dom.SetText(person, "Member " + members)
    dom.Append(dom.ById("team"), person)
end

page:
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: id = "team" padding = "4px 16px" background = "#f5f3ff" border = "2px solid #7c3aed" border radius = 8
        template: shadow root mode = "open"
            heading: size = 3 content = "Team" end
            slot: slot change = slot_changed end
        end
    end
    button: click = add_member content = "Add a member" margin top = 12 end
    paragraph: id = "log" content = "Nothing in the slot yet." end
end
```

## Security policy violations

A Content Security Policy is a list of things a page promises not to do, set by a `meta` element with `http equiv = "Content-Security-Policy"` or by a header. When the page breaks its own promise the browser blocks the act and fires `security policy violation`, with the blocked address in `blockedURI` and the rule in `violatedDirective`. The example forbids style attributes. Setting one with `dom.SetAttr(el, "style", ...)` is blocked and reported on the element itself, while `dom.SetStyle` works because it changes the style object, not the attribute. Some violations, such as a blocked image, are reported on the document and not on the element.

web-mediaev-policy.salam

```salam
import dom

func blocked(e: i64):
    what := dom.GetStr(e, "blockedURI")
    rule := dom.GetStr(e, "violatedDirective")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), "Blocked: " + what + " (" + rule + ")")
end

func by_attribute():
    dom.SetAttr(dom.ById("card"), "style", "background: gold")
end

func by_property():
    dom.SetStyle(dom.ById("card"), "background", "lightgreen")
    dom.SetText(dom.ById("log"), "SetStyle worked.")
end

page:
    meta: http equiv = "Content-Security-Policy" content = "style-src-attr 'none'" end
    global: selector = "body" font family = "system-ui, sans-serif" margin = 24 end
    box: id = "card" security policy violation = blocked padding = 20 border radius = 8 background = "#e2e8f0"
        content = "This card's style attribute is forbidden by the page's policy."
    end
    box: display = flex gap = 8 margin top = 12
        button: click = by_attribute content = "Set the style attribute" end
        button: click = by_property content = "Use SetStyle" end
    end
    paragraph: id = "log" content = "No violation yet." end
end
```

## Events you cannot trigger here

A few events need a network that fails or a graphics system that breaks, so no example can show them. This is when the browser fires them.

- `stalled`: it wants more data and none has come for a few seconds, for example on a slow mobile connection. It may recover on its own.

- `waiting`: playback stopped because the buffer ran dry. `playing` follows when data arrives again. Show a spinner between them.

- `progress`: the browser downloaded another chunk of a remote file. A short `data:` address does not produce it.

- `context lost` and `context restored`: a 2D canvas loses its memory when the graphics driver resets or the system switches graphics cards, and gets an empty drawing back when it recovers. Everything on it has to be drawn again in `context restored`. A page cannot cause it.

## Reference: every event of this lesson

All of these are global attributes, but each one only fires on the elements named in its description. The examples are compiled by the checker; where an example needs a media file it uses an address that does not exist, so the event is described and not run. Three events of this lesson end in end or ended: `ended`, `animation end` and `transition end`. In Persian their names start with `اتمام` and not `پایان`, because `پایان` on its own would end the element.

### Loading

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `load start`
شروع بارگذاری
onloadstart | Fires on an audio or video element when the browser starts to load its file, right after `src` is set or `load()` is called. It is the first event in the life of a media file. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" load start = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Loading started") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `progress`
پیشرفت
onprogress | Fires every so often while the browser is downloading the file. Read `buffered` to see which time ranges are already there. Do not confuse it with `time update`, which is about playing. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" progress = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "More data downloaded") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `suspend`
تعلیق
onsuspend | Fires when the browser stops downloading on purpose and without an error: the buffer is full, or `preload = none` says to wait for the user. It is not a problem; downloading starts again when needed. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" suspend = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Download paused") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `stalled`
متوقف شده
onstalled | Fires when the browser wants more data but none has come for some seconds, for example when the connection is bad. It may recover by itself. You cannot cause it without a slow network, so a page usually only shows a hint when it fires. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" stalled = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The data stopped coming") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `loaded metadata`
بارگذاری ابرداده
onloadedmetadata | Fires when the browser knows the duration and, for video, the size, but may not have any sound or picture yet. Read `duration` here, for example to size a progress bar. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" loaded metadata = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Duration is known") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `duration change`
تغییر مدت
ondurationchange | Fires when `duration` changes: when metadata arrives (from not a number to a real length), when the source changes, and for streams whose length grows. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" duration change = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The length changed") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `loaded data`
بارگذاری داده
onloadeddata | Fires when the first moment of the media can be shown, the first video frame or the first sound. It comes after `loaded metadata`. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" loaded data = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The first data arrived") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `can play`
قابل پخش
oncanplay | Fires when enough data has arrived to start playing from the current position, although more may have to be loaded while it plays. It is the moment to enable a Play button. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" can play = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Ready to play") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `can play through`
قابل پخش کامل
oncanplaythrough | Fires when the browser estimates that, at the current download speed, it can play to the end without stopping to buffer. For a short local file it comes right after `can play`. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" can play through = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Can play to the end") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `emptied`
خالی شدن
onemptied | Fires when the media is reset to its start, because `load()` was called or the source changed after something had loaded. The old duration and position are gone. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" emptied = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The media was reset") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

### Playing

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `play`
پخش
onplay | Fires when playback is asked for: the user pressed play or the code called `play()`. Data may not have arrived yet, so sound can start a moment later; `playing` says when it really does. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" play = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Play was requested") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `playing`
در حال پخش
onplaying | Fires when playback is really running, after `play` and also after a pause for buffering ended (`waiting`). Use it, not `play`, for a button that shows Pause. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" playing = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "It is playing") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `pause`
مکث
onpause | Fires when playback is paused, by the user, by `pause()`, or by the browser just before `ended`. A paused element keeps its position. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" pause = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Paused") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `ended`
اتمام پخش
onended | Fires when playback reaches the end and the element does not `loop`. A `pause` event comes just before it. Use it to show a Play again button or start the next track. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" ended = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Playback finished") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `time update`
به‌روزرسانی زمان
ontimeupdate | Fires when `currentTime` changes, about four times a second while playing and also after a jump. It is the event that moves a progress bar. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" time update = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The time moved") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `seeking`
در حال جابجایی
onseeking | Fires when a jump to another time begins, because the user dragged the slider or the code set `currentTime`. The picture may not be there yet. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" seeking = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Seeking") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `seeked`
جابجا شده
onseeked | Fires when the jump has finished and the media can play from the new time. It is the partner of `seeking`. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" seeked = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The jump is done") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `waiting`
در انتظار
onwaiting | Fires when playback stops because the next data has not arrived, and will go on by itself when it does; `playing` follows. Show a spinner between the two. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" waiting = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Waiting for data") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `volume change`
تغییر صدا
onvolumechange | Fires when `volume` or `muted` changes. The value is from 0 (silent) to 1 (full); read it to update a slider or an icon. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" volume change = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The volume changed") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `rate change`
تغییر سرعت
onratechange | Fires when `playbackRate` or `defaultPlaybackRate` changes. 1 is normal speed, 0.5 half speed, 2 double speed. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/bell.mp3" rate change = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The speed changed") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `cue change`
تغییر نشانه
oncuechange | Fires on a `track` element when the set of active cues changes: a caption starts or ends. Read `track.activeCues` to get the text. The track must be showing or hidden, which `default = true` on a captions track does. | `audio: controls = true source = "/sounds/talk.mp3"
track: kind = "captions" source = "/captions/talk.vtt" default = true cue change = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "A caption changed") end end
end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

### Animations and transitions

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `animation start`
شروع پویانمایی
onanimationstart | Fires on an element when a CSS animation starts, after any `animation-delay`. `event.animationName` says which animation. It does not fire when the animation has a duration of zero. | `box: animation = "spin 2s linear 3" animation start = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The animation started") end content = "Spin" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `animation iteration`
تکرار پویانمایی
onanimationiteration | Fires at the end of each round of an animation that repeats, except the last one (that fires `animation end`). An animation that runs three times fires it twice. | `box: animation = "spin 2s linear 3" animation iteration = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Another round") end content = "Spin" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `animation end`
اتمام پویانمایی
onanimationend | Fires when a CSS animation has finished all its rounds. An animation that repeats forever (`infinite`) never fires it. Use it to remove a class that started the animation. | `box: animation = "fade 1s" animation end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The animation ended") end content = "Fade" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `animation cancel`
لغو پویانمایی
onanimationcancel | Fires when a running animation is cut short without finishing: its element is hidden with `display: none`, removed from the page, or the `animation` property is taken away. No `animation end` follows. | `box: animation = "spin 2s linear infinite" animation cancel = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The animation was cancelled") end content = "Spin" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `transition run`
اجرای گذار
ontransitionrun | Fires when a CSS transition is created, before its delay. `event.propertyName` says which property moves. In our tests Chromium (the engine of Chrome and Edge) did not read this one as an HTML attribute, while Firefox did; attach it with `dom.OnEventE(el, "transitionrun", ...)` to be safe. | `box: transition = "transform 0.4s 0.3s" hover transform = "scale(1.2)" transition run = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The transition was created") end content = "Hover me" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `transition start`
شروع گذار
ontransitionstart | Fires when the transition really begins to move, after its delay is over. Without a delay it comes right after `transition run`. In our tests Chromium (the engine of Chrome and Edge) did not read it as an HTML attribute, while Firefox did; attach it with `dom.OnEventE(el, "transitionstart", ...)`. | `box: transition = "transform 0.4s 0.3s" hover transform = "scale(1.2)" transition start = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The movement began") end content = "Hover me" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `transition end`
اتمام گذار
ontransitionend | Fires when a transition has finished moving, once for every property that changed. `event.propertyName` tells them apart. It does not fire if the transition was cut short (that is `transition cancel`). Browsers read it as an attribute everywhere. | `box: transition = "transform 0.4s" hover transform = "scale(1.2)" transition end = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The transition ended") end content = "Hover me" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `transition cancel`
لغو گذار
ontransitioncancel | Fires when a transition is interrupted before it ends, for example the mouse leaves during a hover transition and the value starts to go back, or the element is hidden. In our tests Chromium (the engine of Chrome and Edge) did not read it as an HTML attribute, while Firefox did; attach it with `dom.OnEventE(el, "transitioncancel", ...)`. | `box: transition = "transform 0.4s 0.3s" hover transform = "scale(1.2)" transition cancel = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The transition was interrupted") end content = "Hover me" padding = 20 end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

### Slots, canvas and security

| Attribute | When it fires | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `context lost`
از دست رفتن زمینه
oncontextlost | Fires on a `canvas` when the browser loses the memory behind its 2D drawing context, for example after a graphics driver reset or when the GPU is switched. Everything drawn is gone. It cannot be provoked from a page; browsers fire it only when the graphics system really fails. (A WebGL canvas has its own `webglcontextlost`.) | `canvas: id = "pad" width = 200 height = 100 context lost = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The drawing was lost") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `context restored`
بازیابی زمینه
oncontextrestored | Fires on a `canvas` after a lost context became usable again, with an empty drawing. Draw everything again here. Like `context lost` it only happens when the graphics system recovers from a failure. | `canvas: id = "pad" width = 200 height = 100 context restored = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "Draw it again") end end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `security policy violation`
نقض سیاست امنیتی
onsecuritypolicyviolation | Fires when the page breaks its own Content Security Policy, the rules set by a `meta` element or a header, for example by writing a `style` attribute when `style-src-attr` forbids it. The event holds `blockedURI` and `violatedDirective`. It bubbles from the element to the document, but a blocked file such as an image is reported on the document only. | `box: security policy violation = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The policy blocked something") end content = "Guarded by a policy" end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

| `slot change`
تغییر شکاف
onslotchange | Fires on a `slot` element inside a shadow tree when the nodes that fill the slot change: one was added, removed or moved. `assignedNodes()` lists the current ones. The shadow tree comes from a `template` with `shadow root mode`. | `box: id = "team"
template: shadow root mode = "open"
slot: slot change = (): dom.SetText(dom.ById("out"), "The slot content changed") end end
end
end
paragraph: id = "out" content = "-" end` |

## Try it yourself

- Add a button to the player that skips 1 second ahead by setting `currentTime`, and show in the log that `seeking` and `seeked` fire.

- Make a button that changes the speed to 2, and a label that follows `rate change`.

- Run the transition example with a transition of one property only, and compare the log with the two property version.

- Add a second slot with a name to the slot example, and add members to it with the `slot` attribute.
