# encoding/value

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-value/

A dynamic value for data whose shape you do not know in advance; the shared language of every format in this group.

`Value` is the dynamic data type shared by the encoding packages. One `Value` is a null, a bool, a 64-bit int, a float, a string, an array of values or an object mapping strings to values, and its `kind` field says which. encoding/json, encoding/yaml, encoding/toml, encoding/msgpack and others decode into it and encode from it, and encoding/serde converts between formats through it.

Reach for a `Value` when the shape of the data is not known when you write the program: a webhook payload, a config with optional sections, a document you only pass along. When the shape is fixed, decoding straight into a struct (for example with `json.Unmarshal`) is shorter and checks the types for you.

### The functions in four groups

| Job | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| Make a value | `ValueNull`, `ValueBool`, `ValueInt`, `ValueFloat`, `ValueString`, `NewValueArray`, `NewValueObject` |
| Ask the kind | `IsNull`, `IsBool`, `IsInt`, `IsFloat`, `IsNumber`, `IsString`, `IsArray`, `IsObject` |
| Read | `AsBool`, `AsInt`, `AsFloat`, `AsString`, `ArrayLen`, `ArrayGet`, `ObjectGet`, `ObjectGetOk`, `ObjectHas`, `ObjectKeys` |
| Change | `ArrayPush`, `ArraySet`, `ObjectSet`, `ObjectDelete`, `ValueClone`, `ValueFree` |

### What trips people up

- Reading never checks the kind. `AsString` of a number is `""` and `AsInt` of a string is 0. Ask `IsString` or `IsNumber` first when the data comes from outside.

- Missing is null, all the way down. `ObjectGet` on a missing key, or on something that is not an object, returns null, so a chain like `ObjectGet(ObjectGet(doc, "a"), "b")` is safe. `ArrayGet` is not: an index past `ArrayLen` stops the program.

- Copies share parts. A copy of an object shares its map, so `ObjectSet` through the copy changes the original. A copy of an array shares its elements but not its length, so `ArrayPush` on an array you got from `ObjectGet` is lost until you `ObjectSet` it back. Use `ValueClone` for a real copy.

- Key order is not kept. `ObjectKeys` comes back in hash order; sort it, or encode with `sort_keys`, when output must be stable.

## Guide: walk a whole document

A recursive function over `Value` handles any shape: for an object, visit each key; for an array, each index; anything else is a leaf. This one prints the path of every leaf, which is handy for logging a webhook payload or comparing two documents line by line.

encoding-value-guide-walk.salam

```salam
import encoding.value
import encoding.json
import encoding.encerr
import sort
import str

func walk(v: value.Value, path: str):
    if value.IsObject(v):
        keys := value.ObjectKeys(v)
        sort.QuickSort(keys)
        each k in keys:
            walk(value.ObjectGet(v, k), path + "." + k)
        end
    else value.IsArray(v):
        repeat value.ArrayLen(v) in i:
            walk(value.ArrayGet(v, i), path + "[" + str.FromInt(i) + "]")
        end
    else:
        println path, "=", value.ToDebugString(v)
    end
end

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    doc := json.Decode(`{"order": 1042, "customer": {"name": "Sara", "vip": true}, "lines": [{"sku": "BK-01", "qty": 2}, {"sku": "PN-07", "qty": 1}], "note": null}`, e)
    walk(doc, "$")
end
```

Output:

```text
$.customer.name = string(Sara)
$.customer.vip = bool(true)
$.lines[0].qty = int(2)
$.lines[0].sku = string(BK-01)
$.lines[1].qty = int(1)
$.lines[1].sku = string(PN-07)
$.note = null
$.order = int(1042)
```

An object does not remember the order of its keys, so the program sorts `ObjectKeys` with `sort.QuickSort` to print the same order every time. `ToDebugString` shows each leaf together with its kind.

## Guide: build a payload with optional fields

A struct always writes all its fields. When some fields should only appear when they have a value, as many HTTP APIs expect, build a `Value` object instead and set only what you have. `json.Encode` with `sort_keys` prints it in a stable order.

encoding-value-guide-build.salam

```salam
import encoding.value
import encoding.json

func payload(name: str, email: str, age: int, tags: Vector<str>): value.Value:
    mut v := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(v, "name", value.ValueString(name))
    if email != "":
        value.ObjectSet(v, "email", value.ValueString(email))
    end
    if age > 0:
        value.ObjectSet(v, "age", value.ValueInt(age))
    end
    if tags.len() > 0:
        mut arr := value.NewValueArray()
        each t in tags:
            value.ArrayPush(arr, value.ValueString(t))
        end
        value.ObjectSet(v, "tags", arr)
    end
    ret v
end

func main:
    opts := json.JSONOptions { sort_keys = true }
    mut tags := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    println json.Encode(payload("Sara", "", 0, tags), opts)
    tags.push("beta")
    tags.push("vip")
    println json.Encode(payload("Reza", "reza@example.com", 41, tags), opts)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"name": "Sara"}
{"age": 41, "email": "reza@example.com", "name": "Reza", "tags": ["beta", "vip"]}
```

## Guide: change a nested field

To change something deep in a decoded document, take the inner part with `ObjectGet`, change it, and store it back with `ObjectSet`. For objects the store is not strictly needed, because the map is shared, but for arrays it is: the program below shows the new order line missing until the array is set back.

encoding-value-guide-edit.salam

```salam
import encoding.value
import encoding.json
import encoding.encerr

func line(sku: str, qty: int): value.Value:
    mut l := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(l, "sku", value.ValueString(sku))
    value.ObjectSet(l, "qty", value.ValueInt(qty))
    ret l
end

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    mut order := json.Decode(`{"id": 1042, "customer": {"name": "Sara"}, "lines": [{"sku": "BK-01", "qty": 2}]}`, e)

    mut customer := value.ObjectGet(order, "customer")
    value.ObjectSet(customer, "tier", value.ValueString("gold"))

    mut lines := value.ObjectGet(order, "lines")
    value.ArrayPush(lines, line("PN-07", 1))
    println "before ObjectSet:", value.ArrayLen(value.ObjectGet(order, "lines")), "line(s)"
    value.ObjectSet(order, "lines", lines)
    println "after ObjectSet: ", value.ArrayLen(value.ObjectGet(order, "lines")), "line(s)"

    println json.Encode(order, json.JSONOptions { sort_keys = true })

    city := value.ObjectGet(value.ObjectGet(order, "shipping"), "city")
    println "shipping city given:", not value.IsNull(city), "[" + value.AsString(city) + "]"
end
```

Output:

```text
before ObjectSet: 1 line(s)
after ObjectSet:  2 line(s)
{"customer": {"name": "Sara", "tier": "gold"}, "id": 1042, "lines": [{"qty": 2, "sku": "BK-01"}, {"qty": 1, "sku": "PN-07"}]}
shipping city given: false []
```

Always writing the changed part back with `ObjectSet` makes the code correct for both kinds, and keeps working if the representation changes. The last line reads a field of a `shipping` object that does not exist: the chain of `ObjectGet` calls returns null and `AsString` gives an empty string, with no crash.

## Guide: deep merge of settings

Settings often come in layers: built-in defaults, then a file per site. A deep merge keeps every default the site file does not mention and replaces only what it does, one level at a time. Arrays and plain values in the override win as a whole.

encoding-value-guide-merge.salam

```salam
import encoding.value
import encoding.json
import encoding.encerr

func merge(base: value.Value, over: value.Value): value.Value:
    if not value.IsObject(base) or not value.IsObject(over):
        ret value.ValueClone(over)
    end
    mut out := value.ValueClone(base)
    each k in value.ObjectKeys(over):
        o := value.ObjectGet(over, k)
        if value.ObjectHas(out, k):
            value.ObjectSet(out, k, merge(value.ObjectGet(out, k), o))
        else:
            value.ObjectSet(out, k, value.ValueClone(o))
        end
    end
    ret out
end

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    defaults := json.Decode(`{"server": {"host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 8080}, "log": {"level": "info", "json": false}, "plugins": ["auth"]}`, e)
    site := json.Decode(`{"server": {"port": 9000}, "log": {"level": "debug"}, "plugins": ["auth", "cache"]}`, e)

    cfg := merge(defaults, site)
    println json.Encode(cfg, json.JSONOptions { indent = "  ", sort_keys = true })
    println "defaults untouched:", value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(value.ObjectGet(defaults, "server"), "port"))
end
```

Output:

```text
{
  "log": {
    "json": false,
    "level": "debug"
  },
  "plugins": [
    "auth",
    "cache"
  ],
  "server": {
    "host": "0.0.0.0",
    "port": 9000
  }
}
defaults untouched: 8080
```

The function clones what it keeps, so `defaults` is the same afterwards. Without the clones, the result would share its objects with the inputs, as the next section shows.

## Guide: copies, conversions and missing keys

Assigning a `Value` to a new variable does not copy its contents: an object's fields live in a shared map, so a change through the copy shows up in the original. Call `ValueClone` when you need an independent copy, and `ValueFree` when you are done with it. Free only values nothing else shares, since freeing a plain copy also frees the original's map.

encoding-value-guide-pitfalls.salam

```salam
import encoding.value

func main:
    mut a := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(a, "n", value.ValueInt(1))

    mut shared := a
    value.ObjectSet(shared, "n", value.ValueInt(2))
    println "after editing a plain copy:", value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(a, "n"))

    mut own := value.ValueClone(a)
    value.ObjectSet(own, "n", value.ValueInt(3))
    println "after editing a clone:", value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(a, "n"))

    println "AsInt of 2.9:", value.AsInt(value.ValueFloat(2.9))
    println "AsFloat of 3:", value.AsFloat(value.ValueInt(3))
    println "AsInt of \"5\":", value.AsInt(value.ValueString("5"))
    println "1 equals 1.0:", value.Equal(value.ValueInt(1), value.ValueFloat(1.0))

    mut found := false
    _ := value.ObjectGetOk(a, "missing", found)
    println "missing key found:", found

    value.ValueFree(own)
end
```

Output:

```text
after editing a plain copy: 2
after editing a clone: 2
AsInt of 2.9: 2
AsFloat of 3: 3
AsInt of "5": 0
1 equals 1.0: false
missing key found: false
```

- `AsInt` cuts a float toward zero and `AsFloat` widens an int, but neither parses text: a string gives 0. Check the kind first with `IsInt`, `IsNumber` or `IsString`.

- `Equal` compares kinds too, so the integer 1 and the float 1.0 are different values.

- `ObjectGet` on a missing key gives a null value; `ObjectGetOk` also tells you whether the key was there.

## Types

### `Value`

```salam
struct Value
```

A dynamic value: null, boolean, whole number, decimal, string, array or object.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int` | The kind of the value; one of the Kind constants. |
| `b` | `bool = false` | The boolean value. |
| `i` | `i64 = 0` | The whole number value. |
| `n` | `f64 = 0` | The decimal value. |
| `s` | `str = ""` | The string value. |
| `arr` | `Vector` | The elements of an array. |
| `obj` | `HashMap` | The keys and values of an object. |

encoding-value-Value.salam

```salam
import encoding.value

func main:
    mut user := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(user, "name", value.ValueString("Narges"))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "age", value.ValueInt(34))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "height", value.ValueFloat(1.68))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "admin", value.ValueBool(false))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "phone", value.ValueNull())
    mut languages := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(languages, value.ValueString("fa"))
    value.ArrayPush(languages, value.ValueString("en"))
    value.ArraySet(languages, 1, value.ValueString("ar"))
    value.ObjectSet(user, "langs", languages)
    println value.ToDebugString(user)
    println value.ObjectLen(user), value.ObjectHas(user, "age"), value.ObjectKeys(user)
    println value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(user, "name")), value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(user, "age")), value.AsFloat(value.ObjectGet(user, "height")), value.AsBool(value.ObjectGet(user, "admin"))
    langs := value.ObjectGet(user, "langs")
    println value.IsArray(langs), value.ArrayLen(langs), value.AsString(value.ArrayGet(langs, 1))
    mut present := false
    _ := value.ObjectGetOk(user, "email", present)
    println present
    phone := value.ObjectGet(user, "phone")
    println value.IsNull(phone), value.IsBool(phone), value.IsInt(value.ValueInt(1)), value.IsFloat(value.ValueFloat(1.0)), value.IsNumber(value.ValueInt(1))
    println value.IsString(value.ValueString("")), value.IsObject(user), phone.kind == value.KindNull, value.KindObject
    mut copy := value.ValueClone(user)
    println value.Equal(copy, user)
    removed := value.ObjectDelete(copy, "phone")
    println removed, value.Equal(copy, user)
    mut numbers := Vector {} as Vector<value.Value>
    numbers.push(value.ValueInt(1))
    mut fields := HashMap {} as HashMap<str, value.Value>
    fields.put("x", value.ValueArray(numbers))
    println value.ToDebugString(value.ValueObject(fields))
    value.ValueFree(copy)
end
```

Output:

```text
object{name: string(Narges), height: float(1.68), age: int(34), admin: bool(false), langs: array[string(fa), string(ar)], phone: null}
6 true ["name", "height", "age", "admin", "langs", "phone"]
Narges 34 1.68 false
true 2 ar
false
true false true true true
true true true 6
true
true false
object{x: array[int(1)]}
```

# encoding/serde

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-serde/

Detecting the format of a piece of text and converting JSON, YAML, TOML, XML and CSV into one another.

This package converts text from one data format to another in one call. `Transcode` reads the input with the matching decoder, holds it as a Value, and writes it with the target encoder. `Detect` guesses which format a text is in. The format names are the lowercase strings `json`, `yaml`, `toml`, `xml` and `csv`; `"JSON"` is not recognised.

It suits tools that take whatever format a user hands them, and one-off migrations. When your program needs the data itself, call the format's own package (encoding/json, encoding/yaml, encoding/toml, encoding/xml, encoding/csv): they return a `Value` or fill a struct and give real error messages, while this package only answers yes or no. MessagePack is binary and is not one of the names here; use encoding/msgpack.

### What survives a conversion

Everything passes through a `Value`, so comments, key order and formatting are always lost. Beyond that, each format can hold less than JSON:

| Format | Reading gives | Writing loses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON, YAML | every kind | YAML writes the float `2.0` as `2`, which reads back as an int |
| TOML | every kind except null; dates as strings | null keys are dropped; the top level must be an object |
| XML | only strings, objects and arrays (for repeated elements); attributes as `@name`, text as `#text`; the outer element's name is dropped | numbers and booleans become text; the output is wrapped in `<root>` |
| CSV | an array of objects, one per row, every cell a string | needs an array of objects; only string fields are written, numbers and booleans come out as empty cells |

### What trips people up

- Detection is a guess. The order is XML (text starts with `<`), JSON, TOML, CSV, then YAML, and nearly any plain text such as `hello world` is valid YAML. Pass the format yourself whenever a file extension or `Content-Type` tells you.

- `Transcode` hides failures as an empty string. Use `TranscodeStrict` and check `ok`.

- CSV in never fails, so `ok` is true for any text read as CSV.

## Guide: accept any format

A tool that takes settings or data from users does not have to insist on one format. `Detect` looks at the text and names the format: XML when it starts with `<`, JSON when it parses as JSON, then TOML, CSV and finally YAML. Pass that name to `TranscodeStrict` to turn whatever came in into the one format your code reads.

encoding-serde-guide-anything.salam

```salam
import encoding.serde

func to_json(text: str): str:
    kind := serde.Detect(text)
    if kind == "":
        ret "(unknown format)"
    end
    mut ok := false
    out := serde.TranscodeStrict(text, kind, "json", ok)
    if not ok:
        ret "(could not read " + kind + ")"
    end
    ret kind + " -> " + out
end

func main:
    println to_json("name: shop\nport: 8080\n")
    println to_json("name = \"shop\"\nport = 8080\n")
    println to_json("name,port\nshop,8080\n")
    println to_json(`{"name": "shop", "port": 8080}`)
    println to_json("")
end
```

Output:

```text
yaml -> {"name": "shop", "port": 8080}
toml -> {"name": "shop", "port": 8080}
csv -> [{"name": "shop", "port": "8080"}]
json -> {"name": "shop", "port": 8080}
(unknown format)
```

Detection is a guess from the shape of the text. Very short inputs can fit more than one format, and almost any plain text is valid YAML, so when you know the format, from a file extension or a `Content-Type` header, pass it yourself.

## Guide: move a config to another format

Changing a project from YAML to TOML, or the other way, is one call. Convert, then check the result: read both the old and the new text back as JSON, decode them, and compare the two values with `value.Equal`. Comparing the JSON text instead would fail on key order alone.

encoding-serde-guide-migrate.salam

```salam
import encoding.serde
import encoding.json
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr

func main:
    old := `server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8080
log:
  level: info
`
    mut ok := false
    as_toml := serde.TranscodeStrict(old, "yaml", "toml", ok)
    println "converted:", ok
    print as_toml

    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    before := json.Decode(serde.Transcode(old, "yaml", "json"), e)
    after := json.Decode(serde.Transcode(as_toml, "toml", "json"), e)
    println "same data:", value.Equal(before, after)
end
```

Output:

```text
converted: true
[server]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 8080
[log]
level = "info"
same data: true
```

Comments do not survive, because a `Value` holds data only, so tell people who edit the file by hand before you convert it.

## Guide: XML in and out

XML has no arrays or numbers, so the mapping follows a few rules: an `@name` key becomes an attribute, an array becomes the same element repeated, `#text` becomes the element's text, and a converted document is wrapped in a `<root>` element. Reading XML gives every value as a string and attributes as `@` keys.

encoding-serde-guide-xml.salam

```salam
import encoding.serde

func main:
    order := `{"@id": 1042, "customer": "Sara", "item": ["tea", "cups"], "total": 39.5, "paid": true}`
    x := serde.Transcode(order, "json", "xml")
    println x
    println "detected:", serde.Detect(x)
    println "back:", serde.Transcode(x, "xml", "json")
    println serde.Transcode("<book lang=\"fa\"><title>Salam</title><pages>153</pages></book>", "xml", "json")
end
```

Output:

```text
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<root id="1042"><item>tea</item><item>cups</item><customer>Sara</customer><total>39.5</total><paid>true</paid></root>
detected: xml
back: {"item": ["tea", "cups"], "customer": "Sara", "total": "39.5", "paid": "true", "@id": "1042"}
{"title": "Salam", "pages": "153", "@lang": "fa"}
```

Numbers and booleans are written as their text, so `39.5` and `true` arrive in the XML. The way back shows what XML cannot express: every value returns as a string, and the outer `<root>` or `<book>` is gone, leaving only its contents. When the element names, order or namespaces matter, build the document with encoding/xml directly.

## Guide: handle failure

`TranscodeStrict` says through `ok` whether both halves worked: reading in the source format, and writing in the target. It fails on broken input, on a format name it does not know, and on data the target cannot hold, such as a top level array for TOML. `Transcode` just returns an empty string in all those cases.

encoding-serde-guide-errors.salam

```salam
import encoding.serde

func try(label: str, data: str, from: str, dest: str):
    mut ok := false
    out := serde.TranscodeStrict(data, from, dest, ok)
    if ok:
        println label, "ok:", out
    else:
        println label, "failed"
    end
end

func main:
    try("good yaml   ", "- 1\n- 2\n", "yaml", "json")
    try("broken json ", `{"a": 1`, "json", "yaml")
    try("unknown from", `a = 1`, "ini", "json")
    try("unknown dest", `{"a": 1}`, "json", "ini")
    try("toml needs a table", `[1, 2]`, "json", "toml")
    println "lenient gives [" + serde.Transcode(`{"a": 1`, "json", "yaml") + "]"
end
```

Output:

```text
good yaml    ok: [1, 2]
broken json  failed
unknown from failed
unknown dest failed
toml needs a table failed
lenient gives []
```

import encoding.serde

# encoding/encerr

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-encerr/

The shared error of the format readers: a kind, a message and a position in the text.

`EncodingError` is the error type the encoding packages share. It is a plain struct with three fields: `kind` (one of the `Kind` constants), `message` (English text) and `position` (a byte offset into the input, or -1). Functions that can fail take it as an `err &:` out-parameter: create one with `NoError()`, pass it in, then test `IsError(err)`.

Among the encoding packages, the ones that fill it are encoding/json (`Decode`, `Unmarshal` and the stream reader), encoding/envfile (`ParseStrict`), encoding/msgpack (`Unmarshal`) and encoding/yaml (`Decode`). Other readers, such as encoding/toml and encoding/xml, report a plain `ok` bool instead. For errors outside encoding, see error.

### What trips people up

- A successful call does not clear the error. Readers only write `err` when something goes wrong, so an error left over from an earlier call stays. `msgpack.Unmarshal` goes further and returns null at once when it is handed an error that is already set. Reset with `e = encerr.NoError()` before each call.

- Not every kind is used. The standard readers produce `KindUnexpectedEOF`, `KindUnexpectedToken`, `KindTrailingData` and `KindCustom`. A field of the wrong type in `json.Unmarshal` arrives as `KindUnexpectedToken`, and too deep nesting as `KindCustom`. Branch on the kinds you will actually see, and treat everything else as "bad input".

- `position` counts bytes, not characters or lines; the first guide converts it. For `yaml.Decode` it points into the JSON the YAML was translated to internally, so do not show it to users.

- `message` is English and meant for logs. Show users your own text chosen by `kind`.

## Guide: point the user at the mistake

`position` is a byte offset into the text, which is exact but not what a person looks for in an editor. Count the line breaks before it to turn it into a line and a column, and print it the way compilers do: file, line, column, message.

encoding-encerr-guide-position.salam

```salam
import encoding.encerr
import encoding.json
import str

func where(text: str, pos: int): str:
    mut line := 1
    mut col := 1
    repeat pos in i:
        if text.substr(i, 1) == "\n":
            line += 1
            col = 1
        else:
            col += 1
        end
    end
    ret "line " + str.FromInt(line) + ", column " + str.FromInt(col)
end

func main:
    text := `{
  "name": "shop",
  "port": 8080
  "debug": true
}`
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    _ := json.Decode(text, e)
    if encerr.IsError(e):
        println "settings.json:", where(text, e.position) + ":", e.message
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
settings.json: line 4, column 3: expected ',' or '}'
```

The reader stops where it noticed the problem, which is often just after the real mistake: here the comma is missing at the end of line 3, and the reader complains at the start of line 4. Columns count bytes, so a line with Persian text before the mistake shows a larger number than the letters you see.

## Guide: one error report for several formats

A program that loads a JSON file, a `.env` file and a MessagePack cache can handle all three failures with one function, because they share the error type. The `report` function below turns the kind into a short description and prints the byte position and the message for the log.

encoding-encerr-guide-handler.salam

```salam
import encoding.encerr
import encoding.json
import encoding.envfile
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.value
import compress

struct Limits:
    pub max_users: int = 0
    pub max_storage_gb: int = 0
end

func report(source: str, e: encerr.EncodingError):
    if not encerr.IsError(e):
        println source, "ok"
        ret
    end
    mut what := "bad input"
    if e.kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedEOF:
        what = "cut off"
    else e.kind == encerr.KindTrailingData:
        what = "extra data after the end"
    else e.kind == encerr.KindCustom:
        what = "not supported"
    end
    println source, what, "at byte", e.position, "(" + e.message + ")"
end

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    mut lim := Limits {}
    _ := json.Unmarshal(`{"max_users": "fifty", "max_storage_gb": 20}`, lim, e)
    report("limits.json:", e)

    e = encerr.NoError()
    _ := json.Decode(`{"plan": "team"} {"plan": "pro"}`, e)
    report("plan.json:  ", e)

    e = encerr.NoError()
    mut env := envfile.ParseStrict("PLAN=team\nSEATS=\"12\n", e)
    report(".env:       ", e)
    envfile.Free(env)

    mut obj := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(obj, "seats", value.ValueInt(12))
    bytes := msgpack.Marshal(obj)
    e = encerr.NoError()
    _ := msgpack.UnmarshalBytes(bytes.data, compress.BufLen(bytes) - 1, e)
    report("cache.bin:  ", e)

    _ := msgpack.Unmarshal(bytes, e)
    report("stale error:", e)
    e = encerr.NoError()
    back := msgpack.Unmarshal(bytes, e)
    report("after reset:", e)
    println "seats:", value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(back, "seats"))
end
```

Output:

```text
limits.json: bad input at byte 14 (value does not match the expected type)
plan.json:   extra data after the end at byte 17 (trailing data after JSON value)
.env:        bad input at byte 10 (envfile: unterminated quoted value)
cache.bin:   cut off at byte 7 (unexpected end of input)
stale error: cut off at byte 7 (unexpected end of input)
after reset: ok
seats: 12
```

The wrong type in `limits.json` comes out as an unexpected token, as described above. The MessagePack data is cut one byte short, so the reader runs out of input. The last three lines show why to reset: decoding the complete cache with the old error still set fails at once, and the same call after `NoError()` works.

## Guide: the same errors in your own parser

When you write a small parser of your own, report errors in the same type, so callers can handle your format and the standard ones with the same code. `ErrUnexpectedEOF`, `ErrUnexpectedToken` and `ErrTypeMismatch` fill in the kind and a standard message; `NewError` with `KindCustom` takes any message. Callers can then branch on `kind`.

encoding-encerr-guide-custom.salam

```salam
import encoding.encerr

struct Size:
    pub w: int = 0
    pub h: int = 0
end

func parse_size(text: str, out &: Size, err &: encerr.EncodingError): bool:
    x := text.find("x")
    if x < 0:
        err = encerr.ErrUnexpectedEOF(text.len())
        ret false
    end
    w := text.substr(0, x)
    h := text.substr(x + 1, text.len() - x - 1)
    if w == "" or h == "":
        err = encerr.ErrUnexpectedToken("expected a number on both sides of 'x'", x)
        ret false
    end
    out.w = w.to_int()
    out.h = h.to_int()
    if out.w <= 0 or out.h <= 0:
        err = encerr.NewError(encerr.KindCustom, "sizes must be positive", 0)
        ret false
    end
    ret true
end

func main:
    inputs := ["1920x1080", "800", "x600", "0x10"]
    each s in inputs:
        mut size := Size {}
        mut e := encerr.NoError()
        if parse_size(s, size, e):
            println s, "->", size.w, "by", size.h
        else e.kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedEOF:
            println s, "-> incomplete:", e.message
        else:
            println s, "-> kind", e.kind, "at byte", e.position
            println "   ", e.message
        end
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
1920x1080 -> 1920 by 1080
800 -> incomplete: unexpected end of input
x600 -> kind 2 at byte 0
    expected a number on both sides of 'x'
0x10 -> kind 99 at byte 0
    sizes must be positive
```

## The error kinds

| Constant | Value | Meaning | Produced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `KindNone` | 0 | No error | `NoError()` |
| `KindUnexpectedEOF` | 1 | The input ended in the middle of a value | json, msgpack |
| `KindUnexpectedToken` | 2 | A character or word that does not belong there, or a JSON value of the wrong type for a struct field | json, envfile |
| `KindInvalidUTF8` | 3 | Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 | reserved, not produced yet |
| `KindInvalidNumber` | 4 | A number that cannot be read | reserved, not produced yet |
| `KindDepthExceeded` | 5 | Nesting deeper than the reader allows | reserved; json and msgpack report depth as `KindCustom` |
| `KindTypeMismatch` | 6 | A value of the wrong kind | only `ErrTypeMismatch`, for your own code |
| `KindKeyNotFound` | 7 | A required key is missing | reserved, not produced yet |
| `KindTrailingData` | 8 | More input after a complete value | json |
| `KindCustom` | 99 | Anything else | json and msgpack (nesting over 512 levels, unsupported MessagePack types), and your own errors |

The reserved kinds exist so that your own parsers, and later versions of the standard readers, have a precise name for these cases. Your code may compare against them, but do not expect the standard readers to return them today.

## Types

### `EncodingError`

```salam
struct EncodingError
```

An error from reading or writing a format.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int` | The kind of error; one of the Kind constants. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The error message, in English. |
| `position` | `int = -1` | Where the error is in the input, as a byte offset from 0, or -1 when it is not known. |

encoding-encerr-Error.salam

```salam
import encoding.encerr
import encoding.json

func main:
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    println encerr.IsError(e), e.kind == encerr.KindNone
    _ := json.Decode(`{"a": }`, e)
    println encerr.IsError(e), e.kind, e.position, e.message
    custom := encerr.NewError(encerr.KindCustom, "a negative value is not allowed", 12)
    println custom.kind, custom.message, custom.position
    println encerr.ErrUnexpectedEOF(40).kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedEOF
    println encerr.ErrUnexpectedToken("expected ':'", 3).kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedToken
    println encerr.ErrTypeMismatch("a number", 5).message
    println encerr.KindInvalidUTF8, encerr.KindInvalidNumber, encerr.KindDepthExceeded, encerr.KindTypeMismatch, encerr.KindKeyNotFound, encerr.KindTrailingData
end
```

Output:

```text
false true
true 2 6 invalid value
99 a negative value is not allowed 12
true
true
expected a number
3 4 5 6 7 8
```

# encoding/msgpack

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-msgpack/

The compact binary MessagePack format for dynamic values.

MessagePack holds the same data as JSON in a shorter binary form that is quicker to read, which suits messages between services, cache entries and RPC. This package turns a Value into a `compress.ByteBuf` with `Marshal` and reads one back with `Unmarshal` (or `UnmarshalBytes` for raw memory). Errors arrive in an EncodingError.

Pick it over encoding/json when both ends are programs and size or speed matters; keep JSON when people read the data or a browser consumes it. For a fixed binary layout of your own, such as a file header, write the fields directly with encoding/binary; for schemas shared across languages, encoding/protobuf.

### How values are written

| Value | MessagePack |
| --- | --- |
| null, bool | `nil`, `true`/`false` |
| int | the smallest int format that fits, from one byte up to 8 |
| float | always `float64` (9 bytes); `float32` is read but never written |
| string | `fixstr`, `str8`, `str16` or `str32` by length |
| array, object | `fixarray`/`array16`/`array32`, `fixmap`/`map16`/`map32` with string keys |

### What trips people up

- No `bin` or `ext` types. Data from another library that stores bytes as `bin`, or timestamps as `ext`, fails with `KindCustom`. Strings stop at the first zero byte, so binary data cannot ride in a string either; Base64 it first.

- Map keys must be strings. A map with integer keys, as some other libraries write, is read with every key turned into `""`, so the entries overwrite each other.

- Trailing bytes are ignored. `Unmarshal` reads one value and does not report what follows it or how many bytes it used, so you cannot read several messages from one buffer. Frame each message yourself, for example with a 4-byte length in front.

- Reset the error between calls. `Unmarshal` returns null at once if the `EncodingError` you pass already holds an error.

- Integers above `i64` (a `uint64` over 9223372036854775807) wrap around to negative numbers.

## Guide: how much smaller is it?

MessagePack drops the quotes, colons and commas of JSON, and stores numbers and lengths in as few bytes as it can. For records with short keys and small numbers it usually comes to a half or two thirds of compact JSON. Decode JSON into a Value once, and `Marshal` writes it as MessagePack.

encoding-msgpack-guide-size.salam

```salam
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.json
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr
import compress

func main:
    text := `[{"id": 1, "name": "tea", "price": 120, "stock": true},
 {"id": 2, "name": "coffee", "price": 90, "stock": true},
 {"id": 3, "name": "cocoa", "price": 75, "stock": false}]`
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    rows := json.Decode(text, e)

    compact := json.EncodeDefault(rows)
    packed := msgpack.Marshal(rows)
    println "JSON bytes:       ", compact.len()
    println "MessagePack bytes:", compress.BufLen(packed)

    back := msgpack.Unmarshal(packed, e)
    println "same data:", value.Equal(rows, back), "error:", encerr.IsError(e)
end
```

Output:

```text
JSON bytes:        169
MessagePack bytes: 90
same data: true error: false
```

The keys are still written in full in every record, so long key names cost as much as in JSON. If size matters more than that, compress the buffer as well with compress.

## Guide: what the bytes look like

Each value starts with a type byte. Small integers from 0 to 127 are a single byte, larger ones get a marker such as `cc` (one byte follows) or `ce` (four bytes follow). Short strings, arrays and maps carry their length in the first byte: `a2` is a string of 2 bytes, `92` an array of 2 items, `81` a map with one pair.

encoding-msgpack-guide-bytes.salam

```salam
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.value
import compress

func hex(v: value.Value): str:
    digits := "0123456789abcdef"
    mut b := msgpack.Marshal(v)
    mut out := ""
    repeat compress.BufLen(b) in i:
        x := compress.BufGet(b, i)
        if i > 0:
            out = out + " "
        end
        out = out + digits.substr(x / 16, 1) + digits.substr(x % 16, 1)
    end
    compress.BufFree(b)
    ret out
end

func main:
    println "5       ", hex(value.ValueInt(5))
    println "-1      ", hex(value.ValueInt(-1))
    println "200     ", hex(value.ValueInt(200))
    println "70000   ", hex(value.ValueInt(70000))
    println "true    ", hex(value.ValueBool(true))
    println "null    ", hex(value.ValueNull())
    println "1.5     ", hex(value.ValueFloat(1.5))
    println "\"hi\"    ", hex(value.ValueString("hi"))

    mut arr := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(arr, value.ValueInt(1))
    value.ArrayPush(arr, value.ValueInt(2))
    println "[1, 2]  ", hex(arr)

    mut obj := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(obj, "a", value.ValueInt(1))
    println "{\"a\": 1}", hex(obj)
end
```

Output:

```text
5        05
-1       ff
200      cc c8
70000    ce 00 01 11 70
true     c3
null     c0
1.5      cb 3f f8 00 00 00 00 00 00
"hi"     a2 68 69
[1, 2]   92 01 02
{"a": 1} 81 a1 61 01
```

The program reads the buffer byte by byte with `compress.BufGet`. Turning the buffer into a `str` first would not work: `70000` contains a zero byte, and a `str` ends at the first zero. Keep MessagePack data in its `ByteBuf`, or use `BufToBase64` when you need text.

## Guide: structs in a cache

A cache such as Redis stores bytes, and MessagePack bytes are quicker to read back than JSON. For a struct, go through JSON on the way in and out: `json.Marshal` and `json.Decode` give a Value to pack, and `json.Unmarshal` fills the struct from the unpacked Value. Here a `HashMap` stands in for the cache.

encoding-msgpack-guide-cache.salam

```salam
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.json
import encoding.encerr
import compress

struct Session:
    pub user: str = ""
    pub role: str = ""
    pub visits: int = 0
end

func save(cache &: HashMap<str, compress.ByteBuf>, key: str, s: Session):
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    v := json.Decode(json.Marshal(s), e)
    cache.put(key, msgpack.Marshal(v))
end

func load(cache: HashMap<str, compress.ByteBuf>, key: str, out &: Session): bool:
    if not cache.has(key):
        ret false
    end
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    v := msgpack.Unmarshal(cache.get(key), e)
    if encerr.IsError(e):
        ret false
    end
    ret json.Unmarshal(json.EncodeDefault(v), out, e)
end

func main:
    mut cache := HashMap {} as HashMap<str, compress.ByteBuf>
    save(cache, "session:9f2", Session { user = "sara", role = "admin", visits = 12 })

    mut s := Session {}
    if load(cache, "session:9f2", s):
        println "found", s.user, s.role, s.visits
    end
    println "missing key loads:", load(cache, "session:000", s)
end
```

Output:

```text
found sara admin 12
missing key loads: false
```

For a real cache, send `b.data` and `b.len` to the client library as a binary value, and decode what comes back with `UnmarshalBytes`.

## Guide: broken, cut and foreign buffers

Network reads can stop halfway, and other programs may use parts of MessagePack this package does not read. Both `Unmarshal` and `UnmarshalBytes` report a buffer that ends in the middle of a value as `KindUnexpectedEOF`, so you can tell "wait for more bytes" apart from data that is simply wrong.

encoding-msgpack-guide-errors.salam

```salam
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr
import compress

func main:
    mut v := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(v, "name", value.ValueString("salam"))
    b := msgpack.Marshal(v)

    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    whole := msgpack.UnmarshalBytes(b.data, b.len, e)
    println "whole buffer:", encerr.IsError(e), value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(whole, "name"))

    mut cut := encerr.NoError()
    _ := msgpack.UnmarshalBytes(b.data, b.len - 3, cut)
    println "cut short:", encerr.IsError(cut), cut.kind == encerr.KindUnexpectedEOF, cut.message

    mut blob := compress.NewByteBuf()
    compress.BufPush(blob, 0xc4)
    compress.BufPush(blob, 2)
    compress.BufPush(blob, 0xca)
    compress.BufPush(blob, 0xfe)
    mut bin := encerr.NoError()
    _ := msgpack.Unmarshal(blob, bin)
    println "bin from another library:", bin.kind == encerr.KindCustom, bin.message

    mut two := compress.BufClone(b)
    compress.BufPush(two, 0x2a)
    mut extra := encerr.NoError()
    first := msgpack.Unmarshal(two, extra)
    println "extra byte after the value:", encerr.IsError(extra), value.ObjectLen(first), "key read"
end
```

Output:

```text
whole buffer: false salam
cut short: true true unexpected end of input
bin from another library: true unsupported msgpack tag (ext/bin types are not supported)
extra byte after the value: false 1 key read
```

The third case is a `bin` value, type byte `c4`, as written by libraries that keep bytes apart from strings; it fails with `KindCustom`. Ask the sender to use strings, or Base64 the bytes, when it has to talk to Salam. The last case shows that one stray byte after a complete value is not noticed, which is why a stream of messages needs its own framing.

## Types

### `MsgpackOptions`

```salam
struct MsgpackOptions
```

The serialising options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `use_str8` | `bool = true` | Use the `str8` format for strings of 32 to 255 bytes; true by default. Set it false for very old readers that predate `str8`; those strings are then written as `str16`. |

encoding-msgpack-Marshal.salam

```salam
import encoding.msgpack
import encoding.value
import encoding.encerr
import encoding
import compress

func main:
    mut v := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(v, "id", value.ValueInt(7))
    value.ObjectSet(v, "ok", value.ValueBool(true))
    b := msgpack.Marshal(v)
    println compress.BufLen(b), compress.BufToBase64(b)
    mut err := encerr.NoError()
    back := msgpack.Unmarshal(b, err)
    println encerr.IsError(err), value.Equal(v, back), value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(back, "id"))
    back2 := msgpack.UnmarshalBytes(b.data, b.len, err)
    println value.Equal(v, back2)
    o := msgpack.MsgpackOptions {}
    println compress.BufLen(msgpack.MarshalWith(v, o))
    println encoding.HexEncode(compress.BufToStrUnsafe(msgpack.Marshal(value.ValueInt(5))))
end
```

Output:

```text
9 gqJpZAeib2vD
false true 7
true
9
05
```

# encoding/binary

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-binary/

Writing and reading numbers as bytes, big-endian or little-endian.

Binary file formats and network protocols store each number as a fixed number of bytes in a fixed order. This package writes and reads such fields: 8, 16, 32 and 64 bit integers, signed or unsigned, and 32 or 64 bit IEEE 754 floats. Big-endian (`BE`) puts the most significant byte first and is the usual order on the network and in PNG; little-endian (`LE`) is the other way round and is what x86 and ARM processors use, and formats such as ZIP and WAV.

Writers append to a `ByteBuf` and readers advance a `ByteReader`, both from compress; that package also has `BufPushBytes` and `RdBytes` for raw byte runs such as magic numbers. Use this package when the layout is fixed by a specification or by you. For self-describing data use encoding/msgpack or encoding/protobuf; for hex or Base64 text, encoding.

### What trips people up

- Reading past the end does not stop the program. The missing bytes read as 0 and the reader's `bad` field turns true and stays true. Read a whole record, then check `r.bad` once, as the first guide does; or check `compress.RdLeft` before reading.

- 32-bit unsigned values come back in an `int`, which is signed, so values from 2,147,483,648 up look negative. `ReadU32BE` and `ReadI32BE` return the same bits. Widen with `(v as i64) & 4294967295`.

- 64-bit unsigned is an `i64` too, so values above 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 are negative.

- Writers do not range check. `WriteU8(b, 300)` writes 44, the low 8 bits.

- `BinaryOptions` is not used by any function yet; the float functions take a `big_endian` bool instead, and the integer functions carry the order in their names.

## Guide: your own file format

A binary format usually starts with a few magic bytes that identify it, then a version number and a count, then the records. Write each field with the function for its size and byte order, and read them back in exactly the same order. `compress.BufPushBytes` writes a fixed text such as the magic, and `compress.RdBytes` reads it back.

encoding-binary-guide-header.salam

```salam
import encoding.binary
import compress
import str

func write_file(scores: Vector<int>): compress.ByteBuf:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    compress.BufPushBytes(b, "SLM1" as void*, 4)
    binary.WriteU16LE(b, 2)
    binary.WriteU32LE(b, scores.len())
    each s in scores:
        binary.WriteI32LE(b, s)
    end
    ret b
end

func read_file(data: compress.ByteBuf, size: int): str:
    mut r := compress.NewByteReader(data.data, size)
    mut head := compress.RdBytes(r, 4)
    defer compress.BufFree(head)
    if compress.BufToStrUnsafe(head) != "SLM1": ret "not our file" end
    version := binary.ReadU16LE(r)
    if version != 2: ret "unknown version " + str.FromInt(version) end
    count := binary.ReadU32LE(r)
    if count < 0 or count > 100000: ret "implausible count" end
    mut total := 0 as i64
    repeat count:
        total += binary.ReadI32LE(r) as i64
    end
    if r.bad: ret "cut short after " + str.FromInt(r.pos) + " bytes" end
    ret str.FromInt(count) + " scores, total " + str.FromInt(total)
end

func main:
    mut scores := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    scores.push(120)
    scores.push(-15)
    scores.push(98000)
    mut data := write_file(scores)
    println "file is", compress.BufLen(data), "bytes"

    println "whole file:", read_file(data, compress.BufLen(data))
    println "first 18:  ", read_file(data, 18)
    compress.BufSet(data, 4, 9)
    println "edited:    ", read_file(data, compress.BufLen(data))
    compress.BufFree(data)
end
```

Output:

```text
file is 22 bytes
whole file: 3 scores, total 98105
first 18:   cut short after 18 bytes
edited:     unknown version 9
```

`read_file` checks the magic and the version before trusting the rest, and refuses a count that is too large to be real, so a damaged file cannot make it loop for a long time. It then reads every record and checks `r.bad` once at the end: the 18-byte copy has room for only two of the three scores, and the reader says so. Changing byte 4 turns the version into 9, which is refused. Keep one byte order for the whole format and write it down in its description.

## Guide: read a header of a real format

PNG is a good example of a big-endian format. A file starts with an 8 byte signature, then chunks, each with a 4 byte length, a 4 letter type and the data. The first chunk, `IHDR`, holds the width and height as big-endian 32 bit numbers. The program builds those first bytes itself so it runs without a file; with a real image, read the file into a buffer first and the parsing is the same.

encoding-binary-guide-png.salam

```salam
import encoding.binary
import compress

func fake_png(): compress.ByteBuf:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    sig := [137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10]
    each x in sig:
        binary.WriteU8(b, x)
    end
    binary.WriteU32BE(b, 13)
    compress.BufPushBytes(b, "IHDR" as void*, 4)
    binary.WriteU32BE(b, 1280)
    binary.WriteU32BE(b, 720)
    binary.WriteU8(b, 8)
    binary.WriteU8(b, 6)
    ret b
end

func main:
    mut png := fake_png()
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(png)
    if binary.ReadU8(r) != 137 or binary.ReadU8(r) != 80:
        println "not a PNG"
        ret 1
    end
    repeat 6:
        _ := binary.ReadU8(r)
    end
    length := binary.ReadU32BE(r)
    mut kind := compress.RdBytes(r, 4)
    println "first chunk:", compress.BufToStrUnsafe(kind), "of", length, "bytes"
    width := binary.ReadU32BE(r)
    height := binary.ReadU32BE(r)
    println "size:", width, "x", height
    println "bit depth:", binary.ReadU8(r), "color type:", binary.ReadU8(r)
    compress.BufFree(kind)
    compress.BufFree(png)
end
```

Output:

```text
first chunk: IHDR of 13 bytes
size: 1280 x 720
bit depth: 8 color type: 6
```

## Guide: length-prefixed messages

A TCP connection delivers a stream of bytes, not separate messages. The usual fix is to send each message with its length in front, here as a 16 bit big-endian number. The reader takes the length, checks that the whole message has arrived with `RdLeft`, and only then reads it.

encoding-binary-guide-frames.salam

```salam
import encoding.binary
import compress

func send(b &: compress.ByteBuf, msg: str):
    binary.WriteU16BE(b, msg.len())
    compress.BufPushBytes(b, msg as void*, msg.len())
end

func main:
    mut wire := compress.NewByteBuf()
    send(wire, "HELLO")
    send(wire, "سلام")
    send(wire, "")
    send(wire, "BYE")
    binary.WriteU16BE(wire, 10)
    compress.BufPushBytes(wire, "par" as void*, 3)
    println "on the wire:", compress.BufLen(wire), "bytes"

    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(wire)
    until compress.RdLeft(r) >= 2:
        n := binary.ReadU16BE(r)
        if compress.RdLeft(r) < n:
            println "incomplete frame, wait for more data"
            break
        end
        mut body := compress.RdBytes(r, n)
        println n, "bytes: [" + compress.BufToStrUnsafe(body) + "]"
        compress.BufFree(body)
    end
    compress.BufFree(wire)
end
```

Output:

```text
on the wire: 29 bytes
5 bytes: [HELLO]
8 bytes: [سلام]
0 bytes: []
3 bytes: [BYE]
incomplete frame, wait for more data
```

The length counts bytes, so `سلام` is 8, not 4. The last frame says 10 bytes but only 3 have arrived; a real server keeps those bytes and tries again when more data comes in.

## Guide: byte order and sign mistakes

Reading with the wrong byte order does not fail, it just gives a wrong number, so these bugs are easy to miss. Unsigned 32 bit values are another trap: they come back in an `int`, so anything at or above 2,147,483,648 looks negative. Widen it to `i64` and mask it to get the unsigned value.

encoding-binary-guide-endian.salam

```salam
import encoding.binary
import compress
import str

func bytes_of(b: compress.ByteBuf): str:
    mut out := ""
    repeat compress.BufLen(b) in i:
        if i > 0:
            out = out + " "
        end
        out = out + str.FromInt(compress.BufGet(b, i))
    end
    ret out
end

func main:
    mut be := compress.NewByteBuf()
    binary.WriteU32BE(be, 1000)
    mut le := compress.NewByteBuf()
    binary.WriteU32LE(le, 1000)
    println "1000 big-endian:   ", bytes_of(be)
    println "1000 little-endian:", bytes_of(le)

    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(le)
    println "read with the wrong order:", binary.ReadU32BE(r)

    mut big := compress.NewByteBuf()
    binary.WriteU32BE(big, -1)
    mut r2 := compress.ReaderFromBuf(big)
    v := binary.ReadU32BE(r2)
    println "u32 0xFFFFFFFF as int:", v, "as unsigned:", (v as i64) & 4294967295

    mut r3 := compress.ReaderFromBuf(be)
    _ := binary.ReadU32BE(r3)
    println "bytes left after reading:", compress.RdLeft(r3)

    compress.BufFree(big)
    compress.BufFree(le)
    compress.BufFree(be)
end
```

Output:

```text
1000 big-endian:    0 0 3 232
1000 little-endian: 232 3 0 0
read with the wrong order: -402456576
u32 0xFFFFFFFF as int: -1 as unsigned: 4294967295
bytes left after reading: 0
```

Reading past the end does not stop the program either: the missing bytes read as zero and `r.bad` turns true. When the input comes from outside, check `r.bad` after each record, or `compress.RdLeft` before it, as the framing example does.

encoding-binary-ReadWrite.salam

```salam
import encoding.binary
import compress

func main:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    binary.WriteU8(b, 255)
    binary.WriteU16BE(b, 4660)
    binary.WriteU16LE(b, 4660)
    binary.WriteU32BE(b, 1)
    binary.WriteI16LE(b, -2)
    println compress.BufToBase64(b)
    binary.WriteU32LE(b, 7)
    binary.WriteU64BE(b, 8)
    binary.WriteU64LE(b, 9)
    binary.WriteI16BE(b, -3)
    binary.WriteI32BE(b, -4)
    binary.WriteI32LE(b, -5)
    binary.WriteI64BE(b, -6)
    binary.WriteI64LE(b, -7)
    binary.WriteF64(b, 1.5, true)
    binary.WriteF32(b, 0.25, false)
    println compress.BufLen(b)
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(b)
    println binary.ReadU8(r), binary.ReadU16BE(r), binary.ReadU16LE(r), binary.ReadU32BE(r), binary.ReadI16LE(r)
    println binary.ReadU32LE(r), binary.ReadU64BE(r), binary.ReadU64LE(r)
    println binary.ReadI16BE(r), binary.ReadI32BE(r), binary.ReadI32LE(r), binary.ReadI64BE(r), binary.ReadI64LE(r)
    println binary.ReadF64(r, true), binary.ReadF32(r, false)
    o := binary.BinaryOptions {}
    println o.big_endian
    compress.BufFree(b)
end
```

Output:

```text
/xI0NBIAAAAB/v8=
69
255 4660 4660 1 -2
7 8 9
-3 -4 -5 -6 -7
1.5 0.25
false
```

# encoding/xml

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/encoding-xml/

Reading, building and writing XML, with XPath, DTD validation, namespaces and a light simple interface.

This package reads, queries, edits and writes XML: feeds, sitemaps, SVG, SOAP replies, office files and old configuration formats. It has three interfaces for three sizes of job.

- The document interface is the complete one. `Parse` reads the text into a `Document`, and every node has a numeric id you pass to functions such as `Name`, `AttributeValue`, `Elements` and `Text`. XPath 1.0 queries, namespaces, entities, DTD validation, editing and canonical output all work on it.

- The simple node interface (`Decode`, `Child`, `Attr`, `Encode`) keeps the tree in plain `XMLNode` structs. It suits a small config or API reply you read once, and it is what encoding/serde uses to convert XML to and from a Value.

- The tokenizer (`NewXMLTokenizer`, `NextToken`) hands out start tags, end tags and text one at a time without building a tree.

If you control both ends and only need to move data, encoding/json is simpler. Reach for this package when the other side speaks XML.

### Untrusted input

`Parse` is safe to run on documents from outside. External entities (`<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">`) are never fetched, so a reference to one fails as undeclared, and entity expansion is capped by `max_entity_expansion` (256 KB by default) and `max_entity_depth` (32), which stops the "billion laughs" attack. Element nesting is capped at 1024 levels.

### What trips people up

- XPath matches names as written. A name test compares the element's full name, prefix included, with the query. `//entry` finds Atom entries in a default namespace, and `//m:thumbnail` works only if the document uses the prefix `m`. When the prefix may vary, test `local-name()` and `namespace-uri()`; the namespaces guide shows how.

- Every value is text. `Text` and `SelectString` return strings; use `SelectNumber` or convert yourself.

- Whitespace-only text is dropped by default. Set `preserve_whitespace` in `ParseOptions` when indentation matters, for example in mixed content.

- Free what you take. A `Document` and each `NodeList` from `Select` hold memory until `Free` and `FreeList`.

- The tokenizer does not check the document. It does not match end tags to start tags, it returns the whitespace between elements as text tokens, and it needs the whole text in memory. Run `WellFormed` first if the input may be broken.

## Guide: read a feed with XPath

RSS and Atom feeds, sitemaps, SVG and office files are all XML, and XPath is the quickest way to pull values out of them. `SelectString` and `SelectNumber` answer a whole query in one call; `Select` returns the matching nodes, and a query run from one of those nodes is relative to it, so `title` means the title of that item.

encoding-xml-guide-rss.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    feed := `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rss version="2.0">
  <channel>
    <title>Salam blog</title>
    <item>
      <title>Salam 0.5.5 is out</title>
      <link>https://example.com/posts/055</link>
      <category>release</category>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Writing a JSON API</title>
      <link>https://example.com/posts/json-api</link>
      <category>tutorial</category>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>The Persian keywords</title>
      <link>https://example.com/posts/persian</link>
      <category>tutorial</category>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>`
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse(feed, err)
    if not err.ok:
        println "bad feed:", xml.ErrorText(err)
        ret 1
    end
    top := xml.DocumentNode(d)
    println "feed:", xml.SelectString(d, top, "/rss/channel/title", err)
    println "posts:", xml.SelectNumber(d, top, "count(//item)", err)

    mut items := xml.Select(d, top, "//item[category = 'tutorial']", err)
    each it in items.items:
        println "-", xml.SelectString(d, it, "title", err), "<" + xml.SelectString(d, it, "link", err) + ">"
    end
    xml.FreeList(items)
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
feed: Salam blog
posts: 3
- Writing a JSON API <https://example.com/posts/json-api>
- The Persian keywords <https://example.com/posts/persian>
```

The filter `[category = 'tutorial']` keeps only the items whose child element has that text. Free the node list with `FreeList` and the document with `Free` when you are done.

## Guide: namespaces in an Atom feed

Atom feeds, SVG, SOAP and office files put their elements in namespaces, often several at once. This feed uses Atom as the default namespace and Media RSS under the prefix `m`. The program shows how XPath in this package treats names, and the query that works whatever prefix the publisher chose.

encoding-xml-guide-namespaces.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    feed := `<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:m="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/">
  <title>Salam videos</title>
  <entry>
    <title>Install Salam</title>
    <m:thumbnail url="https://cdn.example/install.jpg"/>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <title>Your first web server</title>
    <m:thumbnail url="https://cdn.example/server.jpg"/>
  </entry>
</feed>`
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse(feed, err)
    if not err.ok:
        println xml.ErrorText(err)
        ret 1
    end
    top := xml.DocumentNode(d)
    println "entries by name:  ", xml.SelectNumber(d, top, "count(//entry)", err)
    println "with prefix m:    ", xml.SelectNumber(d, top, "count(//m:thumbnail)", err)
    println "with prefix media:", xml.SelectNumber(d, top, "count(//media:thumbnail)", err)

    query := "//*[local-name() = 'thumbnail' and namespace-uri() = 'http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/']"
    mut thumbs := xml.Select(d, top, query, err)
    each t in thumbs.items:
        println xml.Name(d, t), "local:", xml.LocalName(d, t), "->", xml.AttributeValue(d, t, "url")
    end
    xml.FreeList(thumbs)

    root := xml.Root(d)
    println "root namespace:", xml.NamespaceURI(d, root)
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
entries by name:   2
with prefix m:     2
with prefix media: 0
m:thumbnail local: thumbnail -> https://cdn.example/install.jpg
m:thumbnail local: thumbnail -> https://cdn.example/server.jpg
root namespace: http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom
```

`//entry` matches because the entries have no prefix, and `//m:thumbnail` because the document happens to say `m`. A feed that writes `media:thumbnail` instead would break the second query, while the `local-name()` and `namespace-uri()` test keeps working. Outside XPath, `LocalName`, `Prefix` and `NamespaceURI` give the parts of any node's name, and `AttributeValueNS` reads a namespaced attribute.

## Guide: generate a sitemap

To write XML, build a document node by node with `CreateElement`, `CreateText` and `Append`, then write it out. A small helper per repeated element keeps the code short. `WriteWith` with `declaration` and `indent` set produces a file ready to serve as `sitemap.xml`.

encoding-xml-guide-sitemap.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func add_url(d &: xml.Document, parent: int, loc: str, changed: str):
    u := xml.CreateElement(d, "url")
    xml.Append(d, parent, u)
    l := xml.CreateElement(d, "loc")
    xml.Append(d, u, l)
    xml.Append(d, l, xml.CreateText(d, loc))
    m := xml.CreateElement(d, "lastmod")
    xml.Append(d, u, m)
    xml.Append(d, m, xml.CreateText(d, changed))
end

func main:
    mut d := xml.NewDocument()
    root := xml.CreateElement(d, "urlset")
    xml.Append(d, xml.DocumentNode(d), root)
    xml.SetAttribute(d, root, "xmlns", "http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9")

    add_url(d, root, "https://example.com/", "2026-10-01")
    add_url(d, root, "https://example.com/search?q=tea&page=2", "2026-10-12")

    mut o := xml.DefaultWriteOptions()
    o.declaration = true
    o.indent = "  "
    print xml.WriteWith(d, o)
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/</loc>
    <lastmod>2026-10-01</lastmod>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/search?q=tea&amp;page=2</loc>
    <lastmod>2026-10-12</lastmod>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

Text is escaped on the way out, so the `&` in the second URL is written as `&amp;`, as XML requires. Building the document this way means you never have to escape anything by hand.

## Guide: a small config with the simple nodes

For a short file you read once, the simple interface is enough: `DecodeStrict` gives the root as a plain struct, `Child` and `Children` find elements by name, and `Attr` reads an attribute. `Found` tells you whether `Child` found anything, and `HasAttr` lets an attribute have a default.

encoding-xml-guide-config.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    text := `<app name="shop">
  <listen host="0.0.0.0" port="8080"/>
  <plugin name="auth" enabled="true"/>
  <plugin name="cache" enabled="false"/>
  <plugin name="search"/>
</app>`
    mut ok := false
    app := xml.DecodeStrict(text, ok)
    if not ok:
        println "config is not well-formed"
        ret 1
    end
    println "app:", xml.Attr(app, "name")
    listen := xml.Child(app, "listen")
    if xml.Found(listen):
        println "listen:", xml.Attr(listen, "host") + ":" + xml.Attr(listen, "port")
    end
    plugins := xml.Children(app, "plugin")
    each p in plugins.items:
        mut enabled := true
        if xml.HasAttr(p, "enabled"):
            enabled = xml.Attr(p, "enabled") == "true"
        end
        println "plugin", xml.Attr(p, "name"), "enabled:", enabled
    end
    println "has a cache element:", xml.Found(xml.Child(app, "cache"))
end
```

Output:

```text
app: shop
listen: 0.0.0.0:8080
plugin auth enabled: true
plugin cache enabled: false
plugin search enabled: true
has a cache element: false
```

## Guide: scan a product feed with the tokenizer

Price lists and catalogue exports can have hundreds of thousands of records, and you often need only a few fields. The tokenizer walks the text once and builds no tree, so memory stays at the size of the text. Keep a little state, here which product you are in and whether you are inside a `<name>`, and react to the tokens you care about.

encoding-xml-guide-tokens.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml
import str

func main:
    feed := `<products>
  <product sku="TEA-01" stock="14"><name>Green tea</name><price>4.50</price></product>
  <product sku="CUP-02" stock="0"><name>Glass cup</name><price>7.25</price></product>
  <product sku="POT-03" stock="3"><name>Tea pot &amp; lid</name><price>21.00</price></product>
</products>`
    mut tz := xml.NewXMLTokenizer(feed)
    mut current := ""
    mut inName := false
    mut products := 0
    mut outOfStock := 0
    mut done := false
    until not done:
        tok := xml.NextToken(tz)
        if tok.kind == xml.XMLTokEOF:
            done = true
        else tok.kind == xml.XMLTokStartElement and tok.tag == "product":
            products += 1
            current = tok.attrs.get("sku")
            if tok.attrs.get("stock") == "0": outOfStock += 1 end
        else tok.kind == xml.XMLTokStartElement and tok.tag == "name":
            inName = true
        else tok.kind == xml.XMLTokEndElement and tok.tag == "name":
            inName = false
        else tok.kind == xml.XMLTokText and inName:
            println current, "is", str.Trim(tok.text)
        end
    end
    println products, "products,", outOfStock, "out of stock"
end
```

Output:

```text
TEA-01 is Green tea
CUP-02 is Glass cup
POT-03 is Tea pot & lid
3 products, 1 out of stock
```

Attributes of a start tag arrive in `tok.attrs`, and text has its entities decoded, so `&amp;` comes out as `&`. Text tokens include the whitespace between tags, which is why the program trims the name and ignores text outside `<name>`. A self-closing tag such as `<br/>` gives a start token followed by an end token.

## Guide: report broken XML

XML is strict: one root, every tag closed in order, every `&` part of an entity. `Parse` stops at the first problem and `ErrorText` gives a line, a column and a readable reason, ready to show to whoever wrote the file. `WellFormed` only answers yes or no.

encoding-xml-guide-errors.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func check(label: str, text: str):
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse(text, err)
    if err.ok:
        println label, "ok"
    else:
        println label, xml.ErrorText(err)
    end
    xml.Free(d)
end

func main:
    check("good:      ", "<a><b>1</b></a>")
    check("mismatch:  ", "<a>\n  <b>1</a>")
    check("two roots: ", "<a/><b/>")
    check("bad entity:", "<a>&nope;</a>")
    check("raw amp:   ", "<a>salt & pepper</a>")
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    println "quick check:", xml.WellFormed("<x/>", err), xml.WellFormed("<x>", err)
    println "escaped text:", xml.EscapeText("salt & pepper")
end
```

Output:

```text
good:       ok
mismatch:   line 2, column 7: </a> closes <b>
two roots:  line 1, column 5: a document may hold only one root element, and <b> is a second
bad entity: line 1, column 4: the entity "&nope;" is not declared
raw amp:    line 1, column 9: an entity reference has no closing semicolon
quick check: true false
escaped text: salt &amp; pepper
```

The last case is the most common one in hand-written files: a bare `&` in text. When you build XML from strings yourself, pass text through `EscapeText` and attribute values through `EscapeAttr`, or build the document with the functions above, which escape for you.

## Which interface for which job

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Small config or response, read once | `Decode`, `Child`, `Children`, `Attr` |
| Find values anywhere in a document | `Parse` and `Select`, `SelectString`, `SelectNumber` |
| Elements in namespaces | XPath with `local-name()` and `namespace-uri()`, or `LocalName` and `NamespaceURI` |
| Walk or change a document | `Root`, `Elements`, `ChildAt`, `SetText`, `RemoveChild` |
| Write a new document | `NewDocument`, `CreateElement`, `Append`, `WriteIndent` |
| Large files, one pass, no tree | `NewXMLTokenizer` and `NextToken` |
| Check against a DTD | the DTD functions in the reference below |
| Convert to JSON or YAML | encoding/serde |

## Types

### `WriteOptions`

```salam
struct WriteOptions
```

The write options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indent` | `str = ""` | The indent unit; empty means no indenting. |
| `newline` | `str = "
"` | The newline between elements when there is indenting. |

| `declaration` | `bool = false` | Write the `<?xml ...?>` declaration. |
| `doctype` | `bool = false` | Write the DOCTYPE. |
| `empty_as_pair` | `bool = false` | Write an empty element as `<a></a>`. |
| `sort_attributes` | `bool = false` | Put the attributes in alphabetical order. |
| `escape_newlines_in_attributes` | `bool = false` | Write a newline in an attribute value as `&#10;`. |

encoding-xml-Build.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    mut d := xml.NewDocument()
    root := xml.CreateElement(d, "note")
    xml.Append(d, xml.DocumentNode(d), root)
    xml.SetAttribute(d, root, "id", "7")
    xml.SetAttribute(d, root, "draft", "yes")
    recipient := xml.CreateElement(d, "to")
    xml.Append(d, root, recipient)
    xml.Append(d, recipient, xml.CreateText(d, "Maryam & Reza"))
    body := xml.CreateElement(d, "body")
    xml.Append(d, root, body)
    xml.Append(d, body, xml.CreateCData(d, "<b>bold</b>"))
    xml.InsertBefore(d, root, xml.CreateComment(d, "recipient"), recipient)
    xml.Append(d, xml.DocumentNode(d), xml.CreateProcessingInstruction(d, "app", "v=1"))
    println xml.Write(d)
    println xml.RemoveAttribute(d, root, "draft"), xml.RemoveChild(d, root, body)
    xml.SetText(d, recipient, "everyone")
    println xml.WriteIndent(d, "  ")
    println xml.WriteNode(d, recipient), xml.WriteNodeIndent(d, recipient, "\t")
    mut o := xml.DefaultWriteOptions()
    o.declaration = true
    o.empty_as_pair = true
    println xml.WriteWith(d, o)
    println xml.WriteDocument(d)
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d2 := xml.Parse("<r b=\"2\"   a=\"1\"><x/></r>", err)
    println xml.Canonical(d2), xml.CanonicalNode(d2, xml.ChildAt(d2, xml.Root(d2), 0))
    xml.Free(d2)
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
<note id="7" draft="yes"><!--recipient--><to>Maryam &amp; Reza</to><body><![CDATA[<b>bold</b>]]></body></note><?app v=1?>
true true
<note id="7">
  <!--recipient-->
  <to>everyone</to>
</note>
<?app v=1?>

<to>everyone</to> <to>everyone</to>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<note id="7"><!--recipient--><to>everyone</to></note><?app v=1?>
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<note id="7"><!--recipient--><to>everyone</to></note><?app v=1?>

<r a="1" b="2"><x></x></r> <x></x>
```

### `ElementDecl`

```salam
struct ElementDecl
```

| Name | Type | Description |

| `content` | `int = 1` | The content kind; one of the `Content` constants. |
| `model` | `str = ""` | The content model as text, such as `(to, body)`. |
| `root` | `int = -1` | The root of the model tree. |

encoding-xml-DTD.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    dtd := xml.ParseDTD("<!ELEMENT note (to, body)>\n<!ELEMENT to (#PCDATA)>\n<!ELEMENT body (#PCDATA)>\n<!ATTLIST note id ID #REQUIRED kind (a|b) \"a\">")
    println dtd.ok, xml.DeclaredElementCount(dtd), xml.DeclaredAttributeCount(dtd)
    el := dtd.elements[0]
    println el.name, el.content == xml.ContentChildren, el.model
    at := dtd.attributes[1]
    println at.name, at.kind == xml.AttrEnumeration, at.mode == xml.DefaultValue, at.value, at.values
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut good := xml.Parse("<note id=\"n1\"><to>me</to><body>hello</body></note>", err)
    mut report := xml.Validate(good, dtd)
    println report.ok
    xml.FreeReport(report)
    println xml.ApplyDefaults(good, dtd), xml.AttributeValue(good, xml.Root(good), "kind")
    mut bad := xml.Parse("<note><body>no recipient</body></note>", err)
    mut r2 := xml.Validate(bad, dtd)
    println r2.ok, r2.items.len()
    println xml.ReportText(r2)
    xml.FreeReport(r2)
    mut inner := xml.Parse("<!DOCTYPE a [<!ELEMENT a EMPTY>]><a>text</a>", err)
    mut r3 := xml.ValidateInternalSubset(inner)
    println r3.ok, inner.doctype
    xml.FreeReport(r3)
    mut ns := xml.Parse("<a xmlns:x=\"urn:x\"><x:b/></a>", err)
    mut r4 := xml.CheckNamespaces(ns)
    println r4.ok
    xml.FreeReport(r4)
    mut dtd2 := dtd
    xml.FreeDTD(dtd2)
    xml.Free(good)
    xml.Free(bad)
    xml.Free(inner)
    xml.Free(ns)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 3 2
note true (to, body)
kind true true a ["a", "b"]
true
1 a
false 2
line 1, column 1: the children of <note> do not match (to, body)
line 1, column 1: <note> is missing the required attribute "id"
false a
true
```

encoding-xml-Parse.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    src := "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<library xmlns:b=\"urn:books\">\n  <!-- the list -->\n  <b:book id=\"1\" lang=\"en\"><title>Dune</title><year>1965</year></b:book>\n  <b:book id=\"2\"><title>Solaris</title></b:book>\n</library>"
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse(src, err)
    println err.ok, d.version, xml.NodeCount(d) > 0
    r := xml.Root(d)
    println xml.Name(d, r), xml.Kind(d, r) == xml.KindElement, xml.Parent(d, r) == xml.DocumentNode(d)
    mut books := xml.Elements(d, r)
    println books.items.len()
    b := books.items[0]
    println xml.Name(d, b), xml.LocalName(d, b), xml.Prefix(d, b), xml.NamespaceURI(d, b)
    println xml.Line(d, b), xml.Column(d, b), xml.Depth(d, b), xml.Path(d, b)
    println xml.AttributeCount(d, b), xml.HasAttribute(d, b, "lang"), xml.AttributeValue(d, b, "id")
    a := xml.AttributeAt(d, b, 1)
    println a.name, a.value
    t := xml.FirstElementNamed(d, b, "title")
    println xml.Text(d, t), xml.Text(d, b), xml.IsElement(d, t)
    println xml.ChildCount(d, b), xml.Name(d, xml.ChildAt(d, b, 1))
    println xml.Name(d, xml.NextSibling(d, t)), xml.PreviousSibling(d, t)
    mut all := xml.Descendants(d, r)
    mut named := xml.ElementsNamed(d, r, "b:book")
    mut up := xml.Ancestors(d, t)
    mut kids := xml.ChildNodes(d, r)
    println all.items.len(), named.items.len(), up.items.len(), kids.items.len()
    println xml.Exists(d, 9999), xml.Value(d, xml.ChildAt(d, t, 0))
    xml.FreeList(all)
    xml.FreeList(named)
    xml.FreeList(up)
    xml.FreeList(kids)
    xml.FreeList(books)
    _ := xml.Parse("<a><b></a>", err)
    println err.ok, err.line, xml.ErrorText(err)
    println xml.WellFormed("<x/>", err)
    xml.Free(d)
    mut o := xml.DefaultOptions()
    o.keep_comments = false
    mut d2 := xml.ParseWith("<!DOCTYPE p [<!ENTITY site \"hello\">]><p xmlns:x=\"urn:x\" x:id=\"7\">&site; <b>b</b> end</p>", o, err)
    p := xml.Root(d2)
    println err.ok, xml.EntityCount(d2), xml.EntityValue(d2, "site")
    println "[" + xml.DirectText(d2, p) + "]", xml.AttributeValueNS(d2, p, "urn:x", "id")
    println xml.EntityDepthLimit, xml.EntityExpansionLimit, o.max_depth
    xml.Free(d2)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 1.0 true
library true true
2
b:book book b urn:books
4 3 2 /library[1]/b:book[1]
2 true 1
lang en
Dune Dune1965 true
2 year
year -1
9 2 3 3
false Dune
false 1 line 1, column 7: </a> closes <b>
true
true 1 hello
[hello  end] 7
32 262144 1024
```

### `ParseOptions`

encoding-xml-Simple.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml
import encoding.value

func main:
    n := xml.Decode("<config env=\"prod\"><db host=\"localhost\" port=\"5432\"/><feature>search</feature><feature>chat</feature></config>")
    println n.tag, xml.HasAttr(n, "env"), xml.Attr(n, "env")
    db := xml.Child(n, "db")
    println xml.Found(db), xml.Attr(db, "port"), xml.Found(xml.Child(n, "cache"))
    feats := xml.Children(n, "feature")
    println feats.items.len(), feats.items[1].text
    mut item := xml.NewXMLNode("item")
    xml.SetAttr(item, "id", "3")
    mut name := xml.NewXMLNode("name")
    name.text = "book"
    xml.AppendChild(item, name)
    println xml.Encode(item)
    println xml.EncodeIndent(item, "  ")
    println xml.EncodeDeclaration(item)
    println xml.Valid("<a><b/></a>"), xml.Valid("<a><b></a>")
    mut ok := false
    _ := xml.DecodeStrict("<a>", ok)
    println ok
    v := xml.ToValue(n)
    println value.ToDebugString(v)
    println xml.Encode(xml.FromValue(v, "root"))
    println xml.EscapeText("a < b & c"), xml.EscapeAttr(`"x"`), xml.UnescapeEntities("&lt;p&gt; &amp; &#115;")
    mut tz := xml.NewXMLTokenizer("<a x=\"1\">hello<!--c--></a>")
    until true:
        t := xml.NextToken(tz)
        if t.kind == xml.XMLTokEOF or t.kind == xml.XMLTokError:
            break
        end
        println t.kind, t.tag, t.text
    end
    println xml.XMLTokStartElement, xml.XMLTokEndElement, xml.XMLTokText, xml.XMLTokComment, xml.XMLTokCData
end
```

Output:

```text

true 5432 false
2 chat
<item id="3"><name>book</name></item>
<item id="3">
  <name>book</name>
</item>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<item id="3"><name>book</name></item>
true false
false
object{feature: array[string(search), string(chat)], @env: string(prod), db: object{@port: string(5432), @host: string(localhost)}}
<root env="prod"><feature>search</feature><feature>chat</feature><db host="localhost" port="5432"/></root>
a &lt; b &amp; c &quot;x&quot; <p> & s
1 a
3  hello
4  c
2 a
1 2 3 4 5
```

encoding-xml-XPath.salam

```salam
import encoding.xml

func main:
    mut err := xml.NoError()
    mut d := xml.Parse("<shop><item price=\"120\">tea</item><item price=\"80\">sugar</item><item price=\"45\">bread</item></shop>", err)
    r := xml.DocumentNode(d)
    mut cheap := xml.Select(d, r, "//item[@price < 100]", err)
    println cheap.items.len()
    each n in cheap.items:
        println xml.Text(d, n)
    end
    xml.FreeList(cheap)
    println xml.SelectString(d, r, "/shop/item[1]", err), xml.SelectNumber(d, r, "sum(//item/@price)", err), xml.SelectBoolean(d, r, "count(//item) = 3", err)
    last := xml.SelectFirst(d, r, "//item[last()]", err)
    println xml.NodeName(d, last), xml.StringValue(d, last)
    mut v := xml.Evaluate(d, r, "//item/@price", err)
    println v.kind == xml.ValueNodeSet, v.nodes.items.len()
    first := v.nodes.items[0]
    println xml.IsAttributeRef(first), xml.ReferencedAttribute(d, first).value, xml.IsAttributeRef(xml.AttributeRef(0))
    xml.FreeValue(v)
    num := xml.Evaluate(d, r, "string-length('hello')", err)
    println num.kind == xml.ValueNumber, num.number, xml.ValueString, xml.ValueBoolean
    _ := xml.Select(d, r, "//item[@", err)
    println err.ok
    xml.Free(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
2
sugar
bread
tea 245 true
item bread
true 3
true 120 true
true 5 1 3
false
```
