# net/http

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http/

HTTP servers and clients: handlers, text and JSON responses, cookies and sending requests.

This package has both halves of HTTP/1.1: a server for web pages and JSON APIs, and a client for calling other services. The server hands each request to a net/router router, which picks the handler by method and path. Every handler takes one `i64`, the context id of the request; you read the request and write the response with the context functions below, or turn the id into a `Context` struct with `Ctx` and call the same names on it.

The packages around it:

- net/http/middleware for access logs, CORS and cache headers, net/http/session for logins with a cookie, net/http/validate for checking input, and net/http/swagger for API documentation;

- net/http2 for HTTP/2, and net/websocket for connections that stay open.

Things people get wrong:

- Register every route before `Use`. The server keeps a copy of the router.

- `Post`, `Put` and `Patch` label a body as a form (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) unless you pass a `Content-Type`; send JSON with `PostWith` and that header.

- The client does not follow redirects unless you ask. A 302 comes back as a 302 with its `Location` header; set `max_redirects` in `RequestOptions` (or call `SetMaxRedirects` on a client) to follow them. It never hangs or reads without limit: a read or write that is idle for 30 seconds fails, a response over 256 MB fails, and `timeout_ms` caps the whole request.

- `Ok` means a 2xx status. When the server could not be reached at all, `Status` is 0 and `Error` says why.

- A value read from a request is freed when the handler returns; see the end of the page.

The examples run the server with `RunBackground` on 127.0.0.1 and send requests to it from the same program.

## A JSON API in one file

The most common job is a small JSON API: list some records, show one by its id, and create new ones. Register each route on the router with its handler, hand the router to the server with `Use`, and start it. Here the records are Salam structs: `json.Marshal` turns them into the response body, and `json.UnmarshalLenient` reads the posted body back into a struct, ignoring fields it does not know and leaving the missing ones at their defaults.

net-http-guide-api.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import encoding.json
import encoding.encerr
import conv

mut books := Vector {} as Vector<Book>

struct Book:
    @json "id"
    pub id: int = 0
    @json "title"
    pub title: str = ""
end

func list(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, json.Marshal(books))
end

func show(ctx: i64):
    id := conv.Atoi(http.Param(ctx, "id"))
    each b in books:
        if b.id == id:
            http.Json(ctx, json.Marshal(b))
            ret
        end
    end
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 404)
    http.Json(ctx, `{"error":"no such book"}`)
end

func create(ctx: i64):
    mut b := Book {}
    mut e := encerr.NoError()
    if not json.UnmarshalLenient(http.Body(ctx), b, e):
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 400)
        http.Json(ctx, "{" + json.Member("error", e.message) + "}")
        ret
    end
    b.id = books.len() + 1
    books.push(b)
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 201)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Location", "/books/" + b.id)
    http.Json(ctx, json.Marshal(b))
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/books", list)
    router.Get(r, "/books/:id", show)
    router.Post(r, "/books", create)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19761)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19761"
    a := http.Post(base + "/books", `{"title": "The Little Prince"}`)
    println http.Status(a), http.GetHeader(a, "location"), http.Body(a)
    _ := http.Post(base + "/books", `{"title": "Rumi"}`)
    println http.Body(http.Get(base + "/books"))
    println http.Body(http.Get(base + "/books/2"))
    c := http.Get(base + "/books/9")
    println http.Status(c), http.Body(c)
    d := http.Post(base + "/books", `{"title": 7}`)
    println http.Status(d), http.Body(d)
end
```

Output:

```text
201 /books/1 {"id":1,"title":"The Little Prince"}
[{"id":1,"title":"The Little Prince"},{"id":2,"title":"Rumi"}]
{"id":2,"title":"Rumi"}
404 {"error":"no such book"}
400 {"error": "value does not match the expected type"}
```

Nothing is sent until the handler returns: the status, the headers and the body are collected and go out together, and a second body call replaces the first. That is why a handler returns right after it writes an error. A `201` with a `Location` header is the usual answer to a create, and a `404` with a short JSON error is easier for a client to handle than an empty page. Path parameters such as `:id` always arrive as text, so convert them with `conv.Atoi` before comparing.

## HTML forms, query strings and redirects

A browser form arrives as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. `Form` reads one field and decodes it, so `%40` becomes `@` and `+` becomes a space. `Query` does the same for the query string. After a successful POST, answer with `Redirect` so that pressing reload in the browser does not send the form again.

net-http-guide-forms.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import template

mut messages := Vector {} as Vector<str>

func board(ctx: i64):
    mut html := "<ul>"
    each m in messages:
        html = html + "<li>" + template.EscapeHTML(m) + "</li>"
    end
    http.Html(ctx, html + "</ul>")
end

func post(ctx: i64):
    name := http.Form(ctx, "name")
    text := http.Form(ctx, "text")
    if name == "" or text == "":
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 400)
        http.Text(ctx, "name and text are required")
        ret
    end
    messages.push(name + ": " + text)
    http.Redirect(ctx, "/board")
end

func search(ctx: i64):
    word := http.Query(ctx, "q")
    mut found := 0
    each m in messages:
        if m.find(word) >= 0:
            found += 1
        end
    end
    http.Text(ctx, "'" + word + "' found in " + found + " message(s)")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/board", board)
    router.Post(r, "/board", post)
    router.Get(r, "/search", search)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19762)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19762"
    mut form := http.NewHeaders()
    form.insert("name", "Sara")
    form.insert("text", "see you at 5 & bring tea")
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    a := http.PostWith(base + "/board", http.EncodeForm(form), headers)
    println http.Status(a), http.GetHeader(a, "location")
    b := http.PostWith(base + "/board", "name=Reza", headers)
    println http.Status(b), http.Body(b)
    println http.Body(http.Get(base + "/board"))
    mut q := http.NewHeaders()
    q.insert("q", "bring tea")
    println http.Body(http.Get(http.WithQuery(base + "/search", q)))
end
```

Output:

```text
302 /board
400 name and text are required
<ul><li>Sara: see you at 5 &amp; bring tea</li></ul>
'bring tea' found in 1 message(s)
```

Anything a user typed must be escaped before it goes into HTML; otherwise a message containing `<script>` runs in every visitor's browser. `template.EscapeHTML` does that, as the `&amp;` in the output shows. On the client side, `EncodeForm` builds a form body from a map and `WithQuery` adds a query string to a URL, both with correct escaping.

## Route groups and a login check

`router.Group` puts a route under a common prefix, which is how an API is versioned under `/api/v1`. There is no separate middleware chain: a check that several handlers share is a plain function that returns `true` when the request may go on, or writes the error response itself and returns `false`. Each handler calls it on its first line and returns when it fails.

net-http-guide-groups.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func signed_in(ctx: i64): bool:
    if http.Header(ctx, "Authorization") == "Bearer s3cret":
        ret true
    end
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 401)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer")
    http.Json(ctx, `{"error":"sign in first"}`)
    ret false
end

func health(ctx: i64):
    http.Text(ctx, "ok")
end

func profile(ctx: i64):
    if not signed_in(ctx): ret end
    http.Json(ctx, `{"user":"maryam"}`)
end

func remove(ctx: i64):
    if not signed_in(ctx): ret end
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 204)
    http.Text(ctx, "")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/health", health)
    router.Group(r, "/api/v1", "GET", "/profile", profile)
    router.Group(r, "/api/v1", "DELETE", "/posts/:id", remove)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19763)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19763"
    println http.Body(http.Get(base + "/health"))
    a := http.Get(base + "/api/v1/profile")
    println http.Status(a), http.GetHeader(a, "www-authenticate"), http.Body(a)
    mut auth := http.NewHeaders()
    auth.insert("Authorization", "Bearer s3cret")
    println http.Body(http.GetWith(base + "/api/v1/profile", auth))
    println http.Status(http.DeleteWith(base + "/api/v1/posts/3", auth))
    println http.Status(http.Get(base + "/profile"))
end
```

Output:

```text
ok
401 Bearer {"error":"sign in first"}
{"user":"maryam"}
204
404
```

A route that is not registered answers `404` on its own, so `/profile` without the prefix is not found. For a cookie based login instead of a token, see net/http/session.

## Static files and server settings

`router.Static` serves a whole directory under a prefix, with the content type taken from the file extension. A path that tries to climb out of the directory with `..` is refused, and a missing file is a `404`. `HideTokens` drops the version number from the `Server` header, so the answer says only `Salam`.

net-http-guide-static.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import os

func main:
    _ := os.MkdirAll("public/css")
    _ := os.WriteFile("public/index.html", "<h1>Welcome</h1>")
    _ := os.WriteFile("public/css/site.css", "body { margin: 0 }")
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Static(r, "/site", "public")
    mut s := http.NewServer(19764)
    http.HideTokens(s)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19764"
    a := http.Get(base + "/site/index.html")
    println http.Status(a), http.GetHeader(a, "content-type"), http.Body(a)
    b := http.Get(base + "/site/css/site.css")
    println http.GetHeader(b, "content-type"), http.Body(b)
    println http.Status(http.Get(base + "/site/missing.png"))
    println http.Status(http.Get(base + "/site/../secret.txt"))
    println http.GetHeader(a, "server")
end
```

Output:

```text
200 text/html; charset=utf-8 <h1>Welcome</h1>
text/css body { margin: 0 }
404
404
Salam
```

## Running a real server

The examples above use `RunBackground` so that one program can be both the server and its own client. A real service calls `Run`, which never returns. Read the port from the environment, listen on `0.0.0.0` when the server sits in a container or behind a proxy, and turn on the access log while you are getting it running.

net-http-guide-server.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import os
import conv

func home(ctx: i64):
    http.Html(ctx, "<h1>Salam</h1>")
end

func health(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, `{"status":"ok"}`)
end

func main:
    mut port := 8080
    if os.Env("PORT") != "":
        port = conv.Atoi(os.Env("PORT"))
    end
    http.SetMaxBodyBytes(1048576)
    http.SetKeepAliveIdle(5000)
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", home)
    router.Get(r, "/health", health)
    router.Static(r, "/assets", "public")
    mut s := http.NewServer(port)
    http.SetHost(s, "0.0.0.0")
    http.HideTokens(s)
    http.EnableAccessLog(s)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println "listening on port " + port
    http.Run(s)
end
```

Run it and try it from a second terminal:

```salam
PORT=8080 salam run server.salam
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

The limits are for the whole process: `SetMaxBodyBytes` and `SetMaxHeaderBytes` reject requests that are too large, `SetKeepAliveIdle` closes idle connections, and `SetKeepAliveMaxRequests` caps how many requests one connection may send. For HTTPS, call `RunTLS` with a certificate and key file instead of `Run`, or put the server behind a proxy that handles TLS.

## Calling an API as a client

`Get`, `Post` and the other one-line calls send a request and return a `Response`; the `...With` forms take a map of extra headers. The program below shows the four answers a client has to handle. A `Post` without a content type reaches the server as a form, so a JSON API refuses it with 415; the same body through `PostWith` with `Content-Type: application/json` creates the ticket. A redirect is not followed, so `Get` returns the 302 and you read `Location` yourself. A server that is not running gives status 0 and the reason in `Error`.

net-http-guide-client.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import encoding.json

func create_ticket(ctx: i64):
    kind := http.Header(ctx, "Content-Type")
    if kind != "application/json":
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 415)
        http.Json(ctx, "{\"error\":\"expected JSON, got " + kind + "\"}")
        ret
    end
    title := json.Get(http.Body(ctx), "title")
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 201)
    http.Json(ctx, "{\"id\":31,\"title\":" + json.Str(title) + "}")
end

func old_tickets(ctx: i64): http.Redirect(ctx, "/v2/tickets") end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/tickets", create_ticket)
    router.Get(r, "/tickets", old_tickets)
    mut s := http.NewServer(18631)
    http.SetHost(s, "127.0.0.1")
    http.Use(s, r)
    if not http.RunBackground(s):
        println "port 18631 is busy"
        ret 1
    end
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:18631"
    body := `{"title": "Printer is out of paper"}`

    plain := http.Post(base + "/tickets", body)
    println "Post:", http.Status(plain), http.Body(plain)

    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/json")
    made := http.PostWith(base + "/tickets", body, headers)
    println "PostWith:", http.Status(made), http.Ok(made), "id", json.GetInt(http.Body(made), "id")

    moved := http.Get(base + "/tickets")
    println "Get:", http.Status(moved), "Location:", http.GetHeader(moved, "location")

    down := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:1/tickets")
    println "dead server:", http.Status(down), http.Ok(down), http.Error(down)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
Post: 415 {"error":"expected JSON, got application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}
PostWith: 201 true id 31
Get: 302 Location: /v2/tickets
dead server: 0 false could not connect to 127.0.0.1:1
```

Gzip and chunked answers are decoded for you, and every request is sent with `Connection: close`. For a series of calls that share a login, `NewClient` keeps the cookies from each answer and sends them with the next request, plus any headers set with `SetHeader`. A cookie is sent back only to the host that set it; a cookie you add with `SetCookie` goes to the host of the first request, never to a host a redirect leads to.

Any number of threads can use the one-line calls at once, because a call keeps no state outside itself. A `Client` from `NewClient` can be shared by threads too: it carries its own lock, so `SetHeader`, the cookie jar and the settings stay consistent. Call `Free` when you are done with a shared client. A `Client {}` written as a literal has no lock and belongs to one thread.

## Raw requests: your own headers, bytes and time limits

The one-line calls above build the request for you. When you need full control of the request line and headers, for example to sign a request, to send a binary body or to talk to an API with unusual headers, write the request head yourself and send it with `SendRaw`. The aws, webpush, db/meilisearch, db/elasticsearch and db/typesense packages are built on these calls. The examples run against a small server in a thread of the same program, so they need no network.

Every raw call takes an `Endpoint` from `ParseEndpoint` (host, port and TLS on or off; any path in the URL is dropped, because the path goes in your request line) and a request head: the request line, the headers and an empty line, each line ending in `\r\n`. The body is a pointer and a length, so it can hold any bytes. The answer is a `RawResponse` with the body as bytes, chunked bodies already decoded, freed with `FreeRaw`. `SendRaw` waits as long as the server does; `SendRawTimeout` adds a time limit in milliseconds; `SendRawTLS` adds your own `tls.Config`. A response larger than `RawLimit` (256 MB by default) is reported as an error.

Things that catch people out:

- Send `Connection: close` unless the answer is framed. The raw calls stop as soon as an answer with a `Content-Length` or a chunked body is complete. An answer with neither is read until the server closes the connection, so on a kept-alive connection the call waits until then (or until the time limit).

- `ok` means a 2xx status, not "an answer arrived". Check `status` to tell a 404 from a dead server.

- A `str` stops at the first zero byte, so binary bodies stay in `data`; `RawText` cuts at the first zero.

## POST JSON with your own headers

`ParseEndpoint` turns a URL into the host, port and whether to use TLS. The request head is plain text that you write: the request line, a `Host` header, and here an `Authorization` token, the content type and the body length, closed by an empty line. `SendRawTimeout` sends the head and the body and returns the answer; `RawText` turns the reply body into a `str`. `HeaderValue` finds a header in the response head, ignoring case.

net-http-raw-post-json.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp
import encoding.json

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func read_request(conn: tcp.Conn): str:
    mut got := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
    until got.find("\r\n\r\n") < 0:
        got += tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
    end
    head_end := got.find("\r\n\r\n") + 4
    want := http.HeaderValue(got, "content-length").to_int()
    until got.len() < head_end + want:
        got += tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
    end
    ret got
end

func api():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    request := read_request(conn)
    at := request.find("\r\n\r\n") + 4
    body := request.substr(at, request.len() - at)
    name := json.Get(body, "name")
    auth := http.HeaderValue(request, "authorization")
    reply := "{\"id\": 7, \"name\": \"" + name + "\", \"auth\": \"" + auth + "\"}"
    head := "HTTP/1.1 201 Created\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nLocation: /users/7\r\nContent-Length: " + reply.len() + "\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    _ := tcp.Write(conn, head + reply)
    tcp.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(api)
    ep := http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server))
    body := `{"name": "Sara", "role": "editor"}`
    mut head := "POST /users HTTP/1.1\r\n"
    head += "Host: 127.0.0.1\r\n"
    head += "Authorization: Bearer abc123\r\n"
    head += "Content-Type: application/json\r\n"
    head += "Content-Length: " + body.len() + "\r\n"
    head += "Connection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut r := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, body as void*, body.len(), 5000)
    reply := http.RawText(r)
    http.FreeRaw(r)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println "status:", r.status, r.ok
    println "location:", http.HeaderValue(r.head, "Location")
    println "id:", json.GetInt(reply, "id")
    println "body:", reply
end
```

Output:

```text
status: 201 true
location: /users/7
id: 7
body: {"id": 7, "name": "Sara", "auth": "Bearer abc123"}
```

`Content-Length` must be the length in bytes, which is what `str.len()` returns, so it stays right for text in any language. A wrong length makes servers wait for more data or cut the body.

## Status codes and failures

A `RawResponse` tells three cases apart. `ok` is true only for a 2xx status. A 4xx or 5xx answer still has its `status` and a body, which usually explain the problem. When no answer came at all, because the connection was refused, the host was unknown or the URL could not be parsed, `status` is 0 and `error` says why.

net-http-raw-status-errors.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func api():
    repeat 2:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        request := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        if request.find("GET /missing ") == 0:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "404 Not Found", "application/json", `{"error": "no such page"}`)
        else:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "503 Service Unavailable", "text/plain", "try again later")
        end
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func get(ep: http.Endpoint, path: str):
    head := "GET " + path + " HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: " + ep.host + "\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut r := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, null, 0, 5000)
    body := http.RawText(r)
    if r.ok:
        println path, "worked:", body
    else r.status > 0:
        println path, "answered", r.status, "with", body
    else:
        println path, "failed:", r.error
    end
    http.FreeRaw(r)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(api)
    ep := http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server))
    get(ep, "/missing")
    get(ep, "/busy")
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    get(http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:1"), "/nobody-listens")
    bad := http.ParseEndpoint("ftp://files.example.com")
    println "ftp endpoint ok:", bad.ok
    get(bad, "/")
end
```

Output:

```text
/missing answered 404 with {"error": "no such page"}
/busy answered 503 with try again later
/nobody-listens failed: could not connect to 127.0.0.1:1
ftp endpoint ok: false
/ failed: the endpoint could not be parsed
```

A 503 or 429 often means "try again later"; read `Retry-After` with `HeaderValue` before you retry, and do not retry a 4xx such as 404, which will not change.

## A small API client

A struct that holds the endpoint and the token, with one method per kind of request, keeps the header writing in one place. The JSON in the replies is read with encoding/json: `json.Get` for a field and `json.Items` to walk an array.

net-http-raw-api-client.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp
import encoding.json

mut server := tcp.Server {}

struct Api:
    pub ep: http.Endpoint = http.Endpoint {}
    pub token: str = ""

    pub func get(path: str): str:
        mut head := "GET " + path + " HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        head += "Host: " + this.ep.host + "\r\n"
        head += "Authorization: Bearer " + this.token + "\r\n"
        head += "Accept: application/json\r\n"
        head += "Connection: close\r\n\r\n"
        mut r := http.SendRawTimeout(this.ep, head, null, 0, 5000)
        defer http.FreeRaw(r)
        ret http.RawText(r)
    end
end

func backend():
    repeat 2:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        request := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        if request.find("GET /users/7 ") == 0:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "application/json", `{"id": 7, "name": "Sara", "city": "Shiraz"}`)
        else:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "application/json", `[{"item": "pen", "qty": 3}, {"item": "notebook", "qty": 1}]`)
        end
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(backend)
    api := Api { ep = http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server)), token = "abc123" }
    user := api.get("/users/7")
    println json.Get(user, "name"), "from", json.Get(user, "city")
    orders := api.get("/users/7/orders")
    each order in json.Items(orders):
        println " ", json.GetInt(order, "qty"), "x", json.Get(order, "item")
    end
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
Sara from Shiraz
  3 x pen
  1 x notebook
```

## Chunked answers and time limits

A server that does not know the length of its answer in advance sends it in chunks, each one prefixed by its size in hex. `SendRawTimeout` removes that framing for you. The last parameter of `SendRawTimeout` is a time limit in milliseconds for each read and write, and on Linux also for the connect, so a server that accepts the connection and then says nothing cannot hang the program. The second request below hits such a server with a 300 ms limit.

net-http-raw-chunked.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func feed():
    repeat 2 in i:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        _ := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        if i < 1:
            _ := tcp.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n6\r\nnews: \r\n9\r\nall quiet\r\n0\r\n\r\n")
        else:
            _ := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        end
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(feed)
    ep := http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server))
    head := "GET /feed HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"

    mut raw := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, null, 0, 2000)
    println "body:", http.RawText(raw)
    http.FreeRaw(raw)

    mut slow := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, null, 0, 300)
    println "silent server:", slow.ok, slow.status, slow.error
    http.FreeRaw(slow)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
body: news: all quiet
silent server: false 0 the request timed out
```

A timeout is reported as `the request timed out` and an answer cut short by a closing connection as `the response body was cut short`; both are worth a retry later. `SendRaw` has no time limit at all; give `SendRawTimeout` a limit for any server you do not control. `SendRawTLS` takes the same limit plus a `tls.Config` for a private CA.

## Binary downloads

A `str` ends at the first zero byte, so an image or a zip file turned into one is cut short. Read it from the `RawResponse` instead: `data` points at the body bytes and `len` is their count. The program downloads twelve bytes of a PNG header and shows that `RawText`, which turns the body into a `str`, keeps only the eight bytes before the first zero.

net-http-raw-binary.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp
import mem
import conv

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func files():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    _ := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
    image := [137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10, 0, 0, 0, 13]
    buf := mem.Allocate(12 as u64) as u8*
    repeat 12 in i:
        buf[i] = image[i] as u8
    end
    _ := tcp.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: image/png\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
    _ := tcp.WriteBytes(conn, buf as void*, 12)
    mem.Free(buf as void*)
    tcp.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(files)
    ep := http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server))
    head := "GET /logo.png HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut r := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, null, 0, 5000)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println r.ok, r.status, http.HeaderValue(r.head, "content-type")
    println "bytes received:", r.len
    bytes := r.data as u8*
    mut hex := ""
    repeat r.len in i:
        if i > 0: hex += " " end
        if bytes[i] < 16: hex += "0" end
        hex += conv.FormatHex(bytes[i] as u64)
    end
    println hex
    println "is a PNG:", r.len >= 4 and bytes[1] as int == 80 and bytes[2] as int == 78 and bytes[3] as int == 71
    println "RawText keeps", http.RawText(r).len(), "bytes"
    http.FreeRaw(r)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 200 image/png
bytes received: 12
89 50 4e 47 0d 0a 1a 0a 00 00 00 0d
is a PNG: true
RawText keeps 8 bytes
```

A `RawResponse` body is limited to `RawLimit` bytes, 256 MB unless you change it with `SetRawLimit`; a larger answer is reported as an error instead of filling memory. The `data` buffer belongs to you until `FreeRaw`.

## HTTPS

An `https://` URL gives an endpoint with `secure` set, and the same calls then speak TLS through tls, checking the server certificate. Nothing else changes. This example asks the GitHub API about the Salam repository, so it needs the internet; GitHub requires a `User-Agent` header.

net-http-raw-https.salam

```salam
import net.http
import encoding.json

func main:
    ep := http.ParseEndpoint("https://api.github.com")
    println ep.host, ep.port, ep.secure
    mut head := "GET /repos/SalamLang/Salam HTTP/1.1\r\n"
    head += "Host: api.github.com\r\n"
    head += "User-Agent: salam-example\r\n"
    head += "Accept: application/vnd.github+json\r\n"
    head += "Connection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut r := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, null, 0, 10000)
    defer http.FreeRaw(r)
    body := http.RawText(r)
    if r.status == 0:
        println "request failed:", r.error
        ret 1
    end
    println "status:", r.status
    println "rate limit left:", http.HeaderValue(r.head, "x-ratelimit-remaining")
    if r.ok:
        println json.Get(body, "full_name"), "is written in", json.Get(body, "language")
    end
    ret 0
end
```

When this page was written it printed:

```salam
api.github.com 443 true
status: 200
rate limit left: 58
SalamLang/Salam is written in TeX
```

The rate limit number counts down with each call from your address, and the language is what GitHub detects for the repository at the time.

## Timeouts, limits and redirects

Client requests run under the limits below. `RequestOptions` holds the limits and `Do` sends a request with them; a `Client` keeps its own copy, changed with `SetTimeout`, `SetIdleTimeout`, `SetMaxRedirects` and `SetMaxBody`. `idle_ms` (30 seconds by default) is how long one read or write may stall, `timeout_ms` (off by default) is the time for the whole request including redirects, and `max_body` (256 MB by default) bounds the body, also after gzip is unpacked, so a small compressed answer cannot fill memory. Looking up a host name is done by the system resolver, and on systems other than Linux the connect itself waits the system default; neither is covered by these limits. A request that runs out of time reports `the request timed out`, and an answer cut short by a closing connection is an error rather than a smaller body.

Redirects are followed only when `max_redirects` is above zero. A 301 or 302 after a POST and every 303 turn into a GET without the body; 307 and 308 repeat the request as it was. When a redirect leads to another host, the `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers are dropped, and a redirect from https to http is refused. The final address is in the `url` field of the response.

The request is checked before anything is sent: a method, header name or address with a space or a control character, and a header value with a line break, are refused with a message in `err`, so a value taken from outside cannot add headers to the request. A `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection` or `Accept-Encoding` header of yours is replaced by the one the client computes. The example sends a request to a server that answers late and one that never answers, follows a redirect and refuses an answer that is too large.

net-http-guide-limits.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp
import sync

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func backend():
    repeat 6:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        request := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        if request.find("GET /old ") == 0:
            _ := tcp.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 302 Found\r\nLocation: /new\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
        else request.find("GET /silent ") == 0:
            sync.SleepMs(700)
        else request.find("GET /big ") == 0:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "0123456789")
        else:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "landed")
        end
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(backend)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server)
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    c.SetMaxRedirects(3)
    c.SetTimeout(5000)
    c.SetIdleTimeout(2000)
    c.SetMaxBody(1000)
    r := c.Get(base + "/old")
    println r.status, http.Body(r), r.url.find("/new") > 0
    mut tight := http.RequestOptions {}
    tight.max_body = 5
    big := http.Do("GET", base + "/big", http.NewHeaders(), "", tight)
    println big.status, big.err
    mut quick := http.RequestOptions {}
    quick.timeout_ms = 200
    silent := http.Do("GET", base + "/silent", http.NewHeaders(), "", quick)
    println silent.status, silent.err
    raw := c.RequestBytes("GET", base + "/big", "", "")
    println raw.status, raw.body.len
    println c.RequestRaw("GET", base + "/new", "X-Id: 1\r\n", "").status
    c.Free()
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
200 landed true
200 the response body is larger than the 5-byte limit
0 the request timed out
200 10
200
```

## Which function for which job

| Job | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Read a path parameter, query value or form field | `Param`, `Query`, `Form` |
| Read the raw body or a request header | `Body`, `Header` |
| Answer with text, JSON or HTML | `Text`, `Json`, `Html` |
| Choose the status or add a header | `SetStatus`, `SetHeader` |
| Send the browser somewhere else | `Redirect` |
| Hold the request in a struct instead of the bare id | `Ctx`, then the same `Param`, `Json` and the rest |
| A request with a time limit, a size limit or redirects | `Do` with `RequestOptions`, or `SetTimeout`, `SetMaxRedirects` on a client |
| One request from a program | `Get`, `Post`, `GetWith`, `PostWith`, `Request` |
| Several requests that share cookies | `NewClient` |
| A request with headers you write yourself, or a binary body | `ParseEndpoint`, `SendRaw`, `SendRawTimeout`, `SendRawTLS` |
| Read the bytes of a raw answer | `RawResponse` `data` and `len`, `RawText`, then `FreeRaw` |
| Check the answer | `Ok` for a 2xx status, `Status` for the code (0 when nothing answered), `Error` for the reason |

A value you read from the request, such as `Param` or `Form`, belongs to that request and is freed when the handler returns. To keep it longer, in a global list or a session, store a copy made with `str.Clone` or a new string built with `+`.

## Types

### `Endpoint`

```salam
struct Endpoint
```

The address of one server: the host, the port and whether it is secure.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 443` | The port: the one in the URL, else 80 for http and 443 for https. |
| `secure` | `bool = true` | Connect with TLS. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The address was read correctly; false for anything that does not start with `http://` or `https://`. |

net-http-SendRaw.salam

```salam
import tls
import net.http
import net.tcp

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func responder():
    repeat 3:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        _ := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "hello from the server")
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func main:
    remote := http.ParseEndpoint("https://api.example.com:8443")
    println remote.ok, remote.host, remote.port, remote.secure
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(responder)
    local := http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server))
    head := "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut r := http.SendRaw(local, head, null, 0)
    println r.ok, r.status, http.RawText(r), "[" + r.error + "]"
    println http.HeaderValue(r.head, "content-type")
    http.FreeRaw(r)
    mut raw := http.SendRawTimeout(local, head, null, 0, 2000)
    println raw.ok, raw.status, raw.len, http.RawText(raw)
    http.FreeRaw(raw)
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("127.0.0.1")
    cfg.ca_file = "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"
    mut secured := http.SendRawTLS(local, head, null, 0, 2000, cfg)
    println secured.status, secured.len
    http.FreeRaw(secured)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println http.RawLimit() > 0
    http.SetRawLimit(1024 * 1024)
    println http.RawLimit()
end
```

Output:

```text
true api.example.com 8443 true
true 200 hello from the server []
text/plain
true 200 21 hello from the server
200 21
true
1048576
```

### `Cookie`

```salam
struct Cookie
```

One response cookie.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |
| `path` | `str = "/"` | The path the cookie is sent for; `/` by default. |
| `domain` | `str = ""` | The domain; empty means this host. |
| `max_age` | `int = 0` | The lifetime in seconds. |
| `has_max_age` | `bool = false` | A lifetime was set; without one the cookie goes when the browser closes. |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | Send it over HTTPS only. |
| `http_only` | `bool = true` | Keep it out of reach of the page JavaScript; true by default. |
| `same_site` | `str = "Lax"` | The SameSite policy; `Lax` by default. |

net-http-Cookie.salam

```salam
import net.http

func main:
    c := http.NewCookie("theme", "dark")
    println c.name, c.value, c.path, c.http_only, c.same_site, c.has_max_age
    mut s := http.ExpiringCookie("sid", "x1", 3600)
    s.secure = true
    s.domain = "salamlang.ir"
    println s.max_age, s.has_max_age, s.secure, s.domain
    gone := http.ExpiredCookie("sid", "/", "salamlang.ir")
    println gone.max_age, gone.has_max_age
    println http.UrlDecode("a%20b+c")
end
```

Output:

```text
theme dark / true Lax false
3600 true true salamlang.ir
-1 true
a b c
```

### `RawResponse`

```salam
struct RawResponse
```

A response with a binary body.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The status code. |
| `head` | `str = ""` | The headers. |
| `data` | `void*` | The address of the body. |
| `len` | `int = 0` | The length of the body in bytes, after chunked decoding. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The status is 2xx. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The error message, such as `the request timed out` or `the response body was cut short`. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-SendRaw.salam

### `Response`

```salam
struct Response
```

The response to a client request.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The status code. |
| `body` | `str = ""` | The body. |
| `head` | `str = ""` | The raw headers. |
| `err` | `str = ""` | The error message, when the request did not get through or was refused for a limit; the status is 0 when nothing came back. |
| `url` | `str = ""` | The address of the last request, after redirects. |

net-http-Client.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func echo(ctx: i64):
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "X-Tag", "a")
    http.SetCookie(ctx, http.NewCookie("sid", "abc"))
    http.Text(ctx, http.Method(ctx) + " " + http.Header(ctx, "X-Token") + " " + http.Body(ctx))
end

func cookies(ctx: i64):
    all := http.Cookies(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "" + all.size() + " " + http.CookieValue(ctx, "lang") + " " + http.HasCookie(ctx, "sid"))
    http.ClearCookie(ctx, "old")
    http.ClearCookieAt(ctx, "scoped", "/admin", "")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    each method in ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS", "HEAD"]:
        router.Method(r, method, "/echo", echo)
    end
    router.Get(r, "/cookies", cookies)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19623)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    url := "http://127.0.0.1:19623/echo"
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("X-Token", "t1")
    a := http.GetWith(url, headers)
    println http.Ok(a), http.Status(a), http.Body(a), "[" + http.Error(a) + "]"
    println http.Headers(a).has("X-Tag"), http.HeaderValues(a, "set-cookie")
    println http.CookieMap(a).get("sid"), http.RawHeaders(a).len() > 0, http.Raw(a).len() > 0
    println http.Body(http.Post(url, "a")), http.Body(http.PutWith(url, "b", headers))
    println http.Body(http.Delete(url)), http.Body(http.DeleteWith(url, headers))
    println http.Body(http.Patch(url, "c")), http.Body(http.PatchWith(url, "d", headers))
    println http.Body(http.Options(url)), http.Body(http.OptionsWith(url, headers))
    println http.Status(http.Head(url)), http.Status(http.HeadWith(url, headers))
    println http.Body(http.Put(url, "e")), http.Body(http.Get(url))
    println http.Body(http.RequestRaw("POST", url, "X-Token: raw\r\n", "f"))
    mut params := http.NewHeaders()
    params.insert("q", "hello world")
    println http.EncodeForm(params), http.WithQuery("http://x.ir/s", params)
    mut jar := http.NewHeaders()
    jar.insert("lang", "en")
    jar.insert("sid", "abc")
    headers.insert("Cookie", http.CookieHeader(jar))
    b := http.GetWith("http://127.0.0.1:19623/cookies", headers)
    println http.Body(b), http.SetCookieLines(b).len()
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    c.SetCookie("lang", "en")
    println http.Body(c.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19623/cookies"))
    c.ClearCookies()
    mut extra := http.NewHeaders()
    extra.insert("X-Token", "c1")
    println http.Body(c.RequestWith("PUT", url, "g", extra)), http.Body(c.Request("PATCH", url, "h"))
    println http.Body(c.Put(url, "i")), http.Body(c.Delete(url)), http.Body(c.Patch(url, "j")), http.Body(c.Options(url)), http.Status(c.Head(url))
    bad := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:1/")
    println http.Ok(bad), http.Error(bad) != ""
end
```

Output:

```text
true 200 GET t1  []
true ["sid=abc; Path=/; SameSite=Lax; HttpOnly"]
abc true true
POST  a PUT t1 b
DELETE   DELETE t1
PATCH  c PATCH t1 d
OPTIONS   OPTIONS t1
200 200
PUT  e GET
POST raw f
q=hello%20world http://x.ir/s?q=hello%20world
2 en true 2
1 en false
PUT c1 g PATCH  h
PUT  i DELETE   PATCH  j OPTIONS   200
false true
```

### `BytesResponse`

```salam
struct BytesResponse
```

A response whose body is raw bytes, for downloads such as archives and images that a `str` would cut at the first zero byte.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The status code. |
| `head` | `str = ""` | The raw headers. |
| `body` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The body as a `compress.ByteBuf`; free it with `compress.BufFree`. |
| `err` | `str = ""` | The error message, when the request did not get through; the status is then 0. |
| `url` | `str = ""` | The address of the last request, after redirects. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-Client.salam

### `RequestOptions`

```salam
struct RequestOptions
```

The limits of a request: `idle_ms` for one stalled read or write (30000), `timeout_ms` for the whole request (0, none), `max_body` in bytes (256 MB) and `max_redirects` (0).

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idle_ms` | `int = 30000` | How long one read or write may stall, in milliseconds. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int = 0` | The time for the whole request, redirects included; 0 means none. |
| `max_body` | `int = 268435456` | The largest body in bytes, measured after gzip is unpacked. |
| `max_redirects` | `int = 0` | How many redirects to follow; 0 follows none. |

net-http-Do.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.tcp
import sync

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func backend():
    repeat 6:
        conn := tcp.Accept(server)
        request := tcp.Read(conn, 4096)
        if request.find("GET /old ") == 0:
            _ := tcp.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 302 Found\r\nLocation: /new\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
        else request.find("GET /silent ") == 0:
            sync.SleepMs(700)
        else request.find("GET /big ") == 0:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "0123456789")
        else:
            tcp.WriteHTTP(conn, "200 OK", "text/plain", "landed")
        end
        tcp.Close(conn)
    end
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(backend)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:" + tcp.Port(server)
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    c.SetMaxRedirects(3)
    c.SetTimeout(5000)
    c.SetIdleTimeout(2000)
    c.SetMaxBody(1000)
    r := c.Get(base + "/old")
    println r.status, http.Body(r), r.url.find("/new") > 0
    mut tight := http.RequestOptions {}
    tight.max_body = 5
    big := http.Do("GET", base + "/big", http.NewHeaders(), "", tight)
    println big.status, big.err
    mut quick := http.RequestOptions {}
    quick.timeout_ms = 200
    silent := http.Do("GET", base + "/silent", http.NewHeaders(), "", quick)
    println silent.status, silent.err
    raw := c.RequestBytes("GET", base + "/big", "", "")
    println raw.status, raw.body.len
    println c.RequestRaw("GET", base + "/new", "X-Id: 1\r\n", "").status
    c.Free()
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
200 landed true
200 the response body is larger than the 5-byte limit
0 the request timed out
200 10
200
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

An HTTP client that keeps fixed headers and cookies between requests; a simple browser.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cookies` | `HashMap` | The cookies it took from the responses; each is sent back only to the host that set it. |
| `headers` | `HashMap` | The headers sent with every request. |
| `cookie_hosts` | `HashMap` | Which host set each cookie in `cookies`. |
| `cookie_secure` | `HashMap` | The cookies that came with the `Secure` attribute; they are sent back over HTTPS only, never over plain HTTP. |
| `options` | `RequestOptions` | The limits of this client: a `RequestOptions`. |
| `mu` | `sync.Mutex` | The lock that lets threads share a client made by `NewClient`. |

net-http-Context.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func hello(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    name := http.Query(ctx, "name")
    if http.HasCookie(ctx, "seen"):
        http.Text(ctx, "hello again " + name + " (" + http.CookieValue(ctx, "seen") + ")")
    else:
        http.SetCookie(ctx, http.ExpiringCookie("seen", "1", 3600))
        http.Text(ctx, "hello " + name + " (" + http.RawQuery(ctx) + ")")
    end
end

func book(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "X-Method", http.Method(ctx))
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 202)
    http.Json(ctx, `{"id": "` + http.Param(ctx, "id") + `", "path": "` + http.Path(ctx) + `"}`)
end

func form(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    http.Text(ctx, http.Form(ctx, "a") + "|" + http.Body(ctx) + "|" + http.Header(ctx, "Content-Type"))
end

func logout(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    http.ClearCookie(ctx, "seen")
    http.Redirect(ctx, "/hello")
end

func page(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    cookies := http.Cookies(ctx)
    http.Html(ctx, "<p>" + cookies.size() + "</p>")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/hello", hello)
    router.Get(r, "/books/:id", book)
    router.Post(r, "/form", form)
    router.Get(r, "/logout", logout)
    router.Get(r, "/page", page)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19622)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19622"
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/hello?name=Maryam"))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/hello?name=Maryam"))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/page"))
    a := c.Get(base + "/books/7")
    println http.Status(a), http.Body(a), http.GetHeader(a, "x-method")
    c.SetHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    println http.Body(c.Post(base + "/form", "a=1&b=2"))
    b := c.Get(base + "/logout")
    println http.Status(b), http.SetCookieLines(b).len() > 0
end
```

Output:

```text
hello Maryam (name=Maryam)
hello again Maryam (1)
<p>1</p>
202 {"id": "7", "path": "/books/7"} GET
1|a=1&b=2|application/x-www-form-urlencoded
302 true
```

### `Server`


An HTTP server.

| Name | Type | Description |

| `port` | `int = 0` | The port. |
| `host` | `str = "0.0.0.0"` | The listen address; `0.0.0.0` by default, meaning every address. |
| `router` | `router.Router` | The router for the requests. |
| `hide_tokens` | `bool = false` | Hide the server version in the responses. |
| `access_log` | `bool = false` | Log every request to the output. |

net-http-Server.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router
import net.tcp

func hello(h: i64):
    ctx := http.Ctx(h)
    conn := http.ConnOf(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "hello " + tcp.ConnOk(conn))
end

func main:
    http.SetKeepAliveIdle(5000)
    http.SetKeepAliveMaxRequests(100)
    http.SetMaxHeaderBytes(16384)
    http.SetMaxBodyBytes(1048576)
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", hello)
    mut s := http.NewServer(8080)
    http.SetHost(s, "0.0.0.0")
    http.HideTokens(s)
    http.EnableAccessLog(s)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println http.SERVER_VERSION, http.IsEdge()
    if not http.IsEdge():
        http.RunTLS(s, "cert.pem", "key.pem")
    end
    http.Run(s)
end
```

## Functions

### `Method`

```salam
func Method(h: i64): str
```

The request method, such as GET.

net-http-Handle.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.router

func home(ctx: i64):
    http.Text(ctx, "hello from the server")
end

func book(ctx: i64):
    id := http.Param(ctx, "id")
    format := http.Query(ctx, "format")
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "X-Book", id)
    http.Json(ctx, `{"id": "` + id + `", "format": "` + format + `", "raw": "` + http.RawQuery(ctx) + `"}`)
end

func create(ctx: i64):
    name := http.Form(ctx, "name")
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 201)
    http.Text(ctx, http.Method(ctx) + " " + http.Path(ctx) + " " + name + " " + http.Header(ctx, "X-Client"))
end

func raw(ctx: i64):
    answer := http.Own(ctx, "body: " + http.Body(ctx))
    http.Text(ctx, answer)
end

func page(ctx: i64):
    http.Html(ctx, "<h1>hello</h1>")
end

func old(ctx: i64):
    http.Redirect(ctx, "/")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", home)
    router.Get(r, "/books/:id", book)
    router.Post(r, "/books", create)
    router.Put(r, "/raw", raw)
    router.Get(r, "/page", page)
    router.Get(r, "/old", old)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19621)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19621"
    a := http.Get(base + "/")
    println http.Status(a), http.Body(a)
    b := http.Get(base + "/books/42?format=pdf")
    println http.Body(b), http.GetHeader(b, "x-book")
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    headers.insert("X-Client", "salam")
    c := http.PostWith(base + "/books", "name=Maryam", headers)
    println http.Status(c), http.Body(c)
    println http.Body(http.Put(base + "/raw", "data"))
    d := http.Get(base + "/page")
    println http.GetHeader(d, "content-type"), http.Body(d)
    e := http.Request("GET", base + "/old", http.NewHeaders(), "")
    println http.Status(e), http.GetHeader(e, "location")
    println http.Status(http.Get(base + "/nope"))
end
```

Output:

```text
true
200 hello from the server
{"id": "42", "format": "pdf", "raw": "format=pdf"} 42
201 POST /books Maryam salam
body: data
text/html; charset=utf-8 <h1>hello</h1>
302 /
404
```

### `BodyLen`

```salam
func BodyLen(h: i64): int
```

The length of the request body in bytes, zero bytes included; use it with `BodyBytes`.

net-http-Upload.salam

```salam
import mem
import str
import compress
import net.http
import net.mime
import net.router

func echo(ctx: i64):
    n := http.BodyLen(ctx)
    p := http.BodyBytes(ctx) as u8*
    mut zeros := 0
    repeat n in i:
        if p[i] == 0 as u8: zeros += 1 end
    end
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "X-Zeros", http.Own(ctx, str.FromInt(zeros as i64)))
    http.Bytes(ctx, "application/octet-stream", http.BodyBytes(ctx), n)
end

func upload(ctx: i64):
    mut parts := http.Multipart(ctx)
    defer mime.FreeMultipart(parts)
    if parts.items.len() == 0:
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 400)
        http.Text(ctx, "not multipart")
        ret
    end
    mut answer := ""
    each part in parts.items:
        answer = answer + part.name + ":" + part.filename + ":" + str.FromInt(part.body.len as i64) + " "
    end
    answer = answer + "note=" + mime.PartValue(parts, "note")
    http.Text(ctx, http.Own(ctx, answer))
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/echo", echo)
    router.Post(r, "/upload", upload)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19645)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println http.RunBackground(s)
    ep := http.ParseEndpoint("http://127.0.0.1:19645")

    data := mem.Allocate(4 as u64)
    bytes := data as u8*
    bytes[0] = 83 as u8
    bytes[1] = 0 as u8
    bytes[2] = 255 as u8
    bytes[3] = 0 as u8
    head := "POST /echo HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\nContent-Length: 4\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut a := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, head, data, 4, 2000)
    back := a.data as u8*
    println a.status, a.len, http.HeaderValue(a.head, "x-zeros"), http.HeaderValue(a.head, "content-type")
    println back[0] as int, back[1] as int, back[2] as int, back[3] as int
    http.FreeRaw(a)

    mut w := mime.NewMultipartWriter()
    mime.WriteField(w, "note", "holiday")
    mime.WriteFileBytes(w, "photo", "pic.bin", "image/png", data, 4)
    mut body := mime.CloseWriter(w)
    up := "POST /upload HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\nContent-Type: " + mime.ContentTypeHeader(w) + "\r\nContent-Length: " + str.FromInt(body.len as i64) + "\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
    mut b := http.SendRawTimeout(ep, up, body.data, body.len, 2000)
    println b.status, http.RawText(b)
    http.FreeRaw(b)
    compress.BufFree(body)
    mem.Free(data)

    plain := http.Post("http://127.0.0.1:19645/upload", "note=x")
    println http.Status(plain), http.Body(plain)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
200 4 2 application/octet-stream
83 0 255 0
200 note::7 photo:pic.bin:4 note=holiday
400 not multipart
```

### `BodyBytes`

```salam
func BodyBytes(h: i64): void*
```

A pointer to the request body bytes, for uploads and other binary bodies that `Body` would cut at the first zero byte. It belongs to the request and is freed when the handler returns; copy what you keep, and do not free it.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-Upload.salam

### `Multipart`

```salam
func Multipart(h: i64): mime.MultipartParts
```

Reads a `multipart/form-data` body into its parts, each with its name, file name, content type and bytes; no parts when the request is not multipart. The caller owns the result and frees it with `mime.FreeMultipart`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-Upload.salam

### `Bytes`

```salam
func Bytes(h: i64, content_type: str, p: void*, n: int)
```

Sends `n` bytes from a pointer as the body, with the given content type; binary safe, for files, images and archives. The bytes are copied, so the call takes nothing over: free the pointer afterwards only if you allocated it, and never free one the request owns, such as the one `BodyBytes` returns.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-Upload.salam

### `Own`

```salam

```

Hands a string the handler built to the context, so it is freed when the request ends; do not hand it a string that came from the context itself, such as the body.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-Handle.salam

### `GetBytesWith`

# net/http/middleware

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-middleware/

The usual security, cache and CORS headers, and request logging, in one call.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add net.http.middleware`

Five small helpers for net/http handlers: `AllowAll` for CORS, `Secure` for basic security headers, `NoCache` and `Cache` for caching, and `Log` for a line per request. Each takes the context id, as the handler does, and only sets response headers (or prints), so you call them on the first lines of a handler.

There is no middleware chain in Salam and no way to wrap a handler from outside. A middleware is an ordinary function you call with the context id, and the headers it sets go out with whatever the handler writes after it. That keeps the order visible in the handler itself. For logins use net/http/session, and for checking input net/http/validate.

What to know before you rely on them:

- `AllowAll` does not list `PATCH`. It allows GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS with the `Content-Type` and `Authorization` headers, for every origin. A browser refuses a PATCH from another origin, and `*` cannot be used with cookies; write your own rule for those (last section).

- `Secure` is a minimum. It sets `nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `X-XSS-Protection`, a header current browsers ignore. It sets no `Content-Security-Policy` and no `Strict-Transport-Security`.

- The last call wins. A header set twice with the same name keeps the last value, so `NoCache` followed by `Cache` leaves only `max-age`.

- `Log` prints with `println` before the handler runs, so it shows no status; `http.EnableAccessLog` on the server logs the status too.

## CORS for an API used from a browser

A page on another origin can only call your API when the response allows it. For anything other than a simple GET the browser first sends an `OPTIONS` request, the preflight, and checks the `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers on the answer. Register an `OPTIONS` route that calls `AllowAll` and answers `204` with no body, and call `AllowAll` in the real handler too.

net-http-middleware-cors.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.middleware
import net.router

func preflight(ctx: i64):
    middleware.AllowAll(ctx)
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 204)
    http.Text(ctx, "")
end

func notes(ctx: i64):
    middleware.AllowAll(ctx)
    middleware.NoCache(ctx)
    http.Json(ctx, `[{"id":1,"text":"buy bread"}]`)
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Options(r, "/api/notes", preflight)
    router.Get(r, "/api/notes", notes)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19765)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    url := "http://127.0.0.1:19765/api/notes"
    mut asked := http.NewHeaders()
    asked.insert("Origin", "https://app.example.com")
    asked.insert("Access-Control-Request-Method", "GET")
    p := http.OptionsWith(url, asked)
    println "preflight:", http.Status(p)
    each name in ["access-control-allow-origin", "access-control-allow-methods", "access-control-allow-headers"]:
        println "  " + name + ": " + http.GetHeader(p, name)
    end
    g := http.GetWith(url, asked)
    println "get:", http.Status(g), http.Body(g)
    println "  cache-control: " + http.GetHeader(g, "cache-control")
    println "  pragma: " + http.GetHeader(g, "pragma")
end
```

Output:

```text
preflight: 204
  access-control-allow-origin: *
  access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS
  access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type, Authorization
get: 200 [{"id":1,"text":"buy bread"}]
  cache-control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
  pragma: no-cache
```

`AllowAll` allows every origin, the methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS (not PATCH) and the `Content-Type` and `Authorization` headers. That suits a public, read only API. An API that uses cookies or other headers needs its own rule, as the last section shows.

## One helper per kind of response

Instead of repeating the same calls at the top of every handler, group them in a function for each kind of response: private pages that must not be cached and must not appear in a frame, and public files that browsers may keep. `Secure` adds `nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and the XSS header; `NoCache` forbids caching; `Cache` allows it for the given number of seconds.

net-http-middleware-chain.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.middleware
import net.router

func page(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Secure(ctx)
    middleware.NoCache(ctx)
end

func asset(ctx: i64, seconds: int):
    middleware.Cache(ctx, seconds)
end

func account(ctx: i64):
    page(ctx)
    http.Html(ctx, "<h1>Your account</h1>")
end

func logo(ctx: i64):
    asset(ctx, 86400)
    http.Text(ctx, "logo bytes")
end

func news(ctx: i64):
    asset(ctx, 60)
    http.Json(ctx, `["release 0.5.5"]`)
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/account", account)
    router.Get(r, "/logo.svg", logo)
    router.Get(r, "/news.json", news)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19766)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19766"
    each path in ["/account", "/logo.svg", "/news.json"]:
        res := http.Get(base + path)
        println path + " cache-control=" + http.GetHeader(res, "cache-control") + " frame=" + http.GetHeader(res, "x-frame-options")
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
/account cache-control=no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate frame=DENY
/logo.svg cache-control=max-age=86400 frame=
/news.json cache-control=max-age=60 frame=
```

`Log` prints one line per request with the method and path, which helps while developing. In production, `http.EnableAccessLog` on the server logs every request with its status, without a call in each handler.

## Stricter headers for pages with private data

For an invoice or an account page, build on `Secure` with the headers it leaves out: a `Content-Security-Policy` that only lets the page load files from its own origin, `Strict-Transport-Security` so browsers keep to HTTPS (send it only when the site is served over HTTPS), and a `Referrer-Policy`. The second route shows the "last call wins" rule: it calls `NoCache` and then `Cache`, and the answer carries a single `Cache-Control` with the later value.

net-http-middleware-strict.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.middleware
import net.router

func strict(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Secure(ctx)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'self'")
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=31536000")
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Referrer-Policy", "same-origin")
end

func invoice(ctx: i64):
    strict(ctx)
    middleware.NoCache(ctx)
    http.Html(ctx, "<h1>Invoice 1042</h1>")
end

func report(ctx: i64):
    middleware.NoCache(ctx)
    middleware.Cache(ctx, 300)
    http.Text(ctx, "monthly report")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/invoice", invoice)
    router.Get(r, "/report", report)
    mut s := http.NewServer(18641)
    http.SetHost(s, "127.0.0.1")
    http.Use(s, r)
    if not http.RunBackground(s):
        println "port 18641 is busy"
        ret 1
    end
    a := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:18641/invoice")
    each name in ["x-frame-options", "content-security-policy", "strict-transport-security", "referrer-policy"]:
        println name + ": " + http.GetHeader(a, name)
    end
    b := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:18641/report")
    println "cache-control lines on /report:", http.HeaderValues(b, "cache-control")
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: default-src 'self'
strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000
referrer-policy: same-origin
cache-control lines on /report: ["max-age=300"]
```

A policy of `default-src 'self'` also blocks inline `<script>` and `style` attributes, so test your pages with it before you turn it on.

## Writing your own middleware

When the ready made headers are not right, write a function of the same shape. A function that only adds headers returns nothing. A function that may stop the request returns a `bool`: it writes the error response itself and returns `false`, and the handler returns at once. This example allows a single trusted origin and accepts only JSON bodies.

net-http-middleware-own.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.middleware
import net.router

func cors_for(ctx: i64, origin: str):
    if http.Header(ctx, "Origin") == origin:
        http.SetHeader(ctx, "Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
        http.SetHeader(ctx, "Vary", "Origin")
    end
end

func needs_json(ctx: i64): bool:
    if http.Header(ctx, "Content-Type").starts_with("application/json"):
        ret true
    end
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 415)
    http.Json(ctx, `{"error":"send JSON"}`)
    ret false
end

func create(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Secure(ctx)
    cors_for(ctx, "https://shop.example.com")
    if not needs_json(ctx): ret end
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 201)
    http.Json(ctx, http.Body(ctx))
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/orders", create)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19767)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    url := "http://127.0.0.1:19767/orders"
    mut good := http.NewHeaders()
    good.insert("Origin", "https://shop.example.com")
    good.insert("Content-Type", "application/json")
    a := http.PostWith(url, `{"item":"tea"}`, good)
    println http.Status(a), http.Body(a), "[" + http.GetHeader(a, "access-control-allow-origin") + "]"
    mut other := http.NewHeaders()
    other.insert("Origin", "https://evil.example")
    other.insert("Content-Type", "text/plain")
    b := http.PostWith(url, "item=tea", other)
    println http.Status(b), http.Body(b), "[" + http.GetHeader(b, "access-control-allow-origin") + "]"
end
```

Output:

```text
201 {"item":"tea"} [https://shop.example.com]
415 {"error":"send JSON"} []
```

Send `Vary: Origin` whenever the answer depends on the `Origin` header, so that a shared cache does not hand one origin's answer to another.

## Which function for which job

| Job | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Let pages on any origin call the API | `AllowAll` |
| Basic protection for HTML pages | `Secure` |
| Pages with private data | `NoCache` |
| Images, styles and scripts that rarely change | `Cache` with a number of seconds |
| See requests while developing | `Log` |

## Functions

### `Log`

```salam
func Log(ctx: i64)
```

Prints `[HTTP]`, the method and the path of the request to the standard output; no status, since it runs before the handler answers.

net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.middleware
import net.router

func home(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Log(ctx)
    middleware.AllowAll(ctx)
    middleware.Secure(ctx)
    middleware.NoCache(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "hello")
end

func logo(ctx: i64):
    middleware.Cache(ctx, 3600)
    http.Text(ctx, "png")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", home)
    router.Get(r, "/logo.png", logo)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19624)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    a := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19624/")
    each name in ["access-control-allow-origin", "x-content-type-options", "x-frame-options", "cache-control"]:
        println name + ": " + http.GetHeader(a, name)
    end
    println http.GetHeader(http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19624/logo.png"), "cache-control")
end
```

Output:

```text
[HTTP] GET /
access-control-allow-origin: *
x-content-type-options: nosniff
x-frame-options: DENY
cache-control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
max-age=3600
```

### `AllowAll`

```salam
func AllowAll(ctx: i64)
```

Opens CORS to every origin: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, the methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS, and the headers `Content-Type` and `Authorization`. PATCH is not included.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

### `Secure`

```salam
func Secure(ctx: i64)
```

Sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`. No CSP or HSTS.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

### `NoCache`

```salam
func NoCache(ctx: i64)
```

Tells the browser and any proxies not to keep the response: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` and `Pragma: no-cache`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

### `Cache`

```salam
func Cache(ctx: i64, seconds: int)
```

Sets `Cache-Control: max-age=` with this many seconds, replacing an earlier `Cache-Control`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-middleware-Headers.salam

# net/http/validate

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-validate/

Checking form input and answering with a 400.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add net.http.validate`

Five small checks for input that arrives at a net/http handler: `Required`, `Length`, `IsEmail`, `Matches` and `Assert`. The first four take a string and return true or false, so they work anywhere, not only in handlers. `Assert` is the one that answers: when its condition is false it sends a 400 with a JSON message. For patterns beyond `Matches`, such as finding or replacing, use regex directly; for typed JSON bodies, decode with encoding/json and check the fields after.

What the checks really test:

- `Required` only rejects the empty string. A value of spaces passes; trim it with `str.Trim` first.

- `IsEmail` only looks for an `@` and a dot anywhere, so `@.` passes. It catches typing slips, nothing more.

- `Matches` searches, it does not match the whole value: anchor the pattern with `^` and `$`. A pattern that does not compile returns false for every value, which looks like bad input, so test your patterns.

- `Assert` does not stop the handler, and it pastes the message into the JSON without escaping. Return right after a failed `Assert`, and keep user input out of its message.

## Common rules

Each function answers one question about one string. `Matches` takes a regular expression; anchor it with `^` and `$`, or it accepts any text that merely contains a match. `Length` counts characters, not bytes, so a Persian name of four letters has length 4 although it takes eight bytes.

net-http-validate-rules.salam

```salam
import net.http.validate
import str

func check(label: str, ok: bool):
    println label + ": " + (ok ? "ok" : "rejected")
end

func main:
    check("empty name", validate.Required(""))
    check("name of spaces", validate.Required("   "))
    check("trimmed spaces", validate.Required(str.Trim("   ")))
    check("username 'ali_75'", validate.Matches("ali_75", "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,15}$"))
    check("username '7up'", validate.Matches("7up", "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,15}$"))
    check("postal code 1234567890", validate.Matches("1234567890", "^[0-9]{10}$"))
    check("color #1e90ff", validate.Matches("#1e90ff", "^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$"))
    check("password of 6", validate.Length("abc123", 8, 64))
    check("Persian name of 4 letters", validate.Length("مریم", 2, 4))
    println "bytes in the name:", "مریم".len()
    check("email a@b.ir", validate.IsEmail("a@b.ir"))
    check("email @.", validate.IsEmail("@."))
end
```

Output:

```text
empty name: rejected
name of spaces: ok
trimmed spaces: rejected
username 'ali_75': ok
username '7up': rejected
postal code 1234567890: ok
color #1e90ff: ok
password of 6: rejected
Persian name of 4 letters: ok
bytes in the name: 8
email a@b.ir: ok
email @.: ok
```

Two of the results are worth a second look. `Required` only checks that the text is not empty, so a value of spaces passes; trim it first with `str.Trim`. `IsEmail` only checks for an `@` and a dot, so it catches typing mistakes, not fake addresses. The only real proof that an address works is a confirmation email.

## Report every problem at once

A form with several fields should tell the user about all the mistakes in one answer, not one per try. Run every check, collect the messages, and send them together with a `422`. Building the JSON with `json.Str` and `json.Array` escapes the messages correctly.

net-http-validate-signup.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.validate
import net.router
import encoding.json
import str

func signup(ctx: i64):
    name := str.Trim(http.Form(ctx, "name"))
    email := str.Trim(http.Form(ctx, "email"))
    password := http.Form(ctx, "password")
    mut problems := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    if not validate.Required(name): problems.push(json.Str("name is required")) end
    if not validate.IsEmail(email): problems.push(json.Str("email is not valid")) end
    if not validate.Length(password, 8, 64): problems.push(json.Str("password needs 8 to 64 characters")) end
    if problems.len() > 0:
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 422)
        http.Json(ctx, "{" + json.MemberRaw("errors", json.Array(problems)) + "}")
        ret
    end
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 201)
    http.Json(ctx, "{" + json.Member("welcome", name) + "}")
end

func send(form: str):
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    res := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19768/signup", form, headers)
    println http.Status(res), http.Body(res)
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/signup", signup)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19768)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    send("name=+&email=ali&password=123")
    send("name=Ali&email=ali%40example.com&password=123")
    send("name=Ali&email=ali%40example.com&password=long+enough")
end
```

Output:

```text
422 {"errors": ["name is required", "email is not valid", "password needs 8 to 64 characters"]}
422 {"errors": ["password needs 8 to 64 characters"]}
201 {"welcome": "Ali"}
```

## Stop at the first problem with Assert

For a simple API, `Assert` is shorter: when the condition is false it answers `400` with `{"error": message}`. It does not stop the handler, so keep the result in a variable and return when it is false. Otherwise the code after it runs and its response replaces the error.

net-http-validate-assert.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.validate
import net.router

func transfer(ctx: i64):
    amount := http.Query(ctx, "amount")
    account := http.Query(ctx, "to")
    ok_amount := validate.Matches(amount, "^[1-9][0-9]{0,6}$")
    validate.Assert(ctx, ok_amount, "amount must be a whole number from 1 to 9999999")
    if not ok_amount: ret end
    ok_account := validate.Matches(account, "^IR[0-9]{24}$")
    validate.Assert(ctx, ok_account, "to must be an IBAN such as IR followed by 24 digits")
    if not ok_account: ret end
    http.Json(ctx, `{"sent":` + amount + `,"to":"` + account + `"}`)
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/transfer", transfer)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19769)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19769/transfer"
    each query in ["?amount=0&to=IR1", "?amount=500&to=IR1", "?amount=500&to=IR123456789012345678901234"]:
        res := http.Get(base + query)
        println http.Status(res), http.Body(res)
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
400 {"error":"amount must be a whole number from 1 to 9999999"}
400 {"error":"to must be an IBAN such as IR followed by 24 digits"}
200 {"sent":500,"to":"IR123456789012345678901234"}
```

`Assert` puts the message into the JSON as it is, so write it without double quotes or backslashes. For messages that include user input, build the answer with `json.Member` as in the previous section.

## Which function for which job

| Job | Function |
| --- | --- |
| The field must be filled in | `Required` after `str.Trim` |
| A minimum and maximum number of characters | `Length` |
| Something that looks like an email address | `IsEmail` |
| A fixed shape: digits, a code, a phone number | `Matches` with an anchored pattern |
| Answer 400 when a check fails | `Assert`, then return |

## Functions

### `Required`

```salam
func Required(value: str): bool
```

True when the value is not the empty string; spaces count as a value.

net-http-validate-Check.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.validate
import net.router

func signup(ctx: i64):
    email := http.Form(ctx, "email")
    validate.Assert(ctx, validate.IsEmail(email), "invalid email")
    if validate.IsEmail(email):
        http.Text(ctx, "welcome")
    end
end

func main:
    println validate.Required(""), validate.Required("  "), validate.Required("Ali")
    println validate.Length("hello", 2, 5), validate.Length("hello world", 2, 5)
    println validate.IsEmail("ali@example.com"), validate.IsEmail("ali@")
    println validate.Matches("09121234567", "^09[0-9]{9}$"), validate.Matches("12345", "^09[0-9]{9}$")
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/signup", signup)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19625)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    bad := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19625/signup", "email=x", headers)
    println http.Status(bad), http.Body(bad)
    good := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19625/signup", "email=a%40b.ir", headers)
    println http.Status(good), http.Body(good)
end
```

Output:

```text
false true true
true false
true false
true false
400 {"error":"invalid email"}
200 welcome
```

### `Length`

```salam
func Length(value: str, min_len: int, max_len: int): bool
```

True when the number of characters (not bytes) is between the minimum and the maximum, both included.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-validate-Check.salam

### `IsEmail`

```salam
func IsEmail(value: str): bool
```

A very simple email check: the text has to hold an `@` and a dot, in any place. To be sure, send a confirmation email.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-validate-Check.salam

### `Matches`

```salam
func Matches(value: str, pattern: str): bool
```

True when the regular expression matches somewhere in the value; anchor it with `^` and `$` to test the whole value. False when the pattern does not compile.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-validate-Check.salam

### `Assert`

```salam
func Assert(ctx: i64, ok: bool, message: str)
```

When the condition is false, sets status 400 and the body `{"error":"message"}`, with the message not escaped. It does not stop the handler.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http-validate-Check.salam
