# net/http/session

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-session/

User sessions over a cookie: keeping data between requests, and a CSRF token.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add net.http.session`

A session keeps each visitor's data on the server and gives the browser nothing but a random id in an `HttpOnly` cookie. Use it for logins, carts and form tokens on a site built with net/http. When the client is not a browser, or several servers must accept the same login without sharing memory, a signed token from jwt is usually the better fit.

The flow in a handler: `Start` finds the visitor's session from the cookie or makes a new one (and sets the cookie), you read and change values with `Value` and `SetValue`, and `Save` writes the session back. Values are strings. A session expires after `max_age` seconds without a request; every request that finds it starts the clock again.

Things people get wrong:

- Forgetting `Save`. `Start` returns a copy; changes reach the store only when you save it.

- Keeping request strings. `Param`, `Form` and the like are freed when the handler returns, so copy them with `str.Clone` before you store them (see the cart).

- Not calling `Regenerate` after login, which leaves an id an attacker may have planted in the browser valid.

- Expecting the sessions to survive. They live in this process's memory: a restart logs everyone out and two server processes do not share them. Two requests from one visitor at the same moment each save their own copy, and the later `Save` wins.

## Log in and log out

The usual shape: the login handler checks the password, calls `Regenerate` so the user gets a fresh id, stores who they are with `SetValue` and redirects. Every protected page calls `Start` and checks `HasValue`. Logging out calls `End`, which deletes the session on the server and clears the cookie.

net-http-session-login.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.session
import net.router

func login(ctx: i64):
    if http.Form(ctx, "user") != "sara" or http.Form(ctx, "password") != "open sesame":
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 401)
        http.Text(ctx, "wrong user or password")
        ret
    end
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    session.Regenerate(ctx, s)
    session.SetValue(s, "user", "sara")
    session.Save(s)
    http.Redirect(ctx, "/me")
end

func me(ctx: i64):
    s := session.Start(ctx)
    if not session.HasValue(s, "user"):
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 401)
        http.Text(ctx, "please log in")
        ret
    end
    http.Text(ctx, "hello " + session.Value(s, "user"))
end

func logout(ctx: i64):
    session.End(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "logged out")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/login", login)
    router.Get(r, "/me", me)
    router.Post(r, "/logout", logout)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19770)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19770"
    mut browser := http.NewClient()
    browser.SetHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    println http.Body(browser.Get(base + "/me"))
    bad := browser.Post(base + "/login", "user=sara&password=guess")
    println http.Status(bad), http.Body(bad)
    ok := browser.Post(base + "/login", "user=sara&password=open+sesame")
    println http.Status(ok), http.GetHeader(ok, "location")
    println http.Body(browser.Get(base + "/me"))
    println http.Body(browser.Post(base + "/logout", ""))
    println http.Body(browser.Get(base + "/me"))
end
```

Output:

```text
please log in
401 wrong user or password
302 /me
hello sara
logged out
please log in
```

`http.NewClient` keeps cookies between requests the way a browser does, which is why the second `/me` sees the login. A plain `http.Get` sends no cookies and always looks like a new visitor.

## Protect forms with a CSRF token

The browser sends the session cookie with every request to your site, even one started by a form on another site. A CSRF token stops that: `CSRFToken` stores a random token in the session, you put it in a hidden field, and the handler that receives the form checks it with `CSRFVerify`. A forged form does not know the token and is refused.

net-http-session-csrf.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.session
import net.router

func form(ctx: i64):
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    token := session.CSRFToken(s)
    session.Save(s)
    http.Html(ctx, `<form method="post" action="/email"><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="` + token + `"><input name="email"></form>`)
end

func change_email(ctx: i64):
    s := session.Start(ctx)
    if not session.CSRFVerify(s, http.Form(ctx, "csrf")):
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 403)
        http.Text(ctx, "the form has expired, reload the page")
        ret
    end
    http.Text(ctx, "email changed to " + http.Form(ctx, "email"))
end

func token_in(html: str): str:
    start := html.find(`value="`) + 7
    rest := html.substr(start, html.len() - start)
    ret rest.substr(0, rest.find(`"`))
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/email", form)
    router.Post(r, "/email", change_email)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19771)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)
    url := "http://127.0.0.1:19771/email"
    mut browser := http.NewClient()
    browser.SetHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    token := token_in(http.Body(browser.Get(url)))
    println "token length:", token.len()
    forged := browser.Post(url, "email=evil%40example.com")
    println http.Status(forged), http.Body(forged)
    real := browser.Post(url, "csrf=" + token + "&email=sara%40example.com")
    println http.Status(real), http.Body(real)
end
```

Output:

```text
token length: 48
403 the form has expired, reload the page
200 email changed to sara@example.com
```

Call `Save` after `CSRFToken`, because the first call creates the token in your copy of the session.

## Keep data across requests: a shopping cart

Values are strings, so numbers go through `conv.Atoi` and back. Each visitor has a separate session, so two clients filling carts at the same time never see each other's items. `ClearValues` empties a session but keeps the user's id.

net-http-session-cart.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.session
import net.router
import conv
import str

func add(ctx: i64):
    item := str.Clone(http.Param(ctx, "item"))
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    mut count := 0
    if session.HasValue(s, item):
        count = conv.Atoi(session.Value(s, item))
    end
    session.SetValue(s, item, "" + (count + 1))
    session.Save(s)
    http.Text(ctx, "added " + item)
end

func cart(ctx: i64):
    s := session.Start(ctx)
    mut text := ""
    each item in ["tea", "bread", "cheese"]:
        if session.HasValue(s, item):
            text = text + (text == "" ? "" : ", ") + item + " x" + session.Value(s, item)
        end
    end
    http.Text(ctx, text == "" ? "the cart is empty" : text)
end

func empty(ctx: i64):
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    session.ClearValues(s)
    session.Save(s)
    http.Text(ctx, "emptied")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/cart/:item", add)
    router.Get(r, "/cart", cart)
    router.Delete(r, "/cart", empty)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19772)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19772/cart"
    mut sara := http.NewClient()
    mut reza := http.NewClient()
    _ := sara.Post(base + "/tea", "")
    _ := sara.Post(base + "/tea", "")
    _ := sara.Post(base + "/bread", "")
    _ := reza.Post(base + "/cheese", "")
    println "sara:", http.Body(sara.Get(base))
    println "reza:", http.Body(reza.Get(base))
    println http.Body(sara.Delete(base))
    println "sara:", http.Body(sara.Get(base))
    println "reza:", http.Body(reza.Get(base))
end
```

Output:

```text
sara: tea x2, bread x1
reza: cheese x1
emptied
sara: the cart is empty
reza: cheese x1
```

Note the `str.Clone` around `Param`. Values read from the request are freed when the handler returns, and a session outlives the request, so copy anything from the request before you use it as a key or value. Without the copy the cart keys point at freed memory and the cart looks empty.

## Cookie settings and lifetime

`Configure` sets the cookie name, how long a session lives without activity, whether the cookie is sent over HTTPS only, and its `SameSite` mode. Call it once, before the server starts. On a site served over HTTPS, pass `true` for `secure`; `Strict` keeps the cookie off every request that starts on another site, and `Lax`, the default, still sends it when the user follows a link.

net-http-session-config.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.session
import net.router
import str

func hello(ctx: i64):
    s := session.Start(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "session " + (s.id.len() > 0))
end

func main:
    session.Configure("shop_sid", 1800, true, "Strict")
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", hello)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19773)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)
    res := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19773/")
    println http.Body(res)
    line := http.SetCookieLines(res).get(0)
    each part in str.Split(line, "; "):
        if part.starts_with("shop_sid="):
            println "shop_sid=<random id>"
        else not part.starts_with("Expires="):
            println part
        end
    end
    mut s := session.New()
    session.SetValue(s, "theme", "dark")
    session.Save(s)
    println "kept for", s.max_age, "seconds"
    println "removed now:", session.CleanupExpired()
    session.Destroy(s.id)
    mut found := true
    _ := session.Get(s.id, found)
    println "after Destroy:", found
end
```

Output:

```text
session true
shop_sid=<random id>
Path=/
Max-Age=1800
SameSite=Strict
Secure
HttpOnly
kept for 1800 seconds
removed now: 0
after Destroy: false
```

The cookie is always `HttpOnly`, so scripts in the page cannot read the id. Expired sessions are removed every hundred calls to `New` or `Get`; `CleanupExpired` does it at once and returns how many it removed. Sessions live in the memory of one process, so a restart logs everyone out, and two copies of the server behind a load balancer do not share them. For that, keep the data in a database such as db/redis.

## Types

### `SessionData`

```salam
struct SessionData
```

The keys and values of the session.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `HashMap` | The values. |

net-http-session-Session.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.session
import net.router
import conv

func visit(ctx: i64):
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    mut count := 1
    if session.HasValue(s, "visits"):
        count = conv.Atoi(session.Value(s, "visits")) + 1
    end
    session.SetValue(s, "visits", "" + count)
    session.Save(s)
    http.Text(ctx, "visit " + count)
end

func login(ctx: i64):
    mut s := session.Start(ctx)
    session.Regenerate(ctx, s)
    session.SetValue(s, "user", "ali")
    token := session.CSRFToken(s)
    session.Save(s)
    http.Text(ctx, "" + session.CSRFVerify(s, token) + " " + session.CSRFVerify(s, "x"))
end

func logout(ctx: i64):
    session.End(ctx)
    http.Text(ctx, "goodbye")
end

func main:
    session.Configure("sid", 3600, false, "Lax")
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/", visit)
    router.Post(r, "/login", login)
    router.Post(r, "/logout", logout)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19626)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)
    mut c := http.NewClient()
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19626"
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    println http.Body(c.Post(base + "/login", ""))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    println http.Body(c.Post(base + "/logout", ""))
    println http.Body(c.Get(base + "/"))
    mut s := session.New()
    session.SetValue(s, "a", "1")
    session.SetValue(s, "b", "2")
    println session.DeleteValue(s, "a"), s.data.items.size()
    session.Save(s)
    mut found := false
    back := session.Get(s.id, found)
    println found, session.Value(back, "b"), back.max_age, s.id.len() > 0
    session.ClearValues(s)
    session.Destroy(s.id)
    _ := session.Get(s.id, found)
    println found, session.CleanupExpired() >= 0
    println session.DefaultCookieName, session.DefaultMaxAge
end
```

Output:

```text
visit 1
visit 2
true false
visit 3
goodbye
visit 1
true 1
true 2 3600 true
false true
salam_sid 86400
```

# net/http/swagger

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http-swagger/

Writing OpenAPI documentation for an API and serving the documentation page.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add net.http.swagger`

This package writes the documentation of an HTTP API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document and serves it with a viewer page where people can read each operation and try it. Use it with an API built on net/http and net/router: client generators, API gateways and your own front-end team read the same `openapi.json`. The viewer is built into the package, so it works offline and loads nothing from a CDN.

How it fits together:

- A `Doc` holds the whole document. `Route` adds an operation (or `At` picks one that exists), and the calls after it, such as `Summary`, `Query` and `Returns`, describe that operation.

- Body and response schemas come from a sample value: pass an empty struct and its fields, under their `@json` names, become a schema under `components`.

- `Mount` adds the viewer and the spec to your router; `Problems`, `Missing` and `Undocumented` check the document in a test.

Things that catch people out:

- `Mount` copies the spec when you call it, and adds routes to the router. Describe every route first, then `Mount`, then `http.Use`; a description added after `Mount` never reaches the page.

- After an `At` that finds nothing, the following calls do nothing. Check what `At` returns, or use `Route`, which creates the operation.

- The docs are public. Anyone who can reach the server can read `/docs`, and the spec is served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Leave `Mount` out of a production build if the API is private.

## Document an API next to its routes

The simplest habit is to describe each route right after you register it, so the two never drift apart. `Route` starts an operation, and the calls after it fill it in. `Returns` takes a sample value: pass a struct, or an array of one struct for a list, and the schema appears under `components`. `Mount` then serves the spec at `/docs/openapi.json` and the viewer at `/docs`.

net-http-swagger-api.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.swagger
import net.router
import encoding.json

struct Task:
    @json "id"
    pub id: int = 0
    @json "title"
    pub title: str = ""
    @json "done"
    pub done: bool = false
end

func list(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, `[{"id":1,"title":"write docs","done":false}]`)
end

func create(ctx: i64):
    http.SetStatus(ctx, 201)
    http.Json(ctx, http.Body(ctx))
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    mut doc := swagger.New("tasks", "1.0.0")
    router.Get(r, "/tasks", list)
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "GET", "/tasks")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "all tasks")
    swagger.Tag(doc, "tasks")
    swagger.Returns(doc, 200, "the tasks", [Task {}])
    router.Post(r, "/tasks", create)
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "POST", "/tasks")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "add a task")
    swagger.Tag(doc, "tasks")
    swagger.Accepts(doc, "the new task", Task {})
    swagger.Returns(doc, 201, "the task as stored", Task {})
    println "missing:", swagger.Missing(doc, r)
    swagger.Mount(doc, r, "/docs")
    mut s := http.NewServer(19774)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    spec := http.Body(http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19774/docs/openapi.json"))
    println json.Keys(json.Get(spec, "paths"))
    println json.GetPath(spec, "paths./tasks.post.summary")
    println json.GetPath(spec, "paths./tasks.get.responses.200.description")
    println json.GetPath(spec, "paths./tasks.get.responses.200.content")
    println json.Keys(json.GetPath(spec, "components.schemas.Task.properties"))
    println http.Status(http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19774/docs"))
    swagger.Free(doc)
end
```

Output:

```text
missing: []
["/tasks"]
add a task
the tasks
{"application/json":{"schema":{"type":"array","items":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Task"}}}}
["id", "title", "done"]
200
```

`Mount` takes a copy of the spec when you call it, so document every route first and mount last. Path patterns are written the router's way, `/books/:id`, and appear in OpenAPI's form, `/books/{id}`.

## Security schemes and saving the spec

Declare each way to sign in once, with `BearerAuth` for tokens in the `Authorization` header or `ApiKeyAuth` for a key in a header, query value or cookie. Then mark each operation that needs it with `Secure` and the scheme's name. `WriteSpec` saves the spec to a file, for a client generator or for publishing with the site, and `SpecFromFile` reads one back.

net-http-swagger-auth.salam

```salam
import net.http.swagger
import encoding.json

struct Invoice:
    @json "number"
    pub number: str = ""
    @json "total"
    pub total: f64 = 0.0
end

func main:
    mut doc := swagger.New("billing", "1.4.0")
    swagger.Server(doc, "https://billing.example.com", "production")
    swagger.BearerAuth(doc, "user", "JWT")
    swagger.ApiKeyAuth(doc, "partner", "header", "X-Partner-Key")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "GET", "/invoices/:number")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "one invoice")
    swagger.Secure(doc, "user")
    swagger.Returns(doc, 200, "the invoice", Invoice {})
    swagger.ReturnsNothing(doc, 401, "no valid token")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "POST", "/partner/invoices")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "a partner sends an invoice")
    swagger.Secure(doc, "partner")
    swagger.Accepts(doc, "the invoice", Invoice {})
    swagger.ReturnsNothing(doc, 202, "accepted")
    println "problems:", swagger.Problems(doc).len()
    println swagger.WriteSpec(doc, "openapi.json")
    spec := swagger.SpecFromFile("openapi.json")
    println json.Minify(json.GetPath(spec, "components.securitySchemes.user"))
    println json.Minify(json.GetPath(spec, "components.securitySchemes.partner"))
    println json.Minify(json.GetPath(spec, "paths./invoices/{number}.get.security"))
    println json.GetPath(spec, "components.schemas.Invoice.properties.total.type")
    swagger.Free(doc)
end
```

Output:

```text
problems: 0
true
{"type":"http","scheme":"bearer","bearerFormat":"JWT"}
{"type":"apiKey","in":"header","name":"X-Partner-Key"}
[{"user":[]}]
number
```

## Check the documentation in CI

Documentation goes stale quietly. `Problems` finds mistakes in the spec itself: a security scheme that was never declared, a path parameter that does not match the path, a status code outside 100 to 599, a body on a GET, or a repeated operation id. `Missing` compares the spec with the router and lists the routes that have no operation. Print both in a test and fail the build when either is not empty.

net-http-swagger-check.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.swagger
import net.router

func any(ctx: i64):
    http.Text(ctx, "")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/users/:id", any)
    router.Delete(r, "/users/:id", any)
    router.Get(r, "/reports", any)
    mut doc := swagger.New("users", "2.0.0")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "GET", "/users/:id")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "one user")
    swagger.Secure(doc, "token")
    swagger.ReturnsText(doc, 200, "the user")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "DELETE", "/users/:id")
    swagger.PathParam(doc, "id", "the user id")
    swagger.ReturnsNothing(doc, 2040, "deleted")
    mut failed := 0
    each p in swagger.Problems(doc):
        println "problem:", p
        failed += 1
    end
    each m in swagger.Missing(doc, r):
        println "not documented:", m
        failed += 1
    end
    println failed, "issue(s)", failed > 0 ? "so the build fails" : "so the build passes"
    swagger.Free(doc)
end
```

Output:

```text
problem: GET /users/:id: needs security scheme 'token', which no BearerAuth or ApiKeyAuth declared
problem: DELETE /users/:id: 2040 is not an HTTP status code
not documented: GET /reports
3 issue(s) so the build fails
```

In a real check, return `1` from `main` when the count is above zero, so the CI job fails. `Undocumented` is a softer check: it lists operations that exist but have neither a summary, a description nor a response.

## Serve the docs with the API

For an existing router, `Scan` adds an empty operation for every route, so nothing is forgotten. `At` then picks one of them to describe. `AcceptsRaw` and `ReturnsRaw` take a content type and a JSON Schema as text, for bodies that are not a struct.

net-http-swagger-serve.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.swagger
import net.router

func ping(ctx: i64):
    http.Text(ctx, "pong")
end

func echo(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, http.Body(ctx))
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/ping", ping)
    router.Post(r, "/echo", echo)
    mut doc := swagger.New("echo service", "0.1.0")
    swagger.Describe(doc, "Answers pings and echoes JSON back.")
    swagger.Server(doc, "http://localhost:8080", "this machine")
    swagger.Scan(doc, r)
    _ := swagger.At(doc, "GET", "/ping")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "is the service up")
    swagger.ReturnsText(doc, 200, "always pong")
    _ := swagger.At(doc, "POST", "/echo")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "send JSON, get the same JSON back")
    swagger.AcceptsRaw(doc, "any JSON value", swagger.JSON_TYPE, "{}", true)
    swagger.ReturnsRaw(doc, 200, "the same value", swagger.JSON_TYPE, "{}")
    swagger.Mount(doc, r, "/docs")
    mut s := http.NewServer(8080)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println "docs at http://localhost:8080/docs"
    http.Run(s)
end
```

Start it with `salam run` and open `http://localhost:8080/docs` in a browser: the page lists both operations, and the Try it box under each one sends real requests to the running server. If you do not have a router at all, `Serve` runs a small server with only the docs, and `ServeSpec` does the same for a spec written by hand.

## Types

### `Param`

```salam
struct Param
```

One parameter.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `loc` | `str = "query"` | Where it sits: query, header, cookie or path. |
| `required` | `bool = false` | It is required. |
| `description` | `str = ""` | The description. |
| `schema` | `str = "{"type":"string"}"` | The schema. |

net-http-swagger-Build.salam

```salam
import net.http.swagger
import encoding.json

struct Book:
    @json "id"
    pub id: int = 0
    @json "title"
    pub title: str = ""
end

func main:
    mut doc := swagger.New("library", "1.2.0")
    swagger.Describe(doc, "a sample API for books")
    swagger.Server(doc, "https://api.example.com", "the main one")
    swagger.Contact(doc, "the Salam team", "https://salamlang.ir", "team@salamlang.ir")
    swagger.License(doc, "MIT", "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT")
    swagger.BearerAuth(doc, "token", "JWT")
    swagger.ApiKeyAuth(doc, "key", "header", "X-API-Key")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "GET", "/books/:id")
    swagger.Summary(doc, "one book")
    swagger.Details(doc, "Returns the book with this id.")
    swagger.Tag(doc, "books")
    swagger.OperationId(doc, "getBook")
    swagger.PathParam(doc, "id", "the id of the book")
    swagger.Query(doc, "fields", "the fields asked for", false)
    swagger.QueryTyped(doc, "limit", "the greatest number", false, 10)
    mut orders := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    orders.push("title")
    orders.push("id")
    swagger.QueryEnum(doc, "sort", "the order", false, orders)
    swagger.Header(doc, "X-Trace", "the trace id", false)
    swagger.Cookie(doc, "sid", "the session", false)
    swagger.Secure(doc, "token")
    swagger.Returns(doc, 200, "the book", Book {})
    swagger.ReturnsHeader(doc, 200, "ETag", "the version")
    swagger.ReturnsNothing(doc, 404, "not found")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "POST", "/books")
    swagger.Accepts(doc, "the new book", Book {})
    swagger.Returns(doc, 201, "created", Book {})
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "PUT", "/books/:id/cover")
    swagger.AcceptsRaw(doc, "the cover image", "image/png", "{\"type\":\"string\",\"format\":\"binary\"}", true)
    swagger.ReturnsText(doc, 200, "done")
    _ := swagger.Route(doc, "POST", "/books/:id/notes")
    swagger.AcceptsOptional(doc, "the note", Book {})
    swagger.AcceptsForm(doc, "the form", Book {})
    swagger.ReturnsRaw(doc, 200, "the export", "text/csv", "{\"type\":\"string\"}")
    swagger.ReturnsHtml(doc, 200, "the page")
    swagger.ReturnsFile(doc, 200, "the file", "application/pdf")
    swagger.Deprecated(doc)
    println swagger.At(doc, "get", "/books/:id"), swagger.At(doc, "GET", "/nope")
    println doc.ops.len(), doc.ops[0].params.len(), doc.ops[0].replies.len(), doc.ops[3].is_deprecated, doc.schemes.len()
    text := swagger.Spec(doc)
    println json.Valid(text), json.Get(text, "openapi")
    println swagger.SpecIndent(doc).len() > text.len()
    println swagger.Problems(doc).len(), swagger.Undocumented(doc)
    println swagger.WriteSpec(doc, "openapi.json"), swagger.SpecFromFile("openapi.json").len() > 0, swagger.SpecFromFile("missing.json")
    println swagger.TEXT_SCHEMA, swagger.JSON_TYPE
    swagger.Free(doc)
end
```

Output:

```text
true false
4 6 2 true 2
true 3.1.0
true
0 []
true true
{"type":"string"} application/json
```

### `Mount`

```salam

```

Adds the documentation page and `openapi.json` to the router under the given prefix, with the spec as it is at this moment. Call it before `http.Use`.

net-http-swagger-Serve.salam

```salam
import net.http
import net.http.swagger
import net.router
import str

func list(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, "[]")
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Get(r, "/books", list)
    router.Post(r, "/books", list)
    router.Get(r, "/admin/stats", list)
    mut doc := swagger.New("library", "1.0.0")
    println swagger.Missing(doc, r)
    swagger.ScanPrefix(doc, r, "/books")
    println doc.ops.len(), swagger.Missing(doc, r)
    swagger.Scan(doc, r)
    println doc.ops.len(), swagger.Missing(doc, r).len()
    swagger.Mount(doc, r, "/docs")
    mut server := http.NewServer(19627)
    http.Use(server, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(server)
    spec := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19627/docs/openapi.json")
    println http.Status(spec), str.Contains(http.Body(spec), "/admin/stats")
    page := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19627/docs")
    println str.Contains(http.Body(page), "<html")
    mut r2 := router.NewRouter()
    swagger.MountSpec("{\"openapi\":\"3.1.0\"}", "ready made", r2, "/spec")
    println r2.routes.len()
    println swagger.Serve(doc, 19628), http.Status(http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19628/openapi.json"))
    println swagger.ServeSpec("{\"openapi\":\"3.1.0\"}", "another", 19629)
    println str.Contains(swagger.Page("API", "/openapi.json"), "/openapi.json")
end
```

Output:

```text
["GET /books", "POST /books", "GET /admin/stats"]
2 ["GET /admin/stats"]
3 0
200 true
true
3
true 200
true
true
```

# net/http2

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-http2/

The HTTP/2 protocol from the ground up: frames, HPACK header compression and streams.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add net.http2`

This package implements HTTP/2 at the protocol level: it builds and reads frames, compresses the headers with HPACK and carries several requests at once over one connection as "streams". It is not a web server or a ready client. For an ordinary web server or one-off requests use net/http, which speaks HTTP/1.1; reach for this package when you need the protocol itself, for example to talk to a service that only offers HTTP/2, to test a server, or to send many requests over one connection.

How it goes: build a `Transport` over a TCP or TLS socket, take a connection with `NewConn` and do the handshake. Then the client sends a request with `SendHeaders` and reads the answer in `StreamAt` after `AwaitStreamEnd`. Over TLS, the client and the server must have agreed on `h2` through ALPN.

What the package does for you, and what it leaves to you:

- It answers pings, sends window updates for flow control, waits for window space in `SendData`, and refuses server push.

- You write the pseudo-headers yourself: `:method`, `:scheme`, `:authority` and `:path` on a request, `:status` on an answer, before any normal header.

- A stream's body is collected in memory in `s.data` until the stream ends, and finished streams stay in the connection, so open a new connection now and then rather than keeping one for millions of requests.

- A `Conn` belongs to one thread; nothing in it is locked.

## Many requests on one connection

The point of HTTP/2 is that one connection carries many requests at the same time. Each request is a stream with an odd id chosen by the client (1, 3, 5 and so on), and the frames of different streams can be interleaved in both directions. The client below sends three requests before reading anything; the server, in the same program, answers them in reverse order, and each answer still lands on the right stream.

net-http2-multiplex.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import net.tcp
import compress

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func serve():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    mut c := http2.NewConn(http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd), true)
    if not http2.ServerHandshake(c):
        ret
    end
    mut ids := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    until ids.len() < 3:
        ids.push(http2.AwaitAnyHeaders(c, 20))
    end
    mut i := ids.len() - 1
    until i >= 0:
        id := ids.get(i)
        path := http2.HeadersGet(http2.StreamAt(c, id).headers, ":path")
        mut h := http2.HeaderList {}
        http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":status", "200")
        _ := http2.SendHeaders(c, id, h, false)
        _ := http2.SendData(c, id, compress.BufFromStr("page " + path), true)
        i -= 1
    end
    _ := http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, 0, 5)
    http2.CloseConn(c)
end

func request(c &: http2.Conn, path: str): int:
    id := http2.NextStreamId(c)
    mut h := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":method", "GET")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":scheme", "http")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":path", path)
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":authority", "127.0.0.1")
    _ := http2.SendHeaders(c, id, h, true)
    ret id
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(serve)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    mut c := http2.NewConn(http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd), false)
    if not http2.ClientHandshake(c):
        println "handshake failed"
        ret 1
    end
    mut ids := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    each p in ["/a", "/b", "/c"]:
        ids.push(request(c, p))
    end
    println "three requests sent on streams", ids.get(0), ids.get(1), ids.get(2)
    each id in ids:
        _ := http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, id, 50)
        s := http2.StreamAt(c, id)
        println "stream", id, http2.HeadersGet(s.headers, ":status"), compress.BufToStrUnsafe(s.data)
    end
    println "connections used: 1, streams:", http2.StreamCount(c)
    _ := http2.SendGoAway(c, http2.H2_NO_ERROR, "")
    http2.CloseConn(c)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
three requests sent on streams 1 3 5
stream 1 200 page /a
stream 3 200 page /b
stream 5 200 page /c
connections used: 1, streams: 3
```

`AwaitAnyHeaders` on the server reads frames until one arrives for a stream whose headers are complete and returns that stream's id, or `H2_POLL_ERROR` when the connection fails. A request that also has a body sends more frames on the same stream, so a server that accepts bodies should remember which ids it has already seen. `AwaitStreamEnd` on the client reads frames, for any stream, until the one you asked about has ended; the frames of the others are kept in their streams for later. Its last argument is a limit on how many frames to read, so a broken peer cannot keep you waiting forever.

## How much HPACK saves

Requests to one site repeat nearly the same headers every time. HPACK sends a header once, stores it in a table that both sides keep in step, and afterwards sends only its index. The first request below is already smaller than its HTTP/1.1 text because of the static table and the Huffman code; the second and third are about a quarter of the size, because almost everything is now in the dynamic table.

net-http2-hpack-savings.salam

```salam
import net.http2

func request_headers(path: str): http2.HeaderList:
    mut h := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":method", "GET")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":scheme", "https")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":authority", "shop.example.com")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":path", path)
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, "user-agent", "salam-client/1.0")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, "accept", "application/json")
    http2.HeadersAddSensitive(h, "authorization", "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.e30.x")
    ret h
end

func plain_size(h: http2.HeaderList): int:
    mut n := 0
    each item in h.items:
        n += item.name.len() + item.value.len() + 4
    end
    ret n
end

func main:
    mut table := http2.NewDynTable(4096)
    each path in ["/cart", "/cart/items", "/checkout"]:
        h := request_headers(path)
        block := http2.EncodeHeaderList(table, h, true)
        println path, "as HTTP/1.1 text:", plain_size(h), "bytes, HPACK:", block.len, "bytes, table entries:", http2.DynCount(table)
    end
    println "huffman alone, user-agent value:", "salam-client/1.0".len(), "->", http2.HuffmanEncodedLenStr("salam-client/1.0")
end
```

Output:

```text
/cart as HTTP/1.1 text: 180 bytes, HPACK: 76 bytes, table entries: 4
/cart/items as HTTP/1.1 text: 186 bytes, HPACK: 43 bytes, table entries: 5
/checkout as HTTP/1.1 text: 184 bytes, HPACK: 42 bytes, table entries: 6
huffman alone, user-agent value: 16 -> 11
```

The `authorization` header is added with `HeadersAddSensitive`, so it is never put in the table and is sent in full every time. That costs a few bytes but stops an attacker who can influence other headers on the same connection from guessing the token by watching the compressed size, the attack known as CRIME.

## HTTP/2 over TLS to a real server

Servers on the internet offer HTTP/2 only over TLS, and only to clients that ask for it during the TLS handshake. Set `alpn` to `h2` in the tls config, connect with `tls.Dial`, and wrap the connection with `TLSTransport`. If the server did not pick `h2`, `ClientHandshake` fails and you should fall back to HTTP/1.1.

net-http2-tls-get.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import tls

func main:
    host := "www.cloudflare.com"
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig(host)
    cfg.alpn = "h2"
    secure := tls.Dial(host, 443, cfg)
    if not tls.ConnOk(secure):
        println "TLS failed:", tls.ConnError(secure)
        ret 1
    end
    mut c := http2.NewConn(http2.TLSTransport(secure), false)
    if not http2.ClientHandshake(c):
        println "the server did not agree to HTTP/2"
        ret 1
    end
    id := http2.NextStreamId(c)
    mut h := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":method", "HEAD")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":scheme", "https")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":path", "/")
    http2.HeadersAdd(h, ":authority", host)
    _ := http2.SendHeaders(c, id, h, true)
    if http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, id, 100):
        s := http2.StreamAt(c, id)
        println "status:", http2.HeadersGet(s.headers, ":status")
        println "server:", http2.HeadersGet(s.headers, "server")
        println "body bytes:", s.data.len
    end
    http2.CloseConn(c)
    ret 0
end
```

It needs network access, so it is only checked here. Run against Cloudflare, it printed:

```salam
status: 200
server: cloudflare
body bytes: 0
```

The body is empty because the request used `HEAD`. With `GET`, the page arrives in `s.data` as one buffer, after the package has already sent the window updates that flow control needs.

## Types

### `Stream`

```salam
struct Stream
```

One stream: one request and its answer.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int = 0` | The id; odd for the streams a client opens. |
| `state` | `int = 0` | The state, one of the stream state constants. |
| `send_window` | `int = 65535` | The sending window. |
| `recv_window` | `int = 65535` | The receiving window. |
| `headers` | `HeaderList` | The headers received. |
| `trailers` | `HeaderList` | The trailing headers received. |
| `data` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The body received. |
| `got_headers` | `bool = false` | The headers have arrived. |
| `got_trailers` | `bool = false` | The trailing headers have arrived. |
| `end_stream` | `bool = false` | The other side has ended the stream. |
| `reset` | `bool = false` | The stream was closed with a reset frame. |
| `error_code` | `int = 0` | The reset's error code. |
| `live` | `bool = false` | This slot of the table is in use. |

net-http2-Conn.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import net.tcp
import compress

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func answer():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    mut c := http2.NewConn(http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd), true)
    if not http2.ServerHandshake(c):
        ret
    end
    id := http2.AwaitAnyHeaders(c, 20)
    stream := http2.StreamAt(c, id)
    mut headers := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":status", "200")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, "content-type", "text/plain")
    _ := http2.SendHeaders(c, id, headers, false)
    _ := http2.SendData(c, id, compress.BufFromStr("hello " + http2.HeadersGet(stream.headers, ":path")), false)
    mut trailers := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(trailers, "x-done", "1")
    _ := http2.SendTrailers(c, id, trailers)
    _ := http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, 0, 5)
    http2.CloseConn(c)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(answer)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    tx := http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd)
    println tx.ok, tx.kind == http2.H2_TRANSPORT_PLAIN
    mut c := http2.NewConn(tx, false)
    println http2.ClientHandshake(c), http2.ConnOk(c)
    id := http2.NextStreamId(c)
    mut headers := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":method", "GET")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":scheme", "http")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":path", "/books")
    http2.HeadersAdd(headers, ":authority", "127.0.0.1")
    println id, http2.SendHeaders(c, id, headers, true)
    println http2.AwaitStreamEnd(c, id, 20)
    stream := http2.StreamAt(c, id)
    println http2.HeadersGet(stream.headers, ":status"), compress.BufToStrUnsafe(stream.data), stream.got_trailers, http2.HeadersGet(stream.trailers, "x-done"), stream.end_stream
    println http2.StreamCount(c) >= 1, c.remote.max_frame_size
    _ := http2.SendPing(c, compress.BufFromStr("abcdefgh"))
    println http2.Poll(c) >= http2.H2_POLL_CONNECTION
    _ := http2.SendRstStream(c, http2.NextStreamId(c), http2.H2_CANCEL)
    println http2.SendGoAway(c, http2.H2_NO_ERROR, "")
    http2.CloseConn(c)
    join(t)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true true
1 true
true
200 hello /books true 1 true
true 16384
true
true
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One HTTP/2 connection with its tables, settings and streams.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `last_error` | `int = 0` | The last error code. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The connection is healthy. |
| `pending_stream` | `int = 0` | The stream whose headers block is not finished yet by a continuation frame. |
| `pending_block` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The parts of that block that arrived. |
| `pending_end_stream` | `bool = false` | Those headers end the stream. |
| `pending_trailers` | `bool = false` | Those headers are trailing ones. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Conn.salam

### `Frame`

```salam
struct Frame
```

One HTTP/2 frame.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int = 0` | The frame type, one of the frame type constants. |
| `flags` | `int = 0` | The flags. |
| `stream_id` | `int = 0` | The stream id; zero means the whole connection. |
| `payload` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The frame payload. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The frame was read correctly. |

net-http2-Frame.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import compress

func main:
    mut settings := http2.DefaultSettings()
    println settings.header_table_size, settings.initial_window_size, settings.max_frame_size, settings.enable_push
    frame := http2.MakeSettingsFrame(settings)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(frame.kind), frame.stream_id, frame.payload.len
    settings.max_frame_size = 32768
    println http2.ApplySettings(settings, http2.MakeSettingsFrame(http2.DefaultSettings())), settings.max_frame_size
    ack := http2.MakeSettingsAck()
    println http2.FrameHasFlag(ack, http2.H2_FLAG_ACK)
    win := http2.MakeWindowUpdate(3, 1024)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(win.kind), http2.WindowIncrementOf(win)
    rst := http2.MakeRstStream(5, http2.H2_CANCEL)
    println http2.ErrorCodeOf(rst), http2.ErrorName(http2.ErrorCodeOf(rst))
    away := http2.MakeGoAway(7, http2.H2_NO_ERROR, "bye")
    println http2.FrameTypeName(away.kind), http2.ErrorCodeOf(away)
    ping := http2.MakePing(compress.BufFromStr("12345678"), false)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(ping.kind), ping.payload.len
    mut data := http2.NewFrame(http2.H2_DATA, http2.H2_FLAG_END_STREAM, 1)
    compress.BufPushBytes(data.payload, "hello" as void*, 5)
    mut ok := true
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(http2.DataOf(data, ok)), ok
    bytes := http2.FrameEncode(data)
    println bytes.len, compress.BufGet(bytes, 3)
    mut head := http2.NewFrame(http2.H2_HEADERS, http2.H2_FLAG_END_HEADERS, 1)
    compress.BufPush(head.payload, 130)
    println http2.HeaderBlockOf(head, ok).len, ok
    mut one := compress.NewByteBuf()
    http2.PutSetting(one, http2.H2_SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE, 16384)
    println one.len
    http2.FreeFrame(data)
    println http2.H2_DATA, http2.H2_PING, http2.H2_PROTOCOL_ERROR, http2.H2_DEFAULT_FRAME_SIZE, http2.H2_DEFAULT_WINDOW, http2.H2_MAX_FRAME_LIMIT
    println http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_PRIORITY), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_RST_STREAM), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_PUSH_PROMISE)
    println http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_GOAWAY), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_WINDOW_UPDATE), http2.FrameTypeName(http2.H2_CONTINUATION)
    println http2.H2_SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE, http2.H2_SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH, http2.H2_SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS, http2.H2_SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, http2.H2_SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE
    println http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_INTERNAL_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_SETTINGS_TIMEOUT), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_STREAM_CLOSED)
    println http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_FRAME_SIZE_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_REFUSED_STREAM), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_COMPRESSION_ERROR), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_CONNECT_ERROR)
    println http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_INADEQUATE_SECURITY), http2.ErrorName(http2.H2_HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED)
    println http2.H2_STREAM_IDLE, http2.H2_STREAM_OPEN, http2.H2_STREAM_HALF_CLOSED_LOCAL, http2.H2_STREAM_HALF_CLOSED_REMOTE, http2.H2_STREAM_CLOSED_STATE
    println http2.H2_DEFAULT_TABLE_SIZE, http2.H2_POLL_ERROR
end
```

Output:


### `Header`

```salam
struct Header
```

One header.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name; in HTTP/2 always in lower case. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |
| `sensitive` | `bool = false` | It is sensitive and never goes into the HPACK table; for tokens and cookies. |

net-http2-Hpack.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import compress

func main:
    mut list := http2.HeaderList {}
    http2.HeadersAdd(list, ":method", "GET")
    http2.HeadersAdd(list, ":path", "/")
    http2.HeadersAdd(list, "user-agent", "salam")
    http2.HeadersAddSensitive(list, "authorization", "Bearer x")
    println http2.HeadersCount(list), http2.HeadersGet(list, ":path"), http2.HeadersHas(list, "cookie")
    mut sender := http2.NewDynTable(4096)
    mut receiver := http2.NewDynTable(4096)
    block := http2.EncodeHeaderList(sender, list, true)
    println block.len, http2.DynCount(sender), http2.DynSize(sender)
    mut ok := true
    read := http2.DecodeHeaderList(receiver, block, ok)
    println ok, read.items.len(), read.items[2].name, read.items[2].value, read.items[3].sensitive
    block2 := http2.EncodeHeaderList(sender, list, true)
    println block2.len < block.len
    fixed := http2.StaticGet(2)
    println fixed.name, fixed.value, http2.HPACK_STATIC_COUNT, http2.HPACK_ENTRY_OVERHEAD
    dyn := http2.DynGet(receiver, 1)
    println dyn.name
    mut exact := false
    println http2.TableFind(receiver, ":method", "GET", exact), exact
    println http2.TableGet(receiver, 62, ok).name, ok
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    http2.EncodeTableSizeUpdate(b, sender, 256)
    http2.DynSetMaxSize(receiver, 256)
    println b.len, sender.max_size, receiver.max_size
    mut b2 := compress.NewByteBuf()
    http2.EncodeHeader(b2, sender, http2.NewHeader("x-id", "7"), false)
    http2.DynInsert(receiver, http2.NewSensitiveHeader("k", "v"))
    println b2.len, http2.DynCount(receiver)
end
```

Output:

```text
4 / false
17 1 47
true 4 user-agent salam true
true
:method GET 61 32
user-agent
2 true
user-agent true
3 256 256
8 2
```

### `HeaderList`

```salam
struct HeaderList
```

A list of headers, in their order.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The headers. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Hpack.salam

### `DynTable`

```salam
struct DynTable
```

The HPACK dynamic table, which keeps the headers sent or received so that next time only their number is sent. Each side has its own table and the two must stay in step.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The entries. |
| `head` | `int = 0` | The position of the newest entry in the ring. |
| `size` | `int = 0` | The current size in bytes, with the overhead. |
| `max_size` | `int = 4096` | The largest size; older entries are pushed out. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Hpack.salam

### `HufTables`

```salam
struct HufTables
```

The internal tables of the Huffman decoder; they are built once and then used again.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `counts` | `Vector` | The number of codes of each length. |
| `first` | `Vector` | The first code of each length. |
| `syms` | `Vector` | The symbols in code order. |
| `ready` | `bool = false` | The tables are built. |

net-http2-Huffman.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import encoding
import compress

func main:
    b := http2.HuffmanEncodeStr("www.example.com")
    println encoding.HexEncode(compress.BufToStrUnsafe(b))
    println http2.HuffmanEncodedLenStr("www.example.com"), "www.example.com".len()
    mut ok := true
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(http2.HuffmanDecodeBuf(b, ok)), ok
    text := compress.BufFromStr("no-cache")
    println http2.HuffmanEncodedLen(text.data, text.len)
    mut out := compress.NewByteBuf()
    compress.BufPush(out, 0)
    http2.HuffmanEncode(out, text.data, text.len)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(http2.HuffmanDecode(out, 1, out.len - 1, ok)), ok
end
```

Output:

```text
f1e3c2e5f23a6ba0ab90f4ff
12 15
www.example.com true
6
no-cache true
```

```salam
import net.http2
import net.tcp

func main:
    secure := tcp.DialTLS("example.com", 443)
    mut c := http2.NewConn(http2.TLSTransport(secure), false)
    println http2.ClientHandshake(c), c.tx.kind == http2.H2_TRANSPORT_TLS
    http2.CloseConn(c)
end
```


A result of `Poll`: a frame for the whole connection arrived. A positive number is the id of the stream whose frame arrived.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Conn.salam

### `H2_PREFACE`

```salam
const H2_PREFACE: str = "PRI * HTTP/2.0

SM

"
```

The string an HTTP/2 client sends before anything else; 24 bytes.

net-http2-Transport.salam

```salam
import net.http2
import net.tcp
import compress

mut server := tcp.Server {}

func answer():
    conn := tcp.Accept(server)
    mut tx := http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd)
    println "server preface:", http2.ReadPreface(tx)
    frame := http2.ReadFrame(tx, http2.H2_DEFAULT_FRAME_SIZE)
    println "server frame:", frame.ok, http2.FrameTypeName(frame.kind), frame.stream_id, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(frame.payload)
    http2.CloseTransport(tx)
end

func main:
    server = tcp.Bind(0)
    t := spawn(answer)
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", tcp.Port(server))
    mut tx := http2.PlainTransport(conn.fd)
    _ := http2.WritePreface(tx)
    mut data := http2.NewFrame(http2.H2_DATA, 0, 3)
    compress.BufPushBuf(data.payload, compress.BufFromStr("hi"))
    _ := http2.WriteFrame(tx, data)
    join(t)
    http2.CloseTransport(tx)
    tcp.CloseServer(server)
    println http2.H2_PREFACE.len()
end
```

Output:

```text
server preface: true
server frame: true DATA 3 hi
24
```

### The frame flags `H2_FLAG_…`

The flags in the fifth byte of a frame. What each flag means depends on the frame type; that is why `H2_FLAG_END_STREAM` and `H2_FLAG_ACK` are both 1, one for a data or headers frame and the other for settings and ping. Check them with `FrameHasFlag`.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `H2_FLAG_END_STREAM` | `1` |
| `H2_FLAG_ACK` | `1` |
| `H2_FLAG_END_HEADERS` | `4` |
| `H2_FLAG_PADDED` | `8` |
| `H2_FLAG_PRIORITY` | `32` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-http2-Frame.salam

# net/socketio

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/net-socketio/

A Socket.IO client: events, acknowledgements, namespaces and automatic reconnection.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add net.socketio`

Socket.IO is the usual live messaging library in the Node.js world. This package is a client for Socket.IO 3 and 4 servers (Engine.IO protocol 4), over WebSocket or HTTP long polling; it has no server of its own. Use it when the other side already speaks Socket.IO, for example a Node.js chat or dashboard backend. When you control both ends and the client is a browser, a plain net/websocket server is simpler, because Socket.IO adds its own packet format on top of the WebSocket.

The model: `Dial` connects, `On` sets a listener for an event and the `Emit...` functions send events. Nothing is read in the background: listeners run only while the program processes messages with `Run`, `RunFor`, `Pump`, `Next` or `EmitAck`. The arguments of every event are a JSON array, read with `ArgStr`, `ArgInt` and the like. If the sender wants an answer, the event's `ack_id` is not negative and you answer it with `Reply`. For several namespaces on one connection, create a `Manager`.

Things that catch people out:

- A program that never pumps never hears anything. Pings from the server are answered while you pump, so a client that sleeps for longer than the server's ping timeout is disconnected.

- `Next` returns connection events too, such as `EV_CONNECT`; loop until the kind you stop on, not until the first event that is not `EV_EVENT`. Its queue starts with the first `Next` call and keeps the newest `event_queue` events (256 by default), dropping the oldest.

- Free what you build. `ArgsFree` for argument lists and `AckFree` for answers, or a long running client keeps growing.

- Socket.IO 2 servers (from before 2020) speak an older protocol and are not supported.

## Handling events in your own loop

Listeners with `On` are the usual style, but sometimes a plain loop reads better: a worker that handles one event at a time, or a program that must also do other work between messages. `Next` waits up to the given milliseconds and returns one `Event`. Its `kind` says what it is: a message from the server (`EV_EVENT`, with the name and the arguments), a change of the connection such as `EV_DISCONNECT` (the reason is in `message`), or `EV_TIMEOUT` when nothing came.

net-socketio-next-loop.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import net.websocket

mut server := websocket.Server {}

func fake_server():
    mut conn := websocket.Accept(server)
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `0{"sid":"s1","upgrades":[],"pingInterval":20000,"pingTimeout":5000}`)
    m := websocket.Poll(conn, 3000)
    if m.kind == websocket.TEXT and m.text == "40":
        _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `40{"sid":"a1"}`)
        _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `42["price","BTC",61250]`)
        _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `42["price","ETH",2410]`)
        _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `42["halt","maintenance"]`)
        _ := websocket.SendText(conn, "41")
    end
    _ := websocket.Poll(conn, 1000)
    websocket.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = websocket.Listen(0)
    t := spawn(fake_server)
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.transports = socketio.TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET
    o.reconnection = false
    c := socketio.DialWith("http://127.0.0.1:" + websocket.Port(server), o)

    mut going := true
    until going:
        e := socketio.Next(c, 3000)
        if e.kind == socketio.EV_EVENT and e.name == "price":
            println "price", socketio.ArgStr(e, 0), socketio.ArgInt(e, 1)
        else e.kind == socketio.EV_EVENT:
            println "event", e.name, socketio.ArgStr(e, 0)
        else e.kind == socketio.EV_DISCONNECT:
            println "disconnected:", e.message, e.message == socketio.REASON_SERVER_DISCONNECT
            going = false
        else e.kind == socketio.EV_TIMEOUT:
            println "nothing arrived in time"
            going = false
        end
    end
    socketio.Close(c)
    join(t)
    websocket.CloseServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
price BTC 61250
price ETH 2410
event halt maintenance
disconnected: io server disconnect true
```

The program brings its own tiny server, which speaks the Socket.IO wire format over a WebSocket, so it runs without Node.js. A real server sends the same packets: `42["price","BTC",61250]` is an event named `price` with two arguments, and `41` is the server closing the namespace, which arrives as `REASON_SERVER_DISCONNECT`. After that reason the client does not reconnect by itself, because the server meant it.

## Logging in with a token

Socket.IO servers usually check the user in a middleware that reads the `auth` object of the connection. Put that JSON in `Options.auth` before dialling. When the middleware says no, the server answers with a connect error instead of a session; `Refused` is then true and `RefusalReason` holds the message the server gave.

net-socketio-auth.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.auth = `{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.e30.x"}`
    o.reconnection = false
    c := socketio.DialWith("https://chat.example.com", o)
    if socketio.Refused(c):
        println "the server refused us:", socketio.RefusalReason(c)
        ret 1
    end
    if not socketio.IsConnected(c):
        println "could not connect:", socketio.LastError(c)
        ret 1
    end
    println "connected as", socketio.Id(c), "over", socketio.TransportName(c)
    socketio.Close(c)
    ret 0
end
```

This needs a running server, so it is only checked here. With a Node.js server, the matching check is an `io.use((socket, next) => ...)` that reads `socket.handshake.auth.token` and calls `next(new Error("..."))` to refuse.

## Acknowledgements in both directions

An acknowledgement is Socket.IO's request and reply: the sender numbers an event and the other side answers that number. `EmitAck` sends an event and waits, up to the time you give, for the server's answer; `ok` is false when it did not come in time. The other way round, when the server sends an event with an id, `e.ack_id` holds it and `Reply`, `ReplyStr` or `ReplyJSON` answers it. The fake server below shows both packets on the wire: `420[...]` is the client's event with ack id 0 and `4317["yes"]` is the client's answer to the server's ack id 17.

net-socketio-ack.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import net.websocket
import encoding.json

mut server := websocket.Server {}
mut seen := Vector {} as Vector<str>

func fake_server():
    mut conn := websocket.Accept(server)
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `0{"sid":"s1","upgrades":[],"pingInterval":20000,"pingTimeout":5000}`)
    if websocket.ReceiveText(conn) != "40": ret end
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `40{"sid":"a1"}`)
    join := websocket.ReceiveText(conn)
    seen.push(join)
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `430[{"ok":true,"members":3}]`)
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `4217["confirm","order 1042"]`)
    seen.push(websocket.ReceiveText(conn))
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, "41")
    _ := websocket.Poll(conn, 1000)
    websocket.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = websocket.Listen(0)
    t := spawn(fake_server)
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.transports = socketio.TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET
    o.reconnection = false
    c := socketio.DialWith("http://127.0.0.1:" + websocket.Port(server), o)

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "room-1")
    mut answer := socketio.EmitAck(c, "join", a, 2000)
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)
    println "join answered:", answer.ok, "members:", json.GetInt(socketio.AckArg(answer, 0), "members")
    socketio.AckFree(answer)

    mut going := true
    until going:
        e := socketio.Next(c, 3000)
        if e.kind == socketio.EV_EVENT and e.name == "confirm":
            println "server asks:", socketio.ArgStr(e, 0), "ack id", e.ack_id
            _ := socketio.ReplyStr(e, "yes")
        else e.kind == socketio.EV_DISCONNECT or e.kind == socketio.EV_TIMEOUT:
            going = false
        end
    end
    socketio.Close(c)
    join(t)
    websocket.CloseServer(server)
    println "the server saw:"
    each line in seen: println " ", line end
end
```

Output:

```text
join answered: true members: 3
server asks: order 1042 ack id 17
the server saw:
  420["join","room-1"]
  4317["yes"]
```

Answer each acknowledged event once. Servers usually put a timeout on their own `emitWithAck`, so reply before you start slow work, or reply with a "started" status and send the result as a separate event.

## A bot that stays connected

A long running client joins a room, answers some messages and survives network trouble. `EmitAck` sends an event and waits for the server's answer, which is how you know the join worked. `Run` then handles events until the client is closed, and reconnects on its own after a dropped connection, waiting `reconnection_delay` milliseconds and longer each time up to `reconnection_delay_max`. The `disconnect` and `reconnect` listeners let you log both.

net-socketio-chat-bot.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import str

mut client := socketio.Client {}

func main:
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.reconnection_attempts = 10
    o.reconnection_delay = 2000
    client = socketio.DialWith("http://localhost:3000", o)
    if not socketio.IsConnected(client):
        println "cannot reach the chat:", socketio.LastError(client)
        ret 1
    end

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "support")
    mut k := socketio.EmitAck(client, "join", a, 5000)
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)
    if not k.ok:
        println "joining the room timed out"
        ret 1
    end
    println "joined support, members:", socketio.AckInt(k, 0)
    socketio.AckFree(k)

    socketio.On(client, "message", (e: socketio.Event):
        text := socketio.ArgStr(e, 1)
        if str.StartsWith(text, "!time"):
            _ := socketio.EmitStr(client, "message", "office hours are 9 to 17")
        end
    end)
    socketio.On(client, "disconnect", (e: socketio.Event):
        println "lost the connection:", e.message
    end)
    socketio.On(client, "reconnect", (e: socketio.Event):
        _ := e
        println "back after", socketio.Attempts(client), "attempts"
    end)
    socketio.Run(client)
    ret 0
end
```

A bot that only reacts to events can stay in `Run` for its whole life; it returns when `Close` is called or when reconnection gives up.

## Which way to receive

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The program only reacts to events | `On` listeners and `Run` |
| A test or a script that runs for a while and stops | `RunFor` |
| Your own main loop, with other work between events | `Pump` with a short timeout, once per turn of the loop |
| One event at a time, in order, without callbacks | `Next` |
| Several namespaces on one connection | `NewManager`, `Of`, then `PumpManager` |

## Types

### `Endpoint`

```salam
struct Endpoint
```

A parsed server URL.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | HTTPS or WSS. |
| `host` | `str = "localhost"` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 80` | The port; 80 or 443 if it is not given. |
| `path` | `str = "/socket.io"` | The Socket.IO path. |
| `namespace` | `str = "/"` | The namespace, from the URL path. |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The URL is valid. |

net-socketio-URL.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func show(url: str):
    e := socketio.ParseURL(url)
    if not e.ok:
        println url, "invalid"
        ret
    end
    println e.host, e.port, e.secure, e.namespace, "query=" + e.query
    println socketio.Origin(e)
end

func main:
    show("http://localhost:3000")
    show("https://example.com/admin/?token=abc")
    show("ws://[::1]:8080/chat")
    show("ftp://example.com")
end
```

Output:

```text
localhost 3000 false / query=
http://localhost:3000
example.com 443 true /admin query=token=abc
https://example.com
::1 8080 false /chat query=
http://[::1]:8080
ftp://example.com invalid
```

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

Connection options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `str = "/socket.io"` | The path of the Socket.IO server. |
| `query` | `str = ""` | An extra query for the URL. |
| `auth` | `str = ""` | Authentication data as JSON, sent when connecting to the namespace. |
| `headers` | `str = ""` | Extra HTTP headers, one per line. |
| `transports` | `int` | The transport, one of the `TRANSPORT_...` constants. |
| `reconnection` | `bool = true` | Reconnect automatically after a disconnect. |
| `reconnection_attempts` | `int = 0` | The most attempts; zero means no limit. |
| `reconnection_delay` | `int = 1000` | The delay before the first attempt in milliseconds; it doubles every time. |
| `reconnection_delay_max` | `int = 5000` | The longest delay. |
| `randomization_factor` | `int = 50` | A random percentage added to or taken from the delay so that all clients do not come back at the same moment. |
| `timeout` | `int = 20000` | The connect timeout in milliseconds. |
| `insecure` | `bool = false` | Do not check the TLS certificate; for testing only. |
| `auto_connect` | `bool = true` | The client connects right away. |
| `event_queue` | `int = 256` | The most events `Next` keeps waiting; when it is full the oldest is dropped. |
| `ack_timeout` | `int = 0` | The acknowledgement timeout in milliseconds used when `EmitAck` is given 0. |
| `retries` | `int = 0` | How many times to resend messages that got no acknowledgement. |
| `trailing_slash` | `bool = true` | Add a slash to the end of the path, like the JavaScript client. |
| `remember_upgrade` | `bool = false` | If the upgrade to WebSocket worked once, use WebSocket directly next time. |

net-socketio-Options.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    println o.path, o.reconnection, o.reconnection_delay, o.timeout
    println o.transports == socketio.TRANSPORT_AUTO
    o.transports = socketio.TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET
    o.auth = `{"token":"abc"}`
    o.auto_connect = false
    println o.transports, o.auth, o.auto_connect
    println socketio.TRANSPORT_POLLING, socketio.REASON_SERVER_DISCONNECT, socketio.REASON_PING_TIMEOUT
    println socketio.PUMP_OK, socketio.PUMP_TIMEOUT, socketio.PUMP_CLOSED
end
```

Output:

```text
/socket.io true 1000 20000
true
1 {"token":"abc"} false
2 io server disconnect ping timeout
0 1 2
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

One socket on one namespace.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p` | `void*` | The internal pointer. |

net-socketio-Client.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import net.websocket
import str

mut server := websocket.Server {}
mut report := ""

func test_server():
    mut conn := websocket.Accept(server)
    _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `0{"sid":"s1","upgrades":[],"pingInterval":20000,"pingTimeout":5000}`)
    mut going := true
    until going:
        m := websocket.Poll(conn, 3000)
        if m.kind != websocket.TEXT:
            break
        end
        packet := m.text.substr(1, m.text.len() - 1)
        if packet == "0":
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `40{"sid":"a1"}`)
        else str.StartsWith(packet, `2["chat"`):
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `42["chat","welcome"]`)
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, `429["question","2+2"]`)
        else str.Contains(packet, `"add"`):
            id := packet.substr(1, str.Find(packet, "[") - 1)
            _ := websocket.SendText(conn, "43" + id + "[5]")
        else str.StartsWith(packet, "39"):
            report += "reply: " + packet.substr(2, packet.len() - 2)
        else packet == "1":
            going = false
        end
    end
    websocket.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    server = websocket.Listen(0)
    t := spawn(test_server)
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.transports = socketio.TRANSPORT_WEBSOCKET
    o.reconnection = false
    c := socketio.DialWith("http://127.0.0.1:" + websocket.Port(server), o)
    println socketio.IsConnected(c), socketio.Sid(c), socketio.Id(c), socketio.Namespace(c), socketio.TransportName(c)

    socketio.On(c, "chat", (e: socketio.Event):
        println "message:", socketio.ArgStr(e, 0)
    end)
    socketio.On(c, "question", (e: socketio.Event):
        println "question:", socketio.ArgStr(e, 0), e.ack_id >= 0
        _ := socketio.ReplyStr(e, "four")
    end)
    println socketio.ListenerCount(c, "chat"), socketio.HasListeners(c, "news")
    _ := socketio.EmitStr(c, "chat", "hello")
    socketio.RunFor(c, 500)

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddInt(a, 2)
    socketio.AddInt(a, 3)
    mut k := socketio.EmitAck(c, "add", a, 2000)
    println k.ok, socketio.AckInt(k, 0)
    socketio.AckFree(k)
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)

    socketio.Close(c)
    join(t)
    websocket.CloseServer(server)
    println report
end
```

Output:

```text
true s1 a1 / websocket
1 false
message: welcome
question: 2+2 true
true 5
reply: ["four"]
```

### `Manager`

```salam
struct Manager
```

A connection that several namespaces work on.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p` | `void*` | The internal pointer. |

net-socketio-Manager.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut o := socketio.NewOptions()
    o.auth = `{"token":"abc"}`
    o.auto_connect = false
    m := socketio.NewManager("https://example.com", o)
    socketio.SetReconnection(m, true)
    socketio.SetReconnectionAttempts(m, 5)
    socketio.SetReconnectionDelay(m, 500)
    socketio.SetReconnectionDelayMax(m, 10000)
    socketio.SetRandomizationFactor(m, 20)
    socketio.SetTimeout(m, 5000)
    println socketio.OptionsOf(m).reconnection_attempts

    public := socketio.Of(m, "/")
    admin := socketio.Of(m, "/admin")
    socketio.SetAuth(admin, `{"role":"admin"}`)
    println socketio.AuthOf(admin), socketio.Sockets(m).len()
    if not socketio.Open(m):
        println "error:", socketio.ManagerError(m)
        ret
    end
    println socketio.IsOpen(m)
    _ := socketio.Connect(public)
    _ := socketio.Connect(admin)
    if socketio.Refused(admin):
        println "refused:", socketio.RefusalReason(admin)
    end
    println socketio.Active(public), socketio.Disconnected(public), socketio.Recovered(public)
    println socketio.Transport(public), socketio.PingInterval(public), socketio.PingTimeout(public), socketio.MaxPayload(public)
    println socketio.Buffered(public), socketio.Pending(public), socketio.Queued(public), socketio.Attempts(public)
    println socketio.EndpointOf(public).host, socketio.ManagerOf(public).p == m.p
    _ := socketio.PumpManager(m, 1000)
    socketio.Disconnect(admin)
    socketio.CloseManager(m)
end
```

### `Event`

```salam
struct Event
```

An event that arrived.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int` | The kind of event. |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The event name. |
| `nsp` | `str = "/"` | The namespace. |
| `data` | `str = "[]"` | The arguments as a JSON array. |
| `ack_id` | `int = -1` | The acknowledgement number if the sender wants one; otherwise -1. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | A description, for error and disconnect events. |
| `bins` | `Vector` | The binary parts. |
| `client` | `Client` | The socket that received the event. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Client.salam

### `Ack`

```salam
struct Ack
```

An acknowledgement reply.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The reply arrived before the timeout. |
| `id` | `int = -1` | The acknowledgement number. |
| `data` | `str = "[]"` | The arguments as a JSON array. |
| `bins` | `Vector` | The binary parts. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Client.salam

```salam
struct Bytes
```

The bytes of one binary part.

net-socketio-Bytes.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut b := socketio.BytesFromStr("Salam")
    println b.len, socketio.BytesAt(b, 0)
    println socketio.BytesToStr(b)
    println socketio.BytesToBase64(b)
    socketio.BytesFree(b)
    mut c := socketio.NewBytes("hello" as void*, 4)
    println socketio.BytesToStr(c)
    socketio.BytesFree(c)

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "file.txt")
    socketio.AddBinaryStr(a, "abc")
    println socketio.ArgsJSON(a, "upload")
```

### `Packet`

```salam
struct Packet
```

One Socket.IO packet.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int = -1` | The kind. |
| `nsp` | `str = "/"` | The namespace. |
| `id` | `int = -1` | The acknowledgement number; -1 means no acknowledgement. |
| `data` | `str = ""` | The data as JSON. |
| `attachments` | `int = 0` | The number of binary parts. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The packet was read correctly. |

net-socketio-Packet.salam

```salam
import net.socketio

func main:
    mut p := socketio.Packet {}
    p.kind = socketio.PKT_EVENT
    p.nsp = "/chat"
    p.id = 7
    p.data = `["hi",1]`
    text := socketio.EncodePacket(p)
    println text
    d := socketio.DecodePacket(text)
    println d.ok, d.kind, d.nsp, d.id, d.data
    bad := socketio.DecodePacket("x")
    println bad.ok

    payload := socketio.EncodeEngine(socketio.EIO_MESSAGE, text)
    println payload
    println socketio.EngineKind(payload) == socketio.EIO_MESSAGE
    println socketio.EngineBody(payload)

    mut items := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    items.push("2")
    items.push(payload)
    body := socketio.JoinPayloads(items)
    parts := socketio.SplitPayloads(body)
    println parts.len(), parts.get(0), parts.get(1)

    arr := socketio.SplitJSONArray(`["a", {"b":[1,2]}, 3]`)
    println arr.len(), arr.get(1)

    ph := socketio.Placeholder(0)
    println ph
    println socketio.PlaceholderNum(ph), socketio.PlaceholderNum("12")
end
```

Output:

```text
2/chat,7["hi",1]
true 2 /chat 7 ["hi",1]
false
42/chat,7["hi",1]
true
2/chat,7["hi",1]
2 2 42/chat,7["hi",1]
3 {"b":[1,2]}
{"_placeholder":true,"num":0}
0 -1
```

net-socketio-Args.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import encoding.value

func main:
    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "hello \"world\"")
    socketio.AddInt(a, 42)
    socketio.AddFloat(a, 2.5)
    socketio.AddBool(a, true)
    socketio.AddNull(a)
    socketio.AddJSON(a, `{"x":1}`)
    println socketio.ArgsCount(a)
    text := socketio.ArgsJSON(a, "message")
    println text
    println socketio.ItemCount(text)
    println socketio.ItemStr(text, 1)
    println socketio.ItemInt(text, 2)
    println socketio.ItemFloat(text, 3)
    println socketio.ItemBool(text, 4)
    println socketio.Item(text, 6)
    println socketio.Item(text, 9).len()
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)

    mut v := socketio.ItemValue(text, 2)
    println value.IsNumber(v), value.AsInt(v)
    mut a2 := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddValue(a2, v)
    socketio.AddBytes(a2, "xyz" as void*, 3)
    println socketio.ArgsJSON(a2, "")
    socketio.ArgsFree(a2)
    value.ValueFree(v)
end
```

Output:

```text

["message","hello \"world\"",42,2.5,true,null,{"x":1}]
7
hello "world"
42
2.5
true
{"x":1}
0
true 42
[42,{"_placeholder":true,"num":0}]
```

### Event kinds `EV_…`

The value of the `kind` field in the event that `Next` returns. A message event is one of the server's messages; the rest report on the connection itself: connecting and disconnecting, errors, reconnection attempts, pings, timeouts and the upgrade to WebSocket. Listeners are called with the English names of these events, such as `connect` and `disconnect`.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `EV_NONE` | `0` |
| `EV_EVENT` | `1` |
| `EV_CONNECT` | `2` |
| `EV_DISCONNECT` | `3` |
| `EV_CONNECT_ERROR` | `4` |
| `EV_ERROR` | `5` |
| `EV_RECONNECT` | `6` |
| `EV_RECONNECT_ATTEMPT` | `7` |
| `EV_RECONNECT_ERROR` | `8` |
| `EV_RECONNECT_FAILED` | `9` |
| `EV_PING` | `10` |
| `EV_TIMEOUT` | `11` |
| `EV_UPGRADE` | `12` |

net-socketio-Ack.salam

```salam
import net.socketio
import encoding.value

func main:
    c := socketio.Dial("http://localhost:3000")
    if not socketio.IsConnected(c):
        println socketio.LastError(c)
        ret
    end
    socketio.OnAny(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "received:", e.name, socketio.ArgCount(e)
    end)
    socketio.Once(c, "welcome", (e: socketio.Event):
        println socketio.Arg(e, 0)
    end)
    socketio.OnAnyOutgoing(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "sent:", e.name
    end)

    socketio.PrependAny(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "first of all:", e.name
    end)
    socketio.PrependAnyOutgoing(c, (e: socketio.Event):
        println "sending:", e.name
    end)
    println socketio.AnyListenerCount(c)

    _ := socketio.Emit(c, "ping")
    _ := socketio.EmitInt(c, "score", 12)
    _ := socketio.EmitFloat(c, "temp", 21.5)
    _ := socketio.EmitBool(c, "ready", true)
    _ := socketio.EmitJSON(c, "user", `{"name":"Ali"}`)
    _ := socketio.EmitBytes(c, "file", "abc" as void*, 3)
    _ := socketio.Send(c, "a plain message")

    mut a := socketio.NewArgs()
    socketio.AddStr(a, "room-1")
    _ := socketio.EmitArgs(c, "join", a)
    _ := socketio.EmitVolatile(c, "cursor", a)
    _ := socketio.EmitWithAck(c, "join", a, 2000, (k: socketio.Ack):
        println k.ok, socketio.AckCount(k), socketio.AckStr(k, 0)
        println socketio.AckArg(k, 1), socketio.AckFloat(k, 1), socketio.AckBool(k, 2)
        if socketio.AckIsBinary(k, 3):
            println socketio.AckBytes(k, 3).len
        end
        mut v := socketio.AckValue(k, 0)
        value.ValueFree(v)
    end)
    socketio.ArgsFree(a)

    mut e := socketio.Next(c, 5000)
    if e.kind == socketio.EV_EVENT:
        println socketio.ArgInt(e, 0), socketio.ArgFloat(e, 1), socketio.ArgBool(e, 2)
        if socketio.ArgIsBinary(e, 3):
            b := socketio.ArgBytes(e, 3)
            println b.len
        end
        if e.ack_id >= 0:
            _ := socketio.ReplyJSON(e, `{"ok":true}`)
        end
    else e.kind == socketio.EV_DISCONNECT:
        println "disconnected:", e.message
    end
    socketio.EventFree(e)

    mut e2 := socketio.NextEvent(c, 5000)
    mut v2 := socketio.ArgValue(e2, 0)
    println value.IsNumber(v2)
    value.ValueFree(v2)
    socketio.EventFree(e2)

    _ := socketio.Pump(c, 100)
    socketio.Off(c, "welcome")
    socketio.OffAny(c)
    socketio.OffAnyOutgoing(c)
    socketio.OffAll(c)
    socketio.Run(c)
end
```

### Disconnect reasons `REASON_…`

The text in the `message` field of a disconnect event, telling why the connection ended: the server or the program itself closed it, a ping did not arrive in time, the transport closed or failed, or a packet could not be read.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `REASON_SERVER_DISCONNECT` | `"io server disconnect"` |
| `REASON_CLIENT_DISCONNECT` | `"io client disconnect"` |
| `REASON_PING_TIMEOUT` | `"ping timeout"` |
| `REASON_TRANSPORT_CLOSE` | `"transport close"` |
| `REASON_TRANSPORT_ERROR` | `"transport error"` |
| `REASON_PARSE_ERROR` | `"parse error"` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Options.salam

### Pump results `PUMP_…`

The result of `Pump` and `PumpManager`: something arrived and was handled, the timeout ran out, or the connection is closed.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `PUMP_OK` | `0` |
| `PUMP_TIMEOUT` | `1` |
| `PUMP_CLOSED` | `2` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Options.salam

### Engine packet kinds `EIO_…`

Socket.IO runs on a layer called Engine.IO. Every message on that layer starts with a digit that gives its kind: open, close, ping, pong, message, upgrade and noop. Socket.IO packets travel inside messages of the "message" kind.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `EIO_OPEN` | `0` |
| `EIO_CLOSE` | `1` |
| `EIO_PING` | `2` |
| `EIO_PONG` | `3` |
| `EIO_MESSAGE` | `4` |
| `EIO_UPGRADE` | `5` |
| `EIO_NOOP` | `6` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Packet.salam

### Socket.IO packet kinds `PKT_…`

The kinds of Socket.IO packet: connecting to a namespace, disconnecting, an event, an acknowledgement, a connect error, and the binary event and binary acknowledgement whose bytes follow the packet separately.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `PKT_CONNECT` | `0` |
| `PKT_DISCONNECT` | `1` |
| `PKT_EVENT` | `2` |
| `PKT_ACK` | `3` |
| `PKT_CONNECT_ERROR` | `4` |
| `PKT_BINARY_EVENT` | `5` |
| `PKT_BINARY_ACK` | `6` |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: net-socketio-Packet.salam

### `Once`
