### `Claims`

```salam
struct Claims
```

The claims of a token.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iss` | `str = ""` | The issuer. |
| `sub` | `str = ""` | The subject, usually the user id. |
| `aud` | `str = ""` | The audience. |
| `aud_raw` | `str = ""` | The audience as JSON, when it is an array. |
| `exp` | `i64 = 0` | The expiry time in Unix seconds. |
| `nbf` | `i64 = 0` | The time before which it is not valid. |
| `iat` | `i64 = 0` | The issue time. |
| `jti` | `str = ""` | The unique id of the token. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | The other claims, as JSON. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: jwt-Sign.salam

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

The check options.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alg` | `str = "HS256"` | The algorithm expected; a token with another one is rejected. |
| `issuer` | `str = ""` | The required issuer; empty means do not check it. |
| `audience` | `str = ""` | The required audience. |
| `subject` | `str = ""` | The required subject. |
| `leeway` | `i64 = 0` | How many seconds of clock difference to accept. |
| `now` | `i64 = 0` | The time to check against; zero means now. For testing. |
| `require_exp` | `bool = false` | Reject a token with no `exp`. Off by default, so without it a token with no expiry is valid forever. |
| `require_nbf` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `nbf`. |
| `require_iat` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `iat`. |
| `require_sub` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `sub`. |
| `require_jti` | `bool = false` | Reject one with no `jti`. |
| `check_typ` | `bool = true` | Check that the type is `JWT`. |

jwt-Algorithms.salam

```salam
import jwt

func main:
    println jwt.JWT_HS256, jwt.JWT_HS384, jwt.JWT_HS512
    println jwt.IsSupportedAlg("HS512"), jwt.IsSupportedAlg("none"), jwt.DigestSize("HS384")

    mut c := jwt.NewClaims()
    c.sub = "7"
    c.jti = "t-1"
    jwt.ExpiresIn(c, 3600)
    jwt.NotBeforeIn(c, 0)
    mut err := 0
    one := jwt.SignHS384(c, "k", err)
    two := jwt.SignHS512(c, "k", err)
    three := jwt.Sign(c, jwt.JWT_HS256, "k", err)
    four := jwt.SignWithKid(c, "HS256", "key-2026", "k", err)
    println jwt.Decode(one, err).alg, jwt.Decode(two, err).alg, jwt.Decode(four, err).kid

    t := jwt.VerifyHS256(three, "k", err)
    println t.valid, jwt.SecondsRemaining(t) > 3500
    b := jwt.Verify(one, "k", jwt.OptionsFor("HS384"), err)
    println b.valid
    _ := jwt.Verify(one, "k", jwt.DefaultOptions(), err)
    println jwt.ErrorText(err)

    raw := jwt.SignJSON(`{"sub":"1"}`, "HS256", "", "k", err)
    println raw
    d := jwt.Decode(raw, err)
    println d.header_json, d.payload_json
    println jwt.SignatureOf(d.signing_input, "HS256", "k") == d.signature

    encoded := jwt.B64UrlEncode("hello?")
    println encoded.len()
    mut ok := false
    println jwt.B64UrlDecode(encoded, ok), ok
    println jwt.B64UrlEncodeBytes("hi?" as void*, 3)
    _ := jwt.SignHS256(c, "", err)
    println err == jwt.JWT_ERR_EMPTY_SECRET, jwt.ErrorText(err)
    println jwt.JWT_ERR_BAD_BASE64, jwt.JWT_ERR_BAD_JSON, jwt.JWT_ERR_ALG_UNSUPPORTED, jwt.JWT_ERR_ALG_MISMATCH
    println jwt.JWT_ERR_NOT_YET_VALID, jwt.JWT_ERR_ISSUED_IN_FUTURE, jwt.JWT_ERR_ISSUER, jwt.JWT_ERR_AUDIENCE
    println jwt.ErrorText(jwt.JWT_ERR_SUBJECT), "/", jwt.ErrorText(jwt.JWT_ERR_MISSING_CLAIM), "/", jwt.ErrorText(jwt.JWT_ERR_TYPE)
end
```

Output:

```text
HS256 HS384 HS512
true false 48
HS384 HS512 key-2026
true true
true
algorithm mismatch
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIn0.q9rSPf4ratZ1Xkhd3M-FudlLIKYdlSzrHeXV7AICSuw
{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"} {"sub":"1"}
true
8
hello? true
aGk_
true empty secret
2 3 4 5
8 9 10 11
subject mismatch / required claim missing / unexpected typ header
```

### `Guard`

```salam
struct Guard
```

An HTTP route guard: the secret, the check options and the cookie name.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | `str = ""` | The signing secret. |
| `opts` | `Options` | The check options. |
| `cookie` | `str = ""` | The name of a cookie the token is also read from; empty means the Authorization header only. |
| `realm` | `str = "api"` | The name that goes in the `WWW-Authenticate` header. |

jwt-Guard.salam

```salam
import jwt
import net.http
import net.router

mut guard := jwt.NewGuard("a-server-secret-only-the-server-knows")

func login(ctx: i64):
    mut err := 0
    mut c := jwt.NewClaims()
    c.sub = "42"
    jwt.SetStr(c, "scope", "read")
    jwt.SetRaw(c, "roles", `["editor"]`)
    token := jwt.Issue(guard, c, 3600, err)
    jwt.SetSessionCookieInsecure(ctx, guard, token, 3600)
    http.Text(ctx, token)
end

func me(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.Require(ctx, guard, t):
        http.Text(ctx, "hello user " + t.claims.sub)
    end
end

func admin(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.RequireScope(ctx, guard, "admin", t):
        http.Text(ctx, "admin panel")
    end
end

func edit(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.RequireClaim(ctx, guard, "roles", "editor", t):
        http.Text(ctx, "editor")
    end
end

func profile(ctx: i64):
    mut t := jwt.Token {}
    if jwt.RequireSubject(ctx, guard, http.Param(ctx, "id"), t):
        http.Text(ctx, "your own profile")
    end
end

func manual(ctx: i64):
    mut err := 0
    t := jwt.Check(ctx, guard, err)
    if jwt.BearerToken(ctx).len() == 0 and jwt.TokenFrom(ctx, guard).len() == 0:
        jwt.MissingCredential(ctx, guard)
    else err != jwt.JWT_OK:
        jwt.Unauthorized(ctx, guard, jwt.ErrorText(err))
    else t.claims.sub == "0":
        jwt.Forbidden(ctx, "the user is blocked")
    else:
        http.Text(ctx, "valid")
    end
end

func logout(ctx: i64):
    jwt.ClearSessionCookie(ctx, guard)
    http.Text(ctx, "you are logged out")
end

func main:
    guard.cookie = "session"
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/login", login)
    router.Get(r, "/me", me)
    router.Get(r, "/admin", admin)
    router.Get(r, "/edit", edit)
    router.Get(r, "/users/:id", profile)
    router.Get(r, "/check", manual)
    router.Post(r, "/logout", logout)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19630)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    base := "http://127.0.0.1:19630"

    login_response := http.Post(base + "/login", "")
    token := http.Body(login_response)
    println http.CookieMap(login_response).get("session") == token
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
    println jwt.ParseBearer("Bearer " + token) == token
    ask(base, "/me", headers)
    ask(base, "/admin", headers)
    ask(base, "/edit", headers)
    ask(base, "/users/42", headers)
    ask(base, "/users/7", headers)
    ask(base, "/check", headers)
    ask(base, "/me", http.NewHeaders())
    mut bad := http.NewHeaders()
    bad.insert("Authorization", "Bearer x.y.z")
    ask(base, "/check", bad)
    mut cookie := http.NewHeaders()
    cookie.insert("Cookie", "session=" + token)
    ask(base, "/me", cookie)

    mut access := ""
    mut refresh := ""
    mut err := 0
    println jwt.IssuePair(guard, "42", 900, 86400, access, refresh, err), access != refresh
    one := jwt.IssueFor(guard, "42", 60, err)
    println jwt.Verify(one, guard.secret, guard.opts, err).claims.sub, guard.realm
end

func ask(base: str, path: str, headers: HashMap<str, str>):
    response := http.GetWith(base + path, headers)
    println path, http.Status(response), http.Body(response)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true
/me 200 hello user 42
/admin 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"missing scope: admin"}
/edit 200 editor
/users/42 200 your own profile
/users/7 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"not your resource"}
/check 200 valid
/me 401 {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"missing bearer token"}
/check 401 {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"invalid base64url segment"}
/me 200 hello user 42
true true
42 api
```

# tls

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/tls/

Secure TLS 1.3 and 1.2 connections and public key cryptography tools, with no OpenSSL needed.

The tls package is a complete implementation of TLS 1.2 and 1.3 written in Salam, with no outside library. A client connects with `Dial` and checks the server certificate against the system roots; a server reads its certificate and key with `NewServerConfig` and secures each accepted socket with `WrapServer`. Most programs never call it directly: net/http, net/email and net/websocket use it for `https`, SMTPS and `wss`. For code written in the OpenSSL style (a context, `SSL_connect`, `SSL_read`), ssl offers that interface on top of this package.

The cryptography tools here are also useful for protocols and storage of your own: the two sides make a shared secret with ECDH, derive a key from it with HKDF, and encrypt and seal the message with AES-GCM; P-256 signs and verifies. Keys and data are passed around as base64 text, which keeps binary bytes safe inside a `str`.

Things to know:

- Check `ConnOk` after `Dial`. A failed handshake or a bad certificate gives a closed connection, and `ConnError` says why.

- `Read` returns a `str`, which stops at a zero byte. For binary data use `ReadBytes` and `WriteBytes` with your own buffer.

- Clients cannot present a certificate (no mutual TLS), and a `Conn` is passed by reference and belongs to one thread at a time.

- Never repeat an AES-GCM nonce under one key; the sealing section shows a counter that avoids it.

## Connect to a server and handle a bad certificate

`Dial` does the whole handshake and checks the certificate chain against the system roots and the name in `NewConfig`. When something is wrong, the connection is not open and `ConnError` says why: the certificate expired, it was issued for another name, or it does not chain to a trusted root. Always check `ConnOk` before you write. The program below tries a working site and three of the deliberately broken hosts at badssl.com.

tls-https-check.salam

```salam
import tls

func probe(host: str):
    cfg := tls.NewConfig(host)
    mut conn := tls.Dial(host, 443, cfg)
    if not tls.ConnOk(conn):
        println host, "refused:", tls.ConnError(conn)
        ret
    end
    println host, tls.Version(conn), tls.CipherName(conn), tls.PeerCertCount(conn), "certificates"
    tls.Close(conn)
end

func main:
    probe("www.salamlang.ir")
    probe("expired.badssl.com")
    probe("wrong.host.badssl.com")
    probe("self-signed.badssl.com")
end
```

It needs network access, so it is only checked here. When it was run, it printed the lines below; the cipher and the number of certificates depend on the server.

```salam
www.salamlang.ir TLS1.3 TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 3 certificates
expired.badssl.com refused: certificate verification failed: certificate expired
wrong.host.badssl.com refused: certificate verification failed: hostname does not match certificate
self-signed.badssl.com refused: certificate verification failed: no trusted issuer found
```

For a private server with its own certificate authority, set `ca_file` in the config to that CA's PEM file. `insecure_skip_verify` turns the check off; use it only for a quick local test, never in a program others rely on.

## Encrypt records with AES-GCM

`AesGcmSeal` encrypts a text and adds a tag, so that `AesGcmOpen` notices any change: a wrong key, a wrong nonce or a changed byte all make `ok` false instead of returning garbage. The key is 32 random bytes as base64; make it once with `RandomSalt(32)` and keep it secret. The nonce must never repeat under one key. The simple rule is a counter: `GcmNonce(0)` for the first message, `GcmNonce(1)` for the next, and the counter is stored next to the record so that it can be opened later.

tls-sealed-records.salam

```salam
import tls

func main:
    key := "q1V0kA8mY8l3R9m0bJvT0F6c0w2f5yYQ1aZt3pK8sXo="
    records := ["balance=120", "balance=95", "balance=310"]

    mut sealed := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    mut ok := false
    each i, r in records:
        sealed.push(tls.AesGcmSeal(key, tls.GcmNonce(i as i64), r, ok))
    end
    println "sealed", sealed.len(), "records:", ok
    println "first one:", sealed.get(0)

    each i, s in sealed:
        plain := tls.AesGcmOpen(key, tls.GcmNonce(i as i64), s, ok)
        println "record", i, "->", plain, ok
    end

    _ := tls.AesGcmOpen(key, tls.GcmNonce(1), sealed.get(0), ok)
    println "opened with the wrong nonce:", ok
    _ := tls.AesGcmOpen("AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=", tls.GcmNonce(0), sealed.get(0), ok)
    println "opened with the wrong key:", ok
end
```

Output:

```text
sealed 3 records: true
first one: q/F2IqBhzaLO/CFJROFcuA2GEUtg3H4MyDU5
record 0 -> balance=120 true
record 1 -> balance=95 true
record 2 -> balance=310 true
opened with the wrong nonce: false
opened with the wrong key: false
```

With a fixed key and nonce the output is always the same, which is why the program can print it. That is also the danger: the same nonce for two different texts lets an attacker learn about both, so never reset the counter while the key stays the same.

## A shared key from public keys

Two programs that have never met can agree on a key without sending it. Each makes an ECDH key pair with `EcdhP256Generate` and sends the other only its public key. `EcdhP256Shared` then gives both the same secret, and `HkdfSha256` turns it into a key for AES-GCM. Someone who saw both public keys still cannot compute the secret. The `info` text names what the key is for, so one secret can safely give separate keys for separate uses.

tls-secure-channel.salam

```salam
import tls

struct Party:
    pub private_key: str = ""
    pub public_key: str = ""
end

func new_party(): Party:
    mut p := Party {}
    _ := tls.EcdhP256Generate(p.private_key, p.public_key)
    ret p
end

func session_key(me: Party, peer_public: str, salt: str): str:
    mut ok := false
    shared := tls.EcdhP256Shared(me.private_key, peer_public, ok)
    ret tls.HkdfSha256(shared, salt, "notes app v1 session", 32, ok)
end

func main:
    alice := new_party()
    bob := new_party()
    salt := tls.RandomSalt(16)

    alice_key := session_key(alice, bob.public_key, salt)
    bob_key := session_key(bob, alice.public_key, salt)
    println "both sides derived the same key:", alice_key == bob_key

    mut ok := false
    wire := tls.AesGcmSeal(alice_key, tls.GcmNonce(0), "meet at the station at nine", ok)
    println "alice sent", wire.len(), "base64 characters"
    println "bob reads:", tls.AesGcmOpen(bob_key, tls.GcmNonce(0), wire, ok)

    eve := new_party()
    eve_key := session_key(eve, alice.public_key, salt)
    _ := tls.AesGcmOpen(eve_key, tls.GcmNonce(0), wire, ok)
    println "eve, with only the public keys, can read it:", ok
end
```

Output:

```text
both sides derived the same key: true
alice sent 60 base64 characters
bob reads: meet at the station at nine
eve, with only the public keys, can read it: false
```

ECDH alone does not tell you who is on the other side. In a real protocol, sign the public key, or check it against one you already know, or someone in the middle can make a key with each side.

## Sign and verify with P-256

`P256Sign` signs a SHA-256 digest with a private key, and anyone with the public point can check it with `P256Verify`. It suits licence files, update manifests and messages that must be checked by many readers but written by one. The signature follows RFC 6979, so the same key and digest always give the same signature and no random number generator is involved.

tls-signed-license.salam

```salam
import tls
import crypto
import encoding
import mem

func digest_of(text: str): str:
    out := mem.Allocate(32 as u64)
    crypto.Sha256Bytes(text as void*, text.len(), out)
    d := encoding.Base64EncodeBytes(out, 32)
    mem.Free(out)
    ret d
end

func main:
    vendor_private := "cqXpGz8zHwUzjEQonZMVMh4K9+jyX3zMfzeFP0025Rk="
    vendor_public := tls.EcdhP256PublicPoint(vendor_private)

    license := "customer=Pars Co;seats=25;until=2027-12-31"
    mut ok := false
    signature := tls.P256Sign(vendor_private, digest_of(license), ok)
    println "signed:", ok
    println "signature:", signature

    println "genuine license:", tls.P256Verify(vendor_public, digest_of(license), signature)
    edited := "customer=Pars Co;seats=250;until=2027-12-31"
    println "seats edited:", tls.P256Verify(vendor_public, digest_of(edited), signature)
    println "same signature again:", tls.P256Sign(vendor_private, digest_of(license), ok) == signature
end
```

Output:

```text
signed: true
signature: Z9NSfoPJN31QJ2ELmSVzzziGYOZrA/+elf2AUQXUjx4uBr0U+Pyx7HxCt/gsuGacDKrD0KcJ6g1KkSOOjI1Hlg==
genuine license: true
seats edited: false
same signature again: true
```

The private key in the program is there so that the output stays the same. Keep a real one out of the source code: read it from a file or the environment, and ship only the public point with the program that checks.

## Which function for which job

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| An HTTPS or other TLS client | `NewConfig`, `Dial`, `Write`, `Read`, `Close`; for plain web requests, net/http does this for you |
| A TLS server | `NewServerConfig`, then `WrapServer` on each accepted socket |
| Upgrade a socket that is already open (STARTTLS) | `WrapClient` |
| Encrypt data at rest | `AesGcmSeal`, `AesGcmOpen`, `GcmNonce` |
| Agree on a key | `EcdhP256Generate`, `EcdhP256Shared`, `HkdfSha256` |
| Sign and verify | `P256Sign`, `P256Verify` |
| Check a certificate yourself | `LoadRoots`, `VerifyCert`, `VerifyError` |

## Types

### `Config`

```salam
struct Config
```

The client configuration.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server_name` | `str = ""` | The hostname for SNI and for certificate verification. |
| `ca_file` | `str = ""` | The file of root certificates; empty means the system roots. |
| `insecure_skip_verify` | `bool = false` | Do not verify the certificate; for testing only, since it leaves the connection open to eavesdropping. |
| `alpn` | `str = ""` | The protocol for ALPN, such as `h2`. |
| `aes_only` | `bool = false` | Offer AES ciphers only. |

tls-Client.salam

```salam
import tls

func main:
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("example.com")
    cfg.alpn = "http/1.1"
    mut conn := tls.Dial("example.com", 443, cfg)
    if not tls.ConnOk(conn):
        println "error:", tls.ConnError(conn)
        ret
    end
    println tls.Version(conn), tls.CipherName(conn), tls.PeerCertCount(conn)
    _ := tls.Write(conn, "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
    mut body := ""
    until tls.ConnOk(conn):
        chunk := tls.Read(conn, 4096)
        if chunk.len() == 0:
            break
        end
        body += chunk
    end
    println body.len() > 0
    tls.Close(conn)
end
```

### `Conn`

```salam
struct Conn
```

One TLS connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `h` | `Handshake` | The handshake state. |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `open` | `bool = false` | The connection is open. |
| `insecure` | `bool = false` | Without certificate verification. |
| `pending` | `Buf` | Data that has been read but not taken yet. |
| `err` | `str = ""` | The error message. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: tls-Client.salam

### `ServerConfig`

```salam
struct ServerConfig
```

The server configuration: the certificate chain and the private key.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chain` | `Roots` | The certificate chain. |
| `key` | `PrivateKey` | The private key. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Both were read. |

tls-Server.salam

```salam
import tls
import net.tcp
import mem

func main:
    cfg := tls.NewServerConfig("cert.pem", "key.pem")
    if not cfg.ok:
        println "the certificate or key could not be read"
        ret
    end
    server := tcp.Bind(8443)
    until true:
        sock := tcp.Accept(server)
        mut conn := tls.WrapServer(sock.fd, cfg)
        if tls.ConnOk(conn):
            if tls.Readable(conn) or tls.Pending(conn) > 0:
                println tls.Read(conn, 1024)
            end
            buffer := mem.Allocate(256 as u64)
            n := tls.ReadBytes(conn, buffer, 256)
            _ := tls.WriteBytes(conn, buffer, n)
            _ := tls.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello")
            mem.Free(buffer)
            println tls.Fd(conn) >= 0
        end
        tls.Close(conn)
    end
end
```

## Constants and variables

### `TLS10`

```salam
const TLS10: i32 = 769
```

The version number of TLS 1.0; not supported.

tls-Certs.salam

```salam
import tls
import net.tcp
import encoding
import io

func main:
    roots := tls.LoadRoots("/etc/ssl/cert.pem")
    println tls.RootCount(roots)

    chain := tls.LoadCertChainFile("cert.pem")
    println tls.RootCount(chain)
    mut key := tls.LoadPrivateKeyFile("key.pem")
    mut key2 := tls.ParsePrivateKeyPEM("-----BEGIN ...")
    tls.FreePrivateKey(key2)

    cert := tls.HexDecodeBuf("3082...")
    println tls.CertIsValid(cert), tls.CertSubjectCN(cert)
    code := tls.VerifyCert(cert, roots, "example.com")
    println code, tls.VerifyError(code)

    digest := tls.HashDigest(false, "message")
    sig := tls.NewBuf(512)
    println tls.SignRSAPKCS1(key, false, digest, sig)
    println tls.SignRSAPSS(key, false, digest, sig)
    println tls.VerifyRSAPSSWithKey(key, false, digest, sig)
    r := tls.NewBuf(32)
    s := tls.NewBuf(32)
    if tls.SignECDSA(key, digest, r, s):
        der := tls.ECDSADerEncode(r, s, 32)
        println tls.VerifyECDSADERWithKey(key, digest, der)
    end

    pem := io.ReadFile("rsa-key.pem")
    mut good := false
    println tls.RsaKeyBits(pem)
    println tls.RsaSignPkcs1Sha256(pem, encoding.Base64Encode("..."), good)

    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("internal.example")
    cfg.ca_file = "company-ca.pem"
    cfg.aes_only = true
    mut conn := tls.Dial("internal.example", 443, cfg)
    println tls.ConnOk(conn)
    tls.Close(conn)
    sock := tcp.Dial("example.com", 443)
    mut conn2 := tls.WrapClient(sock.fd, tls.NewConfig("example.com"))
    println tls.Version(conn2) == "TLS1.3"
    tls.Close(conn2)
    println tls.TLS10, tls.TLS11, tls.TLS12, tls.TLS13
    println tls.SelfTest()
    tls.FreeRoots(roots)
    tls.FreePrivateKey(key)
end
```

### `EcdhP256Generate`

```salam
func EcdhP256Generate(priv &: str, pub_spki &: str): bool
```

An ECDH key pair on the P-256 curve: the private key as base64 and the SPKI public key as base64.

tls-Crypto.salam

```salam
import tls
import encoding

func main:
    mut priv1 := ""
    mut pub1 := ""
    mut priv2 := ""
    mut pub2 := ""
    println tls.EcdhP256Generate(priv1, pub1), tls.EcdhP256Generate(priv2, pub2)
    mut good := false
    secret1 := tls.EcdhP256Shared(priv1, pub2, good)
    secret2 := tls.EcdhP256Shared(priv2, pub1, good)
    println good, secret1 == secret2

    point1 := tls.EcdhP256PublicPoint(priv1)
    point2 := tls.EcdhP256PublicPoint(priv2)
    println tls.EcdhP256SharedPoint(priv1, point2, good) == tls.EcdhP256SharedPoint(priv2, point1, good)

    salt := tls.RandomSalt(16)
    key := tls.HkdfSha256(secret1, salt, "chat v1", 32, good)
    println good, key == tls.HkdfSha256(secret2, salt, "chat v1", 32, good)
    println tls.HkdfSha256Raw(secret1, salt, encoding.Base64Encode("chat v1"), 32, good) == key

    nonce := tls.GcmNonce(0)
    sealed := tls.AesGcmSeal(key, nonce, "hello, this message is encrypted", good)
    println good
    println tls.AesGcmOpen(key, nonce, sealed, good), good
    _ := tls.AesGcmOpen(key, tls.GcmNonce(1), sealed, good)
    println good
    binary := tls.AesGcmSealBytes(key, nonce, encoding.Base64Encode("abc"), good)
    println encoding.Base64Decode(tls.AesGcmOpenBytes(key, nonce, binary, good))

    digest := encoding.Base64Encode("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
    sig := tls.P256Sign(priv1, digest, good)
    println good, tls.P256Verify(point1, digest, sig), tls.P256Verify(point2, digest, sig)

    b := tls.HashDigest(false, "abc")
    println tls.BufLen(b), tls.HexEncodeBuf(b)
    mut hex := tls.HexDecodeBuf("cafe")
    tls.BufAppendStr(hex, "!")
    println tls.BufLen(hex), tls.HexEncodeBuf(hex)
    mut zeros := tls.NewZeroBuf(4)
    println tls.HexEncodeBuf(zeros)
    mut empty := tls.NewBuf(64)
    println tls.BufLen(empty)
    tls.WipeBuf(hex)
    tls.FreeBuf(hex)
    tls.FreeBuf(zeros)
    tls.FreeBuf(empty)
end
```

Output:

```text
true true
true true
true
true true
true
true
hello, this message is encrypted true
false
abc
true true false
32 ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
3 cafe21
00000000
0
```

# ssl

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ssl/

A familiar OpenSSL style interface for secure connections, on top of Salam's own TLS.

This package gives an OpenSSL style context and connection interface (`SSL_CTX`, `SSL_connect`, `SSL_read` and friends, under Salam names), but underneath it is Salam's own tls and it needs no outside library. Use it when you port C code written against OpenSSL, or when you like that split between a shared context and many connections. For new code tls is shorter, and for web requests net/http does all of it for you.

The flow: make one context, hand each TCP socket to it with `Wrap`, for a client set the hostname and call `Connect` (a server calls `Accept`), then `Read` and `Write`. Things to know:

- A client context checks certificates against the system roots from the start, with TLS 1.2 as the minimum. `LoadVerifyLocationsFile` replaces the system roots with your file; `SetDefaultVerifyPaths` switches back.

- `SetHostname` is required before `Connect` while verification is on; without it the handshake is refused.

- `Shutdown` and `Close` do not close the socket. As in OpenSSL, the TCP connection you wrapped is yours; close it with net/tcp afterwards.

- `SetMinVersion(ctx, TLS1_3)` is checked after the handshake: a server that only offers 1.2 is connected and then refused. `Read` returns a `str`, which stops at a zero byte.

## A complete client

The steps are always the same: one context for the whole program, then for each connection a TCP socket, `Wrap`, `SetHostname` and `Connect`. A context made with `NewClientContext` already trusts the system roots and stops the handshake when the check fails; the calls to `SetDefaultVerifyPaths` and `SetVerify(ctx, VERIFY_PEER)` in the program only make that explicit, the way OpenSSL code usually reads. `Read` returns an empty string when the server closes the connection, which is the end of a `Connection: close` response.

ssl-fetch-page.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp
import str

func fetch(ctx: ssl.Context, host: str, path: str): str:
    sock := tcp.Dial(host, 443)
    if not tcp.ConnOk(sock):
        ret "could not reach " + host
    end
    conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
    _ := ssl.SetHostname(conn, host)
    if not ssl.Connect(conn):
        msg := ssl.ConnErrorString(conn)
        ssl.Close(conn)
        tcp.Close(sock)
        ret "handshake failed: " + msg
    end
    _ := ssl.Write(conn, "GET " + path + " HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: " + host + "\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
    mut response := ""
    until true:
        chunk := ssl.Read(conn, 16384)
        if chunk.len() == 0:
            break
        end
        response += chunk
    end
    ssl.Shutdown(conn)
    ssl.Close(conn)
    tcp.Close(sock)
    ret str.Split(response, "\r\n").get(0)
end

func main:
    ctx := ssl.NewClientContext()
    _ := ssl.SetDefaultVerifyPaths(ctx)
    _ := ssl.SetMinVersion(ctx, ssl.TLS1_2)
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_PEER)
    println fetch(ctx, "example.com", "/")
    println fetch(ctx, "expired.badssl.com", "/")
    ssl.CloseContext(ctx)
end
```

It needs network access, so it is only checked here. Run against the real hosts, it printed:

```salam
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
handshake failed: certificate verification failed: certificate expired
```

## Trusting only your own certificate authority

Services inside a company often use certificates from a private CA. Load that CA with `LoadVerifyLocationsFile` instead of the system roots: the client then accepts only servers whose certificate your CA signed, which is stricter than the public web. `SetMinVersion(ctx, TLS1_3)` refuses anything older than TLS 1.3, and after the handshake `PeerVerified` and `VerifyResult` tell you how the check went.

ssl-private-ca.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp

func main:
    ctx := ssl.NewClientContext()
    if not ssl.LoadVerifyLocationsFile(ctx, "/etc/company/ca.pem"):
        println "cannot read the company CA:", ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret 1
    end
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_PEER)
    _ := ssl.SetMinVersion(ctx, ssl.TLS1_3)

    sock := tcp.Dial("billing.internal", 8443)
    conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
    _ := ssl.SetHostname(conn, "billing.internal")
    ok := ssl.Connect(conn)
    if not ok or not ssl.PeerVerified(conn):
        println "refusing the server, verify result", ssl.VerifyResult(conn), ssl.ConnErrorString(conn)
        ssl.Close(conn)
        tcp.Close(sock)
        ret 1
    end
    _ := ssl.Write(conn, "PING\n")
    println "server said:", ssl.Read(conn, 1024)
    ssl.Shutdown(conn)
    ssl.Close(conn)
    tcp.Close(sock)
    ssl.CloseContext(ctx)
    ret 0
end
```

`VerifyResult` is `CERT_OK` (zero) when the certificate was accepted. Keep the CA file readable by the program but not writable, since anyone who can replace it can impersonate your servers.

## STARTTLS: encrypt a connection that is already open

Mail, IMAP, XMPP and some database protocols start in plain text and switch to TLS on the same connection when the client asks. This is why `Wrap` takes a socket descriptor rather than a host: talk to the server with net/tcp until it agrees, then wrap the very same `fd` and carry on through `ssl.Read` and `ssl.Write`.

ssl-starttls.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp
import str

func say(sock: tcp.Conn, line: str): str:
    _ := tcp.Write(sock, line + "\r\n")
    ret tcp.Read(sock, 4096)
end

func main:
    sock := tcp.Dial("smtp.gmail.com", 587)
    greeting := tcp.Read(sock, 4096)
    println "plain:", str.Split(greeting, "\r\n").get(0)
    _ := say(sock, "EHLO client.example.com")
    reply := say(sock, "STARTTLS")
    if not str.StartsWith(reply, "220"):
        println "no STARTTLS:", reply
        tcp.Close(sock)
        ret 1
    end

    ctx := ssl.NewClientContext()
    _ := ssl.SetDefaultVerifyPaths(ctx)
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_PEER)
    conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
    _ := ssl.SetHostname(conn, "smtp.gmail.com")
    if not ssl.Connect(conn):
        println "handshake failed:", ssl.ConnErrorString(conn)
        ret 1
    end
    _ := ssl.Write(conn, "EHLO client.example.com\r\n")
    println "encrypted:", str.Split(ssl.Read(conn, 4096), "\r\n").get(0)
    _ := ssl.Write(conn, "QUIT\r\n")
    ssl.Shutdown(conn)
    ssl.Close(conn)
    tcp.Close(sock)
    ssl.CloseContext(ctx)
    ret 0
end
```

Against Gmail's submission port it printed the server's greeting in plain text and then its first encrypted reply; the ids at the end of each line change with every run:

```salam
plain: 220 smtp.gmail.com ESMTP ... - gsmtp
encrypted: 250-smtp.gmail.com at your service, [...]
```

A real mail client should check every reply code, not only the one for STARTTLS, and should send `EHLO` again after the switch, as the program does, because the server forgets everything it was told in plain text.

## When something fails

There are three places to look. `LastErrorString` describes the last failure that has no connection yet, such as a context that could not read its certificate. `ConnErrorString` describes what went wrong on one connection, for example a failed certificate check. And when `Read` or `Write` returns zero or less, `ErrorCode(conn, n)` tells a clean close by the other side apart from a protocol or socket error, the same split OpenSSL's `SSL_get_error` makes.

## Types

### `Context`

```salam
struct Context
```

A TLS context, shared between connections.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The pointer to the context state. |

ssl-Client.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp

func main:
    ctx := ssl.NewClientContext()
    if not ssl.CtxOk(ctx):
        println ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret
    end
    _ := ssl.SetMinVersion(ctx, ssl.TLS1_3)
    _ := ssl.SetDefaultVerifyPaths(ctx)
    sock := tcp.Dial("example.com", 443)
    conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
    _ := ssl.SetHostname(conn, "example.com")
    if not ssl.ConnOk(conn) or not ssl.Connect(conn):
        println "the handshake failed:", ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret
    end
    println ssl.PeerVerified(conn), ssl.VerifyResult(conn) == ssl.CERT_OK
    n := ssl.Write(conn, "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
    if n <= 0:
        println "error code:", ssl.ErrorCode(conn, n)
    end
    println ssl.Read(conn, 4096).len() > 0
    ssl.Shutdown(conn)
    ssl.Close(conn)
    ssl.CloseContext(ctx)
    tcp.Close(sock)
end
```

### `VERIFY_NONE`

ssl-Server.salam

```salam
import ssl
import net.tcp

func main:
    ctx := ssl.NewServerContext("cert.pem", "key.pem")
    if not ssl.CtxOk(ctx):
        println ssl.LastErrorString()
        ret
    end
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_NONE)
    _ := ssl.LoadVerifyLocationsFile(ctx, "clients-ca.pem")
    ssl.SetVerify(ctx, ssl.VERIFY_PEER)
    println ssl.FILETYPE_PEM, ssl.TLS1_2
    server := tcp.Bind(8443)
    until true:
        sock := tcp.Accept(server)
        conn := ssl.Wrap(ctx, sock.fd)
        if ssl.Accept(conn):
            request := ssl.Read(conn, 4096)
            _ := ssl.Write(conn, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: " + request.len() + "\r\n\r\n" + request)
        end
        ssl.Close(conn)
    end
end
```

### `VERIFY_PEER`

```salam

```

Verification mode: verify the certificate of the other side.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ssl-Server.salam

# ssh

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ssh/

SSH connections, running a command on a server, and working with files over SFTP.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add ssh`

This package is an SSH client written in Salam and needs neither OpenSSH nor any other library. Make a `Config` with the host and the user, pick the login method, and connect with `Connect`; then run a command with `Exec`, or move files with `SftpOpen`. It suits automating deployments, backups and checks across a fleet of servers. It is a client only; for plain file transfer with an FTP server see ftp.

The host key is checked against the known_hosts file, the way `ssh` itself does. The buffer and reader functions build and read the data format of the SSH protocol; an ordinary program does not need them.

What it supports, and what it does not:

- Keys must be RSA, in the OpenSSH format, without a passphrase. Ed25519 and ECDSA keys, the default of recent `ssh-keygen`, are not read. Make a key for automation with `ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -N "" -f deploy_key`; a password login with `WithPassword` also works.

- The server needs an RSA host key; a server that offers only Ed25519 or ECDSA host keys cannot be checked and the connection fails.

- Key exchange is curve25519 or Diffie-Hellman group 14, and the ciphers are `aes128-ctr` and `aes256-ctr`, which every OpenSSH server accepts. There is no agent support and no port forwarding; an interactive shell with a terminal is available through `NewSession`, `RequestPty` and `Shell`.

- Each `Exec` is a fresh shell: a `cd` or an exported variable does not carry over to the next call.

## Run a deployment, step by step

`Exec` runs one command and waits for it, returning its standard output, its standard error and the exit code in an `ExecResult`. Each call opens a new channel, so a `cd` in one command does not carry over to the next; join commands with `&&` when they belong together. A deployment is then a list of steps that stops at the first one whose exit code is not zero.

ssh-deploy.salam

```salam
import ssh
import str

func run_steps(client &: ssh.Client, steps: Vector<str>): bool:
    each step in steps:
        r := ssh.Exec(client, step)
        if not r.ok or r.exit_code != 0:
            println "FAILED:", step
            println str.Trim(r.stderr)
            ret false
        end
        println "ok:", step
    end
    ret true
end

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("app1.example.com", ssh.DefaultPort, "deploy")
    if not ssh.WithKeyFile(cfg, "/home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa"):
        println "cannot read the key file"
        ret 1
    end
    ssh.WithHostKeyMode(cfg, ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT)
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    if not ssh.Ok(client):
        println "connect failed:", ssh.Error(client)
        ret 1
    end

    mut steps := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    steps.push("cd /srv/app && git fetch --quiet && git checkout --quiet v2.4.0")
    steps.push("cd /srv/app && ./salam build --release")
    steps.push("sudo systemctl restart app")
    steps.push("systemctl is-active app")
    done := run_steps(client, steps)
    ssh.Close(client)
    if not done:
        ret 1
    end
    ret 0
end
```

This needs a real server, so it is only checked here. `WithKeyFile` only reads the file, so it returns false when the path is wrong; a key the package cannot use makes `Connect` fail instead. For a command that runs for a long time and whose output you want as it comes, such as `tail -f`, use `NewSession`, `Start` and `ReadStep` with `DrainOutput` instead, as the example in the reference shows.

## Pull a backup over SFTP

SSH and SFTP share one connection: run the command that writes the file with `Exec`, then open SFTP on the same client and fetch it. `Stat` gives the size, `Download` copies the file, and `Remove` cleans up on the server once the copy has arrived. For whole directories there are `UploadDir`, `DownloadDir` and `MkdirAll`.

ssh-backup.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("db.example.com", 22, "backup")
    _ := ssh.WithKeyFile(cfg, "/home/backup/.ssh/id_rsa")
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    if not ssh.Ok(client):
        println "connect failed:", ssh.Error(client)
        ret 1
    end

    remote := "/tmp/shop-backup.sql.gz"
    dump := ssh.Exec(client, "pg_dump shop | gzip > " + remote)
    if dump.exit_code != 0:
        println "pg_dump failed:", dump.stderr
        ssh.Close(client)
        ret 1
    end

    mut sftp := ssh.SftpOpen(client)
    info := ssh.Stat(client, sftp, remote)
    println "dump size on the server:", info.size, "bytes"
    if ssh.Download(client, sftp, remote, "shop-backup.sql.gz"):
        println "downloaded"
        _ := ssh.Remove(client, sftp, remote)
    else:
        println "download failed:", ssh.Error(client)
    end
    ssh.SftpClose(client, sftp)
    ssh.Close(client)
    ret 0
end
```

## Host keys and known_hosts

The host key is how the client knows it is talking to the right machine and not to someone in between. The mode decides what happens with a key that is not in known_hosts yet. `HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT` refuses it, which is right for automation: add the key once by hand, then every later change is an error you want to hear about. `HOSTKEY_MODE_ACCEPT_NEW` is the default; it records a new key the first time and refuses a changed one later, like `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` in OpenSSH. `HOSTKEY_MODE_INSECURE` checks nothing and belongs only in tests.

ssh-host-keys.salam

```salam
import ssh

func try(mode: int, label: str):
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("new-server.example.com", 22, "admin")
    ssh.WithPassword(cfg, "first-login-password")
    ssh.WithKnownHostsPath(cfg, "known_hosts")
    ssh.WithHostKeyMode(cfg, mode)
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    if ssh.Ok(client):
        println label, "connected, host key", ssh.HostKeyFingerprint(client)
        ssh.Close(client)
    else:
        println label, "refused:", ssh.Error(client)
    end
end

func main:
    try(ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT, "strict, empty known_hosts:")
    try(ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_ACCEPT_NEW, "accept-new, first time:")
    try(ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT, "strict, key now recorded:")
end
```

With an empty known_hosts the first, strict attempt is refused, the second records the key, and the third, strict again, now connects. `HostKeyFingerprint` returns the same SHA-256 fingerprint that `ssh-keygen -lf` prints, so you can compare it with what the server's administrator gave you. The client checks the server's RSA host key (`rsa-sha2-256`, `rsa-sha2-512` or `ssh-rsa`), so the server needs one; a default OpenSSH install usually has it.

## Many hosts from one list

A `Config` is a plain value, so it is easy to build one per line of an inventory and keep the same rules for all of them: the same user, the same known_hosts file and strict checking. Nothing connects until `Connect` is called, so the program below runs without a network.

ssh-inventory.salam

```salam
import ssh
import str
import conv

func parse(line: str): ssh.Config:
    fields := str.Split(line, " ")
    mut port := ssh.DefaultPort
    mut host := fields.get(0)
    if str.Contains(host, ":"):
        parts := str.Split(host, ":")
        host = parts.get(0)
        port = conv.Atoi(parts.get(1))
    end
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig(host, port, fields.get(1))
    ssh.WithHostKeyMode(cfg, ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT)
    ssh.WithKnownHostsPath(cfg, "/etc/deploy/known_hosts")
    ret cfg
end

func main:
    inventory := "web1.example.com deploy\nweb2.example.com deploy\nbastion.example.com:2222 ops"
    each line in str.Split(inventory, "\n"):
        cfg := parse(line)
        println cfg.user + "@" + cfg.host, "port", cfg.port, "strict:", cfg.hostkey_mode == ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
deploy@web1.example.com port 22 strict: true
deploy@web2.example.com port 22 strict: true
ops@bastion.example.com port 2222 strict: true
```

To run the same command on all hosts, loop over the configs, connect, `Exec` and `Close`. If one host is down, `Ok` is false for that client and `Error` says why, and the loop can go on to the next.

## Types

### `Config`

```salam
struct Config
```

The configuration of an SSH connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 22` | The port; 22 by default. |
| `user` | `str = ""` | The user name. |
| `password` | `str = ""` | The password. |
| `use_password` | `bool = false` | Log in with a password. |
| `key_pem` | `str = ""` | The private key as text. |
| `use_key` | `bool = false` | Log in with a key. |
| `hostkey_mode` | `int = 1` | The host key check mode. |
| `known_hosts_path` | `str = ""` | The path of the known_hosts file. |

ssh-Config.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("example.com", ssh.DefaultPort, "deploy")
    println cfg.host, cfg.port, cfg.user, cfg.hostkey_mode == ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_ACCEPT_NEW
    ssh.WithPassword(cfg, "s3cret")
    println cfg.use_password, cfg.use_key
    ssh.WithKeyPEM(cfg, "-----BEGIN OPENSSH KEY-----")
    println cfg.use_key, cfg.key_pem.len() > 0
    println ssh.WithKeyFile(cfg, "/nonexistent/id_rsa")
    ssh.WithHostKeyMode(cfg, ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_STRICT)
    ssh.WithKnownHostsPath(cfg, "/home/deploy/.ssh/known_hosts")
    println cfg.hostkey_mode, cfg.known_hosts_path
    println ssh.HOSTKEY_MODE_INSECURE, ssh.ClientVersion
end
```

Output:

```text
example.com 22 deploy true
true false
true true
false
2 /home/deploy/.ssh/known_hosts
0 SSH-2.0-Salam_1.0
```

### `Session`

```salam
struct Session
```

One session over the connection: one command or one shell.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ch` | `Channel` | The SSH channel. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The session opened. |

ssh-Exec.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("server.example.com", 22, "deploy")
    _ := ssh.WithKeyFile(cfg, "/home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa")
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    if not ssh.Ok(client):
        println "error:", ssh.Error(client)
        ret
    end
    println "host key:", ssh.HostKeyFingerprint(client)

    r := ssh.Exec(client, "uname -a")
    println r.ok, r.exit_code, r.stdout, r.stderr
    r2 := ssh.RunCommand(client, "df -h /")
    println r2.stdout

    mut tail := ssh.NewSession(client)
    _ := ssh.RequestPty(tail, client, "xterm", 120, 40)
    if ssh.Start(tail, client, "tail -f /var/log/app.log"):
        repeat 10:
            _ := ssh.ReadStep(tail, client)
            print ssh.DrainOutput(tail)
            print ssh.DrainStderrOutput(tail)
        end
    end
    ssh.CloseSession(tail, client)

    mut shell := ssh.NewSession(client)
    if ssh.Shell(shell, client):
        _ := ssh.WriteInput(shell, client, "echo hello\nexit\n")
        ssh.CloseInput(shell, client)
        code := ssh.Wait(shell, client)
        println code, ssh.ExitCode(shell), ssh.SessionClosed(shell)
        println ssh.Output(shell), ssh.StderrOutput(shell)
    end
    ssh.CloseSession(shell, client)

    probe := ssh.Dial(cfg)
    println ssh.Ok(probe)
    println ssh.Reconnect(client)
    println ssh.SelfTest()
    ssh.Close(client)
end
```

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: ssh-Exec.salam

### `Sftp`

```salam
struct Sftp
```

An SFTP session for working with the files on the server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ch` | `Channel` | The channel. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It opened. |
| `next_id` | `u32 = 1` | The number of the next request. |

ssh-Sftp.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut cfg := ssh.NewConfig("files.example.com", 22, "ali")
    ssh.WithPassword(cfg, "s3cret")
    mut client := ssh.Connect(cfg)
    mut sftp := ssh.SftpOpen(client)
    if not sftp.ok:
        println ssh.Error(client)
        ret
    end
    println ssh.MkdirAll(client, sftp, "/backup/2026/09")
    println ssh.Upload(client, sftp, "report.pdf", "/backup/2026/09/report.pdf")
    println ssh.UploadDir(client, sftp, "site", "/var/www/site")
    if ssh.Exists(client, sftp, "/backup/2026/09/report.pdf"):
        info := ssh.Stat(client, sftp, "/backup/2026/09/report.pdf")
        println info.name, info.size, info.is_dir, info.permissions
    end
    each info in ssh.ListDir(client, sftp, "/backup"):
        println info.name, info.is_dir
    end
    println ssh.IsLink(client, sftp, "/current"), ssh.Lstat(client, sftp, "/current").name
    _ := ssh.Download(client, sftp, "/etc/hostname", "hostname.txt")
    _ := ssh.DownloadDir(client, sftp, "/var/log/app", "logs")
    _ := ssh.Rename(client, sftp, "/tmp/a", "/tmp/b")
    _ := ssh.Remove(client, sftp, "/tmp/b")
    _ := ssh.Mkdir(client, sftp, "/tmp/x")
    _ := ssh.Rmdir(client, sftp, "/tmp/x")
    _ := ssh.RemoveAll(client, sftp, "/tmp/old")
    ssh.SftpClose(client, sftp)
    ssh.Close(client)
end
```

### `Output`


### `NewBuf`

```salam
func NewBuf(cap0: int): Buf
```

An empty buffer for building SSH protocol messages.

ssh-Wire.salam

```salam
import ssh

func main:
    mut b := ssh.NewBuf(64)
    ssh.BufPutByte(b, 20)
    ssh.BufPutUint32(b, 7 as u32)
    ssh.BufPutUint64(b, 9 as u64)
    ssh.BufPutBool(b, true)
    ssh.BufPutStringStr(b, "ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-256")
    ssh.BufPutString(b, "abc" as void*, 3)
    ssh.BufPutBytes(b, "xy" as void*, 2)
    ssh.BufPutZeros(b, 2)
    ssh.BufPutMpintBytes(b, "\x80" as void*, 1)
    println b.len

    mut r := ssh.ReaderFromBuf(b)
    println ssh.RGetByte(r), ssh.RGetUint32(r), ssh.RGetUint64(r), ssh.RGetBool(r)
    names := ssh.RGetNameList(r)
    println names, ssh.NameListContains(names, "rsa-sha2-256")
    println ssh.RGetStringAsStr(r)
    ssh.RSkip(r, 4)
    println ssh.RRemaining(r)
    n := ssh.RGetMpintView(r)
    println n.len, ssh.RRemaining(r)

    println ssh.NegotiateFirstMatch("aes256-ctr,aes128-ctr", "aes128-ctr,aes256-ctr")
    println ssh.ConstantTimeEqual("abcd" as void*, "abcd" as void*, 4), ssh.ConstantTimeEqual("abcd" as void*, "abce" as void*, 4)

    mut b2 := ssh.NewBuf(16)
    ssh.BufPutStringBuf(b2, b)
    ssh.BufPutMpintBuf(b2, b)
    ssh.BufPutBuf(b2, b)
    mut r2 := ssh.NewReader(b2.p, b2.len)
    view := ssh.RGetStringView(r2)
    println view.len == b.len
    mut copied := ssh.RGetStringCopy(ssh.ReaderFromBuf(b2))
    mut number := ssh.RGetMpintCopy(r2)
    println copied.len, number.len, ssh.RRemaining(r2)
    ssh.WipeBuf(b)
    ssh.FreeBuf(b)
    ssh.FreeBuf(b2)
    ssh.FreeBuf(copied)
    ssh.FreeBuf(number)
end
```

Output:

```text
59
20 7 9 true
ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-256 true
abc
6
1 0
aes256-ctr
true false
true
59 59 59
```

# ftp

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/ftp/

An FTP and FTPS client: listing a directory, uploading and downloading files.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add ftp`

This package connects to FTP servers, for uploading a site to shared hosting or pulling files off old equipment and suppliers' servers. Plain FTP sends the password and the data unencrypted; wherever the server supports it, use `DialTLS`, which encrypts both the commands and the data with AUTH TLS. When the server also speaks SSH, SFTP through ssh is the better choice: one encrypted connection, no separate data channel.

Transfers go in passive mode (EPSV, or PASV when the server lacks it), which works from behind a firewall; active mode (`PORT`) is not offered. The parsing functions, such as `ParseListLine`, are available for writing tools of your own too.

Things to know:

- Call `Binary` before transfers, or a server in ASCII mode may change line endings inside images and archives.

- `Upload` and `Download` hold the whole file in memory, and an interrupted transfer starts again from the beginning; there is no resume. Fine for site files and reports, not for multi-gigabyte backups.

- `Read`, `Write` and `Append` carry a `str`, so they are for text: binary content stops at the first zero byte. Use `Upload` and `Download` for anything else.

- Servers that require TLS session reuse on the data connection refuse every transfer; see the last section.

## Publish a site to shared hosting

The usual job: connect with `DialTLS`, refuse to go on unless both the commands and the data are encrypted, log in, and upload a build directory with `UploadDir`. Switch to binary mode with `Binary` before any transfer, or some servers will change the line endings inside images and archives. Keeping the old `index.html` under another name with `Rename` gives you something to go back to.

ftp-publish-site.salam

```salam
import ftp

func main:
    mut c := ftp.DialTLS("ftp.example-host.com", 21)
    if not ftp.Ok(c):
        println "cannot connect:", ftp.LastReply(c)
        ret 1
    end
    if not ftp.Secure(c) or not ftp.SecureData(c):
        println "the server would not encrypt the session, stopping"
        ftp.Close(c)
        ret 1
    end
    if not ftp.Login(c, "site-user", "app-password"):
        println "login failed:", ftp.LastCode(c), ftp.LastReply(c)
        ftp.Close(c)
        ret 1
    end
    _ := ftp.Binary(c)
    _ := ftp.MkdirAll(c, "/public_html")
    if ftp.Exists(c, "/public_html/index.html"):
        _ := ftp.Rename(c, "/public_html/index.html", "/public_html/index.old.html")
    end
    if not ftp.UploadDir(c, "dist", "/public_html"):
        println "upload failed:", ftp.LastReply(c)
        ret 1
    end
    println "uploaded, index.html is", ftp.Size(c, "/public_html/index.html"), "bytes"
    ftp.Quit(c)
    ftp.Close(c)
    ret 0
end
```

This needs a real server, so it is only checked here. Every function that talks to the server leaves the reply in `LastCode` and `LastReply`, so after a `false` you can always print what the server said.

## Fetch only the new files

`List` returns one `FileInfo` per entry with the name, the size and whether it is a directory or a link. Comparing that with what is already on disk turns a full download into a cheap sync, which suits a nightly job that collects reports from a supplier.

ftp-sync-down.salam

```salam
import ftp
import os

func main:
    mut c := ftp.DialTLS("files.example.com", 21)
    if not ftp.Ok(c) or not ftp.Login(c, "reports", "app-password"):
        println "cannot log in:", ftp.LastReply(c)
        ret 1
    end
    _ := ftp.Binary(c)
    _ := os.MkdirAll("reports")
    mut fetched := 0
    mut skipped := 0
    each f in ftp.List(c, "/daily"):
        if f.is_dir or f.is_link:
            continue
        end
        local := "reports/" + f.name
        if os.Exists(local):
            skipped += 1
            continue
        end
        if ftp.Download(c, "/daily/" + f.name, local):
            fetched += 1
        else:
            println "failed:", f.name, ftp.LastReply(c)
        end
    end
    println "fetched", fetched, "new files, skipped", skipped
    ftp.Quit(c)
    ftp.Close(c)
    ret 0
end
```

For a stricter check than "the file exists", compare `f.size` with the local size, or `ModTime` with the time you stored after the last run.

## Read a directory listing yourself

FTP has no fixed format for listings; most servers send the same columns as `ls -l`. `ParseListLine` reads such a line into a `FileInfo`, which is useful when you get listings from somewhere else, such as a log or a `ListRaw` call, and want to work with them without a connection.

ftp-listing-report.salam

```salam
import ftp
import str

func main:
    raw := "drwxr-xr-x    2 ftp ftp     4096 Jan 01  2026 old\n-rw-r--r--    1 ftp ftp   120034 Oct 02 08:10 sales-2026-10-01.csv\n-rw-r--r--    1 ftp ftp   118702 Oct 03 08:10 sales-2026-10-02.csv\n-rw-r--r--    1 ftp ftp  2251800 Oct 03 08:12 photos.zip\nlrwxrwxrwx    1 ftp ftp       20 Oct 03 08:12 latest.csv -> sales-2026-10-02.csv"

    mut total := 0 as i64
    mut files := 0
    mut biggest := ftp.FileInfo {}
    each line in str.Split(raw, "\n"):
        f := ftp.ParseListLine(line)
        if f.is_dir:
            println "dir ", f.name
            continue
        end
        if f.is_link:
            println "link", f.name
            continue
        end
        println "file", f.name, f.size, f.raw_date
        files += 1
        total += f.size
        if f.size > biggest.size:
            biggest = f
        end
    end
    println files, "files,", total, "bytes; biggest:", biggest.name
end
```

Output:

```text
dir  old
file sales-2026-10-01.csv 120034 Oct 02 08:10
file sales-2026-10-02.csv 118702 Oct 03 08:10
file photos.zip 2251800 Oct 03 08:12
link latest.csv
3 files, 2490536 bytes; biggest: photos.zip
```

## Servers that require TLS session reuse

Some FTPS servers insist that the data connection resumes the TLS session of the command connection. vsftpd does this with its default `require_ssl_reuse=YES`, and so do FileZilla Server and the Rebex test server. This package does not resume sessions yet, so on those servers logging in works but every listing and transfer is refused with reply 425:

ftp-public-demo.salam

```salam
import ftp

func main:
    mut c := ftp.DialTLS("test.rebex.net", 21)
    if not ftp.Ok(c) or not ftp.Login(c, "demo", "password"):
        println "cannot log in:", ftp.LastCode(c), ftp.LastReply(c)
        ret 1
    end
    println "encrypted:", ftp.Secure(c), ftp.SecureData(c)
    println "system:", ftp.System(c)
    entries := ftp.List(c, "/")
    if entries.len() == 0 and ftp.LastCode(c) >= 400:
        println "listing refused:", ftp.LastReply(c)
    end
    each f in entries:
        println f.name, f.is_dir
    end
    ftp.Quit(c)
    ftp.Close(c)
    ret 0
end
```

Run against `test.rebex.net`, it printed:

```salam
encrypted: true true
system: 215 UNIX Type: L8
listing refused: 425 Cannot secure data connection - TLS session resumption required.
```

If you run the server, set `require_ssl_reuse=NO` in vsftpd. If you do not, and the server offers SFTP, use ssh instead; fall back to plain `Dial` only on a network you trust, since it sends the password in the clear.

## Which function for which job

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Connect securely | `DialTLS`, or `DialTLSWith` for a private CA; `Dial` then `AuthTLS` does the same in two steps |
| Check that encryption is on | `Secure` for the commands, `SecureData` for the files |
| Small text files | `Read`, `Write`, `Append` |
| Files on disk | `Upload`, `Download`, `UploadDir`, `DownloadDir` |
| Look before you act | `Exists`, `IsDir`, `Size`, `ModTime`, `List` |
| A command with no function of its own | `Command`, which returns the reply code |

## Types

### `FileInfo`

```salam
struct FileInfo
```

The information about one file from the server listing.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name. |
| `size` | `i64 = 0` | The size. |
| `is_dir` | `bool = false` | It is a directory. |
| `is_link` | `bool = false` | It is a link. |
| `mode` | `str = ""` | The permissions, such as `rw-r--r--`. |
| `raw_date` | `str = ""` | The date exactly as the server wrote it. |

ftp-Parse.salam

```salam
import ftp

func main:
    println ftp.ReplyCode("230 Login successful."), ftp.ReplyCode("broken")
    println ftp.IsFinalLine("211-Features:"), ftp.IsFinalLine("211 End")
    println ftp.ParsePasv("227 Entering Passive Mode (192,168,1,10,19,137)")
    println ftp.ParseEpsv("229 Entering Extended Passive Mode (|||50000|)")
    file := ftp.ParseListLine("-rw-r--r--    1 ftp      ftp          1024 Sep 30 12:00 notes.txt")
    println file.name, file.size, file.is_dir, file.is_link, file.mode, file.raw_date
    folder := ftp.ParseListLine("drwxr-xr-x    2 ftp      ftp          4096 Jan 01  2026 backup")
    println folder.name, folder.is_dir
    link := ftp.ParseListLine("lrwxrwxrwx    1 ftp      ftp             7 Mar 03 09:15 current -> backup")
    println link.name, link.is_link
end
```

Output:

```text
230 0
false true
192.168.1.10:5001
50000
notes.txt 1024 false false rw-r--r-- Sep 30 12:00
backup true
current true
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

One FTP connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conn` | `tcp.Conn` | The TCP connection of the commands. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The connection is healthy. |
| `host` | `str = ""` | The host. |
| `port` | `int = 21` | The port. |
| `rxbuf` | `str = ""` | The data that was read. |
| `last_reply` | `str = ""` | The last reply of the server. |
| `last_code` | `int = 0` | The code of the last reply. |
| `secure` | `bool = false` | The command channel is encrypted. |
| `tls_idx` | `int = -1` | The index of the TLS connection. |
| `prot_p` | `bool = false` | The data channel is encrypted too. |
| `tls_cfg` | `tls.Config` | The TLS configuration. |

ftp-Client.salam

```salam
import ftp
import tls

func main:
    mut c := ftp.DialTLS("ftp.example.com", 21)
    if not ftp.Ok(c) or not ftp.Login(c, "ali", "s3cret"):
        println ftp.LastCode(c), ftp.LastReply(c)
        ret
    end
    println ftp.Secure(c), ftp.SecureData(c)
    println ftp.System(c)
    println ftp.Features(c)
    _ := ftp.Binary(c)
    println ftp.Pwd(c)
    _ := ftp.MkdirAll(c, "/site/assets")
    _ := ftp.Cwd(c, "/site")
    _ := ftp.Write(c, "index.html", "<h1>hello</h1>")
    _ := ftp.Append(c, "log.txt", "one more line\n")
    println ftp.Read(c, "index.html")
    println ftp.Upload(c, "logo.png", "assets/logo.png")
    println ftp.Download(c, "log.txt", "log-copy.txt")
    each entry in ftp.List(c, "."):
        println entry.name, entry.size, entry.is_dir
    end
    each name in ftp.NameList(c, "assets"):
        println name
    end
    println ftp.ListRaw(c, ".").len() > 0
    println ftp.Size(c, "index.html"), ftp.ModTime(c, "index.html")
    println ftp.IsDir(c, "assets"), ftp.IsLink(c, "current"), ftp.Exists(c, "old.html")
    _ := ftp.Rename(c, "log.txt", "log-1.txt")
    _ := ftp.Move(c, "log-1.txt", "archive/log-1.txt")
    _ := ftp.Delete(c, "archive/log-1.txt")
    _ := ftp.CdUp(c)
    _ := ftp.Mkdir(c, "tmp")
    _ := ftp.Rmdir(c, "tmp")
    _ := ftp.RemoveAll(c, "/site/old")
    _ := ftp.UploadDir(c, "public", "/site")
    _ := ftp.DownloadDir(c, "/site", "backup")
    println ftp.Command(c, "SITE CHMOD 644 index.html")
    println ftp.Noop(c)
    _ := ftp.Ascii(c)
    ftp.Quit(c)
    ftp.Close(c)

    mut plain := ftp.Dial("ftp.example.com", 21)
    println ftp.AuthTLS(plain)
    mut cfg := tls.NewConfig("ftp.example.com")
    cfg.ca_file = "company-ca.pem"
    mut configured := ftp.DialTLSWith("ftp.example.com", 21, cfg)
    mut upgraded := ftp.Dial("ftp.example.com", 21)
    println ftp.AuthTLSWith(upgraded, cfg)
    ftp.Close(plain)
    ftp.Close(configured)
    ftp.Close(upgraded)
end
```
