# rpc

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/rpc/

JSON-RPC 2.0 and MessagePack-RPC: a server, a client and registering methods.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add rpc`

With a remote procedure call one program calls another program's methods as if they were its own routines. On the server side you tie each method to a routine with `Register`; that routine takes the call's number, reads the parameters with `CallParamInt` and the like, and answers with `Reply...` or `Fail`.

The messages are exchanged with the JSON codec (JSON-RPC 2.0) or MessagePack, and over TCP they are separated by one of three framings, line, header (like LSP) or length prefixed; the client and the server must have the same framing. `HandleText` does the same thing without a network, so you can put RPC behind an net/http route.

## A small service without a network

The quickest way to design an RPC API is to build it with `HandleText`: it takes one JSON-RPC request (or a batch) as text and returns the answer as text, without any network. Every method is an ordinary function that receives a call slot `c`; it reads parameters with `CallParamStr`, `CallParamInt` and their siblings, and must answer exactly once, with a `Reply...` function or with `Fail`.

rpc-guide-todo.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value

mut todos := Vector {} as Vector<str>

func add_todo(c: i64):
    title := rpc.CallParamStr(c, "title", 0)
    if title == "":
        rpc.FailInvalidParams(c, "title is required")
        ret
    end
    todos.push(title)
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, todos.len())
end

func list_todos(c: i64):
    mut items := value.NewValueArray()
    each t in todos:
        value.ArrayPush(items, value.ValueString(t))
    end
    rpc.Reply(c, items)
end

func count_todos(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, todos.len())
end

func main:
    rpc.RegisterDoc("todo.add", add_todo, "adds a todo and returns how many there are")
    rpc.RegisterDoc("todo.list", list_todos, "returns every todo")
    rpc.Register("todo.count", count_todos)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"todo.add","params":{"title":"buy bread"},"id":1}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"todo.add","params":["call Sara"],"id":2}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"todo.add","params":{},"id":3}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"todo.list","id":4}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"todo.count","id":5},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"todo.delete","id":6}]`)
    println rpc.MethodDoc("todo.add")
    todos.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": 1}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": 2}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "title is required", "code": -32602}, "id": 3}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 4, "result": ["buy bread", "call Sara"]}
[{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "result": 2}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "Method not found", "code": -32601}, "id": 6}]
adds a todo and returns how many there are
```

Each parameter is looked up by name and by position at the same time: `CallParamStr(c, "title", 0)` finds `{"title": ...}` as well as the first element of `[...]`, so clients can use either style. `FailInvalidParams` answers with the standard code -32602, and a method that was never registered gets -32601 without any code of yours. Inside a batch, each request gets its own answer, failures included.

The registry is global for the whole program, so method state, such as the todo list here, lives in a global variable or behind one. If several connections are served in parallel threads, protect that state with a lock from sync.

## A server and a client over TCP

For two programs, `NewServer` with port `0` lets the system pick a free port and `Port` reports it after `Listen`. `ServeCount` serves a fixed number of connections and returns, which suits tests; `Serve` runs until `StopServer`. Both answer one connection at a time: while a client stays connected, the next one waits in the queue. When several clients must be served at once, accept the connections yourself with net/tcp (`tcp.Bind`, then `tcp.Accept` in a loop) and pass each connection's `fd` to `ServeConn` in its own thread from thread. On the other side, `DialClient` connects, `Call` sends one request and waits for its answer.

rpc-guide-tcp.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value
import sync

mut server := rpc.NewServer(0, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func convert(c: i64):
    amount := rpc.CallParamFloat(c, "amount", 0)
    currency := rpc.CallParamStr(c, "to", 1)
    if currency == "EUR":
        rpc.ReplyFloat(c, amount * 0.5)
        ret
    end
    rpc.Fail(c, -32010, "unknown currency " + currency)
end

func run_server():
    _ := rpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := rpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("convert", convert)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)

    mut client := rpc.DialClient("127.0.0.1", rpc.Port(server), rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
    if not rpc.ClientOk(client):
        println "cannot connect:", rpc.ClientError(client)
        ret 1
    end
    mut params := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(params, "amount", value.ValueFloat(40.0))
    value.ObjectSet(params, "to", value.ValueString("EUR"))
    ok := rpc.Call(client, "convert", params)
    println "40 is", rpc.ResultFloat(ok), "EUR"

    value.ObjectSet(params, "to", value.ValueString("XYZ"))
    bad := rpc.Call(client, "convert", params)
    if rpc.IsErrorResponse(bad):
        println "error", rpc.ErrorCode(bad), rpc.ErrorMessage(bad)
    end
    rpc.CloseClient(client)
    join(t)
    rpc.StopServer(server)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
40 is 20 EUR
error -32010 unknown currency XYZ
```

A failed call does not crash anything. Check `IsErrorResponse` first and then read `ErrorCode` and `ErrorMessage`; reading `ResultFloat` on an error response returns 0. Your own error codes should stay outside the range -32768 to -32000 that JSON-RPC reserves, except for the -32000 to -32099 block meant for server errors, which is where -32010 comes from.

Client and server must agree on the codec and the framing. JSON with line framing is the default and easy to debug with a terminal. `RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK` is smaller and faster and uses length prefixed frames; set both ends with `SetFraming` and `ClientSetFraming`.

## Talking over standard input and output

Editor tools, language servers and plugins often run as a child process and exchange messages over standard input and output. `ServeStdio` reads one request per line (or LSP style `Content-Length` frames with `RPC_FRAME_HEADER`), answers each on standard output, and returns the number of requests when the input ends. Logs must go to standard error, as here, or they would corrupt the answers.

Two limits of `ServeStdio` to know before you build on it:

- With line framing, an empty line counts as the end of the input, so the service stops there.

- `RPC_FRAME_HEADER` does not yet work with real LSP clients. They end headers with `\r\n` and send no newline after the body, so the blank `\r` line is answered with a parse error and the next header is read as part of the body. It also never returns at the end of the input. Use line framing over standard input and output for now.

rpc-guide-stdio.salam

```salam
import rpc
import str
import io

func word_count(c: i64):
    words := str.Fields(rpc.CallParamStr(c, "text", 0))
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, words.len())
    words.free()
end

func shout(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyStr(c, str.Upper(rpc.CallParamStr(c, "text", 0)))
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("words", word_count)
    rpc.Register("shout", shout)
    served := rpc.ServeStdio(rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)
    io.EPrintln("answered " + served + " requests")
end
```

This program waits for input, so it is only compiled here. Build it and pipe two requests into it:

```salam
salam build rpc-guide-stdio.salam --output=tool
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"words","params":["one two three"],"id":1}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"shout","params":{"text":"salam"},"id":2}' | ./tool
```

```salam
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": 3}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": "SALAM"}
answered 2 requests
```

## JSON-RPC behind an HTTP route

Because `HandleText` only needs text, putting the same methods behind a web server takes one route. The handler passes the request body in and sends the answer back as JSON with net/http; batches work too. Other programs can then call it with `CallHTTP`, or with any HTTP client.

rpc-guide-http.salam

```salam
import rpc
import net.http
import net.router

mut visits := 0

func hit(c: i64):
    visits += 1
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, visits)
end

func greet(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyStr(c, "salam, " + rpc.CallParamStr(c, "name", 0))
end

func endpoint(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, rpc.HandleText(http.Body(ctx)))
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("hit", hit)
    rpc.Register("greet", greet)
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/rpc", endpoint)
    mut s := http.NewServer(8090)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println "JSON-RPC on http://127.0.0.1:8090/rpc"
    http.Run(s)
end
```

Run the program, then call it from another terminal:

```salam
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/rpc -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"greet","params":{"name":"Sara"},"id":1}'
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/rpc -d '[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hit","id":1},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hit","id":2}]'
```

```salam
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": "salam, Sara"}
[{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": 1}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": 2}]
```

| Transport | Server side | Client side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None, inside one program or a test | `HandleText`, `Invoke` | build the request text yourself |
| TCP | `NewServer`, `Listen`, `Serve` | `DialClient`, `Call`, `CallBatch`, `Notify` |
| Standard input and output | `ServeStdio` | the parent process writes lines |
| HTTP | `HandleText` in a route | `CallHTTP` |

## Types

### `Server`

```salam
struct Server
```

An RPC server.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | `int = 0` | The port; zero means a free port. |
| `codec` | `int = 0` | The codec. |
| `framing` | `int = 0` | The framing. |
| `listen_fd` | `i64 = -1` | The listening socket. |
| `running` | `bool = false` | It is running. |
| `served` | `int = 0` | The number of connections answered. |

rpc-Serve.salam

```salam
import rpc
import net.tcp
import compress

func echo(c: i64):
    rpc.Reply(c, rpc.CallParams(c))
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("echo", echo)
    if rpc.HandleText("").len() == 0:
        _ := rpc.ServeStdio(rpc.RPC_FRAME_HEADER)
        ret
    end

    mut s := rpc.NewServer(4000, rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK)
    rpc.SetFraming(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH)
    if rpc.Listen(s):
        println "on port", rpc.Port(s), s.running
        rpc.Serve(s)
    end

    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 4001)
    _ := rpc.ServeConn(conn.fd, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)

    c := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 4002)
    mut client := rpc.ClientFromFd(c.fd, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
    println rpc.ResultStr(rpc.CallNoParams(client, "version"))

    mut stream := rpc.NewStream(c.fd)
    _ := rpc.WriteFrameStr(c.fd, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"echo","params":[1],"id":1}`)
    _ := rpc.WriteFrame(c.fd, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, compress.BufFromStr(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"echo","id":2}`))
    mut ok := false
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(stream, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok)
    answer := rpc.HandlePayload(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, compress.BufFromStr(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"echo","params":[3],"id":3}`))
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(answer)
    rpc.FreeStream(stream)
    rpc.StopServer(s)
end
```

### `Stream`

```salam
struct Stream
```

The input stream that separates the frames from a socket or from memory.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fd` | `i64 = -1` | The socket. |
| `data` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The data read. |
| `pos` | `int = 0` | The read position. |
| `closed` | `bool = false` | The input is finished. |
| `has_fd` | `bool = false` | It is over a socket. |

rpc-Frames.salam

```salam
import rpc
import compress

func main:
    line := rpc.FrameEncodeStr(rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, `{"a":1}`)
    headed := rpc.FrameEncodeStr(rpc.RPC_FRAME_HEADER, `{"b":2}`)
    sized := rpc.FrameEncode(rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH, compress.BufFromStr(`{"c":3}`))
    println line.len, headed.len, sized.len
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(headed).len() > 0

    mut s := rpc.NewMemStream()
    rpc.FeedStr(s, `{"x":1}` + "\n" + `{"x":2}` + "\n")
    mut ok := false
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok), ok
    println rpc.StreamPending(s)
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok)
    _ := rpc.ReadFrameStr(s, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, ok)
    println ok, rpc.StreamClosed(s)

    mut s2 := rpc.NewMemStream()
    rpc.FeedBuf(s2, headed)
    rpc.FeedBuf(s2, sized)
    println rpc.ReadFrameStr(s2, rpc.RPC_FRAME_HEADER, ok)
    b := rpc.ReadFrame(s2, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH, ok)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(b), ok
    println rpc.RPC_READ_CHUNK, rpc.RPC_MAX_FRAME
    rpc.FreeStream(s)
    rpc.FreeStream(s2)
end
```

Output:

```text
8 28 11
true
{"x":1} true
8
{"x":2}
false false
{"b":2}
{"c":3} true
4096 33554432
```

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

An RPC client over a TCP connection.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conn` | `tcp.Conn` | The connection. |
| `stream` | `Stream` | The reading stream. |
| `codec` | `int = 0` | The codec. |
| `framing` | `int = 0` | The framing. |
| `next_id` | `i64 = 1` | The next request id. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It is healthy. |
| `last_error` | `str = ""` | The last error. |

rpc-Client.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value
import net.http
import net.router
import sync

mut server := rpc.NewServer(0, rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func add(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, rpc.CallParamInt(c, "a", 0) + rpc.CallParamInt(c, "b", 1))
end

func clock(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyStr(c, "12:00")
end

func note(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyNull(c)
end

func run_server():
    _ := rpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := rpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func endpoint(ctx: i64):
    http.Json(ctx, rpc.HandleText(http.Body(ctx)))
end

func main:
    rpc.Register("add", add)
    rpc.Register("time", clock)
    rpc.Register("note", note)
    rpc.SetFraming(server, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)
    println rpc.Port(server) > 0

    mut client := rpc.DialClient("127.0.0.1", rpc.Port(server), rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON)
    rpc.ClientSetFraming(client, rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE)
    println rpc.ClientOk(client)
    mut params := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueInt(2))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueInt(40))
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.Call(client, "add", params))
    println rpc.ResultStr(rpc.CallNoParams(client, "time"))
    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<value.Value>
    args.push(value.ValueInt(1))
    args.push(value.ValueInt(2))
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.CallArgs(client, "add", args))
    println rpc.Notify(client, "note", value.NewValueArray())
    mut batch := Vector {} as Vector<rpc.Request>
    batch.push(rpc.NewRequest("add", params, 10))
    batch.push(rpc.NewRequest("missing", value.NewValueArray(), 11))
    answers := rpc.CallBatch(client, batch)
    println answers.items.len(), rpc.ResultInt(answers.items[0])
    println rpc.IsErrorResponse(answers.items[1]), rpc.ErrorCode(answers.items[1]), rpc.ErrorMessage(answers.items[1])
    rpc.CloseClient(client)
    println rpc.ClientOk(client), rpc.ClientError(client).len() >= 0
    join(t)
    rpc.StopServer(server)

    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/rpc", endpoint)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19631)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)
    answer := rpc.CallHTTP("http://127.0.0.1:19631/rpc", "add", params, 7)
    println rpc.ResultInt(answer)
end
```

Output:

```text
true
true
42
12:00
3
true
2 42
true -32601 Method not found
false true
42
```

### `Error`

```salam
struct Error
```

A JSON-RPC error.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `int = 0` | The code. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message. |
| `data` | `value.Value` | The extra data. |
| `has_data` | `bool = false` | It has data. |

rpc-Messages.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value
import compress

func main:
    mut params := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueInt(2))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueString("hello"))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueFloat(1.5))
    value.ArrayPush(params, value.ValueBool(true))
    req := rpc.NewRequest("calc", params, 1)
    println rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(req)
    println rpc.ParamCount(req), rpc.ParamInt(req, "a", 0), rpc.ParamStr(req, "b", 1)
    println rpc.ParamFloat(req, "c", 2), rpc.ParamBool(req, "d", 3), rpc.HasParam(req, "e", 4)
    println value.AsInt(rpc.ParamAt(req, 0)), value.AsInt(rpc.Param(req, "a", 0))
    mut obj := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(obj, "name", value.ValueString("Ali"))
    req2 := rpc.NewRequestStrId("greet", obj, "req-1")
    println rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(req2)
    println value.AsString(rpc.ParamNamed(req2, "name"))
    note := rpc.NewNotification("tick", value.NewValueArray())
    println rpc.IsNotification(note), rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(note)

    mut ok := false
    read := rpc.JsonDecodeRequest(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":{"a":1,"b":2},"id":9}`, ok)
    println ok, read.method, read.msgid, rpc.ParamInt(read, "b", 1)

    answer := rpc.NewResponse(value.ValueInt(1), value.ValueString("ok"))
    println rpc.JsonEncodeResponse(answer)
    err := rpc.StdError(rpc.RPC_METHOD_NOT_FOUND)
    println err.code, err.message
    println rpc.JsonEncodeResponse(rpc.NewErrorResponse(value.ValueInt(2), rpc.NewError(-32000, "the server is busy")))
    with_data := rpc.ErrorWithData(rpc.RPC_INVALID_PARAMS, "bad", value.ValueString("x"))
    println with_data.has_data, rpc.JsonTopLevelError(rpc.StdError(rpc.RPC_PARSE_ERROR))

    one := rpc.JsonDecodeResponse(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":3.5,"id":1}`, ok)
    println ok, rpc.ResultFloat(one), rpc.IsErrorResponse(one)
    two := rpc.JsonDecodeResponse(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32601,"message":"nope"},"id":2}`, ok)
    println rpc.IsErrorResponse(two), rpc.ErrorCode(two), rpc.ErrorMessage(two)
    all := rpc.JsonDecodeResponses(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":true,"id":1},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":"x","id":2}]`, ok)
    println all.is_batch, all.items.len(), rpc.ResultBool(all.items[0]), rpc.ResultStr(all.items[1])
    println rpc.JsonEncodeResponses(all)

    println rpc.CodecName(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON), rpc.CodecName(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK)
    println rpc.CodecDefaultFraming(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON) == rpc.RPC_FRAME_LINE, rpc.CodecDefaultFraming(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK) == rpc.RPC_FRAME_LENGTH
    packed := rpc.EncodeRequest(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK, req)
    println packed.len, compress.BufGet(packed, 0)
    batch := rpc.DecodeBatch(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK, packed)
    println batch.ok, batch.items[0].method, batch.items[0].msgid
    println rpc.MsgpackDecodeBatch(rpc.MsgpackEncodeRequest(req)).items[0].method
    mp := rpc.MsgpackEncodeResponse(rpc.NewResponse(value.ValueInt(1), value.ValueInt(42)))
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.MsgpackDecodeResponse(mp, ok)), ok
    js := rpc.EncodeRequest(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, req)
    println rpc.ResultInt(rpc.DecodeResponse(rpc.RPC_CODEC_MSGPACK, mp, ok)), js.len > 0
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(rpc.EncodeResponses(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, all)).len() > 0
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(rpc.EncodeTopLevelError(rpc.RPC_CODEC_JSON, err))
    println rpc.RPC_MP_REQUEST, rpc.RPC_MP_RESPONSE, rpc.RPC_MP_NOTIFY
    println rpc.RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, rpc.RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR, rpc.RPC_SERVER_ERROR
    println rpc.RPC_KIND_REQUEST, rpc.RPC_KIND_NOTIFICATION, rpc.RPC_KIND_RESPONSE
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(compress.BufFromStr(rpc.JsonEncodeRequest(req))).len() > 0
end
```

### `Request`

```salam
struct Request
```

One request.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `str = ""` | The method name. |
| `params` | `value.Value` | The parameters: an array or an object. |
| `has_params` | `bool = false` | It has parameters. |
| `id` | `value.Value` | The id; a number or a string. |
| `has_id` | `bool = false` | It has an id; without one it is a notification. |
| `msgid` | `i64 = 0` | The numeric id. |
| `err_code` | `int = 0` | If the request could not be read, the error code. |
| `err_message` | `str = ""` | That error's message. |

rpc-Methods.salam

```salam
import rpc
import encoding.value

func add(c: i64):
    a := rpc.CallParamInt(c, "a", 0)
    b := rpc.CallParamInt(c, "b", 1)
    rpc.ReplyInt(c, a + b)
end

func divide(c: i64):
    divisor := rpc.CallParamFloat(c, "b", 1)
    if divisor == 0.0:
        rpc.FailInvalidParams(c, "division by zero")
        ret
    end
    rpc.ReplyFloat(c, rpc.CallParamFloat(c, "a", 0) / divisor)
end

func hello(c: i64):
    name := rpc.CallParamStr(c, "name", 0)
    if name.len() == 0:
        rpc.Fail(c, -32001, "a name is needed")
        ret
    end
    rpc.ReplyStr(c, "hello " + name)
end

func status(c: i64):
    mut info := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(info, value.ValueString(rpc.CallMethodName(c)))
    value.ArrayPush(info, value.ValueInt(rpc.CallParamCount(c)))
    value.ArrayPush(info, value.ValueBool(rpc.CallParamBool(c, "verbose", 0)))
    rpc.Reply(c, info)
end

func log_event(c: i64):
    println "event:", value.AsString(rpc.CallParam(c, "event", 0)), rpc.CallIsNotification(c)
    _ := rpc.CallParams(c)
    _ := rpc.CallRequest(c)
    rpc.ReplyNull(c)
end

func forbidden(c: i64):
    rpc.FailWithData(c, -32003, "you are not allowed", value.ValueString("admin"))
end

func always(c: i64):
    rpc.ReplyBool(c, true)
end

func main:
    rpc.RegisterDoc("add", add, "adds two numbers")
    rpc.Register("divide", divide)
    rpc.Register("hello", hello)
    rpc.Register("status", status)
    rpc.Register("log", log_event)
    rpc.Register("admin", forbidden)
    rpc.Register("ping", always)
    println rpc.MethodCount(), rpc.HasMethod("add"), rpc.MethodDoc("add")
    println rpc.ListMethods().len()

    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":[2,40],"id":1}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":{"a":5,"b":6},"id":2}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"divide","params":[1,0],"id":3}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hello","params":["Maryam"],"id":"x"}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hello","params":[],"id":4}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"status","params":{"verbose":true},"id":5}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"admin","id":6}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"nope","id":7}`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"log","params":{"event":"start"}}`).len()
    println rpc.HandleText(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"ping","id":8},{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":[1,1],"id":9}]`)
    println rpc.HandleText(`{"jsonrpc":`)

    mut ok := false
    req := rpc.JsonDecodeRequest(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"add","params":[20,22],"id":10}`, ok)
    answer := rpc.Invoke(req)
    println rpc.ResultInt(answer)
    batch := rpc.JsonDecodeBatch(`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"ping","id":1}]`)
    println rpc.InvokeBatch(batch).items.len()

    println rpc.Unregister("ping"), rpc.HasMethod("ping")
    rpc.ResetRegistry()
    println rpc.MethodCount()
end
```

Output:

```text
7 true adds two numbers
7
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": 42}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": 11}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "division by zero", "code": -32602}, "id": 3}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "x", "result": "hello Maryam"}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "a name is needed", "code": -32001}, "id": 4}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "result": ["status", 1, true]}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "you are not allowed", "code": -32003, "data": "admin"}, "id": 6}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "Method not found", "code": -32601}, "id": 7}
event: start true
0
[{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 8, "result": true}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 9, "result": 2}]
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"message": "Parse error", "code": -32700}, "id": null}
42
1
true false
0
```

# grpc

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/grpc/

A gRPC server and client over HTTP/2: unary and streaming calls, metadata and status codes.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add grpc`

gRPC is a way of calling a remote procedure that runs over HTTP/2, and it is common in microservices. On the server side you register each method under its path, like `/demo.Greeter/SayHello`; the method routine reads the client's message with `Recv`, answers with `Send` and ends it with `SetStatus` or `Fail`.

On the client side, `UnaryCall` is a plain request, and for streams you use `StartCall`, `SendMessage`, `RecvMessage` and `FinishCall`. Messages are bytes; you usually build them with protobuf.

Choose gRPC when the other side already speaks it, or when you want typed messages and streams between services. For a simpler protocol that also works over plain TCP, standard input and output or an HTTP route, see rpc (JSON-RPC and MessagePack-RPC).

Limits of the server side to know before you build on it:

- The server handles one connection at a time, and on that connection one call at a time: each method runs to the end before the next stream is read. A long streaming call holds up every other caller. That suits internal tools, tests and light services.

- The server speaks plaintext HTTP/2 (h2c) only. To accept TLS, put a proxy such as nginx or Envoy in front. The client can use TLS with `DialTLS`.

- The connection state lives in one global, so `ServeConn` must not run in several threads at once.

## A unary call with protobuf messages

Real gRPC services exchange protobuf messages, not plain strings. A message is a list of fields, each written as a tag (field number and wire type) followed by the value; encoding/protobuf writes and reads them. The example defines a `Users.Get` method that takes a message with the user id in field 1 and answers with a user message: the id in field 1 and the name in field 2. Server and client run in one program, with the server on a port the system picks.

grpc-guide-protobuf.salam

```salam
import grpc
import encoding.protobuf
import compress
import sync

mut server := grpc.NewServer(0)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func encode_user(id: int, name: str): compress.ByteBuf:
    mut b := compress.NewByteBuf()
    protobuf.WriteTag(b, 1, protobuf.WT_VARINT)
    protobuf.WriteVarint(b, id as u64)
    protobuf.WriteTag(b, 2, protobuf.WT_LEN)
    protobuf.WriteLenPrefixedStr(b, name)
    ret b
end

func get_user(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    req := grpc.Recv(c, ok)
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(req)
    mut good := true
    mut field := 0
    mut wire := 0
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, field, wire, good)
    id := protobuf.ReadVarint(r, good) as int
    if not good or field != 1:
        grpc.Fail(c, grpc.GRPC_INVALID_ARGUMENT, "expected field 1 with the user id")
        ret
    end
    if id != 7:
        grpc.Fail(c, grpc.GRPC_NOT_FOUND, "no user " + id)
        ret
    end
    mut reply := encode_user(7, "Maryam")
    _ := grpc.Send(c, reply)
    compress.BufFree(reply)
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func run_server():
    _ := grpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := grpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func ask(ch &: grpc.Channel, id: int):
    mut req := compress.NewByteBuf()
    protobuf.WriteTag(req, 1, protobuf.WT_VARINT)
    protobuf.WriteVarint(req, id as u64)
    mut st := grpc.Status {}
    answer := grpc.UnaryCall(ch, "/users.Users/Get", req, grpc.NewMetadata(), st)
    compress.BufFree(req)
    if not grpc.StatusOk(st):
        println "user", id, "->", grpc.StatusString(st)
        ret
    end
    mut r := compress.ReaderFromBuf(answer)
    mut good := true
    mut field := 0
    mut wire := 0
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, field, wire, good)
    uid := protobuf.ReadVarint(r, good)
    protobuf.ReadTag(r, field, wire, good)
    println "user", uid, "is", protobuf.ReadLenPrefixedStr(r, good)
end

func main:
    grpc.RegisterMethod(grpc.MethodPath("users.Users", "Get"), get_user)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)
    mut ch := grpc.Dial("127.0.0.1", grpc.Port(server))
    grpc.SetTimeout(ch, 5000)
    ask(ch, 7)
    ask(ch, 8)
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)
    join(t)
    grpc.StopServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
user 7 is Maryam
user 8 -> NOT_FOUND: no user 8
```

`MethodPath` builds the path `/users.Users/Get` from the service and method names, which must match what the other side's `.proto` file says. When the request is wrong or the record does not exist, the method calls `Fail` with a status code instead of sending a message. The client checks `StatusOk` before it reads the answer, and `StatusString` gives a one line description such as `NOT_FOUND: no user 8`.

Writing the fields by hand is fine for small messages. For a larger API, `protobuf.GenerateWithServices` turns a `.proto` file into Salam structs with `Marshal` and `Unmarshal` functions plus the service code, so the field numbers live in one place.

## Tokens in metadata and error status codes

gRPC sends credentials and other per call values as metadata, the gRPC name for HTTP/2 headers. The client adds an entry with `MDAdd`, and the method reads it with `MDGet(CallMetadata(c), ...)`. Choose the status code by what went wrong: `GRPC_UNAUTHENTICATED` when no valid credential came, `GRPC_PERMISSION_DENIED` when the caller is known but not allowed.

grpc-guide-auth.salam

```salam
import grpc
import sync
import compress

mut server := grpc.NewServer(0)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func balance(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    account := grpc.RecvStr(c, ok)
    token := grpc.MDGet(grpc.CallMetadata(c), "authorization")
    if token == "":
        grpc.Fail(c, grpc.GRPC_UNAUTHENTICATED, "missing token")
        ret
    end
    if token != "Bearer good-token":
        grpc.Fail(c, grpc.GRPC_PERMISSION_DENIED, "this token cannot read " + account)
        ret
    end
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, account + ": 1250")
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func run_server():
    _ := grpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := grpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func main:
    grpc.RegisterMethod("/bank.Accounts/Balance", balance)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)
    mut ch := grpc.Dial("127.0.0.1", grpc.Port(server))
    grpc.SetTimeout(ch, 5000)
    each token in ["", "Bearer old-token", "Bearer good-token"]:
        mut md := grpc.NewMetadata()
        if token != "":
            _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "authorization", token)
        end
        mut st := grpc.Status {}
        answer := grpc.UnaryCall(ch, "/bank.Accounts/Balance", compress.BufFromStr("acc-42"), md, st)
        if grpc.StatusOk(st):
            println "ok:", compress.BufToStrUnsafe(answer)
        else:
            println grpc.StatusName(st.code), "(" + st.code + "):", st.message
        end
    end
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)
    join(t)
    grpc.StopServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
UNAUTHENTICATED (16): missing token
PERMISSION_DENIED (7): this token cannot read acc-42
ok: acc-42: 1250
```

Metadata keys are lower case. A value that is binary must use a key ending in `-bin` and is added with `MDAddBinary`. Clients often retry automatically on `GRPC_UNAVAILABLE` but never on an authentication error, so using the right code matters to the caller, not just to the logs.

## Client streaming: many messages in, one answer out

A method registered with `RegisterStreamMethod(path, fn, true, false)` receives a stream from the client and answers once, which suits uploads and batches of readings. The method calls `Recv` in a loop until `ok` turns false, which happens when the client has sent its last message. On the client side, `StartCall` opens the call, `SendMessage` sends each message and its last argument marks the final one, then `RecvMessage` reads the answer and `FinishCall` returns the status.

grpc-guide-stream.salam

```salam
import grpc
import compress
import sync

mut server := grpc.NewServer(0)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func total(c: i64):
    mut sum := 0
    mut count := 0
    mut more := true
    until more:
        mut ok := false
        reading := grpc.RecvStr(c, ok)
        if not ok:
            more = false
        else:
            sum += reading.to_int()
            count += 1
        end
    end
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, "" + count + " readings, total " + sum)
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func run_server():
    _ := grpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := grpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func main:
    grpc.RegisterStreamMethod("/meter.Meter/Upload", total, true, false)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)
    mut ch := grpc.Dial("127.0.0.1", grpc.Port(server))
    grpc.SetTimeout(ch, 5000)
    call := grpc.StartCall(ch, "/meter.Meter/Upload", grpc.NewMetadata())
    readings := ["12", "7", "30", "1"]
    each i, r in readings:
        mut msg := compress.BufFromStr(r)
        _ := grpc.SendMessage(ch, call, msg, i == len(readings) - 1)
        compress.BufFree(msg)
    end
    mut ok := false
    answer := grpc.RecvMessage(ch, call, ok)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(answer)
    println grpc.StatusString(grpc.FinishCall(ch, call))
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)
    join(t)
    grpc.StopServer(server)
end
```

Output:

```text
4 readings, total 50
OK
```

If you do not know in advance which message is the last, send every message with `false` and call `CloseSend` at the end. For the other direction, a server stream, register with `false, true`, call `Send` several times in the method and read on the client with `RecvMessage` until `ok` is false.

## Which call shape for which job

| Shape | Register with | Client calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One request, one answer | `RegisterMethod` | `UnaryCall`, or `UnaryCallStr` for text |
| Many requests, one answer | `RegisterStreamMethod(path, fn, true, false)` | `StartCall`, `SendMessage`, `RecvMessage`, `FinishCall` |
| One request, many answers | `RegisterStreamMethod(path, fn, false, true)` | `StartCall`, `SendMessage` with `true`, then `RecvMessage` in a loop |
| Both directions | `RegisterStreamMethod(path, fn, true, true)` | the same functions, sending and reading in turn |

To reach a public service over TLS, open the channel with `DialTLS(host, 443)`; everything else stays the same. `SetGzip` compresses the messages the client sends.

## Types

### `Status`

```salam
struct Status
```

The final status of a call.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `int = 0` | The code. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message. |

grpc-Calls.salam

```salam
import grpc
import compress
import sync

mut server := grpc.NewServer(0)
mut ready := sync.NewWaitGroup()

func hello(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    name := grpc.RecvStr(c, ok)
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, "hello " + name)
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func countdown(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    _ := grpc.Recv(c, ok)
    repeat 3 in i:
        _ := grpc.Send(c, compress.BufFromStr("" + (3 - i)))
    end
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func trace(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    _ := grpc.RecvStr(c, ok)
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, grpc.MDGet(grpc.CallMetadata(c), "x-trace") + " " + grpc.CallPath(c))
    grpc.SetStatus(c, grpc.GRPC_OK, "")
end

func forbidden(c: i64):
    grpc.Fail(c, grpc.GRPC_PERMISSION_DENIED, "the token expired")
end

func run_server():
    _ := grpc.Listen(server)
    sync.Done(ready)
    _ := grpc.ServeCount(server, 1)
end

func main:
    hello_path := grpc.MethodPath("demo.Greeter", "SayHello")
    println hello_path
    grpc.RegisterMethod(hello_path, hello)
    grpc.RegisterStreamMethod("/demo.Greeter/Countdown", countdown, false, true)
    grpc.RegisterMethod("/demo.Greeter/Trace", trace)
    grpc.RegisterMethod("/demo.Greeter/Admin", forbidden)
    println grpc.MethodCount(), grpc.HasMethod(hello_path)
    sync.Add(ready, 1)
    t := spawn(run_server)
    sync.Wait(ready)

    mut ch := grpc.Dial("127.0.0.1", grpc.Port(server))
    grpc.SetTimeout(ch, 5000)
    println grpc.ChannelOk(ch)
    mut result := grpc.Status {}
    println grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, hello_path, "Maryam", result), grpc.StatusOk(result)

    call := grpc.StartCall(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Countdown", grpc.NewMetadata())
    _ := grpc.SendMessage(ch, call, compress.BufFromStr("go"), true)
    mut more := true
    until more:
        mut ok := false
        msg := grpc.RecvMessage(ch, call, ok)
        if not ok:
            more = false
        else:
            println "message:", compress.BufToStrUnsafe(msg)
        end
    end
    println grpc.MDCount(grpc.CallHeaders(ch, call))
    println grpc.StatusString(grpc.FinishCall(ch, call))

    mut md := grpc.NewMetadata()
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "x-trace", "t-42")
    mut result2 := grpc.Status {}
    answer := grpc.UnaryCall(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Trace", compress.BufFromStr("x"), md, result2)
    println compress.BufToStrUnsafe(answer)

    call2 := grpc.StartCall(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Trace", md)
    _ := grpc.SendMessage(ch, call2, compress.BufFromStr("y"), false)
    _ := grpc.CloseSend(ch, call2)
    mut ok2 := false
    _ := grpc.RecvMessage(ch, call2, ok2)
    _ := grpc.FinishCall(ch, call2)
    println ok2, grpc.CallTrailers(ch, call2).items.len() >= 0

    mut result3 := grpc.Status {}
    _ := grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Admin", "", result3)
    println result3.code, result3.message, grpc.StatusName(result3.code)
    mut result4 := grpc.Status {}
    _ := grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Nope", "", result4)
    println grpc.StatusString(result4)
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)
    join(t)
    grpc.StopServer(server)
    grpc.ResetMethods()
    println grpc.MethodCount()
end
```

Output:

```text
/demo.Greeter/SayHello
4 true
true
hello Maryam true
message: 3
message: 2
message: 1
0
OK
t-42 /demo.Greeter/Trace
true true
7 the token expired PERMISSION_DENIED
UNIMPLEMENTED: unknown method /demo.Greeter/Nope
0
```

### `MDEntry`

```salam
struct MDEntry
```

One metadata entry.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The key. |
| `value` | `str = ""` | The value. |
| `binary` | `bool = false` | It is binary. |

grpc-Wire.salam

```salam
import grpc
import compress
import net.http2

func main:
    one := grpc.FrameMessageStr("hello")
    println one.len, compress.BufGet(one, 0), compress.BufGet(one, 4)
    mut all := compress.NewByteBuf()
    compress.BufPushBuf(all, one)
    compress.BufPushBuf(all, grpc.FrameMessage(compress.BufFromStr("two"), false))
    compress.BufPushBuf(all, grpc.FrameMessageGzip(compress.BufFromStr("three three three"), true))
    println grpc.MessageCount(all), grpc.HasMessage(all, 0)
    mut pos := 0
    mut ok := false
    until grpc.HasMessage(all, pos):
        msg := grpc.NextMessage(all, pos, ok)
        println ok, compress.BufToStrUnsafe(msg)
    end

    mut md := grpc.NewMetadata()
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "authorization", "Bearer abc")
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "x-tag", "a")
    _ := grpc.MDAdd(md, "x-tag", "b")
    _ := grpc.MDAddBinary(md, "trace-bin", "\x01\x02")
    println grpc.MDCount(md), grpc.MDHas(md, "x-tag"), grpc.MDGet(md, "authorization")
    println grpc.MDGetAll(md, "x-tag").len()
    println grpc.MDKeyAt(md, 3), grpc.MDValueAt(md, 3).len()
    mut headers := http2.HeaderList {}
    grpc.MDToHeaders(md, headers)
    println http2.HeadersCount(headers), http2.HeadersGet(headers, "trace-bin")
    println grpc.MDCount(grpc.MDFromHeaders(headers))

    bad := grpc.NewStatus(grpc.GRPC_NOT_FOUND, "there is no user 42")
    println grpc.StatusOk(bad), grpc.StatusString(bad)
    message := grpc.EncodeStatusMessage("100% done")
    println message, grpc.DecodeStatusMessage(message)
    println grpc.FormatStatusCode(14), grpc.ParseStatusCode("14"), grpc.ParseStatusCode("x")
    println grpc.StatusName(grpc.GRPC_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), grpc.StatusName(grpc.GRPC_UNAUTHENTICATED)
    println grpc.GRPC_CANCELLED, grpc.GRPC_UNKNOWN, grpc.GRPC_INVALID_ARGUMENT, grpc.GRPC_ALREADY_EXISTS
    println grpc.GRPC_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, grpc.GRPC_FAILED_PRECONDITION, grpc.GRPC_ABORTED, grpc.GRPC_OUT_OF_RANGE
    println grpc.GRPC_UNIMPLEMENTED, grpc.GRPC_INTERNAL, grpc.GRPC_UNAVAILABLE, grpc.GRPC_DATA_LOSS
    println grpc.GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE, grpc.GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE_PROTO, grpc.GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE_JSON
    println grpc.GRPC_COMP_NONE, grpc.GRPC_COMP_GZIP, grpc.GRPC_MAX_FRAMES, grpc.GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE
end
```

Output:

```text
10 0 5
3 true
true hello
true two
true three three three
4 true Bearer abc
2
trace-bin 2
4 AQI=
4
false NOT_FOUND: there is no user 42
100%25 done 100% done
14 14 2
DEADLINE_EXCEEDED UNAUTHENTICATED
1 2 3 6
8 9 10 11
12 13 14 15
application/grpc application/grpc+proto application/grpc+json
0 1 100000 4194304
```

grpc-TLS.salam

```salam
import grpc
import net.tcp

func echo(c: i64):
    mut ok := false
    _ := grpc.SendStr(c, grpc.RecvStr(c, ok))
end

func main:
    mut ch := grpc.DialTLS("api.example.com", 443)
    if not grpc.ChannelOk(ch):
        println grpc.ChannelError(ch)
        ret
    end
    grpc.SetGzip(ch, true)
    mut result := grpc.Status {}
    println grpc.UnaryCallStr(ch, "/demo.Echo/Say", "hello", result)
    grpc.CloseChannel(ch)

    grpc.RegisterMethod("/demo.Echo/Say", echo)
    mut s := grpc.NewServer(50051)
    if grpc.Listen(s):
        grpc.Serve(s)
    end
    conn := tcp.Dial("127.0.0.1", 50052)
    _ := grpc.ServeConn(conn.fd)
end
```

# db/sql

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-sql/

Read, check and type SQL without a database: a dialect-aware parser, a schema catalog and typed placeholders.

A query is a string, so a typo in it is found by the database, at run time, on the one code path nobody tested. This package reads the string instead: it lexes and parses SQL for one of four dialects, and when you hand it your schema it also resolves every table and column, names the ones that do not exist, and tells you the type of every placeholder and every column that comes back. Nothing here connects to a database; it is all static, so it belongs in a test or in a build step.

It is the same idea as sqlc in Go, with the schema taken from the SQL you already write: the `CREATE TABLE` statements in your migrations are the catalog, so there is no second file to keep in step.

Things that catch people out:

- The dialect is not advice. `?` is a placeholder in SQLite and MySQL and a plain operator in PostgreSQL, which numbers its own as `$1`; `"name"` is a quoted name everywhere except MySQL, where it is a string; `AUTOINCREMENT`, `AUTO_INCREMENT` and `GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY` belong to one engine each. Pass the dialect you will really run against.

- `Check` only resolves names when the statement parses. A report with a syntax error in it says nothing about the columns, so fix the syntax first and run it again.

- A table whose columns are not known, from `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` or a view the package could not read, is left open: columns on it are never reported as missing. No news is not always good news.

- `Apply` reads the DDL in order, so a view has to come after the tables it selects from, exactly as it does in the database.

- Diagnostic messages are English in both language modes; the codes are the same, so a Persian program can match on `code`.

- `Placeholders` hands back a `Vector<str>` you own: free the vector, and the strings in it, when you are done.

- Salam lets a name contain spaces; SQL does not. `SELECT family name FROM t` is a column and an alias, not one name, and it is accepted without complaint - which is worth knowing when the names are Persian, since those are often two words. Quote them: `SELECT "family name" FROM t`.

## Start here: one walk from a schema to checked queries

The six sections after this one take the package apart piece by piece. This one puts it together, in the order you would actually meet it on a project that already has a database and a pile of query strings. The program below is the whole arc, and you can run it as it stands - no server, no connection, nothing to set up.

db-sql-tutorial.salam

```salam
import db.sql
import str

mut g_schema := sql.Catalog {}

func str_of(n: int): str:
    ret str.FromInt(n as i64)
end

func step(n: int, title: str):
    println ""
    println "step " + str_of(n) + ": " + title
end

func try_query(q: str):
    mut r := sql.Check(q, g_schema)
    if r.ok and r.warnings == 0:
        println "  ok   " + q
    else:
        println "  bad  " + q
        mut i := 0
        until i < r.items.len():
            d := r.items.get(i)
            println "       " + d.code + " " + d.message
            if not str.IsEmpty(d.help):
                println "       " + d.help
            end
            i = i + 1
        end
    end
    sql.FreeReport(r)
end

func main:
    step(1, "the schema you already have")
    g_schema = sql.NewCatalog(sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE))
    defer sql.FreeCatalog(g_schema)
    mut ddl := sql.Apply(g_schema, """
        CREATE TABLE authors (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            name TEXT NOT NULL,
            country TEXT
        );
        CREATE TABLE books (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            author_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            title TEXT NOT NULL,
            year INTEGER,
            price REAL
        );
    """)
    println "  loaded " + str_of(sql.TableCount(g_schema)) + " tables, " + str_of(sql.ColumnCount(g_schema, "books")) + " columns on books"
    sql.FreeReport(ddl)

    step(2, "the queries you already have")
    try_query("SELECT id, titles FROM books WHERE author_id = ?")
    try_query("SELECT b.title, a.nationality FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id = b.author_id")
    try_query("INSERT INTO books (title) VALUES (?)")
    try_query("SELECT id FROM books WHERE year = 'recent'")
    try_query("DELETE FROM books")

    step(3, "the same five, put right")
    try_query("SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE author_id = ?")
    try_query("SELECT b.title, a.country FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id = b.author_id")
    try_query("INSERT INTO books (author_id, title) VALUES (?, ?)")
    try_query("SELECT id FROM books WHERE year = 2024")
    try_query("DELETE FROM books WHERE id = ?")

    step(4, "what a query takes and gives back")
    mut a := sql.Analyze("SELECT books.title, books.price, authors.country FROM books JOIN authors ON authors.id = books.author_id WHERE books.year > ?", g_schema)
    println "  it is a " + sql.StmtKindName(a.kind) + " on " + a.table
    p := a.params.get(0)
    println "  takes " + p.column + " as " + sql.SalamType(p.kind, p.not_null)
    mut i := 0
    until i < a.results.len():
        c := a.results.get(i)
        println "  gives " + c.name + " as " + sql.SalamType(c.kind, not c.nullable)
        i = i + 1
    end
    sql.FreeAnalysis(a)

    step(5, "the values go in safely")
    mut args := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddText(args, "O'Brien")
    sql.AddInt(args, 1988 as i64)
    mut rep := sql.Report {}
    filled := sql.Fill("INSERT INTO books (title, year) VALUES (?, ?)", args, sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE), rep)
    println "  " + filled
    sql.FreeReport(rep)
    sql.FreeArgs(args)

    step(6, "or let it write the code for you")
    mut gen := sql.Report {}
    mut queries := sql.ParseQueries("""
-- name: BooksByAuthor :many
SELECT id, title, year FROM books WHERE author_id = ?;
""", gen)
    code := sql.Generate("store", queries, g_schema, gen)
    println code
    sql.FreeQueries(queries)
    sql.FreeReport(gen)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text

step 1: the schema you already have
  loaded 2 tables, 5 columns on books

step 2: the queries you already have
  bad  SELECT id, titles FROM books WHERE author_id = ?
       SQL311 no column named "titles" in this statement
       did you mean "title"?
  bad  SELECT b.title, a.nationality FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id = b.author_id
       SQL311 "a" has no column "nationality"
  bad  INSERT INTO books (title) VALUES (?)
       SQL315 "author_id" is NOT NULL with no default and this INSERT leaves it out
       add it to the column list and to every row
  bad  SELECT id FROM books WHERE year = 'recent'
       SQL330 "year" is int and this compares it with text
       a number goes here without quotes
  bad  DELETE FROM books
       SQL320 this DELETE has no WHERE clause and removes every row
       add a WHERE clause, or use TRUNCATE when that is what you mean

step 3: the same five, put right
  ok   SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE author_id = ?
  ok   SELECT b.title, a.country FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id = b.author_id
  ok   INSERT INTO books (author_id, title) VALUES (?, ?)
  ok   SELECT id FROM books WHERE year = 2024
  ok   DELETE FROM books WHERE id = ?

step 4: what a query takes and gives back
  it is a select on books
  takes year as option.Option<i64>
  gives title as str
  gives price as option.Option<f64>
  gives country as option.Option<str>

step 5: the values go in safely
  INSERT INTO books (title, year) VALUES ('O''Brien', 1988)

step 6: or let it write the code for you
package store

import db
import db.sql
import mem
import option

struct BooksByAuthorRow:
    pub id: i64 = 0 as i64
    pub title: str = ""
    pub year: option.Option<i64> = option.None() as option.Option<i64>
end

func fill_query(c: dyn db.Connection, raw: str, a: sql.Args): str:
    mut rep := sql.Report {}
    out := sql.Fill(raw, a, sql.DialectNamed(c.Kind()), rep)
    sql.FreeReport(rep)
    ret out
end

pub func BooksByAuthor(c: dyn db.Connection, author_id: i64): Vector<BooksByAuthorRow>:
    mut a := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddInt(a, author_id)
    q := fill_query(c, "SELECT id, title, year FROM books WHERE author_id = ?", a)
    sql.FreeArgs(a)
    mut rows := Vector {} as Vector<BooksByAuthorRow>
    r := c.Query(q)
    if r.Ok():
        until r.Next():
            mut out := BooksByAuthorRow {}
            out.id = r.Int64(0)
            out.title = r.Text(1)
            if r.IsNull(2):
                out.year = option.None() as option.Option<i64>
            else:
                out.year = option.Some(r.Int64(2))
            end
            rows.push(out)
        end
        r.Close()
    end
    mem.Free(q as void*)
    ret rows
end
```

Step 1 is the only setup there is. You do not write a schema description for this package; you hand it the `CREATE TABLE` statements you already have. Point `Apply` at your migration files in order and the catalog is the schema your program really runs against.

Step 2 is why you came. Five queries of the kind that live in every codebase, and five different ways of being wrong: a column name remembered in the plural, a column that belongs to the other table in the join, an INSERT that leaves out a NOT NULL column with no default, a number compared against a quoted word, and a DELETE with no WHERE. Each one is found without a database, and each one names what to do about it. The last is a warning rather than an error, because sometimes clearing a table is the intent - the point is that you decide, in a review, rather than at two in the morning.

Step 3 is the same five, put right, and it is worth running your own queries through this pair of steps once before reading any further. The quickest way is the command: `salam sql check src --schema=db` reads the SQL out of your `.salam` files as well as your `.sql` ones.

Step 4 is where it stops being a linter. Once the names resolve, the types follow: the placeholder is an `option.Option<i64>` because `year` can be null, `title` is a plain `str` because the column is NOT NULL. That is the signature your code should have, derived from the schema instead of remembered.

Step 5 is the one that prevents the oldest bug in the book. `Fill` writes the values into the query with the quoting the engine wants - note what happens to the apostrophe in `O'Brien` - and because the query was lexed first, a `?` that lives inside a string is left alone.

Step 6 is the part you can stop writing by hand. Annotate a query with a name and a kind and the generated function has the parameters and the row struct that step 4 worked out. Run it with `salam sql generate queries --schema=db --output=gen/store.salam`.

Two things to carry away. The schema is the DDL you already have, so nothing can drift out of step with it. And every one of these checks happens before the program runs, which is the only time a query mistake is cheap.

## Reading a query without a database

`Lint` parses one statement, or a whole script of them separated by `;`, and returns a `Report`. `r.ok` is false as soon as there is an error; `ReportText` renders the whole list the way a compiler would, with the line, the column, the message and a help line. Most of the dialect rules are in here: the same string is fine for SQLite and wrong for PostgreSQL, and the report says which part of it to change.

db-sql-guide-lint.salam

```salam
import db.sql

func report(title: str, query: str, d: sql.Dialect):
    mut r := sql.Lint(query, d)
    if r.ok:
        println title, "ok"
    else:
        println title, sql.ReportText(r)
    end
    sql.FreeReport(r)
end

func main:
    sqlite := sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE)
    mysql := sql.DialectOf(sql.MYSQL)
    postgres := sql.DialectOf(sql.POSTGRES)

    report("plain select: ", "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?", sqlite)
    report("typo:         ", "SELECT id FROM users WHERE", sqlite)
    report("wrong marker: ", "SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = ?", postgres)
    report("mysql only:   ", "SELECT id FROM users WHERE name ILIKE 'a%'", mysql)
    report("sqlite only:  ", "CREATE TABLE t (id INT AUTO_INCREMENT)", sqlite)

    println "placeholders: ", sql.ParamCount("UPDATE users SET name = ?, age = ? WHERE id = ?", sqlite)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
plain select:  ok
typo:          error[SQL105] 1:27: expected a value, found the end of the statement
  help: a column name, a literal, a function call or a placeholder goes here
wrong marker:  error[SQL201] 1:33: '?' is not a placeholder in postgres
  help: postgres numbers its placeholders: $1, $2
mysql only:    error[SQL205] 1:33: ILIKE is postgres only
  help: use LOWER(x) LIKE LOWER(y), or LIKE on a case-insensitive column
sqlite only:   error[SQL211] 1:24: AUTO_INCREMENT is a mysql keyword
  help: sqlite spells it AUTOINCREMENT
placeholders:  3
```

The compiler ships the same checks as a command, so a whole project can be
checked without writing a program for it: `salam sql check src --schema=db`
reads the `.sql` files under `src`, and the SQL string literals out of
its `.salam` files, and reports them with the position in the Salam source. Without
`--dialect` each Salam file is read with the engine it imports, so a tree that mixes
`db/sqlite` and `db/mysql` is checked correctly with no flags at all. A
query assembled from pieces - glued with `+` or `.concat`, or any literal whose
only fault is that it stops in the middle - is a fragment rather than a statement, so it is
counted and skipped instead of being reported as a syntax error. The count is in the summary,
so nothing is checked silently; a fragment is also the reason to bind values as placeholders
instead of pasting them in.

Every diagnostic carries a code. `SQL0xx` is lexical, `SQL1xx` is syntax, `SQL2xx` is a dialect rule, `SQL3xx` is a name or a count that does not match the schema. Match on the code when you want to allow one particular thing; never match on the message.

## Your migrations are the schema

`Apply` runs DDL into a `Catalog`: `CREATE TABLE` adds a table with its columns, their types, their NOT NULL and PRIMARY KEY, `ALTER TABLE` adds, drops and renames, `DROP` removes, and `CREATE VIEW` records the view's columns. Feed it the same strings you give `db.AddMigration` and the catalog is the schema the program really has.

db-sql-guide-catalog.salam

```salam
import db.sql

mut g_schema := sql.Catalog {}

func check(query: str):
    mut r := sql.Check(query, g_schema)
    if r.ok and r.warnings == 0:
        println "ok   ", query
    else:
        println "bad  ", query
        println sql.ReportText(r)
    end
    sql.FreeReport(r)
end

func main:
    g_schema = sql.NewCatalog(sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE))
    defer sql.FreeCatalog(g_schema)

    mut ddl := sql.Apply(g_schema, """
        CREATE TABLE users (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            email TEXT NOT NULL,
            name TEXT
        );
        CREATE TABLE orders (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            total REAL NOT NULL
        );
    """)
    println "schema loaded:", ddl.ok, " tables:", sql.TableCount(g_schema)
    sql.FreeReport(ddl)

    check("SELECT u.email, o.total FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id = ?")
    check("SELECT id, mail FROM users")
    check("SELECT id FROM user")
    check("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)")
    check("DELETE FROM orders")
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
schema loaded: true  tables: 2
ok    SELECT u.email, o.total FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id = ?
bad   SELECT id, mail FROM users
error[SQL311] 1:12: no column named "mail" in this statement
  help: did you mean "email"?
bad   SELECT id FROM user
error[SQL317] 1:16: no table named "user"
  help: did you mean "users"?
bad   INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)
error[SQL315] 1:1: "email" is NOT NULL with no default and this INSERT leaves it out
  help: add it to the column list and to every row
bad   DELETE FROM orders
warning[SQL320] 1:1: this DELETE has no WHERE clause and removes every row
  help: add a WHERE clause, or use TRUNCATE when that is what you mean
```

With a catalog, `Check` resolves names: an unknown column or table is an error with the closest real name offered, a column that two joined tables both have is an error until you qualify it, an INSERT is checked against the column list and against the columns that are NOT NULL with no default, and an UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE is a warning, because that is almost never what was meant.

It also reads the types it has: comparing a numeric column with a quoted value that is not a number is a warning on SQLite and MySQL, where it silently never matches or silently becomes zero, and an error on PostgreSQL, which refuses it; a column in the result list of a GROUP BY query that is neither grouped nor aggregated is an error on PostgreSQL and a warning elsewhere, with the same exception those engines make - grouping by a table's whole primary key determines the rest of that table's columns, so they are allowed unqualified; and `USING (col)` is checked on both sides of the join. A subquery that returns
the wrong number of columns for the comparison it sits in, an `ORDER BY 3` when the
statement returns two columns, a `LIMIT` that is not a number, an aggregate in
`WHERE` rather than `HAVING`, the same column assigned twice in one
`SET`, and two result columns given the same alias are all reported too.

## Putting the values in safely

The three SQL drivers do not all offer prepared statements - only db/sqlite has `Prepare` and `Bind*` - so code that has to run on MySQL or PostgreSQL ends up gluing values into the SQL by hand, which is where quoting mistakes become injections. `Fill` does that one job properly: it lexes the query, so it knows which `?` is a placeholder and which one is a character inside a string, checks that the number of values matches, and writes each value the way the dialect wants it.

db-sql-guide-fill.salam

```salam
import db.sql

func show(query: str, a: sql.Args, d: sql.Dialect):
    mut r := sql.Report {}
    out := sql.Fill(query, a, d, r)
    if r.ok:
        println out
    else:
        println sql.ReportText(r)
    end
    sql.FreeReport(r)
end

func main:
    sqlite := sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE)
    postgres := sql.DialectOf(sql.POSTGRES)

    mut row := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddText(row, "O'Brien")
    sql.AddInt(row, 41 as i64)
    sql.AddBool(row, true)
    sql.AddNull(row)
    show("INSERT INTO users (name, age, paid, note) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", row, sqlite)
    show("INSERT INTO users (name, age, paid, note) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)", row, postgres)
    sql.FreeArgs(row)

    mut attack := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddText(attack, "x' OR '1'='1")
    show("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?", attack, sqlite)
    sql.FreeArgs(attack)

    mut one := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddInt(one, 7 as i64)
    show("SELECT id FROM notes WHERE body = '?' AND id = ?", one, sqlite)
    show("SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = ? AND org = ?", one, sqlite)
    sql.FreeArgs(one)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
INSERT INTO users (name, age, paid, note) VALUES ('O''Brien', 41, 1, NULL)
INSERT INTO users (name, age, paid, note) VALUES ('O''Brien', 41, TRUE, NULL)
SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = 'x'' OR ''1''=''1'
SELECT id FROM notes WHERE body = '?' AND id = 7
error[SQL400] 1:1: this query takes 2 values but got 1
  help: add or remove an argument so the two agree
```

A text value is wrapped in single quotes with every quote doubled, and on MySQL a backslash is doubled as well, because MySQL reads backslashes as escapes and the other two do not. A boolean is `1` or `0` on SQLite and MySQL and `TRUE` or `FALSE` on PostgreSQL; a null is `NULL`; numbers are written plainly. The `'?'` in the fourth query stays as it was, which a search-and-replace over the string would have got wrong.

This is substitution, not a prepared statement: the database still parses one complete statement, and there is no plan reuse. Where the driver can prepare and bind, as sqlite can, that is still the better tool. Where it cannot, this is the safe way to get the values in, and it is one audited function rather than a quoting rule repeated at every call site.

## The type of every placeholder

`Analyze` does everything `Check` does and also hands back what the query takes and what it returns. Each `Param` says which column it was compared with, in which table, and the type that column has; each `ResultCol` says the name the column comes back under, its type, and whether it can be null. `SalamType` turns that into the Salam type to read it into, so a LEFT JOIN gives you `option.Option<i64>` where an inner join gives you `i64`.

db-sql-guide-analyze.salam

```salam
import db.sql

func describe(query: str, schema: sql.Catalog):
    mut a := sql.Analyze(query, schema)
    println query
    println "  statement:", sql.StmtKindName(a.kind), "on", a.table
    mut i := 0
    until i < a.params.len():
        p := a.params.get(i)
        println "  param", p.ordinal, "is", p.column, "of type", sql.SalamType(p.kind, p.not_null)
        i = i + 1
    end
    mut j := 0
    until j < a.results.len():
        c := a.results.get(j)
        println "  column", c.name, "comes back as", sql.SalamType(c.kind, not c.nullable)
        j = j + 1
    end
    sql.FreeAnalysis(a)
end

func main:
    mut schema := sql.NewCatalog(sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE))
    defer sql.FreeCatalog(schema)
    mut ddl := sql.Apply(schema, """
        CREATE TABLE users (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            email TEXT NOT NULL,
            name TEXT,
            age INTEGER
        );
    """)
    sql.FreeReport(ddl)

    describe("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE email = ? AND age > ?", schema)
    describe("INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?, ?) RETURNING id", schema)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE email = ? AND age > ?
  statement: select on users
  param 1 is email of type str
  param 2 is age of type option.Option<i64>
  column id comes back as i64
  column name comes back as option.Option<str>
INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?, ?) RETURNING id
  statement: insert on users
  param 1 is email of type str
  param 2 is name of type option.Option<str>
  column id comes back as i64
```

That is enough to generate the binding code for a query, or to assert in a test that a query still takes and returns what the code around it believes. Placeholders are numbered in the order they appear, which is the order the driver binds them; for PostgreSQL the ordinal is the number in the `$n` itself, and a gap in those numbers is an error of its own.

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Is this SQL well formed for my engine? | `Lint` |
| How many values does it bind? | `ParamCount`, `Placeholders` |
| Load the schema | `NewCatalog`, `Apply` |
| Do the tables and columns exist? | `Check` |
| What does it take and return? | `Analyze` |
| Which Salam type reads a column? | `SalamType` |
| Put the values into the SQL safely | `NewArgs`, `Add*`, `Fill` |
| Look around the schema | `TableCount`, `TableName`, `ColumnCount`, `ColumnAt`, `HasTable`, `HasColumn` |

## Generating the query functions

With the schema and the analysis in place, the last step is mechanical, so the package does it: annotate a `.sql` file the way sqlc does and `Generate` writes the Salam for it - a row struct per query, a typed function per query, each one checked against the schema as it is generated.

db-sql-guide-generate.salam

```salam
import db.sql

func main:
    mut schema := sql.NewCatalog(sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE))
    defer sql.FreeCatalog(schema)
    mut ddl := sql.Apply(schema, """
        CREATE TABLE users (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            email TEXT NOT NULL,
            name TEXT
        );
    """)
    sql.FreeReport(ddl)

    queries := """
-- name: GetUser :one
SELECT id, email, name FROM users WHERE email = ?;

-- name: CreateUser :exec
INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?, ?);
"""
    mut r := sql.Report {}
    mut parsed := sql.ParseQueries(queries, r)
    println "queries:", parsed.len()
    code := sql.Generate("store", parsed, schema, r)
    if r.ok:
        println code
    else:
        println sql.ReportText(r)
    end
    sql.FreeQueries(parsed)
    sql.FreeReport(r)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
queries: 2
package store

import db
import db.sql
import mem
import option

struct GetUserRow:
    pub id: i64 = 0 as i64
    pub email: str = ""
    pub name: option.Option<str> = option.None() as option.Option<str>
end

func fill_query(c: dyn db.Connection, raw: str, a: sql.Args): str:
    mut rep := sql.Report {}
    out := sql.Fill(raw, a, sql.DialectNamed(c.Kind()), rep)
    sql.FreeReport(rep)
    ret out
end

pub func GetUser(c: dyn db.Connection, email: str, ok &: bool): GetUserRow:
    mut a := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddText(a, email)
    q := fill_query(c, "SELECT id, email, name FROM users WHERE email = ?", a)
    sql.FreeArgs(a)
    mut out := GetUserRow {}
    ok = false
    r := c.Query(q)
    if r.Ok():
        if r.Next():
            out.id = r.Int64(0)
            out.email = r.Text(1)
            if r.IsNull(2):
                out.name = option.None() as option.Option<str>
            else:
                out.name = option.Some(r.Text(2))
            end
            ok = true
        end
        r.Close()
    end
    mem.Free(q as void*)
    ret out
end

pub func CreateUser(c: dyn db.Connection, email: str, name: str): bool:
    mut a := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddText(a, email)
    sql.AddText(a, name)
    q := fill_query(c, "INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?, ?)", a)
    sql.FreeArgs(a)
    done := c.Exec(q) == 0
    mem.Free(q as void*)
    ret done
end
```

The kinds are `:one` (the first row, with an `ok &: bool` out parameter), `:many` (a `Vector` of rows), `:exec` (a bool) and `:execrows` (the number of rows changed). Parameters are named after the column each placeholder is compared with and typed from it; a column that can be null comes back as `option.Option<T>` and is read through `IsNull`. A query that does not resolve against the schema stops the generation with the query's name in the message, so a typo never reaches the generated file.

The command is `salam sql generate queries --schema=db --output=gen/store.salam --package=store`. The generated file takes a `dyn db.Connection`, so one set of functions serves SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL, and it picks each dialect's quoting from `c.Kind()` at run time.

## Types

### `Param`

```salam
struct Param
```

One placeholder, and the column it is bound against.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `marker` | `str = ""` | The placeholder as written: `?`, `$2`, `:name`. |
| `ordinal` | `int = 0` | Its position, counting from 1; for `$n` it is the number itself. |
| `table` | `str = ""` | The table of the column it was compared with, when there was one. |
| `column` | `str = ""` | The column it was compared with, when there was one. |
| `kind` | `int = 7` | That column's `TYPE_*` kind, or `TYPE_UNKNOWN`. |
| `not_null` | `bool = false` | True when that column cannot be null. |

db-sql-Methods.salam

```salam
import db.sql

func main:
    sqlite := sql.DialectOf(sql.SQLITE)
    println sqlite.name, sql.DialectNamed("postgresql").name, sql.DialectOf(sql.MARIADB).name

    mut bad := sql.Lint("SELECT id FROM t WHERE", sqlite)
    println bad.ok, bad.errors, bad.warnings, bad.statements
    println sql.DiagText(bad.items.get(0))
    sql.FreeReport(bad)

    println sql.ParamCount("SELECT a FROM t WHERE b = ? AND c = ?", sqlite)
    mut marks := sql.Placeholders("SELECT a FROM t WHERE b = ? AND c = ?", sqlite)
    println marks.len(), marks.get(0)
    marks.free()

    mut cat := sql.NewCatalog(sqlite)
    mut ddl := sql.Apply(cat, """
        CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL, age INTEGER);
    """)
    println "schema:", ddl.ok, sql.TableCount(cat), sql.TableName(cat, 0)
    sql.FreeReport(ddl)
    println sql.HasTable(cat, "users"), sql.HasColumn(cat, "users", "email"), sql.ColumnCount(cat, "users")
    col := sql.ColumnAt(cat, "users", 1)
    println col.name, col.type_name, sql.KindName(col.kind), col.not_null, col.primary

    mut miss := sql.Check("SELECT nope FROM users", cat)
    println sql.ReportText(miss)
    sql.FreeReport(miss)

    mut a := sql.Analyze("SELECT id, age FROM users WHERE email = ?", cat)
    println sql.StmtKindName(a.kind), a.table, a.params.len(), a.results.len()
    p := a.params.get(0)
    println p.marker, p.ordinal, p.table + "." + p.column, sql.SalamType(p.kind, p.not_null)
    r := a.results.get(1)
    println r.name, sql.KindName(r.kind), r.nullable
    sql.FreeAnalysis(a)

    mut args := sql.NewArgs()
    sql.AddInt(args, 3 as i64)
    sql.AddText(args, "a'b")
    sql.AddBool(args, false)
    sql.AddFloat(args, 2.5)
    sql.AddNull(args)
    println sql.ArgCount(args)
    mut err := sql.Report {}
    filled := sql.Fill("INSERT INTO t (a, b, c, d, e) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", args, sqlite, err)
    println filled
    sql.FreeReport(err)
    sql.FreeArgs(args)

    sql.FreeCatalog(cat)
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
sqlite postgres mariadb
false 1 0 0
error[SQL105] 1:23: expected a value, found the end of the statement
  help: a column name, a literal, a function call or a placeholder goes here
2
2 ?
schema: true 1 users
true true 3
email TEXT text true false
error[SQL311] 1:8: no column named "nope" in this statement
select users 1 2
? 1 users.email str
age int true
5
INSERT INTO t (a, b, c, d, e) VALUES (3, 'a''b', 0, 2.5, NULL)
```

### `ResultCol`

```salam
struct ResultCol
```

One column of what the statement returns.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name it comes back under: the alias, or the column's own name. |
| `table` | `str = ""` | The table it came from, when it is a plain column. |
| `kind` | `int = 7` | Its `TYPE_*` kind. |
| `nullable` | `bool = true` | True when it can come back null, which an outer join makes true for the whole of its side. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Analysis`

```salam
struct Analysis
```

What `Analyze` works out about one statement.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = true` | True when nothing is an error. |
| `kind` | `int = 0` | Which `STMT_*` statement it is. |
| `table` | `str = ""` | The table it reads from or writes to. |
| `params` | `Vector` | Its placeholders, in binding order. |
| `results` | `Vector` | The columns it returns. |
| `report` | `Report` | The diagnostics, as `Check` would give them. |
| `owned` | `Vector` | The strings the analysis owns. `FreeAnalysis` releases them; nothing else should read it. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Args`

```salam
struct Args
```

The values a query binds, in order. Build one with `NewArgs` and the `Add*` functions, and release it with `FreeArgs`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kinds` | `Vector` | Which kind each value is; one entry per value. |
| `ints` | `Vector` | The integer values, by the same index. |
| `floats` | `Vector` | The floating point values, by the same index. |
| `texts` | `Vector` | The text values, by the same index. `AddText` copies the string, so the caller keeps its own. |
| `bools` | `Vector` | The boolean values, by the same index. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Dialect`

```salam
struct Dialect
```

Everything that differs between the engines: how names and strings are quoted, which placeholders exist, which clauses are supported. Build one with `DialectOf` or `DialectNamed`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int = 0` | Which engine: `SQLITE`, `MYSQL`, `MARIADB` or `POSTGRES`. |
| `name` | `str = "sqlite"` | The engine's name, as it appears in diagnostics. |
| `double_quoted_string` | `bool = false` | True when `"x"` is a string instead of a name (MySQL). |
| `backtick_ident` | `bool = false` | True when ``x`` is a name (MySQL, SQLite). |
| `bracket_ident` | `bool = false` | True when `[x]` is a name (SQLite). |
| `hash_comment` | `bool = false` | True when `#` starts a comment (MySQL). |
| `dollar_string` | `bool = false` | True when `$tag$ ... $tag$` is a string (PostgreSQL). |
| `backslash_escape` | `bool = false` | True when a backslash escapes inside a string (MySQL). |
| `qmark_param` | `bool = false` | True when `?` is a placeholder. |
| `numbered_param` | `bool = false` | True when `$1` is a placeholder. |
| `named_param` | `bool = false` | True when `:name` and `@name` are placeholders. |
| `returning` | `bool = false` | True when RETURNING is supported. |
| `on_conflict` | `bool = false` | True when ON CONFLICT is supported. |
| `on_duplicate` | `bool = false` | True when ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE is supported. |
| `limit_comma` | `bool = false` | True when `LIMIT start, count` is supported. |
| `ilike` | `bool = false` | True when ILIKE is supported. |
| `colon_cast` | `bool = false` | True when `x::type` is a cast. |
| `autoincrement_word` | `str = ""` | The engine's own word for an auto-incrementing key. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Diag`

```salam
struct Diag
```

One diagnostic: what is wrong, where, and what to write instead.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `int = 0` | `ERROR`, `WARNING` or `NOTE`. |
| `code` | `str = ""` | The code, for example `SQL311`. Match on this, not on the message. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | What is wrong, in one line. |
| `help` | `str = ""` | What to write instead; empty when there is nothing to suggest. |
| `line` | `int = 1` | The line it starts on, counting from 1. |
| `col` | `int = 1` | The column it starts at, counting from 1. |
| `offset` | `int = 0` | The byte offset into the SQL it starts at. |
| `length` | `int = 0` | How many bytes it covers. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Report`

```salam
struct Report
```

The diagnostics of one run, in the order they were found.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = true` | True when nothing is an error. Warnings do not clear it. |
| `errors` | `int = 0` | How many errors there are. |
| `warnings` | `int = 0` | How many warnings there are. |
| `statements` | `int = 0` | How many statements parsed, which is how a caller counts what it checked. |
| `items` | `Vector` | The diagnostics themselves. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Column`

```salam
struct Column
```

One column of the schema.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | Its name, as the schema spells it. |
| `type_name` | `str = ""` | Its type, as the schema spells it. |
| `kind` | `int = 7` | Which of the `TYPE_*` kinds that type is. |
| `not_null` | `bool = false` | True when it cannot be null. |
| `has_default` | `bool = false` | True when it has a default, which is what lets an INSERT leave it out. |
| `primary` | `bool = false` | True when it is part of the primary key. |
| `auto` | `bool = false` | True when the engine fills it in. |
| `generated` | `bool = false` | True when it is computed and cannot be written. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Table`

```salam
struct Table
```

One table or view of the schema.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | Its name. |
| `is_view` | `bool = false` | True when it is a view. |
| `open` | `bool = false` | True when its columns are not known, which turns off column checking for it. |
| `columns` | `Vector` | Its columns, in declaration order. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Catalog`

```salam
struct Catalog
```

The schema a query is checked against. Build one with `NewCatalog` and fill it with `Apply`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `d` | `Dialect` | The dialect the DDL and the queries are read with. |
| `tables` | `Vector` | The tables and views it holds. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam

### `Query`

```salam
struct Query
```

One annotated query read out of a `.sql` file.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | The name from the `-- name:` header, used for the generated function and its row struct. |
| `kind` | `int = 0` | One of the `Q_*` kinds. |
| `text` | `str = ""` | The SQL itself, with any trailing `;` removed. |
| `line` | `int = 1` | The line its header is on, so a diagnostic can point back at the file. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-sql-Methods.salam
