# db/redis

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-redis/

A Redis client: keys and values, hashes, lists, sets and publishing.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add db.redis`

Redis is an in memory database for caches, sessions, counters, queues and leaderboards. This package speaks the Redis protocol directly over a socket, with no outside library: one function per common command for strings, hashes, lists and sets, plus `Command`, which sends any other command with its arguments and hands back the raw reply. This page starts with a tutorial; the full reference of every function and type comes after it.

## Tutorial: a link shortener in twelve steps

The steps below build the storage of a small link shortener: link records, click counters, a list of recent links, unique visitors and a leaderboard. Each step is a complete program, and the output under it is what it printed against a real Redis 7.4. Run them in order, because each step uses the keys the earlier ones left behind. The last step deletes everything again.

First start a server with a password. With Docker that is one command:

```salam
docker run -p 6379:6379 redis:7.4 redis-server --requirepass s3cret
```

The programs connect to `127.0.0.1:6379` and log in with `s3cret`. To start over at any point, run `docker exec` on the container with `redis-cli -a s3cret flushall`, then begin again at step 1.

## 1. Connect and log in

`Connect` opens one TCP connection and returns a `Client`. `Ok` tells you whether that worked and `Error` says why not. A server with a password refuses every command until `Auth` succeeds, which is why the first `Ping` is false. `Select` switches to another numbered database; a default server has 16, numbered 0 to 15.

db-redis-connect.salam

```salam
import db.redis

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    if not redis.Ok(c):
        println "cannot reach Redis:", redis.Error(c)
        ret 1
    end
    defer redis.Close(c)

    println "ping before login:", redis.Ping(c)
    println "wrong password:", redis.Auth(c, "guess")
    println "right password:", redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")
    println "ping after login:", redis.Ping(c)

    println "database 15:", redis.Select(c, 15)
    println "database 99:", redis.Select(c, 99)
    println "back to 0:", redis.Select(c, 0)

    off := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6390)
    println "port 6390:", redis.Ok(off), redis.Error(off)
end
```

Output:

```text
ping before login: false
wrong password: false
right password: true
ping after login: true
database 15: true
database 99: false
back to 0: true
port 6390: false no connection
```

Every function in this package returns a plain value (a bool, a number, a string or a vector) instead of an error object. When something goes wrong you get the empty value: `false`, 0 or an empty string. Step 10 shows how to tell the cases apart when that matters. Always `Close` a client: it closes the socket and frees the buffer.

## 2. Strings and missing keys

The simplest Redis value is a string under a key. `Set` stores it, `Get` reads it back and `Append` adds to the end. Redis has no NULL: a key is either there or not. `Get` returns an empty string in both cases, so when an empty value is meaningful, ask `Exists`, or send `GET` through `Command` and test the reply with `ReplyIsNil`.

db-redis-strings.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import str

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    redis.Set(c, "site:name", "Short links")
    redis.Set(c, "site:motto", "")
    println "name:", redis.Get(c, "site:name")
    println "motto: [" + redis.Get(c, "site:motto") + "]", redis.Exists(c, "site:motto")
    println "owner: [" + redis.Get(c, "site:owner") + "]", redis.Exists(c, "site:owner")

    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    args.push("GET")
    args.push("site:owner")
    r := redis.Command(c, args)
    println "GET site:owner is nil:", redis.ReplyIsNil(r)
    redis.FreeReply(r)

    tricky := "x\r\nFLUSHALL\r\n"
    redis.Set(c, "site:tricky", tricky)
    println "stored bytes:", redis.StrLen(c, "site:tricky"), "of", tricky.len()
    println "same text back:", str.Equals(redis.Get(c, "site:tricky"), tricky)
    println "name still there:", redis.Exists(c, "site:name")
    redis.Del(c, "site:tricky")

    println "length after append:", redis.Append(c, "site:name", " for Salam")
    println "name:", redis.Get(c, "site:name")
end
```

Output:

```text
name: Short links
motto: [] true
owner: [] false
GET site:owner is nil: true
stored bytes: 13 of 13
same text back: true
name still there: true
length after append: 21
name: Short links for Salam
```

There is no injection to worry about. Each argument travels as a length followed by its bytes, so a value with spaces, quotes or line breaks is stored exactly as it is and can never be read as a second command. The one limit is the NUL byte: Salam strings end at the first one, so keep binary data out of these functions or encode it first, with `Base64EncodeBytes` from encoding for instance.

## 3. Records in hashes

A hash holds named fields under one key, which is the natural place for a record. `Incr` on a counter key hands out ids that never repeat, even with many programs adding links at once. `HSet` writes one field, `HGetAll` reads them all into a `HashMap`, and from there it is one line to fill your own struct. Every value comes back as a string, so convert numbers yourself.

db-redis-hashes.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import conv

struct Link:
    pub id: i64 = 0
    pub url: str = ""
    pub title: str = ""
    pub owner: str = ""
end

func save(c: redis.Client, url: str, title: str, owner: str): i64:
    id := redis.Incr(c, "links:next")
    key := "link:" + conv.FormatInt(id)
    redis.HSet(c, key, "url", url)
    redis.HSet(c, key, "title", title)
    redis.HSet(c, key, "owner", owner)
    ret id
end

func load(c: redis.Client, id: i64): Link:
    m := redis.HGetAll(c, "link:" + conv.FormatInt(id))
    if m.size() == 0:
        ret Link {}
    end
    ret Link { id = id, url = m.get("url"), title = m.get("title"), owner = m.get("owner") }
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    save(c, "https://salamlang.ir", "Salam home", "sara")
    save(c, "https://salamlang.ir/learn/", "Salam course", "omid")
    save(c, "https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam", "Salam on GitHub", "sara")

    repeat 3 in i:
        l := load(c, (i + 1) as i64)
        println l.id, l.title, "->", l.url, "by", l.owner
    end
    println "link 9 found:", load(c, 9).id != 0

    println "fields of link:2:", redis.HLen(c, "link:2")
    println "owner of link:2:", redis.HGet(c, "link:2", "owner")
    redis.HSet(c, "link:2", "note", "for new students")
    println "has note:", redis.HExists(c, "link:2", "note")
    println "note removed:", redis.HDel(c, "link:2", "note")
    println "has note:", redis.HExists(c, "link:2", "note")
end
```

Output:

```text
1 Salam home -> https://salamlang.ir by sara
2 Salam course -> https://salamlang.ir/learn/ by omid
3 Salam on GitHub -> https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam by sara
link 9 found: false
fields of link:2: 3
owner of link:2: omid
has note: true
note removed: true
has note: false
```

`HGetAll` returns an empty map for a key that does not exist, which is how `load` tells a missing link apart. To write several fields in one round trip, send `HSET key f1 v1 f2 v2` with `Command`, as step 9 does.

## 4. Counters

`Incr`, `IncrBy` and `Decr` change a number stored as a string and return the new value. Redis runs each command alone, so two programs counting the same key never lose an update. A key that does not exist counts as 0, so there is nothing to set up first. The value is still a string: `Get` returns its digits and `conv.ParseInt` turns them into a number.

db-redis-counters.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import conv

func click(c: redis.Client, id: int): i64:
    ret redis.Incr(c, "clicks:" + conv.FormatInt(id as i64))
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    click(c, 1)
    click(c, 1)
    click(c, 3)
    click(c, 3)
    println "link 1 clicks:", click(c, 1)
    println "link 2 imported clicks:", redis.IncrBy(c, "clicks:2", 40)
    println "link 2 after a refund:", redis.IncrBy(c, "clicks:2", -2)
    println "link 3 after a bot click is removed:", redis.Decr(c, "clicks:3")

    raw := redis.Get(c, "clicks:2")
    println "stored as text:", raw, "type", redis.Type(c, "clicks:2")
    n := conv.ParseInt(raw)
    println "as a number plus one:", n + 1

    println "next link id would be:", conv.ParseInt(redis.Get(c, "links:next")) + 1
end
```

Output:

```text
link 1 clicks: 3
link 2 imported clicks: 40
link 2 after a refund: 38
link 3 after a bot click is removed: 1
stored as text: 38 type string
as a number plus one: 39
next link id would be: 4
```

## 5. Lists

A list keeps strings in order. `LPush` adds to the front and `RPush` to the end; `LPop` and `RPop` take one off. `LRange` reads a slice by position, both ends included, and negative positions count from the end, so `0, -1` is the whole list. Pushing new ids to the front gives a newest first feed.

db-redis-lists.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import conv

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    repeat 3 in i:
        redis.LPush(c, "links:recent", conv.FormatInt((i + 1) as i64))
    end
    println "recent count:", redis.LLen(c, "links:recent")

    each id in redis.LRange(c, "links:recent", 0, -1):
        println "  link", id, redis.HGet(c, "link:" + id, "title")
    end

    println "newest two:", redis.LRange(c, "links:recent", 0, 1).len()
    println "oldest:", redis.LRange(c, "links:recent", -1, -1).get(0)

    redis.RPush(c, "links:review", "2")
    redis.RPush(c, "links:review", "3")
    println "review first:", redis.LPop(c, "links:review")
    println "review last:", redis.RPop(c, "links:review")
    println "review empty: [" + redis.LPop(c, "links:review") + "]", redis.LLen(c, "links:review")
end
```

Output:

```text
recent count: 3
  link 3 Salam on GitHub
  link 2 Salam course
  link 1 Salam home
newest two: 2
oldest: 1
review first: 2
review last: 3
review empty: [] 0
```

A list that becomes empty is deleted, and popping from it returns an empty string. To keep a feed at a fixed length, follow each push with `LTRIM links:recent 0 99` through `Command`.

## 6. Sets

A set holds each member once. `SAdd` returns 1 for a new member and 0 for one that was already there, which makes it a one step "have I seen this?" check. `SCard` counts the members, `SIsMember` tests one and `SMembers` returns them all.

db-redis-sets.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import sort

func visit(c: redis.Client, link: str, user: str): bool:
    ret redis.SAdd(c, "visitors:" + link, user) == 1
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    println "sara first visit:", visit(c, "1", "sara")
    println "omid first visit:", visit(c, "1", "omid")
    println "sara again:", visit(c, "1", "sara")
    visit(c, "1", "reza")
    visit(c, "3", "sara")

    println "unique visitors of link 1:", redis.SCard(c, "visitors:1")
    println "reza saw link 3:", redis.SIsMember(c, "visitors:3", "reza")

    println "reza removed:", redis.SRem(c, "visitors:1", "reza")
    names := redis.SMembers(c, "visitors:1")
    sort.Sort(names)
    each n in names:
        println "  -", n
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
sara first visit: true
omid first visit: true
sara again: false
unique visitors of link 1: 3
reza saw link 3: false
reza removed: 1
  - omid
  - sara
```

Redis does not keep sets in any order, so sort what `SMembers` returns before you show it. On a set with millions of members, use `SSCAN` through `Command` instead.

## 7. Expiry

Any key can be given a lifetime. `SetEx` stores a string and its lifetime in one command; `Expire` adds one to a key that already exists. `TTL` returns the seconds left, -1 for a key that never expires and -2 for one that is not there. When the time is up Redis deletes the key by itself.

db-redis-expire.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import time

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    redis.SetEx(c, "preview:3", "<b>Salam on GitHub</b>", 600)
    println "preview ttl:", redis.TTL(c, "preview:3")
    println "link ttl:", redis.TTL(c, "link:3")
    println "missing ttl:", redis.TTL(c, "link:99")

    redis.Set(c, "link:3:promo", "half price")
    println "promo expires:", redis.Expire(c, "link:3:promo", 1)
    println "promo now:", redis.Get(c, "link:3:promo")
    time.Sleep(1500)
    println "promo later: [" + redis.Get(c, "link:3:promo") + "]", redis.Exists(c, "link:3:promo")
    println "expire a missing key:", redis.Expire(c, "link:3:promo", 10)

    redis.Set(c, "preview:3", "<b>new preview</b>")
    println "ttl after Set:", redis.TTL(c, "preview:3")
end
```

Output:

```text
preview ttl: 600
link ttl: -1
missing ttl: -2
promo expires: true
promo now: half price
promo later: [] false
expire a missing key: false
ttl after Set: -1
```

Watch the last line: a plain `Set` on a key removes its lifetime. Use `SetEx` again when you replace a value that should keep expiring.

## 8. Any command: a leaderboard

Redis has about two hundred commands and this package has a function for the most common ones. `Command` sends any of them: put the command name and its arguments in a `Vector<str>`. The `Reply` you get back has a type (`REPLY_STRING`, `REPLY_INTEGER`, `REPLY_ARRAY`, `REPLY_NIL`, `REPLY_STATUS` or `REPLY_ERROR`), and you read it with `ReplyStr`, `ReplyInt`, `ReplyArrayLen` and `ReplyArrayGet`. This step uses a sorted set, which has no function of its own, to rank the links by clicks.

db-redis-command.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import conv

func run(c: redis.Client, words: str[]): redis.Reply:
    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    each w in words:
        args.push(w)
    end
    ret redis.Command(c, args)
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    repeat 3 in i:
        id := conv.FormatInt((i + 1) as i64)
        r := run(c, ["ZADD", "links:top", redis.Get(c, "clicks:" + id), id])
        redis.FreeReply(r)
    end

    top := run(c, ["ZREVRANGE", "links:top", "0", "-1", "WITHSCORES"])
    if redis.ReplyType(top) == redis.REPLY_ARRAY:
        mut i := 0
        until i < redis.ReplyArrayLen(top):
            id := redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(top, i))
            score := redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(top, i + 1))
            println score, "clicks:", redis.HGet(c, "link:" + id, "title")
            i += 2
        end
    end
    redis.FreeReply(top)

    rank := run(c, ["ZREVRANK", "links:top", "1"])
    println "link 1 rank:", redis.ReplyInt(rank) + 1, "integer reply:", redis.ReplyType(rank) == redis.REPLY_INTEGER
    redis.FreeReply(rank)

    many := run(c, ["HMGET", "link:1", "title", "owner", "color"])
    repeat redis.ReplyArrayLen(many) in i:
        e := redis.ReplyArrayGet(many, i)
        println "  field", i, "[" + redis.ReplyStr(e) + "]", "nil:", redis.ReplyIsNil(e)
    end
    redis.FreeReply(many)
end
```

Output:

```text
38 clicks: Salam course
3 clicks: Salam home
1 clicks: Salam on GitHub
link 1 rank: 2 integer reply: true
  field 0 [Salam home] nil: false
  field 1 [sara] nil: false
  field 2 [] nil: true
```

Free every reply from `Command` with `FreeReply`. The elements from `ReplyArrayGet` belong to their array and are freed with it, so never free them on their own. A field that is missing comes back as a nil element, as `color` does above.

## 9. Transactions

`MULTI` starts a transaction: the commands after it answer `QUEUED`, and `EXEC` runs them all at once, with nothing from other clients in between. `DISCARD` throws the queue away. Redis does not roll back: if one queued command fails, the others still run, so check each element of the `EXEC` reply when that matters.

db-redis-tx.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import conv

func run(c: redis.Client, words: str[]): str:
    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    each w in words:
        args.push(w)
    end
    r := redis.Command(c, args)
    mut out := redis.ReplyStr(r)
    if redis.ReplyType(r) == redis.REPLY_ARRAY:
        out = "array of " + conv.FormatInt(redis.ReplyArrayLen(r) as i64)
    else if redis.ReplyIsNil(r):
        out = "nil"
    else if redis.ReplyType(r) == redis.REPLY_INTEGER:
        out = conv.FormatInt(redis.ReplyInt(r))
    end
    redis.FreeReply(r)
    ret out
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    println run(c, ["MULTI"])
    println run(c, ["INCR", "links:next"])
    println run(c, ["HSET", "link:4", "url", "https://salamlang.ir/std/", "title", "Salam std", "owner", "omid"])
    println run(c, ["LPUSH", "links:recent", "4"])
    println run(c, ["EXEC"])
    println "link 4:", redis.HGet(c, "link:4", "title"), "next id:", redis.Get(c, "links:next")

    other := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(other)
    redis.Auth(other, "s3cret")

    println run(c, ["WATCH", "link:4"])
    title := redis.HGet(c, "link:4", "title")
    redis.HSet(other, "link:4", "title", "Salam standard library")
    println run(c, ["MULTI"])
    println run(c, ["HSET", "link:4", "title", title + " (checked)"])
    println "exec after a change:", run(c, ["EXEC"])
    println "title kept:", redis.HGet(c, "link:4", "title")

    println run(c, ["MULTI"])
    println run(c, ["INCR", "clicks:4"])
    println run(c, ["DISCARD"])
    println "clicks:4 exists:", redis.Exists(c, "clicks:4")
end
```

Output:

```text
OK
QUEUED
QUEUED
QUEUED
array of 3
link 4: Salam std next id: 4
OK
OK
QUEUED
exec after a change: nil
title kept: Salam standard library
OK
QUEUED
OK
clicks:4 exists: false
```

`WATCH` adds optimistic locking. If another client changes a watched key before `EXEC`, the transaction does not run and `EXEC` answers nil; read the key again and retry. The second client here plays that other user. A transaction lives on its connection, so keep `MULTI` through `EXEC` on one client and one thread.

## 10. Errors

There are two kinds of failure. The server can refuse a command, for a wrong type or a bad argument; the connection stays fine and the reply has type `REPLY_ERROR` with the message in `ReplyStr`. The shortcut functions do not show that message: `Get` on a hash returns an empty string and `Incr` on text returns 0. When you need to know, send the command with `Command`. The other kind is a lost connection, which this step causes on purpose with `CLIENT KILL` from a second client.

db-redis-errors.salam

```salam
import db.redis

func run(c: redis.Client, words: str[]): str:
    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    each w in words:
        args.push(w)
    end
    r := redis.Command(c, args)
    mut out := "ok"
    if not redis.ReplyOk(r):
        out = "no reply: " + redis.Error(c)
    else if redis.ReplyIsError(r):
        out = "server error: " + redis.ReplyStr(r)
    end
    redis.FreeReply(r)
    ret out
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    println "Get on a hash: [" + redis.Get(c, "link:1") + "]"
    println "Incr on text:", redis.Incr(c, "site:name")
    println run(c, ["GET", "link:1"])
    println run(c, ["INCR", "site:name"])
    println run(c, ["HGET", "link:1"])
    println "connection still fine:", redis.Ping(c), "[" + redis.Error(c) + "]"

    admin := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(admin)
    redis.Auth(admin, "s3cret")
    println run(admin, ["CLIENT", "KILL", "TYPE", "normal", "SKIPME", "yes"])

    println "ping after the kill:", redis.Ping(c)
    println "Ok:", redis.Ok(c), "Error:", redis.Error(c)
    println run(c, ["PING"])
end
```

Output:

```text
Get on a hash: []
Incr on text: 0
server error: WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value
server error: ERR value is not an integer or out of range
server error: ERR wrong number of arguments for 'hget' command
connection still fine: true []
ok
ping after the kill: false
Ok: true Error: Server closed the connection
no reply: Server closed the connection
```

After the connection is gone `Ok` still says true, because it only reports whether `Connect` worked. `Error` now holds the reason, every call returns its empty value and `Command` returns a reply that is not `ReplyOk`. The client does not reconnect by itself: close it and call `Connect` again.

## 11. Several threads

A `Client` is one connection with one read buffer, so two threads must never use the same client at once. Give each thread its own, as below. There is no built in pool; for a server that handles many requests, open one client per worker thread and keep it for the life of the thread. The counter comes out exact because Redis applies each `INCR` alone.

db-redis-threads.salam

```salam
import db.redis

const WORKERS := 4
const CLICKS := 250

func worker():
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")
    repeat CLICKS:
        redis.Incr(c, "clicks:4")
        redis.SAdd(c, "visitors:4", "bot")
    end
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")
    redis.Del(c, "clicks:4")

    mut threads := Vector {} as Vector<i64>
    repeat WORKERS:
        threads.push(spawn(worker))
    end
    each t in threads:
        join(t)
    end

    println "clicks on link 4:", redis.Get(c, "clicks:4"), "expected", WORKERS * CLICKS
    println "unique visitors:", redis.SCard(c, "visitors:4")
end
```

Output:

```text
clicks on link 4: 1000 expected 1000
unique visitors: 1
```

## 12. Look around and clean up

`Keys` lists the keys matching a pattern and `Type` says what each one holds. `Keys` walks the whole database in one go and blocks the server meanwhile, which is fine here and a problem on a production server with millions of keys. `SCAN` walks it a page at a time with a cursor; the loop below runs it through `Command`. `FlushDB` deletes every key in the current database.

db-redis-cleanup.salam

```salam
import db.redis
import sort

func scan(c: redis.Client, pattern: str): Vector<str>:
    mut found := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    mut cursor := "0"
    until true:
        mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
        args.push("SCAN")
        args.push(cursor)
        args.push("MATCH")
        args.push(pattern)
        args.push("COUNT")
        args.push("100")
        r := redis.Command(c, args)
        cursor = redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(r, 0))
        page := redis.ReplyArrayGet(r, 1)
        repeat redis.ReplyArrayLen(page) in i:
            found.push(redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(page, i)))
        end
        redis.FreeReply(r)
        if cursor == "0":
            break
        end
    end
    sort.Sort(found)
    ret found
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    keys := redis.Keys(c, "*")
    sort.Sort(keys)
    each k in keys:
        println k, redis.Type(c, k)
    end

    old := scan(c, "visitors:*")
    each k in old:
        redis.Del(c, k)
    end
    println "deleted", old.len(), "visitor sets, left:", scan(c, "visitors:*").len()

    println "flush:", redis.FlushDB(c), "keys left:", redis.Keys(c, "*").len()
end
```

Output:

```text
clicks:1 string
clicks:2 string
clicks:3 string
clicks:4 string
link:1 hash
link:2 hash
link:3 hash
link:4 hash
links:next string
links:recent list
links:top zset
preview:3 string
site:motto string
site:name string
visitors:1 set
visitors:3 set
visitors:4 set
deleted 3 visitor sets, left: 0
flush: true keys left: 0
```

## More

- `Publish` sends a message to every client subscribed to a channel and returns how many got it. This package can publish but cannot subscribe: `Command` reads one reply per command, and a subscriber needs to wait for messages that arrive on their own. For work that must not be lost, use a list as a queue (see below).

- For an ACL user with a name, send `AUTH name password` with `Command`; `Auth` sends only the password.

- Commands such as `HINCRBY`, `SETNX`, `MGET`, `LTRIM`, `ZADD` and `XADD` all go through `Command` in the same way as step 8.

- The connection waits as long as the server takes. Commands that block on purpose, such as `BLPOP`, take their own timeout argument.

## Guide: cache a slow page

The most common use of Redis is a cache in front of something slow. Look for the key first; on a miss, build the value and store it with `SetEx`, so a stale copy disappears by itself. When the source changes, delete the key and the next request rebuilds it. `Exists` rather than an empty `Get` decides the hit, so an empty page can be cached too.

db-redis-cache.salam

```salam
import db.redis

mut renders := 0

func render(id: str): str:
    renders += 1
    ret "<h1>Note " + id + "</h1>"
end

func page(c: redis.Client, id: str): str:
    key := "cache:note:" + id
    if redis.Exists(c, key):
        ret redis.Get(c, key)
    end
    html := render(id)
    redis.SetEx(c, key, html, 60)
    ret html
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    println page(c, "42")
    println page(c, "42")
    println page(c, "7")
    println "rendered", renders, "times for 3 requests"
    println "seconds left:", redis.TTL(c, "cache:note:42")

    redis.Del(c, "cache:note:42")
    println page(c, "42")
    println "rendered", renders, "times after the edit"
    redis.Del(c, "cache:note:42")
    redis.Del(c, "cache:note:7")
end
```

Output:

```text
<h1>Note 42</h1>
<h1>Note 42</h1>
<h1>Note 7</h1>
rendered 2 times for 3 requests
seconds left: 60
<h1>Note 42</h1>
rendered 3 times after the edit
```

## Guide: limit requests per user

A fixed window rate limiter needs one counter per user. `Incr` returns the count, and the first request of a window sets the lifetime, so the counter resets by itself when the window ends. Because `Incr` is atomic, the limit holds even when many server processes check the same user.

db-redis-ratelimit.salam

```salam
import db.redis

func allow(c: redis.Client, user: str, limit: i64, seconds: int): bool:
    key := "rate:" + user
    n := redis.Incr(c, key)
    if n == 1:
        redis.Expire(c, key, seconds)
    end
    ret n <= limit
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    repeat 5 in i:
        println "sara request", i + 1, "allowed:", allow(c, "sara", 3, 60)
    end
    println "omid request 1 allowed:", allow(c, "omid", 3, 60)
    println "sara window ends in:", redis.TTL(c, "rate:sara"), "seconds"
    redis.Del(c, "rate:sara")
    redis.Del(c, "rate:omid")
end
```

Output:

```text
sara request 1 allowed: true
sara request 2 allowed: true
sara request 3 allowed: true
sara request 4 allowed: false
sara request 5 allowed: false
omid request 1 allowed: true
sara window ends in: 60 seconds
```

## Guide: a job queue with a worker

A list makes a simple job queue: producers `RPush` jobs and a worker takes them from the front. `LPop` returns at once, so a worker that polls it wastes time. `BLPOP`, sent through `Command`, waits until a job arrives or the timeout in seconds runs out, and answers nil on a timeout. The worker runs in its own thread with its own client, as step 11 requires.

db-redis-queue.salam

```salam
import db.redis

func take(c: redis.Client, queue: str, seconds: str): str:
    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    args.push("BLPOP")
    args.push(queue)
    args.push(seconds)
    r := redis.Command(c, args)
    mut job := ""
    if redis.ReplyType(r) == redis.REPLY_ARRAY:
        job = redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(r, 1))
    end
    redis.FreeReply(r)
    ret job
end

func worker():
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")
    mut job := take(c, "queue:email", "1")
    until job.len() > 0:
        redis.RPush(c, "done:email", "sent " + job)
        job = take(c, "queue:email", "1")
    end
end

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    defer redis.Close(c)
    redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")

    t := spawn(worker)
    redis.RPush(c, "queue:email", "welcome:sara")
    redis.RPush(c, "queue:email", "welcome:omid")
    redis.RPush(c, "queue:email", "digest:all")
    println "queued 3 jobs"
    join(t)

    each line in redis.LRange(c, "done:email", 0, -1):
        println line
    end
    println "left in queue:", redis.LLen(c, "queue:email")
    redis.Del(c, "done:email")
end
```

Output:

```text
queued 3 jobs
sent welcome:sara
sent welcome:omid
sent digest:all
left in queue: 0
```

A job popped by a worker that then crashes is lost. When that matters, move each job to a processing list with `LMOVE` and remove it only after the work is done.

## Which function for which job

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Cache a value for a while | `SetEx`, then `Get` or `Exists` |
| Count views, hand out ids | `Incr`, `IncrBy`, `Decr` |
| Store a record or a session | `HSet`, `HGetAll`, then `Expire` |
| Recent items, a job queue | `LPush`, `LRange`, `RPush`, `LPop`, `BLPOP` through `Command` |
| Unique visitors, tags, who is online | `SAdd`, `SCard`, `SIsMember` |
| Rankings, scores | `ZADD`, `ZREVRANGE`, `ZINCRBY` through `Command` |
| Several writes together | `MULTI` and `EXEC` through `Command` |
| Tell another service something happened | `Publish` |
| Find keys on a big server | `SCAN` through `Command`, not `Keys` |

## Types

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

A connection to Redis.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The connection pointer; null when `Connect` failed. |

db-redis-Client.salam

```salam
import db.redis

func main:
    c := redis.Connect("127.0.0.1", 6379)
    if not redis.Ok(c):
        println redis.Error(c)
        ret
    end
    _ := redis.Auth(c, "s3cret")
    _ := redis.Select(c, 1)
    println redis.Ping(c)

    _ := redis.Set(c, "greeting", "hello")
    _ := redis.SetEx(c, "session:42", "token", 3600)
    println redis.Get(c, "greeting"), redis.Exists(c, "greeting"), redis.TTL(c, "session:42")
    println redis.Incr(c, "visits"), redis.IncrBy(c, "visits", 10), redis.Decr(c, "visits")
    println redis.Append(c, "greeting", "!"), redis.StrLen(c, "greeting"), redis.Type(c, "greeting")
    _ := redis.Expire(c, "greeting", 60)
    println redis.Keys(c, "session:*").len()
    _ := redis.Del(c, "greeting")

    _ := redis.HSet(c, "user:1", "name", "Maryam")
    _ := redis.HSet(c, "user:1", "city", "Tehran")
    println redis.HGet(c, "user:1", "name"), redis.HExists(c, "user:1", "age"), redis.HLen(c, "user:1")
    all := redis.HGetAll(c, "user:1")
    println all.size()
    _ := redis.HDel(c, "user:1", "city")

    _ := redis.RPush(c, "jobs", "a")
    _ := redis.LPush(c, "jobs", "b")
    println redis.LLen(c, "jobs"), redis.LRange(c, "jobs", 0, -1).len()
    println redis.LPop(c, "jobs"), redis.RPop(c, "jobs")

    _ := redis.SAdd(c, "tags", "go")
    _ := redis.SAdd(c, "tags", "salam")
    println redis.SIsMember(c, "tags", "salam"), redis.SCard(c, "tags"), redis.SMembers(c, "tags").len()
    _ := redis.SRem(c, "tags", "go")
    println redis.Publish(c, "news", "fresh news")

    mut args := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    args.push("GET")
    args.push("visits")
    r := redis.Command(c, args)
    if redis.ReplyOk(r) and not redis.ReplyIsError(r) and not redis.ReplyIsNil(r):
        println redis.ReplyType(r) == redis.REPLY_STRING, redis.ReplyStr(r)
    end
    redis.FreeReply(r)
    mut args2 := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    args2.push("LRANGE")
    args2.push("jobs")
    args2.push("0")
    args2.push("-1")
    r2 := redis.Command(c, args2)
    if redis.ReplyType(r2) == redis.REPLY_ARRAY:
        repeat redis.ReplyArrayLen(r2) in i:
            println redis.ReplyStr(redis.ReplyArrayGet(r2, i))
        end
    end
    println redis.ReplyInt(r2), redis.REPLY_INTEGER, redis.REPLY_NIL, redis.REPLY_STATUS, redis.REPLY_ERROR, redis.REPLY_DOUBLE
    redis.FreeReply(r2)
    _ := redis.FlushDB(c)
    redis.Close(c)
end
```

# db/typesense

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-typesense/

A Typesense client: collections, documents, typo tolerant, faceted, grouped, vector and union search, synonyms, curation, API keys, analytics and clusters.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add db.typesense`

Typesense is an open source search engine with typo tolerance, filters, facets, grouping, vector and hybrid search. This package speaks its HTTP API directly with `net.http` and covers all of it: collections and their fields, documents one at a time or in bulk JSONL imports and exports, every search parameter, multi search and union search, synonym sets and curation sets, presets, stopwords, stemming dictionaries, API keys and scoped search keys signed with no request, analytics rules and events, conversation (RAG) models, natural language search models and the cluster operations. The examples need a running server, so they are only checked.

Every call takes an `Error` as its last argument and fills it when something fails; check it with `Ok`, or with `IsNotFound` and `IsConflict` for the two answers code usually handles. A client can hold several nodes: a node that does not answer, or answers with a 5xx, is skipped for `healthcheck_ms` and the request moves to the next one, the same way the official clients behave. Documents and hits come back as raw JSON text; read them into your own structs with `GetDocumentAs` and `HitsAs`, and send your structs with `ImportOf` and `CreateDocumentOf`. Typesense 30 replaced per collection synonyms and overrides with synonym sets and curation sets; both kinds are here, so the package works with 29 and 30 servers alike. For a route with no function of its own, use `Request`.

## Tutorial: Search with Typesense

Most applications need a search box, and a good one forgives typos, ranks the best match first and answers in milliseconds. The steps below build a small book catalog, from an empty server to a scoped key that a web page can use.

## Running a server

Typesense is a separate program that keeps your data in its own index. The quickest way to start one on your machine is Docker. The `--api-key` value is the admin key your program sends with every request; use your own secret instead of `xyz` outside your own computer.

```salam
docker run -p 8108:8108 typesense/typesense:30.2 --data-dir /tmp --api-key=xyz
```

The examples in this tutorial talk to that server, so they are checked by the compiler but not run when this site is built. The output under each one is what it printed against a real Typesense 30.2 server. Run them in order, because each example builds on the data the earlier ones left behind.

## Connecting

`typesense.New` takes the server address and the API key and gives back a `Client`. Nothing is sent yet; every function that talks to the server takes the client first and an `Error` last. When a call fails the error is filled in: `Ok` tells you whether it worked, `ErrorString` gives one readable line, and `IsNotFound` and `IsConflict` answer the two questions code asks most often. Release the client with `Free` when you are done.

search-connect.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    if not typesense.Health(c, err):
        println "Typesense is not ready:", typesense.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println "connected, server", typesense.ServerVersion(c, err)

    _ := typesense.GetCollection(c, "no_such_collection", err)
    if not typesense.Ok(err):
        println "status", err.status, "not found:", typesense.IsNotFound(err)
        println typesense.ErrorString(err)
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
connected, server 30.2
status 404 not found: true
typesense 404: Collection not found
```

The error has three parts you can use: `status` is the HTTP status (0 when the server could not be reached at all), `kind` says what kind of failure it was, and `message` is the text the server sent.

## Collections and fields

Documents live in a collection, and the collection's schema says which fields exist and what type each one has. `NewField` makes a plain field, `FacetField` one you can count values of, and a `Field` literal lets you set everything else: `optional` for fields some documents leave out, `sort`, `locale` for the language of the text, `infix` for matches in the middle of a word, and more. The types are constants such as `TYPE_STRING`, `TYPE_INT32`, `TYPE_FLOAT`, `TYPE_STRING_ARRAY` and `TYPE_GEOPOINT`.

search-schema.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}
    _ := typesense.DeleteCollection(c, "lesson_books", err)

    mut s := typesense.Schema { name = "lesson_books", default_sorting_field = "year" }
    s.fields.push(typesense.NewField("title", typesense.TYPE_STRING))
    s.fields.push(typesense.NewField("author", typesense.TYPE_STRING))
    s.fields.push(typesense.FacetField("genre", typesense.TYPE_STRING))
    s.fields.push(typesense.NewField("year", typesense.TYPE_INT32))
    s.fields.push(typesense.Field { name = "rating", kind = typesense.TYPE_FLOAT, optional = true })

    col := typesense.CreateCollection(c, s, err)
    if not typesense.Ok(err):
        println typesense.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println "created", col.name, "with", col.fields.len(), "fields"
    each f in col.fields:
        println " ", f.name, f.kind, "facet:", f.facet
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
created lesson_books with 5 fields
  title string facet: false
  author string facet: false
  genre string facet: true
  year int32 facet: false
  rating float facet: false
```

A numeric `default_sorting_field` decides the order when a search does not ask for one. Change a collection later with `AddFields` and `DropFields`, look at it with `GetCollection` and `ListCollections`, and remove it with `DeleteCollection`. To rebuild a collection with no downtime, build the new one next to the old one and move an alias with `UpsertAlias`; programs that search the alias never notice the switch.

## Adding documents

A document is a JSON object whose fields match the schema. You can write that JSON yourself, but usually your program already has the data in a struct. `ImportOf` takes a `Vector` of any struct, turns each one into JSON with the compiler's own encoder and sends them all in one request. `GetDocumentAs` does the opposite and reads a stored document back into your struct.

search-import.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

struct Book:
    pub id: str = ""
    pub title: str = ""
    pub author: str = ""
    pub genre: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
end

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut books := Vector {} as Vector<Book>
    books.push(Book { id = "1", title = "Dune", author = "Frank Herbert", genre = "scifi", year = 1965 })
    books.push(Book { id = "2", title = "Dune Messiah", author = "Frank Herbert", genre = "scifi", year = 1969 })
    books.push(Book { id = "3", title = "Emma", author = "Jane Austen", genre = "novel", year = 1815 })
    books.push(Book { id = "4", title = "Foundation", author = "Isaac Asimov", genre = "scifi", year = 1951 })
    books.push(Book { id = "5", title = "Persuasion", author = "Jane Austen", genre = "novel", year = 1817 })
    r := typesense.ImportOf(c, "lesson_books", books, typesense.WriteOptions { action = typesense.ACTION_UPSERT }, err)
    println "imported", r.success, "failed", r.failed

    _ := typesense.CreateDocument(c, "lesson_books", `{"id": "6", "title": "Walden", "author": "Henry Thoreau", "genre": "essay", "year": "1854"}`, err)
    println "wrong type:", typesense.ErrorString(err)
    println typesense.UpsertDocument(c, "lesson_books", `{"id": "6", "title": "Walden", "author": "Henry Thoreau", "genre": "essay", "year": 1854}`, err)

    mut b := Book {}
    if typesense.GetDocumentAs(c, "lesson_books", "1", b, err):
        println "read back:", b.title, "by", b.author
    end
    println typesense.UpdateDocument(c, "lesson_books", "6", `{"rating": 4.2}`, err)
end
```

Output:

```text
imported 5 failed 0
wrong type: typesense 400: Field `year` must be an int32.
{"author":"Henry Thoreau","genre":"essay","id":"6","title":"Walden","year":1854}
read back: Dune by Frank Herbert
{"author":"Henry Thoreau","genre":"essay","id":"6","rating":4.2,"title":"Walden","year":1854}
```

An import answers even when some documents fail, so check `failed`; `errors` lists every failed line with its reason. `WriteOptions` chooses what happens to existing documents: `ACTION_CREATE` refuses them, `ACTION_UPSERT` replaces them, `ACTION_UPDATE` and `ACTION_EMPLACE` change only the fields you send. For one document at a time there are `CreateDocument`, `UpsertDocument`, `UpdateDocument` and `DeleteDocument`, and `DeleteByFilter` and `UpdateByFilter` change many at once.

## Searching

`NewSearch(q, query_by)` makes the parameters for a search: the text to look for and the fields to look in. `*` as the text matches every document, which is useful together with a filter. The result has `found`, the number of matches, and `hits`, one per document on this page; `hit.document` is the document as JSON.

search-query.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func show(label: str, r: typesense.SearchResult):
    println label, "found", r.found
    each h in r.hits:
        println "   ", h.document
    end
end

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    show("dune:", typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title"), err))
    show("typo:", typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", typesense.NewSearch("persuasoin", "title"), err))

    mut p := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    p.filter_by = "genre:=scifi && year:<1966"
    p.sort_by = "year:desc"
    p.include_fields = "title,year"
    show("filtered:", typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", p, err))

    mut h := typesense.NewSearch("austen", "author,title")
    h.per_page = 1
    r := typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", h, err)
    println "page", r.page, "of", r.found, "results, highlight:", typesense.Highlight(r.hits.get(0), "author")
end
```

Output:

```text
dune: found 2
    {"author":"Frank Herbert","genre":"scifi","id":"1","title":"Dune","year":1965}
    {"author":"Frank Herbert","genre":"scifi","id":"2","title":"Dune Messiah","year":1969}
typo: found 1
    {"author":"Jane Austen","genre":"novel","id":"5","title":"Persuasion","year":1817}
filtered: found 2
    {"title":"Dune","year":1965}
    {"title":"Foundation","year":1951}
page 1 of 2 results, highlight: Jane <mark>Austen</mark>
```

Three things happened that you did not have to ask for. `persuasoin` still found Persuasion, because Typesense forgives a typo or two in each word. The best match came first. And `Highlight` shows which part of a field matched. The other parameters are fields on `SearchParams`: `filter_by` and `sort_by` as in the example, `page` and `per_page` for paging, `include_fields` to return less, `num_typos` to be stricter. A parameter without a field of its own goes through `typesense.Set(p, name, value)`.

| You want | Write |
| --- | --- |
| Only some documents | `p.filter_by = "year:>1950 && genre:=[scifi, novel]"` |
| A different order | `p.sort_by = "year:desc"` |
| Page three, ten per page | `p.page = 3` and `p.per_page = 10` |
| No typos at all | `p.num_typos = "0"` |
| Your structs instead of JSON | `typesense.HitsAs(result, books, err)` |

## Facets and groups

A shop search usually shows a sidebar: how many results are shoes and how many are shirts, how many are under 100. Those counts are facets. Name the facet fields in `facet_by` and every result carries a `Facet` for each one, with the values and how many hits have them. `group_by` answers a different question: it keeps the best few hits for each value, here the oldest book of every genre.

search-facets.salam

```salam
import str
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut p := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    p.facet_by = "genre"
    r := typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", p, err)
    each f in r.facets:
        each fc in f.counts:
            println f.field_name, fc.value, fc.count
        end
    end

    mut g := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    g.group_by = "genre"
    g.group_limit = 1
    g.sort_by = "year:asc"
    rg := typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", g, err)
    each grp in rg.groups:
        println "oldest", str.Join(grp.key, ""), "book:", grp.hits.get(0).document
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
genre scifi 3
genre novel 2
genre essay 1
oldest novel book: {"author":"Jane Austen","genre":"novel","id":"3","title":"Emma","year":1815}
oldest essay book: {"author":"Henry Thoreau","genre":"essay","id":"6","rating":4.2,"title":"Walden","year":1854}
oldest scifi book: {"author":"Isaac Asimov","genre":"scifi","id":"4","title":"Foundation","year":1951}
```

## Many searches in one request

A page that searches books and authors at the same time does not need two round trips. `MultiSearch` sends a list of `SearchRequest`s in one request and returns one result per search; each result has its own `code` and `error`, so one bad search does not spoil the others. The parameters you pass as the common ones apply to all of them. `UnionSearch` goes one step further and merges the hits of all the searches into a single ranked list, and each hit says which search found it.

search-multi.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut searches := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.SearchRequest>
    searches.push(typesense.SearchRequest { collection = "lesson_books", params = typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title") })
    searches.push(typesense.SearchRequest { collection = "lesson_books", params = typesense.NewSearch("austen", "author") })
    common := typesense.SearchParams { per_page = 3 }

    each r in typesense.MultiSearch(c, searches, common, err):
        println "search found", r.found
    end
    u := typesense.UnionSearch(c, searches, common, err)
    println "union found", u.found
    each h in u.hits:
        println "  from search", h.search_index, h.document
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
search found 2
search found 2
union found 4
  from search 0 {"author":"Frank Herbert","genre":"scifi","id":"1","title":"Dune","year":1965}
  from search 0 {"author":"Frank Herbert","genre":"scifi","id":"2","title":"Dune Messiah","year":1969}
  from search 1 {"author":"Jane Austen","genre":"novel","id":"5","title":"Persuasion","year":1817}
```

The union matched four documents but returned three, because the common parameters asked for three per page.

## Synonyms and curation

Search engines only know the words in your documents. A synonym set teaches them that some words mean the same thing, so a search for `sf` also finds books whose genre is `scifi`. A curation set is for the queries you care about most: when a query matches a rule, the rule can pin documents to positions, hide others, add a filter or change the sort. Both kinds of set are created once and then attached to any collection that should use them.

search-tuning.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut words := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    words.push("scifi")
    words.push("science fiction")
    words.push("sf")
    mut syns := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.Synonym>
    syns.push(typesense.Synonym { id = "scifi", synonyms = words })
    _ := typesense.UpsertSynonymSet(c, "lesson_words", syns, err)

    mut pins := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.Pin>
    pins.push(typesense.Pin { id = "4", position = 1 })
    mut rules := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.CurationRule>
    rules.push(typesense.CurationRule { id = "classic-first", query = "dune", match_type = typesense.MATCH_EXACT, includes = pins })
    _ := typesense.UpsertCurationSet(c, "lesson_rules", rules, err)

    _ := typesense.UpdateCollection(c, "lesson_books", `{"synonym_sets": ["lesson_words"], "curation_sets": ["lesson_rules"]}`, err)
    println "sf finds", typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", typesense.NewSearch("sf", "genre"), err).found, "books"
    r := typesense.Search(c, "lesson_books", typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title"), err)
    println "first hit:", r.hits.get(0).document, "curated:", r.hits.get(0).curated
end
```

Output:

```text
sf finds 3 books
first hit: {"author":"Isaac Asimov","genre":"scifi","id":"4","title":"Foundation","year":1951} curated: true
```

The `curated` flag tells your page that a hit was placed by a rule, for example to label it as promoted. A search can turn the rules off with `typesense.Set(p, "enable_curations", "false")`. Typesense 29 and older keep synonyms and rules per collection instead of in sets; for those servers use `UpsertSynonym` and `UpsertOverride`.

## A key for the browser

The admin key can do anything, so it must never reach a web page. `SearchOnlyKey` makes a key that may only search the collections you name. A scoped key goes further: `ScopedSearchKey` signs a search key together with search parameters, such as a filter that keeps every user to their own data. It is made in your program with no request to the server, and the browser cannot remove the filter, because changing it breaks the signature.

search-keys.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut admin := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(admin)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut cols := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    cols.push("lesson_books")
    k := typesense.SearchOnlyKey(admin, "website search", cols, err)
    println "search key made, may:", k.actions.get(0)

    scoped := typesense.ScopedSearchKey(k.value, typesense.SearchParams { filter_by = "genre:=novel" }, 0)
    mut browser := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", scoped)
    defer typesense.Free(browser)
    println "the browser sees", typesense.Search(browser, "lesson_books", typesense.NewSearch("*", ""), err).found, "books"
    _ := typesense.DeleteDocument(browser, "lesson_books", "1", err)
    println "and cannot delete:", err.status
    _ := typesense.DeleteKey(admin, k.id, err)
end
```

Output:

```text
search key made, may: documents:search
the browser sees 2 books
and cannot delete: 401
```

Give the scoped key an expiry time (the last argument, a Unix time) when it is handed out per session, and delete keys you no longer need with `DeleteKey`.

## Vectors and places

Words are not the only way to find things. A `TYPE_GEOPOINT` field holds a latitude and longitude, and a filter such as `location:(35.70, 51.42, 2 km)` keeps only what is near a point, while sorting by the same point puts the nearest first. A vector field (`VectorField`) holds a list of numbers that describes a document, usually made by a machine learning model, and `vector_query` finds the documents whose vectors are closest to yours. With `EmbeddingField`, Typesense makes the vectors itself from the text of other fields.

search-vector-geo.salam

```salam
import db.typesense

func main:
    mut c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "xyz")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    mut err := typesense.Error {}
    _ := typesense.DeleteCollection(c, "lesson_places", err)

    mut s := typesense.Schema { name = "lesson_places" }
    s.fields.push(typesense.NewField("name", typesense.TYPE_STRING))
    s.fields.push(typesense.NewField("location", typesense.TYPE_GEOPOINT))
    s.fields.push(typesense.VectorField("style", 2))
    _ := typesense.CreateCollection(c, s, err)
    mut docs := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    docs.push(`{"name": "Quiet library cafe", "location": [35.7019, 51.4223], "style": [0.9, 0.1]}`)
    docs.push(`{"name": "Loud sports bar", "location": [35.6990, 51.4180], "style": [0.1, 0.9]}`)
    docs.push(`{"name": "Garden tea house", "location": [35.8040, 51.4330], "style": [0.8, 0.2]}`)
    _ := typesense.ImportDocuments(c, "lesson_places", docs, typesense.WriteOptions {}, err)

    mut near := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    near.filter_by = "location:(35.7000, 51.4200, 2 km)"
    near.sort_by = "location(35.7000, 51.4200):asc"
    near.include_fields = "name"
    each h in typesense.Search(c, "lesson_places", near, err).hits:
        println "near:", h.document, h.geo_distance_meters
    end

    mut like := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    like.vector_query = "style:([1.0, 0.0], k: 2)"
    like.include_fields = "name"
    each h in typesense.Search(c, "lesson_places", like, err).hits:
        println "calm:", h.document
    end
    _ := typesense.DeleteCollection(c, "lesson_places", err)
end
```

Output:

```text
near: {"name":"Loud sports bar"} {"location":212}
near: {"name":"Quiet library cafe"} {"location":296}
calm: {"name":"Quiet library cafe"}
calm: {"name":"Garden tea house"}
```

## Running it for real

- A Typesense cluster has several nodes. Give `NewCluster` all of their addresses: a node that does not answer is skipped for `healthcheck_ms` and the request moves on to the next. `SetNearestNode` names one to try first.

- Tune the client with its fields: `timeout_ms` for a single request, `retries` and `retry_interval_ms` for how hard it tries.

- Use an alias in your searches, not a collection name, so you can rebuild the collection without downtime.

- Back up with `CreateSnapshot`, watch the server with `Health`, `Stats` and `Metrics`, and count clicks or popular queries with analytics rules (`CreateAnalyticsRule` and `SendEvent`).

- For an endpoint this package has no function for, `Request` sends any method and path with a JSON body.

Every function, type and field is listed with its own example in the reference below. The repository also has a complete, tested program for each feature in tests/en/db, in the files that start with `tslive_ex_`.

## Types

### `Client`

```salam
struct Client
```

A connection to a Typesense server or cluster. Build it with `New` or `NewCluster` and release it with `Free`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `Vector` | The node URLs, such as `http://localhost:8108`; a path after the host is kept as a prefix. |
| `nearest` | `str = ""` | A node to try before the others, such as the one in the same region; empty for none. |
| `api_key` | `str = ""` | The key sent in the `X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY` header. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int = 10000` | How long one request may take, in milliseconds; 0 waits forever. |
| `retries` | `int = 3` | How many more times to try after a node fails. |
| `retry_interval_ms` | `int = 100` | The pause between two tries, in milliseconds. |
| `healthcheck_ms` | `int = 60000` | How long a node that failed is skipped, in milliseconds. |
| `headers` | `Vector` | Extra header lines added with `AddHeader`. |
| `state` | `Vector` | Internal: the round robin position and when each node may be tried again. |

db-typesense-Client.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    mut nodes := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    nodes.push("http://ts-1:8108")
    nodes.push("http://ts-2:8108")
    nodes.push("http://ts-3:8108")
    mut c := typesense.NewCluster(nodes, "admin-key")
    defer typesense.Free(c)
    typesense.SetNearestNode(c, "http://ts-local:8108")
    typesense.AddNode(c, "http://ts-4:8108")
    typesense.AddHeader(c, "X-Request-Source", "salam")
    c.timeout_ms = 5000
    c.retries = 2
    c.retry_interval_ms = 200
    c.healthcheck_ms = 30000

    mut err := typesense.Error {}
    if not typesense.Health(c, err):
        println "not ready: " + typesense.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println typesense.IsHealthy(c), typesense.NodeHealthy(c, 0), typesense.NodeHealthy(c, -1)
    println "server", typesense.ServerVersion(c, err), typesense.Debug(c, err)
    st := typesense.Status(c, err)
    println st.state, st.committed_index, st.queued_writes
    println typesense.Stats(c, err)
    println typesense.Metrics(c, err)
    println typesense.CreateSnapshot(c, "/data/snapshots/today", err)
    println typesense.Vote(c, err), typesense.ClearCache(c, err), typesense.CompactDB(c, err), typesense.ResetPeers(c, err)
    println typesense.SchemaChanges(c, err).len()
    println typesense.SetSlowRequestLog(c, 1000, err), typesense.UpdateConfig(c, `{"healthy-read-lag": 1000}`, err)

    body := typesense.Request(c, "GET", "/collections?limit=1", "", err)
    if not typesense.Ok(err):
        println err.status, err.kind, err.message
        println err.kind == typesense.KIND_HTTP, err.kind == typesense.KIND_NETWORK, err.kind == typesense.KIND_INVALID, err.kind == typesense.KIND_DECODE
        println typesense.IsNotFound(err), typesense.IsConflict(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println body
    println typesense.RequestAs(c, "POST", "/stemming/dictionaries/import?id=plurals", "text/plain", `{"word":"mice","root":"mouse"}`, err)
    println typesense.VERSION, c.nodes.len(), c.nearest, c.api_key.len(), c.headers.len(), c.state.len()
    single := typesense.New("localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    println single.nodes.get(0)
end
```

### `Error`

```salam
struct Error
```

What went wrong in the last call. Empty when the call worked.

| `kind` | `str = ""` | One of the `KIND_` constants, or empty when the call worked. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message from the server, or a description of the failure. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-Client.salam

### `AnalyticsRule`

```salam
struct AnalyticsRule
```

An analytics rule, in the Typesense 30 form.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = ""` | Its name. |
| `kind` | `str = ""` | One of the `RULE_` constants. |
| `collection` | `str = ""` | The collection whose events it collects. |
| `event_type` | `str = ""` | One of the `EVENT_` constants. |
| `rule_tag` | `str = ""` | A tag to list rules by. |
| `params` | `str = ""` | The rule parameters, as JSON, such as `{"destination_collection":"pq","limit":100}`. |
| `raw` | `str = ""` | The whole rule, as JSON; the only place a Typesense 29 rule keeps its source and destination. |

db-typesense-CreateAnalyticsRule.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    popular := typesense.AnalyticsRule {
        name = "popular-searches", kind = typesense.RULE_POPULAR_QUERIES, collection = "books", event_type = typesense.EVENT_SEARCH,
        params = `{"destination_collection": "popular_queries", "limit": 1000}`
    }
    println typesense.AnalyticsRuleJSON(popular)
    made := typesense.CreateAnalyticsRule(c, popular, err)
    println made.name, made.kind, made.collection, made.event_type, made.params

    clicks := typesense.AnalyticsRule {
        name = "book-clicks", kind = typesense.RULE_COUNTER, collection = "books", event_type = typesense.EVENT_CLICK,
        rule_tag = "homepage", params = `{"destination_collection": "books", "counter_field": "popularity", "weight": 1}`
    }
    println typesense.UpsertAnalyticsRule(c, clicks, err).rule_tag
    println typesense.CreateAnalyticsRuleJSON(c, `{"name": "no-results", "type": "nohits_queries", "collection": "books", "event_type": "search", "params": {"destination_collection": "nohits", "limit": 100}}`, err)
    println typesense.UpsertAnalyticsRuleJSON(c, "old-style", `{"type": "popular_queries", "params": {"source": {"collections": ["books"]}, "destination": {"collection": "pq"}}}`, err)
    println typesense.GetAnalyticsRule(c, "book-clicks", err).raw
    each r in typesense.ListAnalyticsRules(c, "homepage", err):
        println r.name, r.kind
    end

    println typesense.SendEvent(c, "book-clicks", typesense.EVENT_CLICK, `{"doc_id": "42", "user_id": "u-7"}`, err)
    println typesense.SendEventJSON(c, `{"name": "book-clicks", "event_type": "click", "data": {"doc_id": "43", "user_id": "u-7"}}`, err)
    each e in typesense.GetEvents(c, "u-7", "book-clicks", 20, err):
        println e
    end
    println typesense.FlushAnalytics(c, err), typesense.AnalyticsStatus(c, err)
    println typesense.DeleteAnalyticsRule(c, "no-results", err)
    println typesense.RULE_LOG, typesense.EVENT_CONVERSION, typesense.EVENT_VISIT, typesense.EVENT_CUSTOM

    m := typesense.ConversationModel {
        id = "books-assistant", model_name = "openai/gpt-4o-mini", api_key = "sk-...", history_collection = "conversations",
        system_prompt = "You recommend books from our catalog.", max_bytes = 16384, ttl = 86400, account_id = "", vllm_url = "", extra = ""
    }
    println typesense.ConversationModelJSON(m)
    println typesense.CreateConversationModel(c, m, err)
    println typesense.GetConversationModel(c, "books-assistant", err)
    println typesense.ListConversationModels(c, err).len()
    println typesense.UpdateConversationModel(c, "books-assistant", typesense.ConversationModel { system_prompt = "Answer in one sentence." }, err)
    println typesense.DeleteConversationModel(c, "books-assistant", err)

    println typesense.CreateNLSearchModel(c, `{"id": "gpt-4o-nl", "model_name": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", "api_key": "sk-...", "max_bytes": 16000}`, err)
    println typesense.GetNLSearchModel(c, "gpt-4o-nl", err)
    println typesense.ListNLSearchModels(c, err).len()
    println typesense.UpdateNLSearchModel(c, "gpt-4o-nl", `{"temperature": 0.0}`, err)
    println typesense.DeleteNLSearchModel(c, "gpt-4o-nl", err)
end
```

### `ConversationModel`

```salam
struct ConversationModel
```

A large language model for conversational search (RAG). Only the values you set are sent.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str = ""` | Its id. |
| `model_name` | `str = ""` | The model, such as `openai/gpt-4o`. |
| `api_key` | `str = ""` | The key for the model provider. |
| `history_collection` | `str = ""` | The collection that keeps conversation history. |
| `system_prompt` | `str = ""` | The instructions given to the model. |
| `max_bytes` | `int = 0` | How much context the model receives. |
| `ttl` | `int = 0` | How long a conversation is kept, in seconds. |
| `account_id` | `str = ""` | The account id, for Cloudflare models. |
| `vllm_url` | `str = ""` | The server URL, for vLLM models. |
| `extra` | `str = ""` | More members as a JSON object. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-typesense-CreateAnalyticsRule.salam

### `SearchParams`

```salam
struct SearchParams
```

The parameters of one search. Zero values and empty strings are left out; anything else goes through `Set`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | `str = ""` | The text to search for; `*` matches every document. |
| `query_by` | `str = ""` | The fields to search, comma separated. |
| `query_by_weights` | `str = ""` | The weight of each field in `query_by`, such as `2,1`. |
| `text_match_type` | `str = ""` | How field scores combine: `max_score`, `max_weight` or `sum_score`. |
| `prefix` | `str = ""` | Whether the last word matches as a prefix, one value per field such as `true,false`. |
| `infix` | `str = ""` | Infix search per field: `off`, `always` or `fallback`. |
| `filter_by` | `str = ""` | A filter, such as `year:>2000 && genre:=[scifi]`. |
| `sort_by` | `str = ""` | The sort order, such as `year:desc,_text_match:desc`. |
| `facet_by` | `str = ""` | Fields to count values of. |
| `facet_query` | `str = ""` | Narrow the facet values, such as `genre:sci`. |
| `max_facet_values` | `int = 0` | How many values each facet returns. |
| `group_by` | `str = ""` | Group the results by these fields. |
| `group_limit` | `int = 0` | How many hits each group returns. |
| `include_fields` | `str = ""` | Return only these fields. |
| `exclude_fields` | `str = ""` | Leave these fields out of the results. |
| `highlight_fields` | `str = ""` | Highlight only these fields. |
| `highlight_full_fields` | `str = ""` | Highlight the whole value of these fields, not a snippet. |
| `highlight_start_tag` | `str = ""` | The tag before a match; `<mark>` by default. |
| `highlight_end_tag` | `str = ""` | The tag after a match. |
| `snippet_threshold` | `int = 0` | Fields shorter than this many words are highlighted whole. |
| `num_typos` | `str = ""` | How many typos a word may have, 0 to 2, one value per field. |
| `typo_tokens_threshold` | `int = 0` | Look for typo matches only when fewer results than this were found. |
| `drop_tokens_threshold` | `int = 0` | Drop words from the query only when fewer results than this were found. |
| `page` | `int = 0` | The page, from 1. |
| `per_page` | `int = 0` | Hits per page, up to 250. |
| `offset` | `int = 0` | Skip this many hits; an alternative to `page`. |
| `limit` | `int = 0` | Return this many hits; used with `offset`. |
| `pinned_hits` | `str = ""` | Pin documents to positions, such as `12:1,3:2`. |
| `hidden_hits` | `str = ""` | Ids of documents to hide. |
| `override_tags` | `str = ""` | Apply only the curation rules with these tags. |
| `preset` | `str = ""` | Use the parameters saved in this preset. |
| `vector_query` | `str = ""` | A nearest neighbour search, such as `embedding:([0.1, 0.2], k: 10)`. |
| `stopwords` | `str = ""` | A stopword set to apply. |
| `exhaustive_search` | `bool = false` | Consider every variation of the query, slower but complete. |
| `search_cutoff_ms` | `int = 0` | Stop searching after this many milliseconds and return what was found. |
| `use_cache` | `bool = false` | Cache the results on the server. |
| `cache_ttl` | `int = 0` | How long to cache them, in seconds. |
| `conversation` | `bool = false` | Answer the query with a conversation model (RAG). |
| `conversation_id` | `str = ""` | Continue this conversation. |
| `conversation_model_id` | `str = ""` | The conversation model to use. |
| `nl_query` | `bool = false` | Turn a natural language query into filters and sorting with an NL search model. |
| `nl_model_id` | `str = ""` | The NL search model to use. |
| `keys` | `Vector` | Parameter names added with `Set`. |
| `values` | `Vector` | Their values. |

db-typesense-Search.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import str
import db.typesense

struct Book:
    pub id: str = ""
    pub title: str = ""
    pub year: int = 0
end

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "search-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut p := typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title,description")
    p.query_by_weights = "3,1"
    p.filter_by = "year:>1950 && genres:=[scifi]"
    p.sort_by = "_text_match:desc,year:desc"
    p.facet_by = "genres,year"
    p.max_facet_values = 10
    p.per_page = 20
    p.page = 1
    p.num_typos = "2,1"
    p.highlight_start_tag = "<b>"
    p.highlight_end_tag = "</b>"
    typesense.Set(p, "prioritize_exact_match", "false")
    println typesense.SearchQuery(p)
    println typesense.SearchParamsJSON(p)

    r := typesense.Search(c, "books", p, err)
    if not typesense.Ok(err):
        println typesense.ErrorString(err)
        ret 1
    end
    println r.found, r.out_of, r.page, r.search_time_ms, r.search_cutoff
    each h in r.hits:
        println h.document, h.text_match, h.curated, typesense.Highlight(h, "title")
        println h.highlight, h.highlights, h.text_match_info, h.vector_distance, h.geo_distance_meters, h.hybrid_search_info, h.raw.len()
    end
    each f in r.facets:
        print f.field_name, f.sampled, f.stats, ":"
        each fc in f.counts:
            print " " + fc.value + "=" + fc.count + " " + fc.highlighted
        end
        println ""
    end
    mut books := Vector {} as Vector<Book>
    if typesense.HitsAs(r, books, err):
        println books.len()
    end
    println r.request_params, r.raw.len()

    mut g := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    g.group_by = "genres"
    g.group_limit = 3
    g.include_fields = "id,title"
    rg := typesense.Search(c, "books", g, err)
    println rg.found, rg.found_docs
    each grp in rg.groups:
        println str.Join(grp.key, ","), grp.found, grp.hits.len()
    end

    mut v := typesense.NewSearch("*", "")
    v.vector_query = "embedding:([0.12, 0.45, 0.87], k: 10)"
    v.exclude_fields = "embedding"
    println typesense.SearchRaw(c, "books", v, err)

    mut rag := typesense.NewSearch("which books are about deserts?", "title_vector")
    rag.conversation = true
    rag.conversation_model_id = "books-assistant"
    rag.conversation_id = ""
    rag.prefix = "false"
    rag.exhaustive_search = true
    rag.search_cutoff_ms = 200
    rag.use_cache = true
    rag.cache_ttl = 60
    println typesense.Search(c, "books", rag, err).conversation

    mut nl := typesense.NewSearch("science fiction books after 1960 sorted by year", "title")
    nl.nl_query = true
    nl.nl_model_id = "gpt-4o-nl"
    println typesense.Search(c, "books", nl, err).parsed_nl_query

    mut reqs := Vector {} as Vector<typesense.SearchRequest>
    reqs.push(typesense.SearchRequest { collection = "books", params = typesense.NewSearch("dune", "") })
    reqs.push(typesense.SearchRequest { collection = "authors", params = typesense.NewSearch("herbert", "name"), api_key = "scoped-key" })
    common := typesense.NewSearch("", "title")
    each m in typesense.MultiSearch(c, reqs, common, err):
        println m.found, m.code, m.error
    end
    println typesense.MultiSearchRaw(c, reqs, common, err).len()
    u := typesense.UnionSearch(c, reqs, common, err)
    each h in u.hits:
        println h.collection, h.search_index, h.document
    end
    mut rr := typesense.ParseSearchResult(`{"found": 0, "hits": []}`)
    println rr.found, rr.code, rr.error, typesense.MAX_GET_QUERY
    typesense.FreeResult(rr)
end
```

### `KeySpec`

A new API key.

db-typesense-CreateKey.salam

```salam
/*
 * Salam Programming Language (2024-2026)
 *
 *   +-------------------+
 *   |     S A L A M     |
 *   +-------------------+
 *
 * Designed by Seyyed Ali Mohammadiyeh and the Salam Team
 * Born from a decade of language design experience (since 2018)
 *
 * Repository: https://github.com/SalamLang/Salam
 *
 */


import db.typesense

func main:
    c := typesense.New("http://localhost:8108", "admin-key")
    mut err := typesense.Error {}

    mut books := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    books.push("books")
    search := typesense.SearchOnlyKey(c, "website search", books, err)
    println search.id, search.value, search.actions.len(), search.collections.get(0)

    mut actions := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    actions.push("documents:*")
    actions.push("collections:get")
    mut orgs := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    orgs.push("org_.*")
    spec := typesense.KeySpec { description = "tenant writer", actions = actions, collections = orgs, expires_at = 1924992000, autodelete = true }
    println typesense.KeySpecJSON(spec)
    k := typesense.CreateKey(c, spec, err)
    println k.value, k.expires_at, k.autodelete

    mut all := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    all.push(typesense.KEY_ACTION_ALL)
    admin := typesense.CreateKey(c, typesense.KeySpec { description = "admin", actions = all, collections = all, value = "my-chosen-admin-key" }, err)
    println admin.id

    g := typesense.GetKey(c, k.id, err)
    println g.value_prefix, g.description
    each key in typesense.ListKeys(c, err):
        println key.id, key.value_prefix, key.description, key.actions.len(), key.collections.len(), key.expires_at
    end
    println typesense.DeleteKey(c, k.id, err)

    scope := typesense.SearchParams { filter_by = "company_id:=124", exclude_fields = "salary" }
    scoped := typesense.ScopedSearchKey(search.value, scope, 1924992000)
    println scoped
    println typesense.GenerateScopedSearchKey(search.value, `{"filter_by":"user_id:=42"}`)
    mut browser := typesense.New("https://search.example.com", scoped)
    defer typesense.Free(browser)
    println typesense.Search(browser, "books", typesense.NewSearch("dune", "title"), err).found
    println typesense.KEY_ACTION_SEARCH
end
```
