# db/opensearch

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/db-opensearch/

An OpenSearch client: documents, bulk, the query DSL, aggregations, scroll and point in time, index admin, SQL and PPL, k-NN vector search, ISM, security and AWS signing.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add db.opensearch`

OpenSearch is an open source search and analytics engine. This package speaks its REST API directly over `net.tcp` and `tls`, with no outside library: several nodes with retries and dead node skipping, basic, bearer and AWS SigV4 authentication (for Amazon OpenSearch Service and Serverless), and TLS with your own CA file or, for a test server, no verification. On top of that it covers documents, bulk, every common query and aggregation, scroll and point in time paging, index, alias, template and data stream admin, cluster, task, snapshot and pipeline admin, and the plugins that make OpenSearch what it is: SQL and PPL, k-NN and neural search, hybrid search pipelines, ISM policies, the security plugin, alerting monitors and ML Commons.

Queries, aggregations and request bodies are plain JSON text: the builders such as `Match`, `BoolOf` and `TermsAgg` return it, and anything they do not cover can be written as a backtick string. Results come back as Salam structs whose JSON parts (a hit's source, the aggregations) are raw text you read with `Buckets`, `AggValue` and `JsonPath`. Every call records its status and error on the client, so read `Error` or `ErrorType` after a call that returned false. `Conn` boxes a client as a `db.Connection`, so SQL code written for the other engines can query OpenSearch too. For a route with no function of its own, use `Perform`. Only the examples for the query builders and request signing run here; the others need a server, so they are only checked.

db/elasticsearch also talks to the OpenSearch core API. Use this package when you need what only OpenSearch has: PPL, k-NN, neural and hybrid search, ISM, the security plugin, alerting, ML Commons, or AWS SigV4 for Amazon OpenSearch Service and Serverless.

## Tutorial: Search with OpenSearch

You give OpenSearch documents as JSON, and it finds the ones that match a query, ranks them, and counts them by any field you like. The steps below build a small book search, one piece at a time.

## A server to talk to

Every example that talks to a cluster expects one at `http://localhost:9200`. The quickest way to get one is Docker: `docker run -p 9200:9200 -e discovery.type=single-node -e DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true opensearchproject/opensearch:2.17.1`. There is no server behind this page, so those examples are checked by the compiler and show the output they printed when run, in order, against a real OpenSearch 2.17.1. The ones that only build requests or read answers are run every time the site is built.

The package is an official package, not part of the standard library: add it to your project with `salam add db.opensearch` first. Then import it as `db.opensearch` and call it as `opensearch`.

## Connecting

`Connect` takes a node url and gives back a client. Nothing is sent until the first call, so check that the cluster answers with `Ping`, then ask it about itself with `GetInfo` and `ClusterHealth`.

opensearch-connect.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    if not opensearch.Ping(c):
        println "no answer:", opensearch.Error(c)
        ret 1
    end
    info := opensearch.GetInfo(c)
    println info.distribution, info.version, info.cluster_name
    h := opensearch.ClusterHealth(c)
    println "health:", h.status, h.nodes, "nodes"
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
opensearch 2.17.1 docker-cluster
health: green 1 nodes
```

A real deployment usually needs more: several nodes, a user and password, your own certificate authority, a time limit. Put them in a `Config` and pass it to `NewClient`. The client spreads requests over the nodes, skips one that refuses connections for a minute, and retries a request that got a 502, 503 or 504 on another node. `ConnectInsecure` is for the demo setup that ships with a self signed certificate, and `ConnectAWS` signs every request with AWS SigV4 for Amazon OpenSearch Service; use `SERVICE_AOSS` instead of `SERVICE_ES` for a Serverless collection.

opensearch-config.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    mut cfg := opensearch.DefaultConfig()
    cfg.nodes.push("https://node2.example.com:9200, https://node3.example.com:9200")
    cfg.username = "app"
    cfg.password = "s3cret-pass"
    cfg.ca_file = "/etc/ssl/certs/opensearch-ca.pem"
    cfg.timeout_ms = 10000
    cfg.max_retries = 2
    c := opensearch.NewClient(cfg)
    println opensearch.Ok(c), opensearch.Nodes(c)

    local := opensearch.ConnectInsecure("https://localhost:9200", "admin", "admin-pass")
    println opensearch.Ok(local)

    aws := opensearch.ConnectAWS(
        "https://search-books.eu-west-1.es.amazonaws.com", "eu-west-1", opensearch.SERVICE_ES,
        "AKIA...", "secret-key", ""
    )
    println opensearch.Ok(aws)
end
```

Output:

```text
true ["http://localhost:9200", "https://node2.example.com:9200", "https://node3.example.com:9200"]
true
true
```

## An index and its documents

An index is where documents live, and its mapping says what each field is: `text` is split into words for full text search, `keyword` is matched exactly, and numbers and dates can be compared and sorted. OpenSearch guesses a mapping if you give none, but a guess cannot be changed later, so it pays to create the index yourself. `Property` writes one field and `Properties` puts them together.

Documents are JSON text, and every write returns a `WriteResult` with the id, the result and the version. A new document is searchable after the next refresh, about a second later; `REFRESH_WAIT_FOR` makes the call wait for it, which is handy in tests and scripts. `Get` reads a document back by id, and `JsonPath` picks a value out of its source.

opensearch-documents.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut props := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    props.push(opensearch.Property("title", "text"))
    props.push(opensearch.Property("author", "keyword"))
    props.push(opensearch.Property("year", "integer"))
    props.push(opensearch.Property("stock", "integer"))
    println "created:", opensearch.CreateIndexWith(c, "books", 1, 0, opensearch.Properties(props))

    w := opensearch.IndexWith(c, "books", "1", `{"title":"Shahnameh","author":"Ferdowsi","year":1010,"stock":3}`, opensearch.Options { refresh = opensearch.REFRESH_WAIT_FOR })
    println "indexed:", w.ok, w.result, w.version

    d := opensearch.Get(c, "books", "1")
    if d.found:
        println "title:", opensearch.JsonPath(d.source, "title")
    end

    u := opensearch.Update(c, "books", "1", `{"stock":2}`)
    println "updated:", u.result, u.version

    del := opensearch.Delete(c, "books", "1")
    println "deleted:", del.result
end
```

Output:

```text
created: true
indexed: true created 1
title: Shahnameh
updated: updated 2
deleted: deleted
```

## Many documents at once

Sending documents one request at a time is slow. A `Bulk` collects index, create, update and delete actions and sends them together. This example only builds the batch and prints the body it would send, so it runs here:

opensearch-bulk.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    mut b := opensearch.NewBulk()
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "1", `{"title":"Shahnameh","author":"Ferdowsi","year":1010}`)
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "2", `{"title":"Masnavi","author":"Rumi","year":1258}`)
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "3", `{"title":"Golestan","author":"Saadi","year":1258}`)
    opensearch.BulkUpdate(b, "books", "2", `{"stock":4}`)
    opensearch.BulkDelete(b, "books", "99")
    println opensearch.BulkLen(b), "actions"
    print opensearch.BulkBody(b)
    opensearch.BulkFree(b)
end
```

Output:

```text
5 actions
{"index":{"_index":"books","_id":"1"}}
{"title":"Shahnameh","author":"Ferdowsi","year":1010}
{"index":{"_index":"books","_id":"2"}}
{"title":"Masnavi","author":"Rumi","year":1258}
{"index":{"_index":"books","_id":"3"}}
{"title":"Golestan","author":"Saadi","year":1258}
{"update":{"_index":"books","_id":"2"}}
{"doc":{"stock":4}}
{"delete":{"_index":"books","_id":"99"}}
```

`BulkSend` sends it. A bulk request succeeds as a whole even when some actions fail, so look at each item: `ok`, `status` and the error type and reason say what went wrong for that one document.

opensearch-bulk-send.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut b := opensearch.NewBulk()
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "1", `{"title":"Shahnameh, the Book of Kings","author":"Ferdowsi","year":1010}`)
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "2", `{"title":"Masnavi","author":"Rumi","year":1258}`)
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "3", `{"title":"Golestan","author":"Saadi","year":1258}`)
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "4", `{"title":"Kings and Heroes","author":"Anonymous","year":1900}`)
    res := opensearch.BulkSendWith(c, b, opensearch.REFRESH_TRUE)
    opensearch.BulkFree(b)
    println res.succeeded, "stored,", res.failed, "failed"
    each it in res.items:
        if not it.ok:
            println it.id, it.error_type, it.error_reason
        end
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
4 stored, 0 failed
```

## Building queries

A query is JSON as well, and the package has a builder for each common kind. `Match` searches the words of a text field, `Term` wants an exact value, and `Range`, `RangeInt` and `DateRange` compare. To combine them, fill a `BoolQuery`: `must` has to match and adds to the score, `filter` has to match but does not score, `should` raises the score, and `must_not` excludes. A `SearchRequest` adds paging, sorting and which fields to return; `SearchBody` shows what will be sent.

opensearch-query.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    println opensearch.Match("title", "book of kings")
    println opensearch.Term("author", "Ferdowsi")
    println opensearch.RangeInt("year", 1000, 1300)

    mut q := opensearch.BoolQuery {}
    q.must.push(opensearch.Match("title", "kings"))
    q.filter.push(opensearch.RangeInt("year", 1000, 1300))
    q.must_not.push(opensearch.Term("author", "Anonymous"))
    println opensearch.BoolOf(q)

    mut req := opensearch.SearchRequest { query = opensearch.BoolOf(q), size = 5 }
    req.sort.push(opensearch.SortDesc("year"))
    req.source.push("title")
    println opensearch.SearchBody(req)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"match":{"title":"book of kings"}}
{"term":{"author":"Ferdowsi"}}
{"range":{"year":{"gte":1000,"lte":1300}}}
{"bool":{"must":[{"match":{"title":"kings"}}],"filter":[{"range":{"year":{"gte":1000,"lte":1300}}}],"must_not":[{"term":{"author":"Anonymous"}}]}}
{"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"match":{"title":"kings"}}],"filter":[{"range":{"year":{"gte":1000,"lte":1300}}}],"must_not":[{"term":{"author":"Anonymous"}}]}},"size":5,"sort":[{"year":{"order":"desc"}}],"_source":{"includes":["title"]}}
```

Anything the builders do not cover can be written by hand as a backtick string, since a query is only text. The builders, the request body and the answer can all be mixed with your own JSON.

## Reading the hits

`SearchWith` runs the request and returns a `SearchResult`: the total number of matches, the time it took, and the hits of this page, best first. Each `Hit` has its id, score and source, plus the highlighted fragments you asked for.

opensearch-search.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut fields := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    fields.push("title")
    mut req := opensearch.SearchRequest { query = opensearch.Match("title", "kings"), size = 10 }
    req.highlight = opensearch.Highlight(fields)
    r := opensearch.SearchWith(c, "books", req)
    if not r.ok:
        println r.error
        ret 1
    end
    println r.total, "matches"
    each h in r.hits:
        println h.id, h.score, h.source
    end
    ret 0
end
```

Output:

```text
2 matches
4 0.8547784 {"title":"Kings and Heroes","author":"Anonymous","year":1900}
1 0.63807404 {"title":"Shahnameh, the Book of Kings","author":"Ferdowsi","year":1010}
```

The same reader works on an answer you already have, through `ParseSearch`. That is how this example runs here without a server:

opensearch-results.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    answer := `{"took":3,"timed_out":false,"hits":{"total":{"value":2,"relation":"eq"},"max_score":2.1,"hits":[{"_index":"books","_id":"1","_score":2.1,"_source":{"title":"Shahnameh","author":"Ferdowsi"},"highlight":{"title":["<em>Shahnameh</em>"]}},{"_index":"books","_id":"7","_score":0.8,"_source":{"title":"Tales from the Shahnameh","author":"Anonymous"}}]}}`
    r := opensearch.ParseSearch(answer)
    println r.total, "matches in", r.took, "ms"
    each h in r.hits:
        println h.id, h.score, opensearch.JsonPath(h.source, "title"), "by", opensearch.JsonPath(h.source, "author")
    end
    println opensearch.JsonPath(r.hits.get(0).highlight, "title.0")
end
```

Output:

```text
2 matches in 3 ms
1 2.1 Shahnameh by Ferdowsi
7 0.8 Tales from the Shahnameh by Anonymous
<em>Shahnameh</em>
```

## Counting with aggregations

Aggregations answer questions about all the matches at once: how many books per author, the average year, a histogram by month. Add them to a request with `AddAgg`, set `size` to 0 if you only want the numbers, and read the answer with `Buckets` for groups and `AggValue` for single values. Other readers cover the rest: `AggField` for one number of a `stats` result, `AggPercentile` for percentiles.

opensearch-aggs.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    mut aggs := opensearch.AddAgg("{}", "authors", opensearch.TermsAgg("author", 3))
    aggs = opensearch.AddAgg(aggs, "avg_year", opensearch.AvgAgg("year"))
    println opensearch.SearchBody(opensearch.SearchRequest { size = 0, aggs = aggs })

    answer := `{"took":2,"hits":{"total":{"value":40,"relation":"eq"},"hits":[]},"aggregations":{"authors":{"buckets":[{"key":"Saadi","doc_count":12},{"key":"Rumi","doc_count":9},{"key":"Hafez","doc_count":7}]},"avg_year":{"value":1265.5}}}`
    r := opensearch.ParseSearch(answer)
    each b in opensearch.Buckets(r.aggregations, "authors"):
        println b.key, b.doc_count
    end
    println "average year:", opensearch.AggValue(r.aggregations, "avg_year")
end
```

Output:

```text
{"size":0,"aggs":{"authors":{"terms":{"field":"author","size":3}},"avg_year":{"avg":{"field":"year"}}}}
Saadi 12
Rumi 9
Hafez 7
average year: 1265.5
```

## Paging through everything

`from` and `size` are fine for the first pages a person looks at, but not for walking through a whole index. For that, open a point in time with `CreatePit`, which freezes a view of the index, sort by a field, and ask for each next page with `search_after` set to the sort values of the last hit. An empty page means you are done; close the point in time with `DeletePit`.

opensearch-paging.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    pit := opensearch.CreatePit(c, "books", "2m")
    mut req := opensearch.SearchRequest { query = opensearch.MatchAll(), size = 100, pit_id = pit, pit_keep_alive = "2m" }
    req.sort.push(opensearch.SortAsc("year"))
    mut seen := 0
    mut page := opensearch.SearchWith(c, "", req)
    until page.hits.len() > 0:
        seen += page.hits.len()
        req.search_after = page.hits.get(page.hits.len() - 1).sort
        page = opensearch.SearchWith(c, "", req)
    end
    opensearch.DeletePit(c, pit)
    println seen, "books"
end
```

Output:

```text
4 books
```

## SQL and PPL

OpenSearch also answers SQL. `Conn` turns a client into a `db.Connection`, the same interface the SQL engines use, so `db.QueryInt` and the row loop from the db package work unchanged. PPL is OpenSearch's piped query language, handy for logs; `Ppl` returns rows the same way. Long results come in pages, and the rows fetch the next page as you go.

opensearch-sql.salam

```salam
import db
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    conn := opensearch.Conn(c)
    println db.QueryInt(conn, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books WHERE year > 1200")
    rows := conn.Query("SELECT author, COUNT(*) AS n FROM books GROUP BY author ORDER BY n DESC")
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Text(0), rows.Int(1)
    end
    rows.Close()

    p := opensearch.Ppl(c, "source=books | where year > 1200 | stats count() by author")
    until p.Next():
        println p.Text(1), p.Int(0)
    end
    p.Close()
end
```

Output:

```text
3
Anonymous 1
Saadi 1
Rumi 1
Ferdowsi 1
Anonymous 1
Rumi 1
Saadi 1
```

## Vector search

A `knn_vector` field holds an embedding, a list of numbers that places a text or an image in space so that similar things are close together. `KnnIndexBody` creates an index with one, and `Knn` finds the documents nearest to a vector. `Neural` and `Hybrid` go one step further and let OpenSearch make the vector from text with a model it hosts.

opensearch-vectors.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    method := opensearch.KnnMethod { engine = "lucene", space_type = "cosinesimil" }
    mut extra := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    extra.push(opensearch.Property("name", "text"))
    opensearch.CreateIndex(c, "places", opensearch.KnnIndexBody("embedding", 3, method, extra))
    opensearch.Index(c, "places", "1", `{"name":"Naderi Cafe","embedding":[0.1,0.9,0.2]}`)
    opensearch.Refresh(c, "places")

    mut v := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    v.push(0.1)
    v.push(0.8)
    v.push(0.3)
    r := opensearch.Search(c, "places", opensearch.Knn("embedding", v, 3))
    each h in r.hits:
        println h.id, h.score, h.source
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
1 0.99514455 {"name":"Naderi Cafe","embedding":[0.1,0.9,0.2]}
```

## When something goes wrong

No call stops your program. A call that fails returns false, -1 or an empty result, and the client remembers what happened: `Status` is the HTTP status of the last request (0 when no answer came), `Error` is a readable message, and `ErrorType` and `ErrorReason` are what OpenSearch said, such as `version_conflict_engine_exception`. A bad url is caught when the client is made, and `Ok` tells you. A missing document is not an error: `Get` returns `found = false` with an empty `error`.

opensearch-errors.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    mut cfg := opensearch.DefaultConfig()
    cfg.nodes = Vector {} as Vector<str>
    cfg.nodes.push("http://127.0.0.1:1")
    cfg.max_retries = 0
    c := opensearch.NewClient(cfg)
    println "config ok:", opensearch.Ok(c)

    d := opensearch.Get(c, "books", "1")
    println "found:", d.found
    println "status:", opensearch.Status(c)
    println "error:", opensearch.Error(c)

    bad := opensearch.Connect("ftp://example.com")
    println "config ok:", opensearch.Ok(bad), "|", opensearch.Error(bad)
end
```

Output:

```text
config ok: true
found: false
status: 0
error: http://127.0.0.1:1: could not connect to 127.0.0.1:1
config ok: false | the node url could not be parsed: ftp://example.com
```

## Where to go next

The reference below lists every function with an example, including index templates, aliases, snapshots, ingest pipelines, ISM policies, the security plugin, alerting and ML Commons. For anything the package has no function for, `Perform` sends any request you write.

## More

### Which function for which job

| To do this | Use |
| --- | --- |
| page through a whole index | `CreatePit`, `search_after`, `DeletePit` (or `SearchScroll` and `Scroll`) |
| run several searches in one request | `MSearch` |
| change or delete what a query matches | `UpdateByQuery`, `DeleteByQuery` |
| copy an index, then switch with no downtime | `Reindex`, then `SwapAlias` |
| query with SQL or PPL | `Conn` with the db interface, `Sql`, `SqlWith`, `Ppl` |
| vector, neural and hybrid search | `KnnIndexBody`, `Knn`, `Neural`, `Hybrid`, `NormalizationPipeline` |
| delete old indices on a schedule | `DeleteAfterPolicy`, `PutPolicy`, `AddPolicy` |
| users and permissions | `PutUser`, `RoleBody`, `PutRole`, `PutRoleMapping`, `WhoAmI` |
| transform documents while they are indexed | `Pipeline`, `Processor`, `PutPipeline`, `SimulatePipeline` |
| back up and restore | `PutRepository`, `CreateSnapshot`, `RestoreSnapshot` |
| anything else | `Perform`, `PerformNdjson` |

### Test without a server

The tests of this package run against a small fake OpenSearch built with net/http: it records each request and answers with canned JSON, so a test can check both what the client sent and how it read the answer. The suite under `tests/en/stdlib/opensearch` and its Persian twin under `tests/fa/stdlib/opensearch` cover every feature this way and make good starting points for your own tests.

## Types

### `BoolQuery`

```salam
struct BoolQuery
```

The four clause lists and options of a bool query, for `BoolOf`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `must` | `Vector` | Must match and adds to the score. |
| `filter` | `Vector` | Must match, but does not score; cached. |
| `should` | `Vector` | Should match; raises the score. |
| `must_not` | `Vector` | Must not match. |
| `minimum_should_match` | `str = ""` | How many should clauses must match, such as `1` or `75%`. |
| `boost` | `f64 = 0` | Multiplies the score; 0 leaves it out. |

db-opensearch-Query.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func list(a: str, b: str): Vector<str>:
    mut v := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    v.push(a)
    if b.len() > 0: v.push(b) end
    ret v
end

func main:
    println opensearch.MatchAll(), opensearch.MatchNone()
    println opensearch.Match("title", "salam"), opensearch.MatchAnd("title", "salam world")
    println opensearch.MatchFuzzy("title", "slam"), opensearch.MatchPhrase("title", "hello world")
    println opensearch.MatchPhraseSlop("title", "hello world", 2), opensearch.MatchPhrasePrefix("title", "sal")
    println opensearch.MatchBoolPrefix("title", "quick bro")
    println opensearch.MultiMatch("salam", list("title^2", "body")), opensearch.MultiMatchType("salam", list("title", "body"), "phrase")
    println opensearch.Term("tag", "news"), opensearch.TermInt("year", 1403), opensearch.TermBool("published", true)
    println opensearch.TermCaseInsensitive("tag", "News"), opensearch.Terms("tag", list("news", "sport"))
    mut years := Vector {} as Vector<i64>
    years.push(1402)
    years.push(1403)
    println opensearch.TermsInt("year", years), opensearch.TermsLookup("tag", "users", "7", "follows")
    println opensearch.TermsSet("skills", list("go", "salam"), "required")
    println opensearch.Range("date", "2026-01-01", "2026-12-31"), opensearch.RangeExclusive("price", "10", "20")
    println opensearch.RangeNum("price", 9.5, 20.0), opensearch.RangeInt("stock", 1, 100), opensearch.RangeOp("price", "lt", "5")
    println opensearch.DateRange("at", "now-7d/d", "now", "", "+03:30")
    println opensearch.FieldExists("email"), opensearch.Prefix("sku", "AB-"), opensearch.Wildcard("sku", "AB-*-9")
```

### `SearchParams`

```salam
struct SearchParams
```

Settings sent in the url of a search. Empty strings are left out.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routing` | `str = ""` | Search only the shards for this routing value. |
| `preference` | `str = ""` | Which shard copies to prefer, such as `_local`. |
| `search_pipeline` | `str = ""` | A search pipeline to run, such as one for hybrid search. |
| `search_type` | `str = ""` | `query_then_fetch` or `dfs_query_then_fetch`. |
| `scroll` | `str = ""` | Keep a scroll open this long. |
| `request_cache` | `str = ""` | `true` or `false`: use the request cache. |
| `allow_partial_search_results` | `str = ""` | `false` fails the search when a shard fails. |
| `ignore_unavailable` | `bool = false` | Skip missing or closed indices. |

db-opensearch-Search.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut req := opensearch.SearchRequest { query = opensearch.Match("title", "kings"), size = 10 }
    req.sort.push(opensearch.SortDesc("year"))
    req.aggs = opensearch.AddAgg(opensearch.AddAgg("{}", "by_tag", opensearch.TermsAgg("tag", 5)), "avg_year", opensearch.AvgAgg("year"))
    req.aggs = opensearch.AddAgg(req.aggs, "stats", opensearch.StatsAgg("year"))
    mut pcts := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    pcts.push(50.0)
    pcts.push(99.0)
    req.aggs = opensearch.AddAgg(req.aggs, "pages", opensearch.PercentilesAgg("pages", pcts))
    req.suggest = opensearch.TermSuggest("fix", "kngs", "title")
    r := opensearch.SearchWith(c, "books", req)
    println r.ok, r.status, r.took, r.timed_out, r.total, r.total_relation, r.max_score, r.error
    each h in r.hits:
        println h.index, h.id, h.score, h.source, h.sort, h.highlight, h.fields, h.inner_hits, h.matched_queries, h.raw.len()
    end
    each bk in opensearch.Buckets(r.aggregations, "by_tag"):
        println bk.key, bk.key_as_string, bk.doc_count, bk.raw.len()
    end
    println opensearch.AggValue(r.aggregations, "avg_year"), opensearch.AggField(r.aggregations, "stats", "max")
    println opensearch.AggRaw(r.aggregations, "stats"), opensearch.Suggestions(r.suggest, "fix")
    println opensearch.AggPercentile(r.aggregations, "pages", 50.0), opensearch.AggPercentile(r.aggregations, "pages", 99.0)
    println opensearch.Search(c, "books,articles", opensearch.MatchAll()).total
    println opensearch.SearchRaw(c, "books", `{"query":{"match_all":{}},"size":1}`).hits.len()
    p := opensearch.SearchParams {
        routing = "poetry", preference = "_local", search_pipeline = "rerank", search_type = "dfs_query_then_fetch",
        request_cache = "true", allow_partial_search_results = "false", ignore_unavailable = true
    }
    println opensearch.SearchParamsWith(c, "books", `{"size":0}`, p).total, p.scroll.len()
    parsed := opensearch.ParseSearch(r.raw)
    println parsed.hits.len(), parsed.scroll_id, parsed.pit_id

    mut page := opensearch.SearchScroll(c, "books", opensearch.SearchRequest { query = opensearch.MatchAll(), size = 500 }, "1m")
    mut seen := 0
    until page.hits.len() > 0:
        seen += page.hits.len()
        page = opensearch.Scroll(c, page.scroll_id, "1m")
    end
    println seen, opensearch.ClearScroll(c, page.scroll_id)

    pit := opensearch.CreatePit(c, "books", "2m")
    mut preq := opensearch.SearchRequest { query = opensearch.MatchAll(), size = 100, pit_id = pit, pit_keep_alive = "2m" }
    preq.sort.push(opensearch.SortAsc("year"))
    mut pp := opensearch.SearchWith(c, "", preq)
    until pp.hits.len() > 0:
        preq.search_after = pp.hits.get(pp.hits.len() - 1).sort
        pp = opensearch.SearchWith(c, "", preq)
    end
    println opensearch.ListPits(c), opensearch.DeletePit(c, pit), opensearch.DeleteAllPits(c)

    mut bodies := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    bodies.push(`{"query":{"term":{"tag":"poetry"}},"size":0}`)
    bodies.push(`{"query":{"match_all":{}},"size":0}`)
    each one in opensearch.MSearch(c, "books", bodies):
        println one.ok, one.total
    end
    println opensearch.SearchTemplate(c, "books", "by_tag", `{"tag":"poetry"}`).total
    println opensearch.SearchInlineTemplate(c, "books", `{"query":{"term":{"tag":"{{t}}"}}}`, `{"t":"poetry"}`).total
    println opensearch.RenderTemplate(c, `{"query":{"term":{"tag":"{{t}}"}}}`, `{"t":"poetry"}`)
    println opensearch.Explain(c, "books", "1", opensearch.Match("title", "kings"))
    println opensearch.Validate(c, "books", opensearch.Match("title", "kings"))
    mut fields := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    fields.push("title")
    println opensearch.FieldCaps(c, "books", fields)
    println opensearch.JsonPath(r.raw, "hits.hits.0._source.title"), opensearch.JsonPathRaw(r.raw, "hits.total")
    println opensearch.JsonItems(`[1,"two",{"three":3}]`).len()
end
```

### `TaskInfo`

```salam
struct TaskInfo
```

A background task.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The request succeeded and the task did not fail. |
| `id` | `str = ""` | The task id, `node:number`. |
| `completed` | `bool = false` | It has finished. |
| `action` | `str = ""` | What it does, such as `indices:data/write/reindex`. |
| `description` | `str = ""` | A description. |
| `status` | `str = ""` | Its progress as raw JSON. |
| `response` | `str = ""` | Its result as raw JSON, once completed. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | What went wrong. |

db-opensearch-ClusterHealth.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    h := opensearch.ClusterHealth(c)
    println h.ok, h.cluster_name, h.status, h.timed_out, h.nodes, h.data_nodes, h.active_primary_shards
    println h.active_shards, h.relocating_shards, h.initializing_shards, h.unassigned_shards, h.pending_tasks, h.active_shards_percent
    println opensearch.WaitForStatus(c, "books", "yellow", "30s").status
    println opensearch.ClusterStats(c).len() > 0, opensearch.ClusterState(c, "metadata").len() > 0
    println opensearch.PutClusterSettings(c, `{"cluster.routing.allocation.enable":"all"}`, "")
    println opensearch.GetClusterSettings(c)
    println opensearch.AllocationExplain(c, `{"index":"books","shard":0,"primary":true}`).len()
    println opensearch.NodesInfo(c, "os").len() > 0, opensearch.NodesStats(c, "jvm").len() > 0, opensearch.HotThreads(c).len() > 0
    each row in opensearch.Cat(c, "shards?h=index,shard,state"):
        println row
    end
    println opensearch.CatText(c, "nodes"), opensearch.Plugins(c), opensearch.HasPlugin(c, "opensearch-knn")

    rx := opensearch.ReindexBody(c, `{"source":{"index":"books"},"dest":{"index":"books_v4"}}`, false)
    t := opensearch.GetTask(c, rx.task)
    println t.ok, t.id, t.completed, t.action, t.description, t.status, t.response, t.error
    println opensearch.WaitTask(c, rx.task, "60s").completed, opensearch.CancelTask(c, rx.task)
    println opensearch.ListTasks(c, "*reindex").len() > 0

    println opensearch.PutRepository(c, "backups", "fs", `{"location":"/mnt/backups"}`), opensearch.VerifyRepository(c, "backups")
    println opensearch.GetRepository(c, "backups"), opensearch.CreateSnapshot(c, "backups", "nightly-1", "books", true)
    println opensearch.Snapshots(c, "backups"), opensearch.GetSnapshot(c, "backups", "nightly-1").len() > 0
    println opensearch.SnapshotStatus(c, "backups", "nightly-1").len() > 0
    println opensearch.RestoreSnapshot(c, "backups", "nightly-1", `{"indices":"books","rename_pattern":"(.+)","rename_replacement":"restored_$1"}`, true)
    println opensearch.DeleteSnapshot(c, "backups", "nightly-1"), opensearch.DeleteRepository(c, "backups")

    mut procs := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    procs.push(opensearch.Processor("lowercase", `{"field":"tag"}`))
    procs.push(opensearch.Processor("set", `{"field":"seen","value":true}`))
    println opensearch.PutPipeline(c, "clean", opensearch.Pipeline("tidy incoming books", procs))
    mut docs := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    docs.push(`{"tag":"POETRY"}`)
    println opensearch.SimulatePipeline(c, "clean", docs), opensearch.GetPipeline(c, "clean").len() > 0
    println opensearch.DeletePipeline(c, "clean")

    println opensearch.PutScript(c, "double", "doc['stock'].value * 2"), opensearch.GetScript(c, "double")
    println opensearch.PutSearchTemplate(c, "by_tag", `{"query":{"term":{"tag":"{{tag}}"}}}`), opensearch.DeleteScript(c, "by_tag"), opensearch.DeleteScript(c, "double")
end
```

### `AuthInfo`

```salam
struct AuthInfo
```

Who the security plugin says you are.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The request succeeded. |
| `user` | `str = ""` | The user name. |
| `roles` | `Vector` | The security roles. |
| `backend_roles` | `Vector` | The backend roles. |
| `tenants` | `Vector` | The tenants the user may use. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | What went wrong. |

db-opensearch-PutPolicy.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.ConnectInsecure("https://localhost:9200", "admin", "S3cret-pass!")
    mut patterns := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    patterns.push("logs-*")
    println opensearch.PutPolicy(c, "logs-30d", opensearch.DeleteAfterPolicy("drop old logs", "30d", patterns))
    println opensearch.GetPolicy(c, "logs-30d").len() > 0
    println opensearch.UpdatePolicy(c, "logs-30d", opensearch.DeleteAfterPolicy("drop old logs", "60d", patterns), 0 as i64, 1 as i64)
    println opensearch.AddPolicy(c, "logs-000001", "logs-30d"), opensearch.PolicyIdOf(c, "logs-000001")
    println opensearch.ChangePolicy(c, "logs-000001", "logs-30d", "hot"), opensearch.RetryPolicy(c, "logs-000001")
    println opensearch.ExplainPolicy(c, "logs-000001"), opensearch.RemovePolicy(c, "logs-000001"), opensearch.DeletePolicy(c, "logs-30d")

    me := opensearch.WhoAmI(c)
    println me.ok, me.user, me.roles, me.backend_roles, me.tenants, me.error
    println opensearch.SecurityHealth(c)
    mut perms := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    perms.push("cluster_monitor")
    mut actions := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    actions.push("read")
    println opensearch.PutRole(c, "logs_reader", opensearch.RoleBody(perms, patterns, actions)), opensearch.GetRole(c, "logs_reader")
    println opensearch.PutUser(c, "maryam", "Strong-Pass-1!", Vector {} as Vector<str>, `{"team":"ops"}`), opensearch.GetUser(c, "maryam")
    mut users := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    users.push("maryam")
    println opensearch.PutRoleMapping(c, "logs_reader", users, Vector {} as Vector<str>), opensearch.GetRoleMapping(c, "logs_reader")
    println opensearch.Users(c), opensearch.ChangePassword(c, "S3cret-pass!", "N3w-secret-pass!")
    println opensearch.DeleteRoleMapping(c, "logs_reader"), opensearch.DeleteUser(c, "maryam"), opensearch.DeleteRole(c, "logs_reader")

    monitor := `{"type":"monitor","name":"errors","enabled":true,"schedule":{"period":{"interval":5,"unit":"MINUTES"}},"inputs":[{"search":{"indices":["logs-*"],"query":{"size":0,"query":{"match":{"level":"error"}}}}}],"triggers":[]}`
    id := opensearch.CreateMonitor(c, monitor)
    println id, opensearch.GetMonitor(c, id).len() > 0, opensearch.UpdateMonitor(c, id, monitor)
    println opensearch.ExecuteMonitor(c, id, true).len() > 0, opensearch.SearchMonitors(c, opensearch.MatchAll()).total
    println opensearch.DeleteMonitor(c, id)
end
```

### `KnnMethod`

```salam
struct KnnMethod
```

How a `knn_vector` field is indexed.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str = "hnsw"` | The algorithm, `hnsw` or `ivf`. |
| `engine` | `str = "lucene"` | `lucene`, `faiss` or `nmslib`. |
| `space_type` | `str = "l2"` | The distance: `l2`, `cosinesimil`, `innerproduct` and others, depending on the engine. |
| `m` | `int = 0` | The HNSW link count; 0 for the default. |
| `ef_construction` | `int = 0` | The HNSW build quality; 0 for the default. |

db-opensearch-Knn.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    method := opensearch.KnnMethod { name = "hnsw", engine = "lucene", space_type = "cosinesimil", m = 16, ef_construction = 128 }
    mut extra := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    extra.push(opensearch.Property("text", "text"))
    println opensearch.KnnIndexSettings(1, 0), opensearch.KnnVectorField(3, method)
    println opensearch.CreateIndex(c, "places", opensearch.KnnIndexBody("embedding", 3, method, extra))
    opensearch.Index(c, "places", "1", `{"text":"a cafe","embedding":[0.1,0.9,0.2]}`)
    opensearch.Refresh(c, "places")
    mut v := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    v.push(0.1)
    v.push(0.8)
    v.push(0.3)
    r := opensearch.Search(c, "places", opensearch.Knn("embedding", v, 5))
    println r.total
    println opensearch.KnnWarmup(c, "places"), opensearch.KnnClearCache(c, "places"), opensearch.KnnStats(c).len() > 0
    println opensearch.KnnTrainModel(c, "pq-model", `{"training_index":"train","training_field":"v","dimension":3,"method":{"name":"ivf","engine":"faiss"}}`)
    println opensearch.KnnGetModel(c, "pq-model"), opensearch.KnnDeleteModel(c, "pq-model")

    mut w := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    w.push(0.3)
    w.push(0.7)
    println opensearch.PutSearchPipeline(c, "hybrid", opensearch.NormalizationPipeline("min_max", "arithmetic_mean", w))
    println opensearch.GetSearchPipeline(c, "hybrid"), opensearch.DeleteSearchPipeline(c, "hybrid")

    task := opensearch.MlRegisterModel(c, `{"name":"huggingface/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2","version":"1.0.1","model_format":"TORCH_SCRIPT"}`)
    println opensearch.MlGetTask(c, task)
    println opensearch.MlDeployModel(c, "model-1"), opensearch.MlGetModel(c, "model-1").len() > 0
    println opensearch.MlPredict(c, "text_embedding", "model-1", `{"text_docs":["salam"]}`)
    println opensearch.MlUndeployModel(c, "model-1"), opensearch.MlDeleteModel(c, "model-1")
end
```

### `ByQueryResult`

```salam
struct ByQueryResult
```

The result of a delete by query, update by query or reindex.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It finished with no failures. |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status. |
| `took` | `i64 = 0` | How long it took, in milliseconds. |
| `timed_out` | `bool = false` | It ran out of time. |
| `total` | `i64 = 0` | How many documents it looked at. |
| `created` | `i64 = 0` | How many it created. |
| `updated` | `i64 = 0` | How many it updated. |
| `deleted` | `i64 = 0` | How many it deleted. |
| `batches` | `i64 = 0` | How many scroll batches it took. |
| `version_conflicts` | `i64 = 0` | How many hit a version conflict. |
| `noops` | `i64 = 0` | How many a script left unchanged. |
| `failures` | `str = ""` | The failures as raw JSON; empty when there were none. |
| `task` | `str = ""` | The task id, when it runs in the background. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | What went wrong. |

db-opensearch-Index.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    w := opensearch.Index(c, "books", "1", `{"title":"The Book of Kings","year":1010,"stock":3}`)
    println w.ok, w.status, w.index, w.id, w.result, w.version, w.seq_no, w.primary_term
    println w.shards_total, w.shards_successful, w.error
    auto := opensearch.IndexWith(c, "books", "", `{"title":"Masnavi"}`, opensearch.Options { refresh = opensearch.REFRESH_WAIT_FOR, routing = "poetry" })
    println auto.id
    dup := opensearch.Create(c, "books", "1", `{"title":"again"}`)
    println dup.ok, dup.status
    piped := opensearch.CreateWith(c, "books", "2", `{"title":"Golestan"}`, opensearch.Options { pipeline = "clean", timeout = "5s", wait_for_active_shards = "1" })
    println piped.result

    d := opensearch.Get(c, "books", "1")
    println d.found, d.index, d.id, d.version, d.seq_no, d.primary_term, d.routing, d.source, d.fields, d.error
    mut only := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    only.push("title")
    println opensearch.GetFields(c, "books", "1", only, "").source
    println opensearch.GetSource(c, "books", "1"), opensearch.Exists(c, "books", "1")

    println opensearch.Update(c, "books", "1", `{"stock":2}`).result
    cas := opensearch.UpdateWith(c, "books", "1", `{"doc":{"stock":1}}`, opensearch.Options { if_seq_no = d.seq_no, if_primary_term = d.primary_term, retry_on_conflict = -1 })
    println cas.ok, opensearch.ErrorType(c)
    println opensearch.Upsert(c, "books", "9", `{"title":"Shahnameh","stock":1}`).result
    println opensearch.UpdateScript(c, "books", "1", opensearch.Script("ctx._source.stock += params.n", `{"n":5}`), `{"stock":5}`).result
    println opensearch.DeleteWith(c, "books", "9", opensearch.Options { refresh = opensearch.REFRESH_TRUE, version = 3, version_type = "external" }).result
    println opensearch.Delete(c, "books", "2").result

    mut ids := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    ids.push("1")
    ids.push("404")
    each doc in opensearch.MGet(c, "books", ids):
        println doc.id, doc.found
    end
    println opensearch.Count(c, "books", ""), opensearch.Count(c, "books", opensearch.Range("year", "1000", ""))

    mut b := opensearch.NewBulk()
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "10", `{"title":"Divan"}`)
    opensearch.BulkIndexRouted(b, "books", "11", "poetry", `{"title":"Rubaiyat"}`)
    opensearch.BulkCreate(b, "books", "", `{"title":"Bustan"}`)
    opensearch.BulkUpdate(b, "books", "10", `{"stock":4}`)
    opensearch.BulkUpsert(b, "books", "12", `{"title":"Kalila"}`)
    opensearch.BulkDelete(b, "books", "3")
    println opensearch.BulkLen(b), b.count, b.lines.len()
    print opensearch.BulkBody(b)
    br := opensearch.BulkSendWith(c, b, opensearch.REFRESH_FALSE)
    println br.ok, br.status, br.took, br.errors, br.succeeded, br.failed, br.error
    each it in br.items:
        println it.action, it.index, it.id, it.status, it.ok, it.result, it.version, it.error_type, it.error_reason
    end
    opensearch.BulkReset(b)
    opensearch.BulkIndex(b, "books", "13", `{"title":"Makhzan"}`)
    println opensearch.BulkSend(c, b).ok
    opensearch.BulkFree(b)
    println opensearch.ParseBulk(`{"took":1,"errors":false,"items":[]}`).ok

    ub := opensearch.UpdateByQuery(c, "books", opensearch.Term("stock", "0"), opensearch.Script("ctx._source.out = true", ""))
    println ub.ok, ub.status, ub.took, ub.timed_out, ub.total, ub.updated, ub.batches, ub.version_conflicts, ub.noops, ub.failures
    ub2 := opensearch.UpdateByQueryWith(c, "books", "", "", opensearch.Options { conflicts = "proceed", pipeline = "clean" })
    println ub2.updated
    dq := opensearch.DeleteByQuery(c, "books", opensearch.Term("out", "true"))
    println dq.deleted, opensearch.DeleteByQueryWith(c, "books", opensearch.MatchAll(), opensearch.Options { refresh = "true", conflicts = "proceed" }).deleted
    rx := opensearch.Reindex(c, "books", "books_v2")
    println rx.created, rx.error
    task := opensearch.ReindexBody(c, `{"source":{"index":"books"},"dest":{"index":"books_v3"}}`, false)
    println task.task
end
```

### `Config`

```salam
struct Config
```

Everything `NewClient` needs.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes` | `Vector` | Node urls; each entry may hold several separated by commas, and a url may carry `user:password@` and a path prefix. |
| `username` | `str = ""` | The user for basic authentication. |
| `password` | `str = ""` | The password for basic authentication. |
| `bearer` | `str = ""` | A bearer token, sent instead of basic authentication. |
| `ca_file` | `str = ""` | A PEM file of the certificate authorities to trust for https. |
| `insecure` | `bool = false` | Skip certificate checks; only for a test server with a self signed certificate. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int = 30000` | How long one request may take, in milliseconds; 0 for no limit. |
| `max_retries` | `int = 3` | How many more times a request is tried on another node after a failed connection or a 502, 503 or 504. |
| `headers` | `HashMap` | Extra headers sent with every request. |
| `aws_region` | `str = ""` | Sign every request with AWS SigV4 for this region; empty for no signing. |
| `aws_service` | `str = ""` | The AWS service to sign for, `SERVICE_ES` (the default) or `SERVICE_AOSS`. |
| `aws_access_key` | `str = ""` | The AWS access key id. |
| `aws_secret_key` | `str = ""` | The AWS secret access key. |
| `aws_session_token` | `str = ""` | The AWS session token for temporary credentials; empty if none. |

db-opensearch-Client.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    mut cfg := opensearch.DefaultConfig()
    cfg.nodes.push("https://node2.example.com:9200, https://node3.example.com:9200")
    cfg.username = "admin"
    cfg.password = "S3cret-pass!"
    cfg.ca_file = "/etc/ssl/certs/opensearch-ca.pem"
    cfg.timeout_ms = 10000
    cfg.max_retries = 2
    cfg.headers.put("X-Opaque-Id", "shop-api")
    mut c := opensearch.NewClient(cfg)
    if not opensearch.Ok(c):
        println opensearch.Error(c)
        ret 1
    end
    println opensearch.Nodes(c), opensearch.AuthHeader(c).len() > 0, opensearch.VERSION
    println opensearch.Ping(c)

    info := opensearch.GetInfo(c)
    println info.ok, info.name, info.cluster_name, info.cluster_uuid, info.version, info.distribution
    println info.build_type, info.lucene_version, info.minimum_wire_compatibility_version, info.tagline

    r := opensearch.Perform(c, "GET", "/_cat/health?format=json", "")
    println r.ok, r.status, r.body
    if not r.ok:
        println r.error, r.error_type, r.error_reason
    end
    nd := opensearch.PerformNdjson(c, "POST", "/_bulk", "{\"delete\":{\"_index\":\"shop\",\"_id\":\"1\"}}\n")
    println nd.status, opensearch.Status(c), opensearch.ErrorType(c), opensearch.ErrorReason(c)
    txt := opensearch.PerformText(c, "POST", "/_plugins/_sql?format=csv", `{"query":"SELECT 1"}`, "application/json")
    println txt.body
    opensearch.Close(c)

    mut local := opensearch.Connect(opensearch.DEFAULT_URL)
    println opensearch.Ok(local), opensearch.DEFAULT_PORT, opensearch.DEAD_NODE_MS
    opensearch.Close(local)
    mut demo := opensearch.ConnectInsecure("https://localhost:9200", "admin", "S3cret-pass!")
    opensearch.Close(demo)
    mut auth := opensearch.ConnectAuth("https://search.example.com", "reader", "pass")
    println opensearch.EncodeBasic("reader", "pass")
    opensearch.Close(auth)

    mut aws := opensearch.ConnectAWS(
        "https://search-shop.eu-west-1.es.amazonaws.com", "eu-west-1", opensearch.SERVICE_ES,
        "AKIAEXAMPLE", "secret-key", ""
    )
    opensearch.SetSigningTime(aws, 1700000000 as i64)
    println opensearch.ClusterHealth(aws).status
    opensearch.Close(aws)
    mut serverless := opensearch.ConnectAWS(
        "https://abc123.eu-west-1.aoss.amazonaws.com", "eu-west-1", opensearch.SERVICE_AOSS,
        "AKIAEXAMPLE", "secret-key", "session-token"
    )
    opensearch.Close(serverless)
    ret 0
end
```

### `Options`

```salam
struct Options
```

Optional settings for writes. Empty strings and negative numbers are left out.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | `str = ""` | One of the `REFRESH_` values. |
| `routing` | `str = ""` | The routing value, to place a document on a chosen shard. |
| `pipeline` | `str = ""` | An ingest pipeline to run the document through. |
| `timeout` | `str = ""` | How long to wait for shards, such as `5s`. |
| `wait_for_active_shards` | `str = ""` | How many shard copies must be active, or `all`. |
| `conflicts` | `str = ""` | For by query calls: `proceed` keeps going past version conflicts. |
| `if_seq_no` | `i64 = -1` | Write only if the document still has this sequence number. |
| `if_primary_term` | `i64 = -1` | Write only if the document still has this primary term. |
| `retry_on_conflict` | `int = -1` | For updates: how many times to retry on a version conflict. |
| `version` | `i64 = -1` | An explicit document version. |
| `version_type` | `str = ""` | The version type, such as `external`. |
| `require_alias` | `bool = false` | The target must be an alias. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-opensearch-Index.salam

### `SearchRequest`

```salam
struct SearchRequest
```

A search. Empty strings, empty lists and negative numbers are left out of the request body.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query, made with the builders or written as JSON. |
| `from` | `int = -1` | How many hits to skip. |
| `size` | `int = -1` | How many hits to return. |
| `sort` | `Vector` | Sort clauses, such as `SortDesc("date")`. |
| `source` | `Vector` | Return only these source fields. |
| `source_excludes` | `Vector` | Leave these source fields out. |
| `no_source` | `bool = false` | Return no source at all. |
| `fields` | `Vector` | Fields to return in `Hit.fields`. |
| `docvalue_fields` | `Vector` | Doc value fields to return. |
| `aggs` | `str = ""` | The aggregations, built with `AddAgg`. |
| `highlight` | `str = ""` | The highlight settings, from `Highlight`. |
| `post_filter` | `str = ""` | A filter applied after the aggregations are counted. |
| `collapse` | `str = ""` | Collapse hits on a field, from `Collapse`. |
| `suggest` | `str = ""` | Suggesters, from `TermSuggest` or `CompletionSuggest`. |
| `rescore` | `str = ""` | A rescore clause as JSON. |
| `script_fields` | `str = ""` | Script fields as JSON. |
| `search_after` | `str = ""` | The sort values of the last hit, as a JSON array, to fetch the next page. |
| `pit_id` | `str = ""` | A point in time id from `CreatePit`; the search then goes to `/_search` and the index is not named. |
| `pit_keep_alive` | `str = ""` | How much longer to keep the point in time, such as `1m`. |
| `track_total_hits` | `str = ""` | `true`, `false` or a number: how far to count matches exactly. |
| `track_scores` | `bool = false` | Compute scores even when sorting by a field. |
| `min_score` | `str = ""` | Leave out hits below this score. |
| `timeout` | `str = ""` | Stop searching after this long, such as `2s`. |
| `explain` | `bool = false` | Explain how each score was computed. |
| `version` | `bool = false` | Return each hit's version. |
| `seq_no_primary_term` | `bool = false` | Return each hit's sequence number and primary term. |
| `ext` | `str = ""` | Plugin extensions as JSON, such as retrieval augmented generation settings. |
| `extra` | `Vector` | More members written as `"key":value`, added as they are. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-opensearch-Query.salam

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | Every action succeeded. |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status of the request. |
| `took` | `i64 = 0` | How long it took, in milliseconds. |
| `errors` | `bool = false` | The server reported at least one failed action. |
| `succeeded` | `int = 0` | How many actions succeeded. |
| `failed` | `int = 0` | How many failed. |
| `items` | `Vector` | One result per action, in order. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | A summary of what went wrong. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: db-opensearch-Index.salam

db-opensearch-CreateIndex.salam

```salam
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    mut props := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    props.push(opensearch.Property("title", "text"))
    props.push(opensearch.PropertyWith("title_fa", "text", `{"analyzer":"persian"}`))
    props.push(opensearch.Property("tag", "keyword"))
    props.push(opensearch.Property("year", "integer"))
    println opensearch.CreateIndexWith(c, "books", 1, 0, opensearch.Properties(props))
    println opensearch.CreateIndex(c, "logs-000001", `{"aliases":{"logs":{"is_write_index":true}}}`)
    println opensearch.IndexExists(c, "books"), opensearch.GetIndex(c, "books").len() > 0
    println opensearch.PutMapping(c, "books", "{" + opensearch.Property("isbn", "keyword") + "}")
    println opensearch.PutMappingBody(c, "books", `{"dynamic":"strict"}`), opensearch.GetMapping(c, "books")
    println opensearch.PutSettings(c, "books", `{"index":{"refresh_interval":"5s"}}`)
    println opensearch.GetSettings(c, "books").len() > 0, opensearch.GetSetting(c, "books", "index.refresh_interval")
    println opensearch.Refresh(c, "books"), opensearch.Flush(c, "books"), opensearch.ForceMerge(c, "books", 1), opensearch.ClearCache(c, "books")
    println opensearch.CloseIndex(c, "books"), opensearch.OpenIndex(c, "books")
    println opensearch.PutSettings(c, "books", `{"index.blocks.write":true}`)
    println opensearch.CloneIndex(c, "books", "books_clone", ""), opensearch.ShrinkIndex(c, "books", "books_small", ""), opensearch.SplitIndex(c, "books", "books_big", `{"settings":{"index.number_of_shards":2}}`)
    println opensearch.IndexStats(c, "books").len() > 0

    println opensearch.PutAlias(c, "books", "library"), opensearch.AliasExists(c, "library"), opensearch.AliasIndices(c, "library")
    println opensearch.PutAliasFiltered(c, "books", "poetry", opensearch.Term("tag", "poetry"), false)
    println opensearch.GetAliases(c, "books"), opensearch.DeleteAlias(c, "books", "poetry")
    mut acts := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    acts.push(opensearch.AliasAction("add", "books_clone", "library"))
    acts.push(opensearch.AliasAction("remove", "books", "library"))
    println opensearch.UpdateAliases(c, acts), opensearch.SwapAlias(c, "library", "books_clone", "books")

    mut patterns := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    patterns.push("logs-*")
    tpl := opensearch.IndexTemplate(patterns, `{"number_of_replicas":0}`, "{" + opensearch.Property("msg", "text") + "}", 10)
    println opensearch.PutIndexTemplate(c, "logs", tpl), opensearch.IndexTemplateExists(c, "logs"), opensearch.GetIndexTemplate(c, "logs").len() > 0
    println opensearch.PutComponentTemplate(c, "base", `{"template":{"settings":{"number_of_shards":1}}}`), opensearch.GetComponentTemplate(c, "base").len() > 0
    println opensearch.Rollover(c, "logs", `{"max_docs":1000000,"max_age":"7d"}`)
    println opensearch.PutIndexTemplate(c, "events", `{"index_patterns":["events-*"],"data_stream":{}}`)
    println opensearch.CreateDataStream(c, "events-web"), opensearch.DataStreams(c), opensearch.DeleteDataStream(c, "events-web")
    println opensearch.Analyze(c, "", "standard", "Salam to OpenSearch")
    each ix in opensearch.CatIndices(c, "books*"):
        println ix.health, ix.status, ix.index, ix.uuid, ix.primaries, ix.replicas, ix.docs_count, ix.docs_deleted, ix.store_size
    end
    println opensearch.DeleteIndexTemplate(c, "logs"), opensearch.DeleteIndexTemplate(c, "events"), opensearch.DeleteComponentTemplate(c, "base")
    println opensearch.DeleteIndex(c, "books_clone,books_small,books_big"), opensearch.DeleteIndexIfExists(c, "never-made")
end
```

### `SqlRows`

```salam
struct SqlRows
```

The rows of a SQL or PPL query; it fetches more pages as you go and implements `db.Rows`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `void*` | The internal state. |

db-opensearch-Sql.salam

```salam
import db
import db.opensearch

func main:
    c := opensearch.Connect("http://localhost:9200")
    conn := opensearch.Conn(c)
    println conn.Kind(), conn.Ok(), conn.Ping(), db.QueryInt(conn, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books")
    rows := conn.Query("SELECT title, year, price FROM books WHERE year > 1000 ORDER BY year")
    println rows.Ok(), rows.ColumnCount(), rows.ColumnName(0), rows.ColumnType(1)
    until rows.Next():
        println rows.Text(0), rows.Int(1), rows.Int64(1), rows.Float(2), rows.IsNull(2)
    end
    rows.Close()
    println conn.Exec("DELETE FROM books WHERE year < 0"), conn.Changes(), conn.LastInsertId(), conn.Error(), conn.Quote("it's")
    tx := conn.Begin()
    println tx.Ok(), tx.Exec("SELECT 1"), tx.Query("SELECT 1").Ok(), tx.Commit(), tx.Rollback()

    mut params := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    params.push(opensearch.SqlParam("integer", "1000"))
    mut paged := opensearch.SqlWith(c, "SELECT title FROM books WHERE year > ?", params, 100)
    println paged.Total(), paged.ColumnTypeName(0), paged.Error()
    until paged.Next():
        println paged.Raw(0)
    end
    paged.Close()
    rs := opensearch.Sql(c, "SHOW TABLES LIKE books%")
    rs.Close()
    println opensearch.SqlFormat(c, "SELECT title FROM books", "csv")
    println opensearch.SqlExplain(c, "SELECT title FROM books").len() > 0

    p := opensearch.Ppl(c, "source=books | where year > 1000 | stats count() by tag")
    until p.Next():
        println p.Int(0), p.Text(1)
    end
    p.Close()
    println opensearch.PplFormat(c, "source=books | fields title", "raw"), opensearch.PplExplain(c, "source=books").len() > 0
    d := opensearch.Database { handle = c.handle }
    t := opensearch.Txn {}
    println d.Kind(), t.Ok(), conn.Close()
end
```

# graphql

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/graphql/

A GraphQL server: schemas, resolvers, query execution and HTTP handling.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add graphql`

GraphQL is a language for asking an API for data: the client asks for exactly the fields it needs and the server sends back just those. This package is a complete server side implementation of the specification. Write the schema as SDL text and pass it to `ParseSchema`, or build it with the `Add...` functions, register resolvers for the fields and run a query with `ExecuteSource`.

A resolver is a function that takes a slot number; it reads the arguments and the parent object with `ArgStr`, `ParentField` and their siblings, and answers with one of the `Resolve...` functions or with `Fail`. A field without a resolver takes the value of the same name from the parent object. For a web server, call `HandleHttpSimple` inside a net/http handler.

For calling someone else's GraphQL API, the client helpers `BuildRequestBody` and `ParseResponse` build the JSON body and read the answer; send it with net/http. When you control both sides and do not need clients choosing their own fields, a plain JSON route or rpc is less work.

Things that catch people out:

- A subscription runs once and returns one result, like a query. There is no event stream and no WebSocket transport; push updates yourself with net/websocket.

- A field that fails becomes `null` and the rest of the answer still arrives, so check `ResultOk` even when `data` is there.

- Resolvers run one field at a time. A list of 100 posts whose `author` resolver queries a database makes 100 queries; load what the list needs once, as the first guide shows.

## Related types and field resolvers

Most schemas link types together: a post has an author, an author has posts. Give the root field a resolver that returns the list, and give the linking field its own resolver on the child type. Inside it, `ParentField` reads the object being resolved, here the post, so the resolver can look up the author by `authorId`. Fields without a resolver, such as `title` and `name`, are copied from the object by name.

graphql-guide-blog.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value

mut authors := value.NewValueArray()
mut posts := value.NewValueArray()

func person(id: i64, name: str): value.Value:
    mut a := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(a, "id", value.ValueInt(id))
    value.ObjectSet(a, "name", value.ValueString(name))
    ret a
end

func post(id: i64, title: str, author_id: i64): value.Value:
    mut p := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(p, "id", value.ValueInt(id))
    value.ObjectSet(p, "title", value.ValueString(title))
    value.ObjectSet(p, "authorId", value.ValueInt(author_id))
    ret p
end

func all_posts(slot: i64):
    graphql.Resolve(slot, posts)
end

func post_author(slot: i64):
    wanted := value.AsInt(graphql.ParentField(slot, "authorId"))
    repeat value.ArrayLen(authors) in i:
        a := value.ArrayGet(authors, i)
        if value.AsInt(value.ObjectGet(a, "id")) == wanted:
            graphql.Resolve(slot, a)
            ret
        end
    end
    graphql.ResolveNull(slot)
end

func main:
    value.ArrayPush(authors, person(1, "Sara"))
    value.ArrayPush(authors, person(2, "Omid"))
    value.ArrayPush(posts, post(10, "Hello GraphQL", 1))
    value.ArrayPush(posts, post(11, "Salam and SQL", 2))
    value.ArrayPush(posts, post(12, "Resolvers explained", 1))
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    mut s := graphql.ParseSchema(`
type Author { id: Int! name: String! }
type Post { id: Int! title: String! author: Author }
type Query { posts: [Post!]! }`, err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "posts", all_posts)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Post", "author", post_author)
    mut r := graphql.Run(s, `{ posts { title author { name } } }`)
    println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r)
    graphql.FreeResult(r)
    mut r2 := graphql.Run(s, `{ posts { id } }`)
    println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r2)
    graphql.FreeResult(r2)
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"data": {"posts": [{"author": {"name": "Sara"}, "title": "Hello GraphQL"}, {"author": {"name": "Omid"}, "title": "Salam and SQL"}, {"author": {"name": "Sara"}, "title": "Resolvers explained"}]}}
{"data": {"posts": [{"id": 10}, {"id": 11}, {"id": 12}]}}
```

The second query shows the main promise of GraphQL: it asks for ids only, so the `author` resolver never runs. A resolver that is expensive, like a database lookup, only costs something when a client asks for its field. When many posts share authors, load the authors once into a lookup table, such as a `HashMap` keyed by id, instead of searching or querying once per post.

## Mutations with input types

Changes go through the `Mutation` type. An `input` type groups the arguments, and the client sends the values as variables so the query text stays fixed. The resolver receives the input object with `Arg` and reads its fields with encoding/value.

graphql-guide-mutation.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value

mut todos := value.NewValueArray()

func list(slot: i64):
    graphql.Resolve(slot, todos)
end

func add_todo(slot: i64):
    data := graphql.Arg(slot, "input")
    title := value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(data, "title"))
    if title == "":
        graphql.Fail(slot, "title must not be empty")
        ret
    end
    mut t := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(t, "id", value.ValueInt(value.ArrayLen(todos) + 1))
    value.ObjectSet(t, "title", value.ValueString(title))
    mut done := false
    if value.ObjectHas(data, "done"):
        done = value.AsBool(value.ObjectGet(data, "done"))
    end
    value.ObjectSet(t, "done", value.ValueBool(done))
    value.ArrayPush(todos, t)
    graphql.Resolve(slot, t)
end

func main:
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    mut s := graphql.ParseSchema(`
type Todo { id: Int! title: String! done: Boolean! }
input TodoInput { title: String! done: Boolean = false }
type Query { todos: [Todo!]! }
type Mutation { addTodo(input: TodoInput!): Todo }`, err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "todos", list)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Mutation", "addTodo", add_todo)

    add := `mutation Add($t: TodoInput!) { addTodo(input: $t) { id title done } }`
    each title in ["write the report", "", "send invoices"]:
        mut fields := value.NewValueObject()
        value.ObjectSet(fields, "title", value.ValueString(title))
        mut vars := value.NewValueObject()
        value.ObjectSet(vars, "t", fields)
        mut r := graphql.ExecuteSource(s, add, "Add", vars, value.ValueNull(), value.ValueNull())
        if graphql.ResultOk(r):
            println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r)
        else:
            println "error:", graphql.ResultErrorMessage(r)
        end
        graphql.FreeResult(r)
    end
    mut all := graphql.Run(s, `{ todos { id title } }`)
    println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(all)
    graphql.FreeResult(all)
    mut bad := graphql.Run(s, `mutation { addTodo(input: { done: true }) { id } }`)
    println graphql.ResultErrorMessage(bad)
    graphql.FreeResult(bad)
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
end
```

Output:

```text
{"data": {"addTodo": {"done": false, "id": 1, "title": "write the report"}}}
error: title must not be empty (line 1, column 32) at addTodo
{"data": {"addTodo": {"done": false, "id": 2, "title": "send invoices"}}}
{"data": {"todos": [{"id": 1, "title": "write the report"}, {"id": 2, "title": "send invoices"}]}}
argument "input" is invalid: field "title" of required type is missing (line 1, column 0)
```

Two kinds of error show up here. When the resolver calls `Fail`, the request ran but that field failed: the message carries the field path and position. When the input does not match the schema, as in the last query where the required `title` is missing, the request is rejected before any resolver runs. Either way `ResultOk` is false and `ResultErrorMessage` gives the first message.

## Per request context and authorization

Who is asking is not an argument of the query; it comes from the HTTP request, a cookie or a token. Pass it in as the context value of `ExecuteSource` and read it in any resolver with `Context`. A resolver that refuses calls `Fail`, and the other fields of the same query still get their data.

graphql-guide-context.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value

func user_of(slot: i64): str:
    ctx := graphql.Context(slot)
    if value.IsObject(ctx) and value.ObjectHas(ctx, "user"):
        ret value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(ctx, "user"))
    end
    ret ""
end

func me(slot: i64):
    name := user_of(slot)
    if name == "":
        graphql.ResolveNull(slot)
        ret
    end
    graphql.ResolveStr(slot, name)
end

func payroll(slot: i64):
    if user_of(slot) != "admin":
        graphql.Fail(slot, "only admin may read the payroll")
        ret
    end
    graphql.ResolveInt(slot, 182000)
end

func ask(s: graphql.Schema, user: str):
    mut ctx := value.NewValueObject()
    if user != "":
        value.ObjectSet(ctx, "user", value.ValueString(user))
    end
    mut r := graphql.ExecuteSource(s, `{ me payroll }`, "", value.ValueNull(), value.ValueNull(), ctx)
    println "[" + user + "]", graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r)
    graphql.FreeResult(r)
end

func main:
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    mut s := graphql.ParseSchema(`type Query { me: String payroll: Int }`, err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "me", me)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "payroll", payroll)
    ask(s, "")
    ask(s, "sara")
    ask(s, "admin")
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
end
```

Output:

```text
[] {"data": {"me": null, "payroll": null}, "errors": [{"locations": [{"column": 6, "line": 1}], "message": "only admin may read the payroll", "path": ["payroll"]}]}
[sara] {"data": {"me": "sara", "payroll": null}, "errors": [{"locations": [{"column": 6, "line": 1}], "message": "only admin may read the payroll", "path": ["payroll"]}]}
[admin] {"data": {"me": "admin", "payroll": 182000}}
```

Note that a failed field becomes `null`, with an entry in `errors` naming its path, instead of failing the whole response. This is why fields that may be refused should be nullable in the schema: `payroll: Int`, not `payroll: Int!`. A non-null field that fails makes its parent `null` too.

## A GraphQL endpoint over HTTP

`HandleHttp` turns an HTTP request into a GraphQL answer: it accepts `POST` with a JSON body and `GET` with the query in the URL, runs it, and returns the status, content type and body for the response. Its last argument is the context, so the handler below reads a bearer token and hands the user name to the resolvers. `HandleHttpSimple` is the same without a root value and context.

graphql-guide-server.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value
import net.http
import net.router
import str

mut schema := graphql.NewSchema()

func me(slot: i64):
    ctx := graphql.Context(slot)
    if value.ObjectHas(ctx, "user"):
        graphql.ResolveStr(slot, value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(ctx, "user")))
        ret
    end
    graphql.ResolveNull(slot)
end

func echo(slot: i64):
    graphql.ResolveStr(slot, graphql.ArgStr(slot, "text"))
end

func endpoint(ctx: i64):
    mut request_ctx := value.NewValueObject()
    auth := http.Header(ctx, "Authorization")
    if str.StartsWith(auth, "Bearer "):
        value.ObjectSet(request_ctx, "user", value.ValueString(str.TrimPrefix(auth, "Bearer ")))
    end
    res := graphql.HandleHttp(schema, http.Method(ctx), http.Header(ctx, "Content-Type"), http.Body(ctx), http.RawQuery(ctx), value.ValueNull(), request_ctx)
    http.SetStatus(ctx, res.status)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Content-Type", res.contentType)
    http.Text(ctx, res.body)
end

func main:
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    graphql.ParseSchemaInto(schema, "type Query { me: String echo(text: String!): String! }", err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(schema, "Query", "me", me)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(schema, "Query", "echo", echo)
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/graphql", endpoint)
    router.Get(r, "/graphql", endpoint)
    mut s := http.NewServer(8090)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println "GraphQL on http://127.0.0.1:8090/graphql"
    http.Run(s)
end
```

Run the program, then query it from another terminal:

```salam
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/graphql -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ me echo(text: \"salam\") }"}'
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/graphql -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sara' -d '{"query":"{ me }"}'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/graphql?query=%7B%20me%20%7D'
```

```salam
{"data": {"me": null, "echo": "salam"}}
{"data": {"me": "sara"}}
{"data": {"me": null}}
```

A real service checks the token, for example with jwt, before trusting the name in it. `GET` only runs queries; mutations must come by `POST`, so a link or an image tag cannot change data.

## Types

### `GqlHttpRequest`

```salam
struct GqlHttpRequest
```

A GraphQL request over HTTP.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `str = ""` | The query text. |
| `operationName` | `str = ""` | The operation name. |
| `variables` | `value.Value` | The variables. |
| `extensions` | `value.Value` | The extensions. |
| `ok` | `bool = true` | It was read correctly. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | If not, the reason. |

graphql-Http.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value
import net.http
import net.router

mut schema := graphql.NewSchema()

func me(slot: i64):
    ctx := graphql.Context(slot)
    mut name := "guest"
    if value.ObjectHas(ctx, "user"):
        name = value.AsString(value.ObjectGet(ctx, "user"))
    end
    graphql.ResolveStr(slot, name + " (" + graphql.ParentTypeName(slot) + "." + graphql.FieldName(slot) + ")")
end

func add(slot: i64):
    graphql.ResolveInt(slot, graphql.ArgInt(slot, "a") + graphql.ArgInt(slot, "b"))
end

func endpoint(ctx: i64):
    res := graphql.HandleHttpSimple(schema, http.Method(ctx), http.Header(ctx, "Content-Type"), http.Body(ctx), http.RawQuery(ctx))
    http.SetStatus(ctx, res.status)
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Content-Type", res.contentType)
    http.Text(ctx, res.body)
end

func main:
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    graphql.ParseSchemaInto(schema, "type Query { me: String! add(a: Int!, b: Int!): Int! }", err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(schema, "Query", "me", me)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(schema, "Query", "add", add)

    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/graphql", endpoint)
    router.Get(r, "/graphql", endpoint)
    mut srv := http.NewServer(19640)
    http.Use(srv, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(srv)

    mut vars := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(vars, "x", value.ValueInt(40))
    body := graphql.BuildRequestBody("query Sum($x: Int!) { add(a: $x, b: 2) }", "Sum", vars)
    println body
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/json")
    resp := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19640/graphql", body, headers)
    println http.Status(resp), http.Body(resp)
    mut cr := graphql.ParseResponse(http.Body(resp))
    println graphql.ResponseOk(cr), cr.hasData, value.AsInt(graphql.ResponseField(cr, "add"))
    graphql.FreeClientResponse(cr)

    qs := graphql.BuildRequestQueryString("{ me }", "", value.ValueNull())
    resp2 := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:19640/graphql?" + qs)
    println http.Body(resp2)
    resp3 := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19640/graphql", graphql.BuildQueryBody("{ nope }"), headers)
    mut cr3 := graphql.ParseResponse(http.Body(resp3))
    println http.Status(resp3), graphql.ResponseOk(cr3), graphql.ResponseErrorMessage(cr3)
    graphql.FreeClientResponse(cr3)

    mut req := graphql.ParseHttpRequestJSON(`{"query":"{ me }"}`)
    mut context := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(context, "user", value.ValueString("Maryam"))
    mut res := graphql.HandleRequest(schema, req, value.ValueNull(), context)
    println graphql.ResultToJSON(res)
    graphql.FreeResult(res)
    graphql.FreeHttpRequest(req)
    bad := graphql.ParseHttpRequest("PUT", "application/json", "{}", "")
    println bad.ok, bad.error
    resp4 := graphql.HandleHttp(schema, "POST", "application/json", "not json", "", value.ValueNull(), value.ValueNull())
    println resp4.status
end
```

Output:

```text
{"operationName": "Sum", "variables": {"x": 40}, "query": "query Sum($x: Int!) { add(a: $x, b: 2) }"}
200 {"data": {"add": 42}}
true true 42
{"data": {"me": "guest (Query.me)"}}
400 false cannot query field "nope" on type "Query" (line 1, column 3)
{"data": {"me": "Maryam (Query.me)"}}
false only GET and POST are supported
400
```

### `GqlError`

```salam
struct GqlError
```

One error.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `int` | The category. |
| `message` | `str = ""` | The message. |
| `line` | `int = 0` | The line. |
| `col` | `int = 0` | The column. |
| `hasLocation` | `bool = false` | It has a location. |
| `pathKeys` | `Vector` | The keys of the path in the response. |
| `pathIndex` | `Vector` | The indexes of the path; -1 for a key. |
| `code` | `str = ""` | An optional code in extensions. |

graphql-Document.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value

func main:
    source := `query Books($limit: Int = 5) { books(limit: $limit, tags: ["a", "b"]) @include(if: true) { ...Info alias: title } }
fragment Info on Book { id year }`
    println graphql.ParseOk(source), graphql.ParseOk("{ a "), graphql.LexOk("{ a }")
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    mut doc := graphql.Parse(source, err)
    println doc.ops.len(), doc.frags.len()
    print graphql.Print(doc)
    i := graphql.FindOperation(doc, "Books")
    op := doc.ops.get(i)
    println op.name, graphql.OperationTypeName(op.optype), op.shorthand, op.varDefs.len(), op.line
    sel := graphql.SelectionAt(doc, op.selections.get(0))
    println sel.kind == graphql.SEL_FIELD, sel.name, graphql.ResponseKey(sel), sel.args.len(), sel.directives.len(), sel.selections.len(), sel.line, sel.col
    arg := sel.args.get(1)
    println arg.name, graphql.PrintValue(doc, arg.value), graphql.ValueAt(doc, arg.value).kind == graphql.VAL_LIST
    vdef := op.varDefs.get(0)
    println vdef.name, graphql.PrintTypeRef(doc, vdef.typeRef), graphql.TypeRefName(doc, vdef.typeRef)
    println graphql.TypeRefIsNonNull(doc, vdef.typeRef), graphql.TypeRefIsList(doc, vdef.typeRef), graphql.TypeRefAt(doc, vdef.typeRef).name
    frag := doc.frags.get(graphql.FindFragment(doc, "Info"))
    println frag.name, frag.typeCondition, frag.selections.len()
    println graphql.PrintStringValue("hello \"world\"")
    graphql.FreeDocument(doc)

    mut ok := false
    stream := graphql.Tokenize(`{ a(x: 1.5, y: "s") }`, ok)
    println ok, stream.toks.len()
    tok := stream.toks.get(5)
    println graphql.TokenKindName(tok.kind), tok.lexeme, tok.fval, tok.line, tok.col
    println graphql.IsStringToken(graphql.TOK_STRING), graphql.TokenKindName(graphql.TOK_LBRACE)

    _ := graphql.Parse("{ a(", err)
    println err.category == graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, err.line, err.col, err.hasLocation
    println graphql.ErrorString(err)

    mut e := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_EXECUTION, "failed")
    graphql.PathPushKey(e, "books")
    graphql.PathPushIndex(e, 2)
    graphql.PathPushKey(e, "title")
    println graphql.PathLen(e), graphql.PathString(e)
    mut errs := graphql.GqlErrorList {}
    graphql.AddError(errs, e)
    graphql.AddError(errs, graphql.NewErrorAt(graphql.ERR_VALIDATION, "bad", 3, 7))
    graphql.AddError(errs, graphql.SyntaxError("unclosed parenthesis", 1, 4))
    println graphql.HasErrors(errs), graphql.ErrorCount(errs), graphql.ErrorAt(errs, 1).line
    println value.ArrayLen(graphql.ErrorsToValue(errs)), value.IsObject(graphql.ErrorToValue(e))
    graphql.FreeError(err)
    graphql.FreeErrorList(errs)
    println graphql.ERR_REQUEST, graphql.SpecEdition

    mut s := graphql.ParseSchema("type Query { n(x: Int!): Int e: Color } enum Color { RED }", err)
    println graphql.ValidateSource(s, "{ n(x: \"a\") }").items.len() > 0
    mut doc2 := graphql.Parse("{ n(x: 1) e }", err)
    println graphql.ValidateOk(s, doc2), graphql.Validate(s, doc2).items.len()
    c := graphql.CoerceLeafResult(s, "Color", value.ValueString("RED"))
    println c.ok, value.AsString(c.value)
    c2 := graphql.CoerceLeafResult(s, "Int", value.ValueString("x"))
    println c2.ok, c2.message.len() > 0
    graphql.FreeDocument(doc2)
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
end
```
