### `FieldGroup`

```salam
struct FieldGroup
```

The group of selections for one response key.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The key. |
| `sels` | `Vector` | The selections. |

graphql-Execute.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value

func book(id: str, title: str, year: i64): value.Value:
    mut b := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(b, "id", value.ValueString(id))
    value.ObjectSet(b, "title", value.ValueString(title))
    value.ObjectSet(b, "year", value.ValueInt(year))
    ret b
end

func hello(slot: i64):
    graphql.ResolveStr(slot, "Hello " + graphql.ArgStr(slot, "name"))
end

func books(slot: i64):
    mut list := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(list, book("1", "The Blind Owl", 1936))
    value.ArrayPush(list, book("2", "Savushun", 1969))
    graphql.Resolve(slot, list)
end

func one_book(slot: i64):
    if graphql.ArgInt(slot, "id") == 2:
        graphql.Resolve(slot, book("2", "Savushun", 1969))
    else:
        graphql.ResolveNull(slot)
    end
end

func age(slot: i64):
    year := value.AsInt(graphql.ParentField(slot, "year"))
    graphql.ResolveInt(slot, 2026 - year)
end

func score(slot: i64):
    graphql.ResolveFloat(slot, graphql.ArgFloat(slot, "base") * 2.0)
end

func in_stock(slot: i64):
    graphql.ResolveBool(slot, graphql.ArgBool(slot, "only") or graphql.HasArg(slot, "x"))
end

func broken(slot: i64):
    graphql.Fail(slot, "service unavailable")
end

func main:
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    mut s := graphql.ParseSchema(`
type Query {
  hello(name: String = "world"): String!
  books: [Book!]!
  book(id: Int!): Book
  score(base: Float!): Float!
  inStock(only: Boolean!): Boolean!
  broken: String
}
type Book {
  id: ID!
  title: String!
  year: Int!
  age: Int!
}`, err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "hello", hello)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "books", books)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "book", one_book)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "score", score)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "inStock", in_stock)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "broken", broken)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Book", "age", age)
    println graphql.HasResolver(s, "Book", "age"), graphql.HasResolver(s, "Book", "title")

    mut r := graphql.Run(s, `{ hello books { title year age } }`)
    println graphql.ResultOk(r)
    println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r)
    graphql.FreeResult(r)

    mut vars := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(vars, "id", value.ValueInt(2))
    mut r2 := graphql.ExecuteSource(s, `query One($id: Int!) { book(id: $id) { title } missing: book(id: 9) { title } score(base: 1.5) inStock(only: true) hello(name: "Maryam") }`, "One", vars, value.ValueNull(), value.ValueNull())
    println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r2)
    graphql.FreeResult(r2)

    mut r3 := graphql.Run(s, `{ broken hello }`)
    println graphql.ResultOk(r3), graphql.ResultErrorMessage(r3)
    println graphql.ResultToJSONStable(r3)
    graphql.FreeResult(r3)

    mut r4 := graphql.Run(s, `{ nope }`)
    println graphql.ResultErrorMessage(r4)
    graphql.FreeResult(r4)
    graphql.ResetSlots()
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
end
```

Output:

```text
true false
true
{"data": {"books": [{"age": 90, "title": "The Blind Owl", "year": 1936}, {"age": 57, "title": "Savushun", "year": 1969}], "hello": "Hello world"}}
{"data": {"book": {"title": "Savushun"}, "hello": "Hello Maryam", "inStock": true, "missing": null, "score": 3}}
false service unavailable (line 1, column 3) at broken
{"data": {"broken": null, "hello": "Hello world"}, "errors": [{"locations": [{"column": 3, "line": 1}], "message": "service unavailable", "path": ["broken"]}]}
cannot query field "nope" on type "Query" (line 1, column 3)
```

### `FieldGroups`

struct FieldGroups
```

The groups.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Vector` | The groups. |

graphql-Internals.salam

```salam
import graphql
import encoding.value
import encoding.json

func names(slot: i64):
    graphql.ResolveStr(slot, json.EncodeDefault(graphql.Args(slot)))
end

func main:
    mut ok := false
    stream := graphql.Tokenize(`query Q($v: [Int!]! = [1]) @x { ...F a: b(c: 2.5, d: """text""") | & ? }`, ok)
    mut kinds := ""
    each t in stream.toks:
        if kinds.len() > 0:
            kinds += " "
        end
        kinds += graphql.TokenKindName(t.kind)
    end
    println ok, kinds
    println graphql.TOK_EOF, graphql.TOK_NAME, graphql.TOK_INT, graphql.TOK_FLOAT, graphql.TOK_BLOCK_STRING, graphql.TOK_BANG, graphql.TOK_DOLLAR
    println graphql.TOK_AMP, graphql.TOK_LPAREN, graphql.TOK_RPAREN, graphql.TOK_SPREAD, graphql.TOK_COLON, graphql.TOK_EQUALS, graphql.TOK_AT
    println graphql.TOK_LBRACKET, graphql.TOK_RBRACKET, graphql.TOK_RBRACE, graphql.TOK_PIPE, graphql.TOK_ERROR

    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    mut s := graphql.ParseSchema(`
type Query { names(a: Boolean, b: Float, o: In, v: Int): String! book: Book }
input In { x: Int! }
type Book { id: ID! title: String! }`, err)
    _ := graphql.SetResolver(s, "Query", "names", names)

    mut doc := graphql.Parse(`query ($v: Int, $l: [Int!]) { names(a: true, b: 1.5, o: { x: 3 }, v: $v) book { id ...F ... on Book { title } } }
fragment F on Book { title }`, err)
    op := doc.ops.get(0)
    println op.optype == graphql.OP_QUERY
    sel := graphql.SelectionAt(doc, op.selections.get(0))
    mut vars := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(vars, "v", value.ValueInt(42))
    each a in sel.args:
        v := graphql.ValueAt(doc, a.value)
        lit := graphql.LiteralToValue(s, doc, a.value, vars)
        println a.name, v.kind == graphql.VAL_BOOL, v.kind == graphql.VAL_FLOAT, v.kind == graphql.VAL_OBJECT, v.kind == graphql.VAL_VARIABLE, lit.ok, json.EncodeDefault(lit.value)
    end

    lref := op.varDefs.get(1).typeRef
    elem := graphql.TypeRefElement(doc, lref)
    println graphql.PrintTypeRef(doc, lref), graphql.PrintTypeRef(doc, elem), graphql.TypeRefAt(doc, elem).kind == graphql.TREF_NAMED
    mut list := value.NewValueArray()
    value.ArrayPush(list, value.ValueInt(1))
    value.ArrayPush(list, value.ValueString("two"))
    c := graphql.CoerceInput(s, doc, lref, list)
    println c.ok, c.message.len() > 0

    bk := graphql.SelectionAt(doc, op.selections.get(1))
    println graphql.SelectionAt(doc, bk.selections.get(1)).kind == graphql.SEL_FRAGMENT_SPREAD, graphql.SelectionAt(doc, bk.selections.get(2)).kind == graphql.SEL_INLINE_FRAGMENT
    mut groups := graphql.CollectFields(s, doc, bk.selections, "Book", vars)
    each g in groups.items:
        println g.key, g.sels.len(), graphql.MergeSelections(doc, g).len()
    end
    graphql.FreeFieldGroups(groups)

    mut r := graphql.Execute(s, doc, "", vars, value.ValueNull(), value.ValueNull())
    mut ext := value.NewValueObject()
    value.ObjectSet(ext, "ms", value.ValueInt(3))
    graphql.SetExtensions(r, ext)
    println value.IsObject(graphql.ResultToValue(r))
    println graphql.ResultToJSONIndent(r)
    graphql.FreeResult(r)
    graphql.FreeDocument(doc)
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
    graphql.FreeError(err)
end
```

Output:

graphql-Schema.salam

```salam
import graphql

func main:
    mut s := graphql.NewSchema()
    graphql.AddScalarType(s, "Date", "A date as YYYY-MM-DD")
    graphql.AddInterfaceType(s, "Node", "")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Node", "id", "ID!")
    graphql.AddObjectType(s, "Author", "An author")
    graphql.AddInterfaceTo(s, "Author", "Node")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Author", "id", "ID!")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Author", "name", "String!")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Author", "born", "Date")
    mut genres := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    genres.push("NOVEL")
    genres.push("POETRY")
    graphql.AddEnumType(s, "Genre", genres)
    mut members := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    members.push("Author")
    graphql.AddUnionType(s, "SearchResult", members)
    graphql.AddInputObjectType(s, "AuthorInput", "")
    _ := graphql.AddInputField(s, "AuthorInput", "name", "String!")
    graphql.AddObjectType(s, "Query", "")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Query", "authors", "[Author!]!")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Query", "search", "[SearchResult!]!")
    _ := graphql.AddFieldArg(s, "Query", "search", "text", "String!")
    _ := graphql.AddFieldArg(s, "Query", "search", "genre", "Genre")
    graphql.AddObjectType(s, "Mutation", "")
    _ := graphql.AddField(s, "Mutation", "addAuthor", "Author!")
    _ := graphql.AddFieldArg(s, "Mutation", "addAuthor", "input", "AuthorInput!")
    graphql.SetRootTypes(s, "Query", "Mutation", "")
    print graphql.PrintSchema(s)
    println "---"
    println graphql.PrintType(s, "Genre")

    println graphql.HasType(s, "Author"), graphql.TypeIndex(s, "Author") >= 0, graphql.TypeCount(s) > 5
    t := graphql.FindType(s, "Author")
    println t.name, t.kind == graphql.TYPE_OBJECT, t.description, graphql.HasField(t, "born")
    f := graphql.FindField(graphql.FindType(s, "Query"), "search")
    println f.name, graphql.FindArg(f, "genre").name, graphql.FindArg(f, "genre").hasDefault
    println graphql.FindInputField(graphql.FindType(s, "AuthorInput"), "name").name
    println graphql.HasEnumValue(graphql.FindType(s, "Genre"), "POETRY")
    println graphql.IsInputType(s, "AuthorInput"), graphql.IsOutputType(s, "AuthorInput"), graphql.IsLeafType(s, "Genre")
    println graphql.IsAbstractType(s, "SearchResult"), graphql.IsPossibleType(s, "Node", "Author"), graphql.PossibleTypes(s, "Node").len()
    println graphql.RootTypeName(s, graphql.OP_MUTATION), graphql.RootTypeName(s, graphql.OP_SUBSCRIPTION).len()
    println graphql.FindDirectiveDef(s, "deprecated").name
    println graphql.TypeAt(s, 0).name.len() > 0
    println graphql.IsIntrospectionType("__Schema"), graphql.IsIntrospectionType("Author")
    graphql.AddIntrospectionTypes(s)
    println graphql.HasType(s, "__Type"), graphql.PrintSchemaFull(s).len() > graphql.PrintSchema(s).len()
    println graphql.TypeRefText(s, "[Int!]") >= 0

    println graphql.ParseSchemaOk("type Query { a: Int }"), graphql.ParseSchemaOk("type {")
    mut err := graphql.NewError(graphql.ERR_SYNTAX, "")
    graphql.ParseSchemaInto(s, "extend type Author { alias: String }", err)
    println graphql.HasField(graphql.FindType(s, "Author"), "alias"), err.message.len()
    println graphql.TYPE_SCALAR, graphql.TYPE_INTERFACE, graphql.TYPE_UNION, graphql.TYPE_ENUM, graphql.TYPE_INPUT_OBJECT
    graphql.FreeSchema(s)
end
```

scalar Date

interface Node {
  id: ID!
}

"An author"
type Author implements Node {
  id: ID!
  name: String!
  born: Date
}

enum Genre {
  NOVEL
  POETRY
}

union SearchResult = Author

input AuthorInput {
  name: String!
}

type Query {
  authors: [Author!]!
  search(text: String!, genre: Genre): [SearchResult!]!
}

type Mutation {
  addAuthor(input: AuthorInput!): Author!
}
---
enum Genre {
  NOVEL
  POETRY
}

# google

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/google/

Google service account authentication for the Google APIs.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add google`

Server programs reach the Google APIs through a "service account". Get the account JSON file from the Google console, read it with `ParseServiceAccount`, and get a token for the scope you need with `AccessToken`; then send it in your net/http requests with `Authorization`. Keep the service account file as carefully as a password.

The package does one job: it signs a JWT with the account's RSA key (RS256), trades it at Google's token endpoint for an OAuth access token, and keeps that token for reuse. The calls to the APIs themselves are ordinary HTTP requests that you write. For Web Push to browsers without Firebase, see webpush.

Things that catch people out:

- Only service account keys are supported. A user's own Google login (the OAuth consent screen) and the metadata server that Google Cloud machines offer are not.

- When `AccessToken` fails, `ok` is false and there is no message. Check in this order: the account's `ok`, the clock of the machine (a clock that is minutes off makes Google reject the signature), the network, and whether the API is enabled for the project.

- A token is kept for 59 minutes per account and scope, shared by all threads. After you change the account's roles, call `Forget` so the next call fetches a fresh one.

## Loading the service account safely

Download the JSON key from the Google Cloud console (IAM, Service accounts, Keys) and keep it outside the source tree; the usual place to point at it is the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` environment variable, read with env.`GetOr`. `ParseServiceAccount` never fails loudly: it returns an account whose `ok` is false when the text is empty or `client_email` or `private_key` is missing. Check it once at start up and stop with a clear message, so a bad deployment fails at once instead of at the first push notification.

google-guide-load.salam

```salam
import google
import io

func load(path: str): google.ServiceAccount:
    text := io.ReadFile(path)
    if text == "":
        println "cannot read", path
        ret google.ServiceAccount {}
    end
    account := google.ParseServiceAccount(text)
    if not account.ok:
        println path, "is not a service account file: client_email or private_key is missing"
    end
    ret account
end

func main:
    io.WriteFile("good.json", `{"type":"service_account","project_id":"shop-prod","client_email":"push@shop-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com","private_key":"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"}`)
    io.WriteFile("broken.json", `{"type":"service_account","project_id":"shop-prod"}`)
    each p in ["good.json", "broken.json", "missing.json"]:
        account := load(p)
        if account.ok:
            println "project", account.project_id, "as", account.client_email
            println "key loaded:", account.private_key.len() > 0
        end
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
project shop-prod as push@shop-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
key loaded: true
broken.json is not a service account file: client_email or private_key is missing
cannot read missing.json
```

The program prints the project and the account email, which are safe to log, but only whether the key was loaded. Never print or log `private_key`, and never commit the file: anyone who has it can act as your service.

## Sending a push notification with Firebase

Firebase Cloud Messaging takes one HTTP request per message. Get a token for `SCOPE_FCM`, put it in the `Authorization` header, and post the message to `/v1/projects/PROJECT/messages:send`. `AccessToken` keeps the token and reuses it until shortly before it expires, so calling it before every message costs nothing after the first time.

google-guide-fcm.salam

```salam
import google
import io
import net.http

func send_push(account: google.ServiceAccount, device_token: str, title: str, body: str): bool:
    mut ok := false
    token := google.AccessToken(account, google.SCOPE_FCM, ok)
    if not ok:
        println "no access token"
        ret false
    end
    url := "https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/" + account.project_id + "/messages:send"
    message := ```
        {"message": {"token": "${{ device_token }}", "notification": {"title": "${{ title }}", "body": "${{ body }}"}}}
        ```
mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
headers.insert("Authorization", google.Authorization(token))
headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/json")
r := http.PostWith(url, message, headers)
if http.Status(r) != 200:
println "FCM answered", http.Status(r), http.Body(r)
ret false
end
println "sent:", http.Body(r)
ret true
end

func main:
account := google.ParseServiceAccount(io.ReadFile("service-account.json"))
if not account.ok:
println "service-account.json is missing or invalid"
ret 1
end
send_push(account, "DEVICE_REGISTRATION_TOKEN", "Order shipped", "Your parcel is on its way")
send_push(account, "DEVICE_REGISTRATION_TOKEN", "Delivered", "Your parcel has arrived")
ret 0
end
```




This needs a real service account with the Firebase Cloud Messaging API enabled and a device registration token from your app, so it is only compiled here. Save the key as `service-account.json` and replace `DEVICE_REGISTRATION_TOKEN`. On success the body holds the message name, `{"name": "projects/.../messages/..."}`; an error whose body says `UNREGISTERED` means the app was removed from the device and you should delete that token. The title and body are put into the JSON as they are; if they can contain quotes, build the message with encoding/json instead.




## Uploading a file to Cloud Storage


A simple upload is one `POST` of the file's bytes to the upload endpoint, with the object name in the query string and the content type in a header. The token comes from `SCOPE_STORAGE`. Object names may contain `/`, so encode the name with encoding/url before it goes into the URL.



google-guide-storage.salam


```salam
import google
import io
import net.http
import encoding.url

func upload(account: google.ServiceAccount, bucket: str, name: str, content: str, kind: str): bool:
    mut ok := false
    token := google.AccessToken(account, google.SCOPE_STORAGE, ok)
    if not ok:
        ret false
    end
    target := "https://storage.googleapis.com/upload/storage/v1/b/" + bucket + "/o?uploadType=media&name=" + url.EncodePathSegment(name)
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Authorization", google.Authorization(token))
    headers.insert("Content-Type", kind)
    r := http.PostWith(target, content, headers)
    println name, "->", http.Status(r)
    ret http.Status(r) == 200
end

func main:
    account := google.ParseServiceAccount(io.ReadFile("service-account.json"))
    if not account.ok:
        println "service-account.json is missing or invalid"
        ret 1
    end
    upload(account, "my-bucket", "reports/2026-10.csv", "day,sales\n1,120\n2,95\n", "text/csv")
    upload(account, "my-bucket", "notes/hello.txt", "salam", "text/plain")
    google.Forget(account)
    ret 0
end
```

Replace `my-bucket` with a bucket the service account can write to (the Storage Object Creator role is enough). A status of 200 means the object was stored; 403 means the account lacks permission on that bucket. `Forget` drops the kept token, which is useful after you rotate the key or change the account's roles.

| Service | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Firebase Cloud Messaging | `SCOPE_FCM` |
| Cloud Storage | `SCOPE_STORAGE` |
| Most other Google Cloud APIs | `SCOPE_CLOUD`, or the API's own scope string |

## Types

```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

import google

func main:

    account := google.ParseServiceAccount(document)
    println account.ok, account.project_id, account.client_email
    println account.token_uri
    println account.private_key.len() > 0
    println google.ParseServiceAccount(`{"project_id":"x"}`).ok
    println google.Authorization("ya29.abc")

    println google.SCOPE_STORAGE
    println google.SCOPE_CLOUD
end
```

Output:

true

## Functions

### `ParseServiceAccount`

```salam
func ParseServiceAccount(document: str): ServiceAccount
```

Reads the text of a service account JSON file. It never fails loudly: when `client_email` or `private_key` is missing, the result has `ok` false. `token_uri` keeps its default when the file has none.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: google-Account.salam

### `AccessToken`

```salam
func AccessToken(sa: ServiceAccount, scope: str, ok &: bool): str
```

Gets an OAuth access token for the given scope. Several scopes can be passed separated by spaces. The token is kept per account and scope and reused for 59 minutes, so call it before every request. On failure it returns an empty string, sets `ok` to false and gives no reason.

google-Token.salam

```salam
import google
import io
import net.http

func main:
    account := google.ParseServiceAccount(io.ReadFile("service-account.json"))
    if not account.ok:
        println "the service account file is not valid"
        ret
    end
    mut good := false
    token := google.AccessToken(account, google.SCOPE_STORAGE, good)
    if not good:
        println "the token was not granted"
        ret
    end
    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert("Authorization", google.Authorization(token))
    r := http.GetWith("https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b?project=" + account.project_id, headers)
    println http.Status(r)
    google.Forget(account)
end
```

### `Forget`

# telegram/bot

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/telegram-bot/

Building a bot with the Bot API: messages, buttons, webhooks and a polling loop.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add telegram.bot`

To build a bot, get a token from BotFather and make one with `NewBot`. A bot has two ways of taking messages: `Poll`, which asks Telegram itself and suits testing and simple servers, or a webhook, where Telegram POSTs the messages to your server.

With a webhook you can send the answer straight in the body of the HTTP response; the `Reply...` functions build that JSON text. Set a secret with `SetWebhookSecret` and check its header on every request.

Things that catch people out:

- Every API call is an HTTP `GET` with the parameters in the URL. Media therefore go by `file_id` or by a public URL that Telegram downloads; a file on your disk cannot be uploaded with this package. The URL also contains the token, so do not log request URLs.

- `Poll` never returns, and it runs your function for one update at a time. A slow handler delays every chat. When `getUpdates` fails it writes the reason to standard error and tries again a second later.

- An answer sent in the webhook response is fire and forget: you do not learn whether it worked or get the new message id. When you need either, call the matching `Send...` function instead.

## Answering commands

Keep the logic of a bot in a function that takes an `Update` and returns the answer. Then the same function serves a webhook, which sends the answer back in the HTTP response, and a test like this one, which feeds it updates written by hand and needs no network and no token. `IsCommand`, `CommandName` and `CommandArgs` split `/add 2 3` into its parts, and `CommandName` drops the `@my_bot` suffix Telegram adds in groups.

telegram-bot-guide-router.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot
import str

func answer(update: bot.Update): str:
    if not update.has_message:
        ret ""
    end
    m := update.message
    if not bot.IsCommand(m.text):
        ret bot.ReplyMessage(m.chat.id, "You said: " + m.text)
    end
    switch bot.CommandName(m.text):
        "start":
            ret bot.ReplyMessage(m.chat.id, "Hello " + m.from_user.first_name + "! Try /add 2 3")
        end
        "add":
            parts := str.Split(bot.CommandArgs(m.text), " ")
            if parts.len() != 2:
                ret bot.ReplyMessage(m.chat.id, "usage: /add A B")
            end
            sum := str.ToInt(parts.get(0)) + str.ToInt(parts.get(1))
            ret bot.ReplyMessage(m.chat.id, str.FromInt(sum))
        end
    end
    ret bot.ReplyMessage(m.chat.id, "I do not know that command")
end

func main:
    inbox := [`{"update_id":1,"message":{"message_id":1,"text":"/start","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"},"from":{"id":42,"first_name":"Sara"}}}`,
        `{"update_id":2,"message":{"message_id":2,"text":"/add 2 3","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}`,
        `{"update_id":3,"message":{"message_id":3,"text":"/add 2","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}`,
        `{"update_id":4,"message":{"message_id":4,"text":"/weather@my_bot","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}`,
        `{"update_id":5,"message":{"message_id":5,"text":"good morning","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}`]
    each raw in inbox:
        println answer(bot.ParseUpdate(raw))
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
{"method": "sendMessage", "chat_id": 42, "text": "Hello Sara! Try /add 2 3"}
{"method": "sendMessage", "chat_id": 42, "text": "5"}
{"method": "sendMessage", "chat_id": 42, "text": "usage: /add A B"}
{"method": "sendMessage", "chat_id": 42, "text": "I do not know that command"}
{"method": "sendMessage", "chat_id": 42, "text": "You said: good morning"}
```

The `switch` has no `else`, so a command it does not list falls out of it to the line after, which answers that the command is unknown. Always give some answer: a bot that stays silent looks broken to the user.

## Inline buttons

An inline keyboard is a list of rows, and each row a list of buttons. `InlineButton` carries a `callback_data` string of up to 64 bytes that comes back when the user taps it; `InlineButtonURL` opens a link instead. A tap arrives as an update with `has_callback_query` set. Answer it with `ReplyAnswerCallbackQuery`, or the button keeps showing a spinner, and usually edit the original message so the chat shows what was chosen.

telegram-bot-guide-menu.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot

func menu(): str:
    mut first := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    first.push(bot.InlineButton("Tea", "order:tea"))
    first.push(bot.InlineButton("Coffee", "order:coffee"))
    mut second := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    second.push(bot.InlineButtonURL("Opening hours", "https://example.com/hours"))
    mut rows := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    rows.push(bot.Row(first))
    rows.push(bot.Row(second))
    ret bot.InlineKeyboardMarkup(rows)
end

func main:
    mut opts := bot.SendOptions {}
    opts.reply_markup = menu()
    println bot.ReplyMessageOptions(42, "What would you like?", opts)

    click := bot.ParseUpdate(`{"update_id":7,"callback_query":{"id":"cq7","data":"order:tea","from":{"id":42,"first_name":"Sara"},"message":{"message_id":31,"chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}}`)
    if click.has_callback_query:
        q := click.callback_query
        println bot.ReplyAnswerCallbackQuery(q.id, "Got it", false)
        if q.has_message:
            println bot.ReplyEditMessageText(q.message.chat.id, q.message.message_id, "One tea for " + q.from_user.first_name, "")
        end
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
{"method": "sendMessage", "chat_id": 42, "text": "What would you like?", "reply_markup": {"inline_keyboard": [[{"text": "Tea", "callback_data": "order:tea"}, {"text": "Coffee", "callback_data": "order:coffee"}], [{"text": "Opening hours", "url": "https://example.com/hours"}]]}}
{"method": "answerCallbackQuery", "callback_query_id": "cq7", "text": "Got it"}
{"method": "editMessageText", "chat_id": 42, "message_id": 31, "text": "One tea for Sara"}
```

Give `callback_data` a small format of your own, such as `order:tea`, and split it with `str` when it arrives. Never trust it: anyone can send any data to your bot, so check that the order exists before acting on it.

## A bot that runs with long polling

Polling needs no public address, so it is the easiest way to run a bot from your own computer. `Poll` asks Telegram for new updates, waits up to the given number of seconds when there are none, calls your function for each one and remembers the offset, so every update is handled once. A bot can use either polling or a webhook, not both, which is why the program removes any webhook first. `SetMyCommands` fills the command menu Telegram shows next to the text box.

telegram-bot-guide-poll.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot
import env

func main:
    token := env.Get("TELEGRAM_TOKEN")
    if token.len() == 0:
        println "set TELEGRAM_TOKEN to the token BotFather gave you"
        ret 1
    end
    robot := bot.NewBot(token)
    me := bot.GetMe(robot)
    if not bot.Ok(me):
        println "the token was refused:", me.error_code, me.description, me.http_err
        ret 1
    end
    _ := bot.DeleteWebhook(robot)
    mut commands := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    commands.push(bot.BotCommand("start", "say hello"))
    commands.push(bot.BotCommand("echo", "repeat your text"))
    _ := bot.SetMyCommands(robot, commands)
    println "polling, press Ctrl+C to stop"
    bot.Poll(robot, 30, (update: bot.Update):
        if not update.has_message:
            ret
        end
        m := update.message
        _ := bot.SendChatAction(robot, m.chat.id, "typing")
        if bot.CommandName(m.text) == "echo":
            _ := bot.SendMessage(robot, m.chat.id, bot.CommandArgs(m.text))
        else:
            _ := bot.SendMessage(robot, m.chat.id, "Hello " + m.from_user.first_name + ", send /echo something")
        end
    end)
end
```

Run it with the token from BotFather in the environment:

```salam
TELEGRAM_TOKEN=123456:ABC... salam run telegram-bot-guide-poll.salam
```

Every `Send...` call returns an `ApiResponse`. Check it with `Ok`: when it fails, `error_code` and `description` hold Telegram's reason (429 means you are sending too fast) and `http_err` is set when Telegram could not be reached at all.

## A webhook server

In production a webhook is the usual choice: Telegram sends each update to your HTTPS address as soon as it arrives, so nothing has to poll. `SetWebhookSecret` registers the address and a secret, and Telegram then puts that secret in the `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` header (the constant `SECRET_HEADER`) of every request. Anything without it did not come from Telegram and gets a 401.

telegram-bot-guide-webhook.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot
import net.http
import net.router
import env

mut secret := ""

func hook(ctx: i64):
    if http.Header(ctx, bot.SECRET_HEADER) != secret:
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 401)
        http.Text(ctx, "")
        ret
    end
    update := bot.ParseUpdate(http.Body(ctx))
    if not update.has_message:
        http.Text(ctx, "")
        ret
    end
    m := update.message
    http.SetHeader(ctx, "Content-Type", "application/json")
    http.Text(ctx, bot.ReplyMessage(m.chat.id, "Got it: " + m.text))
end

func main:
    token := env.Get("TELEGRAM_TOKEN")
    public_url := env.Get("PUBLIC_URL")
    secret = env.Get("WEBHOOK_SECRET")
    if token.len() == 0 or public_url.len() == 0 or secret.len() == 0:
        println "set TELEGRAM_TOKEN, PUBLIC_URL and WEBHOOK_SECRET"
        ret 1
    end
    robot := bot.NewBot(token)
    set := bot.SetWebhookSecret(robot, public_url + "/telegram", secret)
    if not bot.Ok(set):
        println "setWebhook failed:", set.error_code, set.description
        ret 1
    end
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/telegram", hook)
    mut s := http.NewServer(8443)
    http.Use(s, r)
    println "webhook on port 8443"
    http.Run(s)
end
```

The answer goes back in the response body: `ReplyMessage` builds the JSON for a `sendMessage` call, and Telegram runs it. Reply with an empty body when there is nothing to say, and answer quickly, because Telegram waits for the response before it sends the next update for that chat. Telegram only calls HTTPS addresses on ports 443, 80, 88 or 8443, so run the program behind a proxy with a certificate, or behind a tunnel while you develop. `SetWebhookSecret` also drops updates that were waiting, so a restart does not replay old messages.

## Types

### `User`

```salam
struct User
```

One Telegram user.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `i64 = 0` | The id. |
| `is_bot` | `bool = false` | It is a bot. |
| `first_name` | `str = ""` | The first name. |
| `last_name` | `str = ""` | The last name. |
| `username` | `str = ""` | The user name. |
| `language_code` | `str = ""` | The language of the user, such as `fa`. |

telegram-bot-Parse.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot

func main:
    text := `{"update_id":10,"message":{"message_id":5,"date":1700000000,"text":"/start hello","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private","first_name":"Maryam","username":"maryam"},"from":{"id":42,"is_bot":false,"first_name":"Maryam","language_code":"en"},"reply_to_message":{"message_id":4,"from":{"id":7,"first_name":"Ali"}}}}`
    update := bot.ParseUpdate(text)
    println update.update_id, update.has_message, update.has_callback_query
    m := update.message
    println m.message_id, m.date, m.text, m.chat.id, m.chat.chat_type, m.chat.first_name, m.chat.username
    println m.from_user.id, m.from_user.is_bot, m.from_user.language_code, m.reply_to.message_id, m.reply_to.user_id, m.reply_to.user_name
    println bot.IsCommand(m.text), bot.CommandName(m.text), bot.CommandArgs(m.text)
    println bot.IsCommand("hello"), bot.CommandName("/help@my_bot")

    all := bot.ParseUpdates(`{"ok":true,"result":[{"update_id":11,"callback_query":{"id":"cq1","data":"yes","from":{"id":42,"first_name":"Maryam"},"message":{"message_id":9,"chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}},{"update_id":12,"inline_query":{"id":"iq1","query":"book","offset":"","from":{"id":42,"first_name":"Maryam"}}}]}`)
    println all.len()
    q := all[0].callback_query
    println all[0].has_callback_query, q.id, q.data, q.from_user.first_name, q.has_message, q.message.message_id
    typed := all[1].inline_query
    println all[1].has_inline_query, typed.id, typed.query, typed.offset.len()
    println bot.ParseUser(`{"id":1,"first_name":"x","last_name":"y","is_bot":true}`).last_name
    println bot.ParseChat(`{"id":-100,"type":"supergroup","title":"the group"}`).title
    println bot.ParseMessage(`{"message_id":1,"caption":"a photo","chat":{"id":1}}`).caption
    println bot.ParseCallbackQuery(`{"id":"q","data":"d"}`).data, bot.ParseInlineQuery(`{"id":"i","query":"q"}`).query
    println bot.ParseUpdate(`{"update_id":13,"channel_post":{"message_id":1,"text":"news","chat":{"id":-5}}}`).channel_post.text

    mut row1 := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    row1.push(bot.InlineButton("yes", "yes"))
    row1.push(bot.InlineButton("no", "no"))
    mut row2 := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    row2.push(bot.InlineButtonURL("the site", "https://salamlang.ir"))
    mut rows := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    rows.push(bot.Row(row1))
    rows.push(bot.Row(row2))
    println bot.InlineKeyboardMarkup(rows)
    mut plain := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    plain.push(bot.KeyboardButton("menu"))
    mut plain_rows := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    plain_rows.push(bot.Row(plain))
    println bot.ReplyKeyboardMarkup(plain_rows)
    println bot.RemoveKeyboard(), bot.ForceReply()
    println bot.BotCommand("start", "start it")

    robot := bot.NewBot("123:ABC")
    println bot.FileURL(robot, "photos/file_1.jpg")
    println bot.ReplyMessage(42, "hello")
    mut options := bot.SendOptions {}
    options.parse_mode = "HTML"
    options.reply_to_message_id = 5
    options.disable_notification = true
    println bot.ReplyMessageOptions(42, "<b>hello</b>", options)
    println bot.ReplyAnswerCallbackQuery("cq1", "noted", false)
    println bot.ReplyChatAction(42, "typing")
    println bot.ReplyEditMessageText(42, 9, "updated", bot.RemoveKeyboard())
    println bot.SECRET_HEADER
end

telegram-bot-Bot.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot
import env

func handle(update: bot.Update):
    if not update.has_message:
        ret
    end
    println update.message.from_user.first_name, update.message.text
end

func main:
    robot := bot.NewBot(env.Get("TELEGRAM_TOKEN"))
    me := bot.GetMe(robot)
    if not bot.Ok(me):
        println me.error_code, me.description, me.http_status, me.http_err
        ret
    end
    println me.ok, me.result
    chat := 42 as i64
    _ := bot.SendMessage(robot, chat, "hello")
    _ := bot.SendMessage(robot, "@my_channel", "fresh news")
    mut options := bot.SendOptions {}
    options.parse_mode = "Markdown"
    options.reply_markup = bot.RemoveKeyboard()
    _ := bot.SendMessageOptions(robot, chat, "*important*", options)
    _ := bot.SendPhoto(robot, chat, "https://example.com/a.jpg", "a photo")
    _ := bot.SendDocument(robot, chat, "BQACAgQAAx", "")
    _ := bot.SendVideo(robot, chat, "https://example.com/v.mp4", "")
    _ := bot.SendAudio(robot, chat, "https://example.com/a.mp3", "")
    _ := bot.SendVoice(robot, chat, "AwACAgQ", "")
    _ := bot.SendSticker(robot, chat, "CAACAgI")
    _ := bot.SendLocation(robot, chat, 35.6997, 51.338)
    _ := bot.SendContact(robot, chat, "+989120000000", "Ali")
    _ := bot.SendChatAction(robot, chat, "typing")
    _ := bot.EditMessageText(robot, chat, 10, "edited")
    _ := bot.ForwardMessage(robot, chat, 43, 11)
    _ := bot.PinChatMessage(robot, chat, 10)
    _ := bot.UnpinChatMessage(robot, chat, 10)
    _ := bot.DeleteMessage(robot, chat, 10)
    _ := bot.AnswerCallbackQuery(robot, "cq1", "noted")
    _ := bot.AnswerInlineQuery(robot, "iq1", "[]")
    file := bot.GetFile(robot, "AgACAgQ")
    println file.result.len() > 0
    _ := bot.GetChat(robot, chat)
    _ := bot.GetChatMemberCount(robot, chat)
    _ := bot.GetChatMember(robot, chat, 7)
    _ := bot.BanChatMember(robot, chat, 7)
    _ := bot.UnbanChatMember(robot, chat, 7)
    _ := bot.LeaveChat(robot, -100)
    mut commands := Vector {} as Vector<str>
    commands.push(bot.BotCommand("start", "start it"))
    _ := bot.SetMyCommands(robot, commands)
    _ := bot.SetWebhook(robot, "https://example.com/hook")
    _ := bot.SetWebhookSecret(robot, "https://example.com/hook", "my-secret")
    _ := bot.GetWebhookInfo(robot)
    _ := bot.DeleteWebhook(robot)
    mut params := HashMap {} as HashMap<str, str>
    params.insert("chat_id", "42")
    _ := bot.Call(robot, "getChatAdministrators", params)
    updates := bot.GetUpdates(robot, 0, 10, 30)
    println bot.ParseUpdates(updates.result).len(), robot.token.len() > 0
    bot.Poll(robot, 30, (update: bot.Update):
        handle(update)
    end)
end
```

## Constants and variables

### `SECRET_HEADER`

```salam
const SECRET_HEADER: str = "X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token"
```

The name of the header the webhook secret arrives in.

telegram-bot-Webhook.salam

```salam
import telegram.bot
import net.http
import net.router

func webhook(ctx: i64):
    if http.Header(ctx, bot.SECRET_HEADER) != "my-secret":
        http.SetStatus(ctx, 403)
        http.Text(ctx, "forbidden")
        ret
    end
    update := bot.ParseUpdate(http.Body(ctx))
    if update.has_message and bot.IsCommand(update.message.text):
        answer := "the command " + bot.CommandName(update.message.text) + " arrived"
        http.Json(ctx, bot.ReplyMessage(update.message.chat.id, answer))
    else update.has_callback_query:
        http.Json(ctx, bot.ReplyAnswerCallbackQuery(update.callback_query.id, "all right", true))
    else:
        http.Text(ctx, "ok")
    end
end

func main:
    mut r := router.NewRouter()
    router.Post(r, "/hook", webhook)
    mut s := http.NewServer(19632)
    http.Use(s, r)
    _ := http.RunBackground(s)

    mut headers := http.NewHeaders()
    headers.insert(bot.SECRET_HEADER, "my-secret")
    headers.insert("Content-Type", "application/json")
    a := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19632/hook", `{"update_id":1,"message":{"message_id":2,"text":"/start","chat":{"id":42,"type":"private"}}}`, headers)
    println http.Status(a), http.Body(a)
    b := http.PostWith("http://127.0.0.1:19632/hook", `{"update_id":2,"callback_query":{"id":"cq9","data":"x","from":{"id":42}}}`, headers)
    println http.Body(b)
    c := http.Post("http://127.0.0.1:19632/hook", "{}")
    println http.Status(c)
end
```

# node

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/node/

A Salam program under Node.js: modules, files, processes and JavaScript objects.

This package is for Salam programs that are translated to JavaScript with `salam js` and run under Node.js, such as the VS Code extension or a build script that has to live in an npm project. It gives you the whole of Node: `Require` loads any built-in or npm module, the `Get...` and `Set...` functions read and write properties, and the `Call...` functions call methods. A few helpers wrap the common `fs`, `path`, `os` and `child_process` calls.

Use it only when the program really runs under Node. A native Salam program reads files with fs and starts programs with os/process, and code for a browser page uses dom. A native build cannot call these functions, so the examples on this page are type-checked by the site but not run.

### Core ideas

- Handles. Every JavaScript value (object, array, function, promise, even `undefined`) is held in an `i64`. Nothing needs freeing; Node's garbage collector owns them.

- Typed calls. Salam checks argument types, so each call shape has its own function, named after its arguments: `CallS2` passes two strings, `CallV1` one JavaScript value, `CallSFn0` a string and a function. Pick the one that matches the method you call; the result is always a handle.

- Callbacks run later. A Salam lambda passed to `CallFn1`, `ExecFile` or `SetPropFn1` becomes a JavaScript function. Node calls it after `main` has returned, from its event loop.

### Things that trip people up

- `GetStr` on a missing property returns an empty string and `GetNum` returns 0, without any error. When "missing" and "empty" mean different things, test `IsNullish(GetProp(obj, name))` first.

- Every number from JavaScript is an `f64`, and 64-bit integers do not work under `salam js`. Cast to `int` when you need one.

- Salam strings count bytes, also under Node: `"سلام".len()` is 8, while JavaScript's `length` of the same text is 4. Text itself passes through unchanged.

To try a program, translate it and run the result with Node.js 18 or newer:

```salam
salam js node-guide-files.salam --output=files.js
node files.js
```

The output under each program is what it printed that way under Node 24.

## Files and directories

The file helpers wrap the synchronous calls of Node's `fs` and `path` modules, which keeps a script readable from top to bottom. For anything they do not cover, `Require("fs")` gives you the module itself. `readdirSync` returns a JavaScript array: its `length` is a number property and each element is a property named by its index, so `GetStr(names, "0")` reads the first one.

node-guide-files.salam

```salam
import node
import str

func main:
    folder := node.MkdtempSync(node.PathJoin2(node.TmpDir(), "salam-notes-"))
    node.WriteFileSync(node.PathJoin2(folder, "a.txt"), "one\ntwo\nthree\n")
    node.WriteFileSync(node.PathJoin2(folder, "b.txt"), "only line\n")
    node.WriteFileSync(node.PathJoin2(folder, "c.md"), "# title\n")
    fs := node.Require("fs")
    names := node.CallS1(fs, "readdirSync", folder)
    _ := node.Call0(names, "sort")
    mut total := 0
    repeat node.GetNum(names, "length") as int in i:
        name := node.GetStr(names, str.FromInt(i))
        if not str.EndsWith(name, ".txt"):
            continue
        end
        text := node.ReadFileSync(node.PathJoin2(folder, name))
        lines := str.Count(text, "\n")
        total += lines
        println name, lines
    end
    println "total", total
    node.RmSyncRecursiveForce(folder)
end
```

```salam
a.txt 3
b.txt 1
total 4
```

`MkdtempSync` adds random characters to the prefix, so two runs never collide; `RmSyncRecursiveForce` removes the directory and everything in it at the end.

## Reading JSON from JavaScript

`Global("JSON")` is the same `JSON` object a JavaScript program sees, so `parse` turns text into an object handle and the `Get...` functions read its fields. A field that is missing comes back as `undefined`; test it with `IsNullish` before reading it, and fall back to a default.

node-guide-config.salam

```salam
import node

func main:
    text := `{"name": "shop", "port": 8080, "debug": true, "db": {"host": "127.0.0.1"}}`
    config := node.CallS1(node.Global("JSON"), "parse", text)
    println "name:", node.GetStr(config, "name")
    println "port:", node.GetNum(config, "port")
    println "debug:", node.GetBool(config, "debug")
    db := node.GetProp(config, "db")
    println "db host:", node.GetStr(db, "host")
    mut workers := 4.0
    if not node.IsNullish(node.GetProp(config, "workers")):
        workers = node.GetNum(config, "workers")
    end
    println "workers:", workers
    node.SetNum(config, "workers", workers)
    println node.ToStr(node.CallV1(node.Global("JSON"), "stringify", config))
end
```

```salam
name: shop
port: 8080
debug: true
db host: 127.0.0.1
workers: 4
{"name":"shop","port":8080,"debug":true,"db":{"host":"127.0.0.1"},"workers":4}
```

Numbers always arrive as `f64`, because JavaScript has only one number type. Cast with `as int` where you need an integer. Note the `IsNullish` test: `GetNum(config, "workers")` on its own would have returned 0 for the missing field, not an error.

## Writing a Node module in Salam

`Exports` is `module.exports` of the translated file, so the functions you attach to it with `SetPropFn0`, `SetPropFn1` and `SetPropFn1R` can be called by any JavaScript code that `require`s the file. Arguments and results are JavaScript values (`i64` handles): `ToStr` turns one into a Salam string, and the small `js_str` helper here goes the other way by pushing the string into an array and reading it back.

node-guide-module.salam

```salam
import node
import str

func js_str(s: str): i64:
    box := node.NewArray()
    node.PushStr(box, s)
    ret node.GetProp(box, "0")
end

func slug(text: str): str:
    ret str.Replace(str.Lower(str.Trim(text)), " ", "-")
end

func main:
    exports := node.Exports()
    node.SetStr(exports, "name", "salam-slug")
    node.SetPropFn1R(exports, "slug", (x: i64): ret js_str(slug(node.ToStr(x))) end)
    node.SetPropFn0(exports, "hello", ():
        println "hello from Salam"
    end)
    _ := node.Call0(exports, "hello")
    println node.ToStr(node.Invoke1(node.GetProp(exports, "slug"), js_str("  Hello Salam World ")))
end
```

```salam
hello from Salam
hello-salam-world
```

From JavaScript the module is used as usual: `require("./slug.js").slug("Some Title")`.

## Child processes and events

`ExecFile` starts a program and returns at once; the function you pass runs later, when the program has finished, with a failure flag and everything it wrote to standard output and standard error. That is why started the child is printed first. An `EventEmitter` from the `events` module lets other parts of the program react when the work is done.

node-guide-exec.salam

```salam
import node
import str

func main:
    events := node.New0(node.GetProp(node.Require("events"), "EventEmitter"))
    _ := node.CallSFn0(events, "on", "finished", ():
        println "all jobs finished"
    end)
    args := node.NewArray()
    node.PushStr(args, "-e")
    node.PushStr(args, "console.log(6 * 7)")
    node.ExecFile("node", args, node.TmpDir(), (failed: bool, out: str, err: str):
        if failed:
            println "the child failed:", err
            ret
        end
        println "child printed", str.Trim(out)
        _ := node.CallS1(events, "emit", "finished")
    end)
    println "started the child"
end
```

```salam
started the child
child printed 42
all jobs finished
```

Node keeps the process alive while a child or a timer is pending, so `main` may return long before the callbacks run. Do not free or reuse anything a callback still needs.

`failed` is also true when the program ran but exited with a non-zero status. Both outputs are collected in memory, up to 32 MB each; a program that writes more is stopped and reported as failed. Use `ExecFileRaw` when you need the Node error object itself, for example its `code` property with the exit status.

## Promises and asynchronous files

Most newer Node APIs return a promise instead of taking a callback. A promise is a handle like any other: call its `then` method with `CallFn1` to run code with the result, `catch` to handle a failure and `finally` (with `CallFn0`) for cleanup that must run either way. Here `fs.promises.readFile` reads one file that exists and one that does not.

node-guide-promise.salam

```salam
import node
import str

func main:
    folder := node.MkdtempSync(node.PathJoin2(node.TmpDir(), "salam-orders-"))
    node.WriteFileSync(node.PathJoin2(folder, "orders.csv"), "id,total\n1,40\n2,25\n")
    fsp := node.GetProp(node.Require("fs"), "promises")
    orders := node.CallS2(fsp, "readFile", node.PathJoin2(folder, "orders.csv"), "utf8")
    _ := node.CallFn1(orders, "then", (text: i64):
        println "orders.csv has", str.Count(node.ToStr(text), "\n") - 1, "orders"
        refunds := node.CallS2(fsp, "readFile", node.PathJoin2(folder, "refunds.csv"), "utf8")
        caught := node.CallFn1(refunds, "catch", (err: i64):
            println "refunds.csv failed with", node.GetStr(err, "code")
        end)
        _ := node.CallFn0(caught, "finally", ():
            node.RmSyncRecursiveForce(folder)
            println "temp folder removed"
        end)
    end)
    println "reading started"
end
```

```salam
reading started
orders.csv has 2 orders
refunds.csv failed with ENOENT
temp folder removed
```

A Salam lambda cannot return a value to `then`, so promises do not chain the way they do in JavaScript. To run one step after another, start the next step inside the callback of the previous one, as the second read does here. `NewPromise` goes the other way and makes a promise of your own for JavaScript code to wait on: its function receives the `resolve` and `reject` functions, which you call with `Invoke1`.

## Functions

### `Require`

```salam
func Require(id: str): i64
```

Loads a Node module with `require`.

node-Basics.salam

```salam
import node

func main:
    println node.Platform().len() > 0, node.IsWindows() == (node.Platform() == "win32")
    folder := node.MkdtempSync(node.PathJoin2(node.TmpDir(), "salam-"))
    path := node.PathJoin3(folder, "data", "note.txt")
    println node.PathDirname(path) == node.PathJoin2(folder, "data")
    fs := node.Require("fs")
    _ := node.CallS1(fs, "mkdirSync", node.PathDirname(path))
    node.WriteFileSync(path, "hello from node")
    println node.ReadFileSync(path)
    node.RmSyncRecursiveForce(folder)

    obj := node.NewObject()
    node.SetStr(obj, "name", "Maryam")
    node.SetNum(obj, "age", 30)
    node.SetBool(obj, "admin", true)
    arr := node.NewArray()
    node.PushStr(arr, "a")
    node.Push(arr, obj)
    node.SetProp(obj, "tags", arr)
    println node.GetStr(obj, "name"), node.GetNum(obj, "age"), node.GetBool(obj, "admin")
    println node.GetNum(node.GetProp(obj, "tags"), "length")
    json := node.Global("JSON")
    println node.ToStr(node.CallS1(json, "stringify", "x"))
    println node.IsNullish(node.GetProp(obj, "missing")), node.ToBool(node.GetProp(obj, "admin"))

    math := node.Global("Math")
    println node.ToStr(node.CallV2(math, "max", node.GetProp(obj, "age"), node.GetProp(obj, "age")))
    date := node.New1(node.Global("Date"), node.GetProp(obj, "age"))
    println node.ToStr(node.Call0(date, "getTime"))
    path_module := node.Require("path")
    println node.ToStr(node.CallS2(path_module, "join", "a", "b"))
    println node.ToStr(node.CallS3(path_module, "join", "a", "b", "c"))
    node.SetPropFn0(obj, "hello", ():
        println "hello from a function"
    end)
    _ := node.Call0(obj, "hello")
    node.SetPropFn1R(obj, "twice", (x: i64): ret node.CallV2(math, "max", x, x) end)
    println node.ToStr(node.Invoke1(node.GetProp(obj, "twice"), node.GetProp(obj, "age")))
    println node.IsNullish(node.Exports())
end
```

### `CallV1`

```salam
func CallV1(obj: i64, method: str, a: i64): i64
```

With one JavaScript value.

node-Calls.salam

```salam
import node

func main:
    arr := node.New0(node.Global("Array"))
    node.PushStr(arr, "b")
    node.PushStr(arr, "a")
    _ := node.Call0(arr, "sort")
    println node.ToStr(node.CallS1(arr, "join", ", "))
    number := node.CallV1(node.Global("Math"), "abs", node.GetProp(node.Global("Number"), "MIN_SAFE_INTEGER"))
    println node.ToStr(number).len() > 0
    println node.ToStr(node.CallV3(node.Global("Math"), "max", number, number, number)) == node.ToStr(number)
    date := node.New4(node.Global("Date"), node.GetProp(node.Global("Number"), "EPSILON"), number, number, number)
    println node.IsNullish(date)
    buf := node.CallSB1(node.NewArray(), "includes", "x", false)
    println node.ToStr(buf)
    println node.ToStr(node.CallB1(node.Global("JSON"), "stringify", true))
    println node.ToStr(node.CallVS1(arr, "fill", node.GetProp(arr, "length"), "x"))

    emitter := node.New0(node.GetProp(node.Require("events"), "EventEmitter"))
    _ := node.CallSFn0(emitter, "on", "ping", ():
        println "the ping event arrived"
    end)
    _ := node.CallS1(emitter, "emit", "ping")
    node.SetPropFn1(emitter, "show", (x: i64):
        println "show:", node.ToStr(x)
    end)
    _ := node.Invoke2(node.GetProp(emitter, "show"), arr, arr)
    _ := node.Invoke0(node.GetProp(emitter, "show"))

    _ := node.CallFn0(node.Global("process"), "nextTick", ():
        println "after the current job"
    end)
    _ := node.CallFn1(arr, "forEach", (x: i64):
        println "element:", node.ToStr(x)
    end)
    promise := node.NewPromise((resolve: i64, reject: i64):
        _ := node.Invoke1(resolve, reject)
    end)
    println node.IsNullish(promise)

    args := node.NewArray()
    node.PushStr(args, "-e")
    node.PushStr(args, "console.log('hello from the child')")
    node.ExecFile("node", args, node.TmpDir(), (failed: bool, out: str, err: str):
        println "child:", failed, out.len() > 0, err.len()
    end)
    node.ExecFileRaw("node", args, node.TmpDir(), (code: i64, out: str, _err: str):
        println "raw child:", node.IsNullish(code), out.len() > 0
    end)
end
```

### `ExecFile`

func ExecFile(cmd: str, args: i64, cwd: str, cb: func(bool, str, str))
```

Runs a program with its arguments in the given directory and, once it finishes, calls the function with "it failed", the output and the error output. A non-zero exit status counts as a failure, and each output is capped at 32 MB.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: node-Calls.salam

### `ExecFileRaw`

```salam
func ExecFileRaw(cmd: str, args: i64, cwd: str, cb: func(i64, str, str))
```

The same, with the Node error object itself.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: node-Calls.salam

# aws

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/aws/

Amazon S3, SQS and STS, and any S3 compatible service, with Signature Version 4.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add aws`

This package works with Amazon S3 and any storage compatible with it without the official SDK, including MinIO, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, Backblaze and any other S3 compatible cloud storage. Build the configuration with `ForAws` or `ForEndpoint` and hand it the keys with `WithCredentials`, or let the package find them itself with `FromEnvironment` and `ResolveConfig`.

The `S3...` functions work with objects and buckets: writing and reading, listing, copying, files and folders, multipart uploads for large files, and presigned URLs so a browser can talk to S3 directly. The `Sqs...` functions cover SQS message queues and the `AssumeRole...` functions cover temporary STS credentials. For other services, such as DynamoDB, call any API with `NewJsonCall` and `Invoke`.

Use this package when a program stores files in object storage, hands out upload links, runs queue workers or calls another AWS API. It signs every request with Signature Version 4 itself and sends it over net/http, so it needs no SDK and no C library. For a plain HTTP API that is not AWS, use net/http directly.

### Core ideas

- Config. A `Config` is a plain value: endpoint, region, bucket, keys and whether the bucket goes in the path. Every call takes it first. Change it with the `With...` functions or by setting a field; nothing is global.

- Results, not errors. Calls return a struct with `ok`, the HTTP `status`, AWS's error `code` and a readable `error`. A network failure (`code` is `Transport`), a 429 or a 5xx answer is tried again with a doubling pause, up to `retry` attempts in all (3 by default), before you see it.

- Keys are names. S3 has no folders. `reports/2026/may.csv` is one key, and "folders" are prefixes you list by.

### Things that trip people up

- `S3Get` returns the body as a `str`, which stops at the first zero byte. For images, archives and other binary data use `S3GetBytes` or `S3DownloadFile`.

- `S3ListPrefix` returns one page of at most 1000 keys. `S3ListAll` follows the pages for you, up to 100000 keys, and sets `truncated` when it stopped there. `S3Keys` returns an empty list when the listing failed, so it cannot tell "empty" from "error".

- `Configured` also wants a bucket. A program that only uses SQS, STS or `Invoke` should check `access_key` and `secret_key` itself.

- Lists hold memory of their own: free them with `ListFree`, `KeyFree`, `MessageListFree`, `FreeBytes` and the like.

Never write keys into your code; use environment variables or an IAM role. The examples that need an AWS account or a running MinIO are only checked on the site, not run.

## One program, any S3 provider

Every provider speaks the same S3 API; what differs is the address, the region and whether the bucket goes in the path or in the host name. The `For...` functions fill those in, so the provider can be a setting of your program and the rest of the code never changes. R2 uses the region `auto` and path style addresses; AWS and Spaces put the bucket in the host name.

aws-guide-providers.salam

```salam
import aws

func storage(provider: str, bucket: str): aws.Config:
    switch provider:
        "r2":
            ret aws.ForR2("0123456789abcdef", bucket)
        end
        "spaces":
            ret aws.ForSpaces("ams3", bucket)
        end
        "minio":
            ret aws.ForMinio("http://127.0.0.1:9000", bucket)
        end
    end
    ret aws.ForAws("eu-central-1", bucket)
end

func main:
    each provider in ["aws", "r2", "spaces", "minio"]:
        cfg := storage(provider, "media")
        println provider, cfg.endpoint, cfg.region, cfg.path_style
    end
end
```

Output:

```text
aws https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com eu-central-1 false
r2 https://0123456789abcdef.r2.cloudflarestorage.com auto true
spaces https://ams3.digitaloceanspaces.com ams3 false
minio http://127.0.0.1:9000 us-east-1 true
```

None of these calls touch the network, so the output above is exact. Add the keys with `WithCredentials`, or start from `FromEnvironment`, which reads `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION` and `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`.

## Trying it locally with MinIO

MinIO runs an S3 compatible server on your own machine, which is the cheapest way to develop and test. Start it with Docker:

```salam
docker run -p 9000:9000 -p 9001:9001 minio/minio server /data --console-address :9001
```

The default keys are `minioadmin` and `minioadmin`. The program creates the bucket if it is missing, writes two objects under a date prefix, lists that prefix and reads one object back. Keys are just names: the slashes only look like folders, and listing by prefix is how you walk them.

aws-guide-minio.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    mut cfg := aws.ForMinio("http://127.0.0.1:9000", "backups")
    cfg = aws.WithCredentials(cfg, "minioadmin", "minioadmin")
    if not aws.S3BucketExists(cfg, "backups"):
        made := aws.S3CreateBucket(cfg, "backups")
        if not made.ok:
            println "could not create the bucket:", made.status, made.code, made.error
            ret 1
        end
    end
    _ := aws.S3Put(cfg, "2026/10/notes.txt", "first backup", "text/plain")
    _ := aws.S3Put(cfg, "2026/10/todo.txt", "buy milk", "text/plain")
    mut listing := aws.S3ListPrefix(cfg, "2026/10/")
    each item in listing.items:
        println item.key, item.size
    end
    aws.ListFree(listing)
    got := aws.S3Get(cfg, "2026/10/notes.txt")
    if got.ok:
        println "read back:", got.body
    else:
        println "read failed:", got.status, got.code
    end
end
```

Each call returns a `Result`. When `ok` is false, `status` is the HTTP status and `code` is S3's own error code, such as `NoSuchKey` or `AccessDenied`; branch on `code`, not on the message text. A list holds memory of its own, so free it with `ListFree` when you are done.

## Large files and binary data

`S3UploadFile` reads a file from disk and picks the method by size. Up to the part size (8 MB by default, set `part_size` in `PutOptions`, never less than 5 MB) it sends one `PUT`; above that it streams the file in parts with a multipart upload, so memory use stays at one part. `S3DownloadFile` fetches the object in 8 MB ranges into `name.part` and renames it only when the whole file has arrived, so a failed download never leaves a half-written file under the real name.

aws-guide-files.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    mut cfg := aws.ForMinio("http://127.0.0.1:9000", "backups")
    cfg = aws.WithCredentials(cfg, "minioadmin", "minioadmin")
    opts := aws.PutOptions { content_type = "application/gzip", storage_class = "STANDARD_IA" }
    up := aws.S3UploadFile(cfg, "db/2026-10-17.sql.gz", "/var/backups/shop.sql.gz", opts)
    if not up.ok:
        println "upload failed:", up.code, up.error
        ret 1
    end
    println "uploaded", up.bytes, "bytes in", up.parts, "part(s)"
    down := aws.S3DownloadFile(cfg, "db/2026-10-17.sql.gz", "/tmp/restore.sql.gz")
    if not down.ok:
        println "download failed:", down.code, down.error
        ret 1
    end
    println "restored", down.bytes, "bytes to", down.path
    logo := aws.S3GetBytes(cfg, "site/logo.png")
    if logo.ok:
        println "logo.png is", logo.len, "bytes"
    end
    aws.FreeBytes(logo)
end
```

`TransferResult` tells you how many bytes moved and in how many parts. `storage_class`, `cache_control`, `sse` and the other `PutOptions` fields become the matching S3 headers. For a whole directory there is `S3UploadDir`.

## Letting the browser upload directly

A presigned URL lets a browser upload or download one object without ever seeing your keys, and without the file passing through your server. Your server signs the URL; the browser sends a plain `PUT` to it. When `content_type` is set, it becomes part of the signature and the upload must send exactly that type. `response_content_disposition` on a download makes the browser save the file under the name you choose.

aws-guide-presign.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    mut cfg := aws.ForAws("eu-central-1", "user-uploads")
    cfg = aws.WithCredentials(cfg, "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY")
    at := 1792224000 as i64
    upload := aws.PresignOptions { expires = 300, content_type = "image/jpeg" }
    put_url := aws.S3PresignWith(cfg, "PUT", "avatars/42.jpg", upload, at)
    println "upload:", put_url.len() > 0
    println put_url.substr(0, put_url.find("?"))
    println "expires in 300s:", put_url.find("X-Amz-Expires=300") >= 0
    println "content type is signed:", put_url.find("content-type") >= 0
    download := aws.PresignOptions { expires = 3600, response_content_disposition = "attachment; filename=\"photo.jpg\"" }
    get_url := aws.S3PresignWith(cfg, "GET", "avatars/42.jpg", download, at)
    println "download asks to save:", get_url.find("response-content-disposition=attachment") >= 0
    println "same signature twice:", get_url == aws.S3PresignWith(cfg, "GET", "avatars/42.jpg", download, at)
end
```

Output:

```text
upload: true
https://user-uploads.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/avatars/42.jpg
expires in 300s: true
content type is signed: true
download asks to save: true
same signature twice: true
```

Signing is a local computation, so this program runs without a network. It uses `S3PresignWith` with a fixed time to get the same URL on every run; in a real program use `S3PresignPut` or `S3PresignGet`, which sign with the current time. Keep `expires` short: anyone who has the URL can use it until then.

## A queue worker with SQS

SQS holds jobs until a worker takes them. `SqsReceive` waits up to `wait_seconds` for messages, which costs far less than asking again and again. A received message is hidden from other workers, not removed: delete it with its `receipt` once the work is done, or release it with `SqsRelease` so another worker can try at once. A message that is neither comes back by itself when its visibility timeout ends.

aws-guide-worker.salam

```salam
import aws

func handle(body: str): bool:
    println "resizing", body
    ret body.len() > 0
end

func main:
    cfg := aws.FromEnvironment("")
    if cfg.access_key.len() == 0 or cfg.secret_key.len() == 0:
        println "set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_REGION"
        ret 1
    end
    queue := aws.SqsQueueUrl(cfg, "image-jobs")
    if queue.len() == 0:
        println "the queue image-jobs does not exist"
        ret 1
    end
    _ := aws.SqsSend(cfg, queue, "photos/beach.jpg")
    opts := aws.ReceiveOptions { max_messages = 10, wait_seconds = 20 }
    batch := aws.SqsReceive(cfg, queue, opts)
    if not batch.ok:
        println "receive failed:", batch.code, batch.error
        ret 1
    end
    each m in batch.items:
        if handle(m.body):
            _ := aws.SqsDelete(cfg, queue, m.receipt)
        else:
            _ := aws.SqsRelease(cfg, queue, m.receipt)
        end
    end
    println "handled", batch.items.len(), "message(s)"
end
```

The program checks the keys itself instead of calling `Configured`, because a queue worker has no bucket. Run it with real AWS credentials and an existing queue named `image-jobs`. In a real worker, put the receive in a loop and make each job safe to run twice, because SQS delivers every message at least once.

## Calling any other AWS API

Most AWS services take a signed `POST` with a JSON body and an `X-Amz-Target` header that names the operation. `NewJsonCall` builds such a call (`NewJson11Call` for services that want JSON 1.1, `NewQueryCall` for the older form APIs, `NewRestCall` for REST ones), and `Invoke` signs and sends it. The endpoint comes from the service name and the region. This program looks up one DynamoDB item. `PreparedCall` shows the exact request `Invoke` would send, signed at a fixed time, without touching the network:

aws-guide-dynamodb.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    mut cfg := aws.Config { region = "eu-west-1" }
    cfg = aws.WithCredentials(cfg, "AKIDEXAMPLE", "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG+bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY")
    item := `{"TableName": "orders", "Key": {"order_id": {"S": "A-1042"}}}`
    mut call := aws.NewJsonCall("dynamodb", "DynamoDB_20120810.GetItem", item)
    println aws.PreparedCall(cfg, call, 1760000000 as i64)
    aws.CallFree(call)
end
```

Output:

```text
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: dynamodb.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com
Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.GetItem
x-amz-content-sha256: 4121fbc59183f2c71317b22f5a5e996b56f755df4905a3006519db21410ef47c
x-amz-date: 20251009T085320Z
Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=AKIDEXAMPLE/20251009/eu-west-1/dynamodb/aws4_request, SignedHeaders=content-type;host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date;x-amz-target, Signature=f8e075bd147ac5d5f44a7c371cb66fd2cb421d5156ec10bde939b751b6c9a011
Content-Length: 61
Connection: close

{"TableName": "orders", "Key": {"order_id": {"S": "A-1042"}}}
```

With real keys, `res := aws.Invoke(cfg, call)` sends it; `res.body` is the JSON answer and, on failure, `res.code` is the AWS error type such as `ResourceNotFoundException`. The JSON format of each operation is in the AWS API reference of that service.

## Which function for which job

| Job | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| Choose the provider | `ForAws`, `ForMinio`, `ForR2`, `ForSpaces`, `ForEndpoint`, `FromEnvironment` |
| Write and read small objects | `S3Put`, `S3Get`, `S3Stat`, `S3Delete` |
| Files of any size | `S3UploadFile`, `S3DownloadFile` (multipart when needed) |
| Walk a folder | `S3ListPrefix`, `S3ListAll`, `S3Keys` |
| Browser uploads and downloads | `S3PresignPut`, `S3PresignGet`, `S3PresignPost` |
| Background jobs | `SqsSend`, `SqsReceive`, `SqsDelete` |
| Temporary credentials | `AssumeRole`, then `Apply` |
| Any other AWS API | `NewJsonCall` and `Invoke` |

## Types

### `TransferResult`

```salam
struct TransferResult
```

The result of transferring one file.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | It succeeded. |
| `status` | `int = 0` | The HTTP status code. |
| `bytes` | `i64 = 0` | The bytes transferred. |
| `parts` | `int = 0` | The number of parts; 1 for a small file. |
| `etag` | `str = ""` | The ETag. |
| `path` | `str = ""` | The file path. |
| `key` | `str = ""` | The key. |
| `error` | `str = ""` | The error message. |
| `code` | `str = ""` | The service error code, such as `NoSuchKey`. |

aws-Files.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    cfg := aws.FromProfile("default", "backup")
    if not aws.Configured(cfg):
        println "the default profile was not found in ~/.aws"
        ret
    end

    o := aws.PutOptions { part_size = aws.S3_PART_DEFAULT }
    up := aws.S3UploadFile(cfg, "db/dump.sql", "/tmp/dump_en.sql", o)
    println up.ok, up.bytes, up.parts, up.etag
    println aws.S3FileEtag("/tmp/dump_en.sql", aws.S3_PART_DEFAULT) == up.etag
    _ := aws.S3UploadFileAs(cfg, "img/logo.png", "/tmp/logo_en.png", "image/png")
    down := aws.S3DownloadFile(cfg, "db/dump.sql", "/tmp/restore_en.sql")
    println down.ok, down.path, down.error

    dir := aws.S3UploadDir(cfg, "/var/www/site", "site/", aws.PutOptions {})
    println dir.ok, dir.files, dir.bytes, dir.skipped, dir.failed_path
    _ := aws.S3DownloadPrefix(cfg, "site/", "/tmp/site_en")

    println aws.S3_PART_MIN, aws.S3_PART_MAX_COUNT
    mut upload := aws.S3CreateUpload(cfg, "video.mp4", aws.PutOptions { content_type = "video/mp4" })
    if not upload.ok:
        println upload.error
        ret
    end
    chunk := "x" * aws.S3_PART_MIN
    _ := aws.S3UploadPart(cfg, upload, 1, chunk as void*, chunk.len())
    _ := aws.S3UploadPartCopy(cfg, upload, 2, "old.mp4", aws.CopyOptions {}, 0, 5242879)
    println aws.UploadParts(upload), aws.UploadBytes(upload)
    parts := aws.S3ListParts(cfg, "video.mp4", upload.upload_id)
    repeat aws.PartCount(parts) in i:
        p := aws.PartAt(parts, i)
        println p.number, p.etag, p.size
    end
    println aws.S3CompleteUpload(cfg, upload).ok
    aws.UploadFreeParts(upload)

    pending := aws.S3ListUploads(cfg, "")
    repeat aws.UploadCount(pending) in j:
        u := aws.UploadAt(pending, j)
        _ := aws.S3AbortUpload(cfg, aws.Upload { key = u.key, upload_id = u.upload_id })
    end
    _ := aws.S3PutLarge(cfg, "big.bin", chunk as void*, chunk.len(), 0, aws.PutOptions {})
    _ := aws.S3CopyLarge(cfg, "big.bin", "big2.bin", 0, aws.CopyOptions {})
end
```

aws-Parse.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    mut cfg := aws.ForAws("eu-west-1", "")
    cfg = aws.WithCredentials(cfg, "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY")
    at := 1369353600 as i64

    listing := `<ListBucketResult><Name>photos</Name><Prefix>2026/</Prefix><KeyCount>2</KeyCount><IsTruncated>true</IsTruncated><NextContinuationToken>tok2</NextContinuationToken>

<Contents><Key>2026/b.jpg</Key><Size>800</Size><ETag>"bb22"</ETag><LastModified>2026-03-21T10:00:00.000Z</LastModified><StorageClass>STANDARD</StorageClass></Contents>
<CommonPrefixes><Prefix>2026/thumbs/</Prefix></CommonPrefixes></ListBucketResult>`
    mut list := aws.ParseListing(listing, 200)
    println list.ok, list.name, list.truncated, list.next_token, aws.ListCount(list), aws.ListTotalSize(list)
    entry := aws.ListAt(list, 0)
    println entry.key, entry.size, entry.etag, entry.last_modified, entry.storage_class
    println aws.ListPrefixCount(list), aws.ListPrefixAt(list, 0)
    println aws.ListToResult(list).ok
    aws.ListFree(list)

    mut keys := aws.NewKeyList()
    aws.KeyPush(keys, "tmp/1")
    aws.KeyPush(keys, "tmp/2")
    println aws.KeyCount(keys), aws.KeyAt(keys, 1)
    aws.KeyFree(keys)
    println aws.S3ExpiryRule("logs/", 30, 7)

    queue := "https://sqs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/jobs"
    reply := "<ReceiveMessageResponse><ReceiveMessageResult><Message><MessageId>m-1</MessageId><ReceiptHandle>AQEB==</ReceiptHandle><MD5OfBody>fafb</MD5OfBody><Body>invoice 42</Body><Attribute><Name>ApproximateReceiveCount</Name><Value>2</Value></Attribute><MessageAttribute><Name>tenant</Name><Value><DataType>String</DataType><StringValue>acme</StringValue></Value></MessageAttribute></Message></ReceiveMessageResult></ReceiveMessageResponse>"
    mut messages := aws.ParseReceive(reply, 200)
    println messages.ok, aws.MessageCount(messages)
    msg := aws.MessageAt(messages, 0)
    println msg.id, msg.body, msg.receipt, msg.receive_count, aws.MessageAttribute(msg, "tenant")
    aws.MessageListFree(messages)

    mut out := aws.OutMessage { body = "job", delay = 30, group_id = "g1", dedup_id = "d1" }
    aws.HeaderSet(out.attributes, "tenant", "acme")
    mut send := aws.SqsSendCall(queue, out)
    println aws.CallBodyText(send)
    aws.CallFree(send)
    mut receive := aws.SqsReceiveCall(queue, aws.ReceiveOptions { max_messages = 99, wait_seconds = 60 })
    println aws.CallBodyText(receive)
    aws.CallFree(receive)
    println aws.SQS_VERSION, aws.SQS_MAX_MESSAGES, aws.SQS_MAX_WAIT, aws.SQS_MAX_BATCH
    println aws.SqsRedrivePolicy("arn:aws:sqs:eu-west-1:123456789012:dead", 5)

    mut call := aws.NewQueryCall("sts", "GetCallerIdentity", aws.STS_VERSION)
    aws.CallParam(call, "Name", "ali")
    aws.CallParamInt(call, "DurationSeconds", 900)
    println aws.CallBodyText(call)
    head := aws.PreparedCall(cfg, call, at)
    println head.find("POST / HTTP/1.1") == 0, head.find("Host: sts.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com") >= 0
    aws.CallFree(call)

    mut dynamo := aws.NewJsonCall("dynamodb", "DynamoDB_20120810.ListTables", "{}")
    aws.CallRegion(dynamo, "eu-central-1")
    aws.CallHeader(dynamo, "x-amz-meta-app", "salam")
    println aws.PreparedCall(cfg, dynamo, at).find("X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.ListTables") >= 0
    logs := aws.NewJson11Call("logs", "Logs_20140328.DescribeLogGroups", "{}")
    println logs.content_type

    mut rest := aws.NewRestCall("lambda", "GET", "/2015-03-31/functions")
    aws.CallQuery(rest, "MaxItems", "5")
    aws.CallBody(rest, "", "application/json")
    aws.CallEndpoint(rest, "http://127.0.0.1:4566")
    println aws.PreparedCall(cfg, rest, at).find("GET /2015-03-31/functions?MaxItems=5 HTTP/1.1") == 0

    failure := `{"__type":"com.amazon#ResourceNotFoundException","message":"Table not found"}`
    println aws.ServiceErrorCode(failure), aws.ServiceErrorMessage(failure, 400)
end
```

aws-Buckets.salam

```salam
import aws

func main:
    cfg := aws.FromEnvironment("")
    if not aws.Configured(cfg):
        println "AWS credentials are not set"
        ret
    end

    bucket := "salam-demo-2026"
    _ := aws.S3CreateBucket(cfg, bucket)
    _ := aws.S3CreateBucketAcl(cfg, bucket + "-logs", "private")
    println aws.S3BucketExists(cfg, bucket), aws.S3HeadBucket(cfg, bucket).status, aws.S3BucketRegion(cfg, bucket)

    mut list := aws.S3ListBuckets(cfg)
    println list.ok, list.owner, aws.BucketCount(list)
    repeat aws.BucketCount(list) in i:
        b := aws.BucketAt(list, i)
        println b.name, b.created, b.region
    end
    aws.BucketListFree(list)

    _ := aws.S3SetVersioning(cfg, bucket, true)
    println aws.S3Versioning(cfg, bucket)
    mut tags := aws.NewTags()
    aws.TagSet(tags, "project", "salam")
    _ := aws.S3SetBucketTags(cfg, bucket, tags)
    aws.HeaderFree(tags)
    mut current := aws.S3BucketTags(cfg, bucket)
    println aws.HeaderGet(current, "project")
    aws.HeaderFree(current)
    _ := aws.S3DeleteBucketTags(cfg, bucket)

    policy := `{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:GetObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::salam-demo-2026/public/*"}]}`
    _ := aws.S3SetBucketPolicy(cfg, bucket, policy)
    println aws.S3BucketPolicy(cfg, bucket).len() > 0
    _ := aws.S3DeleteBucketPolicy(cfg, bucket)
    _ := aws.S3SetBucketCors(cfg, bucket, "https://salamlang.ir", "GET,PUT", 3600)
    println aws.S3BucketCors(cfg, bucket).len() > 0
    _ := aws.S3DeleteBucketCors(cfg, bucket)
    _ := aws.S3SetLifecycle(cfg, bucket, aws.S3ExpiryRule("tmp/", 7, 1))
    println aws.S3Lifecycle(cfg, bucket).len() > 0
    _ := aws.S3DeleteLifecycle(cfg, bucket)

    _ := aws.S3DeleteBucket(cfg, bucket + "-logs")
    println aws.S3DeleteBucket(cfg, bucket).ok
end
```
