# llm

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/llm/

Running Llama and Qwen language models from a GGUF file.

This is an official package that does not ship with Salam. Add it to a project first: `salam add llm`

This package runs large language models of the Llama family on the processor, in pure Salam with no outside library. Download a model in GGUF form, read it with `LoadGgufModel` and make text with `Generate`, or drive the loop yourself with `Forward` and a `Sampler` (temperature, top-k, top-p and a repetition penalty).

It is meant for small models running inside your own program: classifying or rewriting short texts offline, a local assistant in a tool, or learning how a transformer works step by step. For large models or high speed, call a server such as llama.cpp or an API over net/http instead.

### What runs, and what it costs

- The layer layout is Llama's: RMSNorm, rotary positions, grouped-query attention and a SwiGLU feed forward block, with the optional attention biases that Qwen2 uses. Qwen2.5 Instruct is tested; Llama and Mistral use the same layout. Architectures with other layouts, such as Phi, fail to load or produce nonsense.

- The file limits of gguf apply: under 2 GB, and only `F32`, `F16`, `Q8_0`, `Q4_0` and `Q4_1` weights, not the K-quants.

- Every weight is expanded to `f32` when the model loads, so Qwen2.5 0.5B, a 0.7 GB file, needs about 3 GB of memory. The key/value cache is sized for `cfg.ctx`, which starts as the model's full context (32768 for Qwen); lower it before `NewKVCache` to save memory.

- `encode` does not recognise special tokens such as `<|im_start|>` in text: it splits them into ordinary pieces, which the model does not understand. Look their ids up in `tok.index` and insert them yourself, as the chat example does.

The tokenizer, sampling and generation also work on a small random model built with `RandomModel`, which is how the reference example at the bottom of this page runs without a download.

## A chat answer, streamed

Instruction tuned models expect the conversation in the exact format they were trained on. Qwen uses `<|im_start|>` and `<|im_end|>` around each turn, and the prompt ends by opening the assistant's turn so the model writes the reply. The format of any model is in its GGUF file under `tokenizer.chat_template`; see `gguf` for reading it. Those markers are single special tokens, so `add_turn` pushes their ids from `tok.index` and only encodes the text between them.

Instead of `Generate`, which returns the whole text at the end, this program runs the loop itself so every token is printed as soon as it is chosen. The first `Forward` call reads the whole prompt; after that each call feeds only the newest token, because the `KVCache` remembers everything before it. The loop stops at the end of turn token, after 80 tokens, or when the context is full. `cfg.ctx` is lowered to 4096 first, which keeps the cache at about 100 MB instead of 800.

```salam
mkdir -p models
curl -L -o models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q8_0.gguf \
  https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q8_0.gguf
salam run llm-guide-chat.salam
```

llm-guide-chat.salam

```salam
import llm
import tensor

func add_turn(tok &: llm.Tokenizer, ids &: Vector<int>, role: str, text: str):
    ids.push(tok.index.get("<|im_start|>"))
    piece := tok.encode(role + "\n" + text)
    each id in piece:
        ids.push(id)
    end
    if text.len() > 0:
        ids.push(tok.index.get("<|im_end|>"))
        newline := tok.encode("\n")
        each id in newline:
            ids.push(id)
        end
    end
end

func main:
    path := "models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q8_0.gguf"
    mut model := llm.Model {}
    mut tok := llm.NewTokenizer(llm.TOK_BPE)
    if not llm.LoadGgufModel(path, model, tok):
        println "could not load", path
        ret 1
    end
    tok.add_bos = false
    end_of_turn := tok.index.get("<|im_end|>")
    model.cfg.ctx = 4096
    mut cache := llm.NewKVCache(model.cfg)
    mut sampler := llm.NewSampler(42)
    sampler.temperature = 0.7
    sampler.top_p = 0.9
    sampler.repeat_penalty = 1.1
    mut ids := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    add_turn(tok, ids, "system", "You are a helpful assistant. Answer in one sentence.")
    add_turn(tok, ids, "user", "Why is the sky blue?")
    add_turn(tok, ids, "assistant", "")
    mut logits := llm.Forward(model, cache, ids)
    mut said := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    mut step := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    step.push(0)
    until said.len() < 80 and cache.len < cache.ctx:
        next := sampler.sample(logits, logits.dim(0) - 1, said)
        tensor.Free(logits)
        if next == end_of_turn or next == tok.eos:
            break
        end
        said.push(next)
        step.set(0, next)
        print tok.decode(step)
        logits = llm.Forward(model, cache, step)
    end
    println ""
    println "tokens in prompt:", ids.len(), "answer:", said.len()
    cache.free()
    model.free()
    tok.free()
end
```

```salam
The sky appears blue because of the scattering of sunlight by tiny water droplets in the atmosphere, which causes them to bounce off each other and scatter into our eyes.
tokens in prompt: 30 answer: 33
```

A half billion weight model writes fluent sentences but gets facts wrong, as here: the real cause is scattering by air molecules, not water droplets. Use such a model for form, not for knowledge. Build with `salam build --release` for real use: the model runs on the processor, and a release build drops the bounds checks from the inner loops. Even so, expect a few seconds per token on an ordinary machine.

## How text becomes tokens

A model never sees letters, only token ids. A BPE tokenizer starts from single characters and applies its list of merges in order, so frequent pieces such as `lower` become one token while rare words fall apart into many. Byte level BPE, the kind GPT 2, Llama 3 and Qwen use, writes a space as `&#288;`, so the space before a word is part of a token. This tokenizer is built by hand with five merges to make the steps visible.

llm-guide-tokens.salam

```salam
import llm

func show(tok &: llm.Tokenizer, text: str):
    ids := tok.encode(text)
    mut parts := ""
    each id in ids:
        parts = parts + "[" + tok.token_text(id) + "]"
    end
    println text, "->", ids.len(), "tokens", parts
end

func main:
    mut tok := llm.NewTokenizer(llm.TOK_BPE)
    each piece in ["l", "o", "w", "e", "r", "n", "s", "t", "Ġ", "lo", "low", "er", "lower"]:
        _ := tok.add_token(piece, 0.0)
    end
    tok.add_merge("l", "o")
    tok.add_merge("lo", "w")
    tok.add_merge("e", "r")
    tok.add_merge("low", "er")
    tok.finish()
    tok.add_bos = false
    show(tok, "low")
    show(tok, "lower")
    show(tok, "slower")
    show(tok, "newest")
    show(tok, "lower tower")
    println "round trip:", tok.decode(tok.encode("lower tower")) == "lower tower"
    tok.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
low -> 1 tokens [low]
lower -> 1 tokens [lower]
slower -> 2 tokens [s][lower]
newest -> 6 tokens [n][e][w][e][s][t]
lower tower -> 6 tokens [lower][Ġ][t][o][w][er]
round trip: true
```

`tower` is not merged into `ow` pieces because the merges only know `lo` and `low`. Counting tokens this way is also how you check that a prompt fits in the model's context before sending it.

## Temperature and top-k

The model gives a score, a logit, for every token in the vocabulary, and the sampler turns the scores into a choice. `Greedy` always takes the highest. A `Sampler` draws at random in proportion to the probabilities: a temperature below one sharpens them toward the favourite, above one flattens them, and `top_k` drops all but the best `k` before drawing. The program draws 1000 times from four fixed scores with each setting and counts how often each token wins.

llm-guide-sampling.salam

```salam
import llm
import tensor

func counts(sampler &: llm.Sampler, logits &: tensor.Tensor): str:
    mut seen := [0, 0, 0, 0]
    mut recent := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    repeat 1000:
        seen[sampler.sample(logits, 0, recent)] += 1
    end
    ret "" + seen[0] + " " + seen[1] + " " + seen[2] + " " + seen[3]
end

func main:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f32>
    each v in [2.0, 1.5, 0.5, -1.0]:
        data.push(v as f32)
    end
    shape := tensor.Shape2(1, 4)
    logits := tensor.FromArray(shape, data)
    println "greedy always picks", llm.Greedy(logits, 0)
    mut plain := llm.NewSampler(1)
    println "temperature 1.0:", counts(plain, logits)
    mut cold := llm.NewSampler(1)
    cold.temperature = 0.3
    println "temperature 0.3:", counts(cold, logits)
    mut hot := llm.NewSampler(1)
    hot.temperature = 2.0
    println "temperature 2.0:", counts(hot, logits)
    mut top2 := llm.NewSampler(1)
    top2.top_k = 2
    println "top_k 2:        ", counts(top2, logits)
end
```

Output:

```text
greedy always picks 0
temperature 1.0: 508 345 121 26
temperature 0.3: 832 164 4 0
temperature 2.0: 386 321 200 93
top_k 2:         599 401 0 0
```

The seed passed to `NewSampler` makes the draws repeatable, which is why this output never changes. For factual answers use a low temperature; for varied writing, around 0.7 to 1.0 with `top_p` 0.9. `repeat_penalty` above 1 lowers the scores of recently used tokens and stops small models from looping.

## Types

### `Tokenizer`

```salam
struct Tokenizer
```

The tokenizer: it turns text into indices and back.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `int` | The kind. |
| `tokens` | `Vector` | The text of the tokens. |
| `scores` | `Vector` | The scores, for SentencePiece. |
| `index` | `HashMap` | The index of each token. |
| `merges` | `HashMap` | The ranks of the BPE merges. |
| `merge_keys` | `Vector` | The merge keys. |
| `bos` | `int = -1` | The index of the beginning token; -1 means there is none. |
| `eos` | `int = -1` | The index of the end token. |
| `unk` | `int = 0` | The index of the unknown token. |
| `add_bos` | `bool = true` | Add the beginning token when encoding. |
| `byte_ids` | `Vector` | The token index of each byte. |
| `b2u` | `Vector` | The byte to character map of byte level BPE. |

llm-Generate.salam

```salam
import llm
import tensor

func main:
    mut tokenizer := llm.NewTokenizer(llm.TOK_BPE)
    each text in ["a", "b", "c", "ab"]:
        _ := tokenizer.add_token(text, 0.0)
    end
    tokenizer.add_merge("a", "b")
    tokenizer.finish()
    tokenizer.add_bos = false
    mut ids := tokenizer.encode("abcab")
    println tokenizer.size(), ids.len(), tokenizer.token_text(ids.get(0)), tokenizer.decode(ids)
    println llm.TOK_SPM, llm.ROPE_NORMAL, llm.ROPE_NEOX

    mut config := llm.Config { vocab = tokenizer.size(), dim = 8, layers = 2, heads = 2, kv_heads = 1, ff = 16, ctx = 32 }
    println config.head_dim()
    mut model := llm.RandomModel(config, 7)
    mut cache := llm.NewKVCache(config)
    println model.ok, model.layers.len(), cache.ctx

    mut logits := llm.Forward(model, cache, ids)
    println tensor.ShapeString(logits), cache.len
    mut last := llm.LogitsRow(logits, ids.len() - 1)
    greedy := llm.Greedy(logits, ids.len() - 1)
    println tensor.ShapeString(last), greedy == tensor.ArgMaxAll(last)

    mut sampler := llm.NewSampler(1)
    sampler.temperature = 0.8
    sampler.top_k = 3
    sampler.top_p = 0.9
    sampler.repeat_penalty = 1.1
    mut recent := Vector {} as Vector<int>
    next := sampler.sample(logits, ids.len() - 1, recent)
    println next >= 0 and next < tokenizer.size()

    cache.reset()
    generated := llm.GenerateIds(model, cache, ids, 4, sampler, -1)
    println generated.len()
    cache.reset()
    text := llm.Generate(model, cache, tokenizer, "ab", 3, sampler)
    println text.len() > 0
    tensor.Free(logits)
    tensor.Free(last)
    cache.free()
    model.free()
    tokenizer.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
4 3 ab abcab
0 0 1
4
true 2 32
3x4 3
1x4 true
true
4
true
```

```salam
import llm
import gguf

func main:
    path := "models/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q8_0.gguf"
    mut model := llm.Model {}
    mut tokenizer := llm.NewTokenizer(llm.TOK_BPE)
    if not llm.LoadGgufModel(path, model, tokenizer):
        println "the model was not loaded:", path
        ret
    end
    mut cache := llm.NewKVCache(model.cfg)
    mut sampler := llm.NewSampler(42)
    sampler.temperature = 0.7
    println llm.Generate(model, cache, tokenizer, "The capital of France", 20, sampler)

    mut good := false
    mut file := gguf.LoadGguf(path, good)
    config := llm.ConfigFromGguf(file)
    println config.vocab, config.dim, config.layers, config.heads, config.kv_heads, config.ff, config.ctx, config.eps, config.rope_theta, config.rope_kind
    mut model2 := llm.ModelFromGguf(file)
    mut tokenizer2 := llm.TokenizerFromGguf(file)
    println tokenizer2.bos, tokenizer2.eos, tokenizer2.unk
    model2.free()
    tokenizer2.free()
    file.free()
    cache.free()
    model.free()
    tokenizer.free()
end
```

# matrix

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/matrix/

Linear algebra: matrices, systems of equations, decompositions, eigenvalues and statistics.

This package is complete linear algebra over 64 bit floats: from making a matrix and multiplying through to solving systems, decompositions, eigenvalues and singular values, and statistical tools such as principal component analysis. To solve one system, call `Solve`; for several systems with one matrix, `Decompose` once and `LUSolve` many times.

Use it when the answer must be exact to the last digits a double allows: engineering, statistics, finance, geometry. For neural networks and large batches of `f32` data see tensor; for means, medians and tests on plain lists, stats; for ready made machine learning models, ml.

### Things to know

- Results carry a little rounding error. Compare with `AllClose` and a tolerance, and show results with `Chop` or `ToStringPrec`.

- Nothing stops the program. A shape mismatch or a singular matrix gives an empty `0x0` matrix; check `is_empty()` before you use a result.

- Every function returns a new matrix that owns its memory. In long loops call `free` on results you are done with, or use the `...InPlace` forms.

## Solve a system of equations

Three shopping baskets with known totals give three equations in three unknown prices. Put the quantities in a matrix `A`, the totals in a column `b`, and `Solve` returns the column of prices. When the equations do not pin down one answer, `Solve` returns an empty matrix, so check `is_empty` before you use the result. `Residual` computes `A x - b`, a quick way to see how good a solution is.

matrix-guide-prices.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func main:
    mut baskets := build(3, 3, "2 1 1 1 3 2 1 0 4")
    mut totals := build(3, 1, "9.5 17 17.5")
    mut prices := matrix.Solve(baskets, totals)
    if prices.is_empty():
        println "the baskets do not pin down the prices"
        ret 1
    end
    names := ["apple", "bread", "cheese"]
    each i, name in names:
        println name, matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Row(prices, i), 2)
    end
    mut check := matrix.Residual(baskets, prices, totals)
    println "largest error is tiny:", matrix.MaxAbs(check) < 0.000001
    mut order := build(1, 3, "4 2 1")
    println "4 apples, 2 bread, 1 cheese:", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.MatMul(order, prices), 2)
    prices.free()
    check.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
apple 1.50
bread 2.50
cheese 4.00
largest error is tiny: true
4 apples, 2 bread, 1 cheese: 15.00
```

The examples build matrices from a string of numbers with a small `build` helper that calls `FromArray`; any other way of filling a `Vector<f64>` row by row works the same.

## One matrix, many right-hand sides

In engineering the matrix often stays the same while the input changes: the same structure under different loads. `Decompose` does the expensive work once, and each `LUSolve` after that is cheap. The decomposition also tells you whether the matrix is singular, before you try to solve anything.

matrix-guide-loads.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func main:
    mut springs := build(3, 3, "20 -10 0 -10 20 -10 0 -10 10")
    mut lu := matrix.Decompose(springs)
    if lu.singular:
        println "the system has no unique solution"
        ret 1
    end
    loads := ["0 0 5", "5 0 0", "1 1 1"]
    each load in loads:
        mut force := build(3, 1, load)
        mut shift := matrix.LUSolve(lu, force)
        println "load", load, "->", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Transpose(shift), 2)
        force.free()
        shift.free()
    end
    println "determinant", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Full(1, 1, matrix.Det(springs)), 1)
    lu.free()
    springs.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
load 0 0 5 -> 0.50 1.00 1.50
load 5 0 0 -> 0.50 0.50 0.50
load 1 1 1 -> 0.30 0.50 0.60
determinant 1000.0
```

## Fit a line or a curve to data

`LinearRegression` fits a straight line and returns the intercept and the slope as a column. For a curve, build the columns 1, x, x² with `Vandermonde` and pass them to `LeastSquares`. `RSquared` says how much of the variation the fit explains; 1 means a perfect fit. Here a parabola through fuel use at six speeds gives the most economical speed.

matrix-guide-fit.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func r(value: f64): str:
    ret matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Full(1, 1, value), 2)
end

func main:
    mut area := build(5, 1, "50 70 90 110 130")
    mut rent := build(5, 1, "520 690 910 1080 1300")
    mut line := matrix.LinearRegression(area, rent)
    println "rent =", r(line.at(0, 0)), "+", r(line.at(1, 0)), "* area"
    mut design := matrix.Vandermonde(area, 2)
    mut fitted := matrix.MatMul(design, line)
    println "R squared", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Full(1, 1, matrix.RSquared(rent, fitted)), 4)
    println "100 square meters:", r(line.at(0, 0) + line.at(1, 0) * 100.0)

    mut speed := build(6, 1, "40 60 80 100 120 140")
    mut fuel := build(6, 1, "7.1 6.0 5.8 6.4 7.5 9.1")
    mut curve := matrix.LeastSquares(matrix.Vandermonde(speed, 3), fuel)
    a := curve.at(0, 0)
    b := curve.at(1, 0)
    c := curve.at(2, 0)
    best := 0.0 - b / (2.0 * c)
    println "most economical speed", r(best), "uses", r(a + b * best + c * best * best)
    line.free()
    design.free()
    fitted.free()
    curve.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
rent = 22.50 + 9.75 * area
R squared 0.9980
100 square meters: 997.50
most economical speed 77.08 uses 5.87
```

## Powers of a matrix: a Markov chain

A transition matrix holds the chance of moving from each state to each other state; here sunny, cloudy and rainy weather. Multiplying today's distribution by the matrix raised to the power n gives the distribution n days later. After a few weeks the answer no longer depends on where you started: that is the long term share of each kind of day.

matrix-guide-markov.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func main:
    mut weather := build(3, 3, "0.7 0.2 0.1 0.3 0.4 0.3 0.2 0.3 0.5")
    println "rows sum to one:", matrix.IsRowStochastic(weather, 0.000001)
    mut today := build(1, 3, "1 0 0")
    each days in [1, 2, 7, 30]:
        mut ahead := matrix.MatMul(today, matrix.MatPow(weather, days))
        println "after", days, "days", matrix.ToStringPrec(ahead, 3)
        ahead.free()
    end
    mut rainy := build(1, 3, "0 0 1")
    mut later := matrix.MatMul(rainy, matrix.MatPow(weather, 30))
    println "from a rainy day", matrix.ToStringPrec(later, 3)
    weather.free()
    today.free()
    rainy.free()
    later.free()
end
```

Output:

```text
rows sum to one: true
after 1 days 0.700 0.200 0.100
after 2 days 0.570 0.250 0.180
after 7 days 0.459 0.282 0.259
after 30 days 0.457 0.283 0.261
from a rainy day 0.457 0.283 0.261
```

## Finding the main directions: PCA

Principal component analysis finds the directions in which data varies most. `PCAFit` centres each column and takes the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix; `ExplainedVariance` gives each direction's share of the total and `PCATransform` projects the rows onto the first k of them. Here six students have marks in mathematics, physics, literature and history.

matrix-guide-pca.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func main:
    mut scores := build(6, 4, "18 17 12 11 15 16 10 9 9 10 18 17 12 11 15 16 19 18 9 10 8 9 19 18")
    mut fit := matrix.PCAFit(scores)
    mut share := matrix.ExplainedVariance(fit)
    println "variance explained", matrix.ToStringPrec(share, 3)
    mut first := matrix.SubMatrix(fit.components, 0, 0, 4, 1)
    println "first direction", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Transpose(first), 2)
    mut flat := matrix.PCATransform(fit, scores, 1)
    println "students on it", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Transpose(flat), 1)
end
```

Output:

```text
variance explained 0.962 0.029 0.009 0.001
first direction  0.55  0.48 -0.50 -0.47
students on it  6.2  6.0 -7.9 -3.8  9.2 -9.9
```

One direction explains 96% of the differences, so four marks per student are almost one number. Its weights are positive for the two sciences and negative for the two humanities: it measures "science rather than humanities", and the projection places each student on that scale. The sign of a direction is arbitrary, so another library may print the same numbers with every sign flipped. `PCAFromSVD` gives the same result through the singular value decomposition, which is more accurate when columns are nearly dependent.

## Singular systems and rounding error

When one equation is a multiple of another, the matrix is singular: `IsSingular` says so and `Solve` gives an empty 0x0 result. `IsConsistent` tells you whether there are infinitely many answers or none, and `SolveGeneral` returns one of them. Some matrices are not singular but nearly so, and `Cond2` measures how much they magnify rounding error; the Hilbert matrix is the classic example. That is why results are compared with `AllClose` and a tolerance, never exactly.

matrix-guide-pitfalls.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func main:
    mut twice := build(2, 2, "1 2 2 4")
    mut b := build(2, 1, "3 6")
    println "singular", matrix.IsSingular(twice), "rank", matrix.RankExact(twice)
    println "Solve gives", matrix.ShapeString(matrix.Solve(twice, b))
    println "consistent", matrix.IsConsistent(twice, b)
    println "one solution", matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Transpose(matrix.SolveGeneral(twice, b)), 2)

    mut h := matrix.Hilbert(8)
    println "Hilbert(8) is badly conditioned:", matrix.Cond2(h) > 1000000000.0
    mut x := matrix.Ones(8, 1)
    mut hb := matrix.MatMul(h, x)
    mut back := matrix.Solve(h, hb)
    println "exact match", matrix.AllClose(back, x, 0.0), "close", matrix.AllClose(back, x, 0.0001)

    mut tenth := build(1, 2, "0.1 0.2")
    mut three := matrix.Scale(tenth, 3.0)
    mut expected := build(1, 2, "0.3 0.6")
    println "0.1 * 3 == 0.3 exactly:", matrix.AllClose(three, expected, 0.0), "within MAT_TOL:", matrix.AllClose(three, expected, matrix.MAT_TOL)
end
```

Output:

```text
singular true rank 1
Solve gives 0x0
consistent true
one solution 3.00 0.00
Hilbert(8) is badly conditioned: true
exact match false close true
0.1 * 3 == 0.3 exactly: false within MAT_TOL: true
```

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Solve `A x = b` once | `Solve` |
| The same `A` with many `b` | `Decompose`, then `LUSolve` |
| More equations than unknowns | `LeastSquares`, `LinearRegression` |
| No unique solution | `IsConsistent`, `SolveGeneral` |
| How trustworthy is the answer | `Cond2`, `Residual` |
| Compare results | `AllClose` with a tolerance such as `MAT_TOL` |

matrix-Stats.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

end

func main:
    show("Hilbert", matrix.Hilbert(2))
    show("Hilbert times its inverse", matrix.MatMul(matrix.Hilbert(3), matrix.HilbertInverse(3)))
    show("Vandermonde", matrix.Vandermonde(build(3, 1, "1 2 3"), 3))
    show("Toeplitz", matrix.Toeplitz(build(3, 1, "1 2 3"), build(1, 3, "1 4 5")))
    show("Hankel", matrix.Hankel(build(3, 1, "1 2 3"), build(1, 3, "3 4 5")))
    show("Circulant", matrix.Circulant(build(1, 3, "1 2 3")))
    show("Companion", matrix.Companion(build(1, 3, "1 -3 2")))
    show("Pascal", matrix.Pascal(3))
    show("Rotation2D", matrix.Rotation2D(0.0))
    show("Rotation3D", matrix.Rotation3D(2, 0.0))
    show("Householder", matrix.Householder(build(2, 1, "1 0")))
    show("Givens", matrix.Givens(2, 0, 1, 0.0))
    show("Permutation", matrix.Permutation(build(1, 3, "2 0 1")))

    mut rng := matrix.NewRng(7)
    println rng.next_bits() > 0, rng.next_float() < 1.0, rng.next_normal() < 10.0
    mut random := matrix.Random(2, 3, -1.0, 1.0, 5)
    println matrix.ShapeString(random), matrix.Min(random) >= -1.0, matrix.Max(random) < 1.0, matrix.AllClose(random, matrix.Random(2, 3, -1.0, 1.0, 5), 0.0)
    println matrix.ShapeString(matrix.RandomNormal(2, 2, 1))
    println matrix.IsSymmetric(matrix.RandomSymmetric(3, 1), 0.000001), matrix.IsPositiveDefinite(matrix.RandomSPD(3, 1), 0.000001), matrix.IsOrthogonal(matrix.RandomOrthogonal(3, 1), 0.00001)

    mut data := build(4, 2, "1 2 2 4 3 6 4 8")
    show("CenterColumns", matrix.CenterColumns(data))
    show("ColumnMeans", matrix.ColumnMeans(data))
    show("ColumnStds", matrix.ColumnStds(data, false))
    show("Standardize", matrix.Standardize(data, false))
    show("Covariance", matrix.Covariance(data, true))
    show("Correlation", matrix.Correlation(data))
    mut pca := matrix.PCAFit(data)
    println matrix.ShapeString(pca.components), matrix.ShapeString(pca.variances), matrix.ShapeString(pca.center)
    show("ExplainedVariance", matrix.ExplainedVariance(pca))
    show("PCATransform", matrix.Abs(matrix.PCATransform(pca, data, 1)))
    pca.free()
    mut pca2 := matrix.PCAFromSVD(data)
    show("from the SVD", matrix.ExplainedVariance(pca2))
    pca2.free()

    mut x := build(4, 1, "1 2 3 4")
    mut y := build(4, 1, "3 5 7 9")
    coefficients := matrix.LinearRegression(x, y)
    show("LinearRegression", coefficients)
    println r(matrix.RSquared(y, y))
end
```

### `Eigen`

```salam
struct Eigen
```

The eigenvalues of a general matrix.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n` | `int = 0` | The size. |
| `re` | `Matrix` | The real part. |
| `im` | `Matrix` | The imaginary part. |

matrix-Eigen.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func show(name: str, m &: matrix.Matrix):
    println name, matrix.ToRepr(matrix.Chop(m, 0.000001), 3)
end

func r(value: f64): str:
    ret matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Full(1, 1, value), 3)
end

func main:
    mut symmetric := build(2, 2, "2 1 1 2")
    mut decomposition := matrix.EigSym(symmetric)
    println decomposition.ok, decomposition.n, decomposition.sweeps >= 0
    show("values", decomposition.values)
    show("EigReconstruct", matrix.EigReconstruct(decomposition))
    decomposition.free()
    show("EigValsSym", matrix.EigValsSym(symmetric))
    println r(matrix.SpectralRadiusSym(symmetric))
    show("PowSym", matrix.PowSym(symmetric, 2.0))
    show("SqrtSym squared", matrix.MatMul(matrix.SqrtSym(symmetric), matrix.SqrtSym(symmetric)))

    mut general := build(2, 2, "0 1 -2 -3")
    mut eigen := matrix.EigVals(general)
    println eigen.ok, eigen.n, matrix.ToRepr(eigen.re, 3), matrix.ToRepr(eigen.im, 3), eigen.iterations >= 0
    eigen.free()
    mut rotation := build(2, 2, "0 -1 1 0")
    mut complex := matrix.EigValsAuto(rotation)
    show("imaginary", complex.im)
    println r(matrix.SpectralRadius(general))
    show("Hessenberg", matrix.Hessenberg(build(3, 3, "1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 10")))
    show("CharPoly", matrix.CharPoly(general))
    mut vector := matrix.EigVecFor(symmetric, 3.0, 50)
    show("EigVecFor", matrix.Abs(vector))
    mut power := matrix.PowerIteration(symmetric, 100)
    mut dominant := matrix.SubMatrix(power, 0, 0, 2, 1)
    println r(power.at(2, 0)), r(matrix.Rayleigh(symmetric, dominant)), r(matrix.ShiftedInverseIteration(symmetric, 0.9, 50))

    mut m := build(3, 2, "3 0 0 4 0 0")
    mut svd := matrix.SVDecompose(m)
    println svd.ok, matrix.ShapeString(svd.u), matrix.ShapeString(svd.v)
    show("singular values", svd.s)
    svd.free()
    show("SingularValues", matrix.SingularValues(m))
    println matrix.MatrixRank(m, 0.000001)
    show("PseudoInverse", matrix.PseudoInverse(m, 0.000001))
    show("NullSpace", matrix.NullSpace(build(2, 2, "1 1 1 1"), 0.000001))
    show("ColumnSpace", matrix.Abs(matrix.ColumnSpace(build(2, 2, "1 1 1 1"), 0.000001)))
    show("LowRankApprox", matrix.LowRankApprox(build(2, 2, "3 0 0 1"), 1))

    tol := 0.000001
    identity := matrix.Eye(3)
    println matrix.IsSquare(identity), matrix.AllClose(identity, identity, tol), matrix.IsZero(matrix.Zeros(2, 2), tol), matrix.IsIdentity(identity, tol)
    println matrix.IsSymmetric(symmetric, tol), matrix.IsSkewSymmetric(rotation, tol), matrix.IsDiagonal(identity, tol)
    println matrix.IsUpperTriangular(build(2, 2, "1 2 0 3"), tol), matrix.IsLowerTriangular(build(2, 2, "1 0 2 3"), tol)
    tridiagonal := build(3, 3, "2 1 0 1 2 1 0 1 2")
    println matrix.IsBanded(tridiagonal, 1, 1, tol), matrix.LowerBandwidth(tridiagonal, tol), matrix.UpperBandwidth(tridiagonal, tol)
    println matrix.IsOrthogonal(rotation, tol), matrix.IsNormal(symmetric, tol), matrix.IsIdempotent(build(2, 2, "1 0 0 0"), tol)
    println matrix.IsInvolutory(build(2, 2, "0 1 1 0"), tol), matrix.IsNilpotent(build(2, 2, "0 1 0 0"), tol)
    println matrix.IsPositiveDefinite(symmetric, tol), matrix.IsPositiveSemiDefinite(build(2, 2, "1 1 1 1"), tol)
    println matrix.IsSingular(build(2, 2, "1 2 2 4")), matrix.IsInvertible(symmetric)
    probability := build(2, 2, "0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5")
    println matrix.IsRowStochastic(probability, tol), matrix.IsColStochastic(probability, tol), matrix.IsDoublyStochastic(probability, tol)
    println matrix.IsPermutation(build(2, 2, "0 1 1 0"), tol), matrix.IsToeplitz(tridiagonal, tol), matrix.IsHankel(build(2, 2, "1 2 2 3"), tol)
    println r(matrix.Density(tridiagonal))
end
```

### `LU`

```salam
struct LU
```

The lower upper decomposition with row swaps.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n` | `int = 0` | The size. |
| `lu` | `Matrix` | L and U in one matrix. |
| `piv` | `Vector` | The row swaps. |
| `sign` | `int = 1` | The sign of the permutation. |
| `singular` | `bool = false` | The matrix is singular. |

matrix-Solve.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func show(name: str, m &: matrix.Matrix):
    println name, matrix.ToRepr(matrix.Chop(m, 0.000001), 3)
end

func r(value: f64): str:
    ret matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Full(1, 1, value), 3)
end

func main:
    mut a := build(3, 3, "4 1 0 1 3 1 0 1 2")
    mut b := build(3, 1, "1 2 3")
    println r(matrix.Det(a)), r(matrix.LogAbsDet(a))
    show("Solve", matrix.Solve(a, b))
    show("SolveVec", matrix.SolveVec(a, b))
    mut lu := matrix.Decompose(a)
    println lu.n, lu.piv.len(), lu.sign, lu.singular, matrix.ShapeString(lu.lu)
    show("LUSolve", matrix.LUSolve(lu, b))
    lu.free()
    mut inverse := matrix.Inverse(a)
    show("a times its inverse", matrix.MatMul(a, inverse))
    show("Adjugate", matrix.Adjugate(build(2, 2, "1 2 3 4")))
    show("Residual", matrix.Residual(a, matrix.Solve(a, b), b))

    mut qr := matrix.QRDecompose(a)
    println qr.m, qr.n, qr.full_rank, matrix.ShapeString(qr.qr), matrix.ShapeString(qr.rdiag)
    show("Q times R", matrix.MatMul(matrix.QRGetQ(qr), matrix.QRGetR(qr)))
    show("QRSolve", matrix.QRSolve(qr, b))
    qr.free()
    mut points := build(4, 2, "1 0 1 1 1 2 1 3")
    mut values := build(4, 1, "1 3 5 7")
    show("LeastSquares", matrix.LeastSquares(points, values))
    show("Orthonormalize", matrix.Gram(matrix.Orthonormalize(points)))

    show("Cholesky", matrix.Cholesky(a))
    show("SolveSPD", matrix.SolveSPD(a, b))
    show("CholeskySolve", matrix.CholeskySolve(matrix.Cholesky(a), b))
    show("InverseSPD", matrix.MatMul(a, matrix.InverseSPD(a)))
    println r(matrix.DetSPD(a)), r(matrix.LogDetSPD(a))
    mut ldl := matrix.LDLDecompose(a)
    println ldl.ok, ldl.n, matrix.ShapeString(ldl.l), matrix.ShapeString(ldl.d)
    show("LDLSolve", matrix.LDLSolve(ldl, b))
    ldl.free()
    show("Inertia", matrix.Inertia(build(2, 2, "1 0 0 -1")))

    mut singular := build(3, 3, "1 2 3 2 4 6 1 1 1")
    show("RowEchelon", matrix.RowEchelon(singular))
    show("RREF", matrix.RREF(singular))
    show("PivotColumns", matrix.PivotColumns(singular))
    println matrix.RankExact(singular), matrix.Nullity(singular)
    show("NullSpaceExact", matrix.NullSpaceExact(singular))
    show("ColumnSpaceExact", matrix.ColumnSpaceExact(singular))
    mut right := build(3, 1, "6 12 3")
    println matrix.IsConsistent(singular, right), matrix.IsConsistent(singular, build(3, 1, "1 3 3"))
    show("SolveGeneral", matrix.SolveGeneral(singular, right))

    println matrix.IsDiagonallyDominant(a)
    mut jacobi := matrix.SolveJacobi(a, b, 200, 0.00000001)
    println jacobi.converged, jacobi.iterations > 0, jacobi.residual < 0.0001
    show("Jacobi", jacobi.x)
    jacobi.free()
    each method in [1, 2, 3]:
        mut result := matrix.SolveGaussSeidel(a, b, 200, 0.00000001)
        if method == 2:
            result = matrix.SolveSOR(a, b, 1.2, 200, 0.00000001)
        else method == 3:
            result = matrix.SolveCG(a, b, 200, 0.00000001)
        end
        show("iterative", result.x)
        result.free()
    end

    mut d := build(2, 2, "1 0 0 2")
    show("Expm", matrix.Expm(matrix.Zeros(2, 2)))
    show("Sqrtm", matrix.Sqrtm(build(2, 2, "4 0 0 9")))
    show("MatrixSign", matrix.MatrixSign(build(2, 2, "2 0 0 -3")))
    show("PolyEval", matrix.PolyEval(d, build(1, 3, "1 0 1")))
    show("CayleyHamilton", matrix.CayleyHamilton(d))
    show("LogmSym", matrix.LogmSym(matrix.Eye(2)))
end
```

matrix-Create.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func main:
    mut a := build(2, 3, "1 2 3 4 5 6")
    matrix.Print(a)
    println matrix.ShapeString(a), a.rows, a.cols, a.a.len(), a.count(), a.min_dim(), a.is_square(), a.is_empty()
    println a.at(1, 2), a.flat(4)
    a.set(0, 0, 10.0)
    a.add_at(0, 1, 0.5)
    a.mul_at(0, 2, 2.0)
    a.set_flat(5, -1.0)
    matrix.PrintPrec(a, 1)
    matrix.PrintLabeled("a", a)

    println matrix.ToString(matrix.Zeros(1, 2)), matrix.ToString(matrix.Ones(1, 2)), matrix.ToString(matrix.Full(1, 2, 7.0))
    println matrix.ToString(matrix.Eye(2))
    println matrix.ToString(matrix.EyeOffset(2, 3, 1))
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    data.push(1.0)
    data.push(2.0)
    println matrix.ShapeString(matrix.RowVector(data)), matrix.ShapeString(matrix.ColVector(data)), matrix.ToString(matrix.Diag(data))
    mut b := matrix.Clone(a)
    matrix.SetAll(b, 0.0)
    matrix.CopyInto(b, a)
    println b.same_shape(a), b.at(0, 0)
    println matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.25), 2)
    println matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Linspace(0.0, 1.0, 5), 2)
    println matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Logspace(0.0, 2.0, 3, 10.0), 1)
    println matrix.ToCSV(a, 1)
    println matrix.ToRepr(a, 1)
    println matrix.MAT_EPS > 0.0, matrix.MAT_TOL > 0.0, matrix.MAT_INF > 1000.0
    matrix.Free(b)
    a.free()
end
```

matrix-Math.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func show(name: str, m &: matrix.Matrix):
    println name, matrix.ToRepr(m, 1)
end

func r(value: f64): str:
    ret matrix.ToStringPrec(matrix.Full(1, 1, value), 3)
end

func main:
    mut a := build(2, 2, "1 2 3 4")
    mut b := build(2, 2, "0 1 1 0")
    mut row := build(1, 2, "10 20")
    mut col := build(2, 1, "1 -1")
    show("Transpose", matrix.Transpose(a))
    show("MatMul", matrix.MatMul(a, b))
    mut out := matrix.Zeros(2, 2)
    println matrix.TransposeInto(a, out), matrix.MatMulInto(a, b, out)
    show("into", out)
    show("TransposeMul", matrix.TransposeMul(a, b))
    show("MulTranspose", matrix.MulTranspose(a, b))
    show("Gram", matrix.Gram(a))
    show("MatVec", matrix.MatVec(a, col))
    show("VecMat", matrix.VecMat(row, a))
    println matrix.Dot(col, col), matrix.Trace(a)
    show("Outer", matrix.Outer(col, col))
    show("Kron", matrix.Kron(matrix.Eye(2), matrix.Full(1, 2, 3.0)))
    show("MatPow", matrix.MatPow(a, 2))
    show("Cross3", matrix.Cross3(build(3, 1, "1 0 0"), build(3, 1, "0 1 0")))

    show("Add", matrix.Add(a, b))
    show("Sub", matrix.Sub(a, b))
    show("MulElem", matrix.MulElem(a, b))
    show("DivElem", matrix.DivElem(a, a))
    show("Neg", matrix.Neg(a))
    show("with scalars", matrix.AddScalar(matrix.SubScalar(matrix.Scale(matrix.DivScalar(a, 2.0), 4.0), 1.0), 1.0))
    mut c := matrix.Clone(a)
    matrix.AddInPlace(c, b)
    matrix.SubInPlace(c, b)
    matrix.MulElemInPlace(c, a)
    matrix.ScaleInPlace(c, 0.5)
    matrix.AddScalarInPlace(c, 1.0)
    matrix.NegInPlace(c)
    matrix.AddScaled(c, a, 2.0)
    show("in place", c)
```

### `HStack`

```salam
func HStack(x &: Matrix, y &: Matrix): Matrix
```

Two matrices side by side.

matrix-Shape.salam

```salam
import matrix

func build(rows: int, cols: int, numbers: str): matrix.Matrix:
    mut data := Vector {} as Vector<f64>
    each number in numbers.split(" "):
        data.push(number.to_float())
    end
    ret matrix.FromArray(rows, cols, data)
end

func show(name: str, m &: matrix.Matrix):
    println name, matrix.ToRepr(m, 1)
end

func main:
    mut a := build(2, 3, "1 2 3 4 5 6")
    mut square := build(3, 3, "1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9")
    show("Reshape", matrix.Reshape(a, 3, 2))
    show("Flatten", matrix.Flatten(a))
    show("FlattenCol", matrix.FlattenCol(a))
    mut row := matrix.Row(a, 1)
    mut col := matrix.Col(a, 2)
    show("Row", row)
    show("Col", col)
    mut b := matrix.Clone(a)
    matrix.SetRow(b, 0, row)
    matrix.SetCol(b, 0, col)
    show("SetRow and SetCol", b)
    show("SubMatrix", matrix.SubMatrix(square, 1, 1, 2, 2))
    show("Minor", matrix.Minor(square, 0, 0))
    show("DeleteRow", matrix.DeleteRow(square, 1))
    show("DeleteCol", matrix.DeleteCol(square, 1))
    show("InsertRow", matrix.InsertRow(a, 1, matrix.Row(a, 0)))
    show("InsertCol", matrix.InsertCol(a, 0, matrix.Col(a, 2)))
    matrix.SwapRows(b, 0, 1)
    matrix.SwapCols(b, 0, 2)
    show("swapped", b)
    show("Diagonal", matrix.Diagonal(square))
    show("DiagonalOffset", matrix.DiagonalOffset(square, 1))
    mut c := matrix.Clone(square)
    matrix.SetDiagonal(c, matrix.Ones(3, 1))
    matrix.ShiftDiagonal(c, 10.0)
    show("new diagonal", matrix.Diagonal(c))
    show("HStack", matrix.HStack(a, a))
    show("VStack", matrix.VStack(a, a))
    show("Augment", matrix.Augment(square, matrix.Eye(3)))
    show("BlockDiag", matrix.BlockDiag(matrix.Eye(1), matrix.Full(1, 1, 2.0)))
    show("Triu", matrix.Triu(square, 0))
    show("Tril", matrix.Tril(square, -1))
    show("SymmetrizeUpper", matrix.SymmetrizeUpper(square))
    show("SymPart", matrix.SymPart(square))
    show("SkewPart", matrix.SkewPart(square))
    show("FlipVertical", matrix.FlipVertical(a))
    show("FlipHorizontal", matrix.FlipHorizontal(a))
    show("Rot90", matrix.Rot90(a, 1))
    show("Roll", matrix.Roll(a, 0, 1))
    show("Tile", matrix.Tile(matrix.Eye(1), 2, 2))
    show("Pad", matrix.Pad(matrix.Eye(1), 1, 0, 0, 1, 9.0))
end
```

# image

https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/std/image/

Reading, editing and saving images, and writing text on them.

This package works with images without any outside library: it reads and writes PNG, JPEG and BMP. It also reads and writes WebP, both lossy and lossless. From a GIF it reads the first frame, and it saves an image in a GIF with at most 256 colors. `Open` and `Save` work the format out from the content or the extension. Drawing, resizing, cropping, rotating and filters such as blurring and sharpening are all there.

For text, read a TrueType font with `LoadFont` and write with `DrawTextStyled`; Persian and Arabic text is shaped and laid out right to left on its own. Use this package for thumbnails, generated cards and charts, watermarks and simple image checks. For computer vision (edges, contours, feature matching) see opencv, and to draw in a browser page, web/canvas.

### Things to know

- Pixels are 8 bit RGBA in memory. Every image owns that memory; release it with `Free`.

- `Save` picks the format from the extension and returns false for one it does not know. It uses quality 90; `SaveQuality` takes your own.

- JPEG has no transparency: transparent pixels are laid on white before saving. WebP at quality 100 is lossless, below that lossy.

- GIF reading gives only the first frame of an animation, and saving reduces the image to 256 colors.

- Persian shaping uses the Arabic presentation forms of the font, so the font must contain them. `FindArabicFont` looks for an installed one that does (or the file in `$SALAM_FONT_ARABIC`).

## Thumbnails and fixed-size cards

An upload form usually needs the same picture in several sizes. `Thumbnail` shrinks the image so that its longer side fits and keeps the shape. `ResizeFill` fills an exact box and cuts off what sticks out, which suits square avatars and product cards. `ResizeFit` keeps the whole picture inside the box and centers it, leaving empty bands at the sides. `Save` chooses the format from the extension, so the same code writes PNG, JPEG or WebP.

image-guide-thumbs.salam

```salam
import image

func size(img: image.Image): str:
    ret "" + img.width + "x" + img.height
end

func main:
    mut photo := image.New(1200, 800)
    defer image.Free(photo)
    image.FillHex(photo, "#3a6ea5")
    image.DrawCircleFilled(photo, 600, 400, 250, image.ParseHex("#f2c14e"))
    if image.Save(photo, "photo.jpg") == false:
        println "could not write photo.jpg"
        ret 1
    end

    mut ok := false
    mut loaded := image.Open("photo.jpg", ok)
    defer image.Free(loaded)
    println "opened:", ok, size(loaded)

    mut thumb := image.Thumbnail(loaded, 200)
    mut card := image.ResizeFill(loaded, 300, 300)
    mut banner := image.ResizeFit(loaded, 600, 200)
    defer image.Free(thumb)
    defer image.Free(card)
    defer image.Free(banner)
    println "thumbnail:", size(thumb)
    println "square card:", size(card)
    println "banner box:", size(banner)
    image.Save(thumb, "thumb.png")
    image.Save(card, "card.webp")
    println "formats:", image.FormatFromExt("thumb.png") == image.FormatPNG, image.FormatFromExt("card.webp") == image.FormatWebP
end
```

Output:

```text
opened: true 1200x800
thumbnail: 200x133
square card: 300x300
banner box: 600x200
formats: true true
```

`Open` reports through its `bool` argument whether the file could be read. Every image allocates memory for its pixels, so release each one with `Free`, as the `defer` lines do.

## Draw a simple chart

Lines, rectangles and circles plus the built-in pixel font are enough for a small bar chart, a badge or a placeholder image, with no font file needed. `LerpColor` mixes two colors, here to make taller bars darker, and `ParseHex` and `ToHexRGB` move between colors and CSS-style hex. `TextWidth` measures text before you draw it, so labels can be centered under their bars.

image-guide-chart.salam

```salam
import image

func main:
    sales := [12, 30, 22, 41, 35]
    labels := ["MON", "TUE", "WED", "THU", "FRI"]
    width := 260
    height := 160
    mut chart := image.NewFilled(width, height, image.RGB(255, 255, 255))
    defer image.Free(chart)
    low := image.ParseHex("#9ecae1")
    high := image.ParseHex("#08519c")
    image.DrawLine(chart, 20, 130, 250, 130, image.Gray(80))
    each i, value in sales:
        bar := value * 2
        x := 30 + i * 45
        shade := image.LerpColor(low, high, (value as f64) / 41.0)
        image.DrawRectFilled(chart, x, 130 - bar, 30, bar, shade)
        image.DrawText(chart, x + 15 - image.TextWidth(labels[i], 1) / 2, 136, labels[i], image.Gray(40), 1)
    end
    image.DrawText(chart, 20, 8, "SALES", image.Gray(20), 2)
    image.Save(chart, "chart.png")

    top := image.GetPixel(chart, 30 + 3 * 45 + 15, 130 - 41)
    println "tallest bar color:", image.ToHexRGB(top)
    println "first bar color:", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(chart, 45, 129))
    println "background:", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(chart, 5, 5))
    println "title width:", image.TextWidth("SALES", 2), "px"
end
```

Output:

```text
tallest bar color: #08519c
first bar color: #72a6cc
background: #ffffff
title width: 60 px
```

The pixel font has only capital English letters, digits and the signs `. , - : ! ?`; anything else, lower case letters included, is drawn as a blank. For Persian or any other script, and for smooth text at large sizes, load a TrueType font with `LoadFont` and use `DrawTextStyled`, which shapes Persian letters and lays them out right to left.

## Filters and measuring the difference

`Blurred` and `Sharpened` return new images; `Grayscale`, `Threshold`, `Brightness` and `Contrast` change the image in place. To compare two images, `MeanAbsError` gives the average difference per channel and `PSNR` the signal to noise ratio in decibels, where higher means more alike. The numbers show that sharpening a blurred image does not bring the original back: it makes the edges stronger, not correct.

image-guide-filters.salam

```salam
import image
import fmt

func main:
    mut base := image.New(64, 64)
    defer image.Free(base)
    image.Fill(base, image.RGB(30, 30, 30))
    image.DrawRectFilled(base, 16, 16, 32, 32, image.RGB(240, 240, 240))

    mut soft := image.Blurred(base, 3)
    mut crisp := image.Sharpened(soft, 1.0)
    defer image.Free(soft)
    defer image.Free(crisp)
    println "edge pixel, original:", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(base, 16, 32))
    println "edge pixel, blurred: ", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(soft, 16, 32))
    println "blur error:", fmt.FloatPrec(image.MeanAbsError(base, soft), 2), "PSNR", fmt.FloatPrec(image.PSNR(base, soft), 1), "dB"
    println "sharpened again:", fmt.FloatPrec(image.PSNR(base, crisp), 1), "dB, edge", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(crisp, 16, 32))

    mut gray := image.Clone(base)
    defer image.Free(gray)
    image.FillHex(gray, "#cc3344")
    image.Grayscale(gray)
    println "red after Grayscale:", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(gray, 0, 0)), "luminance", image.Luminance(image.ParseHex("#cc3344"))
    image.Threshold(gray, 128)
    println "after Threshold(128):", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(gray, 0, 0))
end
```

Output:

```text
edge pixel, original: #f0f0f0
edge pixel, blurred:  #969696
blur error: 10.94 PSNR 19.2 dB
sharpened again: 15.0 dB, edge #969696
red after Grayscale: #626262 luminance 98
after Threshold(128): #000000
```

`Grayscale` uses perceived brightness, the same value `Luminance` returns, so a strong red becomes a fairly dark gray. These measures are also handy in tests: render an image and check that its PSNR against a stored reference stays above a limit.

## A share card with Persian text

A link preview image is a fixed 1200 by 630 canvas with a title that must fit whatever its length. `DrawTextFitBox` finds the largest size up to a limit at which the text fits a share of the box, centers it and returns the size it chose. `TextWidthStyled` measures text first, here to right-align the address in the corner; the y coordinate of `DrawTextStyled` is the baseline.

image-guide-card.salam

```salam
import image
import os

func main:
    args := os.Args()
    mut path := image.FindArabicFont()
    if args.len() > 1:
        path = args.get(1)
    end
    mut ok := false
    font := image.LoadFont(path, ok)
    if not ok:
        println "no font with Persian letters; pass a .ttf path"
        ret 1
    end
    defer image.FreeFont(font)
    mut card := image.NewFilled(1200, 630, image.ParseHex("#1b4332"))
    defer image.Free(card)
    white := image.RGB(255, 255, 255)
    title := image.TextStyle { size = 72.0 }
    size := image.DrawTextFitBox(card, 80.0, 120.0, 1040.0, 260.0, "سلام ۰٫۶ منتشر شد: سریع‌تر و کوچک‌تر", white, font, title, 0.9, 96.0)
    println "title size:", size
    small := image.TextStyle { size = 36.0 }
    width := image.TextWidthStyled(font, "salamlang.ir", small)
    image.DrawTextStyled(card, 1120.0 - width, 560.0, "salamlang.ir", image.ParseHex("#95d5b2"), font, small)
    println "saved:", image.Save(card, "release-card.png")
end
```

The program takes a font path as its first argument and otherwise asks `FindArabicFont`, so it needs a font file and the site only compiles it. With Vazirmatn the title came out at about 61 pixels; the joined letters, the zero width non-joiner in `سریع‌تر` and the right to left order are all handled by the package.

## Watermark a photo

`Overlay` draws one image on top of another at a position, with an opacity from 0 to 1, and respects the transparency of the top image. Here the mark is a half transparent black box with white text, placed ten pixels from the bottom right corner.

image-guide-watermark.salam

```salam
import image

func main:
    mut photo := image.NewFilled(400, 300, image.ParseHex("#2d6a4f"))
    defer image.Free(photo)
    text := "MADE WITH SALAM"
    scale := 2
    mut mark := image.New(image.TextWidth(text, scale) + 8, image.FontHeight * scale + 8)
    defer image.Free(mark)
    image.Fill(mark, image.RGBA(0, 0, 0, 160))
    image.DrawText(mark, 4, 4, text, image.RGB(255, 255, 255), scale)
    println "mark size:", mark.width, "x", mark.height

    x := photo.width - mark.width - 10
    y := photo.height - mark.height - 10
    image.Overlay(photo, mark, x, y, 0.6)
    println "placed at", x, y
    println "untouched corner:", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(photo, 0, 0))
    println "under the mark:", image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(photo, x + 1, y + 1))
    image.Save(photo, "marked.png")
end
```

Output:

```text
mark size: 188 x 22
placed at 202 268
untouched corner: #2d6a4f
under the mark: #1c4231
```

| Job | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Read and write files | `Open`, `Save`, `SaveQuality` |
| Make smaller copies | `Thumbnail`, `ResizeFit`, `ResizeFill`, `Crop` |
| Draw shapes and simple text | `DrawRectFilled`, `DrawLine`, `DrawCircleFilled`, `DrawText` |
| Text with a real font, Persian too | `LoadFont`, `DrawTextStyled`, `DrawTextFitBox` |
| Adjust the look | `Blurred`, `Sharpened`, `Grayscale`, `Contrast` |
| Combine images | `Overlay` |
| Compare images | `PSNR`, `MeanAbsError`, `Diff` |

## Types

### `JPEGOptions`

```salam
struct JPEGOptions
```

Settings for the streaming JPEG writer and for `EncodeJPEGOptions` and `SaveJPEGOptions`: quality, chroma subsampling, the JFIF pixel density and an optional comment. The output is a baseline JPEG with the same coded data libjpeg writes for the same settings.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quality` | `int = 90` | The quality from 1 to 100, 90 by default; values outside that range are clamped. It scales the standard quantization tables the way libjpeg does. |
| `subsample` | `bool = true` | True (the default) stores the color at half width and half height (4:2:0), which makes the file smaller; false keeps full color resolution (4:4:4) for sharper color edges. |
| `density_unit` | `int = 0` | The JFIF density unit: 0 means the densities only give the pixel aspect ratio (the default), 1 is dots per inch and 2 is dots per centimeter. |
| `x_density` | `int = 1` | The horizontal density in `density_unit`, 1 by default; 300 with unit 1 marks a 300 DPI print. |
| `y_density` | `int = 1` | The vertical density in `density_unit`, 1 by default. |
| `comment` | `str = ""` | A text stored in a JPEG comment (COM) segment; empty (the default) writes no comment, and a comment of 65000 bytes or more is left out. |

image-JPEGStream.salam

```salam
import image
import compress
import os

func main:
    opts := image.JPEGOptions { quality = 80, subsample = true, density_unit = 1, x_density = 300, y_density = 300, comment = "made with Salam" }
    mut img := image.NewFilled(40, 24, image.RGB(30, 120, 200))
    image.DrawRectFilled(img, 10, 6, 20, 12, image.RGB(250, 200, 40))

    mut s := image.NewJPEGStream(40, 24, opts)
    println s.ok, s.mcu_w, s.mcu_h, s.mcus_x, s.mcu_rows
    mut top := image.Crop(img, 0, 0, 40, 16)
    image.JPEGStreamWrite(s, top)
    image.Free(top)
    println s.rows_written, s.mcu_row
    mut row := compress.NewByteBuf()
    repeat 8 in y:
        compress.BufReset(row)
        repeat 40 in x:
            c := image.GetPixel(img, x, 16 + y)
            compress.BufPush(row, c.r as int)
            compress.BufPush(row, c.g as int)
            compress.BufPush(row, c.b as int)
        end
        image.JPEGStreamWriteRow(s, row.data as u8*, 3)
    end
    compress.BufFree(row)
    println image.JPEGStreamFinish(s), s.rows_written
    println compress.BufGet(s.out, 0), compress.BufGet(s.out, 1), compress.BufGet(s.out, 13), compress.BufGet(s.out, 14) * 256 + compress.BufGet(s.out, 15)

    mut ok := false
    mut back := image.DecodeJPEG(s.out.data, s.out.len, ok)
    println ok, back.width, back.height
    image.Free(back)
    mut whole := image.EncodeJPEGOptions(img, opts)
    println compress.BufEquals(whole, s.out)
    compress.BufFree(whole)
    compress.BufFree(s.out)

    println image.SaveJPEGOptions(img, "card.jpg", image.JPEGOptions { quality = 95, subsample = false }), os.FileSize("card.jpg") > 0
    os.Remove("card.jpg")
    image.Free(img)
end
```

Output:

```text
true 16 16 3 2
16 1
true 24
255 216 1 300
true 40 24
true
true true
```

### `JPEGStream`

```salam
struct JPEGStream
```

A JPEG encoder that takes the picture a row at a time, so the input pixels never have to be in memory all at once: only one strip of 16 rows (8 without subsampling) is held. The encoded file itself still builds up in memory. Start it with `NewJPEGStream`, feed rows with `JPEGStreamWriteRow` or `JPEGStreamWrite`, then call `JPEGStreamFinish`; the file is in `out`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | `int = 0` | The picture width in pixels, 1 to 65535. |
| `height` | `int = 0` | The picture height in pixels, 1 to 65535. |
| `rows_written` | `int = 0` | How many rows have been fed so far; the picture is complete when it equals `height`. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The stream was set up and is still open. It is false for a bad size or when memory ran out, and `JPEGStreamFinish` sets it to false. |
| `out` | `compress.ByteBuf` | The encoded bytes: the headers right after `NewJPEGStream`, the whole file after `JPEGStreamFinish`. The caller frees it with `compress.BufFree`. |
| `hs` | `int = 2` | The horizontal sampling factor of the brightness channel: 2 with subsampling, 1 without. |
| `vs` | `int = 2` | The vertical sampling factor of the brightness channel: 2 with subsampling, 1 without. |
| `mcu_w` | `int = 16` | The width of one MCU (minimum coded unit) in pixels: 16 with subsampling, 8 without. |
| `mcu_h` | `int = 16` | The height of one MCU in pixels, which is also how many rows are buffered before a strip is encoded. |
| `mcus_x` | `int = 0` | How many MCUs make up one row of the picture. |
| `full_w` | `int = 0` | The row width rounded up to whole MCUs; the last pixel of each row is repeated to fill it. |
| `y_wib` | `int = 0` | The picture width in 8 by 8 brightness blocks, rounded up; blocks past it are padding. |
| `y_hib` | `int = 0` | The picture height in 8 by 8 brightness blocks, rounded up. |
| `c_w` | `int = 0` | The width of the color planes after subsampling, in samples. |
| `mcu_row` | `int = 0` | The number of the next strip (MCU row) to encode. |
| `mcu_rows` | `int = 0` | How many strips the whole picture has. |
| `buffered` | `int = 0` | How many rows of the current strip are waiting to be encoded. |
| `yb` | `void*` | Internal: the brightness (Y) samples of the current strip. |
| `cbb` | `void*` | Internal: the blue difference (Cb) samples of the current strip at full resolution. |
| `crb` | `void*` | Internal: the red difference (Cr) samples of the current strip at full resolution. |
| `cbd` | `void*` | Internal: the Cb samples of the current strip after subsampling. |
| `crd` | `void*` | Internal: the Cr samples of the current strip after subsampling. |
| `lq` | `void*` | Internal: the brightness quantization table, scaled for the quality. |
| `cq` | `void*` | Internal: the color quantization table, scaled for the quality. |
| `hc` | `void*` | Internal: the Huffman codes of the four standard tables. |
| `hl` | `void*` | Internal: the lengths of those Huffman codes. |
| `work` | `void*` | Internal: the 64 value block the DCT works in. |
| `acc` | `i64 = 0` | Internal: the bit accumulator of the entropy coder. |
| `nbits` | `int = 0` | Internal: how many bits are waiting in `acc`. |
| `dc_y` | `int = 0` | Internal: the last brightness DC value; each block stores only the difference from it. |
| `dc_cb` | `int = 0` | Internal: the last Cb DC value. |
| `dc_cr` | `int = 0` | Internal: the last Cr DC value. |

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `AreaResampler`

```salam
struct AreaResampler
```

A shrinker that averages the area under each new pixel, computing exactly what libgd's `gdImageCopyResampled` (PHP's `imagecopyresampled`) gives. Source rows go in one at a time and only a few output rows of sums are kept, so a picture that is still being made, or is too large to hold, can be shrunk on the way. Alpha passes through gd's 7 bit alpha, so it comes out in 128 steps.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src_w` | `int = 0` | The source width in pixels. |
| `src_h` | `int = 0` | The source height in pixels. |
| `dst_w` | `int = 0` | The output width in pixels. |
| `dst_h` | `int = 0` | The output height in pixels. |
| `out` | `Image` | The output RGBA image; each row is filled as soon as its last source row arrives, and rows not reached yet stay transparent. `AreaResamplerFree` leaves it, so the caller frees it with `Free`. |
| `ok` | `bool = false` | The resampler was set up; false when a size is zero or less or the output could not be made, and after `AreaResamplerFree`. |
| `next_row` | `int = 0` | The number of the next source row to push; it equals `src_h` when every row is in. |
| `x_start` | `void*` | Internal: for each output column, where its source spans start in `x_src` and `x_part`. |
| `x_count` | `void*` | Internal: how many source columns each output column covers. |
| `x_src` | `void*` | Internal: the source column of each span. |
| `x_part` | `void*` | Internal: how much of that source column the span covers, from 0 to 1. |
| `y_first` | `void*` | Internal: the first source row each output row covers. |
| `y_last` | `void*` | Internal: the last source row each output row covers. |
| `ring` | `int = 0` | Internal: how many output rows of sums are kept at once. |
| `acc` | `void*` | Internal: the running sums, seven 32 bit floats for every pixel of each kept output row. |

image-ResizeArea.salam

```salam
import image
import compress

func main:
    mut img := image.NewFilled(6, 4, image.Gray(0))
    image.DrawRectFilled(img, 3, 0, 3, 4, image.Gray(255))
    mut small := image.ResizeArea(img, 2, 1)
    println small.width, small.height, image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(small, 0, 0)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(small, 1, 0))
    mut dot := image.ResizeArea(img, 1, 1)
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(dot, 0, 0))
    image.Free(dot)
    image.Free(small)
    image.Free(img)

    mut r := image.NewAreaResampler(6, 4, 3, 2)
    println r.ok, r.dst_w, r.dst_h, r.next_row
    mut row := compress.NewByteBuf()
    repeat 4 in y:
        compress.BufReset(row)
        repeat 6 in x:
            v := x < 3 ? 0 : 255
            compress.BufPush(row, v)
            compress.BufPush(row, y * 60)
            compress.BufPush(row, 100)
        end
        image.AreaResamplerPushRow(r, row.data as u8*, 3)
    end
    compress.BufFree(row)
    image.AreaResamplerFree(r)
    println r.next_row, r.ok
    repeat 2 in y:
        println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(r.out, 0, y)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(r.out, 1, y)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(r.out, 2, y))
    end
    image.Free(r.out)
end
```

Output:

```text
2 1 #000000 #ffffff
#808080
true 3 2 0
4 false
#001e64 #801e64 #ff1e64
#009664 #809664 #ff9664
```

image-Draw.salam

```salam
import image
import os

func main:
    mut img := image.New(8, 6)
    println img.width, img.height, image.IsEmpty(img), image.InBounds(img, 7, 5), image.InBounds(img, 8, 0)
    image.Fill(img, image.RGB(255, 255, 255))
    image.FillHex(img, "#202040")
    image.SetPixel(img, 0, 0, image.RGB(255, 0, 0))
    image.BlendPixel(img, 1, 0, image.RGBA(255, 255, 255, 128))
    println image.ToHex(image.GetPixel(img, 0, 0)), image.ToHex(image.GetPixel(img, 1, 0)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(img, 2, 0))
    image.DrawLine(img, 0, 5, 7, 5, image.Gray(200))
    image.DrawRect(img, 1, 1, 4, 3, image.ParseHex("#ffcc00"))
    image.DrawRectFilled(img, 2, 2, 2, 1, image.ParseHex("#00ff00"))
    image.DrawCircle(img, 6, 2, 1, image.Gray(255))
    image.DrawCircleFilled(img, 6, 2, 0, image.Gray(10))
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(img, 3, 2)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(img, 4, 5))

    color := image.ParseHex("#336699")
    println color.r, color.g, color.b, color.a, image.Luminance(color)
    println image.Equals(color, image.RGB(51, 102, 153)), image.ToHex(image.Blend(color, image.RGBA(255, 255, 255, 0)))
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.LerpColor(image.Gray(0), image.Gray(200), 0.5))

    mut labelled := image.NewFilled(40, 10, image.Gray(0))
    image.DrawText(labelled, 1, 1, "SALAM", image.Gray(255), 1)
    println image.TextWidth("SALAM", 1), image.FontWidth, image.FontHeight

    dir := os.TempDir()
    println image.Save(img, dir + "/salam_en.png"), image.SavePNG(img, dir + "/salam2_en.png"), image.SaveBMP(img, dir + "/salam_en.bmp"), image.SaveJPEG(img, dir + "/salam_en.jpg", 90)
    println image.SaveQuality(img, dir + "/salam2_en.jpg", 50), image.SaveWebP(img, dir + "/salam_en.webp")
    mut ok := false
    read := image.Open(dir + "/salam_en.png", ok)
    println ok, read.width, image.Equals(image.GetPixel(read, 0, 0), image.GetPixel(img, 0, 0))
    png := image.OpenPNG(dir + "/salam2_en.png", ok)
    bmp := image.OpenBMP(dir + "/salam_en.bmp", ok)
    jpg := image.OpenJPEG(dir + "/salam_en.jpg", ok)
    println ok, png.width, bmp.height, jpg.width
    println image.FormatFromExt("a.jpeg") == image.FormatJPEG, image.FormatFromExt("a.png") == image.FormatPNG, image.FormatFromExt("a.txt") == image.FormatUnknown

    buf := image.EncodePNG(img)
    println image.DetectFormat(buf.data, buf.len) == image.FormatPNG, image.IsWebP(buf.data, buf.len)
    from_buf := image.DecodePNG(buf.data, buf.len, ok)
    generic := image.Decode(buf.data, buf.len, ok)
    println ok, from_buf.width, generic.height
    b := image.EncodeBMP(img)
    b2 := image.DecodeBMP(b.data, b.len, ok)
    j := image.EncodeJPEG(img, 80)
    j2 := image.DecodeJPEG(j.data, j.len, ok)
    println image.DetectFormat(b.data, b.len) == image.FormatBMP, image.DetectFormat(j.data, j.len) == image.FormatJPEG, b2.width, j2.width
    any := image.Encode(img, image.FormatBMP, 90)
    web := image.EncodeWebP(img)
    lossy := image.EncodeWebPQuality(img, 75)
    println any.len == b.len, web.len > 0, image.FormatWebP
    clear := image.NewFilled(1, 1, image.RGBA(0, 0, 0, 0))
    println image.ToHex(image.GetPixel(image.FlattenAlpha(clear, image.Gray(255)), 0, 0))
    converted := image.Convert(img, image.FormatJPEG)
    println converted.width
    webp := image.DecodeWebP(web.data, web.len, ok)
    println ok, webp.width, image.Equals(image.GetPixel(webp, 1, 0), image.GetPixel(img, 1, 0))
    webp3 := image.DecodeWebP(lossy.data, lossy.len, ok)
    println ok, webp3.width, webp3.height
    webp2 := image.OpenWebP(dir + "/salam_en.webp", ok)
    println image.SaveGIF(img, dir + "/salam_en.gif"), image.FormatFromExt("a.gif") == image.FormatGIF
    gif := image.OpenGIF(dir + "/salam_en.gif", ok)
    g := image.EncodeGIF(img)
    gif2 := image.DecodeGIF(g.data, g.len, ok)
    println ok, gif.width, gif2.height, image.IsGIF(g.data, g.len), image.Equals(image.GetPixel(gif, 0, 0), image.GetPixel(img, 0, 0))
    println ok, webp2.height
    mut copy := image.Clone(img)
    image.Free(copy)
    image.Free(img)
end
```

### `Histogram`

```salam
struct Histogram
```

A histogram: how many pixels have each value from 0 to 255.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `r` | `void*` | The red histogram. |
| `g` | `void*` | The green histogram. |
| `b` | `void*` | The blue histogram. |
| `luma` | `void*` | The brightness histogram. |

image-Edit.salam

```salam
import image

func size(name: str, img: image.Image):
    println name, "" + img.width + "x" + img.height
end

func main:
    mut img := image.NewFilled(8, 4, image.Gray(100))
    image.SetPixel(img, 0, 0, image.RGB(255, 0, 0))
    size("nearest", image.ResizeNearestNeighbor(img, 4, 2))
    size("bilinear", image.ResizeBilinearFilter(img, 16, 8))
    size("resize", image.Resize(img, 2, 2, image.ResizeBilinear))
    size("near", image.Resize(img, 2, 2, image.ResizeNearest))
    size("scale", image.Scale(img, 0.5))
    size("crop", image.Crop(img, 2, 1, 3, 2))
    clockwise := image.RotateCW(img)
    size("clockwise", clockwise)
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(clockwise, 3, 0))
    size("counterclockwise", image.RotateCCW(img))
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(image.Rotate180(img), 7, 3))
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(image.FlipHorizontal(img), 7, 0)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(image.FlipVertical(img), 0, 3))
    size("fit", image.ResizeFit(img, 4, 4))
    size("fill", image.ResizeFill(img, 4, 4))
    size("thumbnail", image.Thumbnail(img, 2))

    mut c := image.NewFilled(2, 1, image.RGB(200, 100, 50))
    image.Grayscale(c)
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(c, 0, 0))
    image.Invert(c)
    image.Brightness(c, 10)
    image.Contrast(c, 1.5)
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(c, 0, 0))
    image.Threshold(c, 128)
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(c, 0, 0))
    mut dot := image.NewFilled(5, 5, image.Gray(0))
    image.SetPixel(dot, 2, 2, image.Gray(255))
    blurred := image.Blurred(dot, 1)
    println image.GetPixel(blurred, 2, 2).r < 255, image.GetPixel(blurred, 1, 2).r > 0
    println image.GetPixel(image.Sharpened(dot, 1.0), 2, 2).r
    mut base := image.NewFilled(2, 2, image.Gray(0))
    image.Overlay(base, image.NewFilled(1, 1, image.Gray(200)), 1, 1, 0.5)
    println image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(base, 1, 1)), image.ToHexRGB(image.GetPixel(base, 0, 0))

    mut hist := image.ComputeHistogram(dot)
    println image.HistogramGet(hist.luma, 0), image.HistogramGet(hist.luma, 255), image.HistogramGet(hist.r, 255), image.HistogramGet(hist.g, 0), image.HistogramGet(hist.b, 0)
    image.HistogramFree(hist)
    black := image.NewFilled(5, 5, image.Gray(0))
    diff := image.Diff(dot, black)
    println image.GetPixel(diff, 2, 2).r, image.GetPixel(diff, 0, 0).r
    println (image.MeanAbsError(dot, black) * 100.0 + 0.5) as i64, (image.PSNR(dot, black) + 0.5) as i64
end
```

Output:

```text

bilinear 16x8
resize 2x2
near 2x2
scale 4x2
crop 3x2
clockwise 4x8
#ff0000
counterclockwise 4x8
#ff0000
#ff0000 #ff0000

fill 4x4
thumbnail 2x1
```

### `TextStyle`

```salam
struct TextStyle
```

A text style.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `f64 = 16` | The size in pixels. |
| `rotate` | `f64 = 0` | The rotation in degrees. |
| `skew` | `f64 = 0` | The skew. |
| `tracking` | `f64 = 0` | The space added between the characters. |

| `dir` | `int = 0` | The direction, one of the `TextDir...` constants. |

image-Font.salam

```salam
import image
import io

func main:
    println image.FindSystemFont(), image.FindArabicFont()
    mut ok := false
    mut font := image.LoadSystemFont(ok)
    if not ok:
        font = image.LoadFont("Vazirmatn-Regular.ttf", ok)
    end
    if not ok:
        println "no font was found"
        ret
    end
    println image.FontValid(font), image.UnitsPerEm(font), image.NumGlyphs(font)
    size := 32.0
    println image.ScaleFactor(font, size), image.AscentPixels(font, size), image.DescentPixels(font, size), image.LineHeightPixels(font, size)
    a := image.GlyphIndex(font, 65)
    v := image.GlyphIndex(font, 86)
    println image.GlyphAdvance(font, a), image.KernAdvance(font, a, v), image.GlyphHasOutline(font, a)
    mut x0 := 0
    mut y0 := 0
    mut x1 := 0
    mut y1 := 0
    println image.GlyphBox(font, a, x0, y0, x1, y1), x1 - x0, y1 - y0

    mut img := image.NewFilled(400, 120, image.Gray(255))
    black := image.Gray(0)
    _ := image.DrawTextTTF(img, 10.0, 40.0, "Salam", black, font, size)
    println image.TextWidthTTF(font, "Salam", size)
    style := image.TextStyle { size = 28.0, tracking = 1.0, kern = true, dir = image.TextDirAuto, shape = true }
    _ := image.DrawTextStyled(img, 10.0, 80.0, "سلام دنیا", black, font, style)
    println image.TextWidthStyled(font, "سلام دنیا", style), image.TextInkWidth(font, "سلام", style), image.TextInkHeight(font, "سلام", style)
    mut width := 0.0
    mut height := 0.0
    println image.TextInkSize(font, "سلام", style, width, height), width, height
    mut a0 := 0.0
    mut b0 := 0.0
    mut a1 := 0.0
    mut b1 := 0.0
    println image.TextBounds(font, "سلام", style, a0, b0, a1, b1)
    println image.FitSizeToWidth(font, "سلام", style, 200.0, 96.0), image.FitSizeToBox(font, "سلام", style, 200.0, 50.0, 96.0)
    _ := image.DrawGlyphStyled(img, a, 300.0, 40.0, black, font, style)
    _ := image.DrawCodepointStyled(img, 1600, 340.0, 40.0, black, font, style)
    _ := image.DrawTextCentered(img, 200.0, 60.0, "middle", black, font, style)
    _ := image.DrawTextCenteredIn(img, "middle", black, font, style)
    _ := image.DrawTextInBox(img, 0.0, 0.0, 200.0, 60.0, "box", black, font, style, image.TextAlignRight, image.TextVAlignMiddle)
    _ := image.DrawTextFitBox(img, 0.0, 60.0, 200.0, 60.0, "fit", black, font, style, 0.8, 64.0)
    _ := image.DrawTextFitImage(img, "سلام", black, font, style, 0.9, 120.0)
    println image.TextAlignLeft, image.TextAlignCenter, image.TextVAlignTop, image.TextVAlignBottom, image.TextVAlignBaseline
    _ := image.Save(img, "salam-text-en.png")

    data := io.ReadFile("Vazirmatn-Regular.ttf")
    mut f2 := image.ParseFont(data as void*, data.len(), ok)
    mut f3 := image.ParseFontIndex(data as void*, data.len(), 0, ok)
    mut f4 := image.LoadFontIndex("NotoSansCJK.ttc", 0, ok)
    println image.IsCFFFont(data as void*, data.len())
    image.FreeFont(f2)
    image.FreeFont(f3)
    image.FreeFont(f4)
    image.FreeFont(font)
    image.Free(img)
end
```

### `TextDirAuto`

```salam
const TextDirAuto: i32 = 0
```

Text direction: automatic, from the first letter.

image-Bidi.salam

```salam
import image

func main:
    println image.IsRTLText("سلام"), image.IsRTLText("hello")
    println image.BaseDirection("سلام hello") == image.TextDirRTL, image.BaseDirection("hello سلام") == image.TextDirLTR
    println image.TextDirAuto
    visual := image.ToVisualOrder("abc", image.TextDirLTR)
    println visual
    shaped := image.ShapeArabic("سلام")
    println shaped.len() > 0, shaped != "سلام"
    println image.ToVisualOrder("سلام", image.TextDirRTL) != "سلام"
end
```

Output:

```text
true false
true true
0
abc
true true
true
```

### `DecodePNG`

```salam
func DecodePNG(p: void*, n: int, ok &: bool): Image
```

Reads a PNG from bytes: every bit depth from 1 to 16, palette and gray images, tRNS transparency and interlaced PNG. 16 bits comes down to 8 by rounding. A file with a broken signature or CRC is refused.

### `NewJPEGStream`

```salam
func NewJPEGStream(width: int, height: int, opts: JPEGOptions): JPEGStream
```

Starts a streaming JPEG for a picture of width by height pixels and writes the headers into `out`. If a side is not between 1 and 65535 or memory runs out, `ok` is false and nothing else works on the stream.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `JPEGStreamWriteRow`

```salam
func JPEGStreamWriteRow(s &: JPEGStream, p: u8*, step: int)
```

Feeds the next row: `width` pixels whose red, green and blue bytes are at `p[0]`, `p[1]` and `p[2]`, `step` bytes apart (3 for RGB, 4 for RGBA). Alpha is ignored, so flatten transparency first with `FlattenAlpha`. A full strip is encoded at once; rows past the height are ignored.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `JPEGStreamWrite`

```salam
func JPEGStreamWrite(s &: JPEGStream, strip: Image)
```

Feeds every row of an RGBA image strip of any height. The strip must be as wide as the stream; otherwise nothing is written.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `JPEGStreamFinish`

```salam
func JPEGStreamFinish(s &: JPEGStream): bool
```

Encodes the last partial strip (repeating its last row), writes the end marker and frees the work buffers; the finished file is in `out`, which the caller frees with `compress.BufFree`. It returns false when fewer than `height` rows were fed, and the file is then incomplete.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `EncodeJPEGOptions`

```salam
func EncodeJPEGOptions(img: Image, opts: JPEGOptions): compress.ByteBuf
```

The image as JPEG bytes with options; the bytes are the same as feeding it through a `JPEGStream`. Alpha is ignored. For an empty image or a side larger than 65535 it returns an empty buffer. The caller frees the buffer with `compress.BufFree`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `SaveJPEGOptions`

```salam
func SaveJPEGOptions(img: Image, path: str, opts: JPEGOptions): bool
```

Saves the image as a JPEG file with options; it returns true when the writing worked.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-JPEGStream.salam

### `NewAreaResampler`

```salam
func NewAreaResampler(src_w: int, src_h: int, dst_w: int, dst_h: int): AreaResampler
```

Prepares a resampler from `src_w` by `src_h` to `dst_w` by `dst_h` and allocates the output image. If a size is zero or less, `ok` is false.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-ResizeArea.salam

### `AreaResamplerPushRow`

```salam
func AreaResamplerPushRow(r &: AreaResampler, p: u8*, step: int)
```

Feeds the next source row: `src_w` pixels whose red, green, blue and alpha bytes start at `p`, `step` bytes apart; with step 4 the fourth byte is alpha, with step 3 the row counts as opaque. Rows past `src_h` are ignored.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-ResizeArea.salam

### `AreaResamplerFree`

```salam
func AreaResamplerFree(r &: AreaResampler)
```

Frees the work tables and sets `ok` to false; the output image in `out` stays and is freed with `Free`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-ResizeArea.salam

### `ResizeArea`

```salam
func ResizeArea(img: Image, new_width: int, new_height: int): Image
```

Resizes the whole image by area averaging, with the same pixels as PHP's `imagecopyresampled`; best for shrinking photos without the aliasing of nearest neighbor. A size of zero or less gives an empty image, and an empty source gives a transparent image of the new size. The caller frees the result with `Free`.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-ResizeArea.salam

### `EncodeWebP`

```salam
func EncodeWebP(img: Image): compress.ByteBuf
```

Encodes the image as lossless WebP; every pixel's color and alpha stays exact. For an empty image, or one larger than 16384 pixels, it returns an empty buffer.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-Draw.salam

### `EncodeWebPQuality`

```salam
func EncodeWebPQuality(img: Image, quality: int): compress.ByteBuf
```

Encodes the image as WebP with a quality from 0 to 100; quality 100 is the lossless WebP and anything lower makes a lossy WebP, which is much smaller for a photo. The transparency stays exact either way.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-Draw.salam

### `EncodeGIF`

```salam
func EncodeGIF(img: Image): compress.ByteBuf
```

Encodes the image as GIF. If the image has 256 colors or fewer the colors stay exact; otherwise the best 256 colors are picked and put in their place with error diffusion. Pixels with an alpha below 128 become transparent.

The example for this item is shown with the ones above: image-Draw.salam
